Q. 5. ex qua regione hi Magi venerint? Evangelista enim in genere dicit, ipsos venisseαπό ανατολωνab Orientibus, id est, partibus Orientalibus.

Resp. 1. Iustinus in Dial. cum Tryphone pag. 237. statuit, eos venisse ex Araebia, unde etiam Magos vocat Arabicos. Eadem est sententia Epiphanii sub finem Panarii & aliorum. Sed Arabia respectu Iudaeae non est ad Orientem posita, sed versus meridiem. Matth. 12. v. 42. Luc. Burgensis h. l. dicit, venisse ex Chaldaea, aut quod ob propinquiorem situm verisimilius fit, ex Arabia penitiori. Consiat enim, Chaldaeos ut ortu ac regno, ita Magiae studio Persis pri---s fuisse, ac Arabes Chaldaeis vicinos eidem scientiae fuisse deditos, unde Plinius lib. 25. cap. 2. inter celebres Magos à Pytbagora & Demo-rito, priusquam de Na-uris herbarum scriberent, peragratos nume--Magos Arabiae Addit, Iobum etiam & eius amicos fuisse Magos, iam verò Iobum fuisse magnum inter omnes Orientales, vicinum Sab-is, aproinde Arabem.Iob. 1. v. 3. & 15. Ad illud, quod Arabia non fuerit Iudaeae Orientalis, respondet, unae Arabia Iudaeae transa--ana ad Ori--tem conterminae, ulterius inde in Orientem ad Chaldeam us pro-urren-, triplici nomine distingvitur. Una vocatur Arabia deserta, quae vergit ad Aquilonem & metropolin habet Bosram. Altera Arabia petraea, cuius pars quaedam, ut Idumaea, ad meridiem est Iudaeae, metropolis eius Petrae. Tertia Arabia felix, totae ad Orientem Iudaeae sita, media inter desertam ab Aquilone & petraeam à meridie, cuius metropolis Saba (non illa Aethiopiae, Iudaeae admeridiem sita,Matth. 12. v. 42.) sed altera Arabum, quò refert, quod Autor sermonem de Cardinalibus operibus Christi Magos Arabes & incolas Sabae nominat. *(Eandem sententiam, quòd Magi sc. hi Arabes fuerint, amplectuntur quoque Corn. â Lapide, itemque Tirinus, qui tamen parum pensi habentes illam Franc. Lucae distinctionem inter Sabam Aethiopiae, alteramq; Arabum, Magos hos ex eadem Saba venisse scribunt, unde Regina, quae ad Salomonem invisit, 3. Reg. 10. v. 1. neque morantur, quòd illa Austri Regina dicatur, sive â Meridie, Matth. 12. v. 42. hi verò ab Oriente venisse memorentur.

Sed si ex eadem Arabiâ, unde Austri Regina ad Salomonem venit, Sabaeà nempe, quae â Ierusalem distat 606. Leucis Gallicis, (teste Adrichomio in descriptione terrae sanctae, quem laudat Corn. â Lapide Comm. in Matth. c. 12. v. 42. p. 270.) venerunt quoque hi Magi, non video, qui loci distantiam illorum sententiae, qui è Persiâ Magos venisse statuunt, ullâ ratione opponere idem Cornclius possit, quod tamen cumprimis facit: postquam enim è Baronio memoraverat, Clementem Alexandrinum, Chrysostomum, Cyrillum Alexandrinum, & S. Leonem censere, venisse (Magos, gentium primitias) ex Persiae, cùm haec Orientalis sit respectu Iudaeae, subiicit: verùm obstat distantia nimia. Persiae enim trecentis Leucis distat à Iudaea, quod iter tredecim diebus aegrè conficere potuissent Magi. Verum est, drometariis, qui quotidie 40. leucas decurrunt, potuisse absolutè hoc iter tot diebus à cursoribus peragi: verùm reges, deliciis rhedisa suis assueti, non sunt cursores, nec solent, imò nec possunt ita continuò decurrere. Sed falsa quoq; est illa hypothesis, quôd tertio decimo statim die â Christo nato Hierosolymam Magi venerint. Coeterùm suppetias Pontificiis, uti solet, ferre conatus esse Hugo Grotius, cui sententia illa, quòd ab Arabia Magi hi venerint, perplacet, idq; propterea, tum quòd Arabiam Iudaei ut ab ortu adfitam, hoc nomine vulgò appellarint, test. Gen. 10. v. 30.25. v. 6.18.Ios. 1. v. 3.Iud. 6. v. 3.1. Reg. 4. v. 30.Es. 11. v. 14.Ier. 49, 28.

tum quòd munera, quae attulerunt, Arabica sint, non Persica, tum deniq;, quòd non soli Persarum sapientes Ebraeis Graecâ linguâ utentibus Magi dicti, sed & alii. Habuisse enim & Arabiam antiquitus sapientes suos, tum Naturae omnis, tum astrorum cumprimis studiosos. Quin ipsum nomen έλύμας, quod â Luca μάλος vertitur, Act. 13. v. 8. ab Arabiâ venire, & Plinium Magorum Arabiae meminisse &c. An verò hae rationes evincant, Magos, de quibush. l. ex Arabiâ, non verò ex Persiâ venisse, in ipso disputationis actu, ne nimium analecta haec excrescant, videbimus. Sed hâc de re suo loco plura dicendi dabitur fortè D. V. occasio. Si verò vel maximè concedatur, Elymae nomen ex Arabia fortè venisse, non tamen sequitur, etiam aliorum populorum sapientes nomine Magorum fuisse insignitos: imò potiùs apud alios sive de aliis adhibitum plerumq; pro praestigiatore accipitur, ceu ille ipse locus ex Actis confirmat.)*

Sed si vel maximè illa circumstantia, quod ex Oriente venerint, Magis Arabum accommodari posset, tamen ex eo nondum evictum, Magos hosee venisse ex Arabia, cùm scriptores ferè pleriq; omnes Magos in Persiam collocent.

2. Abulensis in cap. 2. Matth. probare conatur, quod ex Mesopotamia venerint.

3. Probabilius est, quòd venerint ex Persia, & quidem ex metropoli regni, videlicet ex urbe Susa, ubi fuit Academia Magorum. Basilius Magnus homilia de nat. Christi: έθνος Περσιηον Μάλθι. Chrysostomus homil. 5. & 6. in Matthaeum semper cos vocat Persas. Strabo, Cicero, Plato Magos in Persiam collocant. Daniel in Chaldaea facit mentionem Magorum cap. 2. ac Abraham, qui venit ex Chaldaeorum, dicitur ex Oriente vocatus, Es. 41. v. 2.Chrysostomo potiùs assentior, inquit Casaubonus in not pag. 182. qui sine ulla dubitatione Evangelista verba Interpretatur de Magis Persarum, quàm Iustino, Epiphanio & nonnullis aeli is, qui istos ex Arabiae deducunt in Iudaeam.

Q. 6. Quare DEUS ex Oriente primitiaes gentilium ad praesepe & regnum Christi vocare voluerit?

Resp. 1. Paradisus, in quo peccatum erat perpetratum, versùs Orientem fuit situs. Quia ergo Christus venerat satisfacturus per peccato, quod in Paradiso Orientali perpetratum & propter quod Paradisus primiparentibus & omnibus eorum posteris fuit clausus, ideò primitias regni sui ex Oriente colligere voluit.

2. In Oriente genus humanum propter peccacum fuerat maledictum. Quia ergo Christus venerat, ut maledictionem illam tolleret, ideò ex Oriente sanctum & benedictum semen colligere caepit.

3. In Oriente turris Babylonica extrui olim erat caepta ex humana & vana praesumtione. Gen. 11. v. 2. August. 16. de Civ. DEI cap. 4. quae ab Hieronymo Epist. 17. vocatur turris superbiae. Christus igitur, qui sua humilitate superbiam nostram expiaturus ve-erat, ex Oriente Magos ad praesepe suum vocavit.

4. In Orience principium omnis idololatriae factum cirea idolum Bel, quod vetustissimum fuit idolum. Berosus lib. 1. Polyd. Virg. lib. 1. de rer. invent. cap. 5. Christus igitur, qui omnem idololatriam destructurus venerat, ex Oriente regni sui primitias accersivit.

5. Christus est Sol iustitiae,Mal. 4. v. 2.Oriens ex altoLuc. 1. v. 18. meritò igitur ex Oriente veniunt gentium primitiae. Bernhard. serm. 3. Epiphan. Meritò ab Oriente veniaent, qui Soliiussitiae novum nobis ortum aununciant, & laetis rumoribus totum orbem illuminant. Chrysost. vel quicunq; alius Autor imperf. oper. homil. 2. Ab Oriente venerunt, unde dies nascitur, inde initium fidei pracessit, quiae fides est lumen animarum.

Q. 7. Quo tempore Hierosolymavenerint? 1. Vulgaris opinio est, quòd die post nativiatem Christi decimo tertio venerint, ipsumque adoraverint. Haec opinio non alio nititur fundamento, quàm incertâ illâ traditione de trimiraculis sexto diIannarii factis. Nicenhorus lib. 1. Hist. Eccl. cap. 13. memorat, quasdam ut hans opinionem tueri possint, fingera, quòd stella Magis biennio -nte Christi na--nitatem apparuerit, propter quod ipsi patriâ relictâ in viam sese dederint. Sed Magi disertè dicunt, se vidisse in Oriente stell-m Regis Iudaeorum, non nascituri, sed nati. v. 2. Alii igitur mirificos comminiscuntur dromedarios, quibus Magi fuerint usi, ut intra tam angustum temporis spacium iter tam longum emetiri potuerint.

2. Eusebius in Chronic. Epiphanius lib. 1. tom. 2. & lib. 1. tom. 2. contra Ebion. statuunt, Magos anno post Christi nativitatem sesundo, biennio ferè expleto venisse Hieresolymam, quam coniecturam Epiphanius probat ex eo, quod Herodes parvulos bimulos occidi iusserit. Niceph. d. l. sic scribit. Duobus annis elapsts post spontaneam illam seminisexpertem conceptionem, uterigestationem, cùm in domicilio Betbleëmitico mater Virgo esset, venerunt. Tatiani etiam Harmonia post purificationis Historiam adventum Magorum collocat. Haec opinio nititur aliâ quadam traditione, quam Autor impers. operis ex Apocrypho quodam libro recitat, quod Magi in extremis Orientis partibus ad ipsum Oceanum habitarint, habentes Scripturam subnomine Seah de apparitura tali stella, & quod stella illa, quae -ato Christo apparuit, Magos proficiscentes per biennium praec-sserit, cùm interea viaticum ipsorum in peris non deficeret.

3. Osiander in Harm. itidem statuit, Magos longo post purificationem intervallo venisse. Primò, quia dies purificationis nato masculo sunt tantùm 33. Lev. 12. v. 4.at intra tam exig-m tempus non potuissent Magi iter tam longum absolvere. Secundò Herodes occidit pucros â bimatu & infra. Effluxerat ergo à nativitate Christi rotum biennium aut paulòo minùs. Tertiò à purificatione parentes Iesu reversi fuère in Bethlehemam. *(Osiandro adstipulatur cumprimis D. Erhardus Leichnerus in comment. anal. de Temp. Magorum, in quâ sententiam hanc, quòd Magorum iter certò contigerit diu sat à peractis diebus & oblatione purificatoriis, athoc nosse, credere, adserere, tanti omninò momenti esse, quanti (in plerissaltem modò recensitis punctis) est ipsa ea Historia, prolixè defendere satagit, qui omninò potest videri.)*

4. Verùm rectiùs statuitur Magos intra dies purificationis venisse, & quidem non longè ante finem istorum -rerum. Primò, quia quod Historia dicit, γεννηθέντος' Ιησου de puero recens nato intelligitur, ut ostendimus superiùs. Et Magi non interrogant de Rege ante biennium nato, sed qui nuper natus v. 2. Secundò, cùm Magi de recens nato Iudaeorum Rege quaerunt, tota Hierosolyma turbatur, ut ob rem novam, de qua nihil hactenus fuerit auditum. v. 3. At post Historiam purificationis solennis illa illustrium personarum Simeonis & Hannae in celebri loco templi facta testificatio, Luc. 2. v. 25. & seqq. non potuit esse in urbe penitus occulta & ignota. Tertiò Lucas dicit, parentes post purificationem non Bethlehemam, sed Nazaretham demigrasse. cap. 2. v. 39. Quartò Chrysostomus ex adverbio ἰδοὺEcce, colligit, Magos non diu post nativitatem venisse. Augustinus itidem haud obscurè statuit, Magos intra dies purificationis advenisse, quem sequitur Gerson in Monotess.

Terminus itineris Magorum statuitur Hierosolyma, Iudaeae metropolis. Fuit haec urbs Regia primò vocata Sedec, unde eius Reges Melchisedec, Adonisedec denominati, Gen. 14. v. 18.Ios. 10. v. 1.Rex iustitiae, Dominus iustitiae. Postea dicta est Salem, pax. Gen. 14. v. 18. Tandem Ierusalem, ex verbo vidit, iuncto cum nomine Salem, ut distingueretur ab altera Salem, de qua Gen. 33. v. 18. quod haec editiori loc in montibus sita ê longinquo videretur. Ioseph. lib. 3. de bello cap. 2. prae caeteris Iudaeae urbibus inter omnes accolas eminens velut caput in corpore. Quidam rationem appellationis desumunt ex Historia Gen. 22. v. 14. ubi nomen illius loci vocatur ab Abrahamo Dominus videbit vel providebit.

Ideò verò Magi rectà contendunt Hierosolymam, quia erat illa totius regni metropolis. Sperabant igitur, vel ibi natum novum illum Iudaeorum Regem, vel ibi posse â Scribis & Legisperitis inquiri, ubi natus sit.

Observ. Christús est ipsa Patris sapientia, ideò sapientes primi omnium ex gentib ad ipsius praesepe deducuntur.

## 2:2
Verse 2. πού ἐστιν ο τεχβεις βασιλεύς. Why did God, who manifested the birth of Christ to the Magi by means of these signs, refuse immediately to make known to those same men the place of his birth? Answer. 1. That through the inquiry of the Magi the birth of Christ might be publicly announced to the Jewish Jerusalemites , and by this means the miracle of the new star might become known to them. 2. That they might be instructed from the prophetic oracle concerning the place of his birth, and thus be more confirmed in faith.

-ιδομεν -υτο τ--ν άςέδα. Concerning this star there is inquiry, 1. What sort was it by Nature?

First, the Author of the books on wonders of Scripture, book 3, chapter 4, states, this star was the Holy Spirit who afterwards appeared at Christ's Baptism in the form of a dove.Luke 3. v. 22. Yet. 1. the author of those books is not Augustine, as we also warned above. 2. this opinion lacks all reason.

Secondly, Chrysostom and Theophylact maintain that it was an Angel, who had appeared to the shepherds. And indeed, angels are often accustomed to appear as flames of fire, Ps. 104. v. 4. nor is it improbable that the brightness of the Lord, which appeared to the Israelite shepherds, was seen by the Gentile Magi in the small form of a star, just as the Lord was once the leader of his people in a pillar of fire, Exod. 13. v. 21. Thirdly, certain mathematicians maintain that it was a planet, under which Christ was born, and by whose power he performed so many miracles, an opinion which Cardan wished to confirm in the previous century.

But Augustine strongly resists this opinion in *Contra Faustum*, book 2, chapter 5. We, he says, place no man’s nativity under the fate of the stars, much less do we believe that the temporal generation of Him who is the creator and Lord of all things was made under the condition of the stars. Thus, that star which the Magi saw, when Christ was born according to the flesh, did not rule over a decree, but served as a testimony; for it did not subject him to its command, but indicated him by its obedience. Likewise. Christ was not born because that star existed, but that new star arose because Christ was born; whence, if it were necessary to speak, we would say that the star was not the fate of Christ, but Christ was the fate of the star; he brought the cause of birth to it, not it to him. The same, Sermon 34 *de tempore*. It did not itself make Christ live miraculously, but Christ made it appear miraculously; nor did it decree Christ’s miracles, but Christ demonstrated it among his own miracles. Fourthly, that this star was not from the number of natural stars created by GOD on the third day of the Hexaemeron, can be proven by various arguments. α.

Fourthly, that this star was not among the number of the natural stars created by GOD on the third day of the hexameron can be proved by various arguments. α. concerning the stars created in the beginning it is written Isaiah 40. v. 26.

Who brings forth their host in number, and in so great multitude not even one has been lacking. But the star which was seen by the Magi neither before nor after did it appear. β. Stars are moved from Rising toward Setting. But now this star advanced from Jerusalem toward Bethlehem, that is, from North into South, in such a way that it showed the road to those making their journey. γ. This star first appears in the East, then hidden it lies concealed, and when the Magi had set out from Jerusalem suddenly appeared again, which the physical account of the celestial sphere does not admit. δ. Nor could the Magi have spoken about a star that would have appeared almost four thousand years before, saying We saw his star. ε. Its position shows that the place of this star was not among the heavenly orbs, but in the air, indeed in its lower region; for by proceeding it points out the way to travelers, and between adjacent buildings it could single out that unique house in which Jesus was. ζ. Chemnit. Harm. pag. 203. This star, as need required, appeared, now in the West, v. 10., some days earlier in the East, v. 2., whereas the stars of heaven are carried by ordinary motion. η. This star came to rest when it directly reached the house in which Christ was, but the natural stars are in perpetual motion.

Fifthly, Origen, book 1. against Celsus, fol. 12., asserts that it was a comet, but this opinion Basil refutes in the sermon on the human generation of Christ, tom. 1. 1. pag. 390., and shows by several arguments that it was a new star, never seen before.

Sixthly, either therefore there was some wonderful μετέωρον in a very low place of the air (for Matthew calls it φαινομένου,, which because it appeared in the appearance of a star, therefore the Evangelist according to the customary phrase of Scripture, whereby things are called not what they are but what they seem, calls it a star, just as also elsewhere unknown and shining visions on account of their form and appearance are often named stars in Scripture, Apoc. 1. v. 16. chap. 8. v. 10. chap. 12. v. 1.); or it was a completely new star wonderfully brought forth by GOD.

Chalcidius, a most ancient Greek author, commenting on Plato's Timaeus, who lived shortly before the birth of Christ, makes mention of this star. When he had reviewed various portents concerning stars, he finally adds: There is something holier and more venerable in History, which tells of the rising of a certain unusual star, announcing not sicknesses deaths, but the venerable descent of GOD for the preservation of humankind, the nature of such things and grace, which they testify was observed by the Chaldeans, who honored God newly born with gifts.

2. How could the Magi know the birth of Christ from the rising of the star?

Ans. 1. Augustine holds that the Magi knew the time of the Messiah's birth by a special divine revelation. For afterwards too they were warned by a divine oracle not to return to Herod. Therefore just as a divine oracle governed the return journey of the Magi, so the same can quite reasonably be thought to have been given to them concerning their first departure. Leo, sermon 3 on Epiphany, likewise holds that this was done through divine inspiration. While they looked upon GOD, he says, He gave understanding. Yet the same man, sermon 1 on Epiphany, seems to go toward this view, that they were able to understand it from the unusual brilliance of this star. That star, he says, brighter than the others and more beautiful than the stars, easily turns to itself the eyes minds of those who gaze at it, so that immediately it would be noticed that what appeared so unusual was not idle. Nicephorus, book 1 of Ecclesiastical History, chapter 13: GOD himself stirring up their minds to this.

2. Chrysostom, homil. 6. in Matth. maintains that they were instructed about this mystery through the response of an Angel. Jacob Faber Stapul. in h. l. What wonder is it if they learned this through the suggestion of the Angel who was presenting the spectacle, just as they also learned, once the King of glory had been adored and the mystical gift offered, what they were to do by his same teaching.

3. Jerome, Chrysostom, and Theophylact maintain, that the Magi were of the posterity of Balaam, who prophesied concerning the Messiah in these words. A Star shall rise out of Jacob &c. Num. 24. v. To which also pertains what Origen, homil. 13. in Matth. near the end says, that the Eastern Magi had everything written down that Balaam had once prophesied. homil 15. near the end, he maintains, that the Magi descended from Balaam, whether by succession of lineage or by tradition of discipline.

4. Chrysostom, or whoever else is the author of the imperfect work, homil. 2. argues, that the Magi possessed a certain writing under the name of Seth concerning such a star that was to appear at the time of Christ’s birth and concerning the gifts to be offered to Him.

5. Augustine Steuchus holds that the Erythraean Sibyl, who was a Chaldean, handed down to the school of the Chaldean Magi both the time of the coming of the Son of GOD in the flesh and the sign by which his birth was to be made known from heaven to come about. Hence Suetonius writes in the life of Vespasian that at that time a report filled the entire East that a King was about to come out of Judaea: and Cicero indicates in book 2 of On Divination that it had been found in the Sibylline books that there would be a King around that time, whom all who wished to be saved would have to acknowledge and call King. They relate that some Sibyl predicted beforehand this indication of the star about to rise, and predicted it so that when they beheld it they might follow the guiding star and adore the great King.

6. Eusebius, in book 9 of *Demonstratio Evangelica*, chapter 1, seems to establish that the Magi could have gathered this from the position of the appearing Star, for he says that it had been established above the zenith and perpendicular to the land of Judea. But to understand this mystery, that the birth of a new King is portended by this star, neither the knowledge of art, nor the brightness of the star, nor its position could provide sufficient evidence.

7. It seems simplest to establish that Daniel, educated in the school of the Magi, without doubt on occasion instilled doctrine about the Messiah into certain Magi: *(To this view B. D. Calixtus also inclines, establishing that the Magi were helped by an extraordinary and supernatural divine revelation when they wondered at this star and investigated its causes but did not find them, imploring the help of GOD; nor would it be entirely unlike the truth if they searched the writings of Daniel, which had been preserved among the Persians up to that day)* therefore, since they understood that that fixed time of weeks Dan. 9. v. 24. had elapsed, and saw a new star appearing in heaven, they could conclude from this that the coming of the Messiah was signified thereby. Add to this that not all Jews returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem, but remained in many places, from whom the savor of the doctrine concerning the Messiah spread even to the nations. Finally, the writings of the Prophets were read in the Greek language even by the nations. Chemn. in Harm. p. 212. If they were Chaldeans, they had among their ancestors those who spoke wondrous things about the Son of God begotten from the eternal mind and destined sometime to come forth into the world. If they were Arabs, they had Abraham among their forebears, who taught his sons to await someday that promised seed in which all nations were to be blessed, Gen. 12. v. 3.cap. 18. v. 19. The Chaldeans received the promise of the coming of the King Messiah while the Hebrews were living in exile in Babylonia and Persia.

3. Why did God call these Magi to the kingdom of Christ by the rising of a new star?

Ans. 1. Chrysostom, homily 6 on Matthew: God calls the Magi by those things which familiarity made customary to them, condescending in a wondrous manner of dispensation to the salvation of men. Theophylactus on this passage: Just as Peter, a fisherman, was impelled by the taking of a huge multitude of fishes to follow Christ: so it was fitting that the Magi, because they were astrologers, should be drawn thither by some sign familiar to themselves. 2. The same Chrysostom brings forward this cause. They are called by a new heavenly body, so that by a new Star they might be taught the truth, who had abused those old stars to all impiety. 3. Mystically, by this star is denoted the word of GOD, which is a lamp unto our feet,Ps. 119. v. 105. by whose guidance we can come to Christ. 2 Petr. 1. v. 19.

4. In what sense do the Magi say that they saw the star of the King of the Jews in the East? Ans. This can be understood in two ways: either because this star appeared in the eastern part of the sky, since it foreannounced the dayspring of the Sun of righteousness and the orient from on high visiting us,Mal. 4. v. 2.Luc. 1. v. 78. or because the Magi, being in the East, saw the star of the Messiah above that place which had been destined by divine appointment for the birth of the King of the Jews. The latter sense agrees better with the text. Προ-κυν-σαι. Some copies read πρ---νήσαι άυτω. others π-οσκυν-σαι άυτον. Compare verse 11.

Latin:

v. 2. πού ἐστιν ο τεχβεις βασιλεύς.Quare Deus, qui nativitatem Christi Magis hisce manifestavit, noluerit statim locum nativitatis iis dem manifestare? Resp. 1. ut per inquisitionem Magorum na-ivitas Christi Iudaeis Hierosolymitanis publicè annunciaretur, ac miraculum novae stellae hac ratione illis innotesceret. 2. ut ex vaticinio Prophetico de loco nativitatis instruerentur, sicq; in fide magis confirmarentur.

-ιδομεν -υτο τ--ν άςέδα. De hac stella quaeritur, 1. Qualis fuerit Naturae?

Primò Autor librorum de mirabil. Script. lib. 3. cap. 4. statuit, hanc stellam fuisse Spiritum S. qui in Baptismo Christi in specie columbae postea apparuit.Luc. 3. v. 22. Atqui. 1. autor illorum librorum non est Augustinus, uti superius etiam monuimus. 2. caret haec sententia omni ratione.

Secundò Chrysost. & Theophyl. statuunt, fuisse Angelum, qui Pastoribus apparuerat. Et sanè Angeli tanquam flammae ignis saepiùs apparere solent, Ps. 104. v. 4. nec improbabile est, claritatem Domini, quae pastoribus Israëliticis apparuit, fuisse Magis Ethnicis visam in formâ exiguâ stellae, sicut iam olim Dominus in columna ignis fuit Dux populi sui, Exod. 13. v. 21.

Tertiò quidam Mathematici statuunt, fuisse Planetam, sub quo Christus natus, & cuius virtute tot miracula ediderit, quam opinionem superiore seculo confirmare voluit Cardanus. Sed huic opinioni acriter reluctatur August. lib. 2. contra Faustum cap. 5. Nos, inquit, sub fato stellarum nullius hominis Genesin ponimus, quantò n--us illius temporalem generationem sub astrorum conditione credimus factam, qui est universorum creator & Dominus. Itaa illa stella, quam viderunt Magi, Christo secundùm carnem naeto, non ad decretum dominabatur, sed ad testimonium famulabatur, nec enim subiiciebat imperio, sed indicabat obsequio. It. Non ideò Christus est natus, quia illa stella extitit, sed ideò illa nova exorta est, quia Christus natus est, unde si dici oportebat, non stellam Christo, sed Christum stellae fatum fuisse, diceremus, ipse quoilli, non illa huic nascendi attulit causam Idem serm. 34. de temp. Non ipsa Christum fecit mirabi-iter vivere, sed Christus ipsam fecit mirabiliter apparere, nec ipsa Christi mirabilia decrevit, sed ipsam Christus int-r sua mirabilia demonstravit.

Quartò, non fuisse hanc stellam ex numero siderum naturalium tertio hexämeri die à DEO creatorum, variis argumentis probari potest. α. de stellis in principio creatis scriptum est Esai 40. v. 26.

Qui educit in numero militiam eorum, & in tanta multitudi-ne unum quidem defuit. Stella verò, quae Magis visa est, nec a-tea, nec post apparuit. β. Stellae moventur ab Ortu in Occasu-. Iam verò haec stella ab Hierosolyma Bethlehemam versus, hoc est, â Septentrione in meridiem ita processit, ut iter facientibus viam monstraret. γ. Haec stella primûm in Oriente apparet, mox occultata latet, & Magis Hierosolymâ egressis repente rursus apparer, quod physica ratio Sphaerae caelestis non admittit. δ. Nec de Stella, quae ante annos fermè quater mille apparuisset, dicere potuissent Magi, Vidimus eius stellam.ε. Situs ostendit, locum huius stellae non fuisse in orbib. caelestibus, sed in aere, & quidem in regione eius inferiore, procedendo enim monstrat proficiscentibus viam, & inter contigua aedificia unicam illam domum, in qua Iesus erat, notare poterat. ζ. Chemn. Harm. pag. 203. Stella haec, prout opus fuit, apparuit, nunc in Occidente v. 10. ante dies aliquot in Oriente. v. 2. cùm caelestes stellae ordinario ferantur motu. η. Quievit haec stella, cùm directè attingeret domum, in qua erat Christus, sed astra naturalia sunt in perpetuo motu.

Quintò Origines lib. 1. contra Celsum fol. 12. statuit, fuisse Cometam, sed hanc opinionem confutat Basilius serm. de humana Christi generatione tom. 1. 1. pag. 390. & aliquot argumentis ostendit, fuisse stellam novam, antè nunquàm conspectam.

Sextò vel ergo fuit mirabile aliquod μετέωρον in loco äeris valde humili (Matthaeus enim vocat φαινομένου, quod quia stellae specie apparuit, ideò Evangelista iuxta usitatam Scripturae phrasin, quâ res vocantur, non quales sunt, sed quales apparent, vocat stellam, sicut etiam aliàs visiones ignotae & lucidae propter speciem & apparentiam saepè in Scriptura nominantur stellae,Apoc. 1. v. 16.cap. 8. v. 10.cap. 12. v. 1.) vel fuit stella planè nova mirabiliter â DEO producta.

Meminit huius stellae Chalcidius vetustissimus autor Graecus super Timaeum Platonis, qui paulò ante Christum natum vixit. Is cùm varia de stellis portenta recensuisset, tandem subiicit. Est quoalia sanctior & venerabilior Historia, quae per-ibet ortum stellae cuiusdam insolitae non morbos mortespronunciantis, sed descensum DEI venerabilem ad humanae servationis, rerummor talium gratiam, quam à Chaldaeis observatam fuisse testantur, qui Deum nuper natum muneribus venerati sunt.

2. Quomodo Magi ex ortu stellae potuerint Christi nativitatem cognoscere?

Resp. 1. Augustinus statuit, Magos ex peculiari patefactione divina tempus nati Messiae cognovisse. Nam & postea divino oraculo moniti sunt, ne reverterentur ad Herodem. Sicut ergo divinum oraculum reditum Magorum gubernavit, ita idem de prima profectione suscipienda ipsis datum, haud absurdè cogitari potest. Leo serm. 3. Epiph. itidem statuit, factum id esse per inspirationem divinam. DEO, inquit, aspicientibus intellectum dante. Idem tamen serm. 1. Epiph. videtur eò abire, quod ex insolito stellae huius fulgore id intelligere potuerint. Stella isthaec, inquit illustrior caeteris pulchriora sideribus facilè in se intuentium oculos animosconvertit, ut confestim anim adverteretur, non esse otiosum, quod tam insolitum apparebat. Niceph. lib. 1. Histor. Eccl. cap. 13. DEO ipso animos eorum ad hoc incitante.

2. Chrysostomus homil. 6. in Matth. per Angeli responsum ipsos de hoc mysterio edoctos statuit. Iacob. Faber Stapul. in h. l. Quid mirum, si id Angelo, qui spectaculum faciebat, insinuante didicerunt, qui etiam discunt, adorato Rege gloriae & mystico munere oblato, eodem docente, quid ipsis sit faciendum.

3. Hieronymus, Chrysostomus & Theophylactus statuunt, Magos fuisse exposteritate Bileami, qui de Messia vatic----tus est his verbis. Orietur Stella ex Iacob &c. Num. 24.v. Quò etiam pertinet, quòd Origen. homil. 13. in Matth. circa finem dicit, Magos Orientales omnia scripto comprehensa habuisse, quae Bileamus olim fuerit vaticinatus. homil 15. circa fin. statuit, Magos à Bileam descendisse, sive per generis successionem, sive per disciplinae traditionem.

4. Chrysostomus vel quicunq; alius Autor operis imperf. homil. 2. disputat, Magos habuisse Scripturam quandam sub nomine Seth de apparitura tali Siella tempore nativitatis Christi & de muneribus ipsi offerendis.

5. Augustinus Steuchus statuit, Sybillam Erythraeam, quae Chaldaea fuit, tradidisse Scholae Magorum Chaldaeorum & tempus adventûs Filii DEI in carnem, & signum, quo caelitus eius nativitas indicanda foret. Atinde Suetonium in Vespasiano scribere, eam famam totum tunc Orientem replevisse, ex Iudaea circa illa tempora Regem venturum: ac Ciceronem lib. 2. de divinat. subindicare, in libris Sibyllinis inventum fuisse, Regem circa illa tempora futurum, qui ab omnibus Rex & agnos-endus & vocandus foret, qui salvi esse vellent. Ferunt, Sibyllam aliquam hoc orituri sideris indicium praedixisse, ac praedixisse, ut illud conspicati ducem stellam sequerentur, Regemq; magnum adorarent.

6. Euseb. lib. 9. demonst. Evang. cap. 1. videtur statuere, Magos id colligere potuisse ex situ Stellae apparentis, dicit enim, illam supra verticem & ad perpendiculum terrae Iudaeae fuisse constitutum. Sed ad intelligendum hoc mysterium, quod per hanc stellam novi Regis nativitas portendatur, nec artis scientia, nec stellae fulgor, nec eiusdem situs sufficiens documentum exhibere potuit.

7. Simplicissimum videtur statuere, quòd Daniel in Schola Magorum educatus sine dubio occasione illius familiaritatis doctrinam de Messia quibusdam Magis instillaverit: *(Huc inclinat quoque B. D. Calixtus statuens, extraordinariâ & supernaturali revelatione divinitus fuisse adivos Magos, quum stellam hanc admirarentur, caussas eius vestigarent, nec invenirent, opemDEI implorantes, scripta Danielis, quae in eam usa diem apud Persas adservaeta fuisse, vero haut absimile esse, scrutarentur)* cùm ergo intelligerent, definitum illud tempus septimanarum Dan. 9. v. 24. effluxisse, & novam in caelo stellam apparere viderent, inde colligere potuerunt, Messiae adventum eâ notari. Accedit, quod non omnes Iudaei ex Babylonico exilio Hierosolymam reversi, sed multis in locis manserunt, â quibus odor doctrinae de Messia etiam ad gentes dimanavit. Deniq; scripta Prophetarum in lingua Graeca etiam â gentibus legebantur. Chemn. in Harm. p. 212. Si fuerunt Chaldaei, habuerunt inter maiores suos, qui de DEI Filio ab aeterna mente genito, inq; mundum aliquando prodituro mira dixerunt. Si fuerunt Arabes, habuerunt inter maiores Abrahamum, qui filios suos docuit, expectandum aliquando promissum illud semen, in quo benedicendae omnes gentes, Gen. 12. v. 3.cap. 18. v. 19. Chaldaei ab Hebraeis in Babylonia & Persia exulantibus acceperunt promissionem de Messiae Regis adventu.

3. Quare Deus hosce Magos per novae stellae exortum ad Christi regnum vocaverit?

Resp. 1. Chrysost. homil. 6. in Matth. per ea Deus Magos vocat, quae familiaria ipsis consuetudo faciebat, mira dispensationis specie ad hominum condescendens salutem. Theophyl. in h. l. Sicut Petrus piscator caeptâ piscium multitudine ingenti ad Christum sequendum impulsus est: ita consentaneum fuit, Magos, quia Astrologi fuêre, signo aliquo sibi familiari eò allectos. 2. Idem Chrysostomus hanc affert causam. Per novum sidus vocantur, ut per novam Stellam docerentur veritatem, qui veteribus illis stellis ad omnem impietatem erant abusi. 3. Mysticè per hanc stellam denotatur verbum DEI, quod est lucerna pedum nostrorum,Ps. 119. v. 105. eius ductu ad Christum pervenire possumus. 2 Petr. 1. v. 19.

4. Quo sensu Magi dicant, se vid-sse stellam Regis Iudaeorum in Oriente? Resp. dupliciter hoc inrelligi potest, vel quòd haec stella in parte caeli Orientali apparuerit, quippe praenuncians ortum iustitiae Solis & visitationem Orientis ex alto.Mal. 4. v. 2.Luc. 1. v. 78. vel quod Magi in Oriente existentes viderint stellam Messiae super illum locum, qui divinitus nativitati Regis Iudaeorum destinatus erat. Posterior sensus magis congruit textui. Προ-κυν-σαι. Quaedam exemplaria legunt πρ---νήσαι άυτω. quaedam π-οσκυν-σαι άυτον. Confer v. 11.

## 2:3
v. 3. -ταράχ-θη has the meaning of violent disturbance and commotion.

But why is Herod troubled? Ans. 1. He knew himself to be a foreigner, and to have obtained the kingdom by force; hence at the mention of the newly born King of the Jews he rages furiously. 2. He feared lest the kinsmen of the nobles slain by him should join themselves with that new King for his overthrow. 3. He also feared danger to himself from the people, most intolerant of foreign rule, whom he had grievously offended by his robberies and cruelty.

4. He was the more disturbed because foreigners announced that that promised King sprung from the stock of the Jews had now been born, and indeed had been born among the Jews, concerning whose birth he had up to then learned nothing whatsoever. Therefore he suspected that the matter was deliberately concealed by the natives.

Why then was all Jerusalem troubled together?

Ans. 1. They knew from the records of preceding Histories that the form of government could be changed, not without a very copious shedding of blood, and slavery shaken off.

2. The Jews feared a servitude even sadder than the former, because they knew that Herod could endure anything rather than the suspicion of a usurped kingdom.

3. Theophylact gives this reason, because -νόητον --ήμα η ποιηρία.

4. It could also happen that some were disturbed by wonderment at the new message.

But both the disturbance of Herod and of the Jerusalemites arose solely from a false opinion about the earthly kingdom of the Messiah, which they had sucked from the breasts of the Pharisees; whence the Church sings. Herod, wicked enemy, why do you fear Christ to come? He takes not mortal things, who gives heavenly kingdoms.

Obs. What will the judgment-seat of the Judge do, when the birth of an infant terrifies proud Kings? What will he do sitting on his throne in heaven, when lying in a manger he terrifies?

Latin:

v. 3. -ταράχ-θη significationem habet vehementis perturbationis & commotionis.

Quare verò Herodes turbatur? Resp. 1. noverat, se esse alienigenam, & regnum vi obtinuisse, inde ad mentionem nati novi Regis Iudaeorum obtimescit. 2. metuebat, ne Procerum â se interfectorum cognati cum novo isto Rege in sui oppressionem sese coniungerent. 3. metuebat etiam sibi â populo alieni regiminis impatientissimo, quem rapinis & crudelitate sua graviter offenderat.

4. Eò magis turbatus est, quod exteri nunciarent, novum illum ex Iudaeorum stirpe promissum natum esse Regem, & quidem inter Iudaeos natum esse, de cuius nativitate nihil prorsus intellexerat hactenus. Suspicabatur itaque, rem de industria celari ab indigenis.

Quare simul tota Hierosolyma turbatur?

Resp. 1. noverant ex actis praecedentium Historiarum, non sine largissima sanguinis effusione formam regiminis mutari & servitutem excuti posse.

2. Metuebant Iudaei servitutem priore adhuc tristiorem, quia noverant Herodem quidvis potiùs ferre posse, quàm suspicionem adfectati regni.

3. Theophyl. hanc reddit rationem, quia -νόητον --ήμα η ποιηρία.

4. Fieri etiam potuit, ut quidam ex novi nuncii admiratione turbarentur.

Sed & Herodis & Hierosolymitanorum perturbatio ex falsâ opinione de terreno Messiae regno, quam ex Pharisaeorum mammillis suxerant, unicè oriebatur, unde Ecclesia canit. Herodes hostis impie, Christum venire quid times? Non arripit mortalia. Qui regna dat coelestia.

Obs. Quid faciet tribunal iudicis, quando superbos Reges terret nativitas infantis? Quid faciet sedens in coelesti solio, quando terret iacens in praesepio?

## 2:4
v. 4. χαί συναγαγων πάντας τούς άδχιεροίς. By Ἀρχιερεῖς. 1. Some understand in general those who, being sprung from the posterity of Aaron, since they alone were called ίερείς, that is, Priest, were heads of their families, who are otherwise called Chiefs -ctuaries. 1. Paralipomenon ch. 24. v. 5. Chiefs of Priests, 2. Paralipomenon ch. 36. v. 11.

2. Theophylact on Mark chapter 14 understands those to be so called who had at some time discharged the office of High Priest; for at that time the high priesthood according to law was no longer perpetual, but purchasable and annual.

3. Some understand chief Priests, who excelled among them in authority, learning, prudence, especially those who were Assessors of the Sanhedrin, without whom no Council could be convened.

Γραμματεῖς τού λαού. Of Scribes three kinds are found in Holy Writ. One of those who attended upon the Kings, whatever finally their function may have been 2. Sam. 9. v. 3.ch. 20. v. 25.2. Reg. 12. v. 10.c. 22. v 3.

Another kind, of those who seem to have written out private contracts and instruments, whom We read in 1. Paralipomenon chap. 2. v. 55. that those who were accustomed to devote themselves to this task were called Notaries, the Cinaeans otherwise having received no inheritance with the tribes; whence David seems to have alluded in Ps. 45. v. 2. Finally, experts in the divine Law were also called Scribes among others, under which name Ezra is praised, Esdras chap. 7. v. 6. 11. & 12., 1. Esdras chap. 7. v. 10.: Ezra prepared his heart, to seek the law of the Lord and to do it, and to teach in Israel precept and judgment. The office therefore of these men was to teach the law both in the synagogues and in the temple, on account of which they are called νομικόι Experts in the Law, Jurists, as appears from Matt. 7. v. 29. chap. 23. v. 10. Mark 12. v. 28. Luke 7. v. 30. chap. 11. v. 46. 1. Cor. 1. v. 20. That Pharisee whom Matthew calls νομικόν an expert in the Law in chap. 22. v. 35., Mark expressly calls a Scribe in chap. 12. v. 28.

Because here they are called Scribes of the people, it appears from this that some had been chosen out of that order who, joined to the chief Priests, filled up the ecclesiastical assembly, just as other Scribes, joined either to the Elders of the people, that is, the Senators, whom at length the Hebrews called the Sanhedrin, or to that civil Council of seventy men, were likewise called Scribes of the people 1. Macc. 5. v. 42., whom most think to have been set over executing the judgments of the Sanhedrin. But that those men were called Scribes because they devoted themselves to writing and interpreting the law, as guardians of the sacred tablets, can be established from Jeremiah 8. v. 8., Beza on this passage of Matt.

With these Scribes, as trustees, the books of the law were deposited as it were in trust, since their interpretation was committed to them, whence they are called Scribes of the people, because they were public interpreters of the divine law before the people. Therefore they took their designation not so much from writing, as from the Sacred Scriptures, whose interpretation and exposition was by reason of their office entrusted to them; although certain ones hold that none but they were permitted to copy out the holy books, lest they should be corrupted, by which reasoning too they might have taken their name from writing.

Elijah the Tishbite. -- The wise are those who are also called Rabbins.

Πού ό χρις ός γεννάται, that is, μέλλει γεννάθαι. thus 1. Cor. 15. v. 35. πως έγείρονται νεκροί, that is, μέλλουσι έγείδει. *(some refer even these passages here Matt. 17. v. 11. chap. 11. v. 3.)* Certain ones say γεννάται

put for γεννηθήσεται so that it is an enallage of tense not lacking emphasis. (Whence also the Syrian has not badly rendered -- he who was to be born, just as the Arabic too, rendering --, and likewise the Ethiopian, which has -- ) For by the verb of present tense regard is had to Scripture as set before the eyes, which bears witness concerning Christ in all ages. Thus Hebr. 2. v. 16. Therefore the sense is, where according to the Scriptures Christ ought to be born, which place the oracles of the Prophets assign to the birth of Christ.

Latin:

v. 4. χαί συναγαγων πάντας τούς άδχιεροίς. Per Ἀρχιερεῖς. 1. quidam in genere intelligunt eos, qui ex posteris Aaronis, ut pote qui soli ίερείς, id est, Sacerdote, dicebantur, oriundi, erant familiarum suarum capita, qui aliàs vocantur Principes --ctuarii. 1. Paral. 24. v. 5. Principes Sacerdotum, 2. Paral. 36. v. 11.

2. Theophylactus in cap. 14. Marc. intelligit eos sic vocatos, qui aliquando Pontificatu maximo functi fuissent, eâ enim tempestate Pontificatus iuxta legem non amplius erat perpetuus, sed venalis atque annuus.

3. Quidam intelligunt primarios Sacerdotes, qui autoritate, eruditione, prudentiâ inter illos eminebant, cumprimis eos, qui erant Assessores Synedrii, sine quibus nullum congregari poterat Concilium.

Γραμματεῖς τού λαού.Scribarum in sacris literis tria reperiuntur genera. Unum eorum qui Regib. apparebant, quodcunq; tandem corum munus fuerit 2. Sam. 9. v. 3.cap. 20. v. 25.2. Reg. 12. v. 10.c. 22. v 3.

Alterum eorum, qui privatorum contractus & instrumenta videntur descripsisse, quos Notarios vocamus, cui rei operam solitos fuisse navare Kinaeos, nullam alioquin hereditatem cum tribubus sortitos, legimus 1. Paral. 2. v. 55. quò videtur allusisse David Ps. 45. v. 2.Scribae denique dicti sunt Iuris divini periti inter caeteros, quo nomine laudatur Ezras, Esdr. 7. v. 6. 11. & 12. 1. Esdr. 7. v. 10. Ezras paravit cor suum, ut investigaret legem Domini & faceret, & doceret in Israël praeceptum & iudicium. Munus igitur hor. fuit, tum in Synagogis, tum in templo legem docere, quâ de causa νομικόιLegisperiti, Legistae dicuntur, ut patet ex Matth. 7. v. 29.cap. 23. v. 10.Marc. 12. v. 28.Luc. 7. v. 30.cap. 11. v. 46.1. Cor. 1. v. 20. Pharisaeum illum, quem Matthaeus cap. 22. v. 35.νομικόνLegisperitum dicit, Marcus disertè Scribam vocat cap. 12. v. 28.

Quia hoc loco dicuntur Scribae populi, ex eo apparet, selectos fuisse ex illo ordine nonnullos, qui primariis Sacerdotibus adiuncti Ecclesiasticum caetum explerent, sicut etiam Senioribus populi, id est, Senatoribus, quos Sanhedrin Hebraei demum vocarunt, sive civili illi LXX. virorum Synedrio adiuncti erant alii Scribae, itidem Scribae populi appellati 1. Macc. 5. v. 42. quos plerisque placet fuisse exequendis Synedrii iudiciis praefectos. Scribas autem illos dictos fuisse ex eo, quod legi scribendae & interpretandae vacarent, quasi Sacrarum tabularum custodes, constare potest ex Ierem. 8. v. 8. Beza in h. l. Matth.

Penes hos scribas tanquam sequestres libri legis erant velut depositi, utpote quorum Interpretatio ipsis commissa, unde vocantur Scribae populi, quia erant publici legis divinae coram populo interpretes. Ergo non tam â scribendo, quàm â Scripturis sacris, quarum Interpretatio & enarratio ratione officii ipsis erat commissa, denominationem acceperunt, quamvis quidam statuunt, non aliis, quàm ipsis licuisse describere Sacros libros, ne depravarentur, quâ ratione etiam à scribendo nomen habere potuissent.

Elias in Thisbi. --sapientes sunt, qui & ipsi dicuntur Rabbanim.

Πού ό χρις ός γεννάται, id est, μέλλει γεννάθαι. sic 1. Cor. 15. v. 35.πως έγείρονται νεκροί, id est, μέλλουσι έγείδει. *(nonnulli huc referunt & haec loca Matth. 17. v. 11.cap. 11. v. 3.)* Quidam dicunt γεννάται

positum pro γεννηθήσεται ut sit enallage temporis non carens emphasi. *(Unde quoque Syrus non malè vertit --nasciturus esset, quemadmodum & Arabs, vertens -- ac pariter Aethiops, qui habet --)* Nam verbo temporis praesentis respicitur ad Scripturam tanquam ante oculos positam, quae omnibus aetatibus testatur de Christo. Sic Hebr. 2. v. 16. Sensus igitur est, ubi Christum secundùm Scripturas nasci oporteat, quem locum nativitati Christi oracula Prophetarum assignent.

## 2:5
v. 5. Either this opinion was widespread among the Jews, or arose from the decision of this Council, that Christ would be born at Bethlehem Ioh. 7. v. 42. or from the prophetic oracle of Micah, which is more likely, whereby this became known to them.

Latin:

v. 5. Vel pervulgata fuit apud Iudaeos opinio, vel ex determinatione huius Concilii orta, Christum Bethlehemi nasciturum Ioh. 7. v. 42. vel ex oraculo Michae Prophetico, quod versimilius, ipsis hoc innotuit.

## 2:6
v. 6. It is asked here, how the citation of the Gospel agrees with the saying of the prophet Micah. 5. In Jerome's commentaries there is cited the version of the Seventy Interpreters, which rendered the prophetic passage quite plainly just as Matthew cites it. For as we warned above, prol. 2., the Evangelists mostly retain the words of the Greek version, which was then customary: but in that edition which we possess, it reads otherwise. The Syrian rendered it thus, as the words are cited negatively in the Evangelist. Jacobus Faber Stapulensis seems to have despaired of reconciling them, therefore he cries out in his commentary on this passage: Would that Matthew the Hebrew survived, so that all obscurity might be removed! Jerome in book 2 -omm. on Micah asserts two responses. This testimony, he says, that it fits neither the Hebrew text nor the version of the Seventy Interpreters, is evident even while I remain silent, and I think that Matthew, wishing to convict the priests and scribes of negligence toward the books of divine Scripture, placed it thus even as it was said by them. (Jerome therefore thinks that these things are recited by the Evangelist from the mouth of the Scribes. But it is more likely that these things are brought forward by the Evangelist from his own mind, in which he wished to show whence the scribes learned that Christ was to be born in Bethlehem.) Jerome continues: There are however those who assert that in almost all testimonies taken from the Old Testament there is such error, either that the order is changed, or the words, and sometimes indeed the very sense itself differs, whether in the Apostles or the Evangelists, because they do not pick testimonies from a book, but trust their memory, which is sometimes deceived. μιμητικως

(But this response is exceedingly harsh and improbable, for how indeed Could -μάά-τημα μνημονευτικ-ν be attributed to those who wrote under divine inspiration? How indeed could they follow a sense different from the prophetic oracles, seeing that they were driven by one and the same Spirit with the Prophets?) Therefore a more fitting reconciliation must be sought. This is the first apparent contradiction. With the Prophet the place of his birth is called Bethlehem Ephrata. With Matthew, Bethlehem of the land of Judah. Answer: Diversity of description does not straightaway introduce any contradiction. Each description is added so as to distinguish it from the other Bethlehem, which was located in the tribe of Zebulon, while this one was in the tribe of Judah, as we pointed out above on v. 1. It took the surname of Ephrata Gen. 35. v. 19.chapt. 48. v. 7.1. Sam. 17. v. 12. from the wife of Caleb. 1. paral. 2. v. 19. Ludov. Vives on book 18. Aug. de C. D. chapt. 30. Ephrata is the district in which lies Bethlehem, the city of David, in the tribe of Judah; which name, being old-fashioned and less familiar to ordinary folk the priests passed over when they spoke to Herod, a foreign-born prince, appending what was better known, of Judah.

The second apparent contradiction is this. The Prophet calls it least; the Evangelist denies that it is least. Answer: 1. Osiander, book 1. Harmony, chapter 10, maintains that the prophetic passage ought to be rendered thus. And hey -u, Bethlehema Ephrata, it is little that thou shouldest be among the Thousands or Chiliarchs of Judah &c. For since the Hebrews lack the neuter gender, they employ a masculine or feminine word in its stead. Now it amounts to the same thing whether you say, Little is it that thou shouldest be among the princes of Judah, or that it is not least among the princes of Judah. The neuter is placed here adverbially, and an infinitive is joined to it τού έίναι, which stands in the Hebrew and Greek text, in this sense: Little is it that thou shouldest be among the thousands of Judah. Osiander presses the point that the Prophet αίτιολογικως adds, out of thee shall he come forth unto me. But there will be no coherence whatsoever if it is rendered: Thou, Bethlehem, art very small, because out of thee the Messiah shall be born unto me. Likewise because the Scribes and Chief Priests understood Micah thus.

2. Very nearly matching this view is what certain persons maintain, namely that the words of Micah are to be read interrogatively, and that the interrogation in this place carries the force of a negation. Art thou least? that is, thou art by no means least, just as the Evangelist rendered it: όυδαμως έλαχίςη, that is, μεγίςη έι. So Herodotus concerning Zalmoxis. έλλήνων όυ τω άθενεςατω οςφιςή Πυθαγρη. *(This reply seems exceedingly well suited to Hugo Grotius likewise, and the same author further remarks, The question-word -- is often omitted, as in Iob. 40. v. 20.1. Reg. 21. v. 7.Zach. 8. v. 6.)*

3. Most seek a reconciliation in considering Bethlehem differently. The Prophet calls Bethlehem small by reason of its external splendour, which was exceedingly meagre, and by reason of earthly wealth; at the same time he hints that God will be hindered not at all by this humble condition so that He might less bestow most ample honour on this little town, namely by bringing forth Christ from it: the Evangelist says she is by no means to be called small, with respect, namely, to that singular honour which the birth of the Messiah had procured for her, and which was esteemed worthy by the favour of GOD. In the time of the Prophet she was small, but not in the time of the Evangelist, since Christ had already been born in her.

That reconciliation will be clearer if, in place of the particle άιτιολογικκς which appears in the Evangelist, there be understood in the Prophet the adversative particle, but yet,Ps. 119. v. 143. Compare Louis Vives in his commentaries on book 18 of On the City of GOD chapter 30, where he labours lengthily over this reconciliation. Among other things he says: It can also have another sense, such that the Prophet indeed said Bethlehem was small, but that an immense greatness would arise thence, namely the eternal Leader of the Israelitic people, not carnal but of the Lord, so that power seems to be born out of weakness, and loftiness out of humility. But the greatness of so great a son no longer permits his native soil to be judged insignificant, insomuch that even the Prophet revered that amplitude which he conceived in his mind amid the smallness which he held before his eyes. γάρ,

Third apparent contradiction is this. In the Prophet: among the thousands of Judah. In Matthew: έν τόις ήγεμόσιν Ιούδα among the princes of Judah.

Ans. 1. Some reconcile this in this way, that instead of -- (which is the little word found in the prophetic text, and signifies thousand) he read -- (which is plural in construction, and signifies princes) written with the same letters, namely, but with different points. But since the points are contemporaneous with the consonants in the Biblical text, noted down beneath it by Moses himself and the Prophets, therefore this reconciliation is not to be approved.

2. More neatly, what some observe holds true, that the word --, which signifies thousand, is sometimes placed for --, which is Leader.

3. It is answered most simply, that regard is had to this, because the Israelitic people were distributed into thousands, Exod. 18. v. 25. Judg. 6. v. 15. 1. Sam. 10. v. 19. and each tribe of this people was distributed into families, which families were named אלופים in the government אלופי thousands or myriads, and the leaders of those thousands were called ἡγέμονες. Chiliarchs, (under whom were the thousands into which the people were distributed); they are called שרי אלפים captains of thousands. The sense is: You are too small to be counted as great among the thousands of your tribe Judah, so many in number and so distinguished; you bring forward few thousands of citizens, and those slight ones, or certainly none at all; you augment your tribe with few men, if you are compared with the other cities of the same tribe, out of which in very many there can be enrolled myriad upon myriad of men. Judg. 6. v. 15.

Ludovicus Vivès on this place: That thou shouldst be in the thousands of Judah. This pertains to the same emphasis of the question. But art thou least even, if it please the Gods, among the thousands of towns and villages of Judah? Thou art not, nor even among the mother-cities and cities which are princes and leaders to others.

The Syrian rendered it, among Kings. Euthymius thus παραφράζει.: Thou art not least in bringing forth rulers of Judah. Some therefore reconcile it thus, that the Prophet affirms something about the thousands of citizens while the Evangelist denies it about the rulers, so that the sense is: Although Bethlehem numbered but few citizens, yet it would bring forth a notable ruler besides the others; although it might be small in extent of place and population, yet it was by no means small in the birth of rulers, since out of it, besides Abesan, Judg. 12. v. 8. Boaz, and David, so great and such a ruler also would come forth.

Fourth apparent contradiction. In the Prophet a relative pronoun is added, from let him go forth for me, which in the Evangelist, as also in the Syrian *(likewise in the Arabic and Ethiopic)* paraphrase, is omitted. But nothing falls away from the sense on account of this, and it is well known that among the Hebrews such pronouns sometimes abound almost superfluously. In certain Greek Codices also it has been added in this very place ἐξελεύσεται μοι,, by which pronoun is signified that by the providence and special ordinance of GOD the Messiah would come forth from Bethlehem, and likewise for the glory of GOD and the salvation of the Israelitic people. Thus Luke 2. v. 30. the Messiah is called the Salvation of GOD.

*( ἐκ σοῦ γὰρ ἐξελεύσεται. The Ethiopian also wished to show the manner, namely how that Ruler ought to go forth from Bethlehem, rendering: Out of you he shall go forth and be born. It is indeed evident also from other sayings of Holy Scripture, such as Gen. 17, 6.ch. 35. v. 11., that to go forth sometimes means the same as to be born. This must be well observed against the objections of the Photinians at Mic. 5. v. 2..)*

ἠγούμενος. The participle is used for the noun ἡγεμὼν. The Syrian rendered King. *(so also the Ethiopian: But the Arab renders , that is, Leader, governor.)* The Chaldean refers it expressly in words to the Messiah.

Ποιμαίνειν signifies both to rule and to feed, because Kings ought to be ποιμένες λαῶν,, as Homer calls them; παραπλήσια ἔρλα εἶναι νομέως ἀλαθοῦ κα βασιλέως άλαθοῦ, says Xenophon. In turn shepherds provide for their flocks, and rule and lead them. Kings ought to rule in the manner of shepherds, not to domineeer tyrannically. *(The Syrian, Arab, and Ethiopian likewise used here such a word, which originally and properly has the meaning of feeding. Here however is intimated the spiritual kingdom of Christ, not worldly or temporal, which must be observed against the papists, who strive to defend the Monarchy of the Pope from John 21. v. 16., where this same word is read.)*

There is emphasis in the word Ισραὴλ. For the sense is: You, Bethlehem, are smaller than to be numbered among the populous and celebrated cities of Judah. But shortly I will make you great and illustrious, for I will cause him to come forth from you who shall rule not only over the tribe of Judah but over the whole people of Israel, just as David, sprung from you, ruled over all Israel. *(These words moreover must be understood not exclusively, but rather so that regard is had especially to the Spiritual Israelites. Compare Rom. 9. v. 7. 8.Gal. 6. v. 16.)*

Latin:

v. 6. Quaeritur hoc loco, quomodo allegatio Evangelisiae conveniaet cum dicto Prophetico Michae. 5. In commentariis Hieronymi citatur versio LXX. Interpretum, quae locum Propheticum planè ita reddidit, sicut Mattliaeus recitat. Ut enim monuimus superiùs proleg. 2. Evangelistae verba versionis Graecae, quae tunc usitata erat, plerumque retinent: in illa verò editione, quam nos habemus, aliter legitur. Syrus ita reddidit, sicut in Evangelista verba negativè citantur. Iacob. Faber Stapul. de conciliatione videtur desperasse, ideò in comm. h. l. exclamat. Utinam superesset Matthaeus Hebraeus, ut omnis caligo amoveretur? Hieronymus libr. 2. -omm. in Mich. duas assert responsiones. Testimonium hoc, inquit, nec Hebraico textui, nec LXX. Interpretum versioni convenire, me quoque tacente, perspicuum est, & arbiitror, Matthaeum volentem arguere Sacerdotum & scribarum erga divinae Scripturae libros negligentiam, sic etiam posuisse, ut ab eis dictum est. (Existimat ergo Hieronymus, μιμητικως haec ab Evangelista ex ore Scribarum recitari. Sed verisimilius est, ab Evangelistâ ex mente propria haec adferri, in quibus monstrare voluerit, unde scribae didicerint, Christum esse in Bethlehem nasciturum.) Pergit Hieronymus. Sunt autem, qui asserunt, in omnibus pene testimoniis, quae de V. T. sumuntur, huius modi esse errorem, ut aut ordo mutetur, aut verba, & interdum quoa sensus ipse diversus sit, vel Apostolis vel Evangelistis, non ex libro carpentibus testimonia, sed memoriae credentibus, quae nonnunquam fallitur.

(At haec responsio perquam dura & improbabilis, quomodo enim -μάά-τημα μνημονευτικ-ν tribui possit illis, qui ex inspiratione divinâ scripserunt? quomodo etiam diversum â Propheticis oraculis sectarentur sensum, qui uno & eodem cum Prophetis impulsi fuêre Spiritu?) Quaerenda igitur aptior conciliatio. Prima apparens contrarietas haec est. Apud Prophetam locus nativitatis vocatur Bethlehem Ephrata. Apud Matthaeum Bethlehem terra Iuda. Resp. diversitas descriptionis non ftatim introducit aliquam contrarietatem. Utraque descriptio additur ad discrimen alterius Bethlehemae, quae sita erat in tribu Zabulonis, haec autem in tribu Iuda, ut monuimus superiùs v. 1. Ephratae cognomen accepit Gen. 35. v. 19.cap. 48. v. 7.1. Sam. 17. v. 12. ab uxore Calebi. 1. paral. 2. v. 19. Ludov. Vives in lib. 18. Aug. d. C. D. cap. 30. Ephrata regio est, in qua Bethlehem civitas David in tribu Iuda, quod nomen utpote priscum, & minùs ad vulgum notum Sa-er dotes praetermiserunt, cùm Herodi alienigenae loquerentur, subiecto quod notius erat Iudae.

Altera apparens contrarietas haec est. Propheta vocat eam minimam, Evangelista negat, esse minimam. Resp. 1. Osiander lib. 1. Harm. cap. 10. contendit, locum Propheticum sic esse vertendum. Et heus -u, Bethlehema Ephrata, parum est, ut sis inter Chiliades seu Chiliarchos Iudae &c. Cùm enim Hebraei careant neutro, voce mas ulina vel foeminina pro eo utuntur. Iam verò idem est, sive dicas, Parum est, ut sis inter principes Iudae, sive dicas, non esse minimam inter principes Iudae. Neutrum genus adverbialiter hîc ponitur, & additur infinitivoτού έίναι,qui in Hebraeo & Graeco textu habetur, hoc sensu: Parum est, ut sis in millib. Iuda. Urget Osiander, quòd Prophetaαίτιολογικωςaddat, ex te mihi nascetur. Atqui nulla erit connexio, si transferatur: Tu Bethlehem es parvula, quia ex te mihi nascetur Messias. Item quod scribae & Pontifices Micheam sicc intellexerint.

2. Cum eo fermè congruit, quod quidam statuunt, verba Michae legenda esse interrogativè, ac interrogationem hoc loco habere vim negandi. Num minima es? hoc est, nequaquam minima es, sicut Evangelista reddidit: όυδαμως έλαχίςη, hoc est, μεγίςη έι. Sic Herodotus de Zamolxide. έλλήνων όυ τω άθενεςατω οςφιςή Πυθαγρη. *(Haec responsio Hugoni quoq; Grotio expeditissima videtur, ac notat insuper idem, -- interrogativum saepè omitti, uti Iob. 40. v. 20.1. Reg. 21. v. 7.Zach. 8. v. 6.)*

3. Plerique conciliationem quaerunt in diversa Bethlehemae consideratione. Propheta Bethlehemam vocat minimam ratione externi splendoris, qui fuit perquàm exiguus, & ratione opum terrenarum, simulque innuit, humilem istam conditionem Deum minimè impediturum, quò minùs amplissimo honore hoc oppidulum afficiat, producendo scilicet ex illo Christum: Evangelista cam nequaquam dicit esse parvam, respectu sc. singularis illius honoris, quem nativitas Messiae ei conciliaverat, & aestimatam ab haDEI dignatione. Tempore Prophetae erat parva, non autem tempore Evangelistae, cùm iam Christus in ea esset natus.

Conciliatio isthaec clarior erit, si loco άιτιολογικκς particulae γάρ, quae extat apud Evangelistam, subaudiatur apud Prophetam particula adversativa, sed tamen,Ps. 119. v. 143. Confer Ludov. Vivem in comm. lib. 18. de Civ. DEI cap. 30. ubi prolixè in hac conciliatione laborat. Inter caetera dicit. Potest & alter esse sensius, ut Propheta parvam quidem dixerit esse Bethelhem, sed ingentem magnitudinem inde nascituram, nempe aeternum Ducem Israëlitici populi, non carnalis, sed Dominici, ita ut ex infirmitate nasci videatur potentia, & ex humilitate sublimitas. Verùm tanti filii magnitudo non ampliùs sinit natale suum solum exiguum censeri, ut etiam Propheta amplitudinem illius, quam animo concipiebat, in exiguitate, quàm oculis habebat subiectam, veneraretur.

Tertia apparens contrarietas haec est. Apud Prophetam, est in millibus Iudae. Apud Matthaeum,έν τόις ήγεμόσιν Ιούδαinter duces Iuda.

Resp. 1. Quidam id conciliant hoc modo, quod pro -- (quae vocula habetur in textu Prophetico, & significat mille) legerit -- (quod est plurale in regimine positum, & significat duces) -isdem sc. literis scriptam vocem, sed diversis punctis. At cùm puncta fint consonantibus in textu Biblico coaeva, ab ipso Mos& Prophetis ei subnotata, ideò haec conciliatio non est approbanda.

2. Concinnius est, quod quidam observant, vocem -- quae mille significat, interdum poni pro -- quod est Dux.

3. Simplicissimè respondetur, respectum eò haberi, quod populus Israëliticus distributus fuerit in Chiliadas, Exod. 18. v. 25.Iud. 6. v. 15.1. Sam. 10. v. 19. ac singulae tribus huius populi distributae fuerint in familias, quae familiae nominatae fuerunt אלופים in regim. אלופיmillia seu chiliades, Duces istarum chiliadum dicti fuêre ἡγέμονες. Chiliarchae, (sub quibus erant chiliades, in quas populus distributus erat) vocantur שרי אלפיםprincipes mille. Sensus est. Minores, quàm ut pro magno numereris inter chiliades tribus tuae Iuda, tot numero, tamq; praestantes, paucas & eas tenues, vel certè nullas affers civium chiliades, paucis tribum tuam auges viris, si cum coeteris eiusdem tribus urbibus conferaris, ex quibus plerisq; multae hominum myriades conscribi possunt. Iud. 6. v. 15.

Lud. Viv. d. l. Ut sis in millibus Iuda. Hoc ad eandem interrogationis emphasin spectat. An verò minima es? Etiam, si Diis placet, in millibus oppidorum, pagoruma Iuda? non es, ne inter metropoles quidem & urbes, quae aliis principes & Duces sunt.

Syrus reddidit, in Regibus. Euthymius sic παραφράζει.Non minima es in producendis principibus Iada. Quidam ergo sic conciliant, quòd Propheta de civium millibus affirmat, illud Evangelistam de principibus negare, ut sit sensus: Bethlehem licet pauconumeraret cives, insignem tamen principem praeter alios producturam; licet parva esset loci amplitudine & frequentia, parvam haud esse principum natalibus, quippe ex qua praeter Abesan, Iud. 12. v. 8. Booz, David, etiam tantus ac talis proditurus sit princeps.

Quarta apparens contrarietas. Apud Prophetam additur relativum, ex tenascetur mihi, quod apud Evangelistam ut & in Syriaca *(Arabica item & Aethiopicâ)* paraphrasi praetermittitur. Sed ex eo nihil decedit sensui, ac notum est, apud Hebraeos eiusmodi pronomina quandoq; quasi abundare. In quibusdam Codd. Graecis etiam hoc loco additum habetur ἐξελεύσεται μοι, quo pronomine significatur, DEI providentiâ ac speciali ordinatione, uti etiam ad DEI gloriam & populi Israēlitici salutem Messiam ex Bethlehema proditurum. Sic Luc. 2. v. 30. Messias vocatur DEI Salutare.

*( ἐκ σοῦ γὰρ ἐξελεύσεται. Aethiops modum quoque, sive quomodo egredi Princeps ille debeat ex Bethlehem, ostendere voluit vertens, Ex te egredietur ac nascetur. Constat verò ex aliis quoque Scr. S. dictis, uti Gen. 17, 6.c. 35. v. 11. egredi interdum idem notare ac nasci. id quod contra Photin. except. ad Mich. 5. v. 2. probè observandum.)*

ἠγούμενος. Participium ponitur pro nomine ἡγεμὼν. Syrus reddidit Rex. *(sic etiam Aethiops: Sed Arabs reddit id est, Dux, gubernator.)* Chaldaeus apud Prophetam disertis verbis refert ad Messiam.

Ποιμαίνειν & regere & pascere significat, quia Reges debent esse ποιμένες λαῶν, ut eos vocat Homerus; παραπλήσια ἔρλα εἶναι νομέως ἀλαθοῦ κα βασιλέως άλαθοῦ, dicit Xenophon. Vicissim pastores gregib. suis provident, eosq; regunt ac deducunt. Debent Reges regere more pastorum, non Tyrannicè dominari. *(Syrus, Arabs, Aethiops similiter tali hic verbo usi sunt, quod originaliter ac propriè pascendi significationem habet. Innuitur verò hic regnum Christi spirituale, non mundanum vel temporale, id quod contra ontificios, ex Ioh. 21. v. 16. ubi itidem verbum hoc legitur, Monarchiam Papae defendere satagentes, observandum.)*

Emphasis est, in voce Ισραὴλ. Sensus enim est. Tu Bethlehem minores, quàm ut numereris inter frequentes ac celebres civitates Iudae. Sed propediem magnam & illustrem te reddam, faciam enim, ut ex te prodeat, qui non solùm tribui Iudae, sed toti populo Israelico dominetur, sicut & David ex te oriundus toti Israël dominatus fuit. *(Intelligenda autem haec verba non exclusivè, sed potiùs ut cumprimis ad Spirituales Israëlitas respectus habeatur. Confer Rom. 9. v. 7. 8.Gal. 6. v. 16.)*

## 2:7
v. 7. Herod secretly calls the Magi to himself; he did not wish the Jews to be privy to those things which he was about to inquire from the Magi, or answer to them themselves, lest they should penetrate his plan, which he had already conceived in his mind.

ἦκρίβώσε carefully and exactly investigated, with a certain singular ἀκριβείᾴ he sought out all the circumstances concerning the newly risen star of the Magi.

Author of the imperfect work on Matthew, homily 2, on Matt., page 777. You write that Herod believed, so that he might persecute Christ: And they themselves did not believe, so that they might receive him.

The Evangelist intimates that the Magi revealed to Herod, without any qualm, the time of the star's arising, and whatever else he asked; for they could not suspect, nor even ought they to have suspected, that he was asking these things with wicked design, and would attempt a deed so monstrous as to rage against a new-born infant, or to try to overthrow the counsel of GOD.

Latin:

v. 7. Herodes clam ad se vocat Magos, nolebat Iudaeos conscios esse eorum, quae ex Magis quaesiturus, vel ipsis responsurus erat, ne in consilium ipsius, quod animo iam tum conceperat, penetrarent.

ἦκρίβώσεaccuratè & exactè perquisivit, singulari quadam ἀκριβείᾴ omnes novae illius stellae Magis exortae circumstantias quaesivit.

Autor oper. imperf. homil. 2. in Matth. pag. 777. Scribis Herodes credidit, ut persequeretur Christum: Et ipsi sibi non crediderunt, ut susciperent eum.

Innuit Evangelista, Magos Herodi tempus ortae stellae, & quaecunq; interrogabat alia, sine scrupulo aperuisse, neq; enim suspicari poterant, vel etiam debebant, ipsum malo consilio isthaec quaerere, ac tam immanem futurum, ut in recens natum infantem saeviret, vel DEI consilium intervertere conaretur.

## 2:8
v. 8. πέμψας ἀντοἀς, From this word some gather that Herod attached certain attendants to the Magi along with these words, lest his bloodthirsty and deceitful mind lie open. *(Perhaps Hugo Grotius also intends this, observing on this passage πεήμπειν that the same thing obtains among the Greeks which is said more frequently προπέμπειν. For this too is strictly proper, to escort one who is departing some distance for honor's sake.)* But because the Magi, hedged about by Herod's attendants, could not conveniently escape Herod's snare, therefore πέμπειν it is more rightly taken for ἀπομέμπειν to send away, the simple form standing for the compound.

*(The Papists make use of—or rather misuse—this, as Lorinus on the Acts of the Apostles, page 294. a., and certain others besides, who take pains, among their other objections, to elude the force of the Orthodox argument against Peter's primacy drawn from Act. 8. v. 14., and in the present passage, seeing that from it it is granted that the sender is not always sent but is superior to him who is sent. Yet 1. it must be noted that our men do not argue against the contrived primacy of Peter from the said passage Act. 8. on the ground that Peter was lesser or inferior to the remaining Apostles, by whom he is there read to have been sent, but at least that from this passage it becomes plain that he was not superior to the rest, since no one superior is delegated by other inferiors. The words of my B. Par. on this matter in the Conf. Cath. lib. 2. Spec. part. 1. p. 545. a. are these: He allows (Peter) himself to be dispatched together with John, as an equal, to the Samaritans, Act. 8. v. 14. Therefore our men gather equality at least from the sending, not subjection—and that against the arrogance of the Roman Pontiff, which the panders of the Roman court strive to establish or to whitewash by means of the invented primacy of Peter—is enough for us. 2. It must be known that in Matth. 2. v. 8. the word is not ἀ ποςέλλειν, but πέμπειν,, which according to Grotius in this place is the same as προπέμπειν,, whereas according to others it is by no means what άποπέμπειν, is; and that this acceptance of the word πέμπειν is quite far from uncommon, both among the Orators and among the prince of poets, it is abundantly settled. I am fully aware that this distinction between The Eastern interpreters take little care concerning ἀποςέλλειν and πέμπειν, since the Syrian expresses either word by , the Arab by , the Ethiopian by indiscriminately; meanwhile nevertheless there can hardly be any doubt that at some time there was some distinction between those words in the Greek language. 3. If we look at the very context, certainly Herodes dismissed the Magi on a far different basis than the disciples did Peter and John. For Herodes was in no way the author of the Magi undertaking their journey, which they had already undertaken spontaneously and nearly completed; but Peter and John did whatever they did here by the counsel of the Apostle. 4. Moreover, the objection rests upon a false hypothesis regarding the Magi, namely that they were Kings. Whence 5. Some Papists, perceiving that they cannot slip away by this reasoning, say that this was done out of charity and humility in Peter, and that he could have refused such a sending if he wished. But if this argument of charity and humility holds in Peter, why does that lying successor of Peter, P. R., not also prove himself similar to Peter in those virtues? But concerning this matter, especially concerning the remaining objections of the Papists, more will be discussed at length in its place.) *

He calls him the young child whom the Magi had called King, because he could neither bear nor utter the name of the new King as most hateful to himself. Nor does he merely command that they seek the young child, but about the young child; for he wants all things that could relate to the matter to be diligently investigated by them: when the child was born, in what house, with what parents, what happened at his birth, whether he was held by the Bethlehemites as the Messiah-King. Περὶ τοῦ Παιδίου,

It came about by divine providence that Herodes hoped the Magi would return to him, and so did not immediately rage against the children of Bethlehem; by which means provision was made both for the Magi and for the child.

Latin:

v. 8. πέμψας ἀντοἀς, Quidam ex hac voce colligunt, quòd Herodes Magis hisce satellites quosdam adiunxerit, quo minus sangvinarius & subdolus ipsius animus pateret. *(Et hoc quoq; fortè intendit Hugo Grotius, annotans ad h. l. πεήμπειν apud Homerum idem esse, quòd frequentiùs dicitur προπέμπειν. Nam & hoc propriè est, abeuntem honoris causâ aliquousq; comitari.)*, Sed quia Magi Herodis satellitibus stipati non potuissent commodè Herodis insidias vitare, ideò, πέμπειν rectiùs accipitur pro ἀπομέμπεινdimittere, simplex pro composito.

*(Utuntur vel abutuntur potiùs Pontificii, uti Lorinus in Acta Apost. pag. 294. a. & alii nonnulli, inter reliquas exceptiones, quibus vim argumenti Orthodoxorum, quod contra Petri primatum, ex Act. 8. v. 14. depromunt, eludere satagunt, & praesenti loco, ut pote ex quo constet, mittentem non esse semper misso si-e eo, qui mittitur, superiorem. Verùm. 1. notandum, nostrates non argumentari contra fictum Petri primatum ex d. l. Act. 8. quòd Petrus minor sive inferior fuerit reliquis Apostolis, â quib. missus ibi legitur, sed saltem quòd ex h. l. elucescat, non fuisse illum reliquis superiorem, cùm nullus superior delegetur ab aliis inferioribus. Verba B. Par. mei de hac re in Conf. Cath. lib. 2. Spec. part. 1. p. 545. a. haec sunt: Patitur (Petrus) se ablegari unà cum Iohanne, tanquam aequali ad Samaritanos,Act. 8. v. 14. Ergò aequalitatem saltem colligunt nostrates ex missione, non subiectionem, idque contra arrogantiam Pontificis Romani, quam per confictum Petri primatum stabilire vel palliare aulae Romanae gnathones sa-agunt, nobis sufficit. 2. Sciendum est, quòd Matth. 2. v. 8. non sit verbum ἀ ποςέλλειν, sed πέμπειν, quod iuxta Grotium h. l. idem est, quod προπέμπειν, iuxta alios minimùm quod άποπέμπειν, & hanc verbi πέμπειν acceptionem tum apud Oratores, tum apud Poëtarum principem haut infrequentem esse, satis constat. Novi equidem, quòd distinctionem hanc inter ἀποςέλλειν & πέμπειν parùm curent Interpretes Orientales, cùm utrumq; verbum Syrus per Arabs per Aethiops per indifferenter exprimant: interea tamen, quin discrimen aliquod in Graecâ Linguâ inter verba illa sit aliquando, vix dubitandum. 3. si contextum ipsum adspiciamus, sanè longè aliâ ratione Herodes Magos, aliâ discipuli Petrum ac Iohannem dimiserunt. Herodes enim minimè Magis itineris, ut quod iamtum spontè susceperant, ac propè confecerant, suscipiendi autor fuit, Petrus verò ac Iohannes quicquid hic egerunt, è consilio Apostol. fecerunt. 4. Nititur insuper exceptio de Magis falsâ hypothesi, quòd fuerint Reges. Unde. 5. deprehendentes Pontificii alii, sese elabi istâ ratione non posse, dicunt charitatis fuisse & humilitatis id in Petro, ac potuisse, si vellet, eiusmodi missionem detrectare. Sed si charitatis ac humilitatis argumentum hoc in Petro, cur ementitus ille Petri successor P. R. non se quoque in istis virtutibus similem Petro probet? Sed de hâc re, cumprimis de reliquis Pontificiorum exceptionibus, suo loco agetur prolixiùs.)*

Περὶ τοῦ Παιδίου,Puerum vocat, quem Magi Regem appellaverant, quia nec nomen novi Regis maximè sibi odiosum ferre vel proferre poterat. Nec tantùm iubet, ut puerum quaerant, sed de puero, vult enim omnia, quae ad rem spectare poterant, accuratè ab ipsis inquiri, quando puer natus sit, in quibus aedibus, quibus parentibus, quae in nativitate acciderint, an â Bethlehemitis pro Messia Rege habeatur.

Divinâ providentiâ factum, ut Herodes speraret, Magos ad se reversuros, nec statim in Bethlehemiticos pueros saeviret, quâ ratione & Magis & puero fuit prospectum.

## 2:9
v. 9. ἐπορεύθησαν. Why then did the Jews not set out together with the Magi to Bethlehem? Answer: out of fear of Herodes, lest they offend him, whose displeasure they knew this announcement of the Magi had been. In that very year in which Christ was born, Herodes had been received as king by the votes of the Jews, and had begun to reign legitimately; therefore they feared to approach the new King.

Why did God wish the star to rise again over Jerusalem after the Magi had departed thence? Answer. 1. That he might heal the scandal which could arise from those things which had happened at Jerusalem, namely that the newborn King should not be offended by them in that metropolis of the whole kingdom, because they saw all disturbed by this news, and because neither Herod nor any of the Jews set out with them. 2. To indicate the place of his birth, lest, if they were compelled to seek the child in the little town of Bethlehem, the matter would be brought back to Herod. 3. Lest the Magi be offended by the humility of the child and his mother. Observation. After the Magi learned the place of Christ's birth from the prophetic oracle, the star rises again before them; thus from the light of the word there arises anew in our hearts the fresh light of faith. 2 Pet. 1. v. 19.

Latin:

v. 9. ἐπορεύθησαν.Quare Iudai non sunt cum Magis simul Betlehemam profecti? Resp. metu Herodis, ne eum offenderent, cui nuncium hoc Magorum parùm gratum fuisse noverant. Eo ipso anno, quo Christus natus, suffragiis Iudaeorum in Regem susceptus erat Herodes, ac legitimè regnare caeperat, veriti ergo sunt, novum adire Regem.

Quare voluit Deus Magis Hierosolymâ egressis S-ellam deunò exoriri? Resp. 1. ut mederetur scandalo, quod oriri poterat ex eis, quae Hierosolymis contigerant, videlicet quòd recens natum Regem in illa totius regni metropoli non offenderint, quòd omnes hoc nuncio turbatos viderint, quòd nec Herodes, nec quisquam Iudaeorum cum ipsis profectus fuerit. 2. ut indicaret nativitatis locum, ne si cogerentur in Bethlehema oppidulo puerum quaerere, res ad Herodem deferretur. 3. ne Magi offenderentur pueri & matris humilitate. Observ. postquam Magi ex oraculo Prophetico locum nativitatis Christi didicerant, stella ipsis denuò oritur, sic ex luce verbi oritur in cordibus nostris nova lux fidei. 2 Petr. 1. v. 19.

## 2:10
v. 10. The threefold emphasis magnifies the joy of the Magi. 1. ἐχάρησαν χάραν, in which some hold there to be Attic elegance, just as Ιλιασ. β. is said πολεμὸν πολεμίζειν. Ιλ. κ. βουλὶς βουλένειν.
