Hoc victu & vestitu Iohannes. 1. insinuare voluit, se venire in virtute & Spiritu Eliae. 2. autoritatem, in novo praeconio necessariam, sibi conciliare. Luc. 3. v. 15. Eò gravius ac maioris autoritatis erat ipsius testimonium, quò ipse non solùm ab omni crimine, sed etiam ab omni rerum terrenarum studio magis erat alienus. Nicephorus lib. 1. Hist. Eccl. cap. 18.Homo quidem ille primo aspectu visus, caeterum mente ipsa & animo divinus prorsus ata magnificentissimus, & ut qu-sp-am dicat Angelus corpore assumto. 3. poenitentiam, quam verbis docebat, victus & vestitus asperitate commendare. Iac. Faber. Stap. in h. l. Vestitus vilis & contemtus monstrabat mundi suiipsius contemtum & transactae vitae d-spl--entiam; asperitas, fugam deliciarum; p-llicea zona circa renes arctam continentiae custodiam, cibus facilis & neglectus gulae frenum; potus aquae omnimodam sobr-etatem.

Quomodo verò cum hac descriptione victus Iohannaei congruit, quod Christus inferius dicit cap. 11. v. 18. ipsum nec come disse nec bibisse. Resp. 1. quidam per ἄυξησιν hoc dictum censent, quod tam parco, vili, & â communi Iudaeorum cibo alieno dicatur usus, ut absque cibo inter Iudaeos vixisse dici possit. 2. ex oppositione verus sensus colligitur. Venit Iohannes nec manducans, sc. vulgares cibos, nec bibens, se. siceram & vinum Luc. 1. v. 15.Venit Filius hominis manducans & bibens, sc. vulgari modo, quin & cum peccatorib. convescens & conviviis interesse non dubitans. Inde Luc. 7. v. 33. additur determinatio. Venit Ioh. Baptista nea manducans panem, neque bibens vinum. Ubi tamen non est vis facienda in voce panis, ut volunt Staplet. Brugens. Baron. quasi ab eius usu Iohannes penitùs abstinuerit, sed significatur, â delicatis & consuetis cibis ipsum abstinuisse. Lyranus in Matth. 11.non comedens, nec bibens i. e. in abstinentia maxima vivens, ille enim, qui parùm comedit, dicitur non comedere secundùm communem modum loquendi, sicut quim alè videt, dicitur non videns. Dionys. Carth. in cap. 7 Lucae: Hoc l-o per panem & vinum consuet a ac delicata hominum fercula, pocul-significantur. Tolet. ib. Cibis ac potibus communibus se abstinens. Congruit hoc idiotismo Hebraeo, iuxta quem panis nomine omne genus edulorum venit.

Bellam. de Monach. cap. 39. Stapleton. antid. Evang. in cap. 3. Matth. Maldonat. ibid. Salmer ----. 4. tract. 4. Baronius ann. 31. n. 11. 12. 13 statuūt, Iohannem hoc suo vestitu & victu Monasticae vitae autorem fuisse. Resp. 1. Iohannes nuspiam legitur hanc vivendi formam discipulis suis praescripsisse. 2. Solus enim ipse fuit Elias ille, cuius adventus in V. T. erat promissus, solus ven-in Spiritu & virtute Eliae. De ipso solo ab Angelo praedictum quod -inum ac siceram non sit bibiturus,Luc. 1. v. 15. de ipso solo Christus memorat tanquam peculiare ac singulare, quod nepanem ede-it, nec vinum biber-t.Luc. 7. v. 33. Ergo κακοζηλία est, si qui ipsun hac in re imitari velint. 3. Tertio demum seculo vita Eremitica & Monastica à Paulo Thebano & Antonio fuit introducta. Ergo Iohannes Bapt. non est eius autor. Polyd Virgil. lib. 7. de-er. invent. cap. 1. Alii An-onio, alii cuidam Paulo Thebaeo in--un huius rei assignant. Sed Antonio huius rei initium iure optimo r-ferri de-et, qui etsi non ante omnes primus fuit, primus tamen Monac-orum -ogma instituit. 4. ibid. addit Polydorus: Quidam altus repaentes Eliam & Iohannem Baptistam eius rei autores faciunt. Sedut is plusquam propheta, ita ille plus quam Monachus censeri debet. 5. Inter varios Monachorum ordines nullus datur, cui cibus nullus praeter locustas & melsylvestre; vestitus nullus, nisi de pilis camelorum. Quomod. ergo Iohannes Monasticae vitae poterit esse autor? 6. Maldonatus in cap. 3. Matth. disputat, Iohannē ideo vestitu singulari & monstroso usum ac in deserto prorsus solitario habitasse, quia de ipso scriptum sit: Vox clamantis in deserto, quia legem in deserto olim promulgatam, in deserto mori oportuerit, quia Messiam videri oportuerit. At hae causae sunt Iohanni propriae & peculiares. Ergo Monachi ex κακοζηλία eius exemplum imitantur. 7. In Regulis Societ. Iesuit. mundities & nitor vestium ac victus praescribitur. Vide Reg. Societ. summ. S. 46. 47. 48. Reg. comm. §. 19. Reg. praepositi Domus Professae. c. 6. Pr-curatoris Generalis, Procuratoris Domus Professae, Procuratoris C-legii per tot. Reg. dispensatoris §. 5. Reg. Praefecti, Refectorii §. 1. 2. Re-. Coq. atque in universum is cultus corporalis ordo statuitur, ut vix esse magis opiparus queat. Quamobrem & Loyola Ord. Institutor Inter Regulas Societatis & hanc esse voluit. Ab aliis religiosis Ordinifaciliùs patiamur nos superari ieiuniis, vigiliis & caeterâ victus cultusa asperitate. Verâ ac perfectâ obaedientiâ, abdicatione voluntatis atque iudicii maximè velim fratres carissimi, esse conspicuos, quicunque in hac societate Deo Domino nostro deserviunt, & tanquam germanam societatis sobolem hac quasi notâ distingui. In Epist. ad socios de virtute obaed. §. 3. (Aut ergo Ioh. Baptista non fuit Monachuaut Iesuitae Monachi non erunt.)

## 3:5
v. 5. Τότς εξεπορέυετο πρὸς αυτὸν. Already ever since the building of the second temple they had lacked prophets, and therefore they were held by a longing to see a prophet, Matth. 11. v. 8. nay, they themselves rendered honor to the Messiah, because he was introducing a new Ceremony of Baptism, and there was added his most holy life, together with the memory of those things which had occurred at his birth.

N-n is said all Jerusalem, because the Chief Priests, Scribes, Pharisees, and most of the Elders rejected the counsel of GOD against themselves, not being baptized by John, Matth. 21. v. 25. Luc. 7. v. 30. yet some of them likewise came to the Baptism of John h. c. v. 7. unless, one wishes to think that they came rather from other cities of Judea *( Among other arguments, by which the Papists strive to prove, See Corn. à Lapide on this place, and likewise on c.

Cornelius à Lapide on this passage, and likewise on chapter 19 of Acts, labors to maintain that the Baptism of John was not a Sacrament of the N.T., divinely instituted and effectual for the remission of sins: Bellarmine also discusses this passage. “They were therefore,” he says, “very few at that time who had not been baptized by John” (as indeed appears from the present passage vv. 5 and 6.), “But on the very day of Pentecost three thousand were baptized, and a little later five [thousand], besides those whom Philip and other disciples baptized in various places of Judaea and Samaria.”Acts 2, 41.ch. 4, 4.Ergo it is necessary that many who were baptized by John were again baptized by the Apostles. Ergo either the Baptism of John was not an efficacious Sacrament for the remission of sins; or in vain did those who had been baptized by John receive Baptism again from the Apostles. Answer: The Papist interpreters themselves acknowledge a synecdoche in the words of the Evangelists, as B. proves in Par. Conf. Cath. l. 2. Sp. part. 2. p. 931 by the testimonies of Denys the Carthusian, Cajetan, Cornelius Jansen, Salmeron and Emmanuel Sa (to whom also Corn. à Lapide on ch. 10, 22. Matt. p. 231 can be added). 2. The consequence is denied. Certain ones baptized by John received Baptism from the Apostles. Ergo it was necessary for all who were baptized by John to receive Baptism from the Apostles. 3. It is not precisely the question whether some after the Baptism of John received Baptism again, for perhaps that might be granted, but whether it was necessary, such that without it they could not become partakers of regeneration and salvation. 4. It must be known that this question about the Baptism of John by no means touches an article of faith necessary for all to know for salvation. And therefore those are not straightway to be smitten with anathema who, upon comparison of the sentences of Holy Scripture, dispute somewhat differently than certain of the ancients about this question, provided this be done with the truth of the doctrine concerning repentance, faith and godliness preserved. Confirm, if you please, more things in B. P. d. l. it. t. IV. -. de Bapt. §. 47. seqq., above all §. 60. B. D. Hutt. LL. Theol. p. 645 646. Moreover, among the Papists Benedict Aretius takes the side of the Calvinians on ch. 1 of John, from whom Wendelin rightly departs, writing expressly: “That which was called” the Baptism of John, “was not because ohn instituted it by his own authority, but because he was the first who administered this ceremony by the command of GOD, in the appearance, of Christ,”John 1, 33. whence the Baptism of John from heaven is said to have been,Matt. 11, 30.nor was the Baptism afterward administered by the Apostles of greater efficacy than the Baptism of John: even if the Papists affirm the contrary maintain the Papists. These things Wendelin, Syst. Theol. L. 1. c. 22. p. 843, where he also answers the arguments of the Papists nearly in the same way as our countrymen, though briefly. To the Anabaptists truly, who likewise infer from this, that the Bapt of John does not possess the same efficacy as the Baptism of Christ, hence conclude “that those who were baptized in infancy” (seeing that at any rate this was done with the Baptism of John) “must be baptized again at adult age,” there ought to be opposed chiefly this, that if the Baptism of John is not the same as ours, then neither did Christ and His Apostles receive true Baptism, inasmuch as they were baptized by John, nor were they re-baptized. But neither can be asserted. Ergo not the latter, since nowhere does Scripture betray this; nor the former, for it would follow that our Baptism was not consecrated in the person of Christ, and likewise that He Himself and the disciples were of a worse condition than we. Indeed Bellarmine comes to the aid of the Anabaptists, asserting “it would have been an insult to Christ if He had received the same Baptism as ourselves.” But if it was not an insult to Him to receive the same circumcision as the boys of Israel, yea rather the same human nature as ourselves (yet without sin), neither was it an insult to Him to take up the same Baptism as ourselves.)*

Pliny describes the river Jordan in Book 5 of his Natural History, chapter 15. The regions neighboring the Jordan are Galilee, Peraea, Batanaea, Trachonitis. *(Here let Buxtorf's Lexicon Chaldaico-Talmudico-Rabbinicum under the word p. 981 be compared.)*

Iam inde ab extructo secundô templo prophetis caruerant, ideò tenebantur desiderio videndi prophetam, Matth. 11. v. 8. imò honorem Messiae ipsi deferebant, quianovam Ceremoniam Baptismi introducebat, accedebat vitae sancti-s, & recordatio eorum, quae in ipsius nativitate acciderant.

N-n dicitur omnis Hierosolyma, quia Principes Sacerdotum, S-ribae, Pharisaei & Seniores plerique spernebant consilium DEI adversus serpsos, non baptizati à Iohanne, Matth. 21. v. 25.Luc. 7. v. 30. quidam tamen eorum itidem ad Ioh. Baptismum venerunt h. c. v. 7. nisi, quvelit cogitare, illos ex aliis potiùs Iudaeae urbib. venisse *( Adducinter alia argumenta, quibus evincere Pontificii, Vid.

Corn. à Lapide in h. l. itemque ad c. 19. Act. satagunt, Baptismum Iohannis non fuisse Sacramentum N. T. divinitus institutum ad remissionem peccatorum efficax: Bell. & hunc locum. Rari itaque, inquit, admodùm erant, eo tempore non baptizati à Iohanne, (ceu ex praesenti sc. loco v. 5. & 6. constat.) At ipso die Pentecostes baptizata sunt tria millia, & paullò post quin-, praeter eos, quos Philippus baptizavit & alii discipuli in variis Iudae & Samariae locis,Act. 2, 41.c. 4, 4.E. necesse est, multos à Iohanne baptizatos, iterum ab Apostolis baptizatos fuisse. E. vel baptismus Iohannis non fuit efficax ad peccatorum remissionem Sacramentum; aut frustra illi, qui à Ioh. fuerunt baptizati, iterum ab Apostolis Baptismum susceperunt. Resp. In verbis Evangelistarum ipsimet Pontificii Interpretes Synecdochen agnoscunt, quemadmodum testimoniis Dionysii Carthusiani, Caietani, Cornelii Iansenii, Salmeronis & Emanuelis Sa (quibus etiam addi potest Corn. à Lapid. in c. 10, 22. Matth. p. 231.) probat B. Par. Conf. Cath. l. 2. Sp. part. 2. p. 931. 2. Negatur conseq. Quidam â Iohanne baptizati susceperunt Baptismum ab Apostolis. E. omnibus à Iohanne baptizatis necessarium fuit, Baptismum ab Apostolis suscipere. 3 Non est quaestio praecisè de eo, an quidam post Ioh. Baptismum iterum Baptismum susceperint, id enim fortè concedi potest, sed an id fuerit necessarium, ita ut sine illo regenerationis & salutis non potuerint fieri participes. 4. Sciendum est, quòd quaestio haec de Baptismo Iohannis nequaquam concernat fidei articulum, omnibus ad salutem scitu necessarium. Ideoque non sunt statim anathemate feriendi, qui de hâc quaestione collatis Scr. S. sententiis paullò aliter, quàm veteres quidam, disputant, si id fiat salvâ veritate doctrinae de poenitentiâ, fide & pietate. Conf. si placet, plura apud B. P. d. l. it. t. IV. -. de Bapt. §. 47. seqq. cumprimis §. 60. B. D. Hutt. LL. Theol. p. 645 646. Caeterùm Pontificiis adstipulature Calvinianis Bened. Aretius in c. 1. Ioh. â quo rectè discedit Wendelinus, expressè scribens: Fuit dictus Baptismus Iohannis, non quòd -ohannes autoritate suâ eum instituerit, sed quod primus fuerit, qui DEI, inspecie, Christi iussu ceremoniam hanc administravit,Ioh. 1, 33.V-de Baptisus Iohannis è coelo fuisse dicitur,Matth. 11, 30.Nec maioris effica-iae Baptismus postmodum ab Apostolis administratus, quàm Iohannis Baptismus: etiamsi contrarium atuunt Pontificii. Haec Wendelinus Syst. Theol. L. 1. c. 22. p. 843. ubi etiam ad argumenta Pontificiorum eodem ferè, quo nostrates, modo breviter respondet. Anabaptistis verò qui itidem ex eo, quòd Bapt. Iohannis non habeat eandem efficaciam cum Baptism. Christi, colligunt, eos, qui in infantiâ baptizati sunt, (utpote cùm Iohannis saltem Baptismate id factum sit) adultâ aetate iterum baptizari debere, opponendum cumprimis, quod si Iohannis Baptismus non idem est cum nostro, nec Christum, eiusque Apostolos verum accepisse Baptismum, quippe à Iohanne baptizatos, aut fuisse rebaptizatos. At neutrum potest adseri. E. Non posterius, cùm nullibi Scr. hoc prodat; nec priùs, sequeretur enim, Baptismum nostrum non fuisse in Christi personâ consecratum, item eundem ac discipulos deterioris, quàm nos fuisse conditionis. Succurrit quidem Anabaptistis Bellarminus, adserens, Contumeliosum fuisse Christo, si eundem nobiscum Baptismum accepisset. At si non fuit ipsi contumeliosum, eandem cum puerulis Israel. circumcisionem accipere, imò eandem nobiscum humanam naturam (sed sine peccato,) nec contumeliosum eidem fuit, eundem nobiscum Baptismum suscipere.)*

## 3:6
v. 6. έξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτία ςἀυτῶν. The ἀξομολόγησις of sins differ, and their έξαγόρευσις. Lev. 16. v. 21. the Supreme Pontiff is commanded to confess the sins of the whole people; that it was a general and public confession is evident from the circumstances.

*(Bellarmine, De Poenitentia, Book 3, ch. 2, labors by means of this place to establish the particular confession of sins. Those who came to John's, he says, Baptism confessed their sins specifically,Matt. 3.Mark 1. Answer: 1. Cornelius à Lapide on this place denies that the Confession made to John the Baptist was a Sacrament, and that it remitted sins, as happens in the confession instituted by Christ. But the consequence from that confession to this one is not valid, since this indeed according to the mind of the Papists is a Sacrament and remits sins, while that one is not; moreover the Papists almost commonly teach that finally John 20. that is, after Christ's resurrection the Sacrament of penance was instituted, and a specific enumeration of sins required. 2. Nowhere is it said that they enumerated each sin individually. 3. Most Papists hold that in Confession before Baptism a specific enumeration of sins is not necessary. And yet John's hearers had confessed before receiving Baptism; which also the Syrian Interpreter seems to intimate at this place, when he translates: And they were baptized by him in the river of Jordan after they had confessed or should have confessed their sins. 4. The Evangelists relate that all Jerusalem and all Judaea and the whole region around the Jordan went out to John. If all who came to John the Baptist had confessed each and every sin, throughout his time of ministry John could do nothing but hear the individual confessions of everyone. 5. It is not disputed whether particular and auricular confession before the Minister of the Church is lawful, useful, and salutary; rather what is censured among the Papists is this: 1. That in auricular confession they require a narration of all and singular mortal sins—however many come to mind after careful premeditation and a strict examination of conscience—from all who have reached years of discretion, at a fixed time yearly, into the ears of the Priest. 2. That they decree that not only mortal sins but also circumstances which change the species of the sin or aggravate it must be recounted in confession. 3. That they establish by divine law that such particular enumeration of sins is necessary. 4. That they hold the same to be meritorious, whereby they think sin is blotted out &c. See more in B. P., Conf. Cath. book 2, special part 3, p. 38 sqq.; likewise vol. 3 LL. Th. on penance §. 102 sqq.; Dn D. Hulf. in the Manual of A.C., pp. 321, 331, 534 sqq.; and other theologians of our side.) *

Franc. Luc. Brug. in h. l. [Francis Lucas of Bruges on this passage.] The Baptism of John did not provide the remission of sins, but through repentance, which it testified to, it prepared the minds of the Jews so that they might be capable of that benefit. Contrà [On the contrary] Luc. 3. v. 3. John was in the desert baptizing and preaching the Baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, which formula of speaking is used concerning the Baptism of the Apostles Act. 2. v. 38. cap. 22. v. 16. And the Baptist himself testifies that the Pharisees could have escaped the wrath to come, if they had received the Baptism administered by him in true repentance and faith, h. c. v. 7. [in this chapter, verse 7.] Luc. 3. v. 7. which because they spurned, they are therefore said to have spurned the counsel of GOD, certainly concerning their own salvation, Luc. 7. v. 30.
