Ideoq; non obstante, quòd aliquando quis maiorem dulcedinem sentiat in aliâ oratione: tamen ista est dignior ratione dicta & plus reverenda. Si n. gemmam vel pretiosum lapidem talem, qui stetisset in ore Christi vel in medio cordis eius, aliquis posset tibi dare nonne maxima reverentia illum teneres: sic est in proposito de Dominica oratione, quae versata est in ore Christi, nec dubium, quin Pater coelestis eam sibi porrectam citiùs exaudiat. quia videmus inter homines, quod Pater carnalis magis exaudit rogamina facta filii dilecti in epistolis, suis manibus scripta. ldem Pelbartus d. l. ex Isidoro de sum, bon. l. 1. c. 22. scribit, quòd tanta sit efficacia Dominicae orationis, quod fidei symbolum, & quòd Dominica Oratio pro totâ lege parvulae Ecclesiae ad coelorum regna sufficiat capessenda.)*

Vide omninò Cyprianum serm. 6. in orat. Dominicae explicatione. *(Pulcrè hic d. l. inter alia: Agnoscat Pater Filii sui verba, cùm precem facimus, qui habit at intus in pectore, ipse sit & in voce. Et cum ipsum apud Patrem habeamus advocatum pro pecatis nostris, quando peccatores pro delictis nostris petimus, advocati nostri verba promamus. Nam cùm dicat, quia quodcun3 petieritis à Patre in nomine meo, dabit vobis, quanto efficaciùs impetramus, quod petimus in Christi nomine, si petamus ipsius oratione.)*

Considerare autem in hac Dominicae orationis formula debemus. 1. artificiosam brevitatem. 2. mirandam rerum ubertatem. Quicquid rectè & convenienter orari potest, illud omne complectitur. 3. elegantem ordinis concinnitatem. Petimus hac oratione. 1. vitae nostrae finem, tum principalem, qui est gloria DEI, petit. 1. tum subordinatam, qui est nostra salus, petit. 2. 2. quae ducunt ad utrúq; illum finem, videl. primò acquisitionem mediorum, tum principalis, quod est pietas, petit. 3. tum secundarii, quod est sustentatio vitae petit. 4. Secundò remotionem impedimentorum, videl. peccatorum, tum praeteritorum, petit. 5. tum futurorum, petit. 6. Tertiò, liberationem ex omnibus adversis, petit. 7. Confer Thomam 2. 2. q. 183. art 9.

Quatuor primis petitionibus precamur bona, trib. reliquis deprècamur mala. Tribus primis petitionibus petimus: aterna, quatuor reliquis temporaria. Tres primae petitiones in DEI gloriam directè respiciunt, caeterae quatuor ad nostras in hac vitâ necessitates compositae sunt.

Cornelius Iansenius sic progreditur. Petimus primò bonorum largitionem. Secundò malorum remotionem. In bonis 1. bonum DEI, pet. 1. 2. bonum nostrum summum, pet. 2. 3. bonum nostrum medium, gratiam sc. implendi mandata, pet. 3. 4. bonum nostrum infimum, petit. 4. In malis. 1. remotionem mali praeteriti, pet. 5. 2. mali futuri, pet. 6. 3, mali praesentis, pet. 7. *(Pelbartus ex Richardo aliisque ita progreditur. Cùm quilibet homo debeat petere 1. consequi bona. 2. removeri mala, & verò: summum bonum sit ipse Deus, quem debemus summè diligere ac colere, inde poni primam petitionem. Secundum bonum est regnum DEI possidere, quod petitur in 2. petitione. Tertium bonum est via, quâ perveniamus ad regnum Dei, sc. conformatio ad voluntatem DEI, de quâ in 3. petitione. Quartum bonum est auxilium, quo possumus nos iuvari ad perveniendum, & hoc est victus, necessarius, corpori quidem ad vitam quotidianam, animae verò ad vitam perpetuam, de quo in 4. petitione. Denique petimus removeri mala, inter quae pessimum est malum culpae, & de hoc in 5. petitione. Secundum malum est tentationis casus, quae inlcinat ad culpam, de quo in 6 petitione. Tertium malum est poenae praesertim perpetuae, de quo in 7. petitione. *)

Sex postulata dividimus in duos ordines, ut tria priora ad Deum directè sive immediaetè pertineant; tria reliqua adnos; sed haec partim in rebus corporeis, at3 his assignari petitionem quartam, partim in religiosis, quae comprehenduntur reliquis duobus. Chamierus tom. 4 lib. 9. cap. 11. §. 26. Sed haec procedunt ex illâ hypothesi, quae Calv. lib. 3. Instit. cap. 20. §. 35. I. Piscatoris in Expos. Orat, Domin, Ursini in Explic. Catech, pag. 887. *(Danaei expl, Orat. Domin p. 101. &. 103. Grynaei in h. l. Matthaei, Polani Synt, pag. 614. Wendelini Christianae Theol. System, mai, 1. 2. c. 5. p. 1602. aliorumque Calvinianorum est. Quos etiam Photiniani hîc sequuntur. Vid. Catech Racov. p. 169. quemadmodum & Armlniani, cen patet ex Confess. c. 14.)* quòd verba illa, & nenos inducas in tentationem, sed liberanos à malo, unam tantùm petitionem contineant. Sed rectiùs dicuntur duas destinctas petitiones continere, cùm aliud beneficium sit conservatio in tentationibus, aliud liberatia ab omni malo. Aug. Enchir. Cap. 115. septem numerat petitiones. lib. 2. de serm. Domini in monte. cap. 16. Ultima & septima petitio est, sed liberanos à malo.

Non est verisimile, Dominum, qui paulò antè dixerat: Orantes non sitis multiloqui, talem orandi formam praescribere, in quâ res una & eadem diversis verbis i. e. sententiis significetur. Praeterea si idem prorsus sint: Ne nos inducas in tentationem, & liber a nos à malo, non petemus liberari à malo praeterito, sed solùm à futuro; nec à malo paenae, sed à malo culpae. Tentatio enim, in quani petimus non induci, non est malum praeteritum, sed futurum; nec malum poenae sed culpae.

*(Conferatur idem August. in Epist. ad Probam. Sequuntur verò Augustini divisionem. Thomas de Aquino p. 2. q. 83. a. 9 Nicol. de Lyra, Gloss. Ordin. in h. l. alii.)*

Vestigia huius precandi formulae extant in libro Musar. 49. 1. Deus noster, qui in coelo unicus es, stabiliatur nomen tuum semper; regnum tuum regnet super nos in seculum & in aeternum; sanctificetur autem nomen tuum per opera nostra. *(Paulò aliter referunt Dn. Dilherrus in Eclog. Syr. p 46. ac Ludov. Capell. in Spic. p. 16.)* Ibid. 9. 12. Ne inducas nos in manus peccati, sed libera nos ab occursu malo.

*(Et haec petitio paullo aliter formata legitur apud Capellum d. 1. Est quoq; penes me liber ritualis Iudaicus satis vetustus, quippe ex Bioliothecâ Ioh. Schröteri, M. D & Com. Pal. Caes. ac primi in Acad. hâc Sal. Rectorisad me translatus, inscriptus הבית יוטם צורת בעל, in quo inter alias & precatio legitur, quae incipit: &c. יהי רצון מלפניך ײ אלהי אלהי אבותי i. e. Fiat voluntas coram te Domine, D Eus meus, Deus Patrum meorum &c.)*

Πάτερ ἡμῶν, ὁ ἐν Τοῖς Ούρανοῖς. In hoc prooemio praedicamus DEI benignitatem, in verbis, Pater noster; & eiusdem immensam potestatem, in verbis, quies in coelis. Haeccsunt duo fiduciae nostrae fulcra, quibus de exauditione confirmari possumus. Aug. lib. 2. de serm. Domini in monte, c. 1. Cyprian, serm de orat. Dom. Hoc nominis (Patris) nemo nostrum in oratione auderet attingere, nisi dignationis eius & bonitatis ubertas id permisisset. Bernh serm. de Natali B. Mariae: Admonent nos baec verba adoptionis divinae, dum, dicimus, Pater noster: & peregrinationis terrenae, dum addimus, qui es in coelis at fimal intelligamus, nos egere auxilio, quia peregrini sumus, & conceptamus, quia filii DEI sumus. Excitant illa verba in nobis DEI timorem & amorem: insinuant rationem, cur Deus debeat & possit nos audire. *( Et pietatis & potestatis appellatio ista est: Tert. lib, de orat.)*

Damasc. lib. 1. orth. fid. cap. 15. Κυριώτερον ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν -ςὶν πατὴρ, ὁἐκ μὴ ὄνΤων εἶναι Παραγαγὼν ἢ ὁι γεννὴσαντες ὁιἰξ αὐτοὑ καὶ Τὸ εἶναι καὶ Τὸ γενναῦ εἰληΦότες.

Pater noster est. 1. respectu creationis & formationis in utero. 2. respectu spiritualis regenerationis & adoptionis. 3. respectu paternae dilectionis. 4. respectu conservationis & nutritionis. 5. respectu defensionis. 6. respectu introductionis in hereditatem coelestem. *(Pelbartus l. cit. Quomodo Deus Pater hominum? Resp. 1. creatione. 2. imaginis impressione, & sic est Pater omnium hominum. 3. adoptione, & sic est Pater Christianorum. 4. Coelesti haereditatione, quam promisit electis, Rom. 8.)*

Quaecunque beneficia pater terrenus praestat liberis suis, eadem, imò plura & maiora Pater coelestis nobis confert, quia ipsius erga nos caritas infinitis modis excedit caritatem, quam terreni parentes erga liberos gerunt. Eph. 3. v. 15.

*(Augustinus: Patris nomine charitas excitatur ( quid enim charius filiis quàm pater?) & supplex affectus, & quaedam impetrandi praesumtio: quid enim non det filiis, qui dedit, ut filii essent. Ingens verò discrimen est, quando Christus patrem suum coelestem vocat Patrem suum, & quando nos Deum vocamus Patrem nostrum. Epiph. haeres. 69. p. 253. Dixit, scribit, Deum meum & Deum vestrum, & Patrem meum & Patrem vestrum: ( Ioh. 20, 17.) Patrem quidem meum secundùm naturam in Deitate: & Patrem vestram per gratiam, per me in adoptione: Deum autem meum, quoniam carnem vestram, adsumsi; & Deum vestrum, secundùm naturam & veritatem. Quae contra Photin. notanda.)*

Exhortetur autem nos haec appellatio ad reciprocum amorem erga Deum, & silialem obedientiam ipsi praetandam. Cyprianus d. l. Meminisse & scire debemus, quiae quando Patrem Deum dicimus, qs. filii DEI agere debemus, ut quomodo nobis placemus de D E O Patre, sic sibi placeat & ille de nobis filiis.

Quaeritur hîc 1. an nomen Patris hîc accipiaturοὐσιωδῶς, an v. ὑΠο ςμΤικῶςde prima persona Trinitatis? Resp. οὐσιωδῶς accipi, ostendit cultus invocationis qui omnibus & singulis Trinitatis personis debetur. ( α)* (Atq; hoc modo, nempe οὐσιωδῶς, sumendū hoc loco esse vocem Patris, monent ipsi Iesuitae Maldonatus, Barradius ac Corn. à Lapide. id quod notandum contra eos Pontificios, qui ad argumentum nostratium, quod ex hoc loco invocationi sanctorum opponunt, cum solus Deus nominetur, qui invocandus à nobis sit, excipiunt, Orationem Dominicam adsolum Patrem referri, & tamen licere invocare Filium & Spiritum Sanctum. Aliter igitur excipit Iesuita Conzen, & istam, & Bellarmini quoque responsionem deserens: ita enim in h. l. Centuriatorum Magdaeb. argumentum est Cent. 1. l. 1. c. 4. Christus cùm modum orandi suos docet, DEum invocare docet, non sanctos, non ergo invocandi. subiungit Conzen. Respondit olim Bellarminus; Christum h. l. ostendere, quae sint petenda: non agere de illis, à quibus petendae sint. Et verò in materia orationis omninò versatur. Potest alia quog 3 dari, & quidem perspicuae solutio. Interrogatum esse Dominum de modo orandi Deum, de, cultu religioso, de materia orationis, non autem de eo, qui sanctis defertur. A sanctis enim nihil nisi intercessio petitur. Eadem precum est utrob: g 3 materia. Neg 3 enim ad haec verba omnind adstringere nos Deus voluit. Alia enim orationes Christianorum ex auditae sunt, aliis concepta verbis, utAct. 4, 24.c. 7.vers. penult.c. 8, 15. 16. 17.Voluit tantùm ostendere, quas res petere oporteret. Nulla erga creatura invocanda est oratione religiosa, sed alià rogari potest, sive vivat in hoc seculo, sive cum DEO in coelis coniuncta, per eum nostras necessitates agnoscat. Resp. 1. Concedimus, per istam Christi orationem non iniungi Christianis, ne aliis omninò verbis, quàm quibus oratio Dominica constat, ea à vero Deo petant, quibus ipsi opus habent, tum quoque nomen DEI celebrent ac pro acceptis beneficiis gratias eidem persolvant. 2. Sed ex eo non sequitur, quòd sicut aliis verbis ea, quae à vero ac summo Deo petimus, proponere possumus, ita quoq; ad alium, praeterquam ad verum h. e. omnipotentem ac omniscium DEUM, dirigere nostras preces possimus, ab illoque tanquam à salutis largitore auxilium sperare. Illud indifferens esse, patet ex Sc. S. quemadmodum etiam dicta à Conzenio adducta hoc ipsum probare minimè diffitemur: sed hoc indifferens esse, h e. ut aequè liberum, mihi sit, an ad Deum verum, creatorem coeli ac terrae preces religiosas dirigere velim, an verò ad meram creaturam, simpliciter negatur.

neque ex Sacris litteris probari unquam poterit. Certè si ae què hoc ex Sc. S. ut illud probari posset, Gonzen vel unicum saltem locum adduxisset, quemadmodum alterum illud, de quo tamen non controvertitur, tribus Scr. S. dictis probavit. 3. Illud quod de vivorum compellatione affert Iesuita, parum ad rem facit: notum quidem est, consequentiam hanc, quâ ex vivorum compellatione religiosam defunctorum invocationem Pontificii communiter colligunt, (Vid. Cotonum Instit. Cath. p. 92. Coturium Epit. Controv. p. 459. Costerū Enchir. controv. p. 659. Becanum Man. Controv. l. 1. c. 7. §. 7.) Achillem Catholicum ab Eccio in Enchir. p. 149. salutari, nec latet nos gloriatio Bell. l. 1. de beat. Sanct. c. 19. quòd nunquam futurum, ut argumentum hoc solvi à nobis possit. Sed vanas has persuasiones esse, quibus Pontificii sibi blandiuntur, satis ostendunt plurima nostratium scripta, quibus infirmitas dictae consequntiae ad oculum monstrata, & Achilles ille funditus prostratus est. Ut enim alia iam praeteream. quanta quaeso est, diffetrentia inter compellationem vivorum, ac invocationem defunctorum. illis calamitates meas possum exponere, certusque adeò sum, quòd eas tum sciant; de his verò defunctis semper dubitare cogor, an vota precesque meas audiant, vel num unquam in illorum perveniat notitiam, quid ab illis sperem oremque. Unde etiam ipsi Pontificii discrepantes admodùm sententias fovent, unde & quomodo sancti defuncti calamitates viventium, sicuti & preces ad illos fusas resciscant. an nempe ex relatione Angelorum, an per defunctos qui hinc in coelum migrant, an ex DEI revelatione, an denique dum ipsi mirâ quadam naturae celeritate ubique sint. (Sicuti modos hos recenset ac refellit B. Par. L. de Morte §. 321. seqq.) Deinde cumprimis notandum, quòd ingens discrimen sit inter compellationis modum, cùm honor ille, qui viventibus exhibetur, dum hi calamitatis nostrae conscii rogantur, ut suas nostris iungere preces velint, merè humanus sit; qui verò sanctis defunctis in corum invocatione exhibetur, plusquam humanus, invocatio quippe ac adoratio religiosa â Pontificiis (Vid. Bell. l. 1. de beat. sanct. c. 14. Suarez t. 2. Com. in Thom. q. 27. D. 22. s. 1.) definiatur. Unde etiam compellatío viventium pertinet ad secundam Decalogi tabulam & est opus charitatis, eiusque in divinis & praecepta & exempla probata extant (Vid. 1. Tim. 2, 1.Iac. 5, I6.1. Sam. 7, 8.Iob. 42, 8.Rom. 15, 30. &c.) defunctorum verò invocatio ad primam Decalogi tabulam spectat & est cultus religionis, soli verò Deo debitus. Tantum itaque abest, utillius in Scriptura S. praeceptum extet (id quod ipsi quoque Pontificii largiuntur, Vid. Eccius in Enchir. pag. 156. Bell. l. 1. de fanct. beat. c. 20. Becanusl. c. §. 26. Cotonus l. c.) sive etiam exemplum probatum, ut potiùs severissimè prohibita ea sit, & quidem in locis illis omnibus, ubi adoratio religiosa soli Deo vindicatur. Quod verò Conzen distinguit inter orationem religiosam, ac nudam invocationem, quâ à viventibus quoque auxilium petimus, ceu Iulius Caesar Coturius in Epit. pag. 466. scribit, & hâc solâ sanctos defunctos à Pontificiis fortè affici, persudere nobis vult, illâ non: in eo repugnat ipsius conatui tum doctrina, tum praxis in Pontificiâ Ecclesia notissima. Urget quidem Iesuita Cotonus d. l. utpote benè sciens, quàm haec distinctio parùm à suis attendatur, bonum esse, potiùs utite, & verò etiam necessarium, Christianos monere omnes sapiùs3 docere ne ex Sanctis Deos efficiant, aut unico Numini unicè venerādo paros & aequipollentes, Sed vereor ne aëré verberet, nisi simul Pontifici vel sanctae modò inquisitionis Patribus persuaserit, ut Psalterium Mariae A. 1476. per Ioh. de Hallis Venetiis impressum, iterumque à Iesuitis in Bavariâ prelo commissum per Indicem Expurgatorium aboleant; ut notent quoq; ac tollant iidem illi per Expurg. Indicem infausta illa dogmata, quòd sancti sint ador andi adoratione propriè sic dicta, quòdin sanctorum bonorem recitanda sit oratio Dominica, quòd ea ab illis postulare debeam, quae elargiri solius Dei est, quòd fiducia in ipsis sit cotlocanda, quae passim â Iesuitis inculcantur. Sed de his alibi plura. Conferantur quae prolixè de invoc. sanct. à nostratibus scripta, cumprimis D. Chemn. part. 3. Exam. Concil. Trident. D. Ioh. Himmelio ac D. Ioh. Iac. Bernhardo in pecul. lib. de Invoc. Sanct. publicatis, D. Mentzero Disp. VI. Antipistor. B. Par. t. 8 LL. Theol. it. Confess. Cathol. t. 3: Dispp. Academ. p. 4. seqq. p. 320. &c. D. Lobech. in A. C. Disp. 23 D. Mylio, D. Gravero aliisque ad Art. 22. A. C.)*

Cùm enim trium harum personarum, Patris sc. Filii & Spiritus Sancti sit una Deitas, ae quails gloria & indivisa essentia, ideò etiam nominatâ unâ personâ, nominatur altera, invocatâ unâ personâ invocature altera.

*(Q. 2. An etiam in V. T. precatio haec fuerit apud fideles in usu Photiniani negant, & exinde porrò colligunt, Christum primam Decalogi tabulam auxisse, adiiciendo illi or ationem Dominicam. Vid. Catech. Racov. p. 164. Smale. de divin. Christi. c. 5. Resp. distinguendum ante omnia inter materiam s. res, quae in oratione petuntur, ac inter formam externam, h. e. verborum nexum atq; ordinem, in praesente oratione observatum. Quod formam concernit, lubentes largimur, quòd in V. T. nullibi talis preacatio legatur, nempe si verba ac litteras numerare quis velit, atque eatenus concedimus, precationem hanc N. T. esse propriam. Quod autem porrò materiam spectat, nempe res, quas à DEO in Orat. Dom, petimus, negari sanè vix ullâ probabilitatis specie poterit, quin eaedem in V. T. fuerint & â DEO piis promissae, & à fidelibus quoque petitae. Id quod adeò clarum est, ut nec ipse Smalcius penitus ire inficias potuerit. Ita enim Disp. 7. contr. Frantz. scribit: Non quaeritur, annon suo modo etiam eadem orare potuerint (nempe vi promissionis divinae de exauditione factae) & oraverint quidam viri sancti sub V. T. quae in Oratione Dominic â nobis praseribuntur: sed an hic modus orandi praescrip: us omnibus generatim fuerit; & an omnes ita oraverint velorare debuerint: hoc in questione est. Ast si hoc modò Photiniani concesserint, quò pii eadem, quae in Orat. Dom. petimus, & orare potuerint, & etiam orarint, facilè ruet illorum dogma, quòd Christus primam tabulam auxerit, adeoque novus legislator sit. Ad hoc enim non sufsicit, ut novâ saltem methodo ea proponantur, quae in V. T. pii orarunt, sed ut aliae etiam res petantur, peti imò iubeantur, ac meliores quoque promissiones extent. Sed dicat aliquis: Nihilominus non omnibus in V. T. mandatum, ut ta, quae in oratione Dom. petimus, ipsi quog 3 à DEO peterent, &, quidem praecisè hâc à Christo praescripta orationis formulâ. Resp. Neg. quòd hîc certa praescripta lex sit, sive quòd praecisè ita formalia verba sint servanda, ut salvâ materiâ nemo possit aliis verbis preces suas ad Deum fundere. Unde ipsi quoque photin. in Catech. Racov. p. 169. moment, liberum esse etiam in N. T. aliàr atione & formâ, quàm in Orat. Dom. praescriptum, Dcum invocare: siquidem nec hîc nec alibi id prohibitum. Saltem caveatur, ne id quod petimus, repugnet voluntati divine. Mandatam vero à Christo hanc or andi formam hoc fine, ut sciremus, quid à Deo semper ac necessariò perere debeamus. Quòd cerò Iudaeis in V. T. per Decalogum (ut omittam nunc insignem, locuoe Ps. 50, 15. tum quoque prophetarum frequentes ad poenitentiam agendam admonitiones.) minimè iniunctum fuerit, ut sanctificationem nominis divini, adventum Regni DEI &c. expeaerent, vix, spero, vel hodierni saltem Iudaei Socinianis largientur. quòd autem fideles haec talia petierint, abunde patet vel ex solis psalmis Davidicis. Accedit, quòd eadem penè verba, è quibus Oratio Dominica constat, in Iudaeorum scriptis etiamnum reperian---: unde sanè co-ligere pronum est, quòd eadem illorum maiores à Deo petierint, quae nos in N. T. à Deo petimus. Decent nos ea, scribit Grotius in h. l. p. 142. quae ex Ebraeorum libris ab aliis sunt sitata, non tam formulam hanc à Christo suis verbis conceptam, quàm in eam congestum quicquid in Ebraeorum praecibus ar at laudabile: Sient & in admonitionibus passim utitur notis eo seculo proverbits. Conferatur omninò Act. 4, 12.c. 15, 11.Matth. 1, 21.)*

Πάτερἡμῶν. Sicur nomen Patris monet nos de amore DEI: ita pronomen noster admonet nos de amore proximi. Quia enim communem habemus in coelis Patrem, ideò fraterno amore nos invicem debemus amplecti. Gregor. Nyssenus orat. 2. de Orat. Domin. monet, eos, qui filii Dei nec sunt, nec esse volunt, quippe qui voluntariè in peccato mortali persistunt, mendaciter dicere; Pater noster qui es in coelis. Nam cùm Patrem invocant, non Deum, sed Diabolum invocant, quia sunt expatre Diabolo, Diabolus, autem non ect in coelis, sed in inferis.

Author operis imperf. in Matth, Noster dixit, non, meus. Libenter audit Deus, quando Christianus non solùm pro se, sed pro altero orat. Pro se enim orare naturae est, pro altero gratiae: pro se orare, necessitas rei cogit, pro altero autem caritas fraternitatis hortatur. Dulcior est autem ante Deum oratio, non quam necessitas rei transmittit, sed quam caritas fraternitatis commendat.

Ambrosius lib. 1. de Cain & Abel cap. 9. Orandum praecipu& pro populo doceris b. e. pro toto corpore, pro membris omnibus matris tuae, in quo mutuae, caritatis ast insigne. Si enim pro teroges, tantummodò pro te rogabis, nunc autem quia singuli orant pro omnibus, etiam omnes orant pro fingulis.

Αγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου. Prima haec petitio à fine rerum expetendarum initium facit. Nomen Dei sanctificatur, non in sensu absoluto, qs. Deus in se & ratione sui à nobis sanctificetur, sed in sensurelativo, quod Deus sanctus existens à nobis talis agnoscatur. Id fit tripliciter. 1. δοθητικῶς per sanam doctrinam. 2. ἐνεργητικῶς per sanctam vitam. 3. πα θητικῶς per passiones, ob Evangelii confessionem toleratas. In precatione non debemus primuomnium de nobis esse soliciti, sed de gloriâ DEI, ad quam tanquam ad finem ultimum omnia referri debent.

Nomen D E I est Deus ipse, ut inter hominess nominatur h. e. agnoscitur & celebratur. Hoc nomen DEI sanctificatur i. e. sanctum habetur & praedicatur.

1. Per infidelium & haereticorum conversionem. 2. Persanctam fidelium conversationem. 3. Per nominis divini glorificationem. Esai. 8. v. 13.Matth. 5. v. 16.1. Petr. 2. v. 12.cap. 3. v. 15.

## 6:10
v. 10. Ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου. γενηθήτω Τὸ θἐλημά σου, ὡς εν οὐρανῶ, καὶ -πὶ τῆς γῆς.

Ἡ βασιλεία σου. In certain Latin Codices of Luke 11. v. this third petition is not had, just as neither is the seventh; to which Bellarm. replies, lib. 1. de bon. oper. in partic. cap. 5. First, it can happen that in the Latin Codices, through the carelessness of the scribes, those two petitions are missing, which are had entire in the Greek and Syriac Codices, and are expounded by Euthymius and Theophyl. in the commentary on Luke. (But this very thing proves the vice of the Vulgate version) Then it can also happen that the Lord in Luke did not deliver the Lord's Prayer entirely, for it is certain that the Lord taught the form of praying in Luke at a different time and to different hearers than in Matthew. (But this is in no way likely, nor does the perfection of this prayer admit it.) Thirdly, those two petitions are omitted in Luke, because they are in some way contained in the preceding ones. (But this contradicts Bellarm.'s hypothesis, that there are seven distinct petitions.) Franciscus Lucas Brugensis, who urges this argument, himself concedes, that which is requested by us in the third petition is in reality the same as that which is comprised in the first petition, but under its own proper rationale, which is different, it is repeated more explicitly: otherwise, indeed, he says, even the second would be included in the first.

The Kingdom of GOD is threefold. Of power, of grace, and of glory. The kingdom of power endures from the beginning of the creature, therefore this petition, by which we pray for the kingdom of God to come, cannot be understood of that. Some prove that the kingdom of grace cannot be understood here from the fact that it is always present in some, and that its arrival is requested by us in the third, fifth, and sixth petitions. But to the former argument it is answered from the Catechism, the kingdom of GOD indeed comes without our petition, but we pray that it may come to us ; to the latter argument it is answered that principally indeed the kingdom of glory or our salvation is understood here, which with respect to us is the ultimate end, meanwhile secondarily and consequently also the kingdom of grace in this life, as its beginning, can be understood, which in the remaining petitions is not so directly requested.

This very thing is proved by the opposition, because to the kingdom of GOD, the arrival of which we request, is opposed the kingdom of Satan, which has its place most of all in this world, the destruction of which we request at the same time. Hence Ambrose, book 5 of the Sacraments, chapter 4, Rupert on chapter 6 of Matthew, and others explain this petition concerning the kingdom of grace.

By Beza understands the decree of GOD concerning us, of being introduced through tribulations into the kingdom of heaven. It is more correctly accepted concerning the will of GOD, revealed in the word. The Scholastics say, the will of sign is understood, not of good pleasure. It can nevertheless also in some way be referred to the will of good pleasure, insofar as, namely, we ought not to rebuke the will of good pleasure, nor murmur against it, but patiently and willingly acquiesce to it. *(But certain Calvinists wrongly oppose the will of sign and of good pleasure to one another, saying, that the sayings of Scripture, which assert that God does not will sin, are to be understood concerning the revealed will or of sign: but not concerning the hidden will or of good pleasure. Thus Zanchius, 3 on the nature of GOD, chapter 4; likewise book 5 on the nature of GOD.

chapter 2. Zeged in LL. P. 232. Bucanus, book 14, p. 135. Compare Piscator, part 1. Response to the rejoinder of Vorstius, p. 259. Which things indeed, since they can scarcely be thought of without impiety, Wendelin wishes to appear as if he does not approve of them at all. For thus in Theological Exercises 1, § 9. The disagreement between divine revelation and the decree or interior will, which appears to exist, is not real: although I do not deny that the formula of speaking: God wills something by the will of sign, which He does not will by the will of good pleasure: which is common to some of our Doctors with Luther (But that he is foreign to this opinion will be shown elsewhere) does not seem to me to be so convenient. But whether W. truly makes a divorce from that opinion, we shall examine on another day.) Matth, 7. v. 21, Christ says: Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father, who is in heaven. Deservedly, therefore, to the petition concerning the coming of the kingdom is added the petition concerning the fulfillment of the divine will.

Cyprian on this subject: We do not ask that God may do what He wills to do, but that we may do what He wills us to do.

The following sayings speak of this will of GOD, which we ask to be done by us. Ioh. 6. v. 40. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life. Rom. 12. v. 2. Be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God. 1. Thess. 4. v. 3. For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication. Hebr. 10. v. 36. For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise. (Cf. also Ps. 119, 5. 12. 33. Luc. 22, 42.)

Contrary to this will of GOD is the will of our flesh, the will of the world, and the will of the Devil. Eph. 2. v. 3. 2. Tim. 2. v. 26. Therefore, in the contrary sense, we ask that these depraved wills be effectively resisted, so that they may not be done. Thy will be done, we say, not the will of our flesh, not of the world, not of the Devil. (

*(In vain do the Papists gather from this petition that man can perfectly fulfill the law of GOD. For unless man, they say, could fulfill the law of GOD, we would ask in vain that the will of GOD be done, since it requires the fulfillment of the law. See Bell. l. 4. de Iustif. c. 13. §. Quarta ratio. I answer by distinguishing between legal fulfillment of the law, and Evangelical. It suffices for us that, if not in the former way, yet in the latter way we can fulfill the law of GOD, which is done when we apprehend by true faith Christ, who is the end and

fulfillment of the law for righteousness to every believer, Rom. 10, 4. And doing this we fulfill the law of GOD, and thus the will of GOD is also done by us. Nor yet must it be denied that new obedience is required from those who have already been justified by faith in Christ, but that is not the perfect fulfillment of the law, meriting eternal life. Conf. B. Par. L. de Lege DEI §. 199.)* *(But here the different ways of considering the divine will must be observed entirely. Since one is antecedent will, another consequent; one absolute, another hypothetical; one efficacious, another inefficacious; one legal, another Evangelical; one efficient, another permissive etc. concerning which many things may be seen in Coll. Isagog. p. 179. 180. 437. also B. Par. Comm. In Gen. pag. 447. Comm in post. ep. Petri p. 391.)*

Ὠς ἐν οὐρανῶ καὶ -πὶ τῆς γῆς. Cyprian, Tertullian, Augustine, and several others understand by heaven our spirit, by earth our flesh, which lusts against the Spirit, Galat. 5. v. 17. Akin to this exposition is that by which the same Cyprian understands by heaven, the faithful and the just, and by earth, the unfaithful and the sinners. And likewise that by which Augustine, in book 2 of De sermone Domini in monte, chapter 11, understands by heaven, Christ, and by earth, the Church.

More correctly, by those who in heaven do the will of GOD are understood the holy Angels, Ps. 103. v. 20. Matth. 18. v. 10. By the name of Angels, however, are simultaneously understood the spirits of holy men piously deceased, who have already become ἰσἀγγελοι, Luc. 20. v. 36. who perfectly fulfill the will of GOD.

The author of the Opus imperfectum on this passage: He commands those living here to have a common conversation with the inhabitants of heaven, and before that heavenly dwelling is provided, he wishes heaven in a certain way to be made from earth, to show us other angels on earth.

The angels in the heavens fulfill the will of GOD. 1. not some, but all. 2. not by half, but wholly and perfectly. 3. from sincere love and free will. 4. constantly and perseveringly. 5. for the glory of GOD alone. Therefore, in the same way, let us also strive to do the will of GOD on earth.

*(Furthermore, τὸ & on earth here is the same as so on earth, just as the prefix occurs elsewhere also, as in Prov. 10, 25. Prov. c. 17, 3. Prov. c. 25, 23. Es. 53, 7. and the Greek καὶ Act. 7, 51. Ioh. 20, 21. as the blessed D. Glassius rightly notes.

Rightly, therefore, the blessed Luther rendered it in the German version also & Syr. through i. e. even. Ethiopian: & in the earth also. The Arab however used it bare. Georgius Pasor indeed in Lex. under the word οὕτως thinks that this particle ἐλλεὶπει in this place, just as also Mark 3, 26.John 20, 21.

*( Stupidly, writes Corn. à Lap. on this place, Luther from this, that is, from this petition, was inferring that the Turk ought not to be resisted: because the Turk, he says, is the scourge of God, he invades us by God's will and compels us. Resp. The Turk is the scourge of GOD, not positive, such as is the scourge of a master whipping a negligent student, but merely permissive: for God wills to permit that the Turk should tyrannically invade and afflict us etc. The same cabbage, so often warmed up and so often rejected, was long ago also not only set forth by the same Cornelius in Canon., Comm. In Prophet. mai. praemissis, can. 36., but also by other Papists, as Alph. De Castro l. 3. adv. Haeres. under the word War, heresy 2., Bell. l. 3. de Laic. c. 16., Laur. Förer in -berschl. Pup. Sax. p. 66., the Margrave of Brandenburg both in Spec. p. 184. and in Apolog. p. 297., Pazmannus l. 8. Hodeg., and most recently also that most noble Jesuit stentor Kettius in various booklets published in the German language. But it must be known that blessed Luther does not dissuade the war itself from being waged against the Turks (for the contrary is evident from his own exhortations to undertake war against the Turk. See vol. 4. Ien. Germ. f 472.) but the preposterous against the Turks manner of waging war. Namely, that war against the Turks is undertaken without previous true and serious repentance, that those about to undertake the expedition attribute too much to Papal Bulls and Indulgences, that under the pretext of the Turkish war Germany is plundered by Roman harpies, that Bishops proceed into the battle line. That this is the mind of blessed Luther has long been shown clearly by our theologians. Let the Saxon Theologians be seen in Defens. fundam. pag. 135. 136. 220. seqq., B. D. Zeaem. against Ungersd. p. 136. seqq., B. Par. Loc. de Mag. Polit. § 386., Confess. Cath. vol. 3. p. 406., L. Laelius against Sartorius p. 168., D. Kesler. in Luther. p. 200. seqq.)

Latin:

v. 10. Ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου. γενηθήτω Τὸ θἐλημά σου, ὡς εν οὐρανῶ, καὶ -πὶ τῆς γῆς.

Ἡ βασιλεία σου. In quibusdam Codicibus Latinis Luc. 11. v. non habetur haec tertia petitio uti nec septima; ad quod resp. Bellarm. lib. 1. de bon. oper. in partic. cap. 5. Primò fieri po-est, ut in Latinis Codd. incuria librariorum desint duae illae petitiones, qua integra habentur in Codd. Graecis & Syriacis, & exponuntur ab Euthymio & Theophyl. in comm. Lucae. (At hoc ipsum probatvitium vulg. versionis) Deinde fieri etiam potest, ut Dominus apud Lucam non integrè traediderit orationem Dominicam, constat enim, alio tempore & aliis au ditoribus Dominum docuisse formam orandi apud Lucam, quàm apud Matth. (At hoc nullo modo verisimile, nec admittithuius orationis perfectio.) Tertiò, duas illas petitiones apud Lucam omitti, quoniam aliquo modo in praecedentibus continentur. (At hoc repugnant Bellarm. hypothesi, quod sint septem distinctae petitiones.) Franciscus Lucas Brugensis, qui hoc argumentum urget, ipsemet concedit, id quod in tertia petitione à nobis petitur, secundum rem idem primâ petitione esse comprehensum, sed sub propriaratione, quae diversa est, disertiù,s repetitum: caeteroqui enim, inquit, & secunda primae includatur.

Regnum DEI triplex est. Potentiae, gratiae & gloriae. Regnum potentiae perdurat ab initio creaturae, ideò non potest haec petitio, quâ precamur regnum Dei venire, de illo intelligi. Regnum gratiae non posse hîe intelligi, quidam probant ex eo, quòd illud in aliquibus semper adsit praesens, quôdque tertiâ quintâ & sextâ petitionibus illius adventus à nobis petatur. Sed priori argumento resp. ex Catechesi, regnum DEI sine nostra petitione quidem venit, sed oramus ut ad nos quaveniat; posteriori argumento resp. quòd principaliter quidem regnum gloriae sive nostra salus hîc intelligatur, qui respectu nostri est finis ultimus, interim secundariò & consequenter etiam regnum gratiae in hac vita, tanquam illius exordium intelligi potest, quod in reliquis petitionibus non ita directè petitur.

Hoc ipsum probat oppositio, quia regno DEI, cuius adventum petimus, opponitur regnum Satanae, quod in hoc mundo vel maxime locum habet, cuius destructionem simul petimus. Inde Ambros. lib. 5. de Sacram. cap. 4. Rupertus in cap. 6. Matth. & alii exponut hanc petitionem de regno gratiae.

Per Beza intelligit DEI decretum de nobis, per tribulationes in regnum coelorum introducendis. Rectiùs accipitur de voluntate DEI, in verbo revelatâ. Scholastici dicunt, intelligi voluntatem signi, non beneplaciti. Potest tamen etiam aliquo modo referri ad voluntatem beneplaciti, quatenus sc. non debemus reprehendere voluntatem beneplaciti, nec illi obmurmurare, sed patienter & libenter ei acquiescere. *(Malè verò Calviniani quidam voluntatem signi ac beneplaciti invicem opponunt, dicentes, quòd dicta Scripturae, quae adserunt, Deum nō velle peccatum, intelligenda sint de voluntate revelata seu signi: non autem de voluntate occultà seu beneplaciti. Ita Zanch. 3. de nat DEI c. 4. it. l. 5. de N. D.

c. 2. Zeged in LL. P. 232. Bucanus L. 14. p. 135. Conf. Piscat. part. 1. Resp. ad dupl. Vostii p. 259. Quae sanè cùm absque impietate cogitari vix possint, videri vult Wendel. ac si minimè approbet. Ita enim Exerc. Theol. 1. § 9. Dissidium patefactionis divinae & decreti seu voluntatis interioris, apparens, non verum est: etsi non diffiteor, loquendi formulam: Vult Deus aliquid voluntate signi, quod non vult voluntate beneplaciti: quae nostris Doctoribus nonnullis cum Luthere (Sed hunc alienum ab istâ sententiâ esse, alibi ostendetur) commumunis est: non usadeò commodam mihi videri. Sed num revera W. ab eâ sententiâ divortium faciat, alio dispiciemus die.)* Matth, 7. v. 21, dicit Christus: Non omnis, qui dicit mihi, Domine, Domine, intrabit in regnum coelorum, sed qui facit voluntatem Patris mei, qui in coelis est. Meritò igitur petitioni de adventu regni subiungitur, petitio de impletione divinae voluntatis.

Cyprianus d. l. Non petimus, ut Deus faciat, quod vult facere, sed ut not faciamus, quod ipse nos vult facere.

De hac voluntate DEI, quam à nobis fieri petimus, loquuntur dicta sequentia. Ioh. 6. v. 40.Haec est voluntas Patris mei, qui misit me, ut omnis qui videt Filium & credit in eum, habeat vitam aternā.Rom. 12. v. 2.Reformemini in novitate sensus vestri, ut probetis, quae sit voluntas DEI bona, & beneplacens & perfecta.1. Thess. 4. v. 3.Hac est voluntas DEI, sanctificatio vestra, ut vitetis scortationem.Hebr. 10. v. 36.Patientia vobis necessaria est, ut voluntatem DEI facientes reportitis promissionem. *(Conf. etiam Ps. 119, 5.12.33.Luc. 22, 42.)*

Huic DEI voluntati contraria est voluntas carnis nostrae, voluntas mundi ac voluntas Diaboli, Eph. 2. v. 3.2. Tim. 2. v. 26. Ergo à contrario sensù petimus, pravis hisce voluntatibus efficaciter resisti, ne fiant. Fiat, dicimus, tua voluntas, non nostrae carnis, non mundi, non Diaboli voluntas.

*(Frustra ex hîc petitione Pontificii colligunt, quòd homo legem DEI perfectè possit implere. Nisi enim homo, inquiunt, posset legem DEI implere, frustra peteremus ut fiat voluntas DEI, quippe quae requirit legis impletionem. Vid. Bell. l. 4. de Iustif. c. 13. §. Quarta ratio. Resp. dist. inter impletionem legis legalem, & Evangelicam. Sufficit nobis, quòd si non priori, tamen posteriori modo legem DEI implere possimus, id quod fit, quando Christum, qui est finis &

impletio legis ad iustitiam omni credenti,Rom. 10, 4. verâ fide apprehendimus. Atque hoc facientes legem DEI implemus, & sic DEI quoque fit â nobis voluntas. Neque tamen negandum, novam obedientiam ab iis, qui iamtum per fidem in Christum iustificati sunt, requiri, sed illa non est perfecta legis impletio, promerens vitam aeternam. Conf. B. Par. L. de Lege DEI §. 199.)* *(Observandi verò hîc omninò sunt diversi modi considerandi voluntatem divinam. Cùm alia sit voluntas antecedens, alia consequens; alia absoluta, alia hypothetica; alia efficax, alia inefficax; alia legalis, alia Evangelica; alia efficiens, alia permittens &c. de quibus dift. plura videantur Coll. Isagog. p. 179. 180. 437. it. B. Par. Comm. In Gen. pag. 447. Comm in post. ep. Petri p. 391.)*

Ὠς ἐν οὐρανῶ καὶ -πὶ τῆς γῆς. Cyprianus, Tertull. Aug. ac alii nonnulli per coelum intelligunt Spiritum nostrum, per terram carnem nostram, quae adversus Spiritum concupiscit, Galat. 5. v. 17. Huic expositioni affinis ea, quâ per coelum idem Cyprianus intelligit fideles & iustos, per terram infideles & peccatores. Itemque ea, quâ Aug. lib. 2. de ferm. dom. In monte cap. 11. per coelum intelligit Christum, per terram, Ecclesiam.

Rectiùs per eos, qui in coelo faciunt DEI voluntatem intelliguntur sancti Angeli,Ps. 103. v. 20.Matth. 18. v. 10.Angelorum autem nomine simul intelliguntur Spiritus sanctorum hominum piè defunctorum, qui iam facti sunt ἰσἀγγελοι,Luc. 20. v. 36. qui perfectè DEI voluntatem implent.

Autor operis imperf. in h. l. Iubet hî degentes conversationem cum coeli habitatoribus habere communem, & antequam superna illa, praestetur habitatio, coelum quodammodo vult fieri è terra, aliosnobis Angelos terram monstrare.

Angeli in coelis voluntatem DEI implent. 1. non aliqui, sed omnes. 2. non ex dimidio, sed ex integro & perfectè. 3. ex sincero amore & libera voluntate. 4. constanter & perseveranter. 5. ad solius DEI gloriam. Eodem igitur modo etiam nos in terra conemur voluntatem DEI facere.

*(Porrò τὸ& in terrâ hîc idem esse, ac sic in terrâ, quemadmodum praefixum ialibi quoque occurrit, uti Prov. 10, 25.Prov. c. 17, 3.Prov. c. 25, 23.Es. 53, 7. & Gr. καὶAct. 7, 51.Ioh. 20, 21. rectè notat B. D. Glassius.

Benè proinde B. Luth. in vers. Germ. reddidit ita & Syr. per i. e. etiam. Aethiops: & in terrâ etiam. Arabs tamen nudum adhibuit. Georgius verò Pasor in Lex. voce οὕτως existimat, particulam hanc ἐλλεὶπει h. l. quemadmodum etiam Marc. 3, 26.Ioh. 20, 21.)*

*( Stolidè, scribit Corn. à Lap. in h. l. Lutherus hinc s. ex petitione hâc, inferebat, Turcae nō esse resistendum: quia Turca, inquit, est flagellum Deum, Deivoluntate nos invadit & cogit. Resp. Turca est flagellum DEI non positivum, quale est flagellum magistri flagellantis negligentem discipulum, sed permissivum duntaxat: vult enim Deus permittere, ut Turca tyrannicè nos invadat & affligat &c. Eandem crambem toties recoctam toties reiectam, pridem quoque non solùm idem Cornelius apposuit in Canon., Comm. In Prophet. mai. praemissis, can. 36. verùm etiam alii Pontificii, uti Alph. De Castro l. 3. adv. Haeres. verbo Bellum, haer. 2. Bell. l. 3. de Laic. c. 16. Laur. Förer im -berschl. Pup. Sax. p. 66. Marchio Brandenb. tum in Spec. p. 184. tum in Apolog. p. 297. Pazmannus l. 8. Germ. f 472.) sed praeposterum contra Turcas belliger andi modum. ## 6:11
v. 11. Τὸν ἄρ-ον Τἡμῶν Τὸν -ὸς ἡμῖν οήμερον. Here begins the second table of the Lord's prayer, in which we ask for those things which are necessary for us for the misery of this life.

By Τὸν ἄρ-ον -πιοὑσιον 1. many of the ancients understand bread spiritual, or Christ, who is that living bread, which came down from heaven,Ioh. 6. vers. 51. or the word of GOD, which is the food of our soul,Matth. 4, 4. or the Eucharist, which is called supersubstantial bread. See Hieron. in cap. 6. Matth. & in c. 2. ad Tit. Ambros. lib. 5. de Sactam. cap. 4. Cyrillus catech. 5. mystag. Cassianus Collat. 9. c 21. & 24. Petrus Chrysologus serm. de Orat Domin. *(Pelbartus de Themeswar serm. 29. in Dom. XI. post Pentec. writes: Principally is understood the bread of the Eucharist and the bread of divine fruition. Of which Luc. 14. Blessed is he who shall eat bread in the kingdom of GOD. Whence Matth. 6. he writes: Supersubstantial bread by reason of excellence, in that the body of Christ in the Eucharist and the vision and fruition of blessed God precedes all substance of the world. How indeed the Eucharist is called daily bread, the same in the said place strives to show at length.)*

But 1. bodily bread ought entirely to have been requested in this perfect prayer, otherwise it would not contain all things which can and ought to be requested from God, Gen. 28. v. 20.Prov. 30. v. 8. which argument among others Abulensis urges q. in cap. 6. Matth. where he proves with many arguments that by bread -πιούσιον the Eucharist is not understood. 2. Angelus Caninius in disquis. locorum N. Test. discourses thus: -πιούσιος is not rightly translated supersubstantial. For it should have been said ὑΠεροὑσιον or at least ἐπούτιον, just as we say ἐπουοάνιον, ἐΦήμερον, not πιουράνιον not επιήμερον.

*(That this petition cannot and ought not to be accepted concerning the Eucharist, as Gregor. de Valentia t. 3. disp. 6. q. 2. punct. 5. col. 1630. Barradius t. 2. Conc. Evang. l. 7. c. 24. p. 475. Alphonsus de Castro l. 6. adv. haeres. haer. ult. voce Eucharistia, Slotanus contra Velsium art. 22. and some other Papists wish, is evident also among other things from this, that the Holy Eucharist had not yet been instituted at that time; how therefore could the Apostles have requested the Lord's Prayer then, or at least have rightly understood the Lord's Prayer regarding this petition? The same argument is urged by Corn. Iansenius Episc. Gand. In Co-. Ev p. 560.)*

2. Chrysostomus & the Author of the imperfect work in cap. 6. Matth. understand it concerning bodily bread, by which, according to the customary Hebraism, are understood all those things which are necessary for leading this bodily life, such as food, clothing, dwelling, health of the body.

3. Bellarmine, in book 1 of On Good Works, in part, chapter 6, establishes that by the name bread it ought not nor can it be understood only spiritual bread, because of the reason brought forward above, taken from the perfection of the Lord's Prayer, nor only corporal bread, both because most Fathers accept this passage either only or principally concerning spiritual bread; and because the Lord's Prayer would be imperfect if the food of the body were so diligently sought through it, and no mention were made of spiritual food; and because it is not credible that the Lord wished corporal bread to be sought so solicitously, either only or principally, when in the same sermon He commanded that solicitude for corporal things must be avoided. He thinks, therefore, that by the name of bread it ought to be understood as nourishment in general, i.e., all subsidies necessary for preserving the life of both soul and body, and since the subsidies of spiritual life, such as the Sacraments, sermons, and other things of that kind, are much more necessary and noble than the subsidies of corporal life, therefore the intention of the one praying ought to be directed toward spiritual bread, as toward that which is primarily sought, but toward corporal bread as toward a certain addition. *(Cornelius à Lapide and other Papists incline toward the same in this place.)*

But 1. by this reasoning one and the same word would have two different meanings. 2. Spiritual bread is sought in the preceding petitions, especially in the second and third. This is my food, that I may do the will of Him who sent me, that I may complete, says Christ John 4:34 His work. Franciscus Lucas Brugensis on this place: The bread of the soul, by which our soul, our spirit, has need to be fed and sustained, does not seem to be understood in this proper petition, since an exact distinction of the petitions must be preserved, but that it had been included in the former: Thy will be done, especially since to do the will of GOD, is itself the food of the life of the soul. *(The Jesuit Tirinus also accepts this passage concerning corporal, frugal, and common bread, and brings forward for this explanation not only the ancient Doctors of the Church, Basil, Cyril, and Chrysostom, but also the Calvinists, Beza, Henricus Stephanus, and others. He could also have added to the Fathers brought forward Tertullian, Cyprian, Jerome, Gregory of Nyssa, and Augustine, whom Cardinal Toletus produces in Luke. The Roman Catechism pronounces indefinitely concerning the Fathers, that the holy Fathers understand this petition concerning the subsidies of this life. Toletus calls this interpretation literal and common.)

In the same way also the Arminians accept it in their Confession, chapter 14, §. 9. The Photinians, however, in the Racovian Catechism, p. 167, accept it concerning spiritual and corporal bread.) 3. The arguments of Bellarmine are not cogent, because from the petition for corporal things it does not immediately follow that there is a preposterous solicitude for them, but rather the contrary. We submit ourselves in this petition to the good pleasure of GOD, who, as our Father, knows what and how much daily bread is useful to us.

(Since, therefore, there are so many discrepant opinions, even among the Papists themselves, while some expressly deny, as Toletus, Maldonatus, Iansenius, Barradius, Gorranus, Franc, Lucas, that it is treated literally concerning the Holy Eucharist in this place; others concede that it can only be expounded spiritually concerning the Holy Eucharist in this place, and yet, according to Bellarmine himself, firm arguments can be drawn only from the literal sense, it is evident how infirm the collection of some Papists is, when they strive to establish communion under one kind, among other things, also from the fact that in the Lord's Prayer mention is made of bread alone and of no other species. And even if it were treated most of all concerning spiritual and corporal bread in this petition, one is certainly no more permitted to infer communion under one kind from it, than if someone wished to conclude from it that, while mention is made of bread alone, we are commanded in this petition to ask of God only food, and not at the same time drink as well. As if it were not manifest that the συνεκδοχικῶς name bread is to be accepted here.)

Concerning the word -πιοὑσιος, there exist likewise diverse opinions. 1. Many translate it as supersubstantial. The Vulgate edition Matth. 6. v. 11. rendered it thus; to which Bellarmine responds: There are not lacking many ancient codices of the Vulgate edition which do not have supersubstantial but daily, just as it is established that St. Cyprian also read, Bell. d. 1. The word -πιοὑσιος, if you look at the sound, signifies supersubstantial. But what is to be determined concerning this version was just stated by Angelus Caninius. Bellarmine, when he sees that corporal bread, concerning which he concedes this petition must be accepted in a certain respect, cannot be called supersubstantial, twists himself in various ways. The word -πιοὑσιος,, he says, if you look at the sound, signifies supersubstantial, yet if you consider the subject matter, it is accepted for the same thing, for which substantial is, so that it may seem to be referred not so much to the excellence as to the necessity of the bread. Then, just as the Greeks -πιοὑσιον read and yet, without regard for the preposition , expound it as substantial, why can we not also read in Latin supersubstantial, so that word may answer to word, and yet, without regard for the preposition, expound it as substantial? Finally, 3 it can also be that supersubstantial is the same as what is very substantial, just as we say superabound and supereminently, to abound greatly and to excel greatly, in which signification supersubstantial bread and daily bread will be altogether the same. But anyone sees that these things are forced, and fabricated to save the thesis in whatever way.

2. Some say -πιοὑσιον must be translated as of tomorrow, Angelus Caninius d. l. Jerome consulted the Gospel of the Hebrews, which was kept among the Nazarenes of Berrhoea, in which it was written, ךמחר tomorrow. Since therefore the Greek Interpreter, whom they say was John the Evangelist, saw no Greek name that corresponded to the Syriac ךמהר, for the Greeks have no word for tomorrow but say ἄυριον for tomorrow, and knew that τῆ δπιοὑση was accepted by all for the day after, he formed a new name, yet suitable and significant, preserving the analogy, and rendered it -πιοὑσιος. Similar things occur in Drusius Epist. 26. Erasmus in annot. h. l. It is most approved by me that -πιούσιος be called of tomorrow, since among the Greeks -πιοῦσα the day is called tomorrow. Act. 7. v. 26. Consistent with this exposition is that -πιούσιος is understood as ὁ δπὶ τῆς δπιούσης i.e. ἡμἐρας bread of the day of tomorrow; and what Benedict Arias rendered, after the present.

But to understand -πιούσιον as tomorrow through bread does not sufficiently suit the discourse of Christ, Matth. 6. v. 25. & seqq. in which he inveighs so sharply against diffidence and anxiety about tomorrow. Hence also Erasmus judges that this epithet should be referred not to corporal bread, but to spiritual. Christ, he says, in such a heavenly prayer does not speak of that bread which even the Gentiles receive from their parents. The sense therefore is, just as earthly Fathers look out for their children for bread, by which they may nourish the body even for the following day: so do you look out for us for heavenly bread, the food of the soul, who are the heavenly Father and Father of Spirits.

3. Some explain it thus, so that it signifies bread, which is added to the part of our substance i. e. to our body to nourish it. Some think it is said, -πιούσιον a substitute, which succeeds the bread consumed, and that it should succeed, the Nature of the body demands, with the word derived from the participle δπιούσ-, which descends from the verb ἔπειμι I succeed or follow. To this exposition can be referred the Latin Vulgate translation, which in Luke 11 rendered, daily bread. *(Luther followed the Vulgate Interpreter, or rather Cyprian himself, Ambrose, Augustine, and Jerome in this place. Although Adversaries everywhere disparage his version, they have nevertheless sufficiently shown its integrity against our people. See B. D. Schilt. in Catech Luth. p. 393. 394. B. D. Meisn. Philos. Sobr. part 2. sect. 1. c. 2. q. 19. and others, especially Dn. D. Walth. Off. Bibl. p. 383. It pleases to note only this in this place, that if faith is to be had in the Jesuit Maldonado himself, not only did the Vulgate and the Greek in this place -πιούσιον render it by daily, but also that all ancient Latin authors read it so. The mentioned Jesuit adds: It is an act of 3 incautiously that some in our time in the Vulgate edition have placed supersubstantial instead of daily: which by no means suits the food of the body, which we have proved is asked for by us. For that which is daily has a perpetual succession, so that the present day succeeds the yesterday. And thus Augustine almost accepts it, 1. 10. Confess. c. 31 n. 1. brought forward by Dn. Dilherro, who also compares it with the present place and beautifully explains the saying Luc. 12, 42. add, James c. 2, 16. See what is noted on Luc. 12, 42.)*

4. The Greek Fathers knew and expressed the force of the Greek word most excellently. Basil in the shorter questions, q. 252. Gregory of Nyssa, oration 4 on the Lord's Prayer. Chrysostom, Theophylact, and Euthymius in their commentaries on chapter 6 of Matthew explain ἄρ-ον -πιούσιον as accommodated to the nourishing of our substance, with which the exposition of Suidas agrees, -πὶ τῆ οὐσία ἡμῶν ἁρμόζον-α, bread suitable for sustaining us. The Syriac version can be accommodated to this exposition. For the Syrian rendered it bread of necessity or of our sufficiency. *(Mr. Dilherrus warns in Eccl. Syr. p. 47 that this is translated less congruously by Scultetus as bread of sufficiency, when it is rendered more aptly and closer to the force of the language as bread of our indigence: since the root signifies: he was in need, had need, had necessity.)* From the word סנק. the Arab has which words are translated in the Roman edition: our bread sufficient for us, (they can also be rendered: of our sufficiency) so that is derived from the root which according to Schindler denotes he was content, had enough, sufficed. The Ethiopian renders it: i.e. bread, which is for our every day, clearly as our Blessed Luther. But what the Blessed Man understands by the name daily bread, he explains sufficiently in the Small Catechism, from where perhaps Scultetus also has it, when in Observ. in Matth. p. 26 he writes: Next in our vernacular language we shall interpret the fourth petition thus: Unser nothdürftig Brot gib uns heut. Who himself nevertheless undeservedly criticizes the version of the Blessed Luther here, as was also noted by Mr. Ostermann, a man most skilled in both languages, as well as the Oriental ones, in Posit. Philol. concerning the Greek context of the N. T. §. 8. Finally, the interpreter of the 4 Evangelists renders it: Give us today our bread of every day.)* And this is that bread, which Solomon Prov. 30. v. 8. calls bread of the prescribed statute. περιουσιον signifies what is more than enough, according to Gellius book 1. chapter 22. Therefore Τὸ -πιοὐσιον signifies what is enough. That Solomon prays against, and Christ commands us to pray for, that this harmful thing, he commands us to pray for what is salutary and congruent to the children of God. *(Pasor in Lex. N. T. and the Blessed Crin. in בבל page 141 approve this explanation.)* Τὸν Πρὸς ἐΦήμερον ζωὴν τῆ οὐσἰα ἡμῶν χξήσιμον ὄν-α, -πὶ τὴν ἡμῶν οὐσίαν καὶ τςοΦὴν ἐπάρκον-α, Τὸν -πὶ τῆ οὐσία καὶ συςάσει ἡμῶν ἀυ-αρκῆ.

Τὸν ἄρ-ον ἡμῶν. It is called ours not by reason of origin, since bodily bread as well as spiritual is given by God; nor by reason of ownership, as if it were so much our own that we could use and enjoy it at our own discretion, but by reason of use, because it is destined by God for the preservation of our life.

The author of the imperfect work warns, that we therefore ask for our bread, because we ought not to desire another’s bread, acquired by theft, rapine, fraud, and evil arts. 2. Thes. 3. v. 11. & 12. That is opposed to the idle. *(Cons. Prov. 30. 8. 9. Ps 128, 1. )* Σήμερον. [

Σήμερον. Cyprian teaches, with this particle added, anxious solicitude -x-mi, so that I may not extend the desires of our petition for a long time.

From this it is manifest that the Savior wished this prayer to be daily and familiar to us, since we need the necessary subsidies of life daily, and yet this petition does not extend itself beyond the day on which it is poured forth. Cyril Catech 5. mystag. August. in Epist. 121 cap. 11. & lib 2. de serm. Domini in monte 12. today they explain, at this time, that is, of this mortal life. Heb. 3.

Tertullian, Cyprian, and Chrysostom explain it in such a way that it signifies precisely on this day. (And so also the Syrian renders it, who has the Arab translates in the day. Namely, in what way the adverb today is likewise circumscribed among the Arabs.)

Latin:

v. 11. Τὸν ἄρ-ον Τἡμῶν Τὸν -ὸς ἡμῖν οήμερον. Hîc incipit qs. Secunda Dominicae orationis tabula, in quâ petimus ea, quae pro huius vitae miseria nobis sunt necessaria.

Per Τὸν ἄρ-ον -πιοὑσιον 1. multi ex veteribus intelligent panem spiritualem, vel Christum, qui est panis ille vivus, qui de coelo desiendit,Ioh. 6. vers. 51. vel DEI verbum, quod est animae nostrae cibus,Matth. 4, 4. vel Eucharistiam, quae dicatur panis super substantialis. Vid. Hieron. in cap. 6. Matth. & in c. 2. ad Tit. Ambros. lib. 5. de Sactam. cap. 4. Cyrillus catech. 5. mystag. Cassianus Collat. 9. c 21. & 24. Petrus Chrysologus serm. de Orat Domin. *(Pelbartus de, Themeswar ferm. 29. in Dom. XI. post Pentec. scribit: Praecipuè intelligitur panis Eucharistiae & fruitionis divinae panis. De quo Luc. 14. Beatus, qui manducat panem in regno DEI. Unde Matth. 6. scribit: Panem supersubstantialem ratione excellentiae eò, quòd corpus Christi in Eucharistia & visio ac fruitio Dei beat a praecedit omnem mundi substantiam. Quomodo verò Eucharistia quotidianus panis vocetur, idem d. l. prolixè ostendere satagit.)*

Atqui 1. debuit omninò in hac perfecta oratione panis corporalis peti, aliàs non contineret omnia, quae à Deo peti possunt & debent, Gen. 28. v. 20.Prov. 30. v. 8. quod argumentum inter caetera urget Abulensis q. in cap. 6. Matth. ubi multis argumentis probat, per panem-πιούσιον non intelligi Eucharist. 2. Angelus Caninius in disquis. locorum N. Test. Sic disserit: -πιούσιοςnon rectè vertitur super substantialis. Dicendum enim suissetὑΠεροὑσιον vel saltem ἐπούτιον, sicut dicimus ἐπουοάνιον, ἐΦήμερον, non πιουράνιον non επιήμερον.

*(Quod de Eucharistia, ceu Gregor. de Valentiât. 3. disp. 6. q. 2. punct. 5. col. 1630. Barradiust 2. Conc. Evang. l. 7. c. 24. p. 475. Alphonsus de Castrol 6. adv. haeres. haer. ult. voce Eucharistia, Slotanus contra Velsium art. 22. aliiq, nonnulli Pontificii volunt, petitio haec nō possit nec debeataccipi, patet etiam inter alia inde, quòd S. Eucharistia tum nondum fuerit instituta; quomodo igitur Apostoli tum petere orationem Dominicam vel saltem rectè quo ad hanc petitionem intelligere Orat. Domin. potuissent? Idem hoc arg. urget Corn. Iansenius Epise. Gand. In Co-. Ev p. 560.)*

2. Chrysostomus & Autor impert operis in cap. 6. Matth. intelligunt de pane corporali, per quem iuxta usitatum Hebraismum, intelliguntur omnia illa, quae ad ducendam hanc corporalem vitam sunt necessaria, qualia sunt victus, amictus, habitatio, sanitas corporis.

3. Bellarminus lib. 1. de bon. operibus in part. cap. 6. statuit, nomine panis non debere nec posse intelligi solum panē spiritualem, propter rationem superiùs adductam, desumtam ex perfectione Dominicae Orationis, nec solum panem corporalem, tùm quia plerique Patres de pane Spirituali vel solùm vel praecipuè hunc locum accipiant; tùm quia imperfecta esset oratio Dominica, si tàm diligenter per eam peteretur cibus corporis, & cibi spiritualis nulla fieret mentio; tùm quia non est credibile, Dominum voluisse tàm, solicitè peti panem corporalem aut solum aut praecipuè, cùm in eodem sermone praeceperit, cavendam esse solicitudinē rerum corporalium. Existimat igitur, nomine panis intelligi debere alimenta in genere i. e. omnia subsidia necessaria ad vitam cùm animae tùm corporis conservandam, & quoniam subsidia vitae spiritualis, ut sunt Sacramenta, conciones & id genus alia, multò magis sunt & necessaria & nobilia, quàm subsidia vitae corporalis, ideò intentionem orantis ferri debere ad panem spiritualem, ut adid, quod primariò petitur, ad panem autem corporalem, ut ad quoddam additamentum. *(Eodem inclinat Corn. à Lapide in h. l. ac Pontificii alii.)*

Atqui 1. hac ratione una eademque vox duas diversas haberet significationes. 2. panis spiritualis in praecedentibus petitionibus petitur, cumprimis in secunda & tertia. Hic est cibus meus, ut faciam voluntatem eius, qui misit me, ut perficiam,, inquit Christus Ioh. 4. v. 34.opus eius. Franc. Luc. Brug. ad h. l. ## 6:12
v. 12 ἌΦες ἡμῖν -ὰ ὀΦειλήμα-α forgive, just as something is forgiven, which is held in the hands. Iust. in qq. & resp. ad orthod. q 97. p. 350. πολλάκις ἁμαρ-άνοντες δῆλον ὅτι καὶ πολλάις τῆς ἀΦέσεως χρήζομεν.

Aug 21. de Civ. Dei cap. 27. By this prayer our Savior wished to show us that however righteous we may live in the darkness and infirmity of this life, sins are not lacking to us, for the forgiveness of which we ought to pray. *(The discourse here is therefore about debts of injury brought upon us, which must be remitted, and injuries must be pardoned, as much as can be done with a safe conscience and by reason of duty, but not about a debt of money given in loan: for it is permitted to demand such a debt, and the debtor is also bound to pay what he received in loan Ps. 37, 21.) nor of restitution of fame and honor: whence public judgments are by no means to be disapproved of with the Anabaptists, as by them provision is made for the injury of fame. Nor are the hands of the Magistrate bound by this petition, so that he cannot or ought not to inflict deserved punishments upon the guilty according to just laws, which the Anabaptists likewise maintain.)*

Sins are called debts, because they render us debtors to God for punishment. (Mr. Dilh. establishes the connection between sins & debts in Ecl; Syr. p. 56.)

From the fact that even the holiest of men must, in the Lord's Prayer, ask for the remission of debts, that is, of sins, for themselves, and indeed most truly, not only humbly (just as the hammer of heretics, St. Augustine, long ago proved against the heresy of Pelagius and Coelestius in De peccatorum meritis et remissione, book 2, chapters 5 and following; likewise in Epistle 108, and also in Enchiridion, chapter 73. Whence also the Jesuit Conzen rightly writes here: It is truly an invincible argument against the Pelagians. For there is no one who does not most truly recite the Lord's Prayer, and even these very words. Therefore, there is no one who is not a sinner.), we rightly conclude against the Papists: 1. That the blessed ones who are reborn in this life are not perfect, nor pure from every stain of adhering sin. Contrary to what Ruard Tapper at Louvain, article 8 on Justification, Bellarmine, book 4 on Justification, chapter 10, § 'Secondly', etc., and some others assert. 2. Nor are sins in this life, even while they are perfectly remitted by God, so blotted out that no remnants of them remain surviving in the flesh. 3. Nor was the Blessed Virgin, the Mother of God, conceived without original sin, a thing which the Jesuit Conzen himself, which is to be well observed, against the common opinion of his associates (See Bellarmine, book 4 on the loss of grace, chapter 15; Suarez on Thomas, part 3, question 27, article 1; Coster in Christian Institutions, book 5; Pererius, who in Disputation 6 on chapter 3 of Romans does not fear to write, It is certain in the Catholic Church that the Blessed Virgin was free from every sin, even the lightest and smallest, throughout her whole life. Add Corn. à Lap. on Luke p. 25, l. c. Gravina c. 16. Curr, Triumph. p. 108, and others.) He undoubtedly concedes this, since to the question: Whether there is any man who has never had any sin, he responds in this place on p. 121 b, together with Augustine, that there has been none, is none, and will be none, except for CHRIST alone, since all have been born in sin. Nor, however, does it follow from the fact that we are commanded to ask daily for the remission of sins that Christ satisfied only for the guilt of sins, and not indeed for all the punishments of the same, which is what the Pontiffs teach, as can be seen in Bell. l. 4 de poenit. c. 2 § 4, Greg. de Valent. t. 2 in Thom. Disp. 6 q 17 punct. 5, and others. But we ask for the relaxation of both guilt and punishment. Even the just man, writes Conzen in this place on p. 142 a, always says: forgive us our debts, namely sin and the punishment of sin, nor does it follow from this that Christ did not satisfy for them plenarily: for he distinguishes between acquisition and application: nor are subordinated things to be opposed to one another. But someone might say: If in the Lord's Prayer we ask that God remit our sins to us, just as we remit them to our debtors, it follows that our sins are not remitted to us gratuitously, namely on account of Christ's satisfaction, but that we merit that by our own forgiveness. Resp. by denying the consequence. Cardinal Toletus correctly says in c. 11 Luc. p. 653, When we ask that debts be forgiven, we ask that sins be blotted out and taken away from us, gratuitously indeed and without price with respect to us, but not with respect to Christ, who paid the price for our sins. But someone might insist, that the particle sicut (as) nevertheless signifies that there is also on our part some impulsive or meritorious cause, by which we effect or merit that God should remit our sins to us. Resp. The particle ὅτι in this place is not τροπογικὴ, showing the manner and rule which God follows in remitting sins: for we ask that much more be remitted to us by GOD than others owe to us, as Corn. à Lap. well advises in this place. Nor is it αἰτιολογικὴ causal. Since we are justified freely, without any merit of our works, as Holy Scripture testifies everywhere (whence also the Jesuit Tirinus not badly notes at this place: pray against the evils which can delay you from obtaining such great goods. First, sins, so that they may be forgiven you by the merits of Christ. If sins are forgiven by the merits of Christ, we do not merit their remission by our works.) But συμπλεκτικὴ is a connecting member with the antecedent, and at the same time including a condition, which God wills to be observed by us. He clearly joined, writes Cyprian in sermon 6 on the Lord's Prayer, p. 239, and added a law, binding us with a certain condition and promise, that we should thus ask for our debts to be forgiven us, according to how we also forgive our debtors. Our Savior also insinuates the same elsewhere, as Matth. 7, 2. Matth. cap. 18, 32. following Marc. 11, 25. 26. But again someone might urge: therefore the promises of the Gospel are conditional, which the Papists teach everywhere, but our people deny. Resp. The controversy between us and the Papists is about a causal and meritorious condition, which precedes divine mercy and moves God, or even merits, that He should remit our sins to us. Here, however, it is a matter of such a condition by which men are bound, lest after God has freely, through and on account of the merit of Christ and that alone, remitted to them that huge debt of sins, they themselves abuse such a great benefit, as a privilege of baseness and license. Therefore, Christ, by adding this clause, binds the purpose of those praying as if by a public and solemn condition and promise, that they wish in the future to avoid sins, to amend their life, and to forgive the offenses of their neighbor, as the example proposed by Christ in Matthew 18 clearly declares this. Consult entirely here B. D. Chenin. in H. E. c. 51 p. 458. In sum, it is one thing to ask about a condition by which we might merit the remission of sins before God or upon which God might suspend the remission of sins and His grace; it is another thing about that which might incite God, so that He might withdraw and retract the benefit of remission freely made. The discourse, therefore, is not about the meritorious cause of remission, but about the mark of remission before God, about the quality of the object, and finally about the removal of the impediment to obtaining remission. See B. Par. Co-. in Prior. ep. Petri p. 640.)*

*( Μὴ εἰσενέγκης εἰς πειρασόν. do not lead us. i. e. do not permit us to be led. For the temptation of the Devil is understood here, Matth. 4, 3.1. Thess. 3, 5. and of the corrupt flesh or evil concupiscence, Iac. 1, 14. we ask to be delivered from this temptation. Compare 1. Cor. 10, 13 That indeed active verbs in the Holy Scripture are sometimes to be understood concerning permission, the Blessed D. Glassius teaches in Gr. S. book 3, p. 256 and 257, by way of example, among other things, he brings forward the following sayings, Iob. 1, 21.Ps. 119, 31.Es. 63, 17.Ier. 15, 15.Ioh. 6, 39.1 Cor. 6, 7.)*

*( Μὴ εἰσενέγκης εἰς πειρασόν. Lud. Capellus in Spic. on this passage reports a similar petition of the Jews from the Seder Tephilloth. Lest anyone should gather from this passage as if God were the cause of sin, when we pray here that He may not lead us into temptation, the passage Iacob 1, 14. must be compared entirely. Therefore, the active verb must be explained here permissively. How it is also used elsewhere. Compare Rom. 1, 24. with Act. 14, 16. also Deut. 28, 28. with Hos. 4, 16. 17. How therefore God concurs to temptation, these sayings teach Ps. 81, 13.1. Cor. 10, 13. Saint Augustine beautifully in tract 43 on John There are two temptations, one which deceives, the other which proves. According to that which deceives, God tempts no one. According to that which proves, the Lord your God tempts you, that He may know if you love Him. Let the same be compared in ep. 146. James chapter 1, 13 deals with the former temptation, and so also the word to tempt is taken for solicitation to evil, Matth. 4, 1. In the latter way it is taken Gen. 22, 1.Deut. 8, 2.Deut. c. 13, 3. God tempts us to good, and this is the temptation of probation. Conversely, the Devil, the world, and our flesh tempt us to evil, and this is the temptation of deception, perdition, and seduction. We pray therefore in the present petition, that the Heavenly Father may not permit us to the power and lust of Satan, nor allow that that enemy of the human race should cast us by his temptation either into sin or into desperation; but rather that He may protect us with His powerful right hand. Compare more in B. Par. Co-. in Deut. p. 800. also in Aphor. Pract. title Temptations, and also B. D. Ronig Cas. Consc. Case 8.)*

Aug. in Psalm 6. It is not expedient for us to be without temptations, nor do we ask God that we may not be tempted, but that we may not be led into temptation.

Peccata dicuntur debita, quia reddunt nos Deo debitores ad poenam. *(Collectionem inter peccata & debita instituit Dn. Dilh. Ecl; Syr. p. 56.)*

*(Ex eo, quòd etiam sanctissimi quique in Oratione Dominicâ debitorum ie. peccatorum remissionem pro se, ac verissimè quidem, non solùm humiliter petere debent, (quemadmod. contra Pelagii ac Coelestii haeresin pridem evicit malleus haereticorum S. Augustinus in de pecc. meritis & remiss. 1. 2. c. 5. seqq. it. ep. 108. nec non in Enchir. c. 73. Unde etiam rectè h. 1. Iesuita Conzen scribit: Invictum sunè contra Pelagianos est argumentum. Nemo enim est, qui non verissimè orationerm Dominicam, adeo3 haec ipsa verba recitet. Nemo igitur non peccator.) rectè contrà Pontificios concludimus 1. B.
