*( Ostende teipsum Sacerdoti. Ita, in singulari nempe, constanter habent Codd. Graeci. Arabs quoque & Aethiops, nec non Vulgatus Latinus: Syrus tamen (consentiente cum reliquis Codd. tum MSS. tum excusis antiquisimo Codice Acad. Altdorff.) in pl. numero habet adductus fortè, quia, morsequitur pluralis, in testimonium illis. Syrum sequitur more suo Persa. Pontificii porrò ex h. l confessionis auricularis necessitatē ita ferè colligūt. Si Sacerdotum in V. T. officium fuit iudicare de lepra. Peccata vero sunt spiritualis lepra, sequitur quòd Sacerdotes N. T. de peccatis iudicare debeant. Iam verò non nisi de cognitis possunt iudicare Ergò si de peccatis iudicare ac hominē ab illis absolvere debent, necesse est, ut praecedat specialis peccatorum enumeratio. Vid. Cornel. à Lapide in h. l. Bell. l. 3 de poenit. c. 2. Costerus Enchir. Controv. pag. 484. Stapletonus in promt. Cath. Dom. 3. post Epiph. Tirinus Ind controv. s-die controv. XXIII. n. 7. & alii. Resp. 1. neg. conseq. Concedimus quidē, quòd inter lepram & peccata sit similitudo aliqua (quemadmodum etiam ipsi nostrates passim ostendunt. Vid. B. D. Glassius Exeg. Dom. 14. Trin. B. Par. Hom. Acad. part. 2. p. 640. 6 6. seqq. B. D. Botsaccus Promt. Alleg. p. 162. & p. 158. M. Binchius part. 2 Mellif. p. 284. cumprimis verò B. Dn. Chemn in Harm. Ev. super h. l.) sed negatur, quòd ratione omnium par ratio sit: sequeretur enim, quòd sicuti leprâ aedes quoque ac vesses inficiebantur, ita eaedem peccatis maculentur, & à Ministris Ecclesia mundari ab his necesse habeant, ceu illae apud Israelitas: fequeretur etiam, quòd quemadmodum lepra tantùm corpus immundum reddebat, non animam, ita nec hanc peccatum. Deinde nec par quoad omnia ratio etiam est Sacerdotum V. ac Minist. Eccl. N. T. sequeretur enim, quòd uti in V. T. Sacerdotes fuerūt uxoran, ita & in N. T. matrimonium Minist. Eccl. possint inire, quod ramen Pontificii acerrimè negant. Sequeretur etiam, quòd fieuti Sacerd. in V. T. leprosos non fecerunt mundos, sed saltem mundos pronunciarunt, ita & in N. T. Minist. Ecclesiae peccatores saltem mundos pronuncient, non verò tales faciant. Hoc verò negant Pontificii. Inde Corn. à Lap. in h. l. Chrysostomus l. 3. de Sacerd. docet, officium Sacerdotum Christianorum longè efficacius & praestantius esse, quàm olim fuerit Aaronicorum, eò quòd hisce lepram non curare, sed curatam duntaxat ostendere; illis verò peccata non curata ostendere, sed verè curare & condonare concessum sit. Si igitur praestantior ratio Sacerdotum N. T. prae Sacerd. V. T. in eo est, quòd peccata etiam condonare possint, cur non etiam eat, differētia inter hos illosq; conceditur, quòd licet illis, V. T. Sacer dotibus, necessarium fuerit, leprosum priùs videre, adeoque leprā antè accurate cognoscere, quàm ut de eo pronunciarent: quoad hos N. T. Sacerdotes tale quid necessarium non sit, cumprimis quoniam nec Christus unquam talem pecc. enumerationem ante pecc. remissionem ex egit, vid. Matth. 9, 2.Luc. 7, 48.c. 15, 18.c. 19, 8. nec in primitiva Ecclesia, Apostolicae vicina talis fuit requisita. -. neg. quòd Ministri Ecclesiae N. T. propriè ac specialiter sint Sacerdotes, imò potiùs omnia V. T. Sacerdotia ad solum Christum sunt translata inq; eo finita. it. quòd si ad ipsos spectat, de peccatis iudicare, ad eosdem quoque pertineat, hominum conscientias, omnium peccatorum confessionem requirendo, excarnificare. 3. urgemus illud Bell. l. 3. de V. D. c. 3. §. sed quanquam, quòd ex solo sensu litter ali peti dibeant argumenta firma. itemq; illud Ludovici ab Alcasar ex Dronysio, quòd Theologia symbola (ac typica) non sit argumentativa. Iam verò haec collectio procedit saltem à typo. Unde etiam Iefuita Conzenius in h. l. graviter invehitur in Calvinum ac Bullingerum, Pontificns tribuentes, quòd ex h. l. confessionem auricularem probent. Nos verò, scribit, nequaquam ex eo iudicio confessionem auricularem probamus; sed multi Catholicorum comparatione ista confessionis usum exponunt. Et paulò post: Explicatio est à simili, non probatio contra contumaces. Similia quoque habet Iesuita Alphonsus à Castro l. 4. adversus haereses verbo Confessio. Nobis sufficit in praesens, ostendisfe, quòd ex h. l. Confessionis auricularis (h. e. ut omnia peccata sig: llatim Sacerdotibus detegantur, iuxta explicationem Bell. l. 3. de Poen. c. 9. § Habemus) absoluta necessitas solidè probari non possit. Conf. pluribus de hâc re B. D. Helvicus vind. LL. SS. V. T. P. 150. & 151 B. P. Conf. Cath. t. 4 p. 62.)*

## 8:5
v. 5. August. lib. 33. contra Faustum cap. 7. He approached Jesus not by the presence of the body, but by the power of faith. In this way he reconciles what Matthew says, that the Centurion approached, but Luke, that he besought Christ through messengers. For in common usage of speech, he who arranges for things to be said or done through envoys is said to do or say them himself. It could also have happened that he first besought Christ through envoys and friends, and afterwards approached himself, which is the opinion of Theophylact and Gerson. Piscator maintains that this history is different from that which Luke narrates cap. 7. v. 1., in which part he follows Osiander in his Harmony, who also denies that the sermon which Matthew cap. 5. begins is the same as that which Luke c. 6 describes. From Luc. 7. v. 7. it seems to be firmly gathered that this Centurion did not approach Christ himself, for he says: I did not judge myself worthy to come into your sight. Therefore, Augustine's reconciliation is to be preferred. lib. 2. de consens. Evang cap. 20. that Matthew studied brevity, and assigned only the principal chapters of this history, but Luke described it more fully and with all circumstances applied, how the Centurion approached, namely through envoys, but it is referred to him because what one does through a friend, he may seem to do by himself. Similar examples Matth. 11, v. 2. 3. Luc. 7. v. 19. Matth. 26. v. 18. Marc. 14. v. 14. Luc. 22. v. 11.

*(The opinion of Theophylact and Gerson, which is also that of Chrysostom hom. 26, as well as Euthymius in this place, is embraced by the Glossators of the Ernestine Bibles, also Mr. Dr. Walther in Harm. Bibl. p. 759, and among the Papists, Corn. à Lapide, Tirinus, Conzen. But the exposition of Augustine, which Bede also has, as well as Leontius in this place, pleases Hugo Grotius in this place, who also refers here that we are said to ροσέρχεσθαι to GOD Ebr. 4, 16. c. 7, 25. c. 10, 22. c. 11, 6. and that ροσέλευσις is taken for a suppliant petition. The same also pleases the Blessed Dr. Hunnius and among the Papists, Francisco Luca, Maldonado, and others. Nor do those words stand in the way: Lord, I am not worthy, v. 8.

for I also am a man. v. 9. For if he who approaches through some other person is said to have approached, even he who answers through another can be said to have answered himself. But how, if the Jews spoke these words to Christ: I am not worthy, etc. and thus asked that he not come, do they nevertheless in Luke c. 7, 3. solicit Jesus to come to the Centurion? Maldonado answers that the elders of the Jews added this of their own, just as the remaining words which are had in v. 4. in Luke. For that they went beyond the bounds of their commission, the same man thinks is evident from the fact that the Centurion afterwards, through others, namely friends or acquaintances, and indeed Gentiles, as the Jesuit suspects, sent and better instructed, caused Christ to be addressed with other words, which are read in v. 6. 7. 8.. But concerning these, more prolixly at Luke c. 7. Furthermore, from the fact that the Centurion used the intercession of the Jews here before Christ, the Papists gather the invocation of the saints, as they call them, who are dead. See Censura Colon. p 209. Eccius in Enchir. Salmeron. t. 6. tr. 23. p. 150. If, writes the Jesuit Conzenius in this place, quest. 1, the living pray for the living, therefore the dead in the Lord also pray, and therefore they are living to the Lord. They can, because they see God present and are loved by Him. They want to, because they love us. For blessedness does not diminish charity, but has increased it, by the very fact that it has made it secure. Resp. 1. It is not asked, whether the dead saints in general intercede for us, for this very thing is conceded in express words in the Apology of the Augsburg Confession, Chapter on the Invocation of Saints, and in the Smalcald Articles, part 3, on the Invocation of Saints, p. 310. The Orthodox have these things: Although the saints on earth, and perhaps also in heaven, may pray for us, yet it does not follow from that that the saints are to be invoked by us, adored, honored with fasts, holidays, Masses, etc. (which the Papists teach and do). Therefore, even if the Papists could prove it from this place (as Conzenius himself finally admits, that at least this is proven from here, that the saints in general care for our affairs, and therefore in general at least pray for our affairs.) which we deny can be proven from here by any firm consequence: yet that idolatrous invocation of dead saints, such as is in use among the Papists, would by no means be established from this. 2. The corpse of the consequence is: The Centurion called upon the living to plead his cause before Christ. Therefore, we can do this same thing through the dead. Concerning the living, we are certain that our calamity in

Let them know by species let them understand when we explain it to them. But who will render me certain that the departed saints are certain, or can become certain, of those things which trouble me? Conzenius indeed says, to see those anguishes of ours, yet soon after, as if correcting himself, he adds, when, how often, and how much God shall have shown. But from where or from what oracles of the Holy Scripture will the Jesuit prove that God wills to show our anguishes to those who have died in blessedness? Indeed, Conzenius himself seems to have hesitated concerning this manner of manifesting, whence he adds: they hear how often from those coming to them from us. Therefore, our anguishes are to be entrusted to those now about to die, and they themselves are to be asked to report them to those saints whom we wish to help us with their prayers before God. Why do the Papists not rather ask those very ones who are about to breathe out their soul, that they immediately expose their own anguishes to GOD? But from where, I ask, and from whom has the Jesuit heard that the blessed inhabitants of heaven, whether from the dead or from the Angels, whom he himself likewise appointed as intermediaries, perceive what calamity presses upon this or that person? Certainly, nowhere in the Holy Scripture is such a ministry of Angels commemorated, nowhere is such a thing concerning the dead handed down. 3. If it could be gathered from the fact that the Centurion sought help from Christ through interpreters, that for the same reason God can also be solicited through the dead, it would follow that even gentile dead and those who are tormented in hell could be invoked to be our intermediaries before God, since the Centurion approached Christ not only through Jews, but also through friends, i.e., acquaintances Luc. 7. 6. whom the Jesuit Maldonatus in this place, p. 180, judges it credible to have been gentiles. 4. Finally, not even a little word is made here that the Centurion used the work or intercession of others because he relied on their merits. And yet this is the principal reason for which the Papists invoke the holy dead. Let it be compared at greater length in B. P. Conf Cath. l. 2. special. part. 2. art. 10. C. 2. L. de Morte §. 370, seqq. as well as B. D. Himmelius, D. Ioh. Iac. Bernhardi and others who professedly impugn the religious invocation of the saints.)

Latin:

v. 5. August. lib. 33. contra Faustum cap. 7. Accessit ad Iesum non corporis praesentia, sed fidei potentia. Hoc modo conciliat, quod Matthaeus dicit Centurionem accessisse, Lucas verò, quòd per internuncios Christum compellaverit. Quae enim qui per Legatos dici vel geri curat, ea ipsemet gerere vel dicere vulgatâ loquendi consuetudine dicitur. Fieri etiam potuit, ut priùs per Legatos & amicos Christum compellaverit, postea ipsemet accesserit, quae est Theoph. & Gersonis sententia. Piscator statuit, hanc Historiam esse diversam ab ea, quam narrat Lucascap. 7. v. 1. quâ in parte sequitur Osiandrum in Harmon, qui etiam negat, concionem, quam Matthaeus cap. 5. exorditur, esse eandem cum ea, quam Lucas c. 6 describit. Ex Luc. 7. v. 7. videtur firmiter colligi. quòd hic Centurio non ipsemet Christum accesserit, dicit enim: Non iudicavi me dignum, ut in conspectum tuum prodirem. Praeferenda igitur Augustini conciliatio. lib. 2. de consens. Evang cap. 20. M--thaeum brevitati studuisse, ac praecipua tantùm huius Historiae capita assignasse, Lucam verò plenius & omnibus adhibit is circumstant iis eam descripsisse, quomodo Centurio accesserit, videlicet per Legatos, referri autem ad ipsum quia quod quis per amicum agat, per seipsum agere videatur. Similia exempla Matth. 11, v. 2. 3.Luc. 7. v. 19.Matth. 26. v. 18.Marc. 14. v. 14.Luc. 22. v. 11.

*(Theophylacti & Gersonis sententiam, quae etiam Chrysostomi est hom. 26. nec non Euthymii in h. l. amplectuntur Glossatores Bibliorum Ernestinorum, item Dn. D. Waltherus in Harm. Bibl. p. 759. & ex Pontificiis Corn. à Lapide, Tirinus, Conzen. Augustini verò expositio, quam & Beda habet, nec non Leontius in h. l. arridet Hugoni Grotio in h. l. qui etiam huc refert, quòd DEO ροσέρχεσθαι dicamur Ebr. 4, 16.c. 7, 25.c. 10, 22.c. 11, 6. & quòd ροσέλευσις pro libello supplice sumatur. Eadem placet quoq; B. D. Hunnio & ex Pontificiis Francisco Lucae, Maldonato, aliis. Nec obstant illa verba: Domine non sum dignus,v. 8.

nam & ego homo sum.v. 9. Si enim ille, qui per alium aliquem accedit, accessisse dicitur etiam is, qui per alium respondet, ipse respondisse dici potest. Sed quî, si Iudaei ad Christum verba haec: Non sum dignus &c. prolocuti sunt, adeoque rogarant qs. ne veniat: iisdem tamen apud Lucam c. 7, 3. sollicitant Iesum, ad Centurionem ut veniat? Respondet Maldonatus, Iudaeorum seniores de suo hoc addidisse, quemadmodum & reliqua verba, quae v. 4. apud Lucam habentur. Quòd enim mandati fines egressi illi fuerint, inde constare putat idem, quòd Centurio posteà per alios, nempe amicosive familiares, & quidem gentiles, ut suspicatur Iesuita, submissos meliùs que instructos, aliis verbis, quae v. 6. 7. 8. leguntur, Christum alloqui fecerit. Sed de his prolixiùs ad Lucae c. 7. Porrò ex eo, quòd Centurio intercessione Iudaeorum hîc apud Christum usus est, colligunt Pontificii invocationem fanctorum, quos vocant, defunctorum. Vid. Censura Colon. p 209. Eccius in Enchir. Salmeron. t. 6. tr. 23. p. 150. Si, Scribit Iesuita Conzenius in h. l. quaest. 1. viventes pro viventibus orant, orant igitur & in Domino mortus, ideoq; Domino viventes. Possunt, quia Deum vident praesentem & ab eo amantur. Volunt, quia nos diligunt. Caritatens enim beatitudo non minuit, sed auxit, hoc ipso quod tutam fecit. Resp. 1. non quaeritur, an sancti defuncti in genere pro nobis intercedant, hoc ipsum enim disertis verbis in Apolog. August. Confess C. de Invoc. Sanct. conceditur. & in Artic. Smalcald. part. 3. de Invocat. Sanct. p. 310. Orthodoxi haec habent: Etsi sancti in terris, & fortassè etiam coelis pro nobis orent, tamē inde non sequitur, sanctos à nobis esse invocandos, adorandos, ieiuniis, feriis, Missis &c. honorandos. (id quod Pontificii docēt ac faciunt.) Itaque si vel maximè ex h. l. evincere possent Pontificii (ceu Conrenius ipse tandem fatetur, id saltem hinc evinci, sanctos generatim res nostras curare, ideoq; generatim saltem or are prorebus nostris.) quod tamen hinc evinci ullâ firma sequela posse, negamus: minimè tamen hinc stabiliretur idololatrica illa, qualis apud Pontificios in usu est, sanctorum defunctorum invocatio. 2. cadaver consequentiae est: Centurio viventes compellavit, ut suam apud Christum causam agant. E. idem hoc per defunctos agere possusmus. De viventibus certi sumus, quòd calamitatem nostram in

Specie sciant intelligant-;, quando illis eam exponimus. Sed quis me reddet certum, quòd sancti defuncti de iis, quae me angunt, certi sint, vel fieri possint? Dicit quidem Conzenius, illos videre angores nostros, mox tamen qs. seipsum corrigens addit, quando, quot & quantum Deus ostenderit. at unde aut quibus Sc. S. oraculis probabit Iesuita, quòd Deus beatè defunctis velit angores nostros ostendere? Sanè ipse Conzenius circa hunc manifestandi modum haesisse videtur, unde subdit: audiunt quot idiè à venientibus à nobis ad ipsos. Itaque iamiam morituris committendi sunt angores nostri, rogandique ipsi, ut sanctis illis referant, quos precibus nos suis apud Deum iuvare volumus. Cur non potiùs ipsos illos, qui mox animam exhalaturi, rogant Pontificii, ut immediatangores suos DEO exponant? Unde verò quaeso, & à quibus inaudiit Iesuita, quòd beati coelites sive à defunctis s. ab Angelis, quos itidem internun cios ipse constituit, percipiant, quae hunc vel istum calamitas premat. Certè nullibi in Sc. S. tale Angelorum ministerium commemoratur, nullibi tale quid dedefunctis traditur. 3. Si exinde, quòd Centurio per interpretes auxilium à Christo petiit, colligi posset, eadem ratione & per defunctos sollicitari Deum posse, sequeretur, etiam gentiles defunctos & qui in inferno cruciantur, invocari posse, ut intenuncii nostri apud Deum sint, cùm Centurio non solùm per Iudaeos, sed etiam per amicos s. familiares Luc. 7. 6. quos Iesuita Maldonatus in h. l. p. 180. gentiles fuisse, credibile censet, Christum accesserit. 4. Denique ne verbulo quidem hîc fit mentio, quòd propterea aliorum operâ vel intercessione usus fuerit Centurio, quòd meritis eorum niteretur. Et haec tamen praecipua ratio est, ob quam Pontificii sanctos defunctos invocant. Conferatur pluribus B. P. Conf Cath. l. 2. special. part. 2. art. 10. C. 2. L. de Morte §. 370, seqq. nec non B. D. Him melius, D. Ioh. Iac. Bernhardi aliique qui ex professo religiosam sanctorum in vocationem impugnatunt.)*

## 8:6
*(v. 6. My boy, i. e. my servant, as B. D. Luther excellently rendered. And it is known that among the Hebrews נער is a name as much for --visterii, as for age. See Gen. 41, 12.Exod. 33, 11.2. Reg. 4, 12. thus also the word παῖς is used Luc. 12, 45. and παιδίσκη ibid. and Gal. 4, 22.30. but especially τοῖς ό is very solemn, d. m.

name παῖς to employ, as among other things is to be seen from Gen. 22, 3.5. 19.cap. 49. 35.1. Sam. 25, 8.1. Reg. 20, 15. etc. And the Oriental interpreters, the Syrian, Arab, and Persian, imitated this mode of speaking in this place, by which boy is put for servant. The Ethiopian employs the name which most commonly and properly denotes son, for it descends from i.e. he begat. But there is no doubt that here by the name of boy a servant is indicated, as Luke also explicitly indicates, while in the account of the same history he employs the name Whence also the Ethiopian, although in v. 8. he employs the same name : yet in verse 13 he uses the word which signifies minister.

Εέβληται is not simply he lies, but he lies prostrate with his whole body, relaxed in his limbs and exhausted of strength, which happens in serious diseases.

Δεινῶς βασανιζόμενος grievously tormented. v. 29. following, it is used concerning infernal torments, as also in Luc. 16. v. 23. Elsewhere it is used concerning the tortures and torments which are employed in the questionings and punishments of the accused. See above cap. 4. v. 24. Some think it was ἡμιπληγίαν, but since that at the same time takes away sense and motion in those limbs which are infested, but this sick man is said to feel most bitter pains not only in the beginning, but also then when the Centurion was interceding for him, so that he was at the point of death, therefore we determine it to have been paralysis properly so called.

*(Hugo Grotius says it is credible, ράλυσιν that here is meant not the resolution of a part, but of the whole body, ἀποπληχίαν namely: and that Celsus teaches that this was also called so in his time. Certainly also by Aretaeus in the book on the causes and signs of diseases, chapter 7, apoplexy is defined by paralysis: and the most noble Lord D. Rolefincius teaches in the Epitome of the knowledge of diseases and the particular affections of the body to be cured, book 1, part 1, chapter 4, page 19, that ἀποπληχία is an acute disease, ἀκρίβῶς καὶ ἐχάτως it is terminated to death by suffocation; to health by paralysis. The same also notes from Hippocrates, 2. aphor. 41, λύειν But that this disease cannot be established as apoplexy, the things just brought forward stand in the way.)*

*( Δεινῶς βασανιζόμενος. See here the blessed D. Chemnitius, Harmony of the Gospels, chapter 53, page 529.)*

Latin:

*(v. 6. Puer meus, i. e. servus meus, uti B. D. Lutherus opumè reddidit. Notumque est, quòd apud Ebraeos נער sit tam --visterii, quàm aetatis nomen. Vid. Gen. 41, 12.Exod. 33, 11.2. Reg. 4, 12. sic quoq; vox παῖς adhibetur Luc. 12, 45. & παιδίσκη ibid. ac Gal. 4, 22.30. cumprimis verò τοῖς ό admodùm solenne est, d. m.

nomen παῖς adhibere, ceu inter alia videre est ex Gen. 22, 3.5. 19.cap. 49. 35.1. Sam. 25, 8.1. Reg. 20, 15. &c. Atque hunc loquendi modū, quo puer pro servo ponitur, imitati h. l. sunt Interpp. Orientales, Syrus, Arabs & Persa Aethiops adhibet nomen quod communissimè ac propriè filium notat, descendit enim à i e. genuit. Sed non est dubium, quin hîc pueri nomine servus indicetur, ceu Lucas etiam disertè indicat, dum in eiusdem historiae relatione adhibet nomen Unde etiam Aethiops, licet v. 8. idem nomen adhibeat: versu tamen 13 utitur voce quae ministrum significat.)*

Εέβληται non est simpliciter iacet, sed toto corpore prostratus iacet, membris resolutus & viribus exhaustus, quod in gravibus morbis accidit.

Δεινῶς βασανιζόμενοςgraviter discruciatus.v. 29. seq. de infernalibus cruciatibus usurpatur, uti etiam Luc. 16. v. 23. Alibi usupatur de cruciatibus & tormentis quae in quaestionibus & suppliciis reorum adhibentur. Vide superiùs cap. 4. v. 24. Quidam putant fuisse ἡμιπληγίαν, sed cùm illa simul auferat sensum & motum in membris illis, quae infestantur, aegrotus verò hic dicatur acerbissimos dolores non tantùm in principio, sed etiam tunc cum Centurio pro ipso intercederet, sentire, ita ut in extremis haereat, ideò paralysin propriè dictam fuisse statuimus.

*(Hugo Grotius, credibile esse dicit, ράλυσινhîc dici non partis, sed totius corporis resolutionem,ἀποπληχίανscilicet: & ita quoq; suo tempore hanc dictam fuisse, Celsum docere. Sanè & ab Aretaeo l. de causis & signis div. cap. 7. Apoplexia per paralysin definitur: docetque Nobiliss. Dn. D. Rolefincius in Epit. Cognosc. morbos & curandi particulares corporis affectus, l. 1. part. l. c. 4. p. 19. quòd ἀποπληχία acutus morbus sit, ἀκρίβῶς καὶ ἐχάτως terminetur ad mortem suffocatione; ad salutem paralysi. Idem etiam ex Hippocr. 2. aphor. 41. notat, λύειν Sed quò minùs apoplexia morbus hic statui possit, obstant modò adducta.)*

*( Δεινῶς βασανιζόμενος. Vid. hîc B. D. Chemnitius Harm. Evang. c. 53. p. 529.)*

## 8:7
v. 7. ChristJohn 4, 49.refused to go to the son of the Nobleman, but here he promises that he will go to the servant of the Centurion. The Author of the imperfect work chap. 22. & Bede in this place reconcile it thus, that the former was denied, lest he should seem to give something to royal magnificence & preeminence, the latter was promised, lest he should seem to despise a servile condition. *(The same reason is also brought forward in the Ernestine Bibles)* Aug. in John There it was yielded to pride, here it was granted to humility. Ibid. When Christ was not asked to go, he promised to go, & again to the Nobleman asking for his son he did not say, I will come, but go, your son lives: here, not asked, he promised to go, lest he should seem to despise the humility of a servant. Chrysost. hom 22. imperfect work He despised him, whom the dignity of the Nobleman lifted up: he honored this one, whom a servile condition humbled. Tostatus however thinks, that the Jews asked for more than they had in their instructions, since the Centurion removes all dignity from himself, but the elders attribute the same to him.

Θεραπεύειν properly is to care for, just as Physicians, with medicine applied, that is, but here καταχρηςικῶς is put for ἰᾶσθαι Pisc. in Seh.

Latin:

v. 7. ChristusIoh. 4, 49.noluit accedere ad filium Reguli, hic autem pollicetur, ad servum Centurionis se accessurum. Id Au or imperf. oper. cap. 22. & Beda h. l. sic conciliant, illud fuisse denegatum, ne regiae magnificentiae & praeeminentiae aliquid darevideratur, hoc fuisse promissum, ne servilem conditionem spernere videretur. *(Eadem ratio affertur quoque in Bibliis Ernestinis)* Aug. in Ioh. Illic cessum est elationi, hîc concessum humilitati. Ibid. Cum non peteretur Christus ut iret, promisit se ire, & rursus Regulo postulanti pro filio non dixit, ego veniam, sed vaniam, sed vade, filius tuus vivit: hic non rogatus promisit ireine videatur humilitatem servi contemnere. Chrysost. hom 22. oper. imperf. Illum contemsit, quem dignitas sublevabat Regulis: istum honoravit, quem conditio humiliavat servilis. Tostatus autem existimat, Iudaeos plus rogasse, quàm in mandatis habuerint, cùm Centurio omnem dignitatem à se removeat, seniores autem eaendem illi tribuant.

Θεραπεύειν propriè est ita curare, sicut Medici, adhibltâ sc. medicina, sed hîc ponitur καταχρηςικῶς pro ἰᾶσθαι Pisc. in Seh.

## 8:8
v. 8. Lyranus thinks; that he had idols at home, & therefore did not want Christ to enter: but he is refuted by Abulensis & Salmer. because it is not likely that he, in whom there is such great faith, should have idols at home. But it could have happened that he did not immediately cast away certain idols, although then, when he believed, he was not a worshiper of idols. Aug. on the words of the Lord. By saying he was unworthy, he showed himself worthy, not into whose walls, but into whose heart Christ would enter* (See Eph. 3, 17.)* nor indeed would he say this with such great faith & humility, unless he carried in his heart him, whom he was afraid to enter into his house: for it would not be a great happiness, if Jesus entered into his walls, & was not in his breast.

*( Worthy. in Gr. is ἱκανὸς, which properly sounds sufficient. But here it is used in the same way, as also above c. 3, 11. just as also elsewhere in the books of the new covenant. See Mark 1, 7.Luke 3, 16. (John in the parallel place c. 1, 27. uses /ἄξιος ). 1. Cor. 15, 9. and in this way also the Apostle uses the verb ἱκανόω Col. 1, 12. Furthermore, similar examples of the acknowledgment of one's own unworthiness are had Gen. 32, 10.Luke 15, 19. Moreover, from the fact that the Centurion professes himself unworthy of the presence of the Lord, the Jesuit Costerus gathers p. 264. Enchir. Controv. that there is need for preparation for justification, and that faith alone does not suffice. Respond.

The question is not: whether the justified ought to pursue Good Works. For we by no means deny this. nor do we assert that those who indulge in sins against knowledge and conscience, and do not perform serious repentance, are justified, but this is in question, whether justification is to be ascribed to faith alone on our part, which we assert. Nor does this passage help the Papists, since by it the pride of their own works is rather overturned, which the Papists teach to be necessary for justification & salvation, and join causally with faith. For if Christ praised the faith of the Centurion because he himself judged himself unworthy of the approach of Christ, how much more will he turn away from the pride of those who vainly persuade themselves that they can merit justification by their own proper works and are proud of their own dignity.)*

Latin:

v. 8. Lyranus existimat; eum domi habuisse simulachra, & ideo noluisse Christum ingredi: sed refellitur ab Abulense & Salmer. quod non sit verisimile, eum in quo tanta est fides, domui habuis. se simulachra. At fieri potuit, ut quaedam idola non starim abiecerit, licet tune, cùm credidit, non fuerit simula chrorū cultor. Aug. de verb. Dom. Dicendo se indignum, praestit it se dignum, non in cuius parietes, sed in cuius intraret cor Christus* (Vid. Eph. 3, 17.)* nec enim hoc diceret cum tantâ fide & humilitate, nisi illum, quem --mebat intrare in domum suam, corde gestaret: nam non erat magna felicitas, si Iesus intraret in parietes eius, & non esset in pectore eius.

*( Dignus. in Gr. est ἱκανὸς, quod propriè sonat sufficient. Sed hîc d. m. adhibetur, uti etiam suprà c. 3, 11. quemadmodum & alibi in novi foederis tabulis. Vid. Marc. 1, 7.Luc. 3, 16. (Ioh. inloco parall. c. 1, 27. adhibet /ἄξιος). 1. Cor. 15, 9. atque h m. etiam Apostolus utitur verbo ἱκανόωCol. 1, 12. Caeterùm fimilia agnitionis propriae indignitatis exempla habentur Gen. 32, 10.Luc. 15, 19. Porrò ex eo, quod Centurio se indignum profiretur prasentiâ Domini, colligit Iesuita Costerus p. 264. Enchir. Controv. opus esse ad iustificationem praeparatione, ac non sufficere solam fidem. Respond.

Non est quaestio: an iustificati B. O. studere debeant. Hoc enim minimè negamus. nec adserimus etiam, illos qui peccatis contra scientiam ac conscientiam indulgent, nec seriam agunt poenitentiam, iustificari, sed hoc in quaestione est, an soli fidei exparte nostra adscribenda sit iustificatio, quod adserimus. Nec iuvat Pontificios hic locus, quippe quo potiùs evertitur fastus proprioroperum, quae ad iustificationem & salutem necessaria esse Pontificii docent, ac cum fide causaliter coniungunt. Si enim Christus laudavit fidem Centurionis eò quòd indignum se ipse censeret Christi accessu, quantò magis aversabitur illorum superbiam, qui suis operibus propriis promereri se iustificationem posse, vanè sibi persuadent ac depropriâ dignitate superbiunt.)*

## 8:9
v. 9. The author of the imperfect work, homily 22, thinks Christ argued from a similarity. Aug. sermon 6 on the words of the Lord, from the lesser to the greater. Which opinion he proves from the words καὶ γδ ἐγὼ,, which words hint at the inequality of his person with Christ. *(And thus where Chrysost. homily 27 on Matthew οὐχ, writes, ραγγέλμ Whence also the blessed D. Glass, Gramm. S. p. 709, rightly warns that the speech in this place is elliptical and is to be understood as how much more you, who are Lord and creator of all, will be able to command even by a word alone, so that my servant may recover.)

*( ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν. the word abstract is here taken concretely, as also Luke 7, 8.Rom. 13, 1.)*

*(Having under me, the Syrian, Arab, Persian under my hand, soldiers. From the fact that the Centurion, set over soldiers, was not rejected by Christ or recalled from this way of life, but rather adorned with an excellent testimony of faith, v. 10. our people rightly conclude against the Anabaptists and Photinians, that the military state can consist with true faith, and therefore that honest and legitimate wars are also lawful in the N. T. Compare similar examples of pious Centurions Matt. 27, 54.Acts 10, 1. 2.)*

Latin:

v. 9. Autor imperf. operis hom. 22. putat, Christum argument art à simili. Aug. serm. 6. de verb. Domini, à minori ad maius. quam sententiam probat ex verbis καὶ γδ ἐγὼ, quae verba inaequalitatem personae suae cum Christo innuunt. *(Et ita quoChrysost. homil. 27. in Matth. οὐχ, scribit, ραγγέλμ Unde etiam rectè monet B. D. Glass. Gramm. S. p. 709. ellipticam h. l. esse orationem ac suòintell. quanto magis tu, qui Dominus & creator omnium es, imperare vel sol verbo poteris, ut revale scat servus meus.)

*( ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν. vox abstracta hî concretè sumitur, uti etiam Luc. 7, 8.Rom. 13, 1.)*

*(Habens sub me, Syrus, Arabs, Persa sub manu mea, milites. Ex eo, quòd Centurio militibus praefectus non fuit à Christo reiectus vel ab hoc vitae genere revocatus, sed potiùs egregio fidei testimonio ornatus, v. 10. rectè colligunt nostrates cont a Anabapt. & Photinianos, quòd status militaris cum verâ fide consistere possit, adeoq; bella honesta & legitima etiam in N. T. licita sint. Conf. similia piorū Centurionū exempla Matt. 27, 54.Act. 10, 1. 2.)*

## 8:10
v. 10. How does Christ marvel? August. book 1 against the adversaries of the law and the Prophets, chapter 7. By marveling he was praising what he was commending to others as to be marveled at. book 1 on Genesis against the Manichaeans, chapter 8. Who had created that faith in him, if not he who was marveling at it? But if another had created it, why would he marvel who was foreknowing? What the Lord was marveling at, he was signifying to be to be marveled at by us, for whom there is still need to be moved in such a way. Therefore all such movements of his are not signs of a troubled mind, but of a teaching Master. Some take θαυμάζειν for δοξάζειν, just as the LXX rendered from the Hebrew Deut. 10. v. 17. Some say, that Christ behaved in the manner of one marveling by external signs, so that he might excite admiration in the minds of those hearing and seeing. Some establish, that Christ truly marveled, namely, regarding experimental knowledge.

(Conf. Marc. 6, 6.Luc. 7, 9. This indeed seems to conflict with the omniscience of Christ. For wonder proceeds from prior ignorance and subsequent discovery. Resp. I distinguish between the divine and human nature of Christ. According to the former He is the omniscient God with the Father and the Holy Spirit; according to the latter, although from the very first moment of conception He received divine attributes through and because of the personal union, He nevertheless assumed the form of a servant and kept the communicated divine glory hidden, so that just as in the state of humiliation He truly was ignorant of certain things Marc. 13, 32., so also in this manner He truly at times wondered. However, one must accurately distinguish here between ignorance of pure negation and of perverse disposition. Compare by all means B. D. Fewrb. Κενωσιγρ. book 6, page 151 et seqq. But if anyone wishes from this to impugn either the true deity of Christ or the true and real communication of attributes, that saying of Athanasius will not inappropriately be applied to him, that the humility of Christ, which ought to have been an incentive of love for all, is for him an occasion of erring. Augustine, book 1 de Genesi contra Manich. ch. 8, which passage was just now cited, as also book 1 contra advers. Legis & Proph. ch. 7, maintains that Christ Himself did not wonder. The Jesuit Maldonatus follows this explanation, and thus rejects the former, which Tirinus, Fr. Lucas, Corn. à Lapide, and others also do. But neither is opposed to the analogy of faith. B. Par. in Homil. Acad part. 1, p. 416, likewise embraces the exposition of Augustine; but in vol. 1, LL. Theol. art. de Deo Patre &c. §. 66, he says the former response is simpler. Compare also the same in Exeg. p. 519. B. D. Chemn. in the golden tract de duabus nat. in Christo ch. 20, item ch. 24, p. 131, ch. 33, p. 203. The same in Harm. Ev ch. 53, p. 534, notes that simply in this place it is signified by τὸ to wonder, celebration just as Luke also says: He marveled at him. And that the Greeks also speak thus, he proves from Deut. 10, 17.c. 28, 50.4. Reg. 5, 1.*

*( So great faith. And yet Peter, 2 ep. 1, 1, indicates that those to whom he writes ἰσότιμον πίστιν have obtained &c. Resp. distinguish between faith considered by reason of degrees, and by reason of the object. Considered in the former way, one is called great, another small; but in the latter it is ἰσότιμος, because faith, no less weak than robust, apprehends Christ with his benefits and makes a man a participant in heavenly goods. See B. Par. Comm. on the latter ep. of Pet. p. 22.)*

Never in Israel, who might implore his help, did he find him who had been instructed with such faith. Thus, therefore, nothing is detracted from the faith of Mary and John the Baptist. See Salmeron. *(For the Savior speaks not of the Jews in general, but of those present, nor yet perhaps of all these, but especially of the common sort of Jews; nor so much of the knowledge of faith, as of trust. As B. D. Chemn. H. E. c. 53. p. 534 and Dn. D. Walth. Harm. Bibl. p. 759 note. For those Jews who were more assiduous hearers of Christ than the Centurion had progressed somewhat more in regard to knowledge: yet they did not extend their trust further than they saw and felt. For which reason Christ also sometimes rebukes the Apostles themselves (see below v. 26. c. 14, 31. c. 16, 8. c. 17, Marc. 16, 14. which passages the Jesuit Maldonatus himself supplies in this place, and warns that it is not inconvenient for the Author of the Imperfect work to assert from this that there was in truth greater faith in the Centurion than in the Apostles. Soon, however, he adds, that Christ in this place does not include his own family of Israel, i.e., the B. Virgin and the Apostles. He repeats the same also in Comment. on c. 1. Ioh. p. 397. D. But nothing prevents the Apostles themselves, such as they were then, from being included here. For how languid their faith was before the Holy Spirit was received on the Feast of Pentecost, both the passages brought forward by Maldonatus and others sufficiently reveal.) But on the contrary, he proclaims the Centurion with admiration to the crowds, in that among the meager beginnings of an incipient recognition he leans upon the efficacy of the word with such firm and illustrious trust, with all the aids of reason and the senses removed, as the praised Chemnitius observes. Nor, however, are these things to be dragged to the point as if faith were better defined by ignorance than by knowledge, as Bell. wishes, which error even those few oracles Hos. 4, 10.Matth. 13, 19.2. 3.Iohan. 6, 69.Galat. 4, 9.Actor. 17, 23. solidly refute, Beautifully Origen opposes the trust of this Centurion to the weakness of Jairus, Nicodemus, etc. Iairus, he writes, a prince of Israel, asking for his daughter, did not say: Speak the word, but come quickly. Nicodemus, hearing about the Sacrament of faith, says: How can this be done? Mary & Martha say: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died; doubting that where the power of God could be present.

Latin:

v. 10. Quomodo Christus miratur? August. lib. 1. contra advers. legis & Prophet. cap. 7. Mirando laudabat, quod mirandum aliis commendabat. lib. 1. de Genes. contra Manich. cap. 8. Quis in illo fecerat illam fidem, nisi qui eam mirabatur. Quod si & alius eam fecisset ut quid miraretur qui praescius erat? Quod mirabatur Dominus, nobis mirandum esse significabat, quibus adhuc opus est sic moveri. Omnes ergo tales motus eius non perturliari animi sunt signa, sed docentis Magistri. Quidam accipiunt θαυμάζειν pro δοξάζειν, sicut LXX. reddiderunt ex Hebraeo Deut. 10. v. 17. Quidam dicunt, Christum se habuisse ad modum admirantis signis externis, ut in in animis audientium & videntium admirationem excitaret. Quidam statuunt, Christum verè fuisse admiratum, sc. quoad cognitionem experiment alem.

*(Conf. Marc. 6, 6.Luc. 7, 9. Videtur quidem hoc pugnare cum Christi omniscientiâ. Admiratio enim ex antegressâignoratione & consecutione proficiscitur. Resp. dist. inter divinam, & humanam Christi naturam. Secundùm illam est cum Patre & Sp. S. Deus omniscius, secundùm hanc licet in primo statim conceptionis momento per ac propter unionem personalem itidem idiomata divina acceperit, servi tamen formam adsumsit, ac communicatam gloriam divinam secretò habuit, adeò ut quemadmodùm in statu exinanitionis quaedam reverà ignoravit Marc. 13, 32. ita etiam h. m. reverà aliquando admiratus fuerit. Accuratè tamen hîc disting. ignorantia purrae negationis, ac prave dispositionis. Confer. omninò B. D. Fewrb. Κενωσιγρ. l. 6. pag. 151. seqq. Si quis verò exinde sive veram Christi deitatem, sive veram ac realem idiomatum communicationem impugnare velit, ad illum non incommodè applicabitur illud Athanasii, quòd humilitas Christi, quae omnibusesse debebat incentivum amoris, sit illi errandi occasio. Augustinus lib. 1. de Genesi contra Manich. c. 8. qui locus modò fuit adductus, uti etiam l. 1. contra advers. Legis & Proph. cap. 7. statuit, non ipsum Christum fuisse admiratum. Sequitur hanc explicationem Iesuita Maldonatus, adeoque priorem etiam reiicit, quod etiam faciunt Tirinus, Fr. Lucas, Corn. à Lapide, alii. Sed neutra fidei analogiae adversatur. B. Par. in Homil. Acad part. 1. p. 416. itid. Augustini expositionem amplectitur; sed t. 1. LL. Theol. art. de Deo Patre &c. §. 66. priorem resposionem simpliciorem esse dicit. Conf. quoque Idem in Exeg. p. 519. B. D. Chemn. in aureo tract. de duabus nat. in Christo c. 20. it. c. 24. p 131. c. 33. p. 203. Idem in Harm. Ev c. 53 p. 534, notat, simpliciter h. l. significari per τὸadmirari, celebratio sicut & Lucas dicat: Admiratus est ipsum. & sic etiam Graecos loqui, probat ex Deut. 10, 17.c. 28, 50.4. Reg. 5, 1.*

*( Tantam fidem. Atqui Petrus 2. ep. 1, 1. indicat, quòd illi, ad quos scribit ἰσότιμον πίστιν sortiti fuerint &c. Resp. dist. inter fidem consideratam ratione graduum, & ratione obiecti. Illo modo considerata dicitur alia magna, alia parva; hôc verò est ἰσότιμος, quia non minùs infirma quàm robusta fides Christum cum beneficiis apprehendit ac bonorum coelestium participem hominem facit. Vid. B. Par. Comm. in post. ep Pet. p. 22.)*

Nunquam in Israēl, qui auxilium eius imploraret, invenit eum, qui tantâ fide fuisset instructus. sic ergo nihil detrahitur fidei Mariae & Ioh: Baptistae. Vide Salmeron. *(Loquitur enim Salvator non de Iudaeis in genere, sed de praesentibus, nec his tamen fortè omnibus, sed cumprimis de vulgò Iudaeorum; nec tam de fidei notitiâ, quàm de fiduciâ. Uti notant B. D. Chemn. H. E. c. 53. p. 534. Dn. D. Walth. Harm. Bibl. p. 759. Illi enim Iudaei, qui magis adsidui auditores Christi erant, quàm Centurio, quoad notitiam plus aliquantulum profecerant: fiduciam tamē nō longiùs extendebant, quàm videbant & sentiebant. Quâ de causa etiam Christus ipsos Apostolos reprehendit quandoq; (vid. infrà v. 26. c. 14, 31. c. 16, 8. c. 17, Marc. 16, 14. quae loca ipse Iesuita Maldonatus in h. l. suppeditat, monetque, non incommodè hinc Autorem operis Imperfecti adserere, revera maiorem in Centurione, quàm in Apostolis fuisse fidem. Mox tamen subdit, Christum h. l. nomine Israelfamiliam suam i. e. B Virginem & Apostolos non comprehendere. Idem etiam repetit Comment. in c. 1. Ioh. p. 397. D. Sed nihil impedit, quò minùs ipsi Apostoli, quales tunc erant, hîc cōprehendantur. Quàm langvida enim eorum fuerit fides ante acceptum in Pentecostes Festo Sp. Sanctum, tum loca à Maldonato adducta, tum alia satis produnt.) Centurionem verò contrà turbis cum admiratione depraedicat, eò quòd inter tenuia inchoatae agnitionis principia tam firma & illustri fiduciâ efficaciae verbi innititur, remotis omnibus rationis & sensuum adminiculis, observante laudato Chemnitio. Neq; tamen haec eò trahenda sunt, qs. fides meliùs per ignorantiam, quàm per notitiam definiatur, uti Bell. vult. quem errorem, vel pauca illa oracula Hos. 4, 10.Matth. 13, 19.2. 3.Iohan. 6, 69.Galat. 4, 9.Actor. 17, 23. solidè refutant, Pulcrè Origenes Centurionis huius fiduciam opponit imbecillitati Iairi, Nicodemi &c. Iairus, scribit, Israelis princepspre filiâ suâ petens non dixit: Dic verbo, sed veni velociter. Nicodemus de fidei Sacramento audiens, ait: Quomodo hoc potest fieri? Maria & Martha dicunt: Domine si fuisses hîc, frater meus non fuisset mortuus; dubitantes, quòd ubiposset adesse Dei potentia.)*

## 8:11
v. 11. ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν. The Greeks use the plural number to denote a triple rising, and likewise a triple setting. Arist. de mund. cap. 4. αἱ ἀνατολαὶ are distinguished into θερινὰς, ἰσημερινὰς & χειμερινὰς, into summer, equinoctial, & winter risings. The reason and proportion is the same for τῶν δυσμῶν i. e. settings. Luc. 13. v. 29.

*( Many from the East Conf. Luc. 13, 29. Apoc. c. 5, 9. and c. 7, 9. Furthermore, the calling of the Gentiles is also predicted in the O. T. Gen. 9, 27. cap. 11, 3. c. 18, 18. Deut. 32, 21. 43. Ps. 2, 8. Ps. 18, 44. 45. Ps. 22, 28. Ps. 72, 8. Ps. 117, 1. Es. 2, 23. c. 9, 2. (coll. with Matth. 4, 16.) c. 11, 10. c. 42, 4, c. 43, 5. 6. c. 49, 6. (coll. with Act. 15, 47.) c. 55, 4. Rom. 11, 17. commanded by Christ to the Apostles Matth. 28, 19. Marc. 16, 15.)*

They shall recline in the kingdom of heaven i. e. they shall become partakers of the heavenly kingdom & of eternal goods. Luc. 13. v. 29. These words are taken by some concerning the kingdom of grace in these lands (to which the passages Ps. 23, 5. Prov. 9, 5. Matth. 22, 2. Luc. 14, 16. contribute) by others concerning the kingdom of glory, where perfect intuition and enjoyment of eternal gifts and goods will follow Psal. 17, v. last Psal. 16. v. last *(And that this is primarily and indeed the subject here, the antithesis v. 12. shows.)* Moreover, the glory of eternal life is compared to human banquets, because in them men especially devote themselves to merriment, but most especially in nuptial ones.

* (The custom of the ancients of reclining will be treated more extensively in the Annot. on Luc. 7, 36. It is otherwise known that in Holy Scripture the kingdom of heaven or eternal blessedness is not rarely compared to a banquet, in which Abraham the Father of believers, then Isaac & Jacob occupy the chief place, but the other guests recline together with Abraham. And the Savior looks to this also, both here and Luc. 13, 30. 16, 22. it. c. 22, 16. 18. 30. Compare Apoc. 19, 9. Es. 6, 13. To be instituted however The comparison of eternal life with a banquet is possible 1. by reason of the preparation, Matth. 25, 34. 1. Cor. 2, 9. 2. by reason of the invitation. 3. by reason of the sumptuous eating and drinking, Ps. 17, 15. Cant. 5, 1. Ps. 36, 9. Apoc. 7, 16. Let us aspire to this banquet Ps. 42, 1. Ps. 73, 25. Apoc. 22, 17. For a fuller explanation of the said comparison see D. Botsacc. Promt. alleg. p. 869. B. D. Glassius Exeg. Evang. Dom. I. post Trinit. page 711. B. Par. Postill. Salom. part. 2. page 279. Homil. Acad. part. 2. page 352. Loc de morte §. 161. L. de vitâ aet. §. 51. Aph. Pract. tit. vita aeterna.)*

Eadem est ratio ac proportio τῶν δυσμῶν i. e. occasuum.Luc. 13. v. 29.

Accumbent in regno coelorum i. e. participes fient regni coelestis & bonorum aeternorum. Luc. 13. v. 29. Accipiuntur haec verba à nonnullis de regno gratiae in his terris (quo faciunt loca Ps. 23, 5.Prov. 9, 5.Matth. 22, 2.Luc. 14, 16.) ab aliis de regno gloriae. ubi perfecta succedet intuitio & fruitio donorum ac bonorum aeternorum Psal. 17, v. ult. Psal. 16. v. ult. *(Et de hoc cumprimis quoque & quidem hîc sermonem esse, antithesis v. 12. ostendit.)* Comparatur autem gloria vit aet. conviviis humanis, quia in illis homines praecipuè hilaritati dant operam, maximè verò in nuptialibus.

* (De more veterum accumbendi prolixiùs agetur in Annot. ad Luc. 7, 36. Notum aliàs est, quòd in Script. S. regnum coelorum sive aeterna beatitudo haut rarò conferatur cum convivio, in quo Abraham Pater credentium, tum Isaac & Iacob principem qs occupent locum, caeteri verò convivae unà cum Abrahamo recumbant. Atque eò respicit etiam Salvator tum hîc, tum Luc. 13, 30.16, 22. it. c. 22, 16.18.30. Confer. Apoc. 19, 9.Es. 6, 13. ## 8:12
* (v. 12. Children of the kingdom i. e. those to whom, by the promise made to the Patriarchs, the heavenly kingdom was as it were destined and proper, who live and are born in the kingdom of GOD i. e. in the Church, who were naturally subject to the kingdom and as it were natives. For the promise was made in general to all the descendants of Abraham. There are, however, those who think that those unbelieving Jews are called children of the kingdom, at least κατὰ τὸ ἔνδοξον, not because they are such, but because they appear to be. Similar examples of such a locution occur elsewhere, as Matth. 9, 12. 1. Cor. 8, 5. Gal. 4, 4. thus B. D. Meisn. establishes Decad. 2. Ανθρωπ. D. 15, 9. 6. §. 24. B. D. Glassius notes in Gr. S. p. 475 that it is said emphatically children of the kingdom rather than children of the King, because there are many in the Kingdom whom the King nevertheless eventually rejects as unfaithful. May the meditation of this matter excite in us a filial fear, so that we may work out our salvation with fear and trembling Phil. 2, 12. For not only those who were never regenerated, but also those who were once regenerated through the word and Sacraments and were admitted into the kingdom of GOD i. e. the Church, nay even adopted by God, can be rejected again, if indeed they conduct themselves unworthily of divine grace and the honor of sonship. For if Aristippus, to one accusing him because he was casting off and neglecting his son, as if he were not born from him, replied cleverly: Do we not also cast away from us as useless both phlegm and lice born from us? feeling that those should not be held as sons who otherwise had nothing by which to commend themselves to the affection of their parents, except that they were begotten by them. Which the old man in the Comedy also intends, saying: I want you to be mine only so long as you do what is worthy of you. Laërtius l. 7. Thus also Alexander, reproved by his wife because he had disinherited a useless son, and she saying, he is from him: when he had spat upon the ground, and this, he said, is from me: but it is useless. Maximus reports this in serm. 25. Let Suetonius also be unrolled in Aug. Caes. But if, I say, those men rightly disinherited and as it were cast away degenerate sons, how much more will God do this, who since He is holiness and justice itself, by nature most vehemently abhors sin, will cast them away, will precipitate them into hell, and will spit them out Apoc. 3, 16. who shall have been degenerate sons. Let there be compared also on this matter Matth. 3, 8. 9.Rom. 11, 20. 21. etc. That also is worthy of observation, that in this place Corn. à Lapide expressly professes, that God promised to the Patriarchs and their seed as well the earthly kingdom of Judea, as the spiritual kingdom of eternal glory in the heavens.

* ( Ἐκβληθήσονται they shall be cast out. So also the Arab and the Ethiopian. In the Syriac version it is which in the London Polyglot Bible edition is pointed as if it were in Peal, just as it is also rendered there in Latin they shall go out. I would prefer in Aphel, and then to translate they shall be cast out. For so the Greek text demands, and in this place the same word is used Luc 13, 28 with the said Bibles also agreeing. Concerning the rejection of the Jews see Rom. 9, 31.Act. 13, 46.)

Σκότος ἐξὼτερον i. e. τὸἔξω darkness, which is outside the kingdom of heaven. Caiet. thinks that outer is said for external, for the distinction of interior and spiritual darkness. August. in the exposition of Ps. 6. takes outer darkness concerning the reprobate sense and blindness of mind in this life, and outer concerning the greatest blindness, which is to be in the damned. Truly they rightly determine, who think that there is understood not only the abdication of the Jews, the blinding, injustice, and all-manner of impiety which are called in the Scriptures works of darkness, temporal calamities, and anxious conscience in this life, but also the most cruel punishments, to be sustained in the infernal prison.

* ( εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξὼτερον. It is a description of the eternal punishment of the damned. Compare below c. 13, 42. 22, 13. c. 24, 51. c. 25, 30. Luc. 13, 28. Peter 2. epist. c. 2, 17. and Jude v. 13. call it ζόφον τού σκότους. B. Par. elegantly shows the emphasis of the phrase in his Commentary on the latter epistle of Peter p. 313. Skilfully Dionysius à Rickel, Carthusian Monk.

Comm. on the latter Peter c. 2, 19. Wicked men in this life walk in the darkness of sins, thence from the darkness of vices they are cast down into the darkness of torments. Conformably to that, Greg. M. lib. 25. moral. c. 11. Then they shall be cast, bound, into the outer darkness, who now are voluntarily blinded by inner things. Since heavenly beatitude is compared with nuptial delights or banquets, which were formerly celebrated by night with many lamps among the Jews, it is not inappropriately said indeed of those who repel the word of GOD and judge themselves unworthy of the kingdom of GOD Act. 13, 46., that they are cast out into the outer darkness: not otherwise than those who were thrust out from those nuptial banquets were compelled to dwell in darkness. Ridiculously Corn. à Lap. in h. l. Gehenna is in the center of the earth, which is distant from the surface of the earth by three thousand miles and more, wherefore such great opacity of the earth causes great darkness in Gehenna.)

By weeping and gnashing of teeth the highest sadness and the highest pain is understood. * (See Note on Luc. 13, 28. The Jesuits raise a question here: whether the damned, having resumed their body on the day of judgment, will shed tears. Maldonatus affirms, Corn. à Lapide denies, who can be unrolled, if it pleases.)*

Latin:

* (v. 12. Filii regni i. e. quibus ex promissione, Patriarchis factà, regnum coeleste qs. destinatum ac proprium erat, qui in regno DEI s. in Ecclesia degunt ac nati sunt, qui naturaliter regno subiecti & qs. indigenae erant. Facta enim promissio in genere omnibus Abrahami posteris. Sunt tamen, qui Iudaeos illos incredulos vocari putant filios regni, saltem κατὰ τὸ ἔνδοξον, non quòd tales sint, sed videantur. Cuiusmodi locutionis similia exempla occurrunt & alibi, ut Matth. 9, 12.1. Cor. 8, 5.Gal. 4, 4. ita B. D. Meisn. statuit Decad. 2. Ανθρωπ. D. 15, 9. 6. §. 24. Notat B. D. Glassius Gr. S. p. 475. dici emphaticè filios regni potiùs, quàm filios Regis, quia multi sint in Regno, quos tamen Rex tandem ut infidos reiicit. Excitet huius in nobis rei meditatio timorem filialem, quò cum tremore salutem nostram operemur Phil. 2, 12. Neque enim illi saltem, qui nun quam fuerunt regeniti, sed illi quoque qui per verbum & Sacramenta aliquando regeniti, sunt atque in regnum DEI h. e. Ecclesiam adsciti, imò à Deo adoptati, reiici iterum possunt, si indignos nempe sese divinâ gerant gratiâ ac filiationis honore. Si enim Aristippus incusanti cuidam, quòd filium sic abiiceret negligeretque, quasi ex ipso natus non esset, scitè respondit: Annon & pituitam & pediculos è nobis natos velut inutiles procul à nobis adiicimus? sentiens, eos non habendos pro filiis, qui nihil haberent alioqui, quo se parentum affectui commendent, nisi quod ab ipsis progeniti sint. Id quod & senex in Comoedia vult, aiens: Tantisper te volo meum, dum id, quod te d gnum, facis. Laërtius l. 7. Sic & Alexander reprehensus ab uxore, quòd filium inutilem abdicasset, dicenteque, ex eo esse: cùm expuisset in terram, & hoc, inquit, ex me est: sed inutile. Refert Maximus serm. 25. Evolvatur etiam Suetonius in Aug. Caes. Quod si, inquam, isti filios degeneres iure exhaeredarunt ac quasi abiecerunt, quantò magis Deus hoc faciet, qui cùm sanctitas ac iustitia ipsa sit, naturà vehementissimè peccatum aversatur, illos abiiciet, in infernum praecipitabit, atque expuet Apoc. 3, 16. qui filli degeneres fuerint. Conferantur quoq; in hanc rem Matth. 3, 8. 9.Rom. 11, 20. 21. &c. Illud quoque observatione dignum est, quòd h. l. Corn. à Lapide disertè profiteatur, Deum Patriarchis eorumque semini uti regnum Iudaeae terrenum, sic spirituale aeternae gloriae in colis promisisse.)*

* ( Ἐκβληθήσονταιeiicientur. Sic quoque Arabs & Aethiops. In Syriacâ versione est quod in edit. Bibl. Polyg. Londinensium punctatur ac si esset in Peal, sicut etiam Latine ibi redditur egredientur. Malim in Aphel. ac tunc vertere eiicientur. Sic enim postulat textus Graecus, & h. m adhibetur idem hoc verbum Luc 13, 28 consentientibus quoque dictis Bibliis. De reiectione Iudaeorum vid. Rom. 9, 31.Act. 13, 46.) *

Σκότος ἐξὼτερον i. e. τὸἔξωtenebrae, quae sunt extra regnum coelorum. Caiet. putat, exteriores dici pro externis, ad distinctionem interiorum ac spiritualium tenebrarum. August. in expos. Ps. 6.exter as tenebras accipit de sensu reprobo & caecitate mentis in hac vita, exteriores de summa caecitate, quae futura est in damnatis. Sanè rectè statuunt, qui putant, non tantùm intelligi abdicationem Iudaeorum excaecationem, iniustitiam & omnigenam impietatem quae dicuntur in Scripturis opera tenebrarum, calamitates temporates & anxiam conscientia in hac vita, verùm etiam crudelissima supplicia, in infernali carcere sustinenda.

* ( εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξὼτερον. Est descriptio aeterni damnatorum supplicii. Conf. infrà c. 13, 42. 22, 13. c. 24, 51. c. 25, 30. Luc. 13, 28. Petrus 2. epist. c. 2, 17. ac Iudas v. 13. vocant ζόφον τού σκότους. emphasin phraseos eleganter ostendit B. Par. Comm. in post. ep. Petri p. 313. Scitè Dionysius à Rickel, Monachus Carthus.

Comm. in post. Petr. c. 2, 19. Homines flagitiosi in hâc vita anabulant in tenebris peccatorum, inde de tenebris vitiorum praecipitantur in tenebras tormentorum. Conformiter illi Gregor. M. lib. 25. moral. c. 11. Tunc coacti in tenebras exteriores mittentur, qui nunc interioribus voluntariè excoecantur. Cùm coelestis beatitudo cum nuptialibus deliciis s. conviviis, quae noctu cum multis lucernis olim apud Iudaeos peragebantur, conferatur, non incommodè sanè de illis, qui verbum DEI repellunt ac seipsos per impoenitentiam & contemtum regno DEI indignos iudicant, Act. 13, 46. dicitur, quòd eiiciantur in tenebras exteriores: haut aliter ac illi, qui è conviviis illis nuptialibus extrudebantur, in tenebris commorari cogebantur. Ridiculè Corn. à Lap. in h. l. Gehenna est in centro terrae, quod à superficie terrae distat tribus millibus milliarium & ampliùs, quare tanta terrae opacitas magnas causat in gehenna tenebras.) *

Per ploratum & stridorem tentium summa tristitia & summus dolor intelligitur. * (Vid. Not. ad Luc. 13, 28. Quaestionem hic movent Iesuitae: an damnati resumto in die iudicii corpore lacrymas effusuri sint. Maldonatus affirmat, Corn. à Lapide negat, qui possunt evolvi, si placet.)*

## 8:13
* (v. 13. As you have believed, so let it be done to you. See below c. 9. 21 22. c. 15, 28. Luc. 8, 50. c. 18, 42)

* ( And he was healed &c. From the fact that Christ healed this boy or servant while absent, our countrymen gather that, although Christ in the state of humiliation was now here, now there visibly present: yet, as often as he miraculously cured men who were absent by reason of place, then he himself, as God and as man, in the unity of his person, at one and the same time, was invisibly present to them. Since divine operation and divine substantial, although illocal, nearness among creatures are inseparably joined. Conf. Matth. 18, 20.c. 28, 20.Eph. 1, 18.c. 4, 10. 11. and especially also let B. D. Siegwart in Anti Paraeo l. 3. c. 3. art, 13 be unrolled. B. D. Fewrb. Fasc. 1. Diss. Theol. disp. 3. p. 140. seqq. and also t. 5. Disp. Marpp. Disp. 23. seqq. t. 8. Dispp. Gies. p. 44. Dn. D. Hannekenius t. 8. Disp. Gies. p. 322. 323.)*

Ex eo, quòd Christus puerum s. servum hunc absens sanavit, colligunt nostrates, quòd licet Christus in statu exinanitionis iam hâc, iam ibi fuerit visibiliter praesens: tamen, quoties homines, ratione loci absentes, miraculosè curavit, tum ipse, ut Deus & ut homo, in unitate suae personae, uno eodemq; tempore, ipsis fuerit invisibiliter praesens. ## 8:14
* (v. 14. And coming into the house of Peter. It seems to stand in the way that Peter's house is mentioned elsewhere to have been in Capernaum. Hugo Grotius answers, that the house is understood here, into which Peter and Andrew, as often as they were in Capernaum, were accustomed to receive themselves. For it is credible, he further adds, that it was the mother-in-law's house, since Peter and Andrew had had a home in Bethsaida, before they followed Christ. The blessed D. Chemn. also concedes in H. E. p. 318 that the house which Peter had in Capernaum, he obtained by reason of marriage. But that he did not entirely abandon it, the same person teaches in the said place. But we shall deal with this matter more fully at Matth. 19, 27.

His mother-in-law (Peter's) &c. Where the mother-in-law is, there is the wife. Therefore the Apostle Peter was married, when on the contrary his fictitious successor the Roman Pontiff says anathema to those who establish, that all, and even clerics, can contract marriage, who do not feel that they have the gift of chastity. See Council of Trent, sess. 8, can. 9. Whence also the champion of the Roman court, Bellarm. l. 1. de Sacr. c. 5. §. sed debuit, writes, The marriage of priests is illegitimate, and marriage in name only, but in reality sacrilegious unchastity. What then do the Papists say to the example of Peter? They concede that he had a wife, but after he followed Christ, he left her, just as also the daughter born from her, later called Petronilla by her father Peter. Thus Corn. à Lapide in this place. The Jesuit Conzen establishes the same in this place. But where is it read that Peter abandoned his wife? Perhaps Matth. 19, 27. But what the genuine sense of the said passage is, will be shown in its own place. Certainly that it is not to be understood as a total abandonment of the wife is clear from 1. Cor. 9, 5. Conzen objects: That the wives of the Apostles went around with them and Christ, neither does Scripture say, nor is any of the heretics so impudent as to profess this. We reply, we do not say that the women who hung upon the mouth of the teaching Christ and ministered to him Matth. 27. Luc. 8. 3. were the wives of Christ, but we bring forward this, that by those women sisters, of whom mention is made in 1. Cor. 9, 5., the wives of the Apostles are to be understood, from whose company they did not entirely abstain. But the Jesuit denies that by those sisters women the wives of the Apostles are to be accepted: he wishes, namely, that by those are understood at least pious women, who ministered to the Apostles. How also his own associates, Salmero, Iustinianus, Tirinus, Corn. à Lapide, and with whom also Dionys. Carthusianus and Estius explain it. But the contrary is clear from the context itself. As in many places in the Annotations to the said place.

will be shown, and at the same time a reply will be made to the exceptions of the Jesuits and especially of Estius, who is sufficiently prolix there. In this place it can at least be noted that not only our interpreters, but also the Fathers, such as Clement of Alexandria, l. 3. Strom., and also from the Papists Laur. Valla and Ambrosius Catharinus, of the order of preachers and Archbishop of Conza, in the said place. By sister women let them understand the wives of the Apostles, Estius himself admitting it. He could have added, moreover, from the Papists, Franc. Vatablus, also Andreas Dudithius, Bishop of the Five Churches (who excellently defends our opinion, in Demonstr. pro Coni. Cleric. p. 56.), from the Fathers Tertullian in Ex-ort. ad Castit. c. 8., Eusebius l. 3. H. E. c. 27., nay, even Leo IX, Roman Pontiff, against the Epistle of Nicetas, add c. Omninò dist. 31. But how great the authority of the Roman Pontiff is among the Papists is known to the common people. And hence it is evident how true is the assertion of Conzenius, writing: that the wives of the Apostles went about with them, neither does Scripture say, nor is any heretic so impudent as to profess this.

Ἐκείνη. Erasmus in his annotations testifies that he found this clause added at the end of the History in ancient Greek Codices: καὶ ὑποτρ Flacius confirms the same in his scholia to c. 7. of Luke. (Other MSS. Codices also have the same appendix, such as that of Montfort, of Gonville College in the University of Cambridge, also the Lincoln and the new Bodleian in the University of Oxford, and also certain Codices of Stephanus. But it is missing in very many most ancient Greek Codices (to which are not undeservedly reckoned the Greek MSS. Ecclogae which are held in the Nuremberg Library), also in the most ancient version, namely the Syriac, just as also in other Oriental versions of the N. T., such as the Arabic and Persian, with the sole exception of the Ethiopic, which has i. e. And the Centurion having returned to his house found his servant healed. From which Ludov. de Dieu also gathers that the Ethiopic was not made from any of the said Oriental versions. Furthermore, Franc. Lucas Brugensis not vainly suspects that that clause was added here by someone from Luc. c. 7, 10., with the words changed according to the manner of narrating which Matthew had used up to this point.)

Syr. It had seized her. אשתא fire, the heat of a fever, the Greek πυρέσθουσα likewise has the origin ὑπὸ τοὑ πυρὸς.

Latin:

* (v. 14. Et veniens in domum Petri. Videtur obstare, quòd Petri domus Capernaumi fuisse alibi commemoratur. Respondet Hugo Grotius, intelligi hîc eam domum, in quam Petrus & Andreas, quories erant Capharnaumi, recipere se solobant. Credibile enim est, subiicit porrò, socrûs domum fuisse, cùm Petrus & Andreas Bethsaidae habuissent larem, antequam Christum sectarentur. Concedit etiam B. D. Chemn. in H. E. p. 318. domum, quam Petrus Capernaumi habuit, ratione coniugii ipsum fortitum esse. Quòd verò eam non penitus deserverit, docet idem d. l. Sed pluribus haede re agemus ad Matth. 19, 27.)*

Socrum eius (Petri) &c. Ubi socrus, ibi uxor. Fuit ergo Apostolus Petrus uxoratus, cùm contrà fictus eius successor Pontifex Romanus anathema dicat statuentibus, posse omnes, adeoetiam clericos contrahere matrimonium, qui non sentiunt, se castitatis habere donum. Vid. Concil. Trid. sess. 8. can. 9. Unde etiam aulae Romanae promachus Bellarm. l. 1. de Sacr. c. 5. §. sed debuit Sacerdotum coniugium, scribit, est illegit imum, & solo nomine coniugium, re autem ipsâ sacrilega impudicitia. Quid igitur Pontificii ad exemplum Petri? Concedunt, habuisse eum uxorem, sed postquam Christum sequutus est, reliquisse, quemadmodū & filiam ex ea genitam, à Patre Petro postea Petronillam dictam. Ita Corn. à Lapide in h. l. Idem statuit Iesuita Conzen in h. l. Sed ubi legitur, quòd uxorem Petrus deserverit? Fortè Matth. 19, 27. Verùm quis dicti loci genuinus sensus sit, suo loco ostendetur. Sanè quòd non de totali uxoris desertione intelligendus sit, patet ex 1. Cor. 9, 5. S-regerit Conzen: Uxores Apostolorum cum ipsis & Christo circumsvisse, nec Scriptura dicit, nec ullus haereticorum tam est impudens, ut hoc profiteatur. Resp. non dicimus, quòd mulieres, quae ab ore docentis Christi pependerunt eique ministrarunt, Matth. 27.Luc. 8, 3. Christi uxores fuerint, sed id adferimus, quòd per mulieres illas sorores, quarum mentio fit 1. Cor. 9, 5. intelligendae sint Apostolorum uxores, à quarum consuetudine illi non penicus atstinuerint. Sed negat Iesuita, quòd per sorores illas mulieres accipiendae sint Apostolorum uxores: vult nempe, per istas intelligi saltem pias foeminas, quae Apostolis ministrârint. Quomodo etiam ipsius socienni, Salmero, Iustinianus, Tirinus, Corn. à Lapide, rum quoq; Dionys. Carthusianus & Estius exponunt. Ast contrarium patet ex ipso contextu. Ceu multis in Annor. ad d. l.

ostendetur, & simul respondebitur ad Iesuitarum ac cumprimie Estii, qui satis prolixus ibi est, exceptiones. Hoc loco illud saltem notari potest, quòd non nostri solùm Interpp. sed & Patres, uti Clemens Alexandrinus, l. 3. Strom. nec non ex Pontificiis Laur. Valla & Ambrosius Catharinus, ord. praedic. ac Compsae Archiepiscopus, d. l. per forores mulieres intelligant Apostolorum uxores, ipso Estio fatente. Addere insuper potuisset ex Pontificiis Franc. Vatablum, it. Andream Dudithium, Quinque Ecclesie-sem Episcopum (qui egregiè sententiam nostram defendit, in Demonstr. pro Coni. Cleric. p. 56.) ex Patribus Tertullianum in Ex-ort. ad Castit. c. 8. Eusebium l. 3. H. E. c. 27. imò ipsum Leonem IX. P. R. contra Epist. Nicetae, add. c. Omninò dist. 31. Quanti verò Pontificis Romani apud Pontificios autoritas sit, in vulgus notum est. Atque hinc patet, quàm vera sit Conzenii adsertio, scribentis: uxores Apostolorum cum ipsis circumivisse, nec Scriptura dicit necullus haereticorum tam est impudens, ut hoc proficatur.)*

Ἐκείνη. Erasmus in annot testatur, se in antiquis Codd. Graecis reperisse hanc in fine Historiae additam clausulam: καὶ ὑποτρ Idem confirmat Flacius in schol. ad c. 7. Luc. *(Eandem appendicem habent quoque alii MSS. Codd. uti Montfortii, Collegii Gonvilli in Acad. Cantabrigiensi, it. Lincolniensis & novi in Acad. Oxon. Bodleianus, nec non Stephani Codd. quidam. Ast deest illa in plurimis Codd. vetustissimis Graecis, (quibus non immeritò accensentur Ecclogae Graecae MSS. quae habentur in Biblioth. Noriberg.) it. in antiquissimâ versione, nempe Syriaca, quemadmodum etiam in aliis N. T. vers. Orient. uti Arabicâ & Persicâ, solâ Aethiopicâ exceptâ, quae habet i. e. Et reverso Centurione in domum suam invenit puerum suum sanatum. Ex quo etiam colligit Ludov. de Dieu, ex nullâ dictarum vers. Orient. factam esse Aethiopicam. Coeterùm non vanè suspicatur Franc. Lucas Brugensis, clausulam illam ab aliquo ex Luc. c. 7, 10. huc esse additam, mutatis verbis ad modum narrandi, quo hactenus Matthaeus fuerat usus.)*

## 8:15
(v. 15. He touched her hand, and the fever left her, See also below c. 9, 29. Mark 7, 33. Beautifully Cyril lib. 1. de Fide ad Reginas t. 3. oper. p. 316. Why was He not content, as in the case of Lazarus, with a word to raise the girl, and He held her hand? Doubtless to show His life-giving body, for the body is of life. Therefore the union of the Word is more natural and true, etc. And again a little after page 317. Christ raised Lazarus, the daughter of the synagogue ruler, and the son of the widow. Now how is He not life according to nature, who was able to repel death not only by a word, but also by the touch of a hand? For it was consequent and necessary that the body which was proper to life should be life-giving. The same l. 4. in John cap. 23. t. 1. page 209. Since the flesh is joined with the life-giving Word, it has been made entirely life-giving. & a little after: Although therefore the Nature of the flesh, as it is flesh, cannot give life: yet it does this, because it has received the whole operation of the Word: For it is the body not of any man, whose flesh is of no avail . For it is not the body of Paul or Peter or the others, but of our life and Savior Jesus Christ himself, in whom the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily, that can do this. To this point also belongs that of Damascene lib. 3. O. F. c. 18. at the end. Naturally indeed it was not omnipotent: (the human will and nature of Christ:) But as of the Word of GOD according to truth and nature, it was made omnipotent. These and very many other sayings of the pious ancients twin to these are to be opposed not only to those Calvinists, who do not blush to write, that the flesh of Christ contributed no more to the performing of miracles than the flesh of the Apostles contributed to the miracles performed by the Apostles, or the rod of Moses was of use to Moses for performing miracles. (as indeed the words of Lamb. Danaeus have in exam. lib. de duabus nat. Chemn. p. 118. & in Vol. Oper. p. 137. But also to those who indeed grant, that the human nature (which is used as an instrument by λόγῳ not as separated, but hypostatically united) concurs in miracles: yet they deny, that that power, by which the human nature of Christ performed miracles, is omnipotence, but strive to argue, that it is distinct from omnipotence. Which

opinion Wendelin holds, who also Exerc. LIX. §. 29. thus rises up against us: But if no one can perform miracles, except through communicated omnipotence, as to the Apostles and to the Prophets the same must be attributed: when they also performed miracles: which, however, no theologian of sound mind would admit. Therefore, according to Wendelin, the human nature of Christ concurs in miracles in no other way and by no other power, divinely communicated to it personally, than the Apostles: because, indeed, otherwise according to him, if divine omnipotence was personally communicated to the human nature through personal union, by which He performed miracles, it follows that such omnipotence was also communicated to the Apostles when they performed miracles. Whence he also further mocks, adding: But behold a new kind of communication! Even the voice of Christ was omnipotent. Indeed, in truth, Damascenus explicitly says that the human nature was made omnipotent. And this is also evident from the fact that it was made entirely life-giving, as we have heard from Cyril. But Wendelin replies with some passages from the same Cyril and other Fathers, in which it is taught that those things which are divine in Christ are to be attributed to the Divinity; those which are human, to the humanity. But the Orthodox have long since warned that the Fathers in such sayings speak of the natures considered in and of themselves: and thus they are by no means opposed to us, as we ourselves confess that divine things originally are to be referred only to the divine nature; human things originally only to the human nature. This does not escape Wendelin. Yet he insists: As if indeed anyone had ever been so delirious as to believe that the works of divine omnipotence, such as miracles, could originally proceed from the human nature considered distinctly and in itself etc. I reply: whether or not there were heretics who were so delirious, it suffices that the Fathers wished to explain the orthodox opinion in this way, so that no one might seize an opportunity for calumny, as if, because of the asserted communication of idioms, they taught that the human nature had been made equal to the divine, or made or changed into the divine nature: just as it is evident that the Calvinists, and among them especially Wendelin, strive greatly, though vainly, to elicit such a thing from our doctrine. But more on this matter elsewhere. Let the blessed D. Sigwart in Admon. Christ. de Irenico Paraei 4. l. 3. c. 3. art. 14, the blessed D. Gerlach in D. spp. Theol. part. post. Disp. 4, the blessed Schröder in Sceptro Regali Christ, lib. 3, the blessed D. Hutter in Expos. lib. Christ. Concord. p. 803, and others be consulted.)*

Latin:

*(v. 15. Tetigit manum eius, & reliquit eam febris, Vid. etiam infrà c. 9, 29. Marc. 7, 33. Pulcrè Cyrillus lib. 1. de Fide ad Reginas t. 3. oper. p. 316. Quare non potius, sicut apud Lazarum contentus fuit sermone ad resuscitandum puellam, & tenuit manum illius? nimirum ut ostenderet vivificum eius corpus, corpus enim est vitae. Igitur naturalis magis & vera est unio verbi &c. Et iterum paullò post pag. 317. Suscitavit Lazarum Christus, archisynagogi filiam & viduae filium. Iam quo pacto non vita secundùm naturam est, qui non solùm sermone repellere mortem poruit, sed etiam tactu manus? Erat enim consequens ac necessarium, vivificum esse corpus, quod. erat proprium vitae. Idem l. 4. in Ioh. cap. 23. t. 1. pag. 209. Quoniam caro cum vivificante Verbo coniuncta est, tota effecta est vivifica. & paullò pòst: Quamvis igitur Natura carnis, ut caro est, vivificare nequeat: facit tamen hoc, quia totam verbi operationem suscepit: Corpus enim est non cuius vis hominis, cuius caro prodesse non p-i est. Non enim Pauli aut Petri aut coeterorum, sed ipsius vitae & Salvatoris nostri Iesu Christi corpus, in quo Deitatis plenitudo corporaliter habitat, facere hoc potest. Huc facit & illud Damasceni lib. 3. O. F. c. 18. in fin. Natur aliter quidem non omnipotens erat: (humana Christi voluntas ac natura:) Ut autem DEI Verbi secundùm veritatem & naturam, facta omnipotens. Quae atque alia plurima his gemella piorum veterum dicta opponenda sunt non solùm illis Calvinianis, qui scribere non erubescunt, ad efficienda miracula non plus carnem Christi contulisse, quàm ad edita ab Apostolis miracula caro Apostolorum contulit, aut virga Mosis ad edenda Miracula Mosi profuit. (uti quidem habent verba Lamb. Danaei in exam. lib. de duabus nat. Chemn. p. 118. & in Vol. Oper. p. 137. Verùm etiam qui quidem largiuntur, naturam humanam (quat ut instrumentum àλόγῳadhibetur, non ut iseparatum, sed hypostaticè unitum) concurrere ad miracula: negant tamen, potentiam istam, quâ humana Christi natura miracula effecit, omnipotentiam esse, sed propugnare satagunt, quòd ea ab omnipotent a sit distincta. Quā

sententiam Wendelinus tenet, qui etiam Exerc. LIX. §. 29. ita contra nos in furgit: Quod si miracula facere nemo potest, nisi per communicatam omnipotentiam, utiApostolis quo& Prophetis eadem fuerit tribuenda: quando & himiracula fecerunt: quod tamen sanae mentis Theologus nemo admiserit. Ergò secundùm Wendelinum, humana Christi natura haut aliter nec aliâ, divinâ se. personaliter ipsi communicatâ, potentiâ concurrit ad miracula, quàm Apostoli: quia nempe aliàs iuxta ipsum, si humanae naturae per unionem personalem divina omnipotentia personaliter communicata fuit, quâ miracula fecit, sequitur, etiam Apostolis talem omnipotentiam communicatam fuisse, quando miracula ediderunt. Unde etiam porrò subfannans addit: Sed ecce novum communicationis genus! Etiam vox Christi fuit omnipotens. Imò vero Damnascenus disertè dicit, quòd nat. hum. facta fuerit omnipotens. Et patet etiam hoc inde, quia tota effecta est vivifica, ceu ex Cyrillo audivimus. Ast reponit Wendelinus nonnulla loca ex eod. Cy--lo aliisq; Patribus, in quibus doceatur, quòd ea quae in Christo divina sūt, Deit ati; quae humana, humanitati sint tribuēda. Verùm Orthodoxi pridem monuerunt, quòd Patres in huiusmodi dictis loquantur de naturis ex & in se consideratis: adeoque minimè nobis adversentur, ut qui ipsi fatemur, divina originaliter non nisi ad divinam naturam; humana originaliter non nisi ad hum. naturam esse referenda. Non fugit hoc Wendelinum. instat tamen: Quasi verò ita unquam aliquis deliraverit, ut divinae omnipotentiae opera, qualia sunt miracula, crediderit ab humana natura distinctè & per se consideratâ originaliter posse proficisci &c. Resp. sive fuerint, sive non fuerint haeretici, qui ita deliraverint: sufficit, quòd ita Patres orthodoxam sententiam voluerint exponere, ne quis scil. calumniandi ansam arriperet, ac si ob adsertam communicationem idiomatum docerent, naturam humanam divinae exae quatam esse, vel factam aut mutatam in divinam naturam: quemadmodum constat, quòd Calviniani, & inter hos cumprimis Wendelinus, tale quid ex nostrâ doctrinâ elicere, summopere, vanè tamen, nitantur. Sed hâc de re plura alibi. Evolvantur B. D. Sigwartus in Admon. Christ. de Irenico Paraei 4. l. 3. c. 3. art. 14. B. D. Gerlachius D. spp. Theol. part. post. Disp. 4. B. Schröderus in Sceptro Regali Christ, lib. 3. B. D. Hutterus in Expos. lib. Christ. Concord. p. 803. alii.)*

## 8:16
(v. 16. And he cured many that were ill. Corn. à Lapide in this place supplies from Luke 4, 40. by the imposition of hands. and adds: To wit, Christ did not disdain to touch with his most pure and divine hands those who were ulcerous, etc., so that he might show the force and efficacy of his divine touch by healing them all instantly. The same author also notes at Matt. 28, 18. that the words of Christ: all power is given to me, are understood by Cyril, Nyssen, Athanasius, and others properly concerning the human nature of Christ, but as he is man. In the same way also the learned John Tirinus explains the place. Quite rightly, contrary to the Socinian Greg. de Valentia himself, who in vol. 4, Disp. 1, q. 13, point 1, p. 319, writes: I say that omnipotence (and yet without this, divine touch cannot be attributed to Christ) is simply neither communicated, nor could it have been communicated to the humanity of Christ, so that Christ might be omnipotent even according to his human nature.
