The comparison, therefore, is instituted between John and others 1. not on account of his miraculous birth from aged parents. 2. not on account of the angelic announcement of his birth. 3. not on account of the accumulation of gifts. *(As indeed it seems to Maldonado, and other Jesuits, see Coster in Enchir. p. 99.)* 4. not on account of his pursuit of a more severe life. 5. not on account of his martyrdom: for in all these he had others as equals: but 1. on account of the double prophecy of Isaiah and Malachi. 2. on account of his office. *(For with his finger he pointed out the present Messiah, which the prophecy of Malachi also indicates.)* 3. On account of the θεφανείας mystery. *(B. Par. explains these members more prolixly in Homil. Acad. part. 2. p. 371. Bernard also recounts more prerogatives of John in his sermon on the privileges of John the Baptist. Conf. Chrysolog. serm. 27. also Chrysost. hom. on John. Meanwhile, Franc. Lucas Brugensis rightly notes in this place that the greatness is referred especially to the office of teaching and prophesying. Just as also Luc. c. 7, 27. adds Prophet. Corn. à Lapide also mentions that Cardinal Toledo notes from Ambrose and Hilary, that John is called greater by Christ, not absolutely, but only as a Prophet.)*

*( ὁμικρότερος the least. See similar examples of enallage in ch. 22, 13. Mark 4, 21.32.John 20, 29.ch. 13, 27.Acts 25, 10.1 Cor. 13, 13.ch. 15, 19.)* But he who is least in the kingdom of heaven, is greater than he (John) is. i.e., he who is least in the kingdom of heaven, that is, in the time of the New Testament, in which the Gospel concerning the kingdom of heaven, obtained through the death of Christ, shall be preached, is more excellent than he, namely as regards the kind of doctrine, since that will then be far more illustrious and more pleasant. Isidore of Pelusium, book 1, ep. 68. He who is perfect in the law, as John was, is altogether inferior to him who has been baptized into the death of Christ. See more in the Harm. Evang. of Chemnitz. John the Baptist was not greater than the Apostles, especially as it pertains to the world, to be illuminated by the revelation of divine truth. Some explain it thus. I, who have been held in the ecclesiastical ministry as lesser than John the Baptist, am truly greater than he. For in his passion Christ was humbled below all men. *(Chrysostom embraces this exposition in hom. 38, inasmuch as the Jews esteemed Christ as lesser than John, calling him a glutton and a wine-bibber, etc. The same also expressly rejects the interpretation of those who think it is said concerning the Apostles, or concerning the Angels. And the context favors the opinion of Chrysostom. For when Christ had so greatly commended the Baptist, and had brought back the multitude, who were doubting concerning the constancy of John, to better things, a greater plague could have followed for the others, who were forming a greater estimation of John because of these words than of Christ. Which error Christ wished to correct with these words, as Chrysostom warns in the aforementioned place, whom Theophylact and Euthymius follow in their custom, and very many of the more recent ones. Thus from the Orthodox Fathers and Doctors, Luther, Osiander, Hunn., also Mr. Dr. Friedlib and several others. The glossators of the Ernestine Bibles also follow this. From the Papists, Salmeron, Fr. Lucas, Corn. Jansenius, Corn. à Lapide, Tirinus, etc. Others, however, take it concerning the Apostles, the 70 Disciples, or even concerning some other most recent one of the ministers, who after the ascension of Christ is to preach the Gospel, which interpretation is of Bucer. And it also pleases the Blessed Dr. Quistorp at Luc. 7, 28. Pelargo in h. l. B. Par. H. E. p. 1287. Cameroni in Myroth. pag. 14. and others. Hugo Grotius embraces the same in such a way that he even rejects that which he accepts concerning Christ. B. D. Chemn. H. E. c. 56. makes mention of both, and gives the reader the option, which he himself has judged to be the simplest. B. D. Calixtus understands by the least in the kingdom of heaven here whosoever, who through faith has been made a participant of ιἱοθεσίας and of the eternal inheritance. But Christ is greater than John 1. by reason of His Deity. 2. by reason of the communicated divine Majesty etc. 3. by reason of the dignity of His office. For He Himself is θεάνσθρωπος and the Savior of the world. See Matth. 28, 18.Ioh. 6, 51.Col. 3, 9.Phil. 2, 9. 10.Eph. 1, 20. 21. He was, however, lesser, not only in the opinion of the common people, but also because He was made lower than the Angels Ps. 8, 6. and men, Ps. 22, 7. namely in the state of emptying. But Smalcius Phorin. against Disp. 6. D. Frantz. de rebus civi lib. p. 395. ineptly gathers from the fact that the least in the kingdom of heaven (by whom he understands any Christian in the N. T.) is said to be greater than John, that the doctrine of John should by no means be proposed to Christians as a rule of life, and that it does not pertain to the N. T. For even if we admit degrees between the revelations made to John and the Apostles, it is not to be gathered from thence that the doctrine of John pertains to us not at all.)*

*( In the kingdom of heaven i. e. OF GOD, as it is expounded by Luc. c. 7, 28. This metonymical locution is indeed very customary among the Orientals, just as Barth. Mayerus shows more fully in Phil. S. part. 2. p. 167. seqq. What is signified by the kingdom of heaven, has been indicated above at c. 3, 2. p. 145. and 146. as well as c. 4, 17. and elsewhere.)*

Latin:

v. 11. Inter natos mulierum i. e. inter eos, qui secundùm communem naturae cursum ex mulieribus nati. Confertur autem Iohannes hîc cum illis, qui ante eum vixerunt, non qui ipsum secuti erant. Illis praeponitur his verbis: his postponitur membro sequente.

Non est maior i. e. qui praestantiore functus fuerit officio, qui tam praeclaram & consolatione plenissimam doctrinam proposuerit. Comparatio igitur inter Iohannem aliosque instituitur 1. non propter miraculosum ex effoetis parentibus ortum. 2. non propter Angelicum nativitatis nuncium. 3. non propter donorum cumulum. *(Uti quidem videtur Maldonato, aliisq; Iesuitis V. Costerum in Enchir. p. 99.)* 4. non propter vitae severioris studium. 5. non propter martyrium: nam in his omnibus alios habuit pares: sed 1. propter duplex vaticinium Esaiae & Malachiae. 2. propter officium. *(Digito enim Messiam praesentem monstravit, quod etiam Malachiae vaticinium in dicat.)* 3. Propter, θεφανείας mysterium. *(Prolixiùs haec membra exponit B. Par. Homil. Acad. part. 2. p. 371. Plures etiam praerogativas Iohannis recenset Bernhardus serm. de Privileg iis Ioh. Baptistae. Conf. Chrysolog. serm. 27. it. Chrysost. hom. de Ioh. Interea rectè monet Franc. Lucas Brugensis in h. l. quòd magnitudo ad prophetandi docendimunus imprimis referatur. Sicuti etiam Luc. c. 7, 27. addit Propheta. Memorat quoque Corn. à Lapide, Card. Toletum ex Ambrosio & Hilario notare, Iohannem maiorem à Christo dici, non absolutè, sed Prophetam duntaxat.)*

*( ὁμικρότεροςminimus. Vid. simil. enall. exempla c. 22, 13. Marc. 4, 21.32.Ioh. 20, 29.c. 13, 27.Act. 25. 10.1. Cor. 13, 13.c. 15, 19.)* Qui verò minimus in regno coelorum, maior eo (Iohanne) est. i. e. qui minimus est in regno coelorum s. tempore N. T. quo praedicabitur Evangelium de regno coelorum, per Christi mortem parto, praeflantior eo est, nempe quoad genus doctrinae, quippe quae tum erit longè illustrior & iucundior. Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 1. ep. 68. Qui in lege perfectus est, ut erat Iohannes, omninò inferior eo est, qui in Christi mortem baptizatus est. Vid. plura in Harm. Evang. Chemn. Non maior fuit Ioh. Baptista Apostolis, quod praesertim attinet ad orbem terrarum, divinae veritatis patefactione illuminandum. Quidam sic exponunt. Ego qui in ministerio Ecclesiastico minor habitus sum Iohanne Baptista, verè sum maior illo. In passione enim Christus infra omnes homines humiliatus est. *(Amplectitur hanc expositionem Chrysostomus hom. 38. siquidem Iudaei Christum minoris fecetint, Iohanne, edacem illum appellantes & vini potatorem &c. Idem quoque disertè reiicit illorum interpretationem, tum qui de Apostolis, tum de Angelis id dictum putant. Et facit pro Chrysost. sententia contextus. Etenim cùm Christus tantopere Baptistam commendasset, ac multitudinem de Iohannis constantia ambigentem ad meliora reduxisset, maior sequi pestis potuisset coeteris, maiorem propter haec dicta de Iohanne, quàm de Christo existimationem facientibus. Quem errorem his verbis Christus corrigere voluit, monente Chrysostomo d. l. quem more suo sequuntur Theophyl. & Euthymius, & ex recentioribus plurimi. Ita ex Orthodoxis Bb. Dd. Lutherus, Osiander, Hunn. it. Dn. D. Friedlib aliique nonnulli. Sequuntur etiam Glossatores Bibliorum Ernestinorum. Ex Pontif. Salmeron, Fr. Lucas, Corn. Iansenius, Corn, à Lapide, Tirinus &c. Alii tamen de Apostolis, 70 Discipulis, imò de novissimo alio ex ministris, qui post ascensionem Christi praedicaturus sit Evangelium, accipiunt, quae interpretatio Buceri est. Arriderque etiam B. D. Quistorpio ad Luc. 7, 28. Pelargo in h. l. B. Par. H. E. p. 1287. Cameroni in Myroth. pag. 14. aliis. Hugo Grotius eandem ita amplectitur, ut eam, quae de Christo accipit, etiam reiiciat. B. D. Chemn. H. E. c. 56. utriusque, mentionem facit, optionemque Lectori dat, quam ipse iudicaverit simplicissimam. B. D. Calixtus per minimum in coelorum regno intelligit hîc quemcun-ue, qui per fidem particeps factus sit ιἱοθεσίας & haereditatis aeternae. Maior verò Iohanne Christus est 1. ratione Deitatis. 2. ratione communicatae divinae Maiestatis &c. 3. ratione officii dignitatis. Ipse enim est θεάνσθρωπος ac mundi Salvator. Vid. Matth. 28, 18.Ioh. 6, 51.Col. 3, 9.Phil. 2, 9. 10.Eph. 1, 20. 21. Minor autem fuit, non solùm opinione vulgi, verùm etiam quia minoratus fuit infra Angelos Ps. 8, 6. ac homines, Ps. 22, 7. nempe in statu exmanitionis. Ineptè verò Smalcius Phorin. contra Disp. 6. D. Frantz. de rebus civi lib. p. 395. ex eo, quòd minimus in regno coelorum (per quem ille quemlibet, Christianum in N. T. intelligit) maior Iohanne dicitur, colligit, quòd Iohannis doctrina minimè proponi debeat Christianis vivendi regula, quòd que ad N. T. ea non pertineat. Ut ut enim, gradus inter revelationes, Iohanni & Apostolis factas, admittamus, non tamen exinde colligendùm, quòd doctrina Iohannis ad nos minimè pertineat.)*

*( In regno coelorum i. e. DEI, prout exponitur à Luc. c. 7, 28. Est verò Orientalibus metonymica ista locutio admodùm usitata, quemadmodum uberiùs monstrat Barth. Mayerus Phil. S. part. 2. p. 167. seqq. Quid per regnum coelorum significetur, suprà indicatum ad c. 3, 2. p. 145. & 146. nec non c. 4, 17. & alibi.)*

## 11:12
v. 12. Violence is offered etc. Hilary: The glory of Israel, owed to the fathers, announced by the Prophets, offered by Christ, is occupied and seized by the faith of the Gentiles. Erasmus in Annor. It is occupied by force, or because of the crowd of those rushing in and striving to break in by force, so much did the time of the Gospel already urge. The kingdom of Heaven is called the new doctrine of the Gospel, to which the crowd was already flowing of its own accord, as if weary of Moses. Whence it follows: All the Prophets and the law until John. where he renders the reason why they are so eager to break in, since the time of the Mosaic law had already passed: Thus Chrysostom connects it. Philippus Melanchthon:

Not slothful, not timid, not yielding to the threats or terrors of the Devil, but struggling and fighting against the Devil. See by all means Chrysost. 2. Tim. 4. The sense is that John the Baptist, by his preaching, made much fruit, and converted many to Christ, who eagerly received the doctrine of the Gospel, and contended for the kingdom of heaven with such Zeal, as if they were attempting to break into it with a certain violence. Luc. 16, 16. *(In this way it is expounded in the Ernestine Bibles)* Βιάζεται is expounded by some passively, by some neutrally. Melanchthon expounds it neutrally. The kingdom of heaven breaks forth by force, proceeds, strives, and indeed by a force not corporal, but spiritual. It pushes through with power. It cannot be hindered by the Devil and the power of the world. The series of the text favors the passive signification. For the quality and excellence of the Church of the N. T. is described, which is twofold. For there is a more illustrious knowledge and frequency of worship in the N. T. than in the Old. The Syrian translates: The kingdom of heaven is received with violence. But he speaks of the calling of the Gentiles, as appears from the following verse in which it is added through αἰτιολογίαιν: For all the Prophets. As once the Israelites occupied the promised land of Canaan by force, so the faithful seize for themselves the sweetest promises of the Gospel, by praying, by suffering, by overcoming. John the Baptist first began to manifest the immense promise of the heavenly kingdom, saying: Repent, it has drawn near etc. But this promise of so excellent a benefit brought such force to the hearts of men, that it drew them, as if bound by certain chains, to the Baptist. *(But let us learn also from this, that the heavenly kingdom must be occupied with great effort and impetus. conf. above c. 7, 13.Luc. 13, 24. that adversities, the cross, temptations must be overcome, and one must break through etc.)*

Latin:

v. 12. Vis affertur &c. Hirarius: Gloria Israel, patribus debita, à Prophetis nunciata, à Christo oblata fide gentium occupatur & rapitur. Erasmus in Annor. Vioccupatur, vel ob turbam irruentium, ac vi conantium irrumpere, adeò iam urgebat tempus Evangelii. Regnum Coelorum dicitur nova Evangelii doctrina, ad quam iam ultrò confluebat turba, ceu pertaesa Mosen. Unde sequitur: Omnes Prophetae & lex usque ad Iohannem. ubi causam reddit, cur ita cuptant irrumpire, cùm Mosaica legis tempus iam praeteriisset: Sic connectit Chrysostomus. Philippus Melanchthon:

Non ignavi, non timidi, non cedentes minis aut terroribus Diaboli, sed certantes & praeliantes adversus Diabolum. Vid. omninò Chrysost. 2. Tim. 4. Sensus est, quòd Iohannes Baptista, suâ praedicatione multum fecerit fructum, ac multos ad Christum converterit, qui avidè susceperint Evangelii doctrinam, ac tanto Zelo ad regnum coelorum contenderint, ac si violentiâ quadam in illud irrumpere conarentur. Luc. 16, 16. *(Hoc modo exponitur in Bibliis Ernestinis)* Βιάζεται à quibusdam exponitur passivè, à quibusdam neutraliter. Melanchthon exponit neutraliter. Regnum coelorum vi erumpit, procedit, enititur, & quidem vi non corporali, sed spirituali. Es dringt mit Macht durch. Non potest impediri à Diabolo & mundi potentiâ. Passivae significationi favet series textûs. Describitur enim qualitas & praecellentia Ecclesiae N. T. quae duplex est. Illustrior enim cognitio & frequentia cultûs est in N. T. quàm in V. Syrus vertit: Regnum coelorum cum violentiâ accipitur. Loquitur autem de vocatione gentium, ut apparet ex versu seq. in quo per αἰτιολογίαιν subiungitur: Omnes enim Prophetae. Ut olim Israelitae promissam terram Canaam vi occupabant, sic fideles dulcissimas Evangelii promissiones ad se rapiunt, precando, patiendo, vincende, Iohannes Baptista primus coepit manifestare ingentem regni coelestis promissionem, dicens: Poenitentiam agite, appropinquavit &c. Haec autem tam praeclari beneficii promissio talem vim intulit hominum cordibus, ut eos quasi vinculis quibusdam ligatos ad Bapt. traheret. *(Discamus autem etiam hinc, magno conatu & impetu regnum coeleste occupandum esse. conf. suprà c. 7, 13.Luc. 13, 24. superandas esse adversitates, crucem, tentationes, ac perrumpendum &c.)*

## 11:13
v. 13. For all the Prophets and the law itself until John- It is commonly explained thus. All the Prophets and the law until John prophesied, that is, insofar as they prophesied concerning the coming of Christ, as if to say, those prophecies do not extend themselves beyond the time in which John was raised up. For this reason, a comma is placed after νόμος.. But if a comma is placed after ἕωςἸωάννου,, the sense will be: All the Prophets and the Law until John, that is, γεγονότες, who were, prophesied, that is, concerning the coming of Christ, as if to say, but not , they showed Christ present, as John did. And Tossanus embraces this latter opinion. (B. Par L. de Leg. Cerem § 27 explains this passage thus: Just as the Prophets prophesied concerning Christ in words, so the Ceremonial law did by types: wherefore as by the advent of the Messiah, whom John pointed out with his finger, the predictions of the Prophets were fulfilled, so the types of the law were abrogated. Compare Theol. Witteb. Refut. Catech. Racov. p. 3. 6. The Apostles and other religious men did indeed observe certain ceremonies around the beginning of the N. T., Act. 15, 29.c. 16, 3.c. 18, 18. but freely, so that the Jewish Synagogue might be buried with honor. Because, therefore, the types and consequently the ceremonial laws were abrogated by the advent of Christ (Conf. Act. 10, 11.c. 15, 6.Gal. 2, 13.c. 4, 10.c. 5, 2.Coloss. 2, 16. &c), not only do the Jews, Ethiopians, and some others act ineptly by retaining circumcision and other ceremonial rites: But also the Papists, by instituting a heap of theatrical ceremonies in imitation of the Levitical worship, when nevertheless the worship of the N. T. ought to be primarily spiritual. Christ speaks, however, in the said place only of the Prophets who predicted that Christ would come, and of those prophecies by which Christ's passion, death, &c. were predicted, but not absolutely of all the prophecies of the O. Test. Epiphanius warned of this long ago, when in heresy 66: Where John preached in the desert and showed, This is that Lamb of GOD, who takes away the sins of the world: there is no longer need for Prophets who would come and preach to us the advent of Christ from a virgin. It is furthermore evident that even after John the Baptist there were still Prophets. See Act. 2. & 1. Conf. Gaspar Sanctius Comm. in c. 11. Act. p. 229. Nor are the law and the Prophets said in this sense until John, as if the writings of Moses and the Prophets, and even the moral law itself, were antiquated by the advent of Christ. The contrary is evident from Matth. 5, 17. 18., but that the predictions concerning Christ were fulfilled by his advent, passion, death, &c. See Luc. 24, 27.44. &c. and the added word προεφήτευσαν. hints at this. Christ therefore speaks of the law prophesying through figures, not of the law instituting the morals of men. Now it is indeed evident that not the moral law, but the ceremonial law prefigured Christ through sacrifices. The Law can also be taken for the O. T., i.e., for the form of the polity and constitution of the Priesthood, which God had prescribed to the people of Israel through Moses . That it is taken in this way in this place is indicated by B. Par L. de Lege Dei § 4.)*

Latin:

v. 13. Nam omnes Prophetae & ipsa lex usad Iohannem- Communiter sic exponitur. Omnes Prophetae & lex usq; ad Iohannem prophetarunt, sc. quatenus prophetarunt de Christi adventu, q. d. prophetiae illae non extendunt se ultra tempus, quo suscitatus est Iohannes. Hac ratione comma ponitur post, νόμος. Si verò comma ponatur post ἕωςἸωάννου, sensus erit. Omnes Prophetae & Lex usque ad Iohannem, scil γεγονότες, qui fuerunt, prophetarunt sc. de adventu Christi, q. d. non autem, Christum praesentem ostenderunt, sicut Iohannes fecit. Et hanc posteriorem sententiam amplectitur Tossanus. *(B. Par L. de Leg. Cerem § 27. locum hunc ita exponit: Quemadmodum Prophetae verbis, ita lex Ceremonialis typis de Christo prophetavit: quare uti per adventum Messiae, quem Iohannes digito monstravit. Prophetarum vaticinia sunt completa, ita quolegis typi abrogati. Confer Theol. Witteb. Refut. Catech. Racov. p. 3. 6. Observarunt quidem circa initium N. T. Apostoli aliique religiosi viri quasdam ceremonias, Act. 15, 29.c. 16, 3.c. 18, 18. sed liberè, quò Synagoga nempe Iudaica cum honore sepeliretur Quia igitur typi ideoque leges ceremoniales per Christi adventum abrogatae sunt (Conf. Act. 10, 11.c. 15, 6.Gal. 2, 13.c. 4, 10.c. 5, 2.Coloss. 2, 16. &c) ineptè faciunt non solùm iudaei, Aethiopes aliique nonnulli, circumcisionem aliosque ritus ceremoniales retinentes: Verùm etiam Pontificii, ad imitationem cultûs Levitici congeriem theatricarum ceremoniarum instituentes, cùm tamen cultùs N. T. esse potissimùm spiritualis debeat. Loquitur autem Christus d. l. tantùm de Prophetis, qui Christum praedixerunt venturum, ac de iis prophetiis, quibus Christi passio, mors &c. praedicta, non verò absolutè de omnibus V. Test. prophetiis. Pridem hoc monuit. Epiph. quando haeresi 66. Ubi Iohannes praedicavit in deserto & ostendit, Hic est Agnus ille DEI, qui peccata mundi tollit: non ampliùs Prophetis opus est, qui veniant & praedicarent nobis Christi ex virgine adventum. Constat praetereà, quòd etiam, post Ioh. Bapt. adhuc fuerint Prophetae. Vid. Act. 2. & 1. Conf. Gaspar Sanctius Comm. in c. 11. Act. p. 229. Nec etiam hoc sensu lex & Prophetae dicuntur usad Iohannem, ac si Mosis ac Prophetarum scripta, ipsaque adeò etiam lex moralis Christi adventu sint antiquata. Contrarium patet ex Matth. 5, 17. 18. sed quòd vaticinia de Christo per eius adventum, pass. mortem &c. impleta. Vid. Luc. 24, 27.44. &c. idq; innuit adiectum verbum προεφήτευσαν. Loquitur igitur Christus de lege per figuras prophetante, non de lege hominum mores instituente. Iam verò constat, quòd non moralis lex, sed ceremonialis per sacrificia Christum praefigurârit. Potest quoque Lex accipi pro V. T. h. e. pro forma politiae ac constitutione Sacerdotii, quam Deus per Mosen populo Isr. praescripserat. Prout isto modo sumi h. l. indicat B. Par L. de Lege Dei § 4.)*

## 11:14
(v. 14. If you are willing to receive. i. e. to believe or to assent, John 1, 11. 12.Acts 8, 14.c. 11, 1. The Savior does not truly intend this by these words, as if He makes it arbitrary for them whether they wish to believe or not, but rather He indicates their obstinacy, as those who did not believe by the preaching of John. Thus generally D. Quistorp. on this passage. Compare Matt. 21, 32.)

*( He is Elias. Not as if the soul of Elias migrated into him by the Pythagorean metempsychosis, but because he is like Elias in freedom of speech, austerity of life, and adversity of fortune. See 1. Reg. 18, 18.c. 19, 2.2. Reg. 1, 18.Matth. 34, 47.c. 14. 4, 5. And hence Cap. 1. of John v. 21. the Baptist denies that he is Elias, namely as regards person, and as if the soul of Elias the Tishbite migrated into him (for thus the Jews understood it. See Kimchi alleged by Drusius on Malachi) but not indeed as regards spirit, i.e. the gifts of the Spirit, and office,Luc. 1, 17. Compare Mal. 4, 5.Matth. 17, 12.Marc. 9, 13.)*

Latin:

*(v. 14. Si vultis recipere. i. e. credere vel adsentiri, Ioh. 1, 11. 12.Act. 8, 14.c. 11, 1. Non verò hoc Salvator verbis hisce vult, ac si arbitrarium iis faciat, an velint credere, nec net sed illorum potiùs pertinaciam indicat, ut qui praedicatione Iohannis non credebant. Ita ferè D. Quistorp. in h. l. Conf. Matth. 21, 32.)*

*( Ipse est Elias. Non qs. anima Eliae in ipsum per Pythag metempsychosin in eum migrarit, sed quia dicendi libertate, vitae austeritate ac fortunae adversitate Eliae similis. Vid. 1. Reg. 18, 18.c. 19, 2.2. Reg. 1, 18.Matth. 34, 47.c. 14. 4, 5. Atque hinc Cap. 1. Iohannis v. 21. negat Baptista, se esse Eliam, nempe quoad personam, ac qs. Eliae Thesbitis anima in ipsum migrarit (ita enim Iudaei intelligebant. Vid Kimchius alleg. à Drusio ad Malach.) nō verò quoad spiritum i. e. dona Spiritûs, & officium,Luc. 1, 17. Conf. Mal. 4, 5.Matth. 17, 12.Marc. 9, 13.)*

## 11:15
(v. 15. He who has ears &c. let him attend, nor expect another Elijah or until Elijah the Tishbite returns in his own person. Concerning the absurdities of the Papists, who likewise persuade themselves that Elijah the Tishbite will return in his own person, it will be treated at Matth. 17, 17.)

Latin:

*(v. 15. Qui aures habet &c. attendat, nec expectet alium Eliam sive dum Elias Thesbites in propriâ personâ redeat. De Pontificiotū ineptiis, qui itidem sibi persuadent, Eliam Thesbitem in propriâ personâ rediturum, agetur ad Matth. 17, 17.)*

## 11:16
v. 16. But to what shall I liken &c. It is most familiar to Hebrew, Chaldean, and Syrian writers to begin parables with questions, as is to be seen in the Jerusalem Talmud, tractate on blessings, chapter 2.

It is like children etc. The children of the Jews very often used to play in the forum or in the streets under the open sky, Zach. 8, 5. and they would imitate now sacred weddings, now funeral processions. But so that individual things might be instituted with so much the greater frequency, they would for the most part provoke their contemporaries to the fellowship of the same game: but if some of these were so morose that they could not be persuaded to play, or would dissolve the game for trivial reasons, they would reproach them with this song μισανσθρωπίαν. But the Jews are accused here,

(Not, however, all: for many had confessed their sins to John and had believed, Matth. 3, 56.Luc. 7, 29. Very many also had adhered to Christ: But the Savior speaks only of those who had rejected the counsel of GOD against themselves, Luc. 7, 30. Compare Prov. 29, 9.)

that neither Lamentations, that is, the preaching of repentance made by John, nor did they wish to accept the Evangelical songs of the Son of man. *(The Blessed Pareus gives the same explanation of this passage in Harm. Evang. c. 151. page 306. and it is the same as Ambrose in sermon 80. likewise Cyril and Theophylact on c. 7 of Luke. Except that in these the Savior seems to look more to the life of both.)*

*( ἐἀγοραἰς in the marketplaces. So also, namely in the plural, the Arab and Ethiopian have it. The Syrian, however, reads in the singular, translating in the marketplace. Thus also the Persian. Truly, just as the Syrian, the Hebrew Interpreter of Matthew renders בשוק. And the reading in the singular number is favored, which also exists in the ancient Codex of Beza ἐ τῇ ἀγορᾷ )*

Latin:

v. 16. Sed cui adsimilabo &c. Familiarissimum est Hebraeis, Chaldaeis & Syris Scriptoribus, ut parabolas incipiant ab interrogationibus, ut videre est in Talmud Hierosolymitane tract. de bened. c. 2.

Similis est pueris &c. Iudaeorum liberi saepiùs in foro vel plateis sub dio ludebant, Zach. 8, 5. & modò sacra nuptialia, modò pompas funebres imitabantur. Ut autem singula tantò maiore frequentiâ instituerentur, plerumque coaevos suos ad eiusdem ludi societatem provocabant: sin horum quidam ita morosi essent, ut ad ludendum persuaderi non possent, vel levibus de causis ludum dissolverent, iis μισανσθρωπίαν hôc cantico exprobrabant. Accusantur verò hîc Iudaei,

*(Non tamen omnes: multi enim Iohanni peccata sua confessi erant ac crediderant, Matth. 3, 56.Luc. 7, 29. Plurimi etiam Christo adhaeserant: Sed loquitur Salv tantùm de illis, qui consiliū DEI contrase contemservnt, Luc. 7, 30. Confer Prov. 29, 9.)*

quòd nec lamenta i. e. praedicationem poenitentiae per Iohannem factam, nec cantilenas Evangelicas Filii hominis accipere voluerint. *(Eandem loci huius explicationem tradit B. Par. Harm. Evang. c. 151. pag. 306. estque eadem Ambrosii serm 80. Cyrilli item ac Theophylacti in c. 7. Lucae. Nisi quòd his magis ad vitam utriusque respicere Salvator videtur.)*

*( ἐἀγοραἰςin foris. Ita quoque, nempe in plurali, habent Arabs & Aethiops. Syrus tamen in sing. legit, vertens in plateâ. Sic Persa quoque. Planè verò ut Syrus, Matthaei Interpres Ebraeus reddit בשוק. Favetque lectioni in sing num. quod etiam in vetust. Bezae Cod. extat ἐ τῇ ἀγορᾷ)*

## 11:17
v. 17. And you have not danced. In the Syrian language there is a beautiful allusion in the words danced and wailed: For they are both of the same root, and do not differ, except only in conjugation רקרתוז you danced, ארקרווז you wailed. *(Some prove from this passage that dances are not simply forbidden to Christians, as certain Calvinists wish, since Christ takes a simile from them. J. G. Grossius, Doctor and Pastor of Basel, objects in Theatro Bibl. Vind. on this passage: among the Jews men and youths danced at least with men and youths: but not with wives or girls, and he tries to prove that from 1 Sam. 6 and 18. But although it may be easily conceded that it was sometimes done so by the Jews, it does not follow from this that dances between youths and girls were not also received into use among the same and approved by God. Furthermore, the Blessed Pareus treats this subject at greater length in L. de Coniug. §. 471. 472. which can be consulted.)*

We have lamented. The boys were indeed imitating the professional mourners who lamented at funerals, as the blessed Dr. Quistorpius on Matth. 9, 23. and the blessed Dr. Tarnovius on Amos c. 5, 16. p. 103. believe. But John Buxtorf in Lex. Talmudico Rabb. p. 766. thinks that the word ribis, is to be understood and repeated here, as their use was likewise in mourning among the Jews, as is evident from c. 9, 23. Matth., and as was also noted above. See also Grotius on this passage.)*

Latin:

v. 17. Et non saltastis. In linguâ Syria eâ est pulcra allusio in vocibus saltastis & planxistis: Su-t enim ambae eiusdem radicis, nec differunt, nisi coniugatione tantùm רקרתוז saltastis, ארקרווז planxistis. *(Probant ex h. l. nonnulli, choreas non, esse simpliciter prohibitas Christianis, ceu Calviniani quidam volunt, quippe cùm Christus simile inde capiat. Excipit I. G. Grossius D. ac Past. Basileensis in Theatro Bibl. Vind. ad h. l. apud Iudaeos saltasse saltem viros & iuvenes eum viris & iuvenibus: non verò cum uxoribus vel puellis, idque probare conatur ex 1. Sam. 6. & 18. Verùm licet, facilè concedatur, ita aliquando factum esse Iudaeis, non tamen hinc sequitur, quòd non etiam apud eosdem choreae iuvenes inter ac puellas usu fuerint receptae & à Deo approbatae. Coeterùm pluribus materiam hanc pertractat B. Par. L. de Coniug. §. 471. 472. qui potest evolvi.)*

*( Lamentati sumus. Imitabantur nempe pueri praeficas, in funeribus quae lamentabantur, uti B. D. Quistorpius ad Matth. 9, 23. ac B. D. Tarnovius ad Amos c. 5, 16. p. 103. existimant. Ioh. verò Buxtorffius Lex. Talmudico Rabb. p. 766. putat, subintelligendam hîc esse repetendam que vocem ribis, ut quarum usus itidem in luctu apud Iudaeos erat, ceu ex c. 9, 23. Matth. constat, ac suprà etiam notatum. Vid. quoque G-otius in h. l.)*

## 11:18
v. 18. John came, neither eating, viz. common foods, nor drinking, viz. wine. Luke 7, 33. *(add Matt. 3, 4. Luke 1, 1. Mr. Dr. Walther in H. B. understands it concerning the promiscuous and customary manner. But the Papists ineptly strive to establish the Monastic life by the example of John the Baptist. Against which error it will be disputed in Analect ad Luc. 7. 33.

*( He hath a devil. The Jews slandered John, who lived most strictly, because he does not live naturally, but is sustained by a devil, just as Matthias Flacius explains these words, or, as they are explained in the Ernestine Bibles, and also by the Blessed Doctor Hunnius, that he is agitated by a devil, or, as it seems to the Blessed Pareus in Harm. Evang. p. 306, that he proposes a diabolical doctrine; or according to Doctor Osiander in Gloss. h. l. that he is obsessed by some evil Spirit, and hence flees the company of men.)*

Latin:

v. 18.Venit Iohannes, nec edens, sc. vulgares cibos, nec bibens, sc. vinum. Luc. 7, 33. *(add Matth. 3, 4.Luc. 1, 1. Dn. D. Walth. in H. B. accipit de more promiscuo & usitato. Ineptè verò Iohannis Baptistae exemplo Monasticam vitam Pontificii stabilire satagunt. Contra quem errorem disputabitur in Analect ad Luc. 7. 33.)*

*( Daemonium habet. Calumniabantur Iudaei Iohannem renuissimè victitantem, quòd non physicè vivat, sed à Daemone sustentetur, uti quidem Matthias Flacius ista verba exponit, vel, uti eadem in Bibliis Ernestinis, itemque à B. D. Hunnio exponuntur, quòd à Daemone agitetur, vel, quod B. Parenti in Harm. Evang. p. 306. videtur, quòd doctrinam proponat Diabolicam; vel iuxta D. Osiandrum in Gloss. h. l. quòd obsessus sit à malo aliquo Spiritu, atque hinc hominum consortia fugiat.)*

## 11:19
v. 19. The Son of man is come eating and drinking, that is, in the common manner, and indeed even with sinners. He takes part in banquets. *(The Pharisees bore this very grievously, and on this account traduced the Savior before the people. Conf. Matth. 9, 11. Marc. 2, 16. )* *( οἰνοπότης |

*( οἰνοπότης a winebibber. Thus indeed the Jews slandered him. But it must be known that in Hebrew שבר or שותהייז & thus h. l. οἰνοπότης is said not of anyone drinking wine, but of one who indulges in wine, as is clear from Proverbs 31, 4. Amos 6, 6. Furthermore, by the example of Christ it is entirely permitted to attend banquets, as the Blessed Doctor Tarnovius also well advises in Comm. in Amos 6, 6. Conf. Matth. 9, 10.Luc. 14, 10.Ioh. 2, 2. But why the Savior wished to attend banquets, especially those of publicans, the Blessed Pareus explains at length in hom. Acad. part. 2. p. 723. seqq.)*

But wisdom is justified of her children. Wisdom is the Son of GOD. *(Namely, hypostatic Wisdom, See Prov. 8, 12.Luc. 7, 35.c. 11, 49.1. Cor. 1, 24.Col. 2, 3. & it is so explained by most Interpreters. Hugo Grotius however in h. l. wishes the name σοφίας here to be nothing other than what is Luc. 7, 30. βουλὴτου θεοῦ. Which also pleases the Blessed Doctor Calixtus in Concord. Evang. p. 151.)* Her children are called listeners. *(For those are also named children in Holy Scripture who are brought to some thing, or to whom it pertains, as is evident from Sirac. 4, 12.Matth. 8, 12.c. 23, 15.Eph. 2, 3.c. 5, 8. &c.)* who ought to hear her words no otherwise than children receive the admonitions of parents and reverently. *(In the same way the Blessed Pareus also explains in Harm. Evang. c. 151. P. 306.)* But to justify h. l. κατ᾽ ἀντίφρασιν is to call to justice indeed to condemn to the verdict to lead and to justify or even by the children i. e. who think themselves to be genuine children of wisdom, & the wisest of all men. *(In this way he takes the word To justify, the blessed D. Luther, both here and Luc. 7, 35. in the German version, and in vol. 4 of the Jena Latin edition, p. 320; likewise D. Brentius in the Würtemberg Confession, D. Förster in the Hebrew Lexicon, D. Osiander and D. Hunnius in the explanation of this passage. Nor is it unusual for the Holy Scripture to take the word to justify for to condemn. See Es. 43, 9. 2. Sam. 15, 4. and compare Drusius in Hebrew Questions, q. 79. Indeed, Camerarius observes on this passage that the word δικαιοῦν occurs in such a meaning even in Thucydides, and Pfochenius approves it. By children, however, are understood degenerate children, Exod. 4, 22. Deut. 32, 5 Es. 1, 4.)* Others explain it thus. There are not wanting some elect who acknowledge and proclaim God's wisdom and goodness in their own calling. Thus Piscator, who also disapproves of Luther's version, which nevertheless is congruent with the text and the words. Tossanus follows Piscator, and therefore explains it thus: Although the Pharisees and the stubborn Jews do not receive the doctrine of the Gospel, in which the most wise counsel of God concerning the redemption of the human race is proposed, yet it is justified, i.e., is acknowledged as true and salutary by its children, i.e., by the truly wise, who are endowed with heavenly grace through the Holy Spirit, Luc. 7, 20. by the disciples or by those who love and seek wisdom, who are called אנשי במה men of wisdom. *(Thus also in the present passage, Chrysostom, Jerome, Augustine, Hilary, Theophylact, and Euthymius take the word to justify, whom the Papists commonly follow. This opinion is favored by the fact that the word to justify is taken in this way both elsewhere, see Ps. 50, 6. Luc. 16, 15. 1. Tim. 3, last Iac. 2, 21., and in the parallel passage Luc. 7, 29., where it is said of the people and the publicans that they justified God, but the Pharisees despised the counsel of God. Compare more on this matter in the blessed Pareus, Book on Justification, §. 3. Furthermore, the blessed D. Quistorpius embraces this interpretation in this passage, and likewise the blessed D. Glassius, Sacred Grammar, p. 605. Compare the same in the cited place, p. 323; and the same men note that the particle καὶ is taken adversatively in this passage, just as it occurs elsewhere in the New Testament, as Matth. 1, 25. c. 12, 39. c. 13, 22. But especially the blessed D. Tarnovius confirms that exposition at greater length in Biblical Exercises, p. 147 ff. The same opinion is approved by Thomas Garakero in the book on the style of the New Testament, p. 81)* Scultetus in Observations, c. 34, disapproves of the exposition of Beza and Piscator. For Christ does not say ἀλλὰ, but καὶ, and after the word ἁμαρτωλῶν a period should have been placed. The scope of Christ also is to accuse the contumacy of the Jewish people, and the perversity of their judgment, to argue and exaggerate by the mention of a most iniquitous thing. The sentence is pronounced as if in a judgment concerning wisdom by those who, as children, ought to hear it and submit themselves to its judgment. (Finally, neither is that to be passed over in silence, that Jerome in this place and Ambrose in chapter 7, 35 of Luke read, by his works as if in the Greek it were ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργον ἀυ τῆς.. Just as the Persian and likewise the Ethiopian have read. But the more common reading, which has ἐπὸ τῶν τὸκνων ἀυτῆς, is confirmed by the Arab, as one who explicitly has (in the Roman edition it is read defectively ) by his children, Thomas Gravius in his Annotations on the Persian version of the Gospels suspects that the Syrian likewise read it so, inasmuch as the Syriac denotes works, and workers or servants and cultivators, and these meanings are accustomed to be distinguished by the varied placement of a single point. The latter meaning, however, is more suitable to this place, the same man proves from that, both because those who give effort to the study of wisdom are accustomed to be called sons by the Orientals, and because Luke 7, 35 where the same sentence is held, the Syrian renders word for word: by his children. Indeed Tremellius also translates by his cultivators, which also pleases Dr. Tarnovius in Exerc. p. 148, Boderianus in the Royal Bibles by his servants, Ludovicus de Dieu however in his Animadversions on this place defends the interpretation by his works, and adds from Jerome: For wisdom does not seek the testimony of the voice, but of works. The same man brings forward besides another exposition of this place, yet one by no means free from every scruple, as he himself acknowledges. Otherwise, the received reading in the Greek text, which has ἀπὸ τῶν τέκνων ἀυτῆς,, both the most ancient and most approved codices approve so much, that hardly one or another manuscript codex is found which offers the other reading to be seen.)

Latin:

v. 19. Filius hominis edit & bibit, sc. vulgari modo, quin & cum peccatoribus. Interest conviviis. *(Perquam dolenter hoc ferebant Pharisaei, atque isto nomine Salvatorem apud populum traducebant. Conf. Matth, 9, 11.Marc. 2, 16.)*

*( οἰνοπότηςbibaculus. Ita nempe calumniabantur Iudaei. Sciendum verò. quòd Ebraeis שבר aut שותהייז & sic h. l. οἰνοπότης dicatur non quivis vinum bibens, sed qui vino in dulget, ceu liquet ex Proverb. 31, 4. Amos. 6, 6. Coeterùm exemplo Christi omninò conviviis interesse licet, uti benè etiam monet B. D. Tarnovius Comm. in Amos. 6, 6. Conf. Matth. 9, 10.Luc. 14, 10.Ioh. 2, 2. Cur verò Salvator conviis interesse voluerit, cum primis publicanorum, prolixè exponit B. Par. hom. Acad. part. 2. p. 723. seqq.)*

Sed iustificata est sapientia à filiis suis. Sapientia est Filius DEI. *(Sapientia nempe hypostatica, Vid. Prov. 8, 12.Luc. 7, 35.c. 11, 49.1. Cor. 1, 24.Col. 2, 3. & ita exponitur ab Interpp. plerisq; Hugo tamen Grotius in h. l. nomen σοφίας hîc nihil aliud esse vult, quàm quod Luc. 7, 30. est βουλὴτου θεοῦ. Id quod etiam B. D. Calixto in Concord. Evang, p. 151. placet.)* Eius filii dicuntur auditores. *(Nominantur enim in Sc. S. filii etiam illi, qui alicui rei adducti sunt, s. ad quos ea pertinet, ceu patet ex Sirac. 4, 12.Matth. 8, 12.c. 23, 15.Eph. 2, 3.c. 5, 8. &c.)* qui ipsius verba non aliter audire, ac filii parentum monita & reverenter excipere de bebant. * (Eod. modo exponit quoque B. P. Harm. Evang. c. 151. P. 306.)* Iustificare verò h. l. κατ᾽ ἀντίφρασιν est in ius vocare imò condemnare zur Gchuse f-hren und rechifertigen vel etiam à filiis i. e. qui existimant, se esse genuinos sapientiae filios, & onium hominum sapientissimos. *(Hoc modo accipit verbum iustificandi B. D. Lutherus tum hîc & Luc. 7, 35. in vers Germ. tum t. 4. Lat Ienes. p. 320. item D. Brentius in Confess. Wūrtenb. D. Fōrsterus in Lex. Ebr. D. Osiander ac D. Hunnius in Expl. huius loci Neque etiam insolens est, Scripturae sacrae, verbum iustificare accipere pro condemnare. Vid. Es. 43, 9.2. Sam. 15, 4. ac conf. Drusium in Qq. Ebr. q. 79. quin apud Thucydidem in tali significatione verbum δικαιοῦν occurrere, observat Cameratius in h. l. approbatque Pfochenius. Per filios autem intelliguntur filii degeneres, Exod. 4, 22.Deut. 32, 5Es. 1, 4.)* Alii ita exponunt. Non desunt aliqui electi, qui DEI sapientiam & bonitarem in suâ vocatione agnoscunt ac praedicant. Ita Piscator, qui etiam Lutheri versionem, quae tamen textui & verbis est congrua, improbat. Piscatorem sequitur Tossanus, ideò sic exponit: Quamvis Pharisaei & pervicaces Iudaei Evangelii doctrinam, in quâ sapientissimum DEI consilium de redemtione generis humani proponitur, non recipiant, tamen iustificatur i. e. vera & salutaris agnoscitur à filiis suis i. e. à verè sapientibus, qui per Sp. Sanctum coelesti gratiâisunt donati, Luc. 7, 20. à discipulis aut ab iis, qui amant & quaerunt sapientiam, qui אנשי במה viri sapientiae dicuntur. *(Ita etiam praesenti loco verbum iustificandi accipiunt Chrysostomus, Hieronymus, Augustinus, Hilarius, Theophylactus, Euthymius, quos sequuntur Pontificii communiter. Favet huic sententiae, quòd tum alibi, Vide Ps. 50, 6.Luc. 16, 15.1. Tim. 3, ult Iac. 2, 21. verbum iustificandi ita accipitur, tum in loco parallelo Luc. 7, 29. Ubi de dopulo ac publicanis dicitur, quòd Deum iustificarint, Pharisaei autem consilium DEI contemserint. Conf. plura in hanc rem apud B. Par. L. de Iustif. §. 3. Amplectuntur portò interpretationem hanc B. D. Quistorpius in h. l. itemque B. D. Glassius Gr. S. p. 605. Conf. idem l. c. p. 323. atque hinc etiam particulam καὶ adversativè h. l. accipi, iidem notant, quomodo alibi quoque in N T. occurrit, uti Matth. 1, 25.c. 12, 39.c. 13, 22. Cumprimis verò expositionem illam pluribus conf--mat B. D. Tarnovius Exerc. Bibl. p. 147. seqq. Eadem sen tetia approbatur Thomae Garakeroin lib. de stylo N. T. p. 81)* Bezae & Piscatoris expositionem improbat Scultetus in Obs. c. 34. Christus enim non dicit ἀλλὰ, sed καὶ, ac post vocem ἁμαρτωλῶν punctum fuisset ponendum. Scopus etiam Christi est, accusare contumaciam populi Iudaici, & perversitatem iudicii ipsorum, mentione rei iniquissimae arguere & exaggerare. Sententia pronunciatur tanquam in iudicio de sapientia ab illis, qui illam ut pueri audire & se eius iudicio submittere debeant. *(Deniq; nec illud praetereundum silentio est, quòd Hieronymus in h. l. & Ambrosius in c. 7, 35. Lucae legant, ab openibus suis ac si in Graeco esset ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργον ἀυ τῆς. Quomodo & Persa itemq; Aethiops legerunt. Sed communior lectio, quae habet ἐπὸ τῶν τὸκνων ἀυτῆς, confirmatur ab Arabe, ut qui disertè habet (in edit Romanâ vitiose legitur ) à filiis suis, Syrum pariter ita legisse suspicatur Thomas Gravius Annot. in Persicam Evangeliorum versionem, siquidem Syriacum opera, & operarios seu servas ac cultores notet, & unius puncti vario situ significationes istae distingvi soleant. Posteriorem verò significationem huic loco magis convenire, probat idem inde, tum quia sapientiae studio operam dantes Orientalibus filu soleant appellari, tum quia Lucae 7, 35. ubi eadem sententia habetur, Syrus ad verbum reddat: filiis suis. Sanè Tremellius quoque vertit à cultaribus suis, quod & D. Tarnovio in Exerc. p. 148. placet, Boderianus in Bibliis Regiis à servis suis, Ludovicus tamen de Dieu in Animadv. ad h. l. interpretationem ab operibus suis tuetur, additque ex Hieronymo: Sapientia enim non petit vocis testimonium, sed operum. Affert praeterea idem aliam loci huius expositionem, minimè tamen omni scrupulo carentem, ceu ipse agnoscit. Coeterùm receptam lectionem in textu Graeco, quae habet ἀπὸ τῶν τέκνων ἀυτῆς, adeò Codd. & antiquissimi & probatissimi approbant, ut vix unus atque alter reperiatur Codex MS. qui alteram lectionem conspiciendam praebeat.)*

## 11:20
(v. 20. Ὀνειδίζειν ταςπόλεις. Vulg. to upbraid the cities. Lud. de Dieu is more pleased by: to expose the cities to reproach i. e. to dishonor them with opprobrium. The greater the benefit exhibited, the greater the punishment that awaits the ungrateful. See Luke 12, 47 John 15, 22 Rom. 2. 4. 5)

( Ξοραζὶν i. e. miracles. In which meaning the same word is used above c. 7, 22. below c. 14. 2. and Luc. 9, 1. But miracles are called δυνάμεις, because they are brought forth by divine virtue and power or by that which is divinely granted.)

Latin:

*(v. 20. Ὀνειδίζειν ταςπόλεις. Vulg. exprobrare civitatibus. Lud. de Dieu magis arridet: probro exponere civitates i. e. opprobrio eas dehonestare. Quò maius exhibitum beneficium, eò maior ingratos manet poena. Vid. Luc. 12, 47.Ioh, 15, 22.Rom. 2. 4. 5)*

*( Ξοραζὶν i. e. miracula In qua significatione eadem vox adhibetur suprà c. 7, 22. infrà c. 14. 2. it Luc. 9, 1. Dicuntur verò miracula δυνάμεις, quia virtute ac potestate divinâ vel divinitùs concessâ eduntur.)*

## 11:21
v. 21. Χοραζὶν. Some Codices have χοροζαὶν, which reading the old interpreter acknowledges, and Jerome confirms, who says that in his age it was a desert, at the second milestone from Capernaum. (That this same thing, that Jerome confirms the reading of the Vulgate interpreter in this place, Casaubon also asserts: from which, however, Morinus concludes less firmly in his Exercit. that Casaubon prefers the Vulgate translation to the Greek text. Furthermore, the Papists commonly establish that Corozain is a city beyond the sea of Galilee. Certainly the Savior understands by the name Corazin a certain most famous city, now devastated, as will be warned more fully below at Luc. 10, 13.)

( If the mighty works had been done &c. Jerome raises a doubt here: Should not the cause of incredulity, and of the consequent damnation, be imputed to God, in that He did not take care that repentance be preached to the Tyrians and Sidonians, since if this had been done, they would have been converted. He answers, however, that we are ignorant of the judgments of GOD and the sacraments of individual dispositions. He adds, that it was the purpose of the Lord not to exceed the borders of Judea, lest He should give a just occasion of persecution to the Pharisees and Priests. He concludes: Do not seek the times, when you behold the salvation of the believers. Bede likewise professes his ignorance here: Why, he writes, it was preached to those who were unwilling (namely the Corazaeans and Capernaites) and not to these (the Tyrians and Sidonians) who would have believed long ago, it is for Him to know, whose ways are all mercy and truth. Others answer that a distinction must be made here between the calling itself, and the manner of the calling. Although the Sidonians and Tyrians were not called by that extraordinary manner of calling of which Christ speaks in this place, namely by miracles, as were the inhabitants of Corazin and Bethsaida, it is not to be inferred from thence by any means that they were not called, as indeed Wendelinus in Exerc. 18. §. 43. strives to persuade the reader from this place. The contrary is evident from Holy Scripture. See below c. 15, 21. 22Marc. 7, 24.Actor. 21, 3. 4. And hence it is that the Savior does not excuse the Tyrians and Sidonians from all but from as much as that of the inhabitants of Corazin &c. was, sin. Nor does the saying stand in the way) John 15:24 as will be shown in the notes to that passage. That the Tyrians and Sidonians were indeed called, we shall prove at greater length at Luke 10:13. Meanwhile, if it pleases, let the following be unrolled: Bb. Dd. Frantzius, On the Interpretation of the Holy Scriptures, Oracle 12; Meisnerus, Ἀνσθρωπολ. Sacred Disputations 13, Q. 2, § 10; B. Par., Collection of Isagogics, Disputation on Predestination, ch. 6, § 11.

They would have repented in ashes. The ancients were accustomed to be sprinkled with ashes and covered in sackcloth during more serious mourning, Jonah 3:6, Esth. 4:1. (Compare Isaiah 58:5, Jer. 6:26, ch. 25:34, Lamentations 2:10, Dan. 9:3. From many profane writers, Mr. Dilherrus in Philological Dialogues 46, Mr. Ioh. C. Dietrich in Philological Disputation on the Use of Reading Secular Scripture in Higher Literature on Judith XIV, v. 15, Kirchm. book 2 on Funerals, Rom. ch. 11, p. 208 seqq., Petrus Faber book 2, Semesters, ch. 10, p. 110, 111, derive this custom. It pleases me at least to note here that in almost all languages the word sackcloth has remained after the confusion of tongues: [in use among the Greeks σάκκος,, Hebrew שק,, Chaldean םקא,, Syrians saco, Arabs , Ethiopians . So also among the Westerners, it is called sac by the French, sacco by the Italians and Spaniards.] The same can be affirmed of almost all other peoples, so that they render it as if testified by this very fact, since sackcloth or haircloth is a sign of repentance and mourning, that all after the fall of the protoplasts are sinners and lack the glory Rom. 3:23 and thus have need of constant repentance. See more in the Annotations to Apoc. 11:3.) The Savior therefore wishes to say: Such is your obstinacy and ingratitude that the Tyrians and Sidonians, who are Gentiles, are righteous in comparison to you, and that you provide them with this excuse, that if the Gospel had been preached to them also, they would not have rejected it with such pertinacity, Ezech. 16:51, Tossanus in the marginal notes. (From the fact that Christ says here that those Gentiles would have done penance if they had seen the signs that were performed in Chorazin and Bethsaida, theologians rightly conclude that future contingencies are also an object of divine omniscience. See B. D. Martini in A. C. Disputation IIX, Q. 5 seqq., B. Par. book on Providence, ch. 6, § 8, to whom, from the Papists, who assert the same with us, add Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, Iansenius, Conzenius, and others on this passage.

Likewise Ludovicus Molina on the first part of Thomas, volume 1, art. 13, q. 14, Disputation 17; Hannib. Rosselus in Pymander of Mercurius Trismegistus, vol. 4 seqq.; Alphonsus Mendoza, Theological Controversies, Q 7; Ignatius Der Kennis on the One and Triune God, Disputation IIX, ch. 6. But this orthodoxy is to be opposed both to the Photinians—see Socinus, Theological Prelections, ch. 10; Val. Smalcius in Refutation of D. Frantzius, p. 427; Crellius, book on God and Divine Attributes, ch. 24, who bitterly attack it—and to the wavering Arminians. See Simon Episcopus, Disputation 4, § 10; and also to Ioannes Cameron himself, to whom in Myrothecium it likewise seems hardly credible that God foresaw the future assent of the Tyrians and Sidonians, provided those signs had been performed among them. But let someone say: If God foresaw, and indeed certainly, that the Tyrians would have believed, had other signs been given among them, such as those at Bethsaida etc., it follows that God did not offer them sufficient grace by which they could have been converted. I respond by denying the consequence. For, just as the Sodomites had Lot, the herald of righteousness: so the Tyrians and Sidonians were neighbors to the Israelite people, who by no means begrudged them the word of God. But since the Tyrians and Sidonians cared little for, or rather despised, this ordinary and sufficient means of conversion, God was certainly not bound to exhibit extraordinary means, namely miracles, to them. It suffices that He willed to convert them through ordinary means, and that they, if only they had not maliciously resisted, could have been converted even through such means. In short: The Tyrians did not lack sufficient grace, but abundant grace. See Bb. Dd. Hunnius on this passage. Meisnerus Ἀνσθρωπ. sacred Disp. 13. Q. 2. §. 16.)

Latin:

v. 21. Χοραζὶν. Nonnulli Codd habent χοροζαὶν, quam lectionem vetus interpres agnoscit, confirmatque Hieronymus, qui sua aetate desertum fuisse ait, in secundo lapide à Capernaum. *(Idem hoc, quòd Hieronymus Vulg. interpretis lectionem h. l. confirmet, adserit quoque Casaubonus: ex quo tamen minùs firmiter Morinus in Exercit. concludit, quòd Casaubonus vulgatam translationem Graeco textui praesferat. Pontificii porrò communiter statuunt, Corozain esse urbem ultra mare Galilaeae. Sanè intelligit Salvator nomine Corazin celeberrimam quandam urbem, nunc devastatam, uti infrà ad Luc. 10, 13. pluribus monebitur.)*

*( Si editae fuissent virtutes &c. Movet hîc Hieronymus dubium: Annon Deo imputari debeat causa incredulitatis, indesecutae damnationis, eò quòd non cur averit Tyriis ac Sidoniis praedicari poenitentiam, cùm si hoc factum fuisset, fuissent illi conversi. Respondet autem, ignorare nos DEI iudicia & singularum dispositionum sacramenta. Addit, propositum fuisse Domino, Iudaeae fines non excedere, ne iustam Pharisaeis ac Sacerdotibus occasionem per secutionis daret. Concludit: Non quaeras tempora, cùm credentium intueris salutem. Beda itidem ignoranitam suam hîc profitetur: Cur, scribit, nolentibus (nempe Corazaeis ac Capernaitis) praedicatum sit, & non his (Tyriis ac Sydoniis) qui olim credere voluerunt, ipsius est scire, cuius universae viae misericordia & veritatis. Alii respondent, quòd distinguendum hic sit inter vocationem ipsam, & vocationis modum. Licet pro inde non extraordinario illo vocationis modo, de quo Christus h. l. loquitur, nempe per miracula, uti incolae Corazin ac Bethsaidae, Sidonii ac Tiril vocati fuerint, exinde tamen hautquaquam inferendum, quòd non fuerini vocati, uti quidem Wendelinus Exerc. 18. §. 43. Lectori ex h. l. persuadero satagit. Contrarium ex Sc. S. patet. Vid. infrà c. 15, 21. 22Marc. 7, 24.Actor. 21, 3. 4. Atque hinc est, quod Salvator Tirios & Sidonios non ab omni, sed à tanto, quantū incolarum Corazin &c. fuit, pecc. excuset. Nec obstat dictum Ioh. 15, 24. uti in notis ad illum locum ostendetur. Quòd verò Tyrii ac Sidonii omninò fuerint vocati, ad Luc. 10, 13. prolixiùs probabimus. Evolvantur intereà, si lubet, Bb. Dd. Frantzius de Interp. Sc. S. Oraculo 12. Meisnerus Ἀνσθρωπολ. Sacrae Disp. 13. Q. 2. § 10. B. Par. Coll. Isagog. Disp. de Praedest. c. 6. § 11.)*

In cinere resipuissent. Cinere adspergi & sacco operiti consueverunt antiqui in graviori luctu, Ionae 3, 6. Esth. 4, 1. *(Conf. Esaiae 58, 5. Ier. 6, 26.c. 25, 34. Thren. 2, 10. Dan. 9, 3. E Prophanis Scriptoribus plusculis morem hunc deducunt Dn. Dilherrus in Dial. Philol. 46. Dn. Ioh. C. Dietrich in Disp. Philol. de Us. lect. Script. secul. in altiori litter ad Iudith. XIV. v. 15. Kirchm. l. 2. de Funer. Rom. c, 11. p. 208. seqq. Petrus Faber l. 2. Semestr. c. 10. p. 110. 111. Id saltem h. l. monere adhuc placet, quòd in omnibus penè Linguis vox saccus post linguarum confusionem remanserit: [Graecis in usu σάκκος, Ebr שק, Chald. םקא, Syris saco, Arabibus Aethiopibus Sic & Occidentalibus, Gallis dicitur sac, Italis & Hispanis sacco. Idem de reliquis affirmari populis ferè omnibus potest,] ut hoc ipso quasi testatum reddant, cùm saccus s. cilicium sit poenitentiae & luctûs signum, quòd omnes post lapsum protoplastorum sint peccatores, ac careant gloriâ Rom. 3, 23. adeoq; iugi poenitentiâ opus habeant. Plura vid. in Annot. ad Apoc. 11, 3.)* Vult igitur Salvator dicere: Tanta est vestra obstinatio & ingratitudo, ut Tyrii & Sidonii, qui sunt gentiles, comparatione vestri sint probi, utque illis hanc excusationem suppeditetis, quòd si ipsis quoque fuisset praedicatum Evangelium, quòd non reiecerint illud tantà pertinaciâ, Ezech. 16, 51. Tossanus in notis marg. *(Ex eo verò, quòd Christus hîc dicit, gentiles illos poenitentiam fuisse acturos, si signa, quae in Corazin & Bethsaidâ edita, vidissent, rectè colligunt Theologi, quòd etiam futura contingentia divinae omniscientiae obiectum sint. Vid. B. D. Martini in A. C. Disp. IIX. Q. 5. seqq. B. Par L. de Provid. c. 6. § 8. quibus ex Pontificiis, idem nobiscum hoc adserentibus, adde Cornelium à Lapide, Tirinum, Iansenium, Conzenium aliosque in h. l.

Ludovicum item Molinam in primam Thomae partem tomo 1. art. 13. q. 14. Disp. 17. Hannib. Rosselum in Pymand. Mercurii Trism. t. 4. seqq. Alphonsum Mendozam Controv. Theolog. Q 7. Ignatium Der Kennis de Deo uno & Trino Disp. IIX. c. 6. Opponenda verò orthodoxia haec tum Photinianis, vide Socinum Praelect. Theol. c. 10. Val Smalcium in Ref. D. Frantzii p. 427. Crellium lib. de Deo & Attrib. div. c. 24. acriter illam impugnantibus, tum Arminianis haesitantibus. Vid Simon Episcopus Disp. 4. §. 10. tum ipsi quoq; Ioanni Cameroni, cui in Myroth. itidem vix credibile videtur, Deum praevidisse adsensum futurum Tyriorum & Sidoniorum, modò illa signa inter eos fuissent patrata. Sed dicat aliquis: Si Deus praevidit, ac certo quidem, Tyrios credituros fuisse, sit alia signa inter eos fuissente dita, qualia Bethsaidae &c. sequitur, quòd Deus non obtulerit eis gratiam sufficientem, quâ potuerint converti. Resp negando consequentiam. Etenim, sicuti Sodomitae habuerunt Lothum Iustitiae praeconem: ita Tyrii & Sidonii fuerunt vicini populo Israēlitico, qui verbum Dei minimè illis invidit. Hoc verò ordinarium ac sufficiens conversionis medium cùm Tyrii & Sidonii parùm curarint, imò contemserint, Deus sanè minimè obstrictus fuit, ut extraordinaria media, miracula nempe, iis exhiberet Sufficit, quòd per media ordinaria convertere eos voluerit, quòdq; illi, si modò non malitiosè repugnassent, per talia etiam converti potuissent. Breviter: Non defuit Tyriis gratia sufficiens, sed abundans. Vid. Bb. Dd. Hunnius in h. l. Meisnerus Ἀνσθρωπ. sacrae Disp. 13. Q. 2. §. 16.)*

## 11:22
*(v. 22. Πλὴν wherefore. This little word is also taken in this way Matt. 26, 64.Luke 6, 35.c. 12, 31. The Savior had exaggerated the offenses of the inhabitants of Chorazin and Bethsaida, by comparing them with the malice of the most deplorable nations, whose crimes were noted everywhere by the mouth and pen of the Prophets. Therefore, when He had said that the sins of the Chorazaeans were greater, especially if you look at their ingratitude and contempt of the Gospel, He adds that heavier punishments also awaited them.)

Ἀνεκτὸτερον. See August. b. 21. City of God ch. 16. *(From the fact, however, that there will be degrees of infernal punishments, and that the condition of some will be more tolerable in hell than that of others, our people conclude that sins also are not equal, but some are graver than others. This they also prove from the explicit assertion of Holy Scripture. See below ch. 12, 44. Luke 11, 26.John 19, 11.1 Tim. 5, 8. etc. The Papists therefore do us an injury, attributing to us that we establish all sins as equal. But the blessed Par. long ago wiped away that stain, Cathol. Confess. vol. 4, p. 471. But the condition of the Sodomites (and thus also of the Tyrians and Sidonians) will be more tolerable than for the Chorazeans etc., not because they had already at that time suffered part of the punishment by fire, as indeed Anastasius, quest. 17, Scr. thinks, but because when God exhibited extraordinary grace to them, the Capernaites, since not only one of the Prophets, but the Son of GOD himself preached to them in his own person, and moreover confirmed the preached doctrine with divine miracles, which grace did not befall the Sodomites, yet they did not believe.

*(v. 22. And you Capernaum. Concerning this city, some things were said above at c. 4, 13.. Christ performed many miracles in this very place, some of which are related above c. 8, 13.15. 16., also Mark 2, 11.Luke 4, 23.c. 7, 10.John 4, 46. seqq. He himself taught in the same Mark 1, 21.Luke 4, 32.John 6, 59., nay, he even dwelt in the same, whence it is also called the city of Christ Matt. 9, 2.)*

( ἕως etc. Which shall be exalted to heaven. The Vulgate translates interrogatively: Shall you be exalted to heaven? it reads indeed in the Greek μὴ ἕως.. Beza testifies that he read it thus also in a certain Codex. But the more approved and better Greek Codices present the former reading. And so also the Syrian, Arab, and Persian read. The Ethiopian however ῥωμαίζει, just as the Hebrew Gospel of Matthew)

*( ἔμηναν ἂν would have remained. Beza and Erasmus do not expound the particle ἂν, just as the Syrian also, the Persian and Ethiopian omitted the same, similarly the blessed Luther. The Vulgate, both here and elsewhere, see below c. 12, 7.Heb. 8, 7.John 8, 19., rendered it by perhaps perchance. Not well enough. And Laurentius Valla himself warns, that the past or Aorist of the indicative with the particle is equivalent to an affirmation or negation, which is expressed by the subjunctive. And in this manner, namely affirmatively, it is rightly translated here, determines the blessed D. Glassius, Sacred Grammar p. 497, since it is certain that temporal punishments are either mitigated or averted by true and serious repentance (a thing which St. Ambrose also confirms with many examples, book 2, on Repentance, ch. 4 and 5). Whence also the Arab rightly expresses it by i.e. uti- or truly, as it is rendered in the English Bibles. But the interpreter of the Arabic version which appeared at Rome is mistaken or is being mistaken, while he renders the same by perhaps. Finally, the Hebrew Gospel of Matthew edited by Münster translated it in agreement with the Vulgate, for it has אולי )*

Latin:

*(v. 22. Πλὴνquapropter. Ita etiam accipitur haec vocula Matth. 26, 64.Luc. 6, 35.c. 12, 31. Exaggeraverat Salvator delicta incolarum Chorazin & Bethsaidae, conferendo illa cum malitià deploratissimarum gentium, ac quarum scelera ore ac calamo Prophetarum passim notata. His igitur cùm maiora esse Chorazaeorum peccata dixisset, praesertim si ingratitudinem eorum & Evangelii contemtum spectes, graviores quoque poenas eos mansuras, subiungit.)*

Ἀνεκτὸτερον. Vid. August. l. 21. Civ. Dei c. 16. *(Ex eo autem quòd poenarum infernalium futuri gradus, quòdq; nonnullorum tolerabilior in inferno conditio futura, quàm aliorum, colligunt nostrates, peccata quoque non esse paria, sed alia aliis graviora. Id quod etiam probant ex disertâ Sc. Sacrae adsertione. Vid infrà c. 12, 44. Luc. 11, 26.Ioh 19, 11.1. Tim. 5, 8. &c. Iniuriâ proinde nos afficiunt Pontificii, tribuentes nobis, quòd omnia peccata paria statuamus. Sed pridem maculam istam abstersit B. Par. Confess. Cathol. t. 4. p. 471. Erit verò tolerabilior Sodomitarum (& sic quoque Tyriorum & Sidoniorum) conditio pro Chorazaeis &c. non quòd iam tum incendio partem aquam poenae hi luissent, uti quidem Anastasius quaest. 17. Scr. existimat, sed quia cùm extraordinariam gratiam Deus iis, Capernaitis, exhibuerit, siquidem non solùm aliquis Prophetarum, sed ipse Filius DEI in propriâ personâ iis praedicavit, ac divinis insuper miraculis doctrinam praedicatam confirmavit, quae gratia Sodomitis non obtigit, tamen non crediderunt.)*

*(v. 22. Et tu Capernaum. De civitate hâc suprà ad c. 4, 13. quaedam dicta. Multa in hâ ipsâ edidit Christus miracula, quorum nonnulla referuntur suprà c. 8, 13.15. 16. it. Marc. 2, 11.Luc. 4, 23.c. 7, 10.Iohan. 4, 46. seqq. Docuit ipse in eadem Marc. 1, 21.Luc. 4, 32.Ioh. 6, 59. quin in eadem etiam habitavit, unde quoq; civitas Christi dicitur Matth. 9, 2.)*

( ἕως &c. Qùae usin coelum sublata. Vulgatus interrogativè vertit: Nunquid in coelum exalt aberis? legit nempe in Gr. μὴ ἕως. Quomodo etiam in quodam Codice legisse se, testatur Beza. Verùm probatiores potiores que Codd. Graeci priorem lectionem sistunt. Et ita quoque legerunt Syrus, Arabs, Persa. Aethiops tamen ῥωμαίζει, sicuti & Evangelium Matthaei Ebraeum)*

*( ἔμηναν ἂνmansissent. Beza & Erasmus particulam ἂν non exponunt, quemadmodum Syrus quoque, Persa & Aethiops eadem omiservnt, similiter B. Lutherus. Vulgatus tum hîc, tum alibi, vit infrà c. 12. 7.Ebr. 8, 7.Ioh. 8, 19. eddidit per fortè forsitan. Non satis benè. Monetque ipse La-rentius Valla, praeteritum vel Aoristum indicativi cum part ic ula av aequipollere affirmationi vel negationi, quae per subiunctivum effertur. Atq; h. m. nempe affirmativè recte hîc verti, statuit B. D. Glassius Gramm. Sacr. p. 497. cùm constet, poenas temporales vel mitigari, vel a verti verâ ac seriâ poenitentiâ (id quod etiam multis exemplis confirmat S. Ambrosius l. 2. de Poenit. c. 4. & 5.) Unde etiam rectè Arabs exprimit per i. e. uti- sive profectò, ceu redditur in Bibliis Anglicanis. Fallit autem vel fallitur Interpres versionis Arabicae quae Romae prodiit, dum eandem reddit per fortè. Matthaei tandem Evangelium Ebraeum à Münstero editum consentaneè Vulg. transtulit, habet enim אולי)*

## 11:24
*(v. 24. Land of Sodom, i.e., the inhabitants. In which way also Chorazin, Bethsaida, etc., in the preceding verse are thus understood, by a metonymy of the container for the contained, of which figure B. Glassius presents several examples in Rhet. S. p. 36. seqq.)* *( It shall be more tolerable. Not only according to external appearance or before men, as Tossanus thinks, but in reality. For there shall be altogether degrees of punishments in hell, as was shown above at c. 10, 15.)*

Latin:

*(v. 24. Terrae Sodomorum i. e. incolis. Quomodo etiam Corazin, Bethsaida &c. in vers. praeced. ita accipiūtur, per metonymiam continentis pro contento, cuius figurae pluscula exempla sistit B Glassius Rhet. S. p. 36. seqq.)* *( Remissius erit. Non solùm iuxta externam speciem vel coram hominibus, prout Tossanus putat, sed reverà. Erunt enim omninò poenarum in inferno gradus, uti suprà ad c. 10, 15. ostensum.)*

## 11:25
*(v. 25. ἀποκριθεὶς. He said. Thus it is also used elsewhere. See below c. 17, 4. c. 22, 1. c. 28, 5. Act. 15, 13. It is indeed a Hebraism, and furthermore a synecdoche of the species, by which a special verb is used for a general one. There are, however, those who think that the verb to answer is taken properly here, and they advise that this thanksgiving was then uttered by Christ when the Apostles returned and explained the things that were successfully done.)* Εξομολογοῦμαι. I confess is taken according to the property of the Hebrew speech for I praise or I give thanks, just as also Basil in Ps. 29. ἐζομολ explains ἀντι τς ἐχαριςήσω. For he confesses and acknowledges a benefit, who gives thanks. *(Compare S. Aug. serm. 8. on the words of the Lord. B. Luther rendered it: Ich preise dich Vater / which version Lud. de Dieu prefers to the Belgian: Ick dancke u Vader. Gataker approves the same explanation by τὸ I praise, I celebrate in de stylo N. T. p. 185. and notes that this meaning is drawn from the Heb. הורה. *(Furthermore, B. D. Glassius observes in Gramm. S. p. 621. that sometimes in Holy Scripture the first member in a discourse does not look to the immediately following, but to a more remote member. As an example he brings forward the present passage, and likewise Rom. 6, 17.1. Tim. 1, 13. 14. Since Christ does not give thanks to the Father because He hid the mysteries from the wise, but because when the mysteries had been hidden from the wise of this age, the heavenly Father nevertheless graciously revealed them to the humble. This explanation is also that of Chrysostom, who explicitly: He does not rejoice, he writes, because the wise did not know, but he is glad because the little ones perceived. The same author compares to this matter the passage Rom. 6. 17. There are, however, those to whom this does not seem an inconvenience, if the thanksgiving is referred also to the next member. So that Christ is established as giving thanks to the Father for this reason, that by a just judgment he avenged the contempt of the divine word in the wise of this world, since these reject the counsel of GOD, Luc. 7, 30. love darkness more than light, Iohan. 3, 19. do not receive Christ, Iohan. 1, 11. Conf. Es. 5, 21. Rom. 1, 20. 21. 22. 1. Cor. 1, 21. so that as far as concerns the impious, that is, the wise of this world, as contemners of the Gospel, it is a matter of the will of GOD not antecedent, but consequent; not absolute and simple, but hypothetical and judicial. Thus generally the Blessed D. Hunnius on this place, likewise the Blessed Par. L. de Elect. §. 187, who also says that this exposition is more consonant with the text than the former one of Chrysostom. Add the Blessed D. Fewrb. Syntagm. Theol. part 1, page 57. The Blessed D. Chemn. Harm. Ev. c. 56 and the Blessed D. Calixtus in Conc. on this place consider both expositions not inconvenient.)* *( ταδτα. Think of heavenly mysteries, but which Christ came into this world to teach and manifest.)*

*(You have hidden. i. e. you have not revealed, on account of preceding sins, namely, and especially the contempt of the divine word. For from the intention of GOD the mysteries of the Gospel ought to have been manifested to all. See Matth. 28, 19. 1. Tim. 2, 4. Act. 20, 27. etc.)*

From the wise. Augustine, sermon 8 on the words of the Lord, understands the arrogant, the falsely great, the rashly swelling. By infants, Isidore of Pelusium, book 1, Ep. 440, understands those who have Πλὴν childlike simplicity and undoubted assent. By νηπίους indeed in this place are understood פתאים simple, by no means evil and unskilled in things, whom they call ἀκάκους, who are not wise according to the flesh. Chemnitius: νήπος in this place is opposed to the wise and prudent. Therefore it denotes not so much age, as a childlike and simple mind. Varinus: νἡπιοι are σάκκο The LXX used this word when they wished to render the Hebrew Pethi, which signifies simple and credulous, to whom it can easily be persuaded . *(Conf. Rom. 2, 20.)* Christ therefore calls νηπίους, those who bring into captivity every thought to the obedience of faith.2. Cor. 10, 5.1. Cor. 2, 18. Thus Christ commands Matth. 18, 3. that we, being converted, be made as little children, not indeed with foolish credulity and gross ignorance 1. Cor 14, 20. *(Formerly for this reason the Monks, called brothers of ignorance, who pleased themselves in their own ignorance, were held worthy of laughter and pity rather than refutation . Concerning whom can be consulted B. D. Balduinus Cas. Cons. page 927. B. Par. Confess. Cathol. vol. 1. p. 926. Mr. Dilherrus Dispp. Acad vol. 2. p. 311. 312.)* or childish inconstancy Eph. 4, 14. But with pious simplicity, or a ready affection for believing the words of GOD, even if they seem foolish to reason. Conversely σοφοὶ καὶ συνετοὶ are understood the wise of this world according to the flesh. 1. Cor. 1, 26.c. 3, 18. *(Hilary: to the wise, by the presumption of their own folly, not by reasons of prudence. Since such wise men seem wise only to themselves, they do not wish to be subjected to the teaching of Christ, but despise the doctrine of the Gospel. Rightly therefore and deservedly are the heavenly mysteries hidden from them. Lyranus: that those who trust in human wisdom are deprived of the revelation of divine mysteries is the good and just will of GOD. Some understand by little ones the humble, and they prove this from coll. Psal. 19. 8.Psal. 119, 130.Es. 66, 2.1. Petr. 2, 2. Which opinion Cameto refutes, but without firm foundation, as will be noted in Analect. on Luc. 10 21..)* Irenaeus book 4. c. 17. p. 243. The Son reveals to all to whom He wills the Father to be known, and no one knows God without the good will of the Father, and without the administration of the Son. Let the same c. 14 be compared.

Latin:

*(v. 25. ἀποκριθεὶς.Dixit. Ita etiam alibi adhibetur. Vid. infrà c. 17, 4. c. 22, 1. c. 28, 5. Act. 15, 13. Est verò Ebaismus, & insuper synecdoche speciei, quâ verbum speciale pro generali adhibetur. Sunt tamen, qui verbum respondendi hîc propriè sumi censent, monentque, hanc gratiarum actionem tum à Christo fuisse prolatam, quando Apostoli redierunt, ac res feliciter gestas exposuerunt.)* Εξομολογοῦμαι.Confiteor iuxta Ebraei sermonis proprietatem accipitur pro laudo seu gratias ago, que madmodum etiam Basilius in Ps. 29.ἐζομολ explicat ἀντι τς ἐχαριςήσω. Confitetur enim & agnoscit beneficium, qui gratias agit. *(Confer S. Aug serm. 8. de verbis Domini. B. Lutherus reddidit. Ich pricise dich Bater / quam versionem Lud. de Dieu praefert Belgicae: If dancte u Bater. Approbat eandem explicationem per τὸlaudo, celebro Gatakerus in de stylo N. T. p. 185. notatque, tractam istam significationem ab Ebr. הורה. *(Coeterùm observat B. D. Glassius Gramm. S. p 621. quòd aliquando in Sc. S. primum in sermone membrum non immediatè consequens, sed remotius membrum spectet. Exempli loco adducit praesentem locum, itemque Rom. 6, 17.1. Tim. 1, 13. 14. Siquidem Christus Patri non agat gratias, quòd mysteria abscondiderit à sapientibus, sed quòd cùm à sapientibus huius seculi mysteria fuerint abscondita, Pater tamen coelestis gratiosè ea humilibus revelarit. Est explicatio haec Chrysostomi quoque, qui disertè: Non, scribit, quia sapientes non cognoverunt, gaudet, sed quia parvuli perceperunt, laet atur. Confert idem in hanc rem locum Rom. 6. 17. Sunt tamen, quibus nec hoc incommodum videtur, si ad proximum etiam membrum gratiarum actio referatur. Ita ut Christus ideo Patri agere gratias statuatur, quòd iusto iudicio verbi divini contemtum in sapientibus huius mundi vindicarit, cùm hi spernant consilium DEI,Luc. 7, 30.tenebras magis diligant, quàm lucem,Iohan. 3, 19.Christum non recipiant,Iohan. 1, 11. Conf. Es. 5, 21.Rom. 1, 20. 21. 22.1. Cor. 1, 21. ut ita quantum ad impios s. sapientes huius mundi, ut contemtores Evangelii, agatur de voluntate DEI non antecedente, sed consequente; non absolutâ & simplici, sed hypothoticâ & iudiciariâ. Ita ferè B. D. Hunnius in h. l. item B. Par. L. de Elect. §. 187. qui etiam expositionem hanc textui magis consonam esse dicit, quàm priorem Chrysostomi. Add. B. D. Fewrb. Syntagm. Theol. part, 1. pag. 57. Utramque expositionem non incommodam censent B. D. Chemn. Harm. Ev. c. 56. B. D. Calixtus in Conc. h. l.)* *( ταδτα. Mysteria puta coelestia, at quae docenda ac manifestanda Christus in hunc mundum venit.)*

*(Abscondisti. i. e. non revelasti, ob antegressa scil. peccata, ac verbi divini cumprimis contemtum. Ex intentione enim DEI Evangelii mysteria omnibus debebant manifestari. Vid. Matth. 28, 19.1. Tim. 2, 4.Act. 20, 27. &c.)*

A sapientibus. Augustinus serm. 8. de verbis Domini intelligit arrogantes, falsò grandes, temerè tumentes. Per infantes Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 1. Ep. 440. illos, qui habent Πλὴν puerilem simplicitatem & indubitatum adsensum. Per νηπίους sanè h. l. intelliguntur פתאיםsimplices, minimè, mali & imperiti rerum, quos vocant ἀκάκους, qui non sapientes secundùm carnem. Chemnitius: νήποςh. l. opponitur sapientibus & prudentibus. N-taigitur non tam aet atem, quàm animum puexilem & simplicem. Varinus:νἡπιοιsuntσάκκο LXX. usi sunt hoc vocabulo, quando voluerunt reddere Ebraeum Pethi, quod significat simplicem ac credulum, cui facilè persuaderi potest. *(Conf. Rom. 2, 20.)* Christus ergo vocat νηπίους, qui captivant omnem intellectum sub obsequium fidei,2. Cor. 10, 5.1. Cor. 2, 18. Sic iuber Christus Matth. 18, 3. ut conversi efficiamur sicut parvuli, non quidem sultâ credulitate & crassâ ignorantia 1. Cor 14, 20. *(Pridem hinc risu ac commiseratione potiûs, quàm refutatione digni habiti fuerunMonachi, fratres ignorantiae dicti, qui in ignorantiâ sibi suâ placebant. De quibus consuli possunt B. D. Balduinus Cas. Cons. pag 927. B. Par. Confess. Cathol. t. 1. p. 926. Dn. Dilherrus Dispp. Acad t. 2. p. 311. 312.)* aut puerili inconstantiâ Eph. 4, 14. Sed piâ simplicitate, aut promto affectu verbis DEI credendi, etiamsi rationi videantur stulta. Vicissim σοφοὶ καὶ συνετοὶ intelliguntur sapientes huius mundi secundùm carnem,. 1. Cor. 1, 26.c. 3, 18. *(Hilarius: sapientibus, stultitiae suae praesumtione, non prudentiae causis. Tales sapientes cùm sibimet solis sapere videantur, nolunt Christi magisterio subiici, sed doctrinam Evangelii contemnunt. Iure igitur meritoque mysteria coelestia ab iis absconduntur. Lyranus: qui confidunt in sapientiâ humanâ, illos privari mysteriorum divinorum revelatione, est bona & DEI iusta voluntas. Nonnulli per parvulos intelligunt humiles, idque probant ex coll. Psal. 19. 8.Psal. 119, 130.Es. 66, 2.1. Petr. 2, 2. Quam sententiam refellit Cameto, sed absque firmo fundamento, uti in Analect. ad Luc. 10 21. monebitur.)* Irenaeus lib. 4. c. 17. p. 243. Revelat omnibus Filius, quibus velit agnosci Pater, & neque fine bonâ voluntate Patris, neque sine administratione Filii eognoscit quis quam DEum. Conferatur idem c. 14.

## 11:26
*(v. 26. ἐγένετο ἐδοκία Not however absolute, (as indeed Camero in Myroth. on this place, Piscator on the friendly duplication of Vorstius part. 1. p. 1. 2. Wendelinus Exerc. 39. §. 3. and other Calvinists persuade themselves, whose reasons will be satisfied at Luc. 10, 21.) but respective, namely presupposing the foreseen malice of men. See vers. 18. 19. also below c. 13, 11.c. 23, 37.Luc. 7, 30.c. 8, 5.Act. 7. 51.c 13, 46. Rightly therefore indeed Maldonatus here taxes the opinion of those who establish that there is no other cause of reprobation besides the will of GOD But in that he is too liberal in pronouncing, and most especially the Jesuit is most unjust toward us, when he adds: in which error all the heretics of our time are most stubbornly insistent. It is certain that the Jesuit considers us also as heretics, who nevertheless are so far from approving the said error of the Calvinists, that we rather vehemently impugn the same. We argue, however, against that absolute decree of the Calvinists in this manner: If God, out of a certain absolute will and good pleasure, hid the heavenly mysteries from those wise men, it follows that by not believing they did not sin at all. But the consequent is absurd, because ἀπιςίσ is the cause of condemnation, and thus a most grave sin. See Mark 16, 16.John 3, 18. The connection is proven, because those wise men by not believing would have fulfilled the good pleasure of GOD. Nor could they believe without the knowledge of the mysteries of faith. Which, when GOD, according to that hypothesis of the Calvinists, withdrew from them out of a certain absolute good pleasure, it ought by no means to be imputed to them that they did not believe.

Latin:

*(v. 26. ἐγένετο ἐδοκία Non tamen absoluta, (uti quidem Camero in Myroth. ad h. l. Piscator ad amicam duplicationem Vorstii part. 1. p. 1. 2. Wendelinus Exerc. 39. §. 3. aliique Calviniani sibi persuadent, quorum rationibus satis fiet ad Luc. 10, 21.) sed respectiva, praesupponens nempe praevisam hominum malitiam. Vid. vers. 18. 19. it. infrà c. 13, 11.c. 23, 37.Luc. 7, 30.c. 8, 5.Act. 7. 51.c 13, 46. Rectè proinde quidem taxat hîc Maldonatus illorum sententiam, qui statuunt. nullam reprobationis causam esse aliam praeter DEI voluntatem Sed in eo nimis liberalis in pronunci ndo, maximèque iniquius in nos Iesuita est, quando addit: in quo errore omnes nostri temporis haeretici pertinacissimè ursantur. Constat, quòd nos quosque Iesuita pro haereticis habeat, qui tamen tantum abest, ut dictum Calvinian orum errorem approbemus, ut potiùs vehementur eundem impugnemus.
