To which also contributes the observation of the famous Hackspan, who in the treatise on the Usefulness of reading Rabbis in Theology, chapter 3, § 41, from the book םמירים shows that that phrase: it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this, nor in the future age, was customary among the ancient Rabbis, even though they themselves, as is held in the same book, teach that there is no expiation of sin after death. Although, therefore, the Savior did not speak according to the rules of Jesuitical prudence, it is nevertheless sufficient for us and for all who are rightly wise that He spoke quite aptly according to the custom of speech received among the Jews. 4. It is to be observed that if it were even granted, in the greatest degree, that Christ implies that certain punishments for sins are remitted in the other age, it does not yet follow from that that it is done through purgatory, since in it there is punishment, not remission: indeed, it can be said that it is done in other ways. And first, indeed, insofar as a sinful man, about to bid farewell to this life, performs serious repentance and apprehends Christ with true faith. For then sins are so perfectly remitted to him in this life that they are also rightly said to be remitted in the other life, i.e., he is not punished on account of them; because through faith in Christ he has been received into grace. Conf. Rom. 8, 1. We also know that blessed are ἀπάρτι all, as many as die in Christ, Apoc. 14, 13. On the contrary, to whom sins have not been remitted in this life, to him they will not be remitted in the future age, since this is not the age of grace, as Jansenius himself teaches in Comm. ad Conc. Ev. p. 379. 1. And he notes furthermore that the future age in Holy Scripture is the perpetual state finally after the resurrection, see Matth. 13, 40.49.c. 24, 3.Marc. 10, 30.Luc. 20, 35. Then it can be said that the punishments of sins are remitted to a man in the other age, insofar as, namely, Christ in the final judgment will publicly declare that his sins had been remitted out of mere mercy. To which pertains the observation that many things are said to be done in Holy Scripture when they are declared to have been done, as this rule can be confirmed by several examples. See Dn. D. Walth. H. B. p. 30. B. D. Quistorp. Annot. Bibl. t. 1. p. 524. Thus the Apostle 2. Tim. 1, 18. prays, that Onesiphorus may obtain mercy in that day, not as if he ought to obtain mercy, i.e., the remission of sins, only at the final judgment (for that by that day in this place not only the Fathers, Chrysostom, Theophylactus, etc., but even the Pontificians themselves, Thomas, Caietanus, Iustinianus, Salmero, Estius, Corn. à Lapide, and others assert that this is to be understood), but because That retribution of eternal life is preceded by the remission of many sins, done in this age, as Estius himself explains, who also agrees with the aforementioned place 2 Macch. 7, 29. Add Acts 3, 19, 20. Therefore, the mercy or remission of sins in the future age and in the final judgment is not a new judgment or a new remission, just as non-remission in the future age is not a new condemnation, but at least the ratification, declaration, and manifestation of the prior remission and condemnation. Compare John 3, 18. chap. 20, 23. But from this, purgatory can in no way be constructed. For why could that remission of punishments of merits not be manifested in the future age and in the final judgment, even though it was done only in this life? I could bring forward more things pertaining to this, but the nature of this place does not permit it. Let the blessed Doctor Meisner be unrolled in his second Opusculum, opposed to Indulgences of the Roman Pontiff, p. 363 et seqq. Lord Doctor Misterus, Speculum Anti-Iesuiticum, p. 742 et seqq. Blessed Father, Consensu Catholico, vol. 3, p. 498 et seqq., also the book On Death § 246 et seqq. To whom, from the Calvinists, can also be added Chamier, Panstratia Catholica, vol. 3, book 26, chapter 10. Rainoldus in Censura librorum Apocryphorum, Praelectiones 171 et seqq. Drusius Ebraica, book 1, question 12.

Latin:

*(v. 32. Quisquis loquutus fuerit adversùs Filium hominis. B. D. Quistorpius exempla huius peccati notat haberi infrà c. 13, 55. c. 27, 63. Luc. 7, 33.Ioh. 6, 42.c. 8, 48. Conf. etiam B. D. Frantz. de Interpr. Sc. S. p. 165. B. D. Fewrb. diss. de pecc. in Sp. S. c. 36.)*

Non remittetur. i. e. punietur & in hoc & in futuro seculo. Qualia sunt: non gaudet stulti pater i. e. vehementer dolet. Non prosunt the sauri improbitatis i. e. plurimùm obsunt. Susciperepersonaman iudicio non est bonum i. e. pessimum. Marc. 3, 29. sic exponitur: --κἔξει ἄφεσινεἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. August. serm. 11. de verbis Domini: Quod scriptum est: non habet remissionem in aeternum, sed reus erit aeterni delicti, quid aliud est, qaeàm id, quod secundùm Matthaeum legitur: non remittetur ei neqùe in hoc seculo, neque in futuro? Aliis quippe verbis & alio loquéndi modo eadem ipsa est expressa sententia. Dicitur irremissibile tùm ratione hominis, tùm respectu DEI. Ratione hominis tùm adiunctivè ob impoenitentiam finalem, tùm formaliter ob quidditatem & requisita. Ratione DEI ob iustitiam vindicatricem & ultricem. *(Porrò quae requirantur ad hoc, ut peccatum aliquod possit dici peccatum in Sp. S. multis ostendunt B. D. Fewrbornius in peculiari Dissertationè de pècc. in Sp. S. excusâ Giesae A. 1619. B. D. Hutter. LL. Th. Mai. p. 367. B. D. Glassius Exeg. Evang. Dom. Oculi p. 626. seqq. B. D. Frantzius de Interpp. Scr. S. pag. 165. seqq. B. D. Martini Photin. p. 281. B. D. Bald. Cas. Cons. p. 230. 231. it. Comm. in Epist. Paul. p. 1263. & 1268. B. D. Hunnius in h. l. B. Par. Coll. Isagog. L. de Pecc. Actual. c. 5. § 9. seqq. Scripsit quoque idem B. P. epistolàm aliquam de pecc. in Sp. S. ad B. D. Hoë, quae nondum lucem vidit, visura tamen aliquando, ubi occasio fuerit data. Hoc loco illud saltem nionemus, quòd peccatum in Sp. S. dicatur irremissibile 1. non quasi difficulter remittatur, ut Lyranus, Greg. de Valentia, Mald. ac Cornelius à Lapide in h. l. Pazmannus in Hodegô, Bell. l. 1. de V. D. c. 17. 1. 2. de poen. c. 16. ac alii Pontificii censent. Nec 2. quia non remittitur sine poenitentia. 3. nec quia peccatum illud committentes sunt reprobi. 4. nec quia peccatum illud non habet excusationem coram hominibus. 5. nec quia peccans non habet, unde remissionem mereatur. Sed dicitur ita, quia ipsum salutis medium, videl. ministerium Sp. Sancti directè impugnat, & cum externâ cordis induratione & finali impoenitentia est coniunctum. Dicitur ergò irremissibile 1. non ob defectum divinae gratiae 2. nec ob defectum meriti Christi. Unde etiam minimè huic Christi adserto contrariantur dicta Ezech. 18, 32.Matth. 11, 28.1. Ioh. 1, 7.c. 2, 2. &c. 3. Sed ob pertinacem contemtum mediorum, per quae Sp. S. ad conversionem & peccati condonationem esse efficax solet. Atque hinc facilè etiam patet, quid respondendum sit ad quaestionem, quam prae aliis prolixius pertractat B. D. Meisn. Qq. Vexat. n. 3. An Christus pro finali impoenitentia etiam satisfecerit. Plura huc facientiae afferentur ad Luc. 12, 10. ubi etiam excutietur Episcopii Arminiani sententia singularis de pecc. in Sp. S. quam proponit in Resp. ad 64. Qq. q. 14.)*

Neq; in futuro seculo. Triplex seculum futurum statuitur à Rabbinis, ut annotavit Isaac Abarbanel in libro, qui possessio Patrum inscribitur. Primum est seculum Messiae, secundum post hanc vitam, tertium post resurrectionem mortuerum. Credebant autem Iudaei veteres, temporibus Messiae remissum iri omnia peccata. Hinc proverbiale vetus: non remittetur ei neq; in hoc seculo, neq; in futuro. Conf. Drusium. *(Corn. à Lapide, Tirinus, Conzenius in h. l. item Coturius Epit. Controv. Demonstr. 22. p. 444. sicuti & alii plurimi Pontificii, quos allegant B. D. Meisnerus opusc. secundo, Indulgentiis P. R. opposito, p. 365. & 366. ac B. Par. Confess. Cath. t. 4. p. 498. ex h. l. Purgatorii ignem succendere satagunt. Vanum enim, scribit Corn. à Lapide in h. l. & atisum esset dicere: Non remittetur ei neq; in hoc seculo, neque in futuro, si in futuro nullum peccatum remittitur: sicut vane & in eptè quis diceret, omninò non ducam uxorem, nec in hoc seculo, nec in futuro, cùm in futuro nulla possit duci uxor. Eodem modo infrant quoq; Iesuitae Maldonatus ac Tirinus in h. l. item Iulius Caes-r. Coturius l. c. Sed misera profectò illatio: Peccatum in Sp. S. non remittitur neque in hoc, neque in futuro seculo. E. quaedam peccata remittuntur in futuro seculo, nempe in Purgatorio. Perinde esset, ac si quis ita vellet inferre: Iesuitae illi, quos Potentissimus Angliae Rex A. 1604 ut perduelles regno suo excedere iussit, vel quos Sor. Resp.

Veneta A. 1606. ut pacis publicae turbatores è ditione sua exturbandos publico decreto censuit, & quidem ita, ne illi in aeternum recipiantur, (ut habent verba Responsi, à Procuratoribus S. Marci Legato Regis Galliae, pro Iesuitarum receptione intercedenti, dati.) nec hoc nec futuris annis in Regnum Angliae vel Reip. Venetae ditiones recipiētur. E. Alii Iesuitae recipientur. Μὴ γένοιτο! Μὴ γένοιτο! exclamabunt Angli ac Veneti, nec sequelam hanc concedent unquam. Cùm licet secundùm regulas prudentiae (talem nempe consequentiam argumenti illius pro Purgatorio ex hoc loco extructi, esse, Bellarminus, Maldonatus, Peltanus aliique Pontificii garriunt) vel fallaciae potiùs Iesuiticae ista conclusio sequatur, minimè tamen sequatur secundùm regulas dialecticorum, ut quas solas vim stringendi habere, eruditi ac rectè sapientes norunt. Ac ratio etiam, cur talis consequentia nulla sit, manifesta est, quia unius neg-atio, non est alterius statim positio. Sic Salvator dicit ad ficum aliquam Matth. 21, 19.Nunquam nascatur ex te fructus in aeternum, minimè tamen hinc sequitur. E. quaedam ficus in futuro seculo, in aeternitate nempe, fructus ferent. Probè etiam hoc vidit Alphonsus Tostatus, Abulensis in Hispania Episcopus, de quo vulgatum inter Pontificios est: Hic stupor est mundi, qui scibile discutit omne, & cuius in N. T. Commentaria admiranda vocat Iesuita Possevinus in Appar. Is verò ita de h. l. q. 74. in Matth. Dicendum quòd Christus non innuit ex littera, quòd aliqua peccata post mortem dimittantur, sed dixit hoc ad super abundam iam, nequis putaret, quòd licet non dimitterentur ei peccata hîc, quòd poterant dimitti post mortem: & iterum: Poterat hoc Christus dicere, non supponendo, quòd aliquod peccatum in futurum dimitteretur post mortem: sed ad tollendum errorem aliqucrum, qui putarent, dimittipeccata post mortem, qui viventibus non fuerant dimissa. Ut ita Christus κατ᾽ ἔνδοξον fuerit loquutus h. e. ex aliorum sensu, non ex rei veritate (quod alibi etiam ab eodem factum esse, ipsi Pontificii docent. Videantur Iesuitae Corn. à Lapide in c. 24. Matth. v. 29. it in c. 3. Ioh. v. 13. & 16. Maldonatus in c. 26. Matth. v. 24. c. 2. Lucae v. 27. alii.) Temerarii igitur sunt Pontificii, qui illum ipsum errorem, quem Christus h. l. refuta vit ac tollere voluit, ex propriis eius verbis stabilire satagunt. Quantò rectiùs Fulgentius Carthaginensis, Episcopus Rùspensis, vir sanctissimus & doctissimus, iudice Bellarmino, & qui floruit circa initium seculi sexlib. 1. de remiss. pecc. ad Euthymium c. 24. Hoc verbo, scribit, Dominus & Salvator noster non aliqua peccata insinuavit is futuro seculo dimittenda, quae in hoc seculo dimissa non fuerint, sed benè intelligentibus ostendit, non alia, sed illa tantùm in future seculo dimittenda, quae in hoc seculo in una & vera Ecclesia Catholica fuerint unicuiq; dimissa. Et paulò pòst: Quod ergo sancta Ecclesia in hoc seculo non solverit, ita in solubile permanet, ut etiam in futuro seculo solvi nullatenus possit.)* Sed quò res fiat clarior, notandum ulterùs I. quòd exemplum, quod instantiae loco Iesuitae afferre solent, ex eodemque evincere conantur, quòd Salvator insipienter locutus fuisset, nisi in altero seculo peccata remitterentur, prorsus sit alienum. Ut adeò si vel maximè concedatur, illum ineptè loqui, qui diceret, se neque in hoc, neque in futuro seculo ducere velle uxorem, non tamen sequatur, etiam Christum ineptè esse loquutum Ratio est, quia ex Matth. 22, 29. satis constat, in resurrectione, sive in futuro seculo omnes fore ἀγάμους. Sed omnes in altero seculo ignis aeterni flammis ustulandos esse, falsissimum est: Constat enim, plurimos ab istis fore immunes, eos nempe, quibus in hâc vitâ peccata omnia propter solius Christi meritum verâ fide apprehensum, remissa, Ioh. 3, 15.18. Neque verò etiam necesse est, ut si quis ab aeternis cruciatibus immunis futurus, demum in alterâ vitâ, in ficto nempe Pontificiorum Purgatorio, peccatorum remissionem obtineat, cùm ea remissio, quam in hac vita homo fidelis consequutus est, istam vim habeat, ne aeternùm is puniatur. 2. sciendum, quòd per sò non remittere h. l. nihil indicetur aliud, quàm sò puniri, prout rectè observavit Ioh. Ferus, quondam summae aedis Moguntiae Concionator, qui disertè in h. l. p. 264. Minùs dicendo plus significat. Vult enim, quòd non solùm in futuro, sed etiam hîc punitur tale peccatum. (Estque in Sc. Sacrae non insolitum, verbo minùs vehementi uti, quàm intendat significare. Exempla sistunt plufcula B. D. Glasius Gr. S. p. 286. 287. cumprimis id patet ex Matth. 24. 22. Conf. etiam Iesuita Tirinus Idiot. L. E. pag. 85. Ubi probè notandum, quòd cum Censores Pontificii plurimis in locis dicti Scriptoris, licet aliàs Romano Catholici, Commentaria in Matthaeum, in editione, quae Lugduni Gallorum A. 1609. prodiit, castrârint, praesentem tamen locum intactum reliquerint, adeoque suo calculo explicationem istam approbârint. Et quidni? Etenim conformem expositioni veterum Ecclesiae Doctorum è quorum numero Ioh. Chrysostomus à Iansenio Episcopo Gandavensi in Conc. Evang. in h. l. p. 379. adductus, ita: Universorum hominum alii & hîc & ibi supplicia dabunt, ut Sodomitae, & hi. de quibus hîc agitur, alii in praesenti solummodo vitâ, ut incestuosus Corinthius; alii tantùm in futurâ, ut dives epulo; alii nec in futuro, nec in praesente, ut Prophetae & Apostoli. Quid quòd Iesuita Svarezt. 4. in 3. p. Disp. 45. s. 1. n. 11. fateatur, praesens dictum à Chrysostomo hom. 24. in Matth. & Graecis Patribus longè aliter, quàm de Purgatorio exponi. Disertè quoque Iesuita Conzen: ait Chrysostomus, puniendos hos (peccatores. nempe in Sp. S.) in futuro & in hoc seculo. Et paulò pòst: totus (Chrysostomus) in eo est, ut dehortetur à peccatis, purgatorii hîc mentionem non facit. Quamvis verò Conzen statim addat: alibiadserit. ac confirmationis quoque loco adferat locum ex hom 69. ad pop. Antioch. nihil tamen praestat aliud, quàm quòd suam sive malitiam, sive ignorantiam orbi prodat. Nosse enim debebat Iesuite è socienno suo, eodemq; E. R. Cardinali Bellarminol. de Script. Eccl. p. 120. quòd homilia illa 69. ad pop. Antioch. fidei dubiae sit. Ita enim Cardinalis d. l. Ea quae in quinto tomo Chryso-tom-i continentur, omniferè certa & in dubitata, exceptis (NB) homiliis ad populum Artiochenum, ex quibus viginti & unatantùm reperiri dicuntur manuscriptae in antiquis Bibliothocis. Contra verò homiliae in Matthaeum sine dubio Chrysostomi sunt, ut habetidem Cardinalis d. l. Repulsam igitur à Chrysostomo aliisq; Graecis passus Iesuit. Conzen provocat ad Latinos, Sed ex his quoque oppidò pauci locum hunc ad fictum illud Purgatorium torquent, imò nullus. Repellunt clientem Iesuitam Hilarius, Hieronymus, Fulgentiuss ac quotquot in h. l. commentati sunt. Unde etiam ne nominare quidem illos audet. Producit tamen Augustinum, uri vetustiorem, ait, & magnae autoritatis, qui lib. 21. de C. D. c. 24 Purgatorium ex h. l. inferat. Sed licet Bell. quoq; ac Corn. à Lapidè in h. l. pariter Augustini patrocinium ambiant, salluntur tamen ac fallunt. Testatur enim Ludovicus, Vives, Valentiae ortus, ac quo decedente doctior nemo in Hispania superfuit, iudice Paulo Iovio, quòd duodècim illi versus, in quibus peccata etiam in futuro seculo remitti dicuntur, in multis antiquis Codd. Brugensibus & Coloniensibus non inveniantur, ac veresimile sit, eos margini primùm adscriptos, postè à intextum irrepsisse. Ubi iterum observationem meretur, quòd vi veritatis convicti tùm Censores Lovamenses, tùm alii librorum Expurgatores, vel rectiùs corruptores, Pontificii, licet Ludovici Commentarios passim turpissimè castrarint, cumprimis in editione novissimâ, quae Coloniae A. 1616. prodiit, allegatum tamen locum, intactum reliquerint. Et audent tamen nihilominus Augustini istum locum etiamnum nobis opponere. Ut vel hinc etiam illorum malitia ac fraus satis pateat. Habet quidem in alia loco, nempe lib. 6. adversus Iulianum c. 15. aliquid Augustinus de remissione in altero seculo, sed in extremo iudicio. Quid verò talis remissio pro Purgatorio? Porrò 3. notandum, quòd Marcus c. 3, 31. quem Iesuitae Maldonatus in h. l. ac Greg. de Valentiâ lib. de indissol. vinculo matrim. c. 4. § Tertio, Matthaei, interpretem & esse & adhibendum agnoscunt, ac de quo Corn. à Lapide in Argum. Marci pag. 572. 2. a. scribit, quod quaedam clariùs explicet, quàm Matthaeus, ut qui post Matthaeum scripsit Evangelium, & quidem prout. Petrum praedicantem audiverat, dicente Bell. l. 2. de P. R. c. 2. Christi verba ita referat, non habet remissionem in aeternum, sed reus erit aeterni delicti. E quibus verbis hoc solùm è contrariô elicitur, quosdam non futuros reos aeterni delicti, id quod facilè largimur. Quo facit etiam observatio CL. Hackspanii, qui tr. de Util. lect. Rabb. in Theol. cap. 3. § 41. è lobro םמירים ostendit, phrasin illam: non condonabitur illi neq; in hoc, neq; in futuro seculo, Rabbinis veteribus fuisse usitatam, cùm tamen ipsi illi, ceu in eodem libro habetur, doceant, quòd nulla peccati expiatio sit post mortem. Licet igitur Salvator non loquutus fuerit ad regulas prudentiae Iesuiticae, sufficit tāmē nobis omnibusq; rectè sapientibus, quòd satis aptè loquutus fuerit ad consvetudinem sermonis inter Iudaeos recepti. 4. Observandum, quòd si vel, miximè concedatur, Christum in nuere, quasdam peccatorum poenas in altero seculo remitti, exinde tamen nondum sequatur, fieri id per purgatorium, cùm in eo sit punitio, non remissio: quin aliis modis fieri illa potest dici. Ac primò quidem quatenus homo peccator vitae huic valedicturus seriamagit poenitentiam & Christum verâ fide apprenèdit. Tum enim ipsi in hâc vitâ ita perfectè pēccata remittuntur, ut etiam alterâ vitâ rectè dicantur remissa h. e. propter illa non puniatur; quia per fidem in Christum receptus in gratiam est. Conf. Rom. 8, 1. Novimus etiam, beatos esse ἀπάρτι omnes, quotquot in Christo moriuntur, Apoc. 14, 13. Econtra cui peccata in hâc vitâ non fuerint remissa, eidem nec in futuro seculo remittentur, cùm hoc non sit seculum graetiae, ipso Iansenio docente in Comm. ad Conc. Ev. p. 379. 1. Ac notat insuper futurum seculum in Sc. S. statum perpetuum demum post resurrectionem, vid. Matth. 13, 40.49.c. 24, 3.Marc. 10, 30.Luc. 20, 35. Deinde potest dici, homini peccatorum poenas in altero seculo remitti, quatenus videl. Christus in extremo iudicio publicè declarabit, quòd illi ex merâ misericordiâ peccata fuerint remista. Quo pertinet observatio, quòd multa tùm fieri in Sc. S. dicantur, cùm facta declarantur, ceu plusculis exemplis regula haec confirmari potest. Vid. Dn. D. Walth. H. B. p. 30. B. D. Quistorp. Annot. Bibl. t. 1. p. 524. Ita Apostolus 2. Tim. 1, 18. precatur, ut Onesiphorus misericordiam consequatur in die illo, non quasi demum in extremo iudicio (hoc enim per diem illum h. l. intelligi non solùm Patres, Chrysost. Theophylactus &c. sed ipsi etiam Pontificii, Thomas, Caietanus, Iustinianus, Salmero, Estius, Corn. à Lapide & alii adserunt) misericordiam s. peccatorum remissionem consequi debeat, sed quia retributienem illam vitae aeternae praecedit multorum peccatorum remissio, in hoc seculo facta, uti ipse explicat Estius, qui etiam cum d. l. consert 2. Macch. 7, 29. Adde Act. 3, 19, 20. Est igitnr misericordia s. remissio pecc. in futuro seculo & in extremo iudicio non novum iudicium s. nova remissio, sicuti non-remissio in futuro seculo non est nova condemnatio, sed saltem prioris remissionis ac condemnationis ratihabitio, declaratio, manifestatio. Conf. Ioh. 3, 18.cap. 20, 23. Sed hinc minimè purgatorium extrui potest. Quidni enim illa remissio poenarum promerita-um in futuro seculo & in extremo iudicio manifestari poterit, licet in hâc solùm vitâ facta fuerit. Possem plura adferre huc facientia. sed loci huius ratio non permittit. Evolvantur B. D. Meisner. Opusculo secundo, Indulg. P. R. opposito p. 363. seqq. Dn. D. Misterus Spec. Anti-Iesuit. p. 742. seqq. B. P. Cons. Cath. t. 3. p. 498. seqq. it. L. de Morte § 246. seqq. Quibus è Calvinianis adiungi quoque possunt Chamier Panstr. Cath. t. 3. l. 26. c. 10. Rainoldus in Cens. libb. Apocr. Praelect. 171. seqq. Drusius QEbr. l. 1. q. 12.)*

## 12:33
v. 33. Either make the tree good &c. Such as the tree is, such also are its fruits. What wonder, therefore, if you Pharisees, since you are evil, bring forth very bad fruits, and burden my doctrine and miracles with calumnies. *(The sense is, either acknowledge and confess that that tree is good which bears good fruits; or conversely, acknowledge an evil tree from its evil fruit. Dionysius the Carthusian: make, i.e., by judging affirm. Cardinal Hugo of Saint-Cher: make, i.e., say, as it is commonly said: this one makes himself good, i.e., says. Similarly Nicholas of Lyra, Cornelius à Lapide, &c. And they are referred to Christ himself and are asserted, because the Savior speaks about himself, and wishes that from the miracle, as a good fruit, he himself, as a good tree, namely the tree of life, i.e., the promised Messiah, be acknowledged. So also the blessed Doctor Glassius, Grammatica Sacra, p. 280. Others, as the blessed Father, book on the Law of God § 86, judge that regard is had to the Pharisees. That is, confess that you are evil trees, since you bear evil fruits, namely, hatreds, calumnies, and the very calumny against the Holy Spirit; or if you wish to be acknowledged as good trees, bear good fruits. But from that, That men are commanded to bring forth good fruits, the enemies of divine grace and patrons of free will gather improperly, that man can by his own natural powers convert himself to God, so that from an evil tree he may become a good tree. The contrary is evident from v. 34. But this matter has been treated elsewhere. Conf. B. D. Hutter. in F. C. p. 211. seqq B. Par. LL. Th. de L. A. §. 86. Dn. D. Walth. in Harm. Bibl. p. 769.)*

Latin:

v. 33. Aut facite arborem pulcram &c. Qualis estarbor, tales quoque sunt illius fructus. Quid ergo mirum, fi vos Pharisaei, cùm sitis mali, proferatis fructus pessimos, meamque doctrinam & miracula calumniis oneretis. *(Sensus est, aut agnoscire & fatemini, arborem illam esse bonam, quae fert fructus bonos; aut vice versâ agnoscite arborem malam ex fructu eius malo. Dionys. à Rickel: facite i. e. iudicando affi-mate. Card. Hugo de S. Charo: facite i. e. dicite sicut vulgariter dicitur: iste facit so bonum i, e. dicit. Similiter Nic, de Lyra, Corn. à Lapide, &c. Referunturque ad Christum ipsum ac adseruntur, quòd Salvator de seipso loquatur, velitque, ut ex miraculo, tanquam fructu bono, ipse tanquam bona arbor, vitae nempe arbor 1. promissus Messias agnoscatur. Ita etiam B. D. Glassius Gr. S. p. 280. Alii, uti B. P. L. de L. A. §. 86. ad Pharisaeos respectum haberi censent. h. s. fatemini, vos esse malas arbores, cùm feratis malos fructus, videl. odia, calumnias & ipsam in Sp. S. calumniam; aut si vultis agnosci pro bonis arboribus, ferte fructus bonos. Ex eo verò, quòd homines iubentur bonos fructus proferre, in-ptè colligunt gratiae divinae hostes ac L. A. patroni, quòd homo propriis naturalibus viribus sese ad Deum convertere possit, ut ex arbore mala fiat arbor bona. Contrarium patet ex v. 34. Sed hac de re alibi actum. Conf. B. D. Hutter. in F. C. p. 211. seqq B. Par. LL. Th. de L. A. §. 86. Dn. D. Walth. in Harm. Bibl. p. 769.)*

## 12:34
v. 34. Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. Theoph. h. l. 49. συνεκδ.

*( How can you &c. i. e. you can in no way. See what is noted at v. 26. It is evident from this verse, that since all men are by nature evil, (as is established both from the present saying, and from John 5, 15.c. 8. 34.Rom. 6, 20.Eph. 2, 1.Col. 2, 13. that men are by nature evil, because they are dead in sins and by nature children of wrath, that they themselves cannot by their own natural powers convert themselves to God. Against the Pelagians and Semipelagians. Conf. what is noted at c. 7, 17. p. 439. But it does not follow: Man cannot by his own powers convert himself to God. Therefore the cause why some are converted, others not, is to be referred to the sole & absolute OF GOD εὐδοκίαν will, as Wendelinus attempts to prove from this in Exerc. 129. §. 1. seqq. For although man cannot by his own powers convert himself to God, he can nevertheless hinder the operation of God through affected morose resistance.)*

Latin:

v. 34. Ex abundantia cordis os loquitur. Theoph. h. l. 49. συνεκδ.

*( Quomodo potestis &c. i. e. minimè potestis. Vid. quae notata ad v. 26. Patet v. hinc, quòd cùm omnes homines naturâ mali sunt, (ceu cōstat tum ex pra-senti dicto, tum ex Ioh. 5, 15.c. 8. 34.Rom. 6, 20.Eph. 2, 1.Col. 2, 13. quòd homines naturâ mali sint, quia mortui in peccatis & naturâ filii irae, quòd ipsi propriis naturalibus viribus ad Deum sese convertere noqueant. Contra Pelagianos & Semipelagianos. Conf. quae notata ad c. 7, 17. p. 439. Non verò sequitur: Homo ex propriis viribus non potest se ad Deum convertere. E. causa cur alii convertantur, alii non, ad solam & absolutam DEIεὐδοκίανreferenda est, prout Wendelinus evincere hinc conatur Exxerc. 129. §. 1. seqq. Licet enim homo non possit sese propriis viribus ad Deum convertere, potest tamen Dei operationē per adfectatam moro sam repugnantiam impedire.)*

## 12:35
*(v. 35. Καὶ ὁπονηρὸς &c. It is asked here, whether the particle καὶ in this place has a copulative, or indeed an adversative meaning. Concerning which matter let Camero Myroth. p. 24 be seen.)*

Latin:

*(v. 35. Καὶ ὁπονηρὸς &c. Quaeritur hîc, num partic. καὶ h. l. copulativam, an verò adversativam significationem habeat. Quâ de re videatur Camero Myroth. p. 24.)*

## 12:36
v. 36. They shall render an account of an idle word. Smalcius in refut. Smigl. de satisf. c. 8. p. 239. That concerning an idle word, of which men shall render an account in the day of judgment, it is not necessary to take it of a light sin, but of such an idle word or at least one similar to it, of which the discourse is there, namely that it contains some blasphemy. *(The same author has similar things in Refut. Thes. D. Frantzii page 368.

Remonstrants in Apolog. Confess. p. 90. through They wish an idle word to be understood only as blasphemy against the Holy Spirit. The Jesuit Maldonatus thinks that at the very least a calumniating word is signified here. Dionysius the Carthusian likewise understands by an idle word such a sin that it completely excludes repentance.)* But Jerome is more correct in this place: An idle word is that which is uttered without the utility of the speaker or the hearer, if, omitting serious matters, we speak of frivolous things and tell ancient fables. But he who explains scurrilous things and dissolves his mouth in laughter, and brings forth some kind of filthiness, he will be held guilty not of an idle word, but of a criminal one. Gregory in his Morals: An idle word is that which lacks either the reason of just necessity or the intention of pious utility. *(The same has similar things in homily 6 on the Gospel near the end; likewise Bernard in his sermon on the triple custody of the hand, tongue, and heart, and others. Regarding the meaning of the word ἐργὸς, one can also consult Don Laur. Ramirez in Pentecont. c. 17. However, this pronouncement of the Savior must be understood with a limitation, unless remission has been made, which the pious obtain through faith, by which they apprehend the satisfaction of Christ. Therefore, whoever shall have departed from here in true faith, an account will by no means be demanded of him concerning an idle word: he shall not come into judgment Ioh. 5, 24. when God shall have cast his sins into the depths of the sea, Mich 7, 19. Conf. Es. 43, 25. Ier. 31, 34. Ezech 18, 22. Add B. D. Fewrb. Syntag. 2. Disquis. sacr. p. 580. seqq. B. P. L. de Extr. Iud. §. 94.)*

They shall render an account. In rendering an account they will not have anything by which they may excuse an idle word before God, so that He might acquiesce. If God wishes to enter into judgment, they will be compelled to render an account even for an idle word. *(It is evident, however, from the fact that even for any idle word, if God wishes to enter into judgment, men are compelled to render an account, that it is inept for the same Jesuit and Cardinal Bellarmine, l. 1. de Amiss. gr. & statu pecc. c. 9. §. Accedant, to conclude that there are certain sins venial by their own nature. We indeed concede that it will be that those who have uttered an idle word will be punished more mildly in the final judgment than those who have committed other more grave and exterior crimes; because, however, both (unless they have obtained the remission of sins in this world through true repentance) will be damned, that is, will be subjected to eternal punishments, it is manifest that no sin is venial by its own nature, although one is graver than another, and also to be punished more gravely. Furthermore, Capellus brings forward the opinion of R. Jonah, not unlike this one of the Savior, in Spicil. p. 22. Conf. also Hacksp. de Util. Script. Rabb. p. 437.)*

*( In the day of judgment. to wit, the final one, as the Jesuits Corn. à Lapide, Maldonatus, and other Papists explain. The Jesuit Conzen expressly in this place, page 252: This word (idle) will be judged in the last day and deemed worthy of punishment etc. It is evident, therefore, that their associates Salmeron, Bunderius, Roffensis, and several others are vain, who strive to build Purgatory from this, since in the final judgment there will no longer be a Purgatory. Compare more on this matter in B. Par. Confess. Cath. vol. 3, p. 501. also L. de Morte. §. 276. B. D. Meisn. de Purg. Op. 2. n. 212. 516.)*

Latin:

v. 36. De verbo otioso rationem reddent. Smalcius in refut. Smigl. de satisf. c. 8. p. 239. Illud de verbo otioso, de quo reddent rationem homines in die iudicii, non de levi peccato necesse est accipere, sed de tali otioso verbo vel saltem eius simili, de quo ibi sermo est, nempe quod blasphemiam quandam contineat. *(Similia habet idem in Refut. Thes. D. Frantzii pag. 368.

Remonstrantes in Apolog. Confess. p. 90. per verbum otiosum solam blasphemiam in Sp. S. intellectum volunt. Iesuita Maldonatus ad minimum verbum calumniatorium significari hîc putat. Dion. Carthusianus itidem per verbum otiosum tale intelligit peccatum, quod prorsus excludat poenitentiam.)* Verùm rectiùs Hieronymus in h. l. Verbum otiosum est, quod sine utilitate loquentis vel audientis profertur, si omissis seriis, de rebus frivolis loquamur, & fabulas narremus antiquas. Caeterùm qui scurrilia explicat & cachinnis ora dissolvit, & aliquid profert turpitudinis, hic non otiosi verbi, sed criminosi tenebitur reus. Gregorius in Moral. Otio sum verbum est, quod aut ratione iustae necessitatis, aut intentione piae utilitatis caret. *(Similia habet idem hom. 6. in Evang. sub finem. it Bernhardus serm. de Tripl. custod. manus, linguae & cordis, alii. De significatione vocis ἐργὸς consuli, quoque potest Don Laur. Ramirez in Pentecont. c. 17. Intelligendum verò hoc Salvatoris pronunciatum cum limitatione, nisi factâ fuerit remissio, quam pii consequuntur per fidem, quâ Christi satisfactionem apprehendunt. Qui igitur in verâ fide hinc discesserit, ab illo minimè exigetur ratio de otioso verbo: nōn. veniet in iudiciū Ioh. 5, 24. cum Deus eius peccata proieccerit in profundum maris,Mich 7, 19. Conf. Es. 43, 25.Ier. 31, 34.Ezech 18, 22. Add. B. D. Fewrb. Syntag. 2. Disquis. sacr. p. 580. seqq. B. P. L. de Extr. Iud. §. 94.)*

Reddent rationem. In reddendâ ratione non habebunt, quo verbum otiosum apud Deum excusent, ut ille acquiescat. Si Deus in iudicium velit intrate, etiam de otioso verbo cogentur rationem reddere. *(Patet verò ex eò quòd etiam de quolibet verbo otioso, si Deus velit in iudicium intrare, homines cogantur rationem reddere, ineptè ex h. l. Iesuitam eundemq; Cardinalem Bell. l. 1. de Amiss. gr. & statu pecc. c. 9. §. Accedant, colligere, esse quaedam peccata sui naturâ venialia. Concedimus quidem, fore, ut mitiùs puniantur in extremo iudicio, qui verbum otiosum protulerint, quàm qui alia graviora & exteriora scelera cōmise: int quia tamen utrique (nisi in hoc mundo per veram poenitentiam remissionem peccatorum fuerint consequuti) damnabuntur h. e. aeternis poenis subiicientur, manifestum est, null um peccatum esse naturâ suâ veniale, licet aliud alio gravius sit, ac graviùs etiam puniendum. Porrò sententiam R. Ionae, isti Salvatoris non absimilem adducit Capellus in Spicil. p. 22. Conf. etiam Hacksp. de Util. Script. Rabb. p. 437.)*

*( In die iudicii. scil. extremi, uti explicant Iesuitae Corn. à Lapide, Maldonatus, aliique Pontificii. Disertè Iesuita Conzen in h. l. pag. 252. Hoc verbum (otiosum) in extremo die iudicabitur & poenâ dignum censebitur &c. Patet igitur, vanos esse eorundē sociennos Salmeronem, Bunderium, Roffensem, aliosque nonnullos, qui hinc Purgatorium extruere satagunt, cùm in extremo iudicio non ampliùs futurum sit Purgatorium. Conf. plura in hanc rem apud B. Par. Confess. Cath. t. 3. p. 501. it. L. de Morte. §. 276. B. D. Meisn. de Purg. Op. 2. n. 212. 516.)*

## 12:37
v. 37. By thy words thou shalt be justified. He who speaks good things, making for the glory of GOD and the edification of his neighbor, is recognized as truly pious; he who speaks evil, by blaspheming God and his neighbor, is recognized as evil and impious. Thus the word to be justified, i.e., to be declared, recognized as just, is also taken elsewhere. See Ps. 51, 9.Luc. 7, 29.Iacob. 2, 21.24. coll. with v. 18. 20.

*( By words, not on account of words or thy good works, shalt thou be justified. Compare Rom. 6, 23.)* *( Thou shalt be justified, and thou shalt be condemned etc. The blessed D. Glass. Gr. S. p. 603 notes that the particle καὶ in this place is disjunctive, since to be condemned and to be justified do not fall upon one subject. In the same way B. Par. takes it, L. de Iustif. §. 5.)*

*( A sign. Understand one more excellent and greater than those hitherto produced. Similar to these are the Papists, who likewise demand miracles from us, when nevertheless they ought rather to lend their ears to St. Augustine, who in book 22, de civ. D. chapter 8, writes expressly: I could, he writes, say that they were necessary (miracles) before the world believed, to the end that the world might believe. Whoever still seeks prodigies in order to believe, he himself is a great prodigy, who does not believe when the world believes. That miracles are not a mark of the Church, B. Par. shows at length in L. de Eccl. §. 271. seqq. Confes. Cath. vol. 2, p. 1227. seqq. P. Martyr, Pererus, and several others also err, who think that signs can be sought from GOD in certain cases even today. See this error refuted in D. Bald. Comm. in c. 6. Zach. p. 393.)*

Latin:

v. 37. Ex verbis tuis iustificaberis. Qui loquitur bona, ad gloriam DEI & proximi aedificationem facientia, is agnoscitur verè pius; qui loquitur mala, Deum & proximum blasphemando, agnoscitur malus & impius. Ita verbum iustificari, h. e. pro declarari, agnosci iustum, alibi etiam accipitur. Vid. Ps. 51, 9.Luc. 7, 29.Iacob. 2, 21.24. coll. cum v. 18. 20.

*( Ex verbis, non propter verba vel opera tua bona, iustificaberis. Conf. Rom. 6, 23.)* *( Iustificaberis, & condemnaberis &c. Notat B. D. Glass. Gr. S. p. 603. particulam καὶ h. l. esse disiunctivam, cùm condemnari ac iustificari non cadant in unum subiectum. Eodem modo accipit B. Par. L. de Iustif. §. 5.)*

*( Signum. Intellige praestantius & maius, quàm hactenus edita. Similes sunt his Pontificii, qui itidem miracula à nobis exigunt, cùm tamen aures potiùs praebere deberent S. Augustino, qui l. 22. dec. d. cap. 8. disertè: Possem, scribit, dicere, necessaria fuisse (miracula) prius quàm crederet mundus, ad hoc ut crederet mundus. Quisquis adhuc prodigia, ut credat, inquirit, magnum ipse est prodigium, qui mundo credente non credit. Quòd verò miracula non sint Ecclesiae nota, prolixè ostendit B. Par. L. de Eccl. §. 271. seqq. Confes. Cath. t. 2. p. 1227. seqq. Errant quoque P. Martyr, Pererus aliique nonnulli, qui hodienum signa certis in casibus peti à DEO posse, censent. Quem errorem refutatum vide ap-D. Bald. Comm. in c. 6. Zach. p. 393.)*

## 12:38
v. 38. Then they answered &c. The word ἀποκρίνεσθουν is used by the Evangelists not only for a direct response to questions, but also for other utterances explaining something in the present, about which a question could have been asked. Just as in this place the Pharisees, as if asking why He performed no miracle in their presence, say that they desire to see some sign from Him. Namely from heaven, as is explained in Mark and Luke, i.e., some peculiar and extraordinary thing, which cannot be drawn into doubt.

Latin:

v. 38. Tunc respondebant &c. Verbum ἀποκρίνεσθουν surpatur ab Evangolistis non solùm de directâ responsione, ad interrogata, sed de aliis etiam locutionibus, explicantiòus aliquid in praesentia, de quo interrogatio fieri potuisset. sicut hoc loco Pharisaei velut quaerentes, cur nullum coram ipsis faceret miraculum, dicunt, cupere se aliquod ab ipso signum videre. Scilicet è coelo, ut apud Marcum & Lucam exponitur, i. e. aliquod peculiare & eximium, quod non possit trabiia dubium.

## 12:39
*(v. 39. An adulterous generation. Conf. Is. 57, 3. They are said to be so, because they did not stand in the faith of Abraham. Add. c. 16, 4. c. 3, 7. It is known that idolatry is expressed in the H. S. by the words of adultery and whoredom. See B. D. Glass. Rhet. S. p. 383)*

*( No sign shall be given except the sign of Jonah. But there exist very many types by which Christ was prefigured in the O. T., such as the sale in Joseph, Gen. 37, 28. the binding in Isaac, Gen. 22, 9. &c. as B. Par. shows at length in Hom. Acad. part. 1. p. 778. Resp. Very many types were indeed exhibited of old, and noted also in the tables of the O. T., but Christ at that time set forth only that one, and taught that what had been prefigured was to be fulfilled in Himself.)*

The sign of Jonah the Prophet. i.e., that sign which was prefigured through the Prophet Jonah, namely the glorious resurrection from the dead after three days. Rom. 1, 4. *(B. D. Glass. Philol. S. p. 316 observes that our Savior, while He here calls the type of Jonah a sign, is adapting His speech to the words of the Pharisees, who were demanding a sign from Him, since otherwise sign and type differ: for a sign can be of a thing dissimilar, but the condition of a type is that it has a similarity with the thing signified.)*

Latin:

*(v. 39. Generatio adultera. Conf. Es. 57, 3. dicuntur ita, quia in fide Abrahami non steterunt. Add. c. 16, 4. c. 3, 7 Notum est, quòd idololatria in Sc. S. adulterii & scortationis vocibus exprimatur. Vid. B. D. Glass. Rhet. S. p. 383)*

*( Signum dabitur nisi signum Ionae. At plurimi extant typi, quibus Christus in V. T. fuit praefiguratus, uti venditio in Iosepho, Gen. 37, 28. ligatio in Isaaco, Gen. 22, 9. &c. ceu prolixè ostendit B. Par. Hom. Acad. part. 1. p. 778. Resp. Plurimi quidem typi olim exhibiti sunt, & in tabulis etiam V. T. annotati, sed Christus tum temporis non nifi unicum illum exposuit, & in se, quod praefiguratum fuit, impletum iri, docuit.)*

Signum Ionae Prophetae. i. e. illud signum, quod per Prophetam Ionam est praefiguratum, gloriosa scil. post triduum è mortuis resurrectio. Rom. 1, 4. *(Observat B. D. Glass. Philol. S. p. 316. Salvatorem nostrum, dum typum Ionae hic signum vocat, accommodare suum sermonem ad Pharisae orum verba, qui signum ab eo postulabant, cùm aliàs signum & typus differant: siquidem signum possit esse rei dissimilis, typi verò ea conditio, ut cum re significata habeat similitudinē.)*

## 12:40
v. 40. The Son of man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. The last part of the day of preparation is taken synecdochically for the whole day, the beginning of the Lord's day is likewise taken for the whole according to the same synecdoche. And thus the number of days is consistent, even if He did not complete those entire days. As regards the nights, first, there are beyond controversy two nights which lie between the day of preparation and the resurrection. Furthermore, just as the last part of the day of preparation is counted for the whole day, so because the Hebrews begin the numbering of natural days from the evening, it is manifest that the preceding night is said to be a part or beginning of that which they call the preparation, and therefore similarly to come into that numbering συνεκδοχικῶς. *(Thus B. D. Hunnius calculates in this place. In the same way they complete the number of three days and nights from the ancients: St. Augustine lib. 1. Qq. Ev. c. 7. similarly ep. 49. q. 6. it. in Ps. 88. Isidor. Pelus. l. 1. ep. 114. Theoph. in this place; and from the more recent ones, Dn. D. Walth. H. E. p. 769. B. P. Harm. E. c. 207. Whence also the Savior says that He will rise on the third day, inf. c. 16, 21. c. 17, 23. &c. B. D. Quistorpius notes that since the word day is ambiguous, and signifies now an artificial, now a natural day: the Hebrews (whose form of speaking the Apostles and Evangelists retain) are accustomed, when they understand νυχθήμερον,, to place parts of the day, even if the thing was not done in the whole day; therefore the integral parts are placed here for the whole, and through the whole συνεκδοχικῶς a part of it is understood. In the same way B. D. Calixtus Conc. Ev. l. 7. c. 1. Dn. D. Friedlieb Obs. in H. S. p. 112. Hugo Grotius in this place, and others.)*

*( In the heart of the earth. i. e. the sepulcher. But the Jesuits insist, Petrus Cotonus lib. 4. Inst. Cath. p. 778. Truly the heart of the earth can in no way be called a sepulcher. Bellarminus l. 2. de Purg. c. 6. Others say that the sepulcher is called the heart of the earth, but the comparison is repugnant. For the heart is in the deepest place of an animal; but the sepulcher is near the surface of the earth, and the sepulcher of Christ seems to have been above the earth; for it was a monument hewn in stone standing above the earth. Item just as Jonah was alive in the belly of the whale, so some-- ought to have been in the heart of the earth, which cannot be understood of the body dead--o, but of the soul living and remaining for three days in hell. Therefore the heart of the earth is not the sepulcher, but hell, --lcro much deeper, where the soul of Christ, remained is. He adds: In the same way they explain this place Irenaeus l. 5. near the end, Tertullianus l. de anim. c. 31. Nyss. Orat. 1. de Res. Ambr. in c. 4. Eph. But other Papists more correctly accept the sepulcher. Thus expressly Iansenius Bishop of Ghent in his Commentaries on the Concord and History of the Gospels (which obtained this eulogy from Ioh. Molanus, Apostolic Censor, appended to the work, that on account of singular piety and erudition, they are most useful to the Christian Republic, and that this is the common judgment of learned men.) Cap. 49. p. 382. Jonah, he writes, was a sign to the Ninevites by this, that he was in the belly of the whale for three days, and then returned alive &c. thus it is signified, that the son of man also for that reason would rest in the sepulcher for three days and then rise again, so that it may be a sign to the Jews, that he himself was sent by God to preach repentance. The Jesuit Conzen on this place: That the heart of the earth is not the sepulcher—for that consists of being hewn in the earth on the surface of the earth—many feel, but rather hell, where the limbo of the fathers was constructed, for that was near the lower regions, that is, the center of the earth. But he immediately adds: Many however (Papists i. e. Roman Catholics, and the Jesuit Ioh. Pineda the Spaniard is also in their number in c. 1. Iob. v. 21. n. 5.) deem that it was the sepulcher. Emanuel Saa also admits, certain Doctors (meaning Papists) understand the sepulcher. The Jesuits Corn. à Lapide and Tirinus on this place, even if they embrace the opinion about limbo, nevertheless do not dare to reject the opinion about the sepulcher, but join both. But if indeed the sepulcher is understood by the heart of the earth, it is inept, certainly less firm, to construct limbo from this place, as both Bellarminus and those who follow him strive to do. For if by the heart of the earth the sepulcher can also be understood, it follows that it does not necessarily have to be understood as the lowest place or the center of the earth. It is also false that the sepulcher of Christ existed above the earth. Whence even Bell. himself speaks doubtfully. But it is well to be noted; that the name heart taken for the middle of something does not always denote an exact midpoint, as even from the single --lo place Ezech. 27, 4. where the Vulgate imitated both the LXX and the text itself, it says expressly concerning Tyre, that it was in the heart of the sea . Which nevertheless, at least on account of the sea, was situated, or an island

the Jesuits are forced to admit that it is closest to the solid earth, and therefore not in the center of the sea, unless they wish of their own accord to expose themselves to the mockery of all. But there are also examples elsewhere in the authentic text, where the word לב does not always denote an exact middle. Thus, Deut. IV, 11, it is said that the mountain burned השמים ער־לב,, which words the Vulgate, following the LXX, correctly expressed as 'unto the midst of heaven'. On the same passage, the Jesuit Corn. à Lapide correctly says: Heb. unto the heart of heaven, i.e. unto heaven itself. Do not understand heaven here as the aerial or ethereal one, in which the clouds are. By a similar Hebraism, Jonah is said, (understand ch. 2, 4) David and others to have been in the midst of the sea, in the midst of the waves, i.e., in the very great and vast sea, in the very vast waves. To this also pertains especially the passage Prov. 30, 19 The way of a ship בלב־ום in the heart of the sea. Just as, therefore, it does not follow: Jonah was in the heart of the sea, the ship and Tyre are in the heart of the sea, and are or were in the lower places of the sea. So neither does it follow: Christ was in the heart of the earth. Therefore, He was in the center of the earth, namely in Limbo. But who taught the Jesuits that Limbo is in the center of the earth? Some Fathers indeed say that the pious ancients descended to the underworld, but by the underworld they understand nothing else than that which is called in the Hebrew text שאול, namely either the grave, or death itself. Furthermore, to the Fathers brought forward by Bellarmine for the confirmation of his opinion, we oppose others. Indeed, Isidore of Pelusium, book 1, ep. 114, expressly says that just as Jonah was for three days in the belly of the whale, so Christ was for as many days ἐνγρ τῷ τάφῳ.. Chrysostom likewise teaches that Christ denoted by the heart of the earth τὸν τάφον. Ignatius also, almost the most ancient of all, in his 2nd epistle, which is to the Trallians, writes that Christ was buried before the setting of the sun, remained under the earth on the Sabbath ἐντῷ μνημείῳ, and rose on the Lord's day, κατα τὸ εἰρημεύων ὑπαυτου Ωσπερ. ἦν Ἰωνᾶς etc. We omit now that the fifth book of Irenaeus, whose chapter 31 the Jesuits Coton in his Instit. Cathol. p. 777 and Cornelius on this passage allege, consists of at least twenty-six chapters. Also, that Irenaeus elsewhere, namely book 4, ch. 45, relies in this matter on tradition ἀγράφῳ.. As regards Tertullian, to whom Bellarmine, Cornelius, Trinus, etc., and others commonly appeal, and indeed to his book on the soul, it should be known that Bellarmine, in his book on Ecclesiastical Writers, page 52, diligently warns, That book, just as certain other books of Tertullian, is to be read with judgment, since in it not a few propositions occur that are either erroneous or certainly suspect. If we have left room for this admonition, and have referred these propositions also to those in which he perhaps seems to favor limbo, the Cardinal will, we hope, bear it not with difficulty. And the same man will remember that elsewhere he holds Tertullian for a heresiarch, nor is his authority great to him. Why, therefore, should we esteem the testimony of Tertullian as great, especially when he departs from the H. S.? And furthermore, Tertullian does not even have γρυ concerning limbo in the place alleged by Bell. Elsewhere indeed, namely in chapter 55, he has something similar, but in the same place he also asserts, every soul, separated from the body, is sequestered in the underworld until the day of the final judgment. But if this can be called erroneous, why not also that concerning limbo? It does not please me now to examine the testimonies of other Fathers. Nor do the Fathers constitute the foundation of our faith, but the H. S. And besides, others disagree, as has just been shown. But what of that, that the body of Jonah was alive, but the body of Christ was dead? We reply that we concede that Christ was truly dead, yet in such a way that his flesh remained life-giving even in the tomb itself. Who, moreover, would deny that Jonah in the belly of the whale was more like a dead man than a living one? And what need is there to seek a likeness in all things between the type and the antitype? It is sufficient that such can be shown in most things, as the blessed D. Chemnitz has performed at length. Harm. Ev. chap. 59.

Latin:

v. 40. Filius hominis erit tres dies & tres noctes in corat -errae. Ultima diei parasceves particula synecdochicè pro totâ die sumitur, initium quoque diei Dominicae itidem pro toto secundùm eandem synecdochen. Atque sic dierum numerus constat, etiamsi non integros illos compleverit. Noctes quod attinet, primùm extra controversiam sunt duae noctes, quae inter diem parasceves & resurrectionem interiacent. Porrò sicut ultima diei parasceves pars pro toto die numeratur, sic quia Hebraei dierum naturalium numerationē à vesperâ incipiunt, palam est, antegressam noctem dici illius, quam parasceven dicunt, esse partem seu initium, ac proinde similiter in numerationem illamσυνεκδοχικῶςvenire. *(Ita calculum ducit B. D. Hunnius in h. l. Eodem modò numerum trium dierum ac noctium complent ex veteribus S. Augustinus lib. 1. Qq. Ev. c. 7. similiter ep. 49. q. 6. it. inPs. 88.Isidor. Pelus. l. 1. ep. 114. Theoph. in h. l. ex recentioribus verò Dn. D. Walth. H. E. p. 769. B. P. Harm. E. c. 207. Unde etiam Salvator dicit, se tertiâ die resurecturum, inf. c. 16, 21. c. 17, 23. &c. B. D. Quistorpius notat, quòd cùm vox diei ambigua fit, & nunc artificialem, nunc naturalem diem significet: solere Ebraeos (quorum loquendi formam Apostoli & Ev. retinent) cùm intelligunt νυχθήμερον, ponere die partes, licet res totô die gesta non sit, partes igitur integrantes poni hîc pro toto, & per totum συνεκδοχικῶς partem eius intelligi. Eodem modo B. D. Calixtus Conc. Ev. l. 7. c. 1. Dn. D. Friedlieb Obs. in H. S. p. 112. Hugo Grotius in h. l. & alii.)*

*( In corde terrae. i. e. sepulcro. Ast instant Iesuitae, Petrus Cotonus lib. 4. Inst. Cath. p. 778. Sanè cor terrae minime sepulcrum appellari potest. Bellarminus l. 2. de Purg. c. 6. Dicunt alii, sepulchrum appellari corterrae, sed repugnat similitudo. Nam cor est in profundissimo loco animalis; sepulcrum autem est prope superficiem terrae, & Christi sepulcrum videtur fuisse supraterram; erat enim monumentiū excisum in lapide supra terram extans. Item sicut Ionas fuit vivus in ventre ceti, ita aliq-- debuisset esse in corde terrae, quod non de corpore mor--o, sed de anima vivente & per triduum in infernô commorante intelligi potest. Non igitur cor terrae est sepulcrum, sed infernus, --lcro multò profundior, ubi Christi anima, idue commorata est. Addit: Eodem modo h. l. explicant Irenaeus l. 5. circa finem, Tertullianus l. de anim. c. 31. Nyss. Orat. 1. de Res. Ambr. in c. 4. Eph. Verùm rectiùs alii Pontificii sepulcrum accipiunt. Ita didisertè Ianseniuss Episcopus. Gandavensis in Conc. & Hist. Evangell Commentariis (quae hoc à Ioh. Molano, Censore Apostolico obtinuerunt elogium operi subiunctum, quòd propter singularem pietatem & eruditionem, Reipubl. Christianae utilissima sint, idq; commune esse doctorum virorum iudicium.) Cap. 49. p. 382. Ionas, scribit, fuit signum Ninivitis per hoc, quòd fuit in ventre ceti tribus diebus, ac deinde vivus redditus &c. sic significatur, etiam filium hominis ob id in sepulcro tribus diebus quieturum ac deinde resurrecturum, ut sit signum Iudaeis, ipsum missum fuisse à Deo ad praedicandam poenitentiam. Iesuita Conzen in h. l. Cor terrae non esse sepulcrumid enim in terrâ excisum in superficie terrae consistit, multi sentunt, sed potiùs infernum, ubi limbus patrum constructus est, ille enim prope inferos fuit, hoc est, centrum terrae. Statim verò subiungit: Multi tamen (Pontificii s. Romano-Catholici, estq; in eorum etiā numero Iesuita Ioh. Pineda Hispanus in c. 1. Iob. v. 21. n. 5.) Sepulcrum fuisse autumant. Etiā Emanuel Saa fatetur, quosdam Doctores (intell. Pontificios) intelligere sepulcrum. Iesuitae Corn. à Lapide ac Tirinus in h. l. ut ut sententiam de limbo amplectantur, non audent tamen sententiam de sepulcro reiicere, sed utramque coniungunt. Quod si verò sepulchrum per cor terrae intelligitur, ineptè, certè minùs firmiter, ex hoc loco limbam adstruere, tum Bellarminus, tum qui eundem sequuntur, satagunt. Si enim per cor terrae etiam sepulcrum intelligi potest, sequitur, quòd non necessariò debeat intelligi locus infimus vel centrum terrae. Falsum etiam est, Christi sepulcrum oxtitisse supra terram. Unde etiam ipse Bell. dubitativè loquitur. Probè verò notandum; quod cordis nomen pro medio alicuius acceptum non exactam semper medietatem notet, ceu vel ex unico --lo loco Ezech. 27, 4. ubi Vulg-imitatus tum LXX. tum ipsum textum, disertè de Tyro dicit, quòd in corde maris fuersita. Quam tamen saltem propter mare fuisse sitam, sive insulam

terrae solidae proximam, adeoque non in maris centro, fateri cogentur Iesuitae, nisi sponte velint omnium ludibrio sese exponere. Sed adsunt etiam alibi in textu authentico exempla, ubi vocabulum לב non exactam semper medietatem notat. Sic Deut. IV, 11. dicitur, quòd mons arseritהשמים ער־לב, quae verba Vulgatus, sequutus LXX. rectè expressit usque ad coelum. In eundem locum rectè Iesuita Corn. à Lapide: Ebr. usq; ad cor coeli h. e. usad coelum ipsum. Coelum hic non aërium sive aethereum, in quo sunt nubes, intellige. Simili hebraismo dicitur Ionas, (intell. c. 2, 4.) David & alii fuisse in medio mari, in mediis fluctibus i. e. in ipso mari magno & vasto, in ipsis vastis fluctibus. Huc quoque facit cumprimis locus Prov. 30, 19.Via navisבלב־וםin corde maris. Quemadmodum igitur non sequitur, Ionas fuit in corde maris, navis ac Tyrus sunt in corde maris E in inferioribus maris locis sunt vel fuerunt. Ita necsequitur. Christus fuit in corde terrae. E. fuit in terrae centro, nempe inlimbo. Quis verò docuit Iesuitas, quòd limbus sit in centro terrae. Patres sanè nonnulli descendisse pios veteres ad inferos dicunt, sed per inferos nihil aliud intelligunt, quàm illud quod in textu Ebr. שאול dicitur, nempe vel sepulcrum, vel ipsam mortem. Praetereà Patribus, à Bell. pro sententiae suae confirmatione adductis, opponimus alios. Sanè Isidorus Pelusiota l. 1. ep. 114. disertè dicit, quòd ceu Ionas tribus diebus fuit in ventre ceti, ita Christus totidem diebus fuerit ἐνγρ τῷ τάφῳ. Chrys. pariter docet, Christum per corterraeτὸν τάφον denotasse. Ignatius etiam, omnium ferè antiquissimus, epist. 2. quae est ad Trallianos, scribit, quod Christus ante solis occasum fuerit sepultus, Sabbato sub terra remanseritἐντῷ μνημείῳ,ac Dominico die resurrexerit,κατα τὸ εἰρημεύων ὑπαυτου Ωσπερ. ἦν Ἰωνᾶς &c. Omittimus iam quòd Irenaei liber quintus, cuius cap. 31. allegant Iesuitae Cotonus Instit. Cathol. p. 777. ac Cornelius in h. l. saltem sex & viginti constet capitibus. it. quòd Irenaeus alibi, nempe l. 4. c. 45. nitatur hâc in re traditione ἀγράφῳ. Quod Tertullianum spectat, ad quem Bellarminus, Cornelius, Trinus &c. aliique cōmuniter Provocant, & quidem ad librum eius de anima, sciendum, quòd Bell. lib. de Script. Eccl. pag. 52. diligenter moneat, librum illum, sicuti & alios quosdam Tertull. libros, cum iudicio legendum esse, quippe cùm in eo propositiones non paucae vel erroneae vel certè suspectae occurrant. Cui admonitioni si locum reliquerimus, & ad propositiones eas, has quoque, in quibus fortè limbo favere ille videtur, retulerimus, haut aegrè, speramus, feret Cardinalis. Ac recordabitur idem, quòd alibi Tertullianum pro haeresiarcha habeat, nec magna eius ipsi sit auctoritas. Cur igitur nos magni testimoniū Tertulliani aestimemus, cumprimis à Sc. S. discendentis? ac insuper ne γρυ quidem Tertull. de limbo habet loco à Bell. allegato. Alibi quidem, nempe c. 55. simile quid habet, sed ibidem etiam adserit, omnem animam, à corpore separatam apud inferos sequestrari usque ad diem extremi iudicii. Quod si hoc dici erroneum potest, cur non & illud de limbo? Aliorum Patrum testimonia excutere iam non libet. Neque etiam Patres fidei nostrae fundamentum constituunt, sed Sc. S. Et repugnant insuper alii, ut modò ostensum. Sed quid ad illud, quòd corpus Ionae fuerit vivum, Christi verò corpus mortuum? Resp. Christum reverà mortuum esse concedimus, ita tamen, ut caro eius etiam in ipso sepulcro manserit vivifica. Quis praeterea neget, Ionam in ventre ceti mortuo, quàm vivo fuisse similiorem? Et quid opus est, in omnibus quaerere similitudinem inter typum & antitypum. Sufficit quod in plurimis talis ostendi possit, ceu prolixè id praestitit B. D. Chemuit. Harm. Ev. cap. 59.)*

## 12:41
v. 41. The men of Nineveh shall rise again. Here is a notable passage for the resurrection of the dead. For they had long since been reduced to ashes when Christ spoke these words.)*

Latin:

*(v. 41. Ninivitae resurgent. Est hic insignis locus pro resurrectione mortuorum. Illi enim iampridem in cinerem redacti erant, cùm Christus haec loqueretur.)*

## 12:42
v. 42. Queen of the South. In the Confession of faith of the Abyssinians, as it is reported by Damião de Góis concerning the customs of the Ethiopians, this Queen is called Maqueda, and she is said to have conceived from Solomon a son, Milech, who afterwards assumed the name of David. Fulgosus calls her Nicaula, Queen of Egypt and Ethiopia. See Theodoret, q. 22 in Numbers. Aben Ezra in chap. 11.

Daniel. The daughter of the King of the South is the Queen of Sheba, which kingdom is called in the Ishmaelite or Arabic language Aliman. This Sheba is Southern with respect to the land of Israel. *(Compare also what the Blessed D. Glass. Gr. S. p. 852 and the Blessed D. Tarnov. on Joel ch. 3, 8, p. 107, note about this Queen.)*

*( From the ends of the earth i. e. from afar. See Mayer Prodr. Philol. S. p. 18.)*

*( And shall condemn. Compare Isid. Pelus. b. 1, ep. 166 & 154. Remig. on 1 Cor. 6, p. 38. The saints, lovers of this world, shall judge by the example of their faith and by comparison having been made better, not as judges of the age. In almost the same way Hieron. writes, He shall condemn, not by the power of a sentence, but by the example of comparison. Compare a similar passage from the Rabbis in Hacksp. on the utility of reading the Rabbis, p. 438.)*

Latin:

v. 42. Regina Austri. In Confessione fidei Abyssinorum, sicut à Damiano à Goes de Aethiopum moribus resertur, haec Regina appellatur Maqueda, & ex Salomone filium Milech, qui postea Davidis nomen assumsit, suscepisse dicitur. Fulgosus eam Nicaulam Aegypti & Aethiopiae Reginam vocat. Vide Theodor. q. 22. in Numer. Aben Ezra in c. 11.

Daniel. Filia Regis Austri est Regina Saba, quod regnum vocatur linguâ Ismaëlitica seu Arabica Aliman. Haec Saba est Australis respectu terrae Israël. *(Conf. etiam quae hâc de Regina annocat B. D. Glass. Gr. S. p. 852. B. D. Tarnov. ad Ioël c. 3, 8. pag. 107.)*

*( A finibus terrae i. e. à longinqno. Vid. Mayerum Prodr. Philol. S. p. 18.)*

*( Et condemnabit. Conf. Isid. Pelus. l. 1. ep. 166. & 154. Remig. in 1. Cor. 6, p. 38. Sancti amatores huius mundi iudicabunt exemplo fidei suae & comparatione meliores facti, non sicut iudices seculi. Eod. ferè modo Hieron. Condemnabit, scribit, non sententiae potestate, sed comparationis exemplo. Conf. similem locum ex Rabb. apud Hacksp. de util. lect. Rabb. pag. 438.)*

## 12:43
*(v. 43. When it has gone out i. e. when it has been cast out, as Theophyl. rightly proposes.)*

Through waterless places. Places ἄνυδρα, in which waters are not found are not convenient for dwelling. The unclean Spirit, therefore, not finding a place in which it may rest, betakes itself to the former. Theophylact sometimes proposes an opinion more remote from the text, for he interprets these things concerning the unbaptized, in whom, he says, the Spirit does not seek rest, because it already has them before in its power, as if it disdained that domicile; it seeks, therefore, the baptized. Zanchius in Miscell. p. 178 thinks that this passage deals only with desperate Jews. And yet the occasion of the saying can be special, and the saying itself general: Ps. 14, 1. Rom. 3, 10. *(Therefore, in this place, by arid places are understood in general the hearts of men, i. e., those not having the dew of divine grace, as Dionysius the Carthusian rightly explains, who nevertheless less rightly accepts that this is said only of the Gentiles. For there are also very many among Christians who despise the streams and dew of the divine word. Thus the Blessed D. Chemnitius Harm. Ev. ch. 59 explains this passage. But the glossators of the Ernestine Bibles, the Blessed D. Calixtus in Conc., and the Blessed D. Glass. in Evang. Dom. Oculi p. 650, understand by arid places desert places, solitudes.)*

*( I will return into my house &c. The reborn, who were temples of the Holy Spirit, 1 Cor. 3:16 6:19 can become houses and stables of the Devil. Whence let us work out our salvation with fear and trembling, and he who thinks he stands, let him see that he does not fall. 1 Cor. 10:12 Therefore the Calvinists err, teaching the absolute inamissibility of faith. Concerning which error more will be treated at length at Luke 11:24)*

Latin:

*(v. 43. Cùm exierit i. e. cùm eiectus fuerit, uti rectè o-ponit Theophyl.)*

Per loca inaquosa. Loca ἄνυδρα, in quibus non reperiuntur aquae, non sunt ad habitandum commoda. Immundus igitur Spiritus non reperiens locum, in quo acquiescat, confert se ad priorem. Theophylactus aliquando remotiorem à textu sententiam proponit, interpretatur enim haec de non-baptizatis, in quibus inquit, Spiritus non quaerit requtē, quia iam antè eos habet in suâ potestate, quasisc. istud domicilium fastidiat, requirit igitur baptizatos. Zanchius in Miscell. pag. 178. tantùm de Iudaeis desperatis hoc loco agi existimat. Atqui dicti occasio potest esse specialis, & dictum ipsum generale: Psal. 14, 1.Rom. 3, 10. *(Intelliguntur igitur h. l. per loca arida in genere hominum corda i. e. gratiae divinae rorem non habentia, ut rectè exponit Dion. Carthusianus, qui tamen minùs rectè de solis gentilibus id dictum accipit. Sunt enim etiam inter Christianos plurimi, qui verbi divini fluenta ac rorem contemnunt. Ita locum hunc exponit B. D. Chemnitius Harm. Ev. c. 59. Glossatores verò Bibliorum Ernestinorum, B. D. Calixtus in Conc. ac B. D. Glass. in Evang. Dom. Oculi p. 650. per loca arida intelligūt loca deserta, solitudines.)*

*( Revertar in domum meam &c. E. renati, qui fuerunt templa Sp. Sancti, 1. Cor. 3, 16.c. 6, 19. possunt fieri domus ac stabula Diaboli. Unde cum tremore operemur salutem, & qui existimat, se stare, videat, ne cadat.1. Cor. 10, 12. Errant proinde Calviniani, absolutam fidei inamissibilitatem docentes. Quô de errore prolixiùs agetur ad Luc. 11, 24.)*

## 12:44
v. 44. Empty. The Syrian: empty of an inhabitant, clean and adorned. σχολάζοντα empty of the works of piety, destitute of the indwelling of Christ and the Holy Spirit.

Σεσαρωμένον, deprived of faith, piety, and Christian virtues and as it were swept clean. Κεκοσμημένον, at the beck, namely, of the Devil, by unbelief, impiety, contumacy, security, &c. *(See another explanation in B. D. Meisner. Ἀνσθρωπ Disp. 19. §. 7.)*

Latin:

v. 44. Vacantem. Syrus: ab habitatore vacuam, nitidam & adornatam. σχολάζοντα vacantem ab operibus pietatis, destitutam Christi ac Sp. Sancti inhabitatione.

Σεσαρωμένον, fide, pietate & Christianis virtutibus privatam & qs. scopus purgatam. Κεκοσμημένον, ad nutum sc. Diaboli, incredulitate, impietate, contumaciâ, securitate &c. *(Aliam explicationem vide apud B. D. Meisner. Ἀνσθρωπ Disp. 19. §. 7.)*

## 12:45
*(v. 45. Seven other spirits worse. It seems to be gathered from this that just as there are ranks among the evil Angels, so also one surpasses another in malice. See Camer. Myroth. Ev. p. 52.)*

*( The last condition becomes worse. This matter can be illustrated by the example of him who is once snatched away against his will. Compare John 3:14 2 Pet. 2:20.)*

Latin:

*(v. 45. Septem alios spiritus peiores. Videtur hinc colligi, quòd ceu inter malos Angelos ordines, ita etiam alter alterum malitiâ superet. Vid. Camer. Myroth. Ev. p. 52.)*

*( Fit ultima conditio deterior. Potest haec res illustari exemplo eius qui semel invito rapitur. Conf. Ioh. 3, 14. 2. Petr. 2, 20.)*

## 12:46
v. 46. Behold his mother and his brothers &c. By brothers are understood his cousins, who are enumerated Matt. 13:55 Christ does not allow an impediment to be cast in his way by relatives in the works of his calling. *(Learned men have observed everywhere that the appellation of brothers extends very broadly in the Holy Scriptures. Jerome, book 1, Against Helvidius, page 115: Now you will be taught that in the divine scriptures brothers are said to be so in four ways, by nature, by nation, by kinship, by affection. And the same man explains these things at greater length in the same place. Compare also on ch. 1 of the epistle to the Galatians; likewise Augustine, book 22, against Faustus, ch. 23.)*

*(As for the rest, those things which make for the illustration of the following verses will be brought forward in the Annotations on Mark 3:31 and following.)*

In this Chapter is proposed: I. The instruction of the people through various Parables, as concerning the man sowing, v. 3, 23. concerning the wheat and the tares, v. 24, 30. concerning the grain of mustard seed, v. 31, 32. concerning the leaven, v. 34. II. The rendering of the causes why Christ spoke through parables, v. 34, 35. III. The explanation of the parable concerning the tares, v. 36, 43. IV. Further preaching through parables, namely concerning the hidden Treasure, v. 44. concerning the pearls, v. 45, 46. concerning the net cast into the sea, 50. V. The scandalization of the Nazarenes in Christ, v. 53. following.

Latin:

v. 46. Ecce mater & fratres eius &c. Per fratres intelliguntur ipsius consobrini, qui enumerantur Matth. 13, 55. Non patitur Christus in operibus vocationis impedimentum sibi obiici à cognatis. *( Fratrum appellationem latissimè in Sc: S. patere, passim observarunt viri docti. Hieronym. lib. 1. Adv. Helvidium, pag. 115. Iam nunc doceberis, quatuor modis in scripturis divinis fratres dici, naturâ, gente, cognatione, affectu. Atque haec prolixiùs explicat idem ibidem. Conf. etiam in c. 1. ep. ad Gal. it. August. l. 22. con-ra Faust. c. 23.)*

*(Coeterùm quae ad illustrationem subseqq. versiculorum faciunt, adducentur in Annot. ad Marc. 3. vers. 31. seqq.)*

Proponitur in hoc Capite I. Populi per diversas Parabolas, uti de homine seminante, v. 3, 23. de tritico & zizaniis. v. 24. 30. de grano sinapis. v. 31, 32. de fermento. v. 34. informatio. II. Causae, cur Christus per parabolas loquutus fuerit, redditio. v. 34, 35. III. Parabolae de zizaniis explicatio v. 36. 43. IV. Ulterior per parabolas praedicatio, nempe de Thesauro abscondito. v. 44. de margaritis. v. 45, 46. de sagenâ in mare iactâ, 50. V. Nazarenorum in Christo scandalizatio. v. 53. seqq.

## 13:1
v. 1. ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείῃ. it is evident from these words that these parables were proposed on one and the same day, and indeed on that very day on which Christ had come into a dispute with the Scribes and Pharisees on account of the miracle of the cast-out demon, Chap. 12, 22. and on which his mother and brothers had visited him, v. 47. There are indeed those who deny that there is a continuous order between these parables and the histories of the preceding Chapter, since in Luke 8, 19, the history concerning the mother and brothers approaching Christ is placed after Christ's parabolic sermon, whence they take the word day for time, σονέκδοχικῶς. Thus Barradius t. 2. lib. 10. cap. 1. Harm. But 1. the particles τῇ and ἐκείνῃ do not admit that exposition of the word here. 2. Matthew and Mark observe the exact same order in the description of those histories. *(The Ethiopian especially favors the former opinion, who notably translates i. e. in that very hour The remaining Oriental Interpreters, such as the Syrian, Arab, and Persian, have: On that day.)*

Q. here: Why did Christ go out from the house to the sea? Theophylact thinks, that it was done on account of his mother, so that he might show due reverence to her, who had previously interrupted him while he was preaching. Chrysostom says, that it was done on account of a mystical cause, so that the place of teaching might indicate that the hearers were bitter and unstable like the sea. It is more correctly said that Christ, after the exhausted labors of healing, teaching, and disputing with virulent enemies, went out to the sea for the sake of relaxing his mind: But having noticed the desire of the people to hear the word, he instituted this long sermon.

ON CHAPTER XIII. SUMMARY AND DISPOSITION.

Latin:

v. 1. ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείῃ. constat ex his verbis, parabolas has uno eodemque die fuisse propositas, & quidem eo ipso die, quo Christus in concertationem cum Scribis & Pharisaeis ob miraculum eiecti daemonii venerat, Cap. 12, 22. ac quo mater ac fratres ipsius ipsum visitaverant, v. 47. Sunt quidem qui negant, inter has parabolas & praecedētis Capitis historias esse ordinem continuum, cùm Lucae 8, 19. Historia de matre & fratribus, Christum accedentibus, parabolicae Christi concioni postponatur, unde vocabulum diei pro tempore,σονέκδοχικῶς accipiunt. Ita Barradius t. 2. lib. 10. cap. 1. Harm. Sed 1. particulae τῇ & ἐκείνῃ illam vocabuli expositionē hîc non admittunt. 2. Matthaeus & Marcus eundem plane ordinem in descriptione Historiarum istarum observant. *(Favet priori sententiae cumprimis etiam Aethiops, qui notanter vertit i. e. in ipsâ horâ Reliqui Interp. Orientales, uti Syrus, Arabs, Persa habent: In illo die.)*

Q. hîc: Quare Christus è domo exierit ad mare? Theophylactus putat, id factū propter matrem, ut debitā illi reverentiā exhiberet, quae anteà inter praedicandum ipsum interpellaverat. Chrysostomus, id esse factum, ait, propter causam mysticam, ut locus docendi indicaret, auditores esse amaros & instabiles instar maris. Rectiùs dicitur, Christum post exantlatos labores sanandi, docendi & disputandi cum hostibus vitulentis, animi relaxandi gratiâ mare egressum esse: Sed desiderio populi verbum audiendi animadverso, hunc longum sermonem instituisse.

AD CAP. XIII. SUMMA AC DISPOSITIO.

## 13:3
(ON CHAPTER XIII. SUMMARY AND DISPOSITION.) *(v. 3. He spoke many things in parables. Jerome on this passage. It is not to be understood that (Christ) spoke everything in parables, but many things. He mixes clear things with obscure ones, so that through those things which they understand, they may be provoked to the knowledge of those things which they do not understand. )* Ἐ ραθολαῖς.

Ἐ ραθολαῖς. The Greeks define a parable as τὸ Item ἀδυ This description exists in Suidas: ἐπαχύ *(the blessed D. Glassius in Philol. Sacr. book 2, treatise 2, section 5, presents many other definitions and divisions of parables, as well as most useful canons concerning parables. Corn. à Lapide also reads some rules to be observed concerning the doctrine of parables in Proleg. Super. Evang. p. 23 & 24.)* A beautiful and necessary admonition concerning parables exists in Chrysostom, homily 65 on Matthew, vol. 2, fol. 408. τοῦ in parables one ought not to be overly concerned with individual words. See also on this matter Isidore of Pelusium, book 3, ep. 107. *(which Isidore in the said place notably says among other things: τούτου i.e., A parable or every similitude is to be explained according to the present purpose. Also deserving of observation here is that of Basil in the short rules, interrogation 55: indeed, the similitudes that are brought forward do not by any means correspond in every part to the things to which they are applied; but they act to direct the mind to the argument that is being treated. See also the excellent passage on this matter by Augustine in the blessed D. Glassius, Philol. S. book 2, page 349. The Jesuits also praise the same passage of Augustine: Salmero, vol. 7, tr. 3, page 16; Corn. à Lapide, Proloq. in Evang. page 24, and others: But they do not always observe it in practice. Thus the Jesuit Maldonatus also correctly warns throughout, that in parables individual parts are not to be subtly explored, nor are all to be accommodated. See his Comm. on the IV. Gospels, vol. 1, page 283, 741, col. 2, page 195, 298, 230, 271, 769, 907. The Jesuit Tirinus does the same in his Comm. on Matth. 20, 12. Beautifully also on this matter Ioh. Camero, Myroth. Evang. page 17.)* It must be noted that the parables of Christ are to be used as a painted picture, namely so that we do not think that whatever is painted has a meaning, but only a certain thing, for the sake of which it is necessary that the rest be painted. So that the anxiety and solicitude of some seems to be reprehensible, who in the parables of Christ strive to cut everything to the quick, which is not to interpret, but to vex and torture the parable.

Latin:

*(v. 3. Loquebatur multa per parabolas. Hieronymus in h. l. Non andum, quod non omnia loquutus sii (Christus) in parabolis, sed multa. Perspicua miscet obscuris, ut per ea, quae intelligunt, provotentur ad eorum notitiam, quae non intelligunt.)*

Ἐ ραθολαῖς. Graeci definiunt parabolam, quòd sit, τὸ Item ἀδυ Apud Suidam haec extat descriptio: ἐπαχύ *(alias plures Parabolae definitiones, divisiones, tum quoque canones de parabolis utilissiomos exhibet B. D Glassius Philol. Sacr. lib. 2. tr. 2. sect. 5. Col. legit quoque nonnullas regulas circa doctrinam de Parabolis observandas Corn. à Lapide Proleg. Super. Evanp. p. 23. & 24.)* Pulcra & necessaria de Parabolis admonitio extat apud Chrysostomum homil. 65. in Matth. t. 2. fol. 408. τοῦin parabolis non oportet nimia in singulis verbis curâ perangi. Vide etiam hac de re Isidorum Pelusiotam lib. 3. ep. 107. *(qui Isidorus d. l. inter alia notanter. τούτου i. e. Parabola s. similitudo omnis ex praesenti instituto est explicanda. Observationem quoque meretur hic illud Basilii in reg. brev. interrog. 55. sanè quae afferuntur similitudines nequaquā eae omninò singulis earū rerum ad quas allata sunt, partibus respondent; sed illud agunt, ut mentem ad id, de que agitur, argumentum dirigant. Vide quoque egreglum in hanc rem locum Augustini apud B. D. Glassium Philol. S. lib. 2. pag. 349. Laudant eundem Augustinis locum etiam Iesuitae, Salmero t. 7. tr. 3. pag. 16. Corn. â Lapide. Praeloq. in Evang. pag. 24. alli: Sed non semper in praxi observant. Sic Iesuita Maldonatus passim quoque rectè monet, quòd in parabolis singulae partes non sint subtiliter explorandae, nec omnes accommodandae. Vid. Comm. illius in IV. Evang. t. 1. pag. 283. 741. c. 2. pag. 195. 298. 230. 271. 769. 907. Idem facit Iesuita Tirinus Comm. ad Matth. 20, 12. Pulcre quoque in hanc rem Ioh. Camero Myroth. Evang. pag. 17. Animadvertendum, parabolis Christi utendum esse tanquam pictâ tabellâ, nempe ut ne putemus, quicquid pingitur, id habere significationem, sed certum quid duntaxat, quod ut pingatur, reliqua pingi necesse est. Ita ut reprehendenda videatur illa nonnullorum anxietas & sollicitudo, qui in parabolis Christi omnia student ad vivum resecare, quod est non interpretari, sed vexare & torquere parabolam)*

(v. 4. the birds came and devoured them, The spiritual birds are the Devils v. 19. drive away those birds with Abraham, Gen. 15, 11.)

## 13:5
(v. 5. καὶ ἐυθέως. The Blessed D. Glassius rightly advises in Gr. S. page 171. that the Adverb immediately, quickly sometimes include a delay of time. Thus also it is accepted Mark 1, 21.Jas. 1, 24.John 3, v. 14.Matt. 24, 29.)

They did not have βάθος γῆς depth of earth i. e. deep earth. A Hebraism (Similar examples are had Luke 1, 48.1 Cor. 1, 21.Rev. 17, 1. &c.)
