Non habebantβάθος γῆςprofunditatem terrae i. e. profundam terram. Hebraismus *(Similia exempla hahentur Luc. 1, 48.1. Cor. 1, 21.Apoc. 17, 1. &c.)*

## 13:7
(v. 7. they fell among thorns. Thus the Rabbis proverbially say concerning a benefit bestowed upon an ungrateful person אחיזי שקילא טיבותך ושריא i. e. your kindness has been taken away, and cast among thorns. It is read in Schabbas f. 63. 2. John Calvin in Instit. and from him John Georg Grossius in Theatro Bibl. in Vind of this place page 875. exclaim here, that the Ubiquitarians (by which name Grossius designates the Orthodox) are not helped by this parable of Christ for establishing the oral eating of the body of Christ. But it must be known, that our people by no means prove from this place the oral eating of the body of Christ with respect to the unworthy, as Grossius persuades himself: But that there are given ρόσκαιροι i. e. that faith can be lost, and this very thing also is evident not so much from this verse, as from v. 21. and the parallel place Luke 8, 13.. What Wendel objects, will be discussed in its own place.)

Latin:

*(v. 7. ceciderunt in spinas. Sic Rabbini de beneficio in ingratum collato proverbialiter dicunt אחיזי שקילא טיבותך ושריא i. e. ablata est benignit as tua, & proiecta in spinas. Legitur Schabbas f. 63. 2. Iohan. Calvinus in Instit. & ex eo Iohan. Georg. Grossius in Theatro Bibl. in Vind huius loci pag. 875. exclamant hîc, quòd Ubiquitarios (quo nomine Orthodoxos insignit Grossius) non iuvet haec Christi parabola ad stabiliendam manducationem oralem corporis Christi. Verùm sciendum, quòd nostrates minimè ex h. l. probent oralem corporis Christi manducationem respectu indignorum, ceu Grossius sibi persuadet: Sed quòd dentur ρόσκαιροι h. e. quòd fides amitti possit, & hoc ipsum etiam non tàm ex hoc versu, quàm ex v. 21. ac loco parallelo Luc. 8, 13. luculenter patet. quae Wendel. excipit, suo discutientur loco.)*

## 13:8
(v. 8. ὅ δὲ &c. Note that the repetition of the particle ὅ δὲ in this place indicates distribution, just as Erasmus also rightly translates another.)

( Into good ground. not φύσει, but χάριτι. See Eph. 2, 1. following 5. Gen. 6, 5.chap. 8, 21. )

*( A hundredfold. The Savior refers here to the fertility of the Holy Land. The history which is read in the Jerusalem Talmud contributes to this, where mention is made of a certain man who sowed one seah, which produced three hundred seahs. See Buxtorf, Talmudic Lexicon, under the word חךךל. Hugo Grotius notes that something similar, namely concerning the land producing a hundredfold fruit, was reported by Varro concerning the Sybarite field, in his book on agriculture, and likewise by Pliny concerning the Byzacian and Babylonian [lands].)*

Latin:

*(v. 8. ὅ δὲ &c. Nota quòd repetitio particulae ὅ δὲ h. l. distributionem in dicet, sicuti etiam Frasmus rectè vertit aliud.)*

(* In terram bonam. non φύσει, sed χάριτι. Vid. Eph. 2, 1. seqq. 5. Gen. 6, 5.cap. 8, 21. *)

*( Centena. Ad fertilitatem terrae sanctae respicit hic Salvator. Facit huc historia, quae in Talmud Hierosolymitano legitur, ubi commemoratur de quodam, qui sevit satum unum, quod fecit s. protulit Sata trecenta. Vid. Buxt. Lex. Talm. voce חךךל Hugo Grotius annotat, quòd simile quid, nempe de terrâ centuplum fructum proferente, â Varrone proditum de Sybaritano agro, in lib. de re rusticâ, item â Plinio de Byzacico & Babylonia.)*

## 13:9
*(v. 9. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. In what sense men are commanded to hear the word of GOD, when nevertheless they have no power of themselves to turn salutarily to God, has been said elsewhere. They are commanded, namely, to provide external discipline, and not maliciously to oppose the Holy Spirit, who desires to perfect His work in them. Nor does it follow from this, however, that they can turn themselves to God by natural powers. Whence also the Jesuit Corn. à Lapide rightly notes on the following verse, 11, that Christ indicates by those words: to you it is given, etc., that this capacity cannot be obtained by one's own powers, but must be suppliantly requested from GOD.)*

Latin:

*(v. 9. Qui habet aures ad audiendum audiat. Quo sensu homines audire iubeantur verbum. DEI, cùm tamen nonam pliùs habeant vires salutariter sese ad Deum convertendi, alibi dictum. Iubentur nempe externam disciplinam praestare, nec Sp. Sancto, suum opus in iis perficere cupienti, malitiosè sese opponere. neque tamen hinc sequitur, quòd possint sese naturalibus viribus ad Deum converere, Unde rectè quoque ad v. seq. 11. notat Iesuita Corn. â Lapide, Christum indicare illis verbis: vobis datum est &c. capacitatem hanc non posse obtineri propriis viribus, sed â DEO suppliciter postulandam.)*

## 13:11
*(v. 11. But to you it is given, etc. Theophylact on this passage explains that ὑμῖν to you as Μήποτε to those seeking to learn, for everyone who asks, receives. Euthymius: To you who rightly see and hear: but to them who see and hear deceitfully, and thus do not believe. *(For the Pharisees either did not wish to hear Christ teaching and proposing the mysteries of the kingdom in parables, or they interpreted his doctrine most wickedly: whence it is evident that they were not excluded by some absolute hatred or decree from having the mysteries of the kingdom manifested to them as well. But because they rejected the word of Christ. Compare Act. 13; 46. and pursued the Savior with a hatred more than Vatinian. Wendelin, Exercise 97, § 71, acknowledges that the Savior had just causes why he did not explain the parables to all and each of his hearers. But lest he overturn the absolute decree of reprobation, he soon denies that Christ offered the exegesis of figurative expressions to all. But it pleases one to ask of Wendelin and his associates, what is the cause and reason why the explanation was not handed down to all. Here, without ambiguity, the Calvinists will flee to the mere ἐυδοκίαν of GOD if they confess an absolute decree of reprobation. But the Savior indicates the true cause in other places in clear words.)* Matth. 23, 37. Add Ier. 7, 14.Prov. 1, 24.Luc. 7, 30.Actor. 7, 51.2. Corinth. 4, 3. 4. Whence Chrysostom well says, hom. 46. on Matthew, regarding those words: To you it is given, etc. This, he says, he said, not showing any necessity, nor an attribution of doctrine to some by chance and as it happens, rashly brought in: but that he might signify that the cause of all evils is in them themselves. And again: Unless he had wished them to be converted and to be saved, he would surely have been silent, nor would he have spoken anything in parables: but now, by this very thing, because the speech is obscured by darkness, he moves them to seek. For God does not wish the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live. And a little later: Nor can you object that these things were said to them obscurely: for they could have approached opportunely and asked, just as the disciples also did: But corrupted by torpor and negligence, they did not want to. Why did I say they did not want to? Nay, they were even studiously striving against him: for they not only did not believe, or did not listen, but they even attacked and persecuted the one preaching. And from this it is also clear that there is a distinction between natural repugnance or blindness, and affected malice, concerning which distinction elsewhere. Whence it is also easily clear what must be answered to the question proposed by Wendel, Exerc. 117. § 21. Why only some, and not all; and why these rather than those understood Christ preaching? Resp. The cause of the difference is not natural blindness, which is equal among all, 1. Corinth. 2, 14. but affected malice, by which some morosely resist the operation of the Holy Spirit. But someone might say, nevertheless it cannot be denied that among the Scribes and Pharisees and other despisers of Christ there were mixed in some pious and simple ones, to whom the exegesis of the parables should have been handed down entirely. Resp. Even if the exposition of the parables was not proposed to these at that very time, this was nevertheless done afterwards and at another time. Or if it was not done elsewhere, it is certain that they too were despisers, and thus by their own fault, well perceived by Christ καρδιογνώςῃ, they were deprived of that benefit. Furthermore, these things were not said to the Apostles alone, but also to others who remained with Christ. And, if there were any desirous of learning, they could approach Christ privately outside the crowd, and seek an explanation of those things which they could not sufficiently grasp by themselves, as H. Grotius rightly notes in this place. Conf. B. D.

Fewbr. Synt. 1. Sacr. Disquis. page 58. & 75. B. D. Frantz. de Interp. Sc. S. page 160. seqq. B. P. L. de Reprob. § 143.)*

Latin:

*(v. 11. Vobis autem datum est &c. Theophyl. in h. l. illud ὑμῖνvobis exponit Μήποτεquaerentibus discere, nam omnis, qui postulat, acoipit. Euthymius: Vobis recte videntibus & audientibus: illis verò doloiè videntibus & audientibus, & ita non credentibus. *(Pharisaei enim Christum docentem & in Parabolis mysteria regni proponentem audire vel nolebant. vel doctrinam eius pessimè traducebant: unde patet, quòd non absoluto quôdam odio vel decretô fuerint exclusi, quò minùs & ipsis mysteria regni manifestarentur. Sed quia verbum Christi reiiciebant. Conf. Act. 13; 46. ac odio plusquam Vatiniano Salvatorem prosequebantur. Wendelinus Exerc. 97. § 71. agnoscit, Salvatorē iustas habuisse causas, cur omnibus & singulis auditoribus suis parabolas haut explicarit. Verùm ne absolutum reprobationis decretum everrat, mox negat, Christum omnibus exegesin figuratarum locutionum obtulisse. Sed quarere placet ex Wendelino eiusque sociennis, quae causa sit ac ratio, cur explicatio non omnibus tradita. Hîc procul ambiguo Calvinisequi ad meram DEI ἐυδοκίαν si absolutum reprobationibus decretum confugient. ast veram causam alibisat claris verbis indicat Salvator Matth. 23, 37. Add Ier. 7, 14.Prov. 1, 24.Luc. 7, 30.Actor. 7, 51.2. Corinth. 4, 3. 4. Unde benè Chrysost. hom. 46. in Matth. ad illa verba: Vobis datum est &c. Hoc, inquit, dixit, non necessitatem quampiam ostendens nec tomerariam ad aliquos doctrinae attributionem â casu, & ut contingit, illatam: sed ut in ipsis omnium causam esse malorum, significaret. & iterum: Nisi voluisset, eos converti ac salvos esse, tacuisset profectò, neque in parabolis quicquam locutus esset: nunc vero hac ipsâre, quia tenebris obfuscatur oratio, ad quaerendum eos movet. Deus enim non vult mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur & vivat. & paulò post: Nec obiicere potes, obscurè illis haec dicta fuisse: potuissent enim opportunè accedere ac interrogare, sicut & discipuli fecerunt: Sed torpore atque negligentiâ corrupti noluerunt. Cur dixi noluerunt? imò etiā adversus eum studiosè nitebantur: nec enim non solùm non credebant, aut non audiebant, verùm etiam impugnabant & persequebantur praedicantem. Atque hinc etiam patet, quòd dist. sit inter repugnantiam sive caecitatem naturalem, & malitiam affectatam. de quâ dist. alibi. Unde etiam facilè patet, quid respondendum sit ad quaestionem, à Wendel. Exerc. 117. § 21. propositam. Cur aliqui tantùm, & non omnes; & curbi potius, quàm illi concionantem Christum intellexerint? Resp. Causa discriminis est non coecitas naturalis, quae apud omnes aequalis, 1. Corinth. 2, 14. sed malitia affectata, quâ Sp. S. operationis morosè aliqui resistunt. Sed dicat quis, nihilo tamen minùs negari haut posse, Scribis ac Pharisaeis aliisq; Christi conremtoribus immixtos fuisse aliquos pios ac simplices, quibus omninò parabolarum exegesis fuisset tradenda. Resp. Etsi his quammaximè isto statim tempore expositio parabolarum non fuit proposita, factum tamen hoc posteà ac alio tempore. Vel si non factum alibi, certum est, quòd illi quoque fuerint contemtores, adeòque propriâ culpa, Christo καρδιογνώςῃ probè perspectâ, isto beneficio privati. Praetereà nec ad solos Apostolos, sed alios etiam, qui apud Christum manserunt, haec fuerunt dicta. Et, si qui erant discendi cupidi, poterant extra turbam Christum privatim accedere, & explicationē petere eorum, quae per se nō satis ad se quebantur, uti rectè notat H. Grotius in h. l. C ōf. B. D.

Fewbr. Synt. 1. Sacr. Disquis. pag. 58. & 75. B. D. Frantz. de Interp. Sc. S. pag. 160. seqq. B. P. L. de Reprob. § 143.)*

## 13:12
v. 12. For whoever has, to him it shall be given.Syrac. 33, 2. He who seeks the word of GOD, shall find it abundantly, i. e. To those who hear the word of GOD more often and attentively, GOD will bestow progress and increases of faith: but those who think they have learned everything and disdain the word, just as many hearers were doing when departing from Christ, in them the persuasion of divine knowledge will vanish. *(Blessed D. Glassius also explains this in the same way in Gr. S. page 282.)* Chrysostom hom. 79. in Matth. He who uses the gifts of GOD studiously and diligently, will obtain greater grace. *(Ioh. Camero in Myroth. Evang. page 17 rightly warns that this is a proverbial expression, by which Christ wishes to signify this: That those who make much of the gifts of GOD are enriched with new gifts, but the contemners of offered grace are deprived of that light which shone upon them. But lest any absolute decree of detriment should be taken, he adds: But Christ in that place nevertheless does not say what some say, that it is not from us to abuse the gifts of GOD, perinde at-; it is from us that we abuse them etc. Resp. Although we willingly grant that GOD works in us both to will and to perform,Phil. 2, 13. and thus that our salutary conversion depends in no way on our own powers. See 2. Corinth. 3, 6. it is nevertheless certain that in pedagogical or external actions not only τὸ to abuse, but also τὸ not to abuse the gifts of GOD is from us, i. e. that a man can both maliciously resist the preached word, and in this manner also not resist. Distinguish, therefore, between gifts of nature, and of grace. τὸ not to resist maliciously pertains to the gifts of nature. Nor does it follow, however: a man by malicious resistance merits to be blinded, therefore conversely by non-malicious resistance and the hearing of the word he merits the increase of divine benefits and grace, which the Papists wish, See Felicianus Capito Narniensis Explic. Cathol. part. 2. page 525. seqq. Furthermore, the Blessed P. H. E. treat of the present passage at greater length on pages 874, 875, 1311, 1328. Blessed D. Frantzius de, Interp. Sc. S. page 260.)*

But whoever does not have, even that which he has, shall be taken from him. i. e. what he seems to have, as it is expounded Luc. 8, 18. *(so also Dn. D. Walth. H. B. and Gatakerus compare this in Cinno p. 40.)*

*( it shall be taken away from them. H. Grotius in this place It is not just that I should heap upon those people other things, as long as they disdainfully reject what was given long ago and is necessary for salvation. And to the despisers and therefore the reprobate, those things which were necessary for them for salvation were preached.)*

Latin:

v. 12. Quis quis enim habet, dabitur illi.Syrac. 33, 2.Qui quaerit verbum DEI, opulenter hoc nansciscetur, i. e. Qui verbum DEI saepiùs & attentè audiunt, illis DEUS progressus & incrementa fidei largietur: qui verò putant, se omnia didicisse ac verbum fastidiunt, sicut cum faciebant plerique auditores, à Christo discedentes, in illis persuasio divinae agnitionis evanescer. *(eodem prorsus modo explicat etiam B. D. Glassius Gr. S. pag. 282.)* Chrysostomus hom. 79. in Matth. Qui studiosè ac sedulo utitur DEI donis, maiorem gratiam impetrabit. *(Ioh. Camero Myroth. Evang. pag. 17. rectè monet, proverbialem hanc esse locutionem, quâ hoc velit Christus significare: Eos qui magni faciunt DEI dona, locupletari novis donis, contemtores autem oblatae gratiae privari illo lumine, quod illis affulsit. ne vero quid decretum absolutum detrimenti caperet, addit: At Christus eo loco tamen non dicit, quod dicunt nonnulli, non abuti DEI donis a nobis esse, perinde at-; à nobis est, quod iis abutimur &c. Resp. Licet libenter largiamur, DEUM operari in nobis & velle & persicere,Phil. 2, 13. adeoque minimè à nostris viribus dependere salutarem nostri conversionem. Vid. 2. Corinth. 3, 6. certum tamen est, quod in actionibus praedagogicis s. externis non solùm τὸabuti, sed etiam τὸnon-abuti DEI donis sit â nobis h. e. quòd possit homo verbo praedicato & malitiosê repugnare, & h. m. etiam non repugnare. Disting. igitur inter dona naturae, & gratiae.τὸnon repugnare malitiosè pertinet ad dona naturae. Neque tamen sequitur: homo per repugnantiā malitiosam meretur excoecariergo vice versa per non repugnantiam malitiosam ac verbi auditum beneficiorum divinorum ac gratiae augumentum meretur, quod Pontificii volunt, Vid. Felicianus Capito Narniensis Explic. Cathol. part. 2. pag. 525. seqq. Coeterum pluribus de praesentiloco agunt B. P. H. E. pag. 874. 875. 1311. 1328. B. D. Frantzius de, Interp. Sc. S. pag. 260.)*

Qui autem non habet, etiam illud quod habet, tolletur ab eo. i. e. quod videtur habere, ut exponitur Luc. 8, 18. *(ita etiam confert Dn. D. Walth. H. B. ac Gatakerus in Cinno p. 40.)*

*( auferetur ab iis. H. Grotius in h. l. Aequum non est, ut istis, quamdiu pridem data & ad salutem necessaria fastidiosè respuunt, alia ingeram. E. & contemtoribus adeoque reprobis ea quae ad salutem iis necessaria erant, fuerunt praedicata.)*

## 13:13
*(v. 13. Therefore by parables &c. Various causes can be recounted why Christ used parables so often. The blessed Par. Hom. Acad. in Expos. dom. Sexag. recalls them to four classes. Of which 1. the fulfillment of Scripture, Matth. 13, 34.Psal. 78, 2. 2. our instruction, Marc. 4, 33. add. 1. Corinth. 2. 1.cap. 3, 1.2. 3. the excitement of the hearers 4. the refutation of the despisers. Which is indicated in this place. For those others were despisers, who did not wish to see the clear truth, and therefore rejected it: but hearing this parabolic [truth], and either disdaining its clear meaning or not desiring to understand it, they sufficiently testify that the divine truth is not in their heart. As Simon Episcopius explains in this place, Instit. Theol. lib. 3. c. 14. p 181. Much more correctly than his Socinian-Calvinist [followers], who, lest they cast the blame of reprobation onto the malice of men, persuade [us] here that we should at least think that God is the lord of all creatures and therefore has the free power of ordaining concerning them i. e. of giving saving gifts only to some. See Piscator in this place.)*

Seeing they do not see. Chrysost. hom. 46. in Matth. ψωσι They were not only held by the crime of unbelief, but they also rebuked, accused, and laid snares. *(and this is the true cause of believing ἀδυναμίας,. Therefore, the canon must be observed here, which the blessed D. Glass. delivers, Gr. S. page 248, that words which denote an active signification are sometimes to be explained by I will with their own infinitive. So that by τὸ they do not understand in this place it may be signified they do not wish to understand. Just as Exod. 16, 23. what you will cook i. e. what you wish to cook. Similar examples are had Luc. 11, 52.Ioh. 15, 15.)*

Latin:

*(v. 13. Propterea per parabolas &c. Variae possunt recenseri causae, cur Christus toties parabolis usus fuerit. Revocar illas B. Par. Hom. Acad. in Expos. dom. Sexag. ad quatuor classes. quarum 1. Scripturae impletio, Matth. 13, 34.Psal. 78, 2.2. nostri informatio, Marc. 4, 33. add. 1. Corinth. 2. 1.cap. 3, 1.2. 3. auditorum excitatio 4. contemtorum redargutio. quae h. l. indicatur. Erant enim coeteri illi contemtores, qui claram veritaiem videre nolebant, adeoque respuebant: hanc verò parabolicam audientes, & sensum eius luculentum aut fastidientes aut intelligere non desiderantes satis testantur, sibi veritatem divinain cordi non esse. uti h. l. exponit Simon Episcopius Instit. Theol. lib. 3. c. 14. p 181. Rectius omninò, quàm eius ex socienni Calviniani, qui ne reprobationis culpam in hominū malitiam reiiciant, cogitandum saltem hîc suadent quòd Deus sit dominus omniū creaturarū ac proinde liberam habeat potestatem de illis statuendi h. e. dona salvifica dandi tantùm aliquibus. Vid Piscator in h. l.)*

Videntes non vident. Chrysost. hom. 46. in Matth. ψωσιNon tantùm incredulitatis crimine tenebantur, verùm etiam increpabant, accusabant insidiabantur. *(est que haec vera credendi ἀδυναμίας, causa. Observandus igitur hîc canon, quem tradit B. D. Glass. Gr. S. pag. 248. quòd verba, quae activam significationem not ant, aliquando per volo cūproprio infinitivo exponenda sint. ut ita per τὸnon intelligunt h. l. significetur non volunt intelligere. Sicuti Exod. 16, 23.quod coquetis i. e. quod vultis coquere. Similia exempla habentur Luc. 11, 52.Ioh. 15, 15.)*

## 13:14
*(v. 14. and the prophecy is fulfilled in them. The Jews did not despise Christ's sermons and were not blinded because the Prophets predicted that blindness: But because the Prophets foresaw the extreme malice of those Jews and that the blinding would follow it by the just judgment of GOD, therefore they predicted it. That which the primitive pillars of the Church teach no less beautifully than piously. Justin Martyr and Philosopher Qq. & Respons. ad Orthod. or whoever is the author of these, q. 58. page 330.)* μήποτ Id. Apol. 2. for the Christians p. 64. κῶς Similarly Athanasius in Pass. & Crucem domini, p. 788. where among other things: τοροσώπως i. e. not because they (the Prophets) say so, do the things that happen come to pass, but because that is to be in the future, it is therefore foretold by them: nor can it be that the Prophets lie, since they truly see. Compare what is noted at Ioh. 12, 39.)*

*( The Prophecy might be fulfilled. In how many ways Prophecy is fulfilled is said in Holy Scripture, the Blessed D. Chemn. shows in H E. c. 12.)*

With your ears you shall hear. In the Prophet they are Imperative words: Hear by hearing, and do not understand. See by seeing, and do not know. But here in Matthew the verb is placed in the future tense. By hearing you shall hear. Whence Drusius gathers, that the prophet uses the Imperative for the Future, for it is a prophecy concerning the blinding of the Jews. *(Conf. B. D. Glass. Gr. S. p. 623. B. Par. H. E. cap. 147. But it is well to be noted here, that it is treated here not of the antecedent will, but of the consequent or judicial will, vindicating the contempt of the preached word. The sense is, because they are totally immersed in incredulity and diabolical obstinacy, so much so that seeing the miracles, they do not see (namely with the eyes of the mind, so that they might receive me) thence it is evident, that in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled. Furthermore concerning the present Hebraism, Gataker can be consulted in de style N. T. p. 94. and 236.)*

Latin:

*(v. 14. ac completur in ipsis Prophetia. Non propterea Iudaei Christi conciones contemserunt adeoque excoecati fuerunt, quòd Prophetae illam excoecationem prodixerunt: Sed quia Prophetae praeviderunt summam Iudaeorum illorum malinam eamq; secutura iusto DEI iudicio excoecationem, ideò eam praedixerunt. Id quod pulcrè non minùs, quàm piè docent primitivae Ecclesiasticae Atlantes. Iustinus Martyr ac Philosophus Qq. & Respons. ad Orthod. vel quicunque harum autor, q. 58. pag. 330. μήποτ Id. Apol. 2. pro Christianis pag, 64. κῶς Similiter Athanasius in Pass. & Crucem domini, p. 788. ubi inter alia: τοροσώπως i. e. non ideò quod dicunt (Prophetae) ideò fiunt, quae fiunt sed quia id futurū, ideò ab illis praedicitur: nec fieri potest, ut Prophetae mentiantur, quum verè videant. Confer quae notat aad Ioh. 12, 39.)*

*( Compleretur Prophetia. Quot modis Prophetia implers dicatur in Sc. Sacrâ, ostendit B. D. Chemn. in H E. c. 12.)*

Auribus audietis. Apud Prophetam sunt verba Imperativa: Audite audiendo, & ne intelligite. Videte videndo, & ne cognoscite. Sed hîc apud Matthaeum ponitur verbum in tempore futuro. Auditu audietis. Unde colligit Drusius, prophetam usurpare Imperativum pro Futuro, est enim vaticinium de excoecatione Iudaeorum. *(Conf. B. D. Glass. Gr. S. pag. 623. B. Par. H. E. cap. 147. Probè verò hîc notandum, quòd agatur hîc non de voluntate antecedente, sed consequente sive iudiciariâ, verbi praedicati contemtum vindicante. Sensus est, quia in incredulitate & obstinatione diabolicâ toti immersi sunt, adeò ut videntes miracula, non videant (oculis sc. mentis, ut me recipiant) inde patet, quod in ipsis impleatur prophetia Esaiz. Porrò de Ebraismo praesenti consuli potest Gatakerus in de style N. T. pag. 94. ac 236.)*

## 13:15
v. 15. ἐπαχύνθη ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου. In the Prophet it is said: make fat their heart, but in this place their heart is made fat, because what the Prophet narrates, as commanded to him by the Lord, that by his preaching he would accidentally effect in that people, that Christ warns, has been fulfilled in his hearers through the preaching of the Gospel. It is more correctly said, that Christ followed the version of the LXX. interpreters. *(what is said here concerning the contemners of the divine word, that Their heart has been made fat, elsewhere, for instance Zach. 7., it is expressed thus, that they have made their heart as an adamant, Iob. 15. that they run against GOD with an outstretched neck. Such persons therefore deserve blindness, because they resist God not out of ignorance or infirmity, but out of malice. Who therefore would doubt that by a just judgment GOD withdraws His grace from such, as those who abuse the gifts of GOD so shamefully. But this matter will be treated more at length in the Analects on Rom. 9, 18.

Μήποτε ἐπιστρέψωσι If at any time they should be converted, and their sins be forgiven them. For that is the meaning the particle μήποτε obtains, just as in 2. Timoth. 2, 25. It is hinted, therefore, that by this means they can be converted, provided they hear in the proper manner, and do not so securely despise Christ teaching. (B. Luther, vol. 4, Jena Latin edition, fol. 338. This people has a hardened heart and closed eyes, whereby it happens that they cannot be converted. I would wish, says GOD, to heal, therefore I send the Son, but the hardening of the heart stands in the way of My will and their salvation.)

And I should heal them. In the prophet it is said in the third person, and he shall heal him, namely Jehovah, the people: But Christ here says in the first person: And I should heal them, so that He may show that He is the true God.

Latin:

v. 15. ἐπαχύνθη ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου. Apud Prophetam dicitur: pinguefac cor eorum, sed hoc loco pinguefactum est cor eorum, quia quod Propheta narrat, sibi â Domino praeceptum, ut praedicatione suâ in illo populo per accidens efficeret, id Christus monet, in auditoribus suis per praedicationem Evangelii esse impletum. Rectiùs dicitur, Christum secutum esse LXX. interpp. versionem. *(quod hîc dicitur de contemtoribus verbi divini, quòd incrassatum sit cor eorum, id alibi, puta Zach. 7. ita effertur, quòd cor suum firmaverint ut adamantem,Iob. 15. quòd currant contra DEUM extento collo. Merentur igitur tales excoecationem, quia non ex ignorantiâ vel infirmitare, sed ex malitiâ Deo resistunt. quis igitur dubitet, quin iusto iudicio DEUS talibus subtrahat suam gratiam, ut qui donis DEI adeò turpiter abutuntur. Sed de hâc re prolixiùs agetur in Analect. ad Rom. 9, 18.)*

Μήποτε ἐπιστρέψωσιSi quando convertantur, & dimittantur eis peccata. Id enim significatum particula μήποτε obtinet, perinde ut 2. Timoth. 2, 25. Innuitur ergo, hâc ratione posse illos converti, modò debitó modô audiant, nec adeò securè Christum docentem contemnant. *(B. Lutherus t. 4. Ienensi Lat. f. 338. Populus iste habet cor induratum & oculos clausos, quo fit, ut non possint converti. Vellem, inquit DEUS, sanare, ideò mitto Filium, sed meae voluntati & eorum saluti obstat induratio cordis.)*

Et sanem illos. Apud prophetam in tertia personâ dicitur, & sanet eum, nempe Iehova, populum: Sed Christus hîc in prima personâ dicit: Et sanem eos, ut ostendat, se esse verum Deum.

## 13:16
(v. 16. Blessed are your eyes &c. A fuller exposition of this verse and the following ones is held in the Analects on Luc. 10, 23. One may also consult the Academic Homilies of the Blessed Pareus, part 2, likewise the Exegesis of the Sunday Gospels of the Blessed D. Glassius, part 4, and other Doctors in the Explanation of the Gospel for the 13th Sunday after Trinity. The passage Ioh. 20, 29. does not stand in the way of this assertion. For Christ here compares bodily vision joined with spiritual vision with merely spiritual vision, and prefers the former to the latter. But Ioh. 20, 29. institutes a comparison between spiritual vision and merely bodily vision, and prefers the former to the latter, since this bodily vision, unless spiritual vision is added, is a cause of greater condemnation, Es. 6, 10. Ioh. 15, 22. However, even if we should easily grant that the bodily vision of Christ by no means made the Apostles blessed, unless spiritual vision had been added: there is nevertheless no necessity that we should treat this passage concerning the eyes and ears

of the mind, as we might assert with Hugo Grotius, but rather verse 17 seems to indicate sufficiently that here regard is had to the bodily vision of Christ, yet joined with the spiritual, not to the mental or spiritual alone. It pertains indeed to that. Because this was given to the Apostles, that they could always converse with Christ, by that occasion they were able to learn many secrets of the divine dispensation.)

Latin:

*(v. 16. Beati sunt vestri oculi &c. Plenior versiculi huius & seqq. expositio habetur in Anal. ad Luc. 10, 23. Evolvi quoque possunt B. Par. Hom. Acad. part. 2. it. B. D. Glassius Exeg. Ev. Dom. part. 4. aliique Dd. in Explic. Ev. Domin. 13. post Trinitatis. Non obstat huis adserto locus Ioh. 20, 29. Confert enim hîc Christus visionem corporalem cum spirituali coniunctam cum visione merè spirituali, & huic illam praefert. Sed Ioh. 20, 29. instituit collationen inter visionem spiritualem, ac merè corporalem, illamque huic profert, cùm haec corporalis, nisi spiritualis accedat, maioris condemnationis causa sit, Es. 6, 10.Ioh. 15, 22. Ut ut porrò facilè largiamur, corporalem Christi visionem minimè Apostolos fecisse beatos, nisi accessisset spiritualis: nulla tamen adest necessitas, ut hunc locum de oculis auribus.

que mentis agere, cum Hugone Grotio adseramus, quin potius v. 17. satis indicare videtur, quòd hîc ad corporalem, eum spirituali tamen coniunctam, Christi visionem respectus habeatur, non ad solam mentalem s. spiritualem. Partinet verò ad illam. quod quia datum Apostolis fuit, ut semper conversari cum Christo possent, istâ occasione multa arcana divinae dispensationis discere potuerint.)*

## 13:17
v. 17. they desired to see, namely, the fulfillment of the promises of GOD concerning the Messiah and the liberation of the human race, as Toussain explains. *(That there was a desire of the pious in the O. T. is evident from Gen. 4, 1.c. 5, 29.John 8, 56.Gen. 49, 18.Ps. 14, 7.Isa. 64, 1.1 Pet. 1, 10. 11. Let us imitate their piety and let us sigh for the coming of Christ, Matt. 24, 30.Rev. 22, 17.20. certain that we ourselves shall then see our Savior face to face 1 Cor. 13, 12.)*

*( And did not see. The assertion of Christ John 8, 56. seems to stand in the way. But distinguish between a merely spiritual vision, and a spiritual vision joined with a bodily one. The pious in the O. T. saw Christ τυπικῶς, in types and predictions, the Apostles ἀυτοροσώπως κὶ ἐυτοφώνως in most sweet conversations and sermons. The former saw Christ in a riddle, the Apostles face to face. Felicianus Capito in Expl. Cath. part 2, page 529, presents other reconciliations of some, partly erroneous, partly ridiculous. But from the fact that the pious in the O. T. did not see what the Apostles saw, namely the Son of GOD, in the assumed or personally united human nature to himself, preaching and manifesting his glory by truly divine miracles, the Anabaptists ineptly conclude, as can be seen in the Colloq. Franckenth. page 318, that the pious in the O. T. did not actually, but only by hope, obtain eternal salvation . against John 5, 12Acts 15, 9.Rom. 4, 2. It is one thing to enjoy the visible θεανθρώπου conversation of Christ; it is another to have actual possession of eternal salvation. Not the latter, but the former, according to the present saying, was denied to the pious in the O. T.)*

Latin:

v. 17. desiderarunt videre, sc. impletionem promissionum DEI de Messia & liberationem generis humani, uti explicat Tossanus. *(De desiderio piorum in V. T. constat ex Gen. 4, 1.c. 5, 29.Ioh. 8, 56.Gen. 49, 18.Psal. 14, 7.Esai. 64, 1.1. Petr. 1, 10. 11. Imitemur nos illorum pietatem ac suspiremus ad Christi adventum, Matth. 24, 30.Apoc. 22, 17.20. certi, quòd & ipsi tunc visun simus Salvatorem nostrum â facie ad faciem 1. Cor. 13, 12.)*

*( Et nō viderunt. Videtur obstare adsertio Christi Ioh. 8, 56. Verùm dist. inter visionem merè spiritualem, ac visionem spiritualem cum corporali coniunctam. Pii in V. T. viderunt Christū τυπικῶς, in typis & praedictionibus, Apostoli ἀυτοροσώπως κὶ ἐυτοφώνως in dulcissimis alloquiis & concionibus. Illi viderunt Christum in aenigmate, Apostoli à facie. Alias partim erroneas, ridiculas partim nonnullorum conciliationes exhibet Felicianus Capito in Expl. Cath. part. 2. pag. 529. Ex eo verò, quòd pii in V. T. non viderunt, quae Apostoli viderunt, nempe Filium DEI, in adsumtâ sibi-ue personaliter unitâ humanâ naturâ concionantem ac miraculis verè divinis suam gloriam manifestantem, ineptcolligunt Anabapt. ceu in Colloq. Franckenth. pag. 318. videre est, quòd pii in V. T. non actu, sed spe tantùm aeternam salutem si-consecuti. contra Iohan. 5, 12Actor. 15, 9.Rom. 4, 2. Aliud est, frui visibili Christi θεανθρώπου conversatione; aliud actuali salutis aeternae possessione. Non haec, sed illa iuxta praesens dictum piis in V. T. fuit denegata.)*

## 13:19
v. 19. Καὶ μὴ συνιέντος. Συνιέναι. otherwise signifies to understand, here it is rightly translated, to attend. The emphasis of the Greek verb is to send together, when, namely, he who hears sends his mind together with the speech which he hears, so that they may proceed as if with an equal pace. But then the mind is sent together with the speech, when he understands it, or at least attends to it. Hence the phrase of the Latins: I do not follow what you mean.

*( He who received the seed by the wayside. Christ speaks of those who hear with their ears, but do not apply their heart, for they are concerned with other things, so that the heart lies open to all thoughts like a public road.)*

Latin:

v. 19. Καὶ μὴ συνιέντος. Συνιέναι. aliàs significat intelligere, hîc rectè vertitur, attendere. Emphasis Graeci verbi est simumittere, cùm sc. is, qui audit, mentem suam simul mittit cum sermone, quem audit, ut pari quasi passu incedant. Tum autem cum sermone simul mittitur mens, cùm eum intelligit, aut saltem tem ad eum attendit. Inde phrasis Latinorum: non adsequor quid velis.

*( Qui iuxta viam semen excepit. Loquitur Christus de iis, qui audiunt auribus, sed cor non apponunt, curantes quippe alia, ita ut cor pateat omnibus cogitationibus tanquam publica via.)*

## 13:20
v. 20. He receives the word with joy. Tossanus thinks that this joy προσκαίρων is merely earthly and worldly joy, when, for instance, someone conceives a hope of earthly advantages and honors to be acquired through the confession of the Gospel, or when he listens out of a desire for novelty, Acts 17, 21. But it is gathered from Heb. 6, v. 4. that they are also participants in spiritual joy προσκαίρους.

Latin:

v. 20. Cum gaudio accipit verbum. Tossanus existimat, gaudium hocπροσκαίρωνesse duntaxat terrenum & mandanum gaudium, quando scil. quis spem concipit terrenorum commodorum, ac honorum, per Evangelii confessionem acquirendorum, vel quando ex studio novitatis audit, Actor. 17, 21. Sed ex Ebr. 6. v. 4. colligitur, etiam spiritualis gaudii participes esse προσκαίρους.

## 13:21
v. 21. They have no root. Tossanus: he is not rooted and founded by faith in Christ, through whom Christ dwells in our hearts, Eph. 3, 17. *(But it does not follow that πρόσκαιροι they are not rooted by faith, therefore they never had true and saving faith. Therefore, that phrase indicates the instability and amissibility of justifying faith in προσκαίροις, but by no means its nullity, as is evident from the parallel passage Luke 8, 13. to which see the Analysis, where the exception of Wendelin will also be answered, and Conf. Giesens. t. 7. Disp. 14.)*

He is temporary. πρόσκαιρος is he who either accommodates himself to the time, or lasts only for a certain time; he is a plant of a certain time, as that solstice plant in Plautus's Pseudolus.

Latin:

v. 21. Non habent radicem. Tossanus: non est radicatus & & fundatus fide in Christo, per quam Christus habi-t in cordibus nostris, Eph. 3, 17. *(Non verò sequitur πρόσκαιροι non sunt radicati fide, ergò nunquam habuerunt fidem veram & salvificam. Indicatur igitur phrasi illâ fidei iustificantis in προσκαίροιςinstab litas & amissibilitas, hautquaquam verò nullitas, ceu patet ex loco parall. Luc. 8, 13. ad quem Vid. Anal. ubi etiam ad except. Wendel. repondebitur, ac Conf. Giesens. t. 7. Disp. 14.)*

Temporalis est.πρόσκαιρος est, qui vel tempori se accommodat, vel ad quoddam tempus solummodo durat, certi quasi temporis herba est. sicut illa solstitialis in Pseu dolo Plautinâ.

## 13:22
v. 22. Ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου, an abduction from the way or deceitfulness of riches. For ἀπάτη is derived from α, which privates, and πάτος.. It can also be translated deceptive or deceitful riches, by hypallage, as if it were ὁ πλοῦτος τῆς ἀπάτης, in the Hebrew phrase. *(Riches are called deceitful, because they are uncertain and unstable. Hence the Apostle also seriously exhorts 1 Tim. 6, 17. that if riches abound, we should not trust in the uncertainty of riches. Since indeed it can truly be said of them, what is said of dreams Sirach 34, 2. Furthermore, just as in this place and its parallels Mark 4. Luke 8. three things are recounted which hinder men from the word of God bearing fruit in their hearts, so also elsewhere, namely Luke 14., the Savior brings forward almost the same impediments, add also 1 John 2, 16. and compare the Expositions of the Gospel for Sexagesima Sunday and likewise for Trinity Sunday especially also B. D. Feuerbornius, Disquis. Sacr. Synt. 2. Disp. 10. § 22 & seqq)*

Latin:

v. 22. Ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου, extra viam abductio sive deceptio divitiarum.ἀπάτη enim dicta ex α privante & πάτος. Potest etiam verti, fallaces seu deceptrices divitiae. per hypallagen, quasi sit ὁ πλοῦτος τῆς ἀπάτης, phrasi Ebraicâ. *(Dicuntur divitiae fallaces, quia incertae sunt & instabiles. Inde Apostolus quoque seriò hortatur 1. Tim. 6, 27. ne si divitiae affluant, speremus in incerto divitiarum. Siquidem verè de illis potest dici, quod de insomniis Sirac. 34, 2. Coeterùm quomodo h. l. eiusque parall. Marc. 4.Lucae 8. tria recensentur, quae homines impediunt, quò minus verbum DEI in ipsorum cordibus fructum ferat, ita quoque alibi, nempe Luc. 14. ferè eadem impedimenta Salv. adducit, add. etiam 1. Ioh. 2, 16. ac confer. Expositores Ev. Dom. Sexagesimae item que Dom. posse Trinit cumprimis etiam B. D. Fewrbornius disquis Sacr. Synt. 2. Disp. 10. § 22 & seqq)*

## 13:23
(v. 23. But he who received the seed into the good ground, etc. We learn from this that the word must be retained by faith of the heart, lest the devil snatch it away; it must be guarded by confession of the mouth, lest it fail in the time of temptation; it must be fulfilled by execution of the work, lest either the anxiety of sustenance, or the love of riches, or the pleasure of life suffocate and oppress it. See Luke 11, 28Rom. 2, 13.James 2, 22.Deut. 6, 6. following Prov. 6, 6.21. Conf. B: Par. Harm. Evang. chap. 177 p. 1409.)

( And understands. If a faithful, that is, a right hearer of the word ought to understand what is heard, it follows that justifying faith is by no means more rightly defined by ignorance than by knowledge, as Bellarmine wishes in book 1 of De Iustif, chap. 7. Which error B. Par. refutes at length in L. de Iustif § 67, 68, also Confess. Cath art 23, l. 1.)

Produces a hundredfold. Jerome refers the hundredfold yield to virgins, the sixtyfold to widows, the thirtyfold to married persons. Others attribute the first yield to martyrdom, the second to virgins, the third to continent widows, and none to marriage holding the place. Augustine in Qq Evang question 9 attributes the first to martyrs, the second to widows, the third to the married. More rightly and simply it is understood thus, that Christ, for the sake of teaching, placed a hundredfold for the highest, thirtyfold for the lowest, sixtyfold for the mediocre, just as He did with the ten, five, and one talents. *(The Papists, as Bellarm. t. 2. lib. 2. de Monach. chap. 9, try to prove their doctrine concerning Evangelical counsels from this passage. But we reply: 1. Symbolic theology is not argumentative, as the Jesuit Lud. ab Alcasar admits in chap. 7 of the Apocalypse; add Bell. lib. 3. de V D. chap. 3. § But although. 2. The sentence of Christ is general, dealing with all hearers of the word, whence the Jesuit Maldonatus explains it concerning the spiritual fruits of the Gospel, which are otherwise explained in Scripture, namely that by the thirtyfold is understood the least, by the sixtyfold the mediocre, by the hundredfold the greatest. Which exposition does not displease even Corn. à Lapide in this place, who explicitly adds that Christ intends here precisely this much according to the letter. It is indicated, therefore, that the preaching of the word does not produce the same fruit in all hearers. 3. It cannot be denied that the Patriarchs living in marriage brought forth a richer fruit than many virgins, even those living most chastely, not to mention those who live in celibacy under compulsion and are subsequently tormented by the flames of lust, or for whom forced celibacy is more difficult than honest marriage, as is the case for most Monks and Jesuits. 4. Nor, however, do all or even most of the Fathers explain it in this way. But perhaps at least Jerome, the hater of marriage, and he who followed him, Anselm, whose calculations, however, one could hardly read here without laughter. Augustine is usually added, but he himself determines nothing certain, as B. Par. showed long ago in L. de Evang. § 95. Furthermore, Gregory the Great, whose authority as P. R. ought to be sacrosanct to the Jesuits, hom. -7. in Ezech. explains it otherwise. Nor does Isidore of Pelusium in lib. 2. ep 144 acquiesce in that Hieronymian exposition. I add that Theophylact and likewise Euthymius also take this passage concerning the fruit of the divine word in general, and give the thirtyfold) to those beginning, the sixtieth to those making progress, the hundredth to those perfect, from which exposition Nazianzen departs most closely; as the Jesuit Cornel. à Lapide himself reports. Whence it is clear; that the Papists can by no means urge the exposition of the Fathers here for Evangelical Counsels, since they are split into diverse parts.)*

*( He who received the seed, this is he who hears the word &c. From the fact that the preached word, which today is comprised in the Sacred writings, is compared with the fructifying seed, it is easy to gather, that Sacred Scripture is not a dead letter, as Suencfeldius, Weigelius and the Jesuits trifle, as the Blessed Par. shows from their writings L. de Minist. Eccl. §. 52. item dispp. Acad page 82. Let the following sayings be noted furthermore against the horrendous error of those men Deut. 32, 47.Esa 38 16.cap. 55, 10.Iohan. 5, 39.cap. 6, 63.68.cap. 8, 3.51.cap. 17, 20.Ebr. 4, 12.Rom 1. 16.c. 10, 17 But that which the Prophets & Apostles first preached, afterwards by the will of God they handed down to us in the Scriptures, according to Irenaeus lib. 3. cap. 1. page 169 Add. 1. Petr. 1, 25.Ioh. 1 v. 1.)*

Latin:

*(v. 23. Qui verò interram bonam excepit semen &c. Discimus hinc, quòd verbum fide cordis retinendum, ne diabolus cripiat; confessione oris custodiendum, ne tempore tentationis deficiat 3. executione operis implendum, ne vel victûs solicitudo, vel divitiarum amor, vel vitae voluptas suffocet & opprimat. Vid. Luc. 11, 28Rom. 2. 13.Iac. 2, 22.Deut. 6, 6. seqq. Prov. 6, 6.21. Conf. B: Par. Harm. Evang. cap. 177 p. 1409.)*

*( Et intelligit. Si fidelis s. rectus verbi auditor debet intelligere audita, sequitur, quòd fides iustificans hautquaquam rectiùs per ignorantiam, quàm pro notitiam definiatur, uti Bellarminus vult lib. 1. de Iustif cap. 7. Quemerrorem prolixè refutat B. Par L de Iustif § 67. 68. it. Confess. Cath art 23. l. 1.)*

Facit centuplum. Hieronymus centuplum proventum refert ad virgines, sexageplum ad viduas, trigecuplū ad coni-gatos Alii primum proventum trib-ūMartyrio, secundum virginibus, tertium viduis continentibus, coniugio nullum te-nquentes locum August. in Qq Evang quaest. 9. primas tribuit martyribus, secundas viduis, tertias coniugatis. Rectiùs ac simpliciù sic a-ipitur, quò Christus dotendi gratiâ posuerit centuplum pro summo, trigecuplum pro infimo, sexagecuplum pro mediocri, quemadmodum fecit in talentis decem, quinque & uno. *(Pontificii, uti Bellat. t. 2. lib. 2. de Monach. cap. 9. ex h. l. doctrinam suam de consiliis Evangelicis probare conantur. Verùm resp. 1. Theologia symbolica non est argumentativa, fatente Iesuiti Lud. ab Alcasar in cap. 7. Apoc. add. Bell. lib. 3. de V D. cap. 3. § Sed quanquam. 2. Sententia Christi est generalis, agens de omni bus verbi auditoribus, unde Iesuita Maldonatus explicat de fru-tibus Evangelii spiritualibus, qui aliàs in Scr. exponuntur. nem pe quòd per trigesimum intelligatur minimus, per sexagesimum midocris, per centesunum maximus. Quae expositio nec Corn. à Lapide in h l. displicet, qui disertè addit, quòd hoc duntaxat praecisè ad litteram intendat hîc Christus. Indicatur igitur quòd praedicatio verbi non eundèm apud omnes auditores fructum proferat. 3. negari non potest, quòd Patriarchae in coniugio viventes uberiorem fructum attulerint, quàm multae virg nes, etiam castissimè viventes, nedum illi, qui in coelibatu vivunt coacti, ac subinde ustionum flammis excruciantur, vel quibus imp-rus coelibatus prae honesto coniugio artidet, ceu Monachis ac Iesuitis plerisque. 4. Nec tamen omnes vel etiā plerique Patres d. m. exponunt. Sed fortè saltem Hieronymus, Coniugii osor, & qui eundem sequutus. Anselmus Cuius tamen calculationes vix absque risu aliquis hîc legat. Addi solet Augustinus, sed nihil certi ipse determinat, uti pridem ostendit B. Par. L. de Evang. §. 95. Coeterùm Gregorius M. cuius ut P. R autoritas sacrosancta esse Iesuitis debebat, hom. -7. in Ezech. aliter exponit. nec in expositione illa Hieronymiana Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 2. ep 144. acqiescit. Addo, quod Theophylactus itemque Euthymius itidem de fructu verbi divini in genere locum hunc accipiant, actrigesimum dent incipientibus, sexagesimum profi--entibus, centesimum perfectis, à quâ expositione proximè abit Nazianzenus; ipso referente Iesuita Cornel. à Lapide. Unde liquet; quòd minimè Patrum expositionem urgere hîc Pontificii pro Evangelicis Consiliis possint, cùm in diversas scindantur illi partes.)*

*( Qui excepit semen, hic est quo verbum audit &c. Ex eo quod verbum praedicatum, quod hodie Sacris literis comprehenditur, confertur cum semine fructificante, pronum est colligere, quòd Scriptura Sacra non sit litera mortua, prout Suencfeldius, Weigelius ac Iesuitae nugantur, ceu ex illorum scriptis ostendit B. Par. L. de Minist. Eccl. §. 52. item dispp. Acad pag 82. Notentur praetereà contra horrendum istorum errorem seqq. dicta Deut. 32, 47.Esa 38 16.cap. 55, 10.Iohan. 5, 39.cap. 6, 63.68.cap. 8, 3.51.cap. 17, 20.Ebr. 4, 12.Rom 1. 16.c. 10, 17 Quod verò Prophetae & Apostoli primùm praeconiaverunt, posteà per Dei voluntatem in Scripturis nobis tradiderunt, iuxta Itenaeum lib. 3. cap. 1. pag 169 Add. 1. Petr. 1, 25.Ioh. 1 v. 1.)*

## 13:24
v. 24. Παρέηκεν he set before, he added another parable.

Tossanus says, that by seed here is not understood the word, as in the prior parable, But the children of the kingdom: by tares likewise is not understood false doctrine, which is not to be tolerated in the church, Gal. 2. 5.

cap. 5, 9. but the children of iniquity,v. 38. But altogether by field, is understood the Church, as the scope of the parable shows, which is, to show the face of the Church militant in these lands. Christ calls the field the world by synecdoche 1. because the Church is gathered in the world. 2. respect is had to the prophecies concerning the nations, about to come into the inheritance of Christ. 3. because Christ was about to lead his plow through all the regions of the world.

(The same explanation, namely that by seed the word of GOD is understood, and by field the militant Church, is also handed down by B. Par. L. de Eccl. § 134. Furthermore, since in verse 38 seed is explained by the Savior Himself as the children of the kingdom, it is to be noted that the word seed is accepted in two ways by Matthew in this chapter: 1. as it is sown, and thus by the name of seed the word of GOD is understood; 2. as it bears fruit and regenerates the hearts of men, and in this way the children of the Kingdom themselves, i.e., believers, come under the appellation of seed by a Metonymy, namely of the cause for the caused, i.e., the effect. Compare more in Mr. D. Waltherus H Bibl. page 770.)

Latin:

v. 24. Παρέηκενapposuit, adiecit aliam parabolam.

Tossanus vul, per semen hîc nō intelligi verbum, ut in priori parabola, Sed filios regni: per zizania itidem non intelligi falsam doctrinam, quae non est n cclesia toleranda, Gal. 2. 5.

cap. 5, 9. sed filios iniquitatis,v. 38. Verùm omninò per agrum. intelligitur Ecclesia, ut ostendit scopus parabolae, qui est, ostendere faciem Ecclesiae in his terris militantis. Christus agrum vocat mundum per synecdochen 1. quia Ecclesia in mundo colligitur. 2. respectus habetur ad vaticinia de gentibus, in Christi haereditatem venturis. 3. quia Christus aratrum suum ducturus erat per omnes mundi plagas.

*(Eandem explicationem, quòd nempe per semen intelligatur verbum DEI, per agrum vero Ecclesia militans, tradit quoque B. Par. L. de Eccl. § 134. Coeterùm cùm versu 38. semen de filiis regni ab ipso Salvatore exponatur, notandum, quòd seminis vox dupliciter accipiatur à Matth. hoc capite 1. prout spargitur, & sic nomine seminis intelligitur verbum DEI, 2. prout fructificat & corda hominum regenerat, & hoc modô ipsi etiam filii Regni s. credentes, per Metonymiam sc. causae pro causato s. effectu, seminis adpellatione veniunt. Conf. pluribus Dn. D. Waltherus H Bibl. pag. 770.)*

## 13:25
(v. 25. He sowed tares. From the fact that tares are read to have been sown after the good seed, the Papists gather that antiquity is a mark of the Church. Resp. 1. We concede that the true Church is prior to the false, and thus that antiquity is a mark of the Church, but joined with the truth of doctrine. 2. It is to be noted that the scope of Christ here is not to treat of the antiquity of the Church, but to show that in the visible Church the evil are always mixed with the good. Compare more on this matter in B. P. L. de Eccl. § 164. But it does not follow: in the visible and external assembly of the Church there are also hypocrites and sinners, therefore true faith, i.e., saving faith, can be in sinners separated from good works, as the Papists attempt to evince from this passage. See the Jesuit Coster. in Enchir. page 172. But B. Par. disputes at length against that error in Confes. Cathol. art. 23. c. 3. § 3.)

ζιζάνιον as if ὅπως, or as if σιτοσίνιον. from σῖτος and σίνω I harm, because it harms the crops. Suidas ζιζάνιον ἡ ὐν τᾡ σίτῳ αἶρα tares of the grain, corruption of the grain, grain-like seed, arising from the corruption of grain. But by tares here are not understood indiscriminately all criminals. 1. What is the reason for the seed, that is also of the tares. But by Seed is understood as the word of God, and those who propose it. Therefore, by tares are understood heresies, and those who propose them. 2. Otherwise it would follow that the Magistrate ought not to remove wicked men. 3. The nature of the tare proves this. For before it reaches maturity, it is similar to wheat; thus heretics imitate sincere Doctors. (To this point contributes the fact that tares here, according to some *(See Buxt. Lex. Talm. under the word זונין)*, does not signify vetch and darnel, but that species of wheat which we call Brandweigen, scorched, which can scarcely be separated from wheat and scarcely be pulled up without the wheat being pulled up. Etymology: ζιζάνιον is πρόσκαιρος and Παρέηκ I harm, σάτ. Therefore it exhibits to us a beautiful picture of hypocrites) 4. -dem teach Chrysostom homily 47 on chapter 13 of Matthew, Cyprian book 3, epistle 3, Jerome on Matthew, citing Jansenius, Lyra, Stapleton, Becanus on keeping faith with heretics, folio 103. By servants, Minus Celsus understands the Angels. But these servants are ignorant of the enemy's deed, which cannot be said of the Angels. Bellarmine and the Calvinists understand them only as those ministers whom God has appointed over His family. But Christ speaks in general of servants, i.e., the pious. *(Since, therefore, by tares are not understood in general wicked men, but specifically heretics, as such, i.e., those who are entangled in simple heresy or error in religion, and neither join blasphemies, nor stir up sedition, nor are infamous for other crimes, it is clear that the Anabaptists very ineptly strive to prove from the present passage that the Magistrate ought not to eradicate criminals, or punish them with the sword. For besides the fact that parabolic Theology is not argumentative, the words of Paul Rom. 13. 4. cry out against this opinion of the Anabaptists, by which he teaches clearly enough that it pertains to the office of the Magistrate to take action against criminals even with capital punishment: which is also clear from other utterances of Holy Scripture. See Matth. 26, 52.Gen. 9, 6. etc. Reasons also proving the same are exhibited by B. Par L de Mag Pol. §. 302. Let there also be compared entirely B. D. Konig Casuum Catech. page 673. seqq. Furthermore, because the servants are commanded here, as the tares, (by which heretics are understood, as shown above, and which Corn. à Lapide also willingly grants in this place, as do Chrysostom, Euthymius, and likewise Augustine in book Quaest. in Matth. 9, 11. being explained, they allow them to grow until the time of the harvest; from this the Orthodox conclude that heretics as such are not to be killed. Corn. à Lapide objects in this place, that Christ does not here absolutely forbid that these tares be rooted out, but that no one should attempt to root out everything entirely, nor at that time when they cannot be distinguished from the wheat, or when there is danger that the wheat might be rooted out along with them. I reply: Christ expressly mentions, v. 30. that the Lord commanded the servants to allow the tares to grow until the time of the harvest: but since that is the consummation of the age, v. 39. it is manifest that the Lord by no means wills that they be extirpated sooner. The householder does not say that the servants ought not to extirpate all the tares, or that some are to be rooted out, or that one must serve the time here: but he warns that the extirpation is simply to be left to the reapers. As concerns the authority of the Fathers, Cornelius himself knows that we have an almost unanimous consensus of the Fathers; he objects, however, that Augustine retracts his opinion in book 3 against the Epistle of Parmenianus, chapter 2. But it must be noted that not even in this place does Augustine urge the killing of heretics, but only their coercion. But Cornelius insists further, that a manifest heretic, especially if he infects others with his heresy, harms the faithful and the Church more gravely than a murderer; since the latter kills the body, the former the soul, 1. Cor. 5. 13. Gal. 5. 12. where the Apostle commands false teachers to be extirpated. I reply: The sayings 1. Cor. 5. and Gal. 5. will be treated in their own place. As regards the argument, that heretics are worse than murderers, since they kill the soul, we admit that heretics are spiritual murderers, therefore they are also to be killed with the spiritual sword, that is, they are to be anathematized, but they are not to be removed from the midst by corporal punishments. But the masters Geiss. t. 3. Disp. p. 535, the masters of Theology S-x in Fundam. Des. pupillae p. 94. following, B. Par. L. de Mag. Pol. §. 318. following, Confess. Cathol. t. 1. pag. 827. B. D. Bald. in a special dissertation on the coercing of heretics, Witteb. Ann. 160 printed, B. D. König Vind. Sacr. L 65, where he also shows that Cyprian, whose authority the Papists especially object to us, is by no means opposed to our opinion, discuss the controversy here at greater length. B. D. Quistorp brings forward an excellent passage of Salvian, book on the Governance of GOD, page 163, which is relevant here.

Annotations on this place. Lactantius, book 5 of the Divine Institutes, beautifully [says]. cap. 10.Religion is to be defended not by killing, but by advising; not by cruelty, but by patience; not by wickedness, but by faith. Conf. Aug. lib. 2. contra litt. Petil. cap. 24. & elsewhere.)*

Latin:

*(v. 25. Seminavit zizania. Ex eô quòd zizania post semen bonum leguntur seminata, colligunt Pontificii, antiquitatem esse notam Ecclesiae. Resp. 1. Concedimus, quòd vera Ecclesia prior sit falsâ, adeòque antiquitatem esse notam Ecclesiae, sed cum veritate doctrinae coniunctam. 2. notandum, quòd scopus Christi hîc nō sit, agere de Ecclesiae antiquitate, sed ostēdere, quòd in Ecclesiâ visibili semper mali sint mixti bonis. Conf. plura in hanc rem apud B. P. L. de Eccl. §. 164. Non vero sequitur: in visibili & extetno Ecclesiae coetu sunt quoq; hypocritae ac peccatores, E. fides vera h. e. salvifica potest esse in peccatoribus s à bonis operibus separata, prout Pontificii ex hoc loco evincere conantur. Vid. Iesuita Coster. in Enchir. pag. 172. Prolixè verò contra illum errorem disputat B. Par. Confes. Cathol. art. 23. c. 3. §. 3.)*

ζιζάνιον quasi ὅπως, vel quasi σιτοσίνιον. à σῖτος & σίνω noceo, quòd noceat frugibus. Suidas ζιζάνιον ἡ ὐν τᾡ σίτῳ αἶραlolium frumenti, corruptio frumenti, semen frumentaceum, ex frumenti corruptione proveniens. Intelliguntur vero hîc per zizania non promiscuè omnes facinorosi. 1. Quae est ratio seminis, ea etiam zizaniorum. At per semen intelligitur verbum Dei, & qui illud proponunt. E. per zizania haereses, & qui illas proponunt. 2. aliàs sequeretur, Magistratus non debere homines sceleratos tollere. 3. Natura zizanii hoc probat. illud enim antequam ad maturitatem perveniat, tritico est simile, sic haeretici imitantur sinceros Doctores. (Quo facit, quòd zizania hîc iuxta quosdam *(Vid. Buxt. Lex. Talm. voce זונין)* non significat viciam & lolium, sed illam speciem tritici, quam vocamus Brandweigen adustam, qui à tritico vix potest secerni ac vix evelli, quin triticum evellatur. Etymologicum: ζιζάνιον est πρόσκαιρος & Παρέηκ noceo, σάτ. Pulcram ergò picturam hypocritarum nobis exhibet) 4. -dem docent Chrysostomus homil. 47. in cap. 13. Matth. Cyprianus lib. 3. ep. 3. Hieronymus in Matth. citante Iansenio, Lyra, Stapletonus, Becanus de fide haereticis servandâ fol. 103. Per servos Minus Celsus intelligit Angelos. At hi servi ignorant inimici factum, quod de Angelis dici nequit. Bellarminus & Calviniani intelligunt eos tantùm ministros, quos Deus constituit super samiliam suam. Sed Christus loquitur in genere de servis i. e. piis. *(Cùm igitur per zizania non intelligantur in genere homines scelerati, sed in specie haeretici, ut tales h. e. qui simplici haeresi s. errori in religione impliciti, neq; blasphemias iungunt, nec seditionē movēt, aut aliis sceleribus sunt infames, patet, quòd ineptè admodùm è praesenti loco Anabaptistae evincere satagant, non debere Magistratum facinorosos eradicare, sive gladiô punire. Praeterquam enim quòd Theologia parabolica non sit argumentativa, reclamant isti Anabaptistarum sententiae verba Pauli Rom. 13. 4. quibus satis clarè docet, pertinere ad officium Magistratus, ut capitali etiam supplicio in facinorosos animadvertat: quod etiam patet ex aliis Sc. S. effatis. Vid. Matth. 26, 52.Gen. 9, 6. &c. Rationes etiam idem evincentes exhibet B. Par L de Mag Pol. §. 302. Conferatur quoque omninò B. D. Konig Casuum Catech. pag. 673. seqq. Porrò quia iubentur hîc servi, ut zizania, (per quae haereticos intelligi, suprà ostensum, ac lubens quoque largitur Corn. à Lapide in h. l. ita à Chrysostomo, Euthymio item que Augustino lib. Quaest. in Matth. 9, 11. exponi) crescere sinant usque ad tempus messis, colligunt inde Orthodoxi, quòd haeretici quà tales interficiendi haut sint. Excipit Corn. â Lapide in h. l. Christum non prohibere hîc absolutè, ne hae zizania evellantur, sed ne quis evellere conetur omnia omninò, neque tunc, cùm à tritico dignosci nequeunt, sive cùm periculum est, ne triticum cum iis simul evellatur. Resp. Christus disertè memorat, v. 30. quòd Dominus mandaverit servis, quò crescere finant zizania usque ad tempus messis: illud verò cum sit consummatio seculi, v. 39. manifestum est, Dominum minimè velle, ut citiùs extripentur. Ndicit paterfamilias, quod servi non omnia zizania extirpare debeant, aliqua tamen eradicare, vel tempori hîc inserviendum esse: Sed simpliciter extirpationem messoribus relinquendam esse monet. Quod Patrum autoritatem concernit, novit ipse Cornelius, unanimem nos penè habere Patrum consensum excipit tamen, Augustinum retractare suam sententiam. lib. 3. cont. Epist. Parmen. cap 2. Verùm notandum, quòd nec h. l. Augustinus haereticorum interfectionem, sed saltem cōercitionem suadeat. Instat vero Corn. porrò, quòd manifestus haerticus, maxime si alios suâ haeresi inficiat, graviùs laedat fideles & Ecclesiam, quàm homicida; cùm hic corpus, ille animam occidat,1. Cor. 5. 13.Gal. 5. 12.ubi Apostolus falsos Dd. extirpari iubeat. Resp. De dictis 1. Cor. 5. & Gal. 5. suô. agetur locô. quod artinet rationem, quòd haeretici sint homicidis deteriores, cum animam interficiant, admittimus, haereticos esse homicidas spirituales, ergò etiā spirituali gladio interficiendi h. e. anathematizandi, non verò corporalibus suppliciis è medio tollendi sunt. Sed de controversia hic prolixiùs disserunt Dnn. Geiss. t. 3. Disp. p. 535. Dnn Theol. S-x in Fundam. Des. pupillae p. 94. Seqq. B. Par. L. de Mag. Pol. §. 318. seqq. Confess. Cathol. t. 1. pag. 827. B. D. Bald. in pecul. disert. de haereticis coërcendis, Witteb. Ann. 160excusa. B. D. Kōnig Vind. Sacr. L 65. ubi etiam ostendit, quòd Cyprianus, cuiuautoritatem cumprimis nobis Pontificii obiiciunt, minimè nostrae sententiae adversetur. Egregium verò locum Salviani lib. de Gubernat. DEI pag. 163. hùc facientem adducit B. D Quistorp.

Annot. in h. l. Pulcrè Lactantius l b 5. Instit. divin. cap. 10.de sendenda est religio non occidendo, sed monendo; non saevitiâ, sed patientiâ; non scelere, sed fide. Conf. Aug. lib. 2. contra litt. Petil. cap. 24. & alibi.)*

## 13:30
v. 30. Let them grow. It is not one of confirmation & approbation of them, but of our consolation & exhortation to patience, as if He were saying: Because you are compelled to bear these evil ones and you do not have a Church without evil ones, therefore be patient. Chrysostom hom 47. on Matthew: The Lord says this, so that He might prohibit wars and the shedding of blood. For if heretics were slaughtered without a treaty of peace, war would be brought upon everyone. Theophyl. in the same place: God does not permit heretics to be consumed by wars, lest the just be consumed along with them. Christ opposes this parable to the untimely zeal of those who wish to pluck out and cast out from the Church whatever seems to them evil and iniquitous, when nevertheless it cannot be that the Church in this life be freed from all tares, and it often happens that if everything is cut back to the quick by that method, more harm than benefit is brought to the Church. Thus Toussain. *(Similarly Johannes Piscator in this place and Grossius in Vind. in this place, who themselves also rightly warn, that by this very thing the Savior wishes nothing to be derogated from ecclesiastical discipline. For although heretics are not to be afflicted with capital punishment, they ought nevertheless to be restrained, lest they spread their poison more widely. Much less should we think that the elenctic office, severely enjoined upon the ministers of the Church, is abolished by this admonition of Christ. Conf. Tit. 1, 9. Heretics are to be refuted entirely, although not slaughtered. Therefore the Papists do us an injury, see among others Felicanus Capito Expl. Cath. part. 2. p 534, when they attribute to us, as if we gather from this place, that it is granted to heretics here, that they may with impunity exercise heretical depravity. We teach indeed, that heretics are to be restrained, those who are truly such, (not, as Capito wishes, from the definition of the Roman Pontiff, whose definition indeed is not only fallible, but also perverse, but rather from the judgment of Holy Scripture) yet not to be killed on account of mere or simple heresy. But this matter will be treated more prolixly in Analect. on Gal. 5, 12. where also the argument of Paludanus, which he brings in this place in his Vindications, will be answered.)*

*( Until the consummation of the age. Less firmly from this place

do the Papists gather that the Church will always be established in external splendor. For distinguish between the duration of the universal Church, and the splendor of a particular Church. Concerning the former we have divine promises, not concerning the latter; nor does the present statement speak of the flower or splendor, but of the duration. Indeed, it is so far from being able to be gathered from this that the face of the Church will always be splendid, that it is rather manifestly gathered from this that the wicked are always mixed with the good, who may sometimes prevail, namely in particular Churches, as the times of Elijah and the passion of Christ teach. And the same is beautifully taught by Justin Martyr, or whoever may have been the author of the Qq. & Resp. ad Orthod ascribed to Justin, Q 22. Compare more things pertaining to this in B. Par. L de Eccl. §. 98.)*

Latin:

v. 30. Sinite crescere. Non confirmationis & approbationis est illorum, sed consolationis & exhortationis nostrae ad patientiam quasi dicat: Quia ferre cogimini istos malos & sine malis Ecclesiam non habetis, ideo estote patientes. Chrysostomus hom 47. in Matthaeum: Hoc Dominus dicit, ut bella & effusionem sanguinis prohiberet. Nam si trucidarentur haeretici absque foedere paecis & induciis bellum inferretur omnibus. Theophy l. h. l. Deus non permittit, haereticos bellis consumi, ne simul consumantur & iusti. Opponit -hristus hanc parabolam intempestivo illorū zelo, qui ex Ecclesia volūt evellere & eiicere, quicquid ipsis videtur malum & iniquum, cum tamen fieri non possit, ut Ecclesia in hac vita ab omnibus zizaniis liberetur, ac saepè sit, ut si eâ ratione omnia ad vivum resccentur, Ecclesiae plus da-ni quàm commodi afferatur. ita Tossanus. *(Similiter Iohan. Piscator in h l ac Grossius in Vind. h. l. qui ipsi etiam rectè monent, quod per hoc ipsum Salvator disciplinae Ecclesiasticae nihil velit derogatum. licet enim haeretici capitali supplicio afficiendi haut sint, debent tamen coerceri, ne virus suum latiùs spargant. Multò minùs sublatum per hoc Christi monitum existimemus officium elenchticū, severè Ecclesiae ministris iniunctum. Conf. Tit. 1, 9. Refutandi omninò sunt haeretici, licet non trucidandi. Iniuriâ igitur nos afficiunt Pontificii, videatur inter alios Felicanus Capito Expl. Cath. part. 2. p 534. quando nobis tribuunt, qs. ex h l. colligamus, quòd haereticis hîc concedatur, uti impunè haeret-cam pravitatem exerceant. Docemus utique, coë-endos esse haereticos, reverà tales, (non, uti Capito vult, ex d--nitione Pontificis Romini, cuius quippe definitio non solùm fallibilis est, sed etiam perversa, verùm ex Sc. S. iudicio) non tamen propter meram sive simplicem haeresin interficiendos. Sed de hàc re prolixiùs agetur in Analect. ad Gal. 5, 12. ubi etiam ad arg. Paludani, quae h. l. in Vindiciis suis affert, respondebitur.)*

*( Usque ad con sammationem seculi. Minùs firmiter ex h. l.

colligunt. Pontificii, Ecclesiam semper in splendore externô fore constitutam. Dist. enim inter durationem Ecclesiae universalis, & splendorem Ecclesiae particularis. De illa habemus promissiones divinas, non de hoc; nec loquitur praesens dictum de slore vel splendore, sed de duratione. Imò tantum abest, ut colligi hinc possit, faciem Ecclesiae semper fore splendidam, ut potiùs manifestè hinc colligatur, bonis semper admixtos esse malos, qui aliquando praevalere possint, in Ecclesiis nempe particularibus, ceu tempora Eliae ac passionis Christi docent. Idemque hac pulcrè docet Iustinus Martyr sive quicunque fuerit autor Qq. & Resp. ad Orthod Iustino adscriptarum Q 22. Conf. plura huc facientia apud B. Par. L de Eccl. §. 98.)*

## 13:31
v. 3-. The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed. Why the kingdom of heaven is compared to mustard, Isidore of Pelusium explains in book 1, ep. 199, page 49.

It is said σίνατιπα ρὰ τὸ σίνεσθαι τὸυς ὠπας that it hurts the eyes. *(Some by the kingdom of GOD in this place understand the King himself, namely Christ, and say that Christ is compared with a grain of mustard seed, since nothing was more abject, nothing more humble than he, before he was sown into the earth through death. See Es. 53, 2.Phil. 2, 7. but once cast into the earth he grew so that he ascended even to the seat of GOD. Phil. 2, 9. 10. 11.Eph. 1, 20. etc. A little differently Athanasius, or whoever is the author of the treatise ascribed to Athanasius, on the sayings & interpretations of the parables of Holy Scripture, vol. 2, page 327. Christ calls himself like a grain of mustard seed on account of his human nature: for when he was rich etc. Phil 2. But he calls it a great tree luxuriant with leaves on account of his divinity. And the birds of the air, sitting on its branches. he understands the Prophets etc. But there is no doubt that the scope of Christ is to compare the Gospel with a grain of mustard seed, as that than which nothing in the world is more vile and despised, and yet it is the power of GOD unto salvation to every one that believeth. B. D. Chemn. H. E. c. 61 institutes a beautiful comparison of the Gospel and a grain of mustard seed.)*

Latin:

v. 3-. Simile est regnum coelorum grano sinapis. Quare regnum coelorū comparetur sinapi, exponit Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 1. ep. 199 pag. 49.

Dicitur σίνατιπα ρὰ τὸ σίνεσθαι τὸυς ὠπας quòd laedat oculos. *(Nonnulli per regnum DEI h. l. ipsum Regem. Christum sc. intelligunt, dicuntque, Christum conferri cum grano sinapis, cùm nihil eo fuerit abiectius, nihil humilius, antequam in terram seminaretur per mortem. Vid. Es. 53, 2.Phil. 2, 7. proiectum vero in terram crevit ita, ut adscenderet usque ad consessum DEI. Phil. 2, 9. 10. 11.Eph. 1, 20. &c. Paulò aliter Athan. vel quicunque autor tr. Athanasio adscripti, de dictis & Interp. Parab. Sc. S. t. 2. pag. 327. Christus similem se dicit grano sinapis propter humanam suam naturam: dives enim cùm esset &c. Phil 2.Magnam autem & foliis luxuriantem arborem dicit propter divinitatem. Volucres autem coeli, in ramis eius insidentes. Prophet&c. intelligit. At non est dubium, quin scopus Christi sit, conte-re cum grano sinapis Evangelium, uti quo nihil in mundo vilius & contemtius est, & tamen est potentia DEI ad salutem omni credenti. Pulcram vero collationem Evangelii ac grani sinapis instituit B. D. Chemn. H. E. c. 61.)*

## 13:32
v. 32. It is the greatest. *(in the Greek text it is the comparative μεῖζον. But it is put for the superlative.)* Tremellius recounts examples of the prodigious size of the mustard plant from the Rabbis in his notes on the Syriac Paraphrase on this place. *(Compare also Buxtorff. Lex. Rabb. Talm. p. 823.)*

Latin:

v. 32. Maximum est. *(in textū Graec. est compar. μεῖζον. Sed ponitur pro superlat.)* De prodigiosa magnitudine plantae sinapis exempla ex Rabbinis recenset Tremellius in notis ad Syr. Paraph. h. l. *(Conf. etiam Buxtorff. Lex. Rabb. Talm. p. 823.)*

## 13:33
v. 33. It is like leaven. Just as leaven penetrates the whole mass and makes it pleasant for eating: so the doctrine of the Gospel penetrates the hearts of many men, so that they may become acceptable and pleasing to God. *(The author of the book on the sayings and interpretations of the Holy Scriptures attributed to St. Athanasius, vol. 2, page 325, departs further from the purpose of Christ, who understands by leaven in this place faith, and for three measures of meal the three-day resurrection of the Savior. The word leaven is otherwise generally taken in a bad sense in Holy Scripture, as is evident from Luke 12, 1.1. Corinthians 5, 6. 7.Galatians 5, 9. It is evident therefore from this, that leaven, with the word taken metaphorically, is threefold: Pharisaical, Apostolic, malicious. Compare Mr. Dr. Walth. H. B. on this place.)*

It is enough for three. םאה, In Chaldean םאתא whence σάτον a satum. It is a measure not only of dry things, but also of liquids. Lev. 15, 5. forty sata of water. One satum is Jerusalemite, another is rustic. R. Solomon in Levit. Five Jerusalemite sata are six rustic ones. A satum held six cabs, a cab four logs, a log six common hen's eggs. The parable is derived from Gen. 18. Abraham is the image of God, sacrificing the calf, i.e., His Son. Sarah is the Church, which proposes the Law and the Gospel, in a certain pleasing mixture. Hunnius in c. 18. Gen.

*( Without a parable he spoke nothing to them. These words are to be understood not absolutely, but concerning that time. Conf. Marc. 4, 2. For elsewhere the Savior more often set forth the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven clearly enough. Nor did Christ speak through parables as if he begrudged salvation to his hearers, but so that he might excite in them the attention of listening. See more in Dn. D. Walth. Harm. Bibl. p. 771)*

That it might be fulfilled. The interpreters of Holy Scripture rightly note that just as the Greek and Latin that, often signifies not the cause, but only the event or consequence, just as the Jesuit Tirinus also proposes a canon of this kind in his Explanation of Hebrew and Greek idioms (which examination the Londoners also inserted into the Apparatus to the Polyglot Bibles, though the name of Tirinus was suppressed, which was also done in the treatise on Ancient Weights, coins, etc., which those same men, having borrowed it from Tirinus, wished to be read in the aforementioned Apparatus, yet likewise omitting the name of the creditor). And the present passage also looks to that rule. For the particle does not ὅπως here is causal, as if the prediction of Isaiah were the cause why -hrist spoke through parables, much less that the Jews hearing with their ears might not -ear, but it is demonstrative of the event, that what was predicted has most certainly come to pass.

That it might be fulfilled etc. Q. Why did Christ speak through parables? See Tertull. lib. 4. adv. Marcion. cap. 11. *(Add by all means B. D Glass Philol. Sacr. lib. 2. part. 1. t. 2. sect. 5 art. 4. where he also brings forward many things most -orthy of note concerning the exposition of parables. But concerning the accommodation of Psal 78, 2. to Christ, speaking through Parables, the same author treats in Rhet. S. page 581. as does Mr. Dr. Walth H. B. at this place.)*

*( from the foundations of the world being laid. It is a description of eternity. Compare B. Par. in Apoc. page 101. Socinus is mistaken in Praelect page 5, when he -ontends that this passage is parallel to the Pauline saying Rom 1, 20.. See Mr. D. Calov. Theol. Nat & Rev. page 89. B. P. in Epist. ad Rom. page 47.)*

Latin:

v. 33. Simile est fermento. Sicut fermentum totam massam penetrat & esui gratam reddit: sic doctrina Evangelii multorum hominum corda penetrat, ut Deo fiant accepti & grati. *(Longiùs à Christi scopo abit autor libri de dictis & interpret. p-rab. Sc. S. Athanasio tributi, t. 2. pag. 325. qui per fermentum h. l. intelligit fidem, & pro tria sata triduanam Salvatoris resurrectionem. Fermenti vox aliàs in Sc. S. plerumque in malam accipitur partem, ceu patet ex Luc. 1, 1.1. Corinth. 5, 6. 7.Gal. 5, 9. Patet igitur hinc, quòd fermentum, sumtâ voce metaphoricè, sit triplex, Pharisaicum, Apostolicum, malitiosum. Conf. Dn. D. Walth. H. B. h. l.)*

Satis tribus.םאה, Chaldaicè םאתא unde σάτονsatum. mensura est non tantùm aridorum, sed etiam liquidorum. Lev. 15, 5. quadraginta sata aquae. Satum aliud Hierosolymitanum, aliud agreste. R. Salamon in Levit. Quinque sata Hierosolymitana sunt sex agrestia. Satum capiebat sex cabos, cabus quatuor logos, logus sex communia ova gallinacra. Deducta est parabola ex Gen. 18. Abraham est imago Dei, mactantis vitulum i. e. filium suum. Sara Ecclesiae, quae proponit legem & Evangelium, gratâ quadam temperaturâ. Hunnius in c. 18. Gen.

*( Sine parabola nihil locutus est illis. Intelligenda haec verba non absolutè, sed de illo tempore. Conf. Marc. 4, 2. Alibi enim saepiùs mysteria regni coelorum satis clarè Salvator proposuit. nec locutus est Christus per parabolas, quasi auditoribus salutem invideret, sed ut attentionem audiendi in iis excitaret. Vid. plura apud Dn. D. Walth. Harm. Bibl. p. 771)*

*( Ut impleretur. Rectè notant Interpp. Sc. S. quòd sicuti Dita & Lat. ut, saepe non causam, sed solùm eventum sive consecutionem significet, quemadmodum etiam istiusmodi canonem proponit Iesuita Tirinus in Explicatione idiot. Ebr. & Gr. L. (quam diascepsin etiam Londinenses Apparatui ad Biblia Polyglotta inserverunt, suppresso tamen Tirini nomine, quod etiam factum in tractatu de Antiquis Ponderibus, monetis &c. quem iidem illi à Tirino mutuo acceptum, in Apparatu laudato legi voluerunt. pariter tamen omisso creditoris nomine) Atque ad illam regulam spectat quoque praesens locus. Neque enim particula ὅπως hîc causalis est, quasi praedictio Esaiae causa fuerit, cur -hristus per parabolas loqueretur, multò minus, ut Iudaei auribus audientes non -udirent, sed est demonstrativa eventûs, quòd certissimè evenerit, quod fuit praedictum)*

Ut compleretur &c. Q. Cur Christus per parabolas loquutus fuerit? Vid. Tertull. lib. 4. adv. Marcion. cap. 11. *(Add. omninò B. D Glass Philol.
