Cor. 10, 4. add. 1. Cor. 3, 11.]* ἦ ὁ χριστὸς.Neenim in te Petro, sed in me, ut diligentissimus notat Augustinus, aedificabo dicit Ecelesiam means Haec Meletius. Vid. & Gloss. in c. Dominus dist. 19. Et super hanc. *[Locus ex August. adductus extat serm. 13. de verbis.

Domini. Conf. Idem Aug. tr. 124. in Ioh. Ineptè igitur Pontificii vocem πέτρα h. l. ad Petri personam referunt, ac nil eos iuvat versio, ad quam Bell. l. 1. de P. R. c. 10. Iansen. in Comm. c. 66 Lorinus in Acta p. 39. Baron. t. 1. Annal. A. 31. n. 24. allique provocant, Syriaca, ut pridem à nostratibus ostensum est. Vid. B. D. Glass. Rh. S. p. 527. Dn. Dilherrus Eclog. Syr. p. 85. Hoc loco saltem notetur, quòd Syrus licet utrobique eâdem voce, nempe utatur, nihilo tamen minùs discrimen indicedum priori masc. praeponit, posteriori foem )*

Aedificabo Ecclesiam meam. Salmero t. 4. part. 3. tr. 3. verba Christi sic interpretatur: Super hanc petram i. e. super te edificabo Ecclesiam meam, & portae inferorum non praevalebunt adversùs eaem petram. Probat. 1. Christus remuneraturus confessionem Petritertiò repetivit con-unctionem &, nimirum: Et ego dico tibi, & super hanc petram, & portae inferorum &c. Ubi vides ex praecedentibus & sequentibus sermonem accipiendum de Petro. 2. Q-d novi, in Ecclesiam Universalem, supra petram fundatam, neinfernum nemundum praevalere posse. Resp. 1. Petra illa nec Petrus est, nec Petri, sedes, sed Christus 2. cùm petram in verbis Christi interpretantur, pertinaciter clamant, pronomen referendum ad id, quod proximè processit, ubi tamen solum pronomen non est: hîc verò ubi solum pronomen est, eam, remotius investigant. 3. Chrysostomus, Euthymius, Theophylactus Anselmus in h. l. Athanasius Orat. quâ disputat, unum esse Christum, Syriaca it. versio &c. disertè referunt ad Ecclesiam. Ad 1. Salmeronis argumentum Resp. particula & nihil habet, quod repugnet ei, quam tuemur, constructioni. Etiam Syrus eam expressit, qui tamen mutatione generis ostendit, pronomen eam ad Ecclesiam referendum. Nec sequitur, si praecedentia & sequentia de Petro intelligantur, etiam media intelligenda de Petro. Nam illud quidē fit non vi particulae illius, sed pronominis TU es, Tibi dabo. Postea verò mutatur phrasis in tertiam personam, hanc petram, adversus eam. Vix autē ita solet abrumpi orationis filum, ut eâdem personâ manente, nunc te dicamus, nunc eum. Ad2. cur non novum fuerit effatum de Ecclesiae firmitate, & si non novum, cur non magnum? *(Urget Staple. ton exemplum ex Genesi, ubi Deus ad Abraham: Tu vocaberi Abraham, ratione additâ, quia patrem multarum gentium consti tui te. Quemadmodum igitur d. l. ratio appellationis adiecta ipsum Abrahamum concernit, ita h. l. rationem additam in ipsius Petri personâ fundari, putat Stapleton. Verùm resp. esse diversitatem, cùm ibi addatur pronomen Te, quod hîc non apparet. Deinde si vel maximè in Petro quaerenda appellationis ratio, non necesse tamen est, ut in persona Petri ea fundetur sufficit, quòd in confessione. Instant alii, quòd dicatur super petram adhuc aedificanda Ecclesia. At verò iam olim super Christum erat aedificata. Resp. super Christum s. confessionem de Christo dicitur Ecclesia aedificanda, quat. doctrina coelestis in N. Test. per totum terrarum orbem spargenda & Ecclesia colligenda. Dicitur quoque de Christo, quòd salvaturus sit populum,Matth. 1, 21. & tamen iam olim quoque populum suum à peccatis suis salvum fecit. Sed dicat aliquis: Hîc Christus dicit, quòd velit aedificare Ecclesiam super petram. Iam verò nemo super seipsum aedificat. Resp. Christus super seipsum aedificat, dum ipse dat incrementum à seipso; Eph. 4, 16.)* Et probè notandum, quòd Petrus dicat, credentes aedificari tanquam lapides vivos super petram Christum 1. ep. 2, 4. nenquaquam igitur credidit, Ecclesiam super se extructam. *(Unde benè notant Interpretes relativum τὰυτῃ nō ad proximè praecedens sive ad Petrum, cuius mentio immediatè praecesserat, sed ad Christum, quem Petrus v. 16. confessus erat, f. confessionem Christi à Petro editam, referendum esse. Vid. B. D. Glass. Rhet. S. p 183. nec insolens etiam, pronomina οὗτος, &c. ad remotius referri quandoque. Vid. Ioh 8, 10. ubi οὗτος non ad immediatè antecedens v. 49. sed ad remotius v. 48. referendum. Hûc facit etiam locus Ioh 2, 15. Et ita, nempe de Christo, vel quod eodem recidit, de fide verâ in Christum eiusque confessione intellexerunt quoque non solùm Patres, isidorus Pelus. l. 1. Ep. 235. Hieronymus in h. l. it. l. 2. adv. Iovin. ac Comm in c. 54. Es. Hilarius l. 6. de Trin. p. 74. August serm. 15. de verbis Dom, it. tr. 124. in Ioh. Ambr. de incarn. c. 5. Cyrillus Alexandrinus lib. 33. in Es. c. 3. Beda ac Theoph. in h. l. Gregorius Nyssenus serm. ut petra vitae Christus p. 255. edit. Sifanii. verùum etiam ipsi primi Romani Pontifices, ceu prolixè, ceu prolixè ostendit B. Par. Conf. Cath. l. I. gener. p. 291. Clarissimè Eutychianus I. Ep. Rom. (qui sedit circa A. 275. in Decretali Epist. 1. ad Iohan. & omnes Episcopos Provinciae Beticae t. 1. Concil. Unum hoc, scribit, immobile fundamentum, una haec felix fideipetra, Petri ore confessa, Tues Christus, Filius ille Dei vivi. Sic quoq; Gregorius M. in Pf. 7. ab ipso Corn. à Lap. h. l. adductus: Christus, ait, est petra, à qua Petrus nomen accepit, & super quam se aedificaturum (Ecclesiam) dixit. Similia habet Leo M. Felix, iunior dictus 3. Felix 3. dictus 4. Gregorius M. Adrianus 1. Nicolaus 1. & alii, adducti à B P. l. c. Quid quod ipsum Concilium Tridentinum in Decreto 3. Sess. §. Credo, profiteatur, Symbolum fidei esse tanquam principium illud, in quo omnes, qui fidem Christi profitentur, necessariò conveniunt ad fundamentum firmum & unicum, contra quod portae inferni nunquam praevalebunt. Excipiunt quidem Alph Mendoza Controv. Theol. Quaest. 4. p. 295. aliique Pontificii, Christum quidem esse fundamentum ac petram: sed etiam Petrum, adeoeius quoque in sede Rom. successores. Verùm enim verò cùm tot exempla PP. RR. in haeresin prolapsorum (quae in scenam producit B. Par. Confess. Cath. l. 1. Gen. p. 224. ita ut vana sit gloriatio Iesuitae Costeri in Enchir. Controv. p. 137. Quòd in tanto Pontificum numero, qui B. Petro successervnt, ne unus quidem usad Paulum V. adduci potuerit, qui vel haeresin docuerit, vel in errorem fit lapsus.) satis testentur, quòd Pontifices Romani, qui se Petri successores esse gloriantur, deprehensi fuerint à fide devii, ut loquitur Ius Can. c. si Papa dist. 40. manifestum est, quòd admodùm lubricum futurum fundamentum Ecclesiae, si quaerendum illud esset in persona eorum, qui Petri sese iactitant successores. Quin rectè potiùs super h. l. scripsit Nicol. de Lyra (qui vixit circa A. 1320. monente Bellarm. in de script. Eccl. itemq; Iesuitâ Ant. Possevino in Appar. cui etiam per doctus vir salutatur:) Ecclesia non consistit in hominibus ratione potestatis vel dignitatis Ecclesiastisae vel secularis, quia multi Principes & SUMMI PONTIFICES

& alii inferiores inventi sunt APOSTATASSE A FIDE, propter quod Ecclesia consistit in illis personis, in quibus est notitia & vera confessio fidei & veritatis. Conferatur quoque omninò Erasmus Roterodamus in Annot. ad h. l. Cumprimis etiam notandum, quòd etiam superstructi dicamur super fundamentum Apostolorum & Prophetarum h. e. super fidem illorum, ab iis sc praedicatam & annuncitam, ut explicant Vasquetz in 2. 2. disp. 210. c. 7. Gagnaeus in Ep. ad Eph doctrinā, ab illis nobis traditam, Eph. 2, 20. add. Apoc. 21, 14. quod si igitur licitum esset colligere: Ecclesia aedificata est super Petra h. e. Confessione vel doctrina Petri de Christo, ergò ipse Petrus eiusque fictitii successores PP. RR. sunt infallibiles, pari ratione etiam ex Eph 2. concludere possemus. E. etiam Apostoli eorumque successores, omnes nempe fideles Ecclesiae Ministri, infallibiles sunt. Excipit quidem Corn. à Lapide h. l. Petrum esse fuudamentum & petram totius Ecclesiae, adeoipsorum Apostolorum. Additque, Petri enim, quasi primatis & principis erat, Apostolos in fide, religione & officio continere, dirigere, & sicubi errarent, corrigere. Resp. eadem potestas Apostolis in Petrum data, ceu satis patet ex Gal. 2, 11. ubi Paulus satis acriter, ut loquitur ipse Bell. l. 1. de P. R. c. 27. §. Apostolus, Petrum reprehendit, vel ut habet Corn. à Lapide in Prooem. super Ep. Pauli, à recto tramite deviantem redarguit, revocavit & correxit. Nullum verò dubium, quin idem ius, quod Paulus in Petrum habuit, & reliqui Apostoli in eum, à recto tramite deviantem, habuerint. Ac posito denique, Apostolum Petrum habuisse infallibilitatis privilegium, minimè tamen hinc subsumere ad P. P. R. R. licet, cùm, monente Melch. Cano l. 6. LL. c. 8. probè illud advertendum sit, P. R. Petro succedere, non esse per se in sacris litteris revelatum, sed aliunde constare, ex eo scil. quòd Historiae gravissimae prodiderint, Petrum Romae Cathedram suam collocasse &c. Ast Historici illi, qui hoc commemorarunt, fuére homines. Iam verò omnis homo mendax. Unde patet, quòd infallibilitas R. P. fallibili ac lubrico nitatur fundamento, si vel maximè Petrus à Christo acceperit hîc infallibilitatis privilegium. Quemadmodum verò Pontificis Romani infallibilitas nullâ omninò ratione è praesenti dicto potest probari, ita monarchicum

illius dominatum stabilire è praesenti dicto aviae Romanae gnathones frustra satagunt. Talem certè nec Christus s. Petro s. aliis Apostolis concessit, sed potiùs seriò ab eo appetendo dehortatus eos est. Conf. Matt. 20, 25. 26. 27.c. 23, 8. 9. 10. nec ullatenus etiam cum ipso Petri facto convenit. Vid. Act. 8, 14.c. 15, 5.Gal. 2, 14.1. Petr. 5, 3. Confer plura huc facientia apud B. D. Hutter. LL. Theol. p. 32. B. Par. Confess. Cathol. lib. 2. Spec. part. 1 art. 3. c. 1. &c 2. it. L. de Minist. Eccles. §. 217. Coeterùm nec ipsam universalem Ecclesiam habere h. l. promissionem, quòd ad mundi usque finem perstitura sit, Photiniani statuunt, adeoque ad praesentem locum excipiunt, quòd non promittatur, semper fore fideles, sed si futuri sint, tum Christum eis adfuturum. Resp. Quid opus foret gratiosae praesentiae ac tutelae promisso, si non futura Ecclesia? Aliter igitur excipiunt, nempe, per portas inferni non intelligi diaboli potestatem, sed permanendi in morte necessitatem. Verùm exceptioni isti mox satisfiet.)*

*( Ecclesiam meam. Peti hinc argumentum pro Christi deitate potest, ceu pridem observatum Theophylacto, qui ita in h. l. Quum dixit, Ecclesiam meam, ostendit se Dominum universi: DEO enim serviunt omnia.)*

Portae inferorum Erant portae veterum turres munitae, similes nostris Curiis. Unde per eas metonymicè significantur Imperia. Porta Osmanidarum est regia sedes Suldanorum Turcicorum. Portae inferi h. l. ponuntur pro consiliis ministrorum Satanae saepè convenire solitorum, & imperiis, gerentibus bella adversùs Ecclesiam. Videmus hîc 1. Ecclesiae aedificationem. 2. Eiusdem oppugnacionem. Portae significant certamina civilia & alia, quibus acerrimè dimicari solet de magnis rebus, nam in portis olim exercebantur iudicia ac consultationes. Affirmat ergo, Ecclesiam nec impiâ fraude haereticorum, nec manifestâ vi Tyrannorum everti posse. *(Isid. Pelusiota lib. 1. ep. 238. ροσκαίρ Eod. modo exponit quoque idem ep. 373. it. l. 3. ep. 5. Sic quoque August. in Ps. contra partem Donati, aliique Interpptum veteres, tum recentiores plerique. Praeter causam verò miratur hîc Hugo Grotius, tanto consensu locum hunc de Diabolo aut etiam improborum molitionibus exponi. Urget verò contra receptam expositionem, quòd nusquam reperiaturἅδουvox neapud Hellinistas, neapud novi foederis scriptores in alia significatione, quàm aut mortis aut sepulcri, aut status post mortem. Resp. Non nova est H. Grotii explicatio, sed pridem eandem proposuit Camero, unde procul ambiguo ipse hausit, licet autorem dissimulet. nisi quis dicere malit, quòd à Photinianis, vid. Ostorod. Instit. Germ. p. 413. Smalc. contra Frantz. disp. 7. p. 409. Socin. tr. de Eccl. p. 69 quorum etiam sententiam more suo cupidè amplectitur Sim. Episcopius lib. 4. Instit. s. 1. c. 13. item Respons. ad Epist. Wadingi t. 2. Op. p. 118. interpretationem illam suam, quam receptae in Ecclesia Orthodoxâ tententiae homo κενόφιλος καὶ καινόφιλος frustra praefert, didicerit. Quomodo verò sub istâ expositione, Photinianae haereseos venenum lateat, docet idem B. Par. L. de Inferno §. 6. qui ipse etiam d. §. 4. & 5. itemque L. de Morte §. 173. multis ostendit, omnino nomen שאול ac Gr. ἃδης de inferno, quin de Diabolo quoq; adhiberi. Conf. Dn. D. Calov. Socin. Proflig p. 930. 9Largimur, quòd Christus fidelibus immunitatem à mortis imperio promiserit. Conf. Ioh. 6, 39. 40.44c. 11, 25. 26. Ast de eossam non est quaestio. Sed de eo disputatur, annon etiam ipse Ecclesiae suae militanti h. l. promiserit, quòd omnes Satanae insultus & machinationes non sint contra eam praevaliturae. Probe verò notandum, quod Salvator loquatur generaliter, minimèq; certo alicui coetui talem perpetuam durationem concedat Et testatur etiam experientia, quòd contra particulares Ecclesias portae inferorum saepiùs praevaluerint. Unde si vel maximè probaverint Pontificii, Ecclesiam visibilem, (de quâ tamen h l. Christum non loqui, multis probat B. Par. L. de Eccles. §. 79. Unde etiam rectè Card. Caietanus explicat de Ecclesia, quae constat ex congregatione fidelium, unâ fide, spe & caritate. Similiter Ioh. Ferus in h. l. Talis verò est invisibilis, cùm fides non possit infallibiliter in aliquo cognosci.) non penitus defecturam, nondum tamen obtinuerunt quod volunt, nempe, Ecclesiam Romanam s. quatenus Pontifici Romano adhaeret eiusque dictatoriam autoritatem agnoscit, praevalituram adversùs inferorum portas. Hanc enim particularem Ecclesiam esse, pridem monuit Alphonsus de Madrigal, Episcopus Abulensis, summae apud Pontificios autoritatis, disertè scribens Prologo 2. q. 4. super Matth. edit. Venetae A. 1529. p. 26. a. Ecclesia Latinorum non est Ecclesia Universalis, sed quaedam pars eius: ideò etiamsi tota ipsa errasset, non errabit Ecclesia universalis. Nec sequitur, universali Ecclesiae haec promissio data est. E nec Romanae, utpote eius parti, portae inferorum praevalebunt. Resp. enim, Romanam Ecclesiam tum demum universalis s. verae ac Catholicae Ecclesiae esse partem, quando fidem Catholicam, hoc est scriptis Prophetarum & Apostolorum comprehensam sincerè amplecitur. Aliàs, si contrariam amplexa fuerit doctrinam, nil eam attinent promissiones, Ecclesiae universali à Christo datae. Nec sequitur: Ecclesiae Catholicae talis promissio facta. E. nec Romana Ecclesia excludenda. Resp. notandam hîc esse Regulam, quam proponunt Iesuitae, Sanctius in Act. c. 10. n. 56. ac Corn. à Lapice praelog. in Evang. p. 21. A. In promissis, intelligitur conditio, quae alibi explicatur. Itemque illa altera, itidem in Sc. S. fundata, quam suggerit Dn. D. Waltherus Proleg. H. Bibl. §. 44. Quando promissiones Dei non leguntur impletae, culpa non fuit in Deo, sed in hominibus, eas non dignè accipientibus. Licet proinde promissio stabilitatis Ecclesiae universali, adeoque & particularibus facta sit, certum tamen est, quòd quad Eccl particularibus facta sit, certum tamen est, quòd quòad Eccl particulares cum certâ cōditione id factum intelligi debeat, nempe si permanserint Ecclesiae illae in serm one Christi, Iohan. 8, 31. si maneant aedificatae supra petra. Quâ conditione non impletâ, nec promissionem impleri, necesse est. Ac denique notandum, quòd promissio haec impleatur, si vel maximè aliquando persecutionibus vera Ecclesia prematur, ut non ab omnibus videatur. Videtur autem promissioni de Eccl. stabilitate obstare effatum Salvatoris Luc. 18, 8. Verùm quomodo illud intelligendum sit, monebitur in Analectis ad eum locum. Plura huc facientia suggerunt B. Par. Confess. Cathol. l. 2. spec. part. l. p. 17. Dn. D. Mullerus in Iudaismo p. 115. Porrò si limitatio illa h. l. subintelligatur, h. e. quòd tum demum portae inferorum nō praevalebunt piis, si ipsi nō non recedant à salutis petra Christo, h e. si firmâ fide ei adhaereant, facilè largimur, quòd etiam quilibet pius sese isthâc promissione erigere queat. Minimè verò inferre hinc licet, quòd fideles absolutè non possint amittere fidem & Sp. Sanctum. ceu Ioh. quidem Camero sibi persuadet in Myroth. Evang. ad h. l. Urget contra nos, quos SemiPelagianos Novatores appellat, quòd si Ecclesia aliquando à Christo seiungeretur h. e. si verè fideles aliquando à fide deficerent, & in totalem apostasiam inciderent, sanè praevalerent adversus Ecclesiam inferorum portae. Resp. dist. inter Ecclesiam consid. ratione divinae electionis s. ratione fidei perseverantis, eandemque confideratam ratione gratio sae vocationis s. ratione fidei praesentis. Quod attinet electos, concedimus, quòd non possint finaliter amittere fidem, & fic non praevalent contra eos portae inferni. Hoc tamen non obstante, possunt ad tempus per peccata contra conscientiam excutere Sp. Sanctum, unde & fide totaliter amittunt. Quod ροσκαίρους concernit, penes illos non consistit Ecclesia. Unde si vel maximè tum totaliter, tum finaliter amittant fidem, adeoque contra eos praevaleant portae inferni, nihil tamen per hoc decedit promissioni Christi. Conf. Theoph. h. l. ac notata ad 1. Ioh. 3, 6.)*

ὀυ κατιχύσουσιnon praevalebunt. Valet Satan, sed non praevaler.

## 16:19
(v. 19. I will give to you etc. Theoph. in this place As God he says with great power: I will give to you. Furthermore, if the keys were given to Peter alone, it follows that Peter alone received the power of binding and etc. Resp. I distinguish between the act of promising, which concerns Peter alone, and the thing promised, which concerns others also. See Matth. 18, 18. Ioh. 20, 23. A similar example is had at Matth. 4, 19. Theoph. in this place Although it was said to Peter alone, I will give to you: yet they were granted to all the Apostles. When? When he said: Whose sins you shall remit etc.)

( The keys of the kingdom of heaven. See the notes at c. 18, 18. In this place at least let it be noted, that when Anacletus the Pontiff in c. in novo dist. 21. had said, that Peter first received the power of binding and loosing, he immediately adds: The other Apostles however received honor and power with him IN EQUAL PARTNERSHIP. Therefore the Papists are inept, who strive to construct from the present saying either the primacy of Peter or the authentic and supreme judgment of the Pope. See Cost. Ench. p. 142. and 150. For if The Apostles have equal power as Peter, it follows that the Roman Pontiffs less correctly arrogate it to themselves alone. It is indeed well to be noted that Cornelius à Lapide, intending to prove here that this power was granted to the Roman Pontiff, brings forward as an example Ambrose and Hosius, Bishop of Cordoba, exercising that power. Therefore, it does not belong to the Roman Pontiff alone. Theophylact notes in this place: Although it was said to Peter alone, I will give to you: yet it was granted to all the Apostles. When? When he said: Whose sins you shall forgive &c. Nor can we disapprove of the observation of the same Cornelius, when he writes in the same place: Note, that Christ did not say, I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of the earth, lest this power be thought earthly and temporal, but of the kingdom of heaven, so that it might be signified that this power extends properly and directly to spiritual things, which pertain to the kingdom of heaven. In which words the particle directly deserves further observation, as it is in this that Jesuitical subtlety lies. For since the Canonists were formerly so crude as to assert that the Roman Pontiff has by divine right the most full power over the whole world, both in Ecclesiastical and Political matters, so that all Kings are vassals of the Pope, as Augustinus Steuchus argues in his book on the Donation, the Jesuits, perceiving that this assertion, if brought forward so nakedly, is full of odium to Christian Princes, therefore thought it should be limited in such a way as to assert that the Pope does not have any merely temporal jurisdiction directly by divine right. Just as Cardinal Bellarmine softens the opinion of the Papists in book 5 of the Roman Pontiff, chapter 4. However, the modesty or temperament of Bellarmine pleased Sixtus V, the Roman Pontiff, very little, as Barclay the Papal jurist reveals, namely in his book on the power of the Pope, chapter 13, page 101, mentioning that it was very close that he would have abolished all of his (Bellarmine's) works by Papal Censure on that account. Nevertheless, most Jesuits today follow that temperament, as we have already seen from Cornelius à Lapide. Who, however, lest he seem to have restricted the power of the Pope too much, soon adds: but to temporal things not except indirectly, insofar, namely, as they are referred to spiritual things as necessary or very useful. But someone might ask, what are those necessary and very useful things? Cornelius indicates in some way, when a little later he notes, that the Roman Pontiff not only binds and looses men, but also sins, vows, oaths &c. Certainly, the Pontiff knows excellently how to usurp this power when he drives Princes from their throne and absolves subjects from their oath. Furthermore, how excellent are the little flowers that sprout from that indirect power of the Roman Pontiff in temporal matters, and how erroneous this opinion is, has long since been shown quite prolixly by our people. See B. Par. Cont. Cathol. book 2, special part 1, article 3, chapter 9. In this place, it pleases at least to whisper to the Jesuit Cornelius that statement of John of Paris, of the Order of Preachers (who flourished around the year 1290), in his tract on Royal and Papal Power chapter 15: It would be foolish to understand that by this ( Matthew 16 Whatsoever you shall loose) is given A POWER OF ABSOLVING from the BOND OF DEBTS. Now, indeed, the obedience of subjects is a debt by which they are bound to the Magistrate. Therefore, it is foolish to assert that the Roman Pontiff, through this promise of Christ, received the power to loose subjects from the bond of obedience. From which opinion perhaps Pineda does not shrink, when in chapter 12 of Job, verse 14, number 3, he writes that the reason for shutting and opening in this place is a symbol of supreme power and the free administration of all things. The handing over of keys is indeed a symbol of power and authority conferred upon someone, compare Apocalypse 3, 7, but not always absolute, but rather restricted. That the present does not include the power of lording over Kings and driving them from their throne is clear from comparing this place with Matthew 20, 5. Furthermore, although Peter bore the person of the whole Church when he received the keys from Christ, as Augustine rightly observes in tractate 124 on John, and likewise in book 1, d. D. C., chapter 18, and proves more prolixly in B. Par. Book on Ministry, section 87, nevertheless the Photinians ineptly infer from this that the right of teaching belongs to all the faithful, and that no peculiar calling is required for the office of teaching. For although the keys were given to Peter for the benefit of the whole Church, the administration of them must be committed by the Church to certain persons, namely those to whom Christ gave the power of shutting and opening, that is, the Apostles and their successors in the Ecclesiastical ministry. Compare John 20, 23.

1. Ioh. 4, 1. Nor yet ought the Church to commit the use of the keys to others in such a way that it itself retains no further right of calling the ministers of the Church, which Bell. seems to do in l. 1. de Cler. c. 7. Concerning which matter let B. Par. L. de Minist. Eccl. §. cit. be consulted at greater length. Much less have the keys been granted to the ministers of the Church in such a way that they ought to arrogate to themselves a certain power ἀυτοκρατορικὴ. Against which error B. Par. argues in the same place, l. c. §. 199. 200.)*

(v. 19. Ἔσται δεδεμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς. i. e. it will be ratified and approved before God, as Dionysius the Carthusian correctly explains, and after him the Jesuit Maldonatus, and likewise Fr. Lucas, or: Whatever existing upon earth you shall have bound, this God will hold ratified and will deem bound in heaven, as the Jesuit Corn. à Lapide, not caring for the preposterous ἀκρίβειαν of the Socinians, of Alphonsus de Castro in his treatise against heresies, title Pope, and of Greg. de Valentia in his Analysis, book 7, chapter 2 (to whom, as you deserve, Corn. Jansenius, a writer otherwise serious and learned, in his Concordance of the Gospels, chapter 66, gives his vote), who think that the primacy of Peter can be confirmed also from the fact that here the Lord speaks in the plural number τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, but in the parallel passage Matth. 18, 18. where He speaks to the Apostles, in the singular ἐ τῷ οὐρανῷ. But that subtlety proceeds from an ignorance of Hebraism: for it is certain that among the Hebrews the noun שמים, heaven, otherwise denoting it, is used everywhere for God Himself (as has been shown in the Analysis at c 11, 11. and elsewhere, and will be warned of at greater length at Matth. 21, 25.), as He who manifests His majesty especially in heaven (see the analysis at Matth. 6, 9.). Which mode of speaking the Savior Himself also retained elsewhere, see below c. 21, 25. above c. 11, 11. etc. But since the word שמים is of the dual number, hence in the Greek text it is expressed now by the singular, now by the plural number, so that therefore no mystery of Papal primacy can be sought in the plural number. And hence also the Oriental interpreters, the Syrian, the Arab, and the Ethiopian, use the plural number not only here, but also at c. 18, 18., namely here that this Just as the Persian also uses the same word in both places, namely which why the Londoners render now in the singular, now in the plural here, no reason appears. Furthermore, the Savior spoke in Syriac, the Papists themselves granting it. But since the Syrian interpreter observes no distinction, it is clear how inept they are who seek a mystery of monarchical Papal power in the speech of Christ. Which vanity Cardinal Bellarmine, and the Jesuits Cotton and likewise Becanus have detected without ambiguity, of whom, although the latter in his Manual of Controversies, book 1, chapter 4, §. 45, p. 69, has striven with anxious zeal to scrape together from everywhere in Holy Scripture thirteen (in the index it is mentioned that fifteen are referred to, therefore perhaps some were taken away again) prerogatives of Peter, and the former twenty, so that they might establish the Papal monarchy, they are nevertheless completely silent about this one. Deservedly, therefore, we praise the ingenuousness of the Jesuit Maldonatus, who, mocking that subtlety, burst forth into these words in his commentary on this passage: As if Peter had received the power of binding and loosing in all the heavens, and the other Apostles in one. Franciscus Lucas also, although perhaps he had nothing more in his desires than to demonstrate from the present text itself that the power of binding and loosing was given to Peter and his successors, whom alone he wishes to be the Roman Pontiffs, by another reason, namely by eminence of authority, than to the other Apostles and their successors, yet he did not dare to seek a distinction in the number here, nor could he find anything here in the text to establish his opinion. Whence he was content to have shown that by the authority of the Synod of Alexandria alone. That, however, that Synod does not establish the primacy, has been noted elsewhere. But neither does the Jesuit Costerus in Ench. p. 146, in the solution of the objection that the power of binding and loosing was granted to the Apostles as well, seek any patronage in the name οὐρανοῖς. Nor furthermore will indulgences be able to be proved from the granting of these keys, as will be noted in the Anal. on Matth. 18, 18. Indeed, not even ἀυτοκρατορικὴ power, as will likewise be shown at the said place. Some add that if it denotes a greater power when power is given ἐν οὐρανοἱς, than when it is said ἐ οὐρανῶ,, it follows that Peter received greater power than Christ himself. As he who in the last chapter of Matthew v. 18. professes that power was given to him ἐ οὐρανῶ, but not ἐ οὐρανοῖς.. It can also be noted that Erasmus found the plural number in the older codices also in Matth. 18, 18. Finally, this also is to be observed against Socinus on this place, p. 72 and 75, that these words concerning the loosing of the bound, that is, the remission of sins, are not to be accepted only declaratively and significatively, but also

properly, that is, efficiently: for although the ministers of the Church open the kingdom of heaven only instrumentally, they are nevertheless the organs of God, through which He does it. Nor does the principal cause exclude the instrumental. Thus men are also said to regenerate and save, 1. Cor. 4, 15.c. 9, 1.Gal. 4, 19.1. Tim. 4, 16.)*

Latin:

*(v. 19. Dabo tibi &c. Theoph. in h. l. Tanquam Deus magnâ potestate dicit: Dabo tibi. Porrò si soli Petro datae claves, sequitur, quòd solus Petrus acceperit potestatem solvendi &c. Resp. dist. inter promittendi actum, qui solum Petrum concernit, & rem promissam, quae etiam alios. Vid. Matth. 18, 18.Ioh. 20, 23. Simile exemplum habetur Matth. 4, 19. Theoph. in h. l. Quamvis Petro soli dictum sit, dabo tibi: omnibus tamen & Apostolis concessa sunt. Quando? quum dixit: Quorum remiseritis &c.)*

*( Claves regni caelorum. Vid. notata ad c. 18, 18. Hoc loco saltem notetur, quòd cùm Anacletus Pontifex c. in novo dist. 21. dixisset, Petrum primum accepisse potestatem ligandi ac solvendi, mox subiiciar: Caeteri verò Apostoli cum eo PARI CONSORTIO, honorem, & potestatem acceperunt. Inepti igitur sunt Pontificii, qui è praesenti dicto vel primatum aliquom Petri vel authenticum ac summum Papae iudicium adstruere satagunt. Vide Cost. Ench. p. 142. ac 150. Si enim parem potestatem habent Apostoli, quam Petrus, sequitur quòd minùs rectè sibi solis PP. RR. eam arrogent. Probè verò notandum, quòd Corn. à Lapide istam potestatem P. R. concessam hîc probaturus, adducat exempli loco Ambrosium ac Hosium Episcopum Cordubensem, istam potestatem exercentes. E. nō soli P. R ea competit. Notanter Theophylactus in h. l. Quamvis Petro soli dictune sit, dabo tibi: Omnibus tamen & Apostolis concessae sunt. Quando? quum dixit: Quorumcunremiseritis is peccata &c. Nec improbare possumus eiusdem Cornelii observationem, quando ibid. scribit: Nota, non dixisse Christum, dabo tibi claves regni terrarum, ne terrena & temporalis putaretur haec potestas, sed regni coelorum, ut significaretur haec potestas propriè & directè extendi ad spiritualia, quae spectant adregnum coelorum. In quibus verbis observationem ulteriorem meretur particula directè, upote in qua subtilitas Iesuitica latet. Cùm enim Canonistae olim adeò crassi fuerint, ut asserveriut, Pontificem Romanum iure divino habere plenissimam potestatem in universum terrarum orbem tum in rebus Ecclesiasticis, tum Politicis, ita ut omnes Reges sint Papae vasalli, ceu disputat Augustinus Steuchus in lib. de Donat. deprehendentes Iesuitae, adsertionem hanc, si ita nude proferatur, invidiae plenam esse Principibus Christianis, quapropter ita eam limitandam putarunt, ut adsererent, Papam non habere ullam merè temporalem iurisdictionem directè iure divino. quemadmodum ita Pontificiorum sententiam emollit Card. Bellarminus lib. 5. de P. R. c. 4. Ut ut verò Bellarmini modestia sive temperamentum parùm placuerit Sixto V. P. R. ceu prodit Barclaius Ictus Pontificius, quippe libr. de potest. Papae c. 13. p. 101. co-emorans, quòd parùm abfuerit, quin omnia illius (sellarmini) opera Pontificiâ Censurâ proptera aboleret. Sequuntur tamen tempermantum illud Iesuitae hodiè plerique, ceu ex Corn. à Lapide iam vidimus. Qui tamen, ne nimiùm coarctasse Pontificis potestatem videatur, mox subiicit: ad temporalia verò non nisi indirectè, quat. scil. ad spiritualia ut necessaria vel valdè utilia referuntur. Sed quaerat aliquis, quaenam sint illa necessaria & valdè utilia? Indicat aliquo modo Cornelius, quando paulò post annotat, Pontificem Rom. non tantùm homines ligare & solvere, sed & peccata, vota, iuramenta &c. Sanè egregiè novit usurpare hanc potestatem Pontifex, quando Principes è solio deturbat, & subditos à iuramento absolvit. Coeterùm quàm egregii ex illâ indirectâ P. R. in temporalibus potestate propullulent flosculi, & quàm erronea sit haec sententia, pridem satis prolixè à nostratibus ostensum Vid. B. Par. Cont. Cathol. l. 2. spec. part. 1. art. 3. c. 9. Hoc loco placet saltem insusurrare Iesuitae Cornelio illud Ioh. Parisiensis, Ord. Praedic. (qui floruit circa A. 1290.] tract. de Potest. reg. & Papali cap. 15.Stultum esset intelligere, quòd per hoc ( Matth. 16. Quodcunque solveris) datur POTESTAS ABSOLVENDI à VINCULO DEBITORUM, Iam verò obedientia subditorum est debitum, quo Magistratui sunt illi obstricti. E. stultum est adserere, quòd P. R. per hanc Christi promissionem potestatem acceperit, subditos à vinculo obedientiae solvere. A quâ sententia fortè nec Pineda abhorret, quando in c. 12. Iobi. v. 14. n. 3. seribit, concludendi & aperiendi rationem h. l. supremae potestatis & liberae rerum omnium administrationis symbolum esse. Est sanè traditio clavium symbolum potestatis atque autoritatis in aliquem collatae, Conf. Apoc. 3, 7. sed nō semper absolutae, verùm restrictae. Quòd verò praesens non includat potestatem dominandi super Reges, eosque de throno deturbandi, patet ex coll. h. l. cum Matth. 20, 5. Porrò licet Petrus personam totius Ecclesiae gesserit, quando à Christo claves accepit, uti rectè observat August. tr. 124. in Ioh. itemque l. 1. d. D. C. c. 18. & prolixiùs probat B. Par. L. de Minist. §. 87. ineptè tamen hinc inferunr Photiniani, quòd omnibus fidelibus competat ius docendi, nec requiratur peculiaris vocatio ad officium docendi. Etenim licet claves datae sint Petro in commodum totius Ecclesiae, administratio tamen earum committi ab Ecclesiâ certis personis debet, illis nempe, quibus Christus potestatem dedit claudendi & aperiendi, h. e. Apostolis, eorumque in ministerio Ecclesiastico successoribus. Conf. Ioh. 20, 23.

1. Ioh. 4, 1. Neque tamen ita clavium usum Ecclesia aliis committere debet, ut ipsa nullum ampliùs ius vocandi Ecclesiae ministros retineat, quod Bell. videtur l. 1. de Cler. c. 7. Quâ de re consulatur pluribus B Par. L. de Minist. Eccl. §. cit. Multò minùs ita Ministris Ecclesiae claves concessae sunt, ut ipsi potestatem quandam ἀυτοκρατορικὴ arrogare sibi debeant. Quem contra errorem ibid. disputat B. Par. l. c. §. 199. 200.)*

*(v. 19. Ἔσται δεδεμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς. i. e. erit ratum & approbatum coram Deo, uti rectè explicat Dionysius à Rickel, & post cum Iesuita Maldonatus, itemq; Fr. Lucas, vel: Quicquid super terram existens ligaveris, hoc Deus ratum habebit censebit que ligatum in coelo, uti Iesuita Corn. à Lapide, non curans praeposteram ἀκρίβειαν sociennorum, Alphonsi de Castro tr. adv. haeres: tit. Papa, ac Greg. de Valentia in Anal. l. 7. c. 2. (quibus, quod mereris, Corn. Iansenius, scriptor alioquin gravis ac doctus, in Concord. Ev. c. 66. suffragatur) existimantium, primatum Petri ex eo quoq; confirmari posse, quòd hîc Dominus in pl, numero loquatur τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, in loco verò parallelo Matth. 18, 18. ubi ad Apostolos loquitur, in singulariἐ τῷ οὐρανῷ. Ast ex ignorantiâ Ebraismi subtilitas illa proficiscitur: constat quippe, quòd apud Ebraeos nomē שמים,coelum alioqui notans, passim pro ipso Deo, (ceu in Anal, ad c 11, 11. & alibi ostensum, ac pluribus monebitur ad Matth. 21, 25.) ut qui in coelo maiestatem suam cumprimis manifestat (vid, anal. ad Matth. 6, 9.) adhibeatur. quem loquēdi modum etiam ipse Salvator alibi, vid. infrà c. 21, 25. suprà c. 11, 11. &c. retinuit quoq; Cùm verò vox שמים sit dualus numeri, inde in textu Graeco modò per singularem, modò per pluralem numerum exprimitur, ut adeò nullum principatûs Papalis mysterium in pl. numero quaeri possit. Atq; hinc etiam Orientales Interpp. Syrus, Arabs & Aethiops non hîc solùm, sed etiam c. 18, 18. plurali numero utuntur, nempe hic ille iste Quemad. & Persa utrobiq; eandem vocem adhibet, videl. quam cur Londinenses modò in sing. modò in pl. hîc reddant, nulla apparet ratio. Praeterea Salvator Syriacè loquutus est, ipsis Pontificiis largientibus. cùm verò Syrus Interpres nullum discrimen observet, pater, quàm inepti sint, qui in Christi sermone mysterium Monarchicae potestatis Papalis quaerunt. Quam vanitatem procui ambiguo deprehenderunt Cardinalis Bellarminus, ac Iesuitae Cotonus itemque Becanus, quorum licet hic in Man. Controv. l. 1. c. 4. §. 45. p. 69. tredecim (in indice quinde cim referri memoratur, ergo aliquae forsan iterum ademptae) Petri praerogativas, ille ipsas viginti anxio studio undique è Sc. S. corradere sategerint, quò monarchiam Papalem stabiliant, de hâc tamen prorsus tacent. Meritò hinc laudamus ingenuitatem Iesuitae Maldonati, qui subtilitatem istam irridens in haec erupit Comm. h. l. verba: Quasi Petrus in omnibus coelis, alii Apostoli in uno solvendi potestatem acceperint. Franciscus quoque Lucas licet nihil fortè magis in desideriis habuerit, quàm ut ex ipso praesenti textu demonstraret, quòd aliâ ratione, nempe auctoritatis eminentiâ, ligandi solvendique potestas Petro eiusq; successoribus, quos solos vult esse PP. RR. data sit, quàm coeteris Apostolis eorumque sucessoribus, non ausus tamen fuit, discrimen in numero hîc quaerere, nec quicquam etiam potuit hîc pro sua sententia stabilienda in textu invenire. Unde contentus, solius Synodi Alexandrinae id ostendisse autoritate. Quòd tamen nec Synodus ea primatum stabiliat, alibi monitum. Sed nec Iesuita Costerus in Ench. p. 146. in solutione obiectionis, quòd Apostolis quoque potestas ligandi & solvendi concessa, ullum in nomine οὐρανοῖς patrocinium quaerit. Nec probari porrò è clavis huius concessione indulgentiae poterunt, uti monebitur in Anal. ad Matth. 18, 18. Quin nec ἀυτοκρατορικὴ potestas, uti itidem ad d. l. ostendetur. Addunt nonnulli, quòd si maiorem notat potestatem, quando potestas data ἐν οὐρανοἱς, quàm cum dicitur ἐ οὐρανῶ, consequens sit, Petrum maiorem accepisse potestatem, quàm ipse Christus. Ut qui Matth. ult v. 18. profitetur, quòd data sibi potestas ἐ οὐρανῶ, nō verò ἐ οὐρανοῖς. Notari & hoc potest, quòd etiam Matth. 18, 18. numerum pluralem in vetustioribus Codd. Erasmus invenerit. Denique & hoc contra Socinum super h. l. p. 72. & 75. observandum, quòd verba haec de solutione ligatorum, s. peccatorum remissione non accipienda sint tantùm declarativè & significativè, sed etiā

propriè s. efficienter: licet enim ministri Ecclesiae tantùm instrumentaliter regnum coelorum aperiant, sunt tamen DEI organa, per quae id facit. Nec causa principalis excludit instrumentalem. Sic dicuntur etiam homines regenerare ac salvare, 1. Cor. 4, 15.c. 9, 1.Gal. 4, 19.1. Tim. 4, 16.)*

## 16:20
v. 20. He commanded his disciples that they should tell no one that he was Jesus Christ. Christ forbids that they should tell anyone that he was the Christ, because there was a danger that the Jews, in their insolence, might convert the concept of knowledge which they had concerning Christ to a different end, just as Ioh. 6. they offer him a kingdom. They were not yet sufficiently instructed with sufficient gifts, the time of suffering was at hand. Basil in Apol. ad Caesarem: He had not yet finished his course, he preferred therefore to be recognized as the Messiah from the predictions of the Prophets, rather than from the testimonies of his own household. *(Chrysost. hom. 55. a little differently: If the disciples, who saw very many things, heard many mysteries, were scandalized by hearing alone, and not they alone, but even the vertex of all, Peter: consider now with yourself what the common people, who had inspected nothing higher in secret, were not established by any grace of the Spirit, would have suffered, if they had learned that he whom they saw being crucified and agitated by every insult was the Son of GOD. Theophylact adds for this reason he hides himself from many, so that after the resurrection he might be known by many without a stumbling block, the Holy Spirit making all things equal to the operations of miracles. Compare more things pertaining to this in Ioann. Cameron in Myrothecio p. 42. 43. 44. Furthermore, in most and the more approved Greek and Latin Codices, (which the Ethiopian also supports, as it expressly has: i. e. that he himself is the Lord Jesus Christ) the name Jesus is read, placed before the name Christ. Franc. Lucas Brugensis suspects, however, that it was added to the text by some sciolist scribe, just as it seems to be redundant to Beza and likewise to Erasmus, and indeed to Grotius it is without doubt an interpretation. Understand, inserted into the text not by the Evangelist himself, but by some other person. Corn. à Lapide seems to think the same thing, which you might deservedly wonder at in a Jesuit, departing so easily from the Vulgate Latin version, which was nevertheless pronounced authentic in the Council of Trent. But although we do not minutely deny that in certain Greek Codices the name Jesus is not seen in this place, just as besides those three MSS. Codices which Fr. Lucas collated, the Lincoln Codex, which D. Walton warns is very ancient in Var. Lect. Gr. N. Test., and also another Codex of New College Oxford, and likewise a certain Codex of Montfort and another of Henry Gvoge, just as also it is omitted by the Syrian, with the Altdorf MS. consenting, and likewise the Arab and the Persian, yet there does not appear a sufficient reason why that word should be established as having been inserted into the text by some sciolist, since the remaining most ancient and most approved Greek and Latin Codices acknowledge it. H. Grotius indeed urges, That Jesus was a proper name, by which he was known among all: but that Christ is a name of dignity. But even if the Savior was known to the Jews under the name Jesus, inasmuch as they were not ignorant that it had been bestowed upon him at his circumcision: yet this escaped them, that he himself was that Jesus Christ, that is to say, the Savior of the world, Matth. 1, 21. and the promised Messiah. Therefore, to the Greek codices in which the name Jesus is missing, we oppose many other most ancient and most approved ones, concerning which D. Walton, as well as Brugensis, Erasmus, and Beza themselves testify that they exhibit the name Jesus here. Furthermore, Grotius urges against the received reading the Fathers, Origen, Ambrose, and Theophylact. But what then? It may be conceded that Origen had such a copy where the name Jesus was missing, which kind of copy the Syrian, the Arab, and the Persian perhaps also had. But that concludes nothing against the received reading, since it is certain that the aforementioned interpreters also sometimes used less approved copies. Moreover, regarding Theophylact, the matter is very uncertain whether he read it so. Certainly, in the Latin version which Oecolampadius prepared, it is said entirely in Theophylact, that he himself was Jesus Christ. Nor is there anything else held in the explanation than what is also read in Chrysostom, namely that Christ did not wish to be manifested before the cross, that he himself is God, that is, the Son of God. But since this same thing is also indicated by the name Jesus, in that sense in which this name was imposed upon our Savior, it is so far from the case that the received reading conflicts with Theophylact's interpretation that it rather confirms it. The same can be said of Ambrose. But especially on our side is Jerome, who so approves the received reading that he denies that the Apostles before to have preached Jesus, i.e., the Son of the living GOD, i.e., the true and natural God, such as Peter had now confessed. The same man testifies, that in many copies it is read Jesus Christ, not as some think, the name Jesus is redundant. The same man notes that this opinion is opposed by the fact that Jesus, which signifies Savior, is the name of God, while Christ is the name of man.)*

Latin:

v. 20. Edixit discipulis suis, ne cui dicerent, quòd ipse esset Iesus Christus. Christus prohibet, ne cui dicerent, quòd esset Christus, quia periculum erat, ne protervè, quod haberent de Christo notitiae conceptum, Iudaei in alienum finem converterent, sicut Ioh. 6. regnum ei offerunt. Nondum satis instructi erant donis suffcientibus, aderat tempus patiendi. Basilius in Apol. ad Caesarem: Nondum absolverat suum cursum, maluit igitur ex Prophetarum praedictionibus, quàm ex domesticorum testimoniis pro Messiâ agnosci. *(Chrysost. hom. 55. paulò aliter: Si discipuli, qui plurima viderunt, multaaudierunt arcana, solo auditu scandalizati fuerunt, nec ipsi solùm, verùm etiam & vertex omnium Petrus: cogita nunc tecum, quid vulgus, qui nihil altius secretè inspexerūt, nulla Spiritûs gratiâ stabili fuere, perpessi fuissent, si quem Filium DEI esse didicissent, eum crucifigi & omni contumeliâ exagitari viderent. Addit Theoph. propterea occultat se multis, ut post resurrectionem absoffendiculo à multis sciatur, Sp. Sancto omnia miraculorum operationibus adaequante. Confer plura huc facientia apud Ioann. Cameronem in Myrothecio p. 42. 43. 44. Coeterùm in plerisque ac probatioribus Codd. Graecis ac Latinis, (quibus etiam suffragatur Aethiops, ut qui expressè habet: i. e. quòd ipse Dominus Iesus Christus) legitur nomen Iesus, praemissum nomini Christus. Suspicatur tamen Franc. Lucas Brugensis, à sciolo quodam librario textui additum fuisse, quemadmodum & Bezae itemque Erasmo abundare videtur, quin & Grotio haut dubie interpretamentum est. Intellige, textui non ab ipso Evangelista, sed ab alio quodam insertum. Idem etiam Corn. à Lapide sentire videtur, quod meritò mireris in Iesuita, adeò facilè à Vulg. vers. Latina, quae tamen in Concil. Trident. authentica pronunciata, discedente. Verùm licet mi-inè negemus, quòd in quibusdam Codd. Graecis nomen Iesus h. l. non conspiciatur, quemadmodum praeter tres illos MSS. Codd. quos Fr. Lucas contulit, Codex Lincolniensis, quem vetustissimum esse, D. Walthonus monet in Var. Lect. Gr. N. Test. nec non Codexalius Col. Novi Oxoniensis, itemq; Codex quidam Montfortii ac alius Henrici Gvoge, sicuti etiam idem à Syro, consentiente MSS Altdorffino, Arabe item ac Persa omissum est, nondum tamen sufficiens apparet ratio, quare vox illa textui à sciolo quodam inserta statui debeat, cùm reliqui Codd Graeci iuxta ac Latini antiquissimi & probatissimi eam agnoscant. Urget quidem H Grotius, Iesum fuisse nomen proprium, quo apud omnes no scebatur: Christum verò esse nomen dignitatis. At si vel maximè sub nomine Iesu Salvator Iudaeis fuerit notus, quippe quod ipsi in circumcisione tributum fuisse, non ignorabant: hoc tamen eos fugiebat, quòd ipse esset Iesus ille Christus h. e. mundi Salvator,Matth. 1, 21. ac promissus Messias. Codicibus igitur Graecis, in quibus nomen Iusus defideratur, opponimus alios plures antiquissimos ac probatissimos, de quibus tum D. Walthonus, tum Brugensis, Erasmus ac Beza ipsimet testantur, quod nomen Iesus hîc exhibeant. Urget porrò Grotius contra receptam lectionem Patres, Originem, Ambrosium, Theophylactum. Sed quid tum? Concedi potest, Origenem tale habuisse exemplum, ubi nomen Iesu defuit, quale exemplum etiam Syrus, Arabs ac Persa fortè habuerunt. Id verò nihil concludit contra receptam lectionem, cùm constet, etiam praedictos Interpp. aliquando usos fuisse exemlis minùs probatis. De Theophylacto insuper res valdè incerta, an ita legerit. Certè in versione Latina, quam Ocolampadius adornavit, integrè in Theophylacto dicitur, quod ipse esset Iesus Christus Nec in explicatione quicquam habetur aliud, quàm quod etiam apud Chrysostomum legitur, quòd nempe Christus noluerit ante crucem manifestari, quòd ipse sit Deus s. Filius DEI. Cùm verò idem hoc etiam nomine Iesu indicetur, eo sc sensu, quo Salvatori nostro hoc nomen fuit impositum, tantum abest, ut recepta lectio pugnet cum Theophylacti interpretatione, ut potiùs eandem confirmet. Idem de Ambrosio dici potest. Cumprimis verò noster est Hieronymus, qui adeò receptam lectionem approbat, ut neget, Apostolos antè praedicasse Iesum i. e. Filium DEI vivi h. e. verum & naturalem Deum, qualem nunc Petruc confessus erat. Testatur idem, in plerisexemplaribus legi Iesum Christum, neut nonnulli putant, nomen Iesum abundare. Cui opinioni hoc adversari notat idem, quòd Iesus DEI, qui Servatorem significat, Christus hominis nomen sit.)*

## 16:21
*(v. 21. That he must. See Greg. Nyssenus Orat 1. on the Resurrection of Christ p 148. Then he proclaimed etc. Theoph. He predicts the passion to them, lest they be offended by its unexpected arrival, as if he had suffered unwillingly or without foreknowledge. Πρεσβυτέρων. Buxtorffius correctly notes in Lex. Talm. under the word סוהרריז, that by Elders in this place are understood the Senators in the Great Sanhedrin, concerning whom learned men treat everywhere. We have cited some in Analect. on c 5, 21.)*

Latin:

*(v. 21. Quòd oporteret. Vid Greg. Nyssenus Orat 1. de Resurr. Christi p 148. Tunc edixit &c. Theoph. Praedicit illis passionem, ne inexpectata illâ veniente offenderentur, quòd invitus, vel non praescius passus esset.Πρεσβυτέρων. Rectè notat Buxtorffius Lex. Talm. voce סוהרריז, per Presbyteros h. l. intelligi Senatores in Synedrio Magno. de quo passim agunt viri docti. allegavimus quosdam in Analect. ad c 5, 21.)*

## 16:22
v. 22. Ἵλεώς σοι Κύριε. A formula of deprecation and aversion, used in the version of the LXX Interpreters 1. Paral. 11, 19. 2. Sam. 23, 16. The sense is: God be propitious to you. i.e., he is more propitious than that such a thing should happen to you. Thus Gen. 42. v. 23. ἵλεως ὑμῖν, μή φοβεῖσθε. Where the name God must necessarily be understood. Therefore, the Vulgate correctly rendered it as to the sense: Far be it from you Lord, this shall not be to you. 1. Macc. 2, 21. *[Conf. B. D. Glass Gr. S. p. 637. Nic. Fullerus l. 2. Misc. c. 2. Furthermore, for similar examples of the error of the human mind from ignorance of the divine counsel see 2. Sam. 7. 1. 2. 3. Matth. 3, 14. Ioh. 13, 6. Moreover, the Orthodox correctly gather from Peter's error (concerning which Ambrose writes in Ps. 118. Peter was wandering in the darkness of ignorance, he denied that Christ was to die, because he did not yet believe he would die and rise again.) that he did not absolutely receive the gift of infallibility through the words of the Savior: You are Peter etc. So that the Roman Pontiffs, who falsely sell themselves as Peter's successors, ineptly boast that they are endowed with it. Let those things which are read on this matter in B. D. Chemnitius Harm. Evang. c. 86. p. 948, Marcus Anton. de Dominis t. 1. de Rep. Eccl. l. 1. c. 6. p. 59 be unrolled. Indeed, Peter's lapse and error is so manifest that although some Papists strive to excuse Peter and keep him immune from all error, the Jesuit Conzenius, nevertheless, convinced by the force of truth, confesses that Peter is not to be excused, Comm. in h. l. q. 1. to v. 22. The same man warns, just as Bell. t. 1. l. 1.

on the Roman Pontiff c. 28, that Peter erred in sense, not in affection. We admit the distinction, which Jerome also uses, but we deny that by this Peter is freed from error. Which suffices for us. Tirinus in this place distinguishes between error in morals and deeds, and in dogmas of faith, to be defined in the Chair. But the vanity of this distinction has been shown elsewhere. Compare more in the Analysis on Luke 22:31.

Latin:

v. 22. Ἵλεώς σοι Κύριε. Formula deprecandi & aversandi, in LXX. Interpp. vers. usitata 1. Paral. 11, 19. 2. Sam. 23, 16. Sensus est: Propitius est tibi Deus. q. d. magis propitius est, quàm ut tale quid tibi accidat. Sic Gen. 42. v. 23.ἵλεως ὑμῖν, μή φοβεῖσθε. Ubi necessariò subaudiendum nomen Deus. Rectè ergo quoad sententiam reddidit Vulgatus: Absit à te Domine, non erit tibi hoc.1. Macc. 2, 21. *[Conf. B. D. Glass Gr. S. p. 637. Nic. Fullerus l. 2. Misc. c. 2. Similia porrò exempla erroris humanae mentis ex ignoratione consilii divini vid. 2. Sam. 7. 1. 2. 3.Matth. 3, 14.Ioh. 13, 6. Coeterùm rectè existo Petri errore (de quo Ambrosius in Ps. 118.Errabat, scribit, Petrus in tenebris ignorantiae, negabat, Christum esse moriturum, quia adhuc non credebat moriturum, & resurrecturum.) rectè colligunt Orthodoxi, quòd per verba Salvatoris: Tu es Petrus &c. non absolutè acceperit infallibilitatis donum. Ut adeò ineptè PP. RR. qui se Petri successores falsò venditant, eo se instructos esse glorientur. Evolvantur quae in rem hanc leguntur apud B. D. Chemnitium Harm. Evang. c. 86. p. 948. Marcum Anton. de Dominis t. 1. de Rep. Eccl. l. 1. c. 6. p. 59. Est verò Petri lapsus ac error adeò manifestus, ut licet nonnulli Pontificii excusare, & immunem ab omni erore Petrum satagant, Iesuita tamen Conzenius vi veritatis convictus fateatur, non excusandum esse Petrum, Comm. in h. l. q. 1. ad v. 22. Monet idem, quemadmodum & Bell. t. 1. l. 1.

de p. R c. 28. quòd errarit Petrus sensu, non affectu. Admittimus distinctionem, quâ Hieronymus quoque utitur, sed negamus, quòd per hoc liberetur Petrus ab errore. Quod nobis sufficit. Tirinus h. l. dist. inter errorem in moribus ac factis, & in dogmatibus fidei, in Cathedrâ definiendis. Sed vanitas huius distinct. alibi ostensa. Conf. plura in Anal. ad Luc. 22, 31.)*

## 16:23
v. 23. Get behind me Satan. The phrase seems taken from 2 Sam. 19:22. where David says to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, persuading him to kill Shimei: What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah, that you become to me this day a Satan? [See Glassius, Sacred Rhetoric, p. 221, discussing this expression at greater length. Hilary in this place maintains that the Lord, having turned to him through whom that opinion was suggested, namely the Devil, added: Satan, you are a scandal to me: since it is not fitting to think that the name of Satan and the offense of scandal are attributed to Peter after those so great proclamations of blessedness and power granted to him. But however much this opinion may seem to favor the Papists, it is nevertheless abandoned by the Jesuit Pineda in ch. 1, v. 6. of Job, no. 8, just as it is also in this place by Corn. à Lapide, who also notes that all other interpreters join τὸ Satan with get behind me, and judge the whole thing to have been said to Peter. The same man also rightly observes, that Peter is called Satan, insofar as, receding from God, he was following human affection. Let the Jesuit therefore grant to us also, that we rightly salute the Roman Pontiff as a slave of Satan and Antichrist, since in his decrees he recedes very far from God, exalts himself above all that is called God, and indulges himself excessively in human affections, pride, avarice, and tyranny. To which fact very many Papist writers could be brought as witnesses. B. Par. sets forth some testimonies in Book on the Church, § 263. Compare the same in Catholic Confession, vol. 2, p. 604, following.]

Satan. שטו signifies an adversary to the Hebrews, whence Christ calls Peter Satan, because he was opposing the divine counsel with human affection. Origen observes that , [ὕπααγε ὀοσ ου, is said to Peter in this place, but , [ὕπααγε ὀοσ ου, is said simply to the Devil Matt. 4:10, and behind me is not added, because it is of obedience to go behind Christ. Some take it in a special signification, as if Peter by this dissuasion had shown himself similar and obedient to an evil spirit. For the Evangelist retained the Hebrew appellation, but he could have expressed the general signification with the word ἀντικείμθοος or ἀντίδικος. That counsel, that Christ ought to spare Himself, and not fulfill the will of GOD, was from the suggestion of Satan. *(Pineda treats more prolixly of the various acceptation of the word Satan at c. 1. Iobi v. 6. n. 8. who can be consulted. But Mr. Dr. Walther rightly warns in Cent. Miscell. Theol. c. 70. that the name Satan is not taken properly here, but appellatively for any adversary whatsoever.)*

*[ Σκάνδαλον μου εὶ. But Christ cannot be scandalized, nor did Peter have in mind to scandalize Christ. Resp. Holy Scripture does not always estimate scandals and seductions from the mind of the one scandalizing, but from the thing itself, that is, because a person in reality speaks and does something, which can seduce and scandalize another. Similar examples are had at 1. Ioh. 2, 26.c. 3, 7. See B. Par. L on Original Sin §. 37.)*

Οὐ φρονεῖς του θεοῦ. You do not savor the things that are of GOD. σὐ φρονεῖν τὰ του θεοῦ is nothing else than not to estimate things from the decree and will of GOD, but from the sense of the flesh and the judgment of men. Theoph. ἐ οὐρ Casaub.

Latin:

v. 23. Abipost me Satana. Phrasis desumta videtur ex 2. Sam. 19, 22. ubi David ad Abisai filium Serviae, suadentem ut Simei interficeret, dicit: Quid mihi & vobis, filii Se-uiae, quia efficimini mihi hodie in Satan? *[Vide pluribus hac de locutione differentem Glassium Rhet. S. p. 221. Hilarius in h. l. statuit, quod in eum, per quem opinio ista suggerebatur, nempe Diabolum, conversus Dominus adiecerit: Satana scandalum mihi es: cùm non conveniat existimare, Petro Satanae nomen & offensionem scandali deputari post illa indultae & beatitudinis & potestatis tanta praeconia. Verùm ut ut haec sententia favere Pontificiis videatur, deseritur tamen à Iesuita Pineda in c. 1. v. 6. Iobi n. 8. quemadmodum etiam h. l. à Corn. à Lapide, qui notat quoq;, coeteros Interpp omnes τὸSatana iungere cum vade post me, totumque Petro dictum arbitrari. Idem etiam rectè observat, quòd Petrus Satan dicatur, quatenus à Deo recedens humanum sequebatur affectum. Concedat ergò & nobis Iesuita, quòd Pontificem Romanum rectè salutemus Satanae mancipium & AntiChristum, cùm in suis ille decretis Iongissimè à Deo recedat, supra omne id, quod dicitur Deus, sese efferat, ac humanis affectibus, superbiae, avaritiae, ac tyrannidi nimium quantum indulgeat. Cuius rei testes plurimi Pontificii Scriptores possent adduci. Sistit connulla testimonia B. Par. L. de Eccl. §. 263. Conf. idem Confess. Cathol. t. 2. p. 604. seqq)*

Satan.שטו Hebraeis significat adversarium, unde Christus Petrum vocat Satanam, quòd affectu humano adversaretur consilio divino. Origenes observat, Petro hoc loco dici , [ὕπααγε ὀοσ ου, sed Diabolo Matth. 4, 10. simpliciter dici , [ὕπααγε ὀοσ ου, nec addi post me, quòd obedientiae sit, ire post Christum. Quidam accipiunt in significatione speciali, quasi Petrus hâc dissuasione Cacodaemoni similem & obsequentem se praebuerit. Evangelista enim retinuit appellationem Ebraeam, generalem verò significationem exprimere potuisset vocabulo ἀντικείμθοος vel ἀντίδικος. Consilium illud, quòd Christus debeat sibi parcere, nec implere voluntatem DEI, erat ex Satanae suggestione. *(De variâ acceptione vocis Satanas prolixiùs agit Pineda ad c. 1. Iobi v. 6. n. 8. qui potest consuli. Rectè autem monet Dn. D. Waltherus in Cent. Miscell. Theol. c. 70. nomen Satanae non propriè hîc accipi, sed appellativè pro quô vis adversario.)*

*[ Σκάνδαλον μου εὶ. Atqui Christus non potest scandalizari, nec Petrus habuit in animo Christum scandalizare. Resp. Scriptura S. scandala & seductiones non semper aestimat ex animo scandalizandi, sed ex reipsâ, h. e. quia persona reverâ aliquid loquitur & facit, quod alterum seducere & scandalizare potest. Exempla similia habentur 1. Ioh. 2, 26.c. 3, 7. Vid. B. Par. L de Pecc. Orig. §. 37.)*

Οὐ φρονεῖς του θεοῦ.Non sapis ea, quae sunt DEI.σὐ φρονεῖν τὰ του θεοῦ nihil est aliud, quàm res non aestimare ex decreto & voluntate DEI, sed ex sensu carnis & hominum iudicio. Theoph. ἐ οὐρ Casaub.

## 16:24
v. 24. Let him deny himself. What it is to deny himself, is understood from the occasion of this saying, namely, to put off carnal affections, by which he desires the comforts of this life, and to put on spiritual affections, by which he seeks the glory of GOD, to renounce his own honor, his own will, his own comforts, to lay aside confidence and admiration of his own wisdom, and righteousness, and to glory in Christ alone, 1. Cor. 1. *(Compare 2. Cor. 10, 5.Gal. 5, 24. which explanation, since it leans on the suffrage of Holy Scripture, and is approved even by Thomas Aquinas himself in this place, as one who explicitly says: Then we leave and deny ourselves, when we avoid what we were through oldness, and strive toward that to which we are called through newness. just as also the Jesuit Corn. à Lapide rightly writes in this place: He commands, (the Savior) that one should lay aside, mortify, and cut off his own affections and natural and sensual loves, repugnant to the law and will of God, and should take up, put on, and follow in all things the law and will of God. Conformably to the other Cornelius, namely Jansenius, formerly Bishop of Ghent in Conc. Ev. in this place, but this denial by all s. to all the faithful it is required, as Cornelius rightly advises in the said place, from everyone, who wishes to be a true disciple of Christ and to become a citizen of the kingdom of heaven, which is preached and promised by Christ, as Franc. Lucas Brugensis, Dean of the Church of Saint-Omer, comments in this place, it is evident that Cardinal Bellarmine is inept, while he restricts this most sweet sentiment of the Savior and most wholesome admonition, concerning absolutely all who desire to become heirs of heaven at some time, to Monks and Nuns alone; and from thence he strives to establish Monastic obedience, concerning which, however, insofar as it is distinguished from the obedience of other Christians, not even γρυ is held in this place. Nor does the passage Matth. 19, 2127. make for this. For he distinguishes between the general following of Christ, (that is, common to all Christians, consisting indeed in the imitation of Christ, which is commanded to all, see 1. Cor. 11, 1.Ephes. 5, 1.1. Petr. 2, 21. August. book 8 de C. D. ch. 17. the sum of the Christian religion is to imitate him whom you worship. Bernhard has similar things in sermon 21 on the Song of Songs 550. Paulinus ep. 2 to Sulp. Conf. B. Par. Aphor. Pract. title imitation of Christ. and this following is treated here, as is evident from the context, especially v. 25. add. ch. 10, 38. 39. Luc. 24, 27. whence Bellarmine himself also confesses, that in this place it is a matter of the obedience which is necessarily owed to God;) and between the special following of Christ if personal, which is commanded to some at least, concerning which it is treated in Matth. 19, 21.27.c. 9, 9.Marc. 9, 38.Luc. 8, 59. But that this personal one is not commanded to all is evident from Marc. 5, 18.Luc. 9, 58. But how neither can Monastic obedience be established from this special one will be shown in the Analysis to Matth. 19, 21. Compare also more things making for this in B. Par. Conf. Cath. vol. 3 book 2 spec. art. 7. ch. 1 and 4.)

Let him take up his cross. Piscator thinks that by the name σταυρὸν is understood here a gallows, but it is a Synecdochical word, through which it is hinted that Christ sanctified our calamities by his own cross. *(Likewise this admonition of the Savior, just like the one immediately preceding, regards all Christians, as Corn. à Lapide rightly observes in this place where among other things: Luke, he writes, adds, daily, to signify that every day and often every hour something troublesome will occur TO ANYONE, and so forth. as therefore ANYONE must live on the cross. And again to the word his. that is. firstly his own proper one, FOR TO EACH his own is proper cross-: one from a wife, children etc. Therefore this invitation of Christ does not concern only the religious, as they are called, as the Jesuit Bailius in Catech. Controv. tr. 2. q. 23. Bellarm. vol. 2. Controv. book 2 on Monks ch. 21. § Second, and perhaps also Costerus in Enchir. Controv. ch. 7. p. 286. persuade themselves. But it is a general admonition, by which Christ exhorts all, that they should not impatiently cast away the cross sent by God as if it were a medicine sent in, as Corn. à Lapide speaks, not drawn on by one's own will, much less seized by an opinion of merit, (such as that of the religious,) but that they should patiently and bravely tolerate it, certain that God will not allow us to be tempted beyond what we are able, as Paul testifies 1. Cor. 10, 13. Furthermore, concerning the benefit of tribulation, it is treated more lengthily elsewhere. Nor yet from the fact that all Christians must submit themselves to the burden of the cross do the Anabaptists rightly infer, that a Christian Magistrate ought not to draw the sword against criminals, since Christ handed over not the sword, but the cross to his own. Resp. Things that are subordinate ought not to be opposed. For one can patiently take up the cross sent by God, and likewise bear the sword, if indeed it was girded upon him by God as a public person Rom. 13, 6. Sim. Episcopius vol. 2 Op. page 87 also shows this same thing at length, and thus he sacrifices little here to the Photinians, to whom he is otherwise too much addicted.)*

Latin:

v. 24. Abneget seipsum. Quid sit seipsum abnegare, intel ligitur ex occasione huius dicti, videl. exuere carnales affectus, quibus desiderat huius vitae commoda, & induere spirituales affectus, quibus quaerat gloriam DEI, renunciare suo honori, suae voluntati, suis commodis, deponere fiduciam & admirationem propriae sapientiae, & iustitiae & gloriari in solo Christo, 1. Cor. 1. *(Conf. 2. Cor. 10, 5.Gal. 5, 24. quae explicatio cùm nitatur Scripturae S. suffragio, & approbetur etiam ipsi Thomae de Aquino in h l. ut qui disertè. Tum nosmet ipsos relinquimus & abnegamus, cùm vitamus, quod per vetustatem fuimus, & ad hoc nitimur, ad quod per novitatem vocamur. quemadmodum etiam iesuita Corn. à Lapide rectè in h. l. scribit: Iubet, (Salvator) ut quissuos affectus & amores naturales & sensuales, Dei legi & voluntati repugnantes, deponat, mortificet & resecet, ac Dei legem & voluntatem adsumat, induat & per omnia sequatur. Conformiter alteri Cornelio, puta Iansenio, Episcopo quondam Gandavensi in Conc. Ev. h. l. haec verò abnegatio ab omnibus s. quibusvis fidelibus requiratur, uti rectè monet Cornelius d. l. s. ab unoquoque, qui verus Christi vult esse discipulus ac civis fieri regni coelorum, quod à Christo praedicatur & promittitur, uti in h. l. commentatur Franc. Lucas Brugensis, Ecclesiae Audomerop. Decanus, patet, quòd ineptus sit Cardinalis Bellarminus, dum suavissiman hanc sententiam Salvatoris & saluberrimum monitum, omnes omninò concernens, qui coeli haeredes aliquando fieri gestiunt, ad solos Monachos Moniales-; restringit, indeq; obedientiam Monasticam stabilire satagit, de quâ tamen quatenus ab aliorum Christianorum obedientiâ distinguitur, ne γρυ quidem h. l. habetur. Nec facit huc locus Matth. 19, 2127. Disting. enim inter sequelam Christi generalem,(h. e. omnibus Christianis communem, consistentem quippe in Christi imitatione, quae omnibus mandata, vid. 1. Cor. 11, 1.Ephes. 5, 1.1. Petr. 2, 21. August. l. 8. de C. D. c. 17. summa religionis Christianae est, imitari eum, quem colis. Similia habent Bernhardus serm. 21. in Cant Cant. 550. Paulinus ep. 2. ad Sulp. Conf. B. Par. Aphor. Pract. tit. Christi imitatio. atq; de hac sequela hîc agitur, ceu ex contextu patet, cumprimis v. 25. add. c. 10, 38. 39. Luc. 24, 27. unde etiam Bell. ipse fatetur, quòd h. l. agatur de obedientiâ, quae necessariò debetur Deo;) & inter sequelam Christi specialem si personali, quae aliquibus saltem mandata, de quâ agitur Matth. 19, 21.27.c. 9, 9.Marc. 9, 38.Luc. 8, 59. Quod verò haec personalis non omnibus mandata sit, patet ex Marc. 5, 18.Luc. 9, 58. Sed quomodo nec ex hac speciali obedientia Monastica stabiliri queat, ostendetur in Anal. ad Matth. 19, 21. Conf. etiam plura huc facientia apud B. Par. Conf. Cath. t. 3. l. lib. 2. spec. art. 7. c. 1 & 4.)*

Tollat crucem suam. Piscator existimat, nomine σταυρὸν hîc intelligi patibulum, sed est vox Synecdochica, per quam innuitur, Christum sua cruce nostras calamitates sanctificâsse. *(Itidem monitum hoc Salvatoris, uti proximè praecedens, omnes Christianos respicit, uti rectè observat Corn. à Lapide in h. l. ubi inter alia: Lucas, scribit, addit, quotidiè, ut significet, omni die & saepè omni horâ aliquid molesti CUILIBET occursurum, &c. as proinde CUILIBET vivendum esse in cruce. Et iterum ad vocem suam. id est. primò sibi propriam, CUIQUE enim sua propria est cru-: uni ab uxore, filiis &c. Non solos igitur religiosos, quos vocant, invitatio haec Christi concernit, ceu Iesuita quidem Bailius in Catech. Controv. tr. 2. q. 23. Bellarm. t. 2. Controv. lib. 2. de Monach. c. 21. § Secunda, ac fortè etiam Costerus in Enchir. Controv. c. 7. p. 286. sibi persuadent. Sed est generale monitum, quo Christus omnes hortatur, ne crucem divinitùs quasi medicinam immissam, ut loquitur Corn. à Lapide, non sponte attractam, multò minùs opinione meriti arreptam, (qualis illa religiosorum,) impatienter abiiciant, sed patienter ac fortiter tolerent, certi, quòd Deus non passurus sit, nos tentari super id, quod possumus, teste Paulo 1. Cor. 10, 13. Coeterum de tribulationis commodo alibi prolixiùs actū. Neque tamen ex eo, quòd omnes Christiani crucis oneri sese submittere debent, rectè inferunt Anabaptistae, quòd Christianus Magistratus non debeat stringere gladium in facinorosos, siquidem Christus non gladium, sed crucem suis tradiderit. Resp. Non sunt opponenda, quae sunt subordinata. Potest enim quis crucem à Deo immissam patienter suscipere, ac pariter gerere gladium, si nempe illi ut personae publicae à Deo is fuerit accinctus Rom. 13, 6. Idem hoc prolixè quoque ostendit, adeoque Photinianis parum hîc litat, aliàs nimiùm illis addictus Sim. Episcopius t. 2. Op. pag. 87.)*

## 16:25
(v. 25. For whoever wishes to save his soul i.e. his natural life, by denying me, so that he may not be killed, will lose it, i.e. he will nevertheless die at some point, and will suffer the loss of eternal life, on account of his denying me. But it does not follow that the denial of Christ is the meritorious cause of damnation, therefore the confession of Christ and perseverance on the cross is the meritorious cause of eternal life. For although patience is necessary for us, and God has promised to reward constancy and patience on the cross most generously, it is not to be immediately inferred: Therefore we merit eternal life by constancy on the cross, since there is no comparison between the afflictions of this time and the heavenly glory, 2. Cor. 4, 17. Rom. 8, 18. Whence also the Apostle expressly declares that eternal life is χάρισμα του Θεοῦ, Rom. 6, last.)

Latin:

*(v. 25. Qui enim voluerit animam suam servare i. e. vitam suam naturalem, me sc. abnegando, ne interficiatur, perdet eā, h. e. nihilominus aliquando morietur, vitaeq; aeternae, propter mei sc. abnegationem, iacturam faciet. Non verò sequitur, abnegatio Christi est causa damnationis meritoria, ergò confessio Christi ac perseverantia in cruce est vitae aeternae causa meritoria. Etenim licet patientia nobis necessaria sit, Deus etiam constantiam & patientiam in cruce largissimè remunerari promiserit, non tamen statim inferendum. E. meremur constantiâ in cruce vitam aeternam, cùm nulla fit comparatio inter afflictiones huius temporis ad gloriam coelestem, 2. Cor. 4, 17.Rom. 8, 18. Unde etiam Apostolus disertè pronunciat, quòd vitaaet. sit χάρισμα του Θεοῦ,Rom. 6, ult.]*

## 16:26
v. 26. If he shall have gained the whole world. The word world is either taken hyperbolically for the whole structure of the world, or metonymically for all things which are judged precious in this world, such as pleasures, honors, riches, power. *(Beautifully Augustine in Enarr. Ps. 48. They who store up treasures on earth are like those who hide their crops in low and damp places, not noticing that it will come to pass from this that they will rot most quickly. The passages Matth. 6, 19. Iac. 5, 1. 2. 3. also make for this. Bernard on Conversion to the Clergy c. 15. Would that only the things gathered perished, and that the gatherer of them did not also perish worse; it would surely be more tolerable to toil for a labor that is about to perish than for one that is destructive &c.)*

*( If he shall have gained the whole world &c. Conf. Psal. 62, 11. above c 6, 20. 21. Phil. 3, last. Thus therefore let us use these earthly things, so that they may be for us in use, the heavenly in desires. See 1. Cor. 7, 31. Col. 3, 1. &c. Conf. entirely B. P. L. on the Consummation of the age §. 103.)*

*( He shall render to each according to κατὰ τὴν πραξι αυτου. If God is about to render to each according to works. Therefore in conferring the reward, account is not held of the mere promise or liberality, or indulgence of GOD, but also of the dignity and efficacy of the works, exclaims Card. Bell. l. 5. on Justification c. 3. His associates agree, Pererius Disp. 5. in c. 2. Rom. n. 39. Conzen. both in this place and in the epistle to the Romans q. 1. to c. 2, 6. But we answer and oppose to the Cardinal with his troop the Roman Pontiff, whose infallibility as they boast, so they will not evade his authority. He indeed is Gregory the Great who in Ps. 7. of the penitential psalms, It is one thing, he writes, to render according to works, another to render according to the merits of works, or to render because of works. And the matter is manifest. For Τὸ to render according to works denotes the testimony of works, τὸ to render because of works denotes their merit. Especially however it is to be noted here, that not only election and justification are done out of grace, as is evident from Rom. 3, 24. c. 4, 4. Ephes. 2, 8. 9. but even eternal life itself is called ξάρισμα του θεοῦ, Rom. 6, last. Whence also merit is denied to all works of the reborn, Luc. 17, 7. Conf. also Roman. 8, 18. &c. Parallel passages are Matth. 25, 34. seqq. Apoc. 22, 12. Ioh. 5, 29. 2. Cor. 5, 10. Sirac. 16, 12. Therefore τὸ according to does not infer dignity or merit. See those dealing more fully with this matter B. D. Chemn in Harm. Ev. c. 86. B. Par.

Confess. Cath. t. 4. p. 877. seqq. it. L. de B. O. §. 115. Annot. in Epist. ad Rom. c. 2, 9. Lord D. Weller on this passage. The Calvinists Camero on this passage and Grossius in his Theatrum Biblicum have also vindicated this passage. Furthermore, since the power of judging the world is attributed to Christ as man in this passage, the Orthodox rightly conclude that Majesty and glory, truly divine, and therefore also omnipotence, have been conferred upon Him according to His human nature. This is what the Jesuits today, along with the Calvinists, deny, as is evident from Corn. à Lapide on this passage. Camero objects in Myroth. page 44, that by the son of man in this passage, as elsewhere also, the human nature of Christ is not understood, but the person adorned with the Mediatorial office, and that it is not signified thereby that the human nature of Christ was endowed with infinite power, but only this, that the person adorned with that office was endowed with infinite power to judge all men. Namely, that to Christ the Mediator, who is neither simply man, nor even simply God, but θεαύθρωπος,, infinite power was given. Wendelinus, Exercit. 130. §. 1. seqq., attempts to escape the force of this passage in almost the same way. But even if we easily grant that the person who will administer the judgment is not a mere man, but θεαύθρωπον,, nevertheless our assertion is not infringed, that, since that power of administering judgment is infinite, as it includes omniscience and omnipotence, and that power was given to Christ ὄτι ιἱς ἀνθρώπου ὐςί, Ioh. 5, 27., that is, because he is the son of man, namely according to his human nature, since nothing divine can be given in time, and the Son of man is to administer judgment in the glory of the Father, which is a glory altogether divine and infinite, power truly divine and infinite was given to Christ as man, namely to the human nature of Christ. But the Lords Theologians of Marburg treat of this passage at greater length in Fundam. Deduct. page 224 seqq., B. Schröterus in Sceptro Regali book 1, ch. 11, p. 163 seqq., also p. 276, B. D. Chemnitius in his treatise on the two natures in Christ, ch. 24, page 129, also p. 102, 108, 132, 140, 169, B. Par. Exeg. L. on the person and office of Christ §. 205, which, if they are well considered, it will easily appear what should be thought of the exceptions of Wendelinus proposed in Exerc. 130. Cyril beautifully says in book 2 on Ioh. c. 144. Christ has submitted the cause, why he said that life and the power of judgment were given to him by the Father, because he is the Son of man, so that we may understand that all things were given to him as man. But the Only-begotten Son is not a partaker of life, but is life by nature. Meanwhile, from that assertion, that this infinite glory was communicated to Christ as man, it does not follow that the argument which the ancients drew from this for the true Deity of Christ is undermined: For unless divine majesty belonged to Christ essentially according to His Deity, it could not have been communicated personally to the assumed human nature. Whence we entirely embrace that statement of Chrysostom, hom. 56 in Matth., when he says to the words: the son of man is to come in the glory of the Father, thus: εἶδες πῶς And a little later: φῶς To which Isidore of Pelusium, book 3, ep. 166, has things altogether twin.)*

v. 26. Si totum mundum lucratus fuerit. Vocabulum mundi vel accipitur hyperbolicè pro tota mundi compage, vel metonymicè pro omnibus, quae in hoc mundo iudicantur preciosa, ut sunt voluptates, honores, divitiae, potentia. *(Pulcrè August. in Enarr.
