*( Reddet unicuisecundùmκατὰ τὴν πραξι αυτου.Si secundùm opera Deus unicuiredditurus. E. in praemio conferendo non habetur ratio solius promissionis vel liberalitatis, vel indulgentiae DEI, sed etiam dignitatis & efficaciae operum, exclamat Card. Bell. l. 5. de Iustif. c. 3. Adstipulantur socienni, Pererius Disp. 5. in c. 2. Rom. n. 39. Conzen. tum h. l. tum in ep. ad Rom. q. 1. ad c. 2, 6. Verùm respondemus opponimus que Cardinali cum suâ catervâ Pontificem Romanum, cuius infallibilitatem uti iactitant, ita autoritatem non subterfugient. Is verò est Gregorius M. qui in Ps. 7. poenit. Aliud est, scribit, secundùm opera reddere, aliud secundùm merita operum, vel propter opera reddere. Et res manifesta est. Τὸ enim secundùm opera reddere notat operum testimonium,τὸpropter opera reddere notat eorum meritum. Cumprimis verò hîc notandum, quòd non solùm electio & iustificatio ex gratiâ fiant, ceu constat ex Rom. 3, 24.c. 4, 4.Ephes. 2, 8. 9. sed ipsa etiam vita aeterna dicatur ξάρισμα του θεοῦ,Rom. 6, ult. Unde etiam omnibus renatorum operibus meritum denegatur, Luc. 17, 7. Conf. etiam Roman. 8, 18. &c. Loca parall. sunt Matth. 25, 34. seqq. Apoc. 22, 12.Ioh. 5, 29.2. Cor. 5, 10.Sirac. 16, 12. E. τὸsecundùm non infert dignitatem vel meritum. Vid. pluribus hâc de re agentes B. D. Chemn in Harm. Ev. c. 86. B. Par.

Confess. Cath. t. 4. p. 877. seqq. it. L. de B. O. §. 115. Annot. in Epist. ad Rom. c. 2, 9. Dn. D. Weller. in d. l. Vindicarunt quoque hunc locum è Calvinianis Camero in h. l. Grossius in Theatro Bibl. Porrò cùm Christo homini h. l. tribuatur potestas iudicandi mundum, rectè colligunt Orthodoxi, quòd ipsi secundùm humanam naturam collata sit Maiestas ac gloria verè divina, adeoque & omnipotentia. Id quod cum Calvinianis hodiè Iesuitae negant. ut patet ex Corn. à Lapide in h. l. Excipit Camero in Myroth. pag. 44. per filium hominis h. l. ut alibi etiam, non intelligi naturam Christi humanam, sed personam munere Mediatorio ornatam, neque eo significari, naturam humanam Christi potestate infinitâ esse donatam, sed hoc duntaxat, personam eo munere ornatam, potestate iudicandi omnes homines infinita esse praeditam. Christo nempe Mediatori, qui neque est simpliciter homo, neque etiam simpliciter Deus, sed θεαύθρωπος, datam esse potestatem infinitam. Eôdem propè modô effugere vim h. l. conatur Wendelinus Exercit. 130. §. 1. seqq. Verùm ut ut facilè largiamur, personam, quae iudicium administrabit, non esse nudum hominem, sed θεαύθρωπον, exinde tamen non infringitur nostra adsertio, quòd, cùm potestas illa iudicium administrandi sit infinita, quippe includens omniscientiam & omnipotentiā, illa verò Christo data sit ὄτι ιἱς ἀνθρώπου ὐςί,Ioh. 5, 27. h. e. quat. filius hominis est s. secundùm humanam naturam, cùm divinae nihil possit in tempore dari, ac Filius hominis sit administraturus iudicium in gloria Patris, quae divina omninò ac infinita gloria est, Christo homini s. humanae Christi naturae data sit potestas verè divina & infinita. Sed pluribus de h. l. agunt Dnn. Theologi Marpurg. in Fundam. Deduct. pag. 224. seqq. B. Schrōterus in sceptro Regali l. 1. c. 11 p. 163. seqq. it. p. 276. B. D. Chemnitius tr. de duabus naturis in Christo c. 24. pag. 129. it. p. 102. 108. 132. 140. 169. B. Par. Exeg. L. de pers. & off. Chr. §. 205. quae si benè suerint considerata, facilè apparebit, quid de Wendelini exceptionibus, Exerc. 130. propositis, habendum sit. Pulcrè Cyrillus l. 2. in Ioh. c. 144.Christus causam subiecit, quare vitam & potestatem iudicii sibi à Patre datam dixerit, quia Filius hominis est, ut intelligamus, omnia sibi data esse, ut homini. Unigenitus verò Filius, non vitae particeps, sed vita naturaliter est. Intereà per adsertionem illam, quòd Christo homini ista gloria infinita communicata sit, non sequitur, quòd labefactetur argumentum, quòd veteres pro verâ Christi Deitate hinc depromservnt: Etenim nisi Christo secundùm Deitatem maiestas divina essentialiter competeret, non potuisset eadem adsumtae humanae naturae personaliter communicari. Unde amplectimur omninò illud Chrysostomi hom. 56. in Matth. quando ad verba: venturus est filius hominis in gloria Patris, ita: εἶδες πῶς Et paulò pòst: φῶς Quibus prorsus gemella habet Isid. Pelusiota l. 3. ep. 166.)*

## 16:28
v. 28. Until they see the Son of man &c. Theophylact explains that this was said concerning Peter, James, and John, to whom he exhibited in the transfiguration a certain specimen of his glory and kingdom. *(Others along with the Ancients embrace this, such as Chrysostom, Euthymius, Hilary, Jerome, Ambrose; among our own, the blessed D. Chemnitz in the Harmony, the Lord D. Friedlieb, and the blessed D. Hunnius on this passage. Among the Papists, Maldonatus, Corn. à Lapide or others. Lyranus and Thomas Aquinas likewise understand it in the same way. Yet, all these being set aside, the Jesuit Conzen wishes these words of Christ to be taken entirely concerning the coming of Christ to the final judgment.)* Others take that coming of Christ in his kingdom to mean the glory and power of the resurrection from death and the divine efficacy of the evangelical proclamation. There are those who take it to mean the mission of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost. However, the two latter expositions can be joined, so that the kingdom of grace is denoted, which, having begun at Jerusalem in the New Testament from Christ's resurrection, reached into all parts of the world. *(In this way, besides Gregory and Bede, the blessed D. Glass in Philologia Sacra, page 526, also explains it. In the Ernestine Bibles, the first and second opinions are joined and approved, and the passage Mark 9, 1. is compared. What Matthew says ἕως αν ἴδωςι)

id Luke c. 9, 27. renders it thus: ἕως αὔ Mark c. 9, 1. γευσιν This is an anticipation of a question which could arise from the preceding. The Savior had said that He would come in the glory of the Father, and would render to each one according to his deeds. From this it could be asked, are You then about to depart from this world into heavenly glory, so that You may return from there for judgment? That, indeed, Christ answers, is so certain that some of those standing by, namely the Apostles, are to see it with their eyes. *(Conf. more things pertaining to this in the Analecta on Mark 9, 1.]

There is proposed in the present Chapter I. The transformation of Christ on the mountain. v. 1-8. II. The information of the disciples concerning the coming of Elijah. v. 9-13. III. The healing of the lunatic v. 14-18. And the instruction of the Apostles as to why they themselves could not cure him v. 19-21. IV. The prediction of the passion, death & resurrection of Christ v. 22-23. V. The payment of the tribute, v. 24 to the end.
