Quia verò in ipsa vita aeterna distinctè fulgebunt lumina meritorum (i. e. operum) mansiones multae sunt apud Patrem, in quibus honoratur alius -lio clariùs. Conf. B. P. L. de vita aet. §. 128. ac 131. 3. Scopus Christi est, in parabola hâ ostendere, vitam aet. esse gratuitum DEI donum. Probeque observat B. P. L. de B. O. §. 114. duplices operarios in hâc parabolâ nobis proponi. Quidam in operibus suis spectant mercedem, existimant que, labores suos esse dignos praemio; ideò pro maiori labore maiorem exigunt mercedem, enumerant Deo merita sua, invident proximo gratiam Dei, extollunt sese supra alios, murmurant contra patremfamilias, accusant eum iniustitiae, suâ opinione & iudicio sunt primi; illi accipiunt denarium i. e. coguntur esse contenti praemiis huius vitae. Deus enim tam beneficus est, ut nihil quicquam boni relinquat immune à praemio: sed qui volunt operibus confidere, eadem iactare &c. illi ablegantur particulâ praemiorum huius vitae, coguntur enim abire, non habent, quod de iniuriâ sibi factâ conqueri possint. Quidam verò non respiciunt in operibus suis mercedem, contenti sunt gratuitâ illa promissione patrisfamiliàs: quod iustum est, dabo vobis. Obseq-untur vocationi, strenuè laborant, serviunt Deo in simplicitate cordis sui, & sunt in oculis suis novissimi, iudicant se & opera sua non esse digna, quibus merces debeantur, committunt se totos divinae gratiae &c. illi fiunt primi, h. e. Deus suâ gratiâ eos complectitur, & pietatem eorum huius & futurae vitae praemiis ex gratiâ remuneratur. 4. Atque haec expositio analogiae fidei consentanea est. Quòd enim B. O. non sint vitae aeternae meritoria, satis patet vel ex sola adsertione Christi Luc. 17, 10. & Apostoli Rom. 6, ult. Vid. omninò Dn. D. Wellerus Comm. rum in memoratum cap. 6. ep. ad Rom. tum in c. 4, 5. p. 258. Dn. D. Friedlieb Obs. in H. E. p. 160. sequutus Dd. Lyserum, Balduinum, Meisnerum, Bakium, Erythrophilum, accipit denarium de ipsomet Christo, qui iam olim se mercedem Abrahamo futurum responderit, Gen. 15, 2. Hunc, ait, omnes accipiunt, qui per Baptismum in Ecclesiae vineam intromittuntur, Gal. 3, 27 Hunc solvit paterfamilias circa vesperam i. e. Christius venit sub mundi senectam in carnē. Nec obstare huic sententiae observat idem, quòd etiam illi, qui murmurarunt, accepisse denarium dicuntur. Cùm acceperint, quoad oblationem, non quoad applicationem. Ut adeò illis Christus factus fuerit denarius iudicii, quoniam illo, quod acceperunt non rectè usi fuerunt. Coeterùm Ioh. Paludanus D. & Prof. Lov. in Vindic. Theol. p. 233. scribit: Sciendum est, Lutherum idem adserere cum multis sectariis huius temporis, quod olim docuit Iovinianus, quod attinet ad Beatos, quos omnes pares esse etiam B. Virgini, in sanctitate & meritis coram DEO, uti Iovinianus, omnes virtutes inter se aequales faciebat. Fundamentum sectariorum hoc est, quia existimant, homines esse iustos per Christi iustitiam: non autem propriam. Praeterea omnibus, qui fidem habent, aequaliter Christi iustitiam imput ari: item aiunt, omnes accipere praemium non per propria, sed Christi merita, quae omnibus, qui fidem habent, aequaliter applicantur. Illis positis, concludit, quid mirum, si cum Ioviniano consentiant. Resp. 1. dist. inter sanctitatem Christi imputatam, quâ sola iustificamur ac salvamur, ut quae sola coram rigoroso DEI iudicio subsistere potest, & inter sanctitatem inhaerentem inchoat am, quâ licet nec iustificemur, cùm sit imperfecta multisque adhaerentibus infirmitatibu& pec-atis contaminata, nec vitam mereamur aeternam, utpote quod est donum DEI in Christo Iesu, Rom. 6. ult. add. cap. 11, 6. non tamen â nobis negat-r, quòd in uno maior ea sit, quàm in altero, adeoque posteriori hoc respectu maior fuerit sanctitas in B. Virgine, quàm in latrone -onverso, vel aliis etiam cre dentibus. 2. nec B. Lutherus de hâc, sed de priori sanctitate loquitur. Disertè enim scribit: tam B. Mariae ad gratiam (iustificantem) adspirandum fuit per Christi sanguinem, quàm nobis 3. nec sequitur, solo Christi merito fide apprehenso vitam consequimur aeternam, nec ullis nostris operibus eam promereri possumus: ergo nulli dantur g-oriae in vitâ aeternâ gradus. Etenim, uti iamtum suprà monuimus, accuratè distinguendum inter vitam aeternam s. beatitudinem ipsam, & gradum beatitudinis. Nom licet omnes pii in Christo morientes aequaliter beatitudine essentiali beati futuri sir-t; gradus tamen gloriae erunt distincti. 4. nec sequitur, nemo potest seu vitam aeternam ipsam seu gradum gloriae in vitâ aeternâ suis operibus vel iustitiâ inhaerente promereri. Ergo non dantur gloriae gradus. Siquidem, licet nec ipsa vita aeterna, nec gloriae gradus ex operum nostrorum merito obtingat, conf. Rom. 8, 18. potest tamen nihilominus accidentalis beatitudo seu gradus, gloriae variare ex liberali DEI promisso, utpote qui unicuique daturus secundùm, non propter opera,Matth 16, 27.Rom. 2, 6.2. Cor. 5, 10.Apoc. 22, 12.1. Cor. 3, 8. Fundamentum diversitatis gloriae non quaerendum in meritoriâ operum nostrorum dignitate, sed in gratuita DEI liberalitate. 5. Atque hanc ipsissimam B. Lutheri nostri mentem ac sententiam esse, clarè patet ex eiusdem explic. c. 15. prioris ad Cor. t. 6. Ienensi p. 256. 261. Pulcrè Augustinus lib. de Grat. & L. A. c. 9. Gratia DEI vita aeterna, ut intelligeremus, non pro meritis nostris, Deum nos ad vitam aeternam, sed pro suâ misericordiâ perducere. Conf. idem in Ps. 32. Prosper Aquitanicus l. 1. de vocat. gent. c. 5. Non labori pretium solvit, sed divitias bonitatis suae in eos, quos sine operibus eligit, effundit, ut etiam ii, qui multo labore sudarunt, nec amplius quàm novissimi acceperunt, intelligant, donum se gratiae, non operum accepisse mercedem.)*

## 20:11
(v. 11. They murmured against the master of the house. Cornelius à Lapide, following Salmeron, Suarez, Vasquez, and several other Papists, takes murmurare here for to wonder, and thus thinks it is signified that the Saints of the Old Testament, since they knew that they had labored more than others (suppose the faithful in the New Testament, as those who excelled in greater grace and spirit), would wonder that they, being lesser than these in glory, were here preferred to them in glory. But it is entirely unusual in Holy Scripture for murmurare to be put for to wonder, and it is well to be noted that it is expressly said here that they murmured against the master of the house. By whom it is certain that God is indicated here. Indeed, even if the word διγγαζειν placed absolutely might seem sometimes to be taken in a better sense, as in John 6:41, yet with the preposition χατὰ against, towards, I doubt whether it is ever used otherwise than in a bad sense. To which must be referred that which the Apostle 1. Cor. 10, 10. expressly prohibits that. Conf. Act. 6, 1.Philipp. 2, 14.1. Petr. 4, 9. Whence also Chrysost. judges that murmuring is at least an emblem of the parable; but the Gloss notes that not all murmured, but at least the wicked, who did not bring to an end the good which they had begun, and therefore, deprived of the reward, they murmur. The Jesuit Tirinus also, otherwise strenuously following in the footsteps of Cornelius, abandons the explanation of Cornelius. And in a similar sense he advises that Christ says in verse 31 of the following chapter: Publicans and harlots shall go before you into the kingdom of GOD. and Luke 13, 29. They shall come from the East &c. Now indeed the Pharisees, of whom the following chapter speaks, and those whom He says will be cast out Luke 13. did not marvel at the divine ordination and liberality but rather were indignant &c. Furthermore, those also are murmurers who show themselves impatient in adversities, and securely indulge in their sins. Such are certainly rightly deprived of the denarius of eternal life promised. But if indeed we have fallen from this denarius through sins, let us not be idle, but with that woman Luke 15, 6. let us diligently seek it again, with true faith, serious repentance, a holy life &c.

Latin:

*(v. 11. Murmurabant adversùs patremfamilias. Corn. à Lapide sequutus Salmeronem, Suarezium, Vasquez ac alios nonnullos Pontificios ΤῸ murmurare hîc accipit pro admirari, adeoque id significari putat, quòd Sancti V. T. cùm scirent, se plus laborasse, quàm alios (puta fideles in N. T. ut qui maiori excelluerunt gratiâ & spiritu-,) minores tamen his esse in gloriâ, miraturi sint, illos sibi in gloriâ, hîc anteponi. Verùm prorsus insolens est in Sc. S., murmurare poni pro admirari, ac probè notandum est, disertè hîc dici, quòd murmarint adversùs patremfamilias. Per quem Deum hîc indicari, certum est. Sanè si vel maximè verbum διγγαζειν absolutè positum in meliorem accipi quandoque partem videatur, uti Ioh. 6, 41. cum praepositione tamen χατὰcontra, adversùs, dubito, an ullibi aliter, quàm in malam adhibeatur partem. Quo referendum, quòd Apostolus 1. Cor. 10, 10. disertè illud prohibeat. Conf. Act. 6, 1.Philipp. 2, 14.1. Petr. 4, 9. Unde etiam Chrysost. censet, quòd murmur saltem sit emblema parabolae; Glossa verò notat, quòd non omnes murmurarint, sed saltem mali, qui bonum, quod inceperant, ad finem non perduxerunt, ideo que praemio privati murmurent. Iesuita quoque Tirinus, strenuè aliàs Cornelii vestigia premens, explicationem Cornelii deserit. ac pari sensu cap. sequentis v. 31. Christum dicere monet: Publicani & meretrices praecedent vos in regnum DEI. & Lucae 13, 29.Venient ab Oriente &c. Iam. verò Pharisaei, de quibus cap. seq. ac illi, quos eiectum iri dicit Luc. 13. non admirabantur divinam ordinationē ac liberalitatem sed potiùs indignabantur &c. Coeterùm murmurantes quo que illi sunt, qui in adversitatibus impatientes sese praebent, & peccatis suis securè indulgent. Tales certè denario vitae aeternae promisso iure privantur. Quod si verò per peccata denario hoc exciderimus, ne simus otiosi, sed cum muliere illâ Luc. 15, 6. iterum diligenter illum quaeramus, fide verâ, poenitentiâ seriâ, vitâ sanctâ &c.)*

## 20:12
v. 12. Εποίησαν. here is taken rather for λλατςιβείν, than for έργάζεσθαι. (Furthermore, Ludov. Capellus reports in Spicil. p. 28 that a parable clearly twin to this one of our Savior is brought forward by R. Jonah in Arcano poenit., which can be read there. But how its equity stands regarding the equal distribution of the reward, when nevertheless the labor was unequal, St. Gregory Nazianzen shows in Orat. 40. p. 651. Above all but he strives to declare it at length, Cornelius à Lapide in this place. Who himself however not lightly errs, when he pronounces absolutely concerning the Jews in the O. T., that to them, laboring for so many ages of the world long, laboriously and troublesomely in the worship of GOD and the Church, the denarius promised by God was a temporal reward, namely, an abundance of temporal things, of grain, of oil, and of wine; but to the Gentile Christians, laboring in the one and last age of the world, was promised by Christ the denarius, i.e., a spiritual reward far better, namely, eternal life. But however much you may rightly say concerning the Scribes and Pharisees and their disciples, who despised and persecuted Christ with His word, that seeking to be justified by the works of the law, they fell from the denarius of eternal life, it is nevertheless false that to the Jews in the O. T. only temporal goods were promised. Nay rather, no less in the O. than in the N. T. was eternal life promised to those believing in Christ, and also given to those departing in true faith in the future Messiah, the Redeemer of the World. Conf. preface to the Commentary on Deuteronomy, also B. P. L. on eternal life § 30. In this place we add at least this, that Cornelius himself a little later, namely on page 381. A., expressly writes, The Fathers everywhere, just as also Bellarmine and Suarez, understand by the Denarius, which is read to have been given to the first as well as the last, eternal life. item, that the hiring, according to Chrysostom, whom Cornelius himself also cites at v. 6, is the promise of eternal life. Now, truly, not less were the Jews in the Old Testament hired into the vineyard than Christians in the New. Therefore, to both was eternal life promised.)*

By τό βάρος τες εμέςας they understand the entire day's labor. χαασονα or the heat of midday they oppose to the somewhat cooler breeze, which is accustomed to blow toward the setting of the Sun, at which time those last ones had first begun to labor.

Latin:

v. 12. Εποίησαν. hîc potiùs accipitur pro λλατςιβείν, quàm pro έργάζεσθαι. *(Coeterùm refert. Ludov. Capellus in Spicil. p. 28. planè gemellam parabolam isti nostri Salvatoris à R. Iona in Arcano poenit. allatam, quae ibipotest legi. Quomodo verò aequali mercedis distributioni, cùm tamen labor inaequalis fuerit, aequitas sua constet, ostendit S. Gregorius Nazianzenus Orat. 40. p. 651. Cumprimis a-tem prolixè id declarare satagit Corn à Lapide in h. l. Qui ipse tamē haut leviter -rrat, quando absolutè de Iudaeis in V. T. pronunciat, quòd illis per tot mundi aetates diu, operosè & molestè laborantibus in DEI cultu & Ecclesiâ, denarius à Deo promissus fuerit merces temporalis, scil. abundantia rerum temporalium, frumenti, olei, & vini; Gentilibus verò Christianis, unicâ & ultimâ mundi aetate laborantibus promissus sit à Christo denarius i. e. merces spiritualis longè melior, sc. vita aeterna Verùm ut ut de Scribis ac Pharisaeis horumq; discipulis, qui Christum cum suo verbo contemnebant & persequebantur, rectè dixeris, quòd per legis opera iustificari quaerentes, vitae aeternae denario exciderint, falsum tamen est, quòd Iudaeis in V. Test. saltem temporalia bona fuerint promissa. Imò potiùs haut minùs in V. quàm in V. T. credentibus in Christum vita aeterna promissa fuit, atque etiam in verâ fide in futurum Messiam Mundi redemtorem discedentibus data. Conf. raefat. ad Comment. in Deuteron. it. B. P. L de vitâ aeternâ § 30. Hoc loco illud saltem addimus, quòd ipse Cornelius paullò pòst, pag. scil. 381. A. disertè scribat, Patres passim, quemadmodum etiam Bellarminus ac Suarez per Denarium, qui primis iuxta & ultimis datus legitur, accipere vitam aeternam. it. quòd conductio, iuxta Chrysostomum, quem ipse etiam Cornelius ad v 6. allegat, sit promissio vitae aeternae. Iam verò non Iudaei minùs in V. quàm Christiani in N. Test. conducti fuerunt in vineam. E. utris que vita promissa aeterna fuit.)*

Per τό βάρος τες εμέςας intelligunt laborem diurnum integrum. χαασονα sive aestum meridiei opponunt aurae frigidiusculae, quae flare solet sub occasum Solis, quo tempore ultimi illi primùm laborare coeperant.

## 20:13
v. 13. But he answered one of them. That one in the mind of the Savior was Peter, to whose little boast at the end of the preceding chapter Christ had opposed this parable. Indeed, Christ’s admonition rests upon 1. the justice of GOD, v. 13. 2. truth, v. 13, 14. 3. liberty, v. 15. 4. goodness. ibid)* *(

Latin:

*(v. 13. Ipse verò dixit uni corum. Unus ille in mente Salvatoris erat Petrus, cuius gloriolae circa fin. cap. praeced. parabolam hanc Christus opposuerat. Nititur verò Christi admonitio 1. DEI iustitiâ v. 13. 2. veritate, v. 13 14. 3. libertate, v. 15. 4. bonitate. ibid)*

## 20:15
*(v. 15. Is it not lawful for me to do what I will &c. From this D. Ioh. Crocius gathers in part 2 of the Controv. Pruten. c. 13 p. 417, that no other cause is expressed in Holy Scripture why God wills to confer the grace of saving faith upon these rather than those, than the mere good pleasure of GOD. But it is manifest that Christ is not dealing here with the donation of saving faith, but with the gratuitous and liberal remuneration of the troubles and labors exhausted in the cultivation of the spiritual vineyard. The same is also to be noted against Ioh. Scharpius the Scot-Briton, who in his Cursus Theolog. p. 126 attempts to construct from this place that election is from mere grace of GOD. Furthermore, it is one thing to be mere grace, i.e., excluding our works as merits of salvation and election; it is another thing to be absolute grace, i.e., exterminating from election the intuition of faith itself, which apprehends the merit of Christ. From the former to the latter the consequence does not hold. The former Scripture teaches, the latter it does not know.)*

Is your eye evil, etc. The eye πονηεός denotes not only envy, but also stinginess and avarice. (Conf. Prov. 23. 6,Tob. 4, 7. & 17.Eccles. 14, 10.) Siracid. 31, 13. An evil eye is wicked, i.e., restricted and stingy. Conversely Sirac. 35, 7. With a good eye honor the Lord, i.e., generously and kindly, Prov. 22, 9. a good eye, i.e., liberal and kind. Theophylact interprets it concerning an envious man. Thus the Greeks βασχαίνειν say τό θθονείν or to envy, because envious men seem to harm and kill with εοοίς θάεσιχαίνειν eyes. Casaubon. (St. Jerome: What more do you seek, and do you not desire not so much to receive more yourself, as that another receive nothing? As if the merit of the reward were diminished by the fellowship of another? By no means, therefore, let us envy others their salvation, but rather let us rejoice over the conversion of others. See Luc. 15, 10.Act. 11, 18.)

Latin:

*(v. 15. Annon licet mih, quod volo &c. Colligit hinc D. Ioh. Crocius part. 2. Controv. Pruten. c. 13 p. 417. non aliam in Sc. S. exprimi causam, cur Deus his potiùs quàm illis velit fidei salvificaegratiam conferre, quàm meram DEI beneplacitum. Ast manifestum est, Christum hîc non agere de fidei salvificae donatione, sed de gratuitâ & liberali, molestiarum laborumque in vineae spiritualis cultu exantlatorum remuneratione. Idem quoque notandum contra Ioh. Scharpium Scoto Britannum, qui in cursu Theolog. p. 126. adstruere ex h. l. conatur, electionem esse ex merâ DEI gratiâ. Praeterea aliud est gratia mera i. e. opera nostra, ut salutis & electionis merita, excludens; aliud gratia absoluta h. e. ipsius quoque fidei, Christi meritum apprehendentis intuitum ab electione exterminans. Ab illa ad hanc non valet consequentia. Illam docet Scriptura, hanc nescit.)*

An oculus tuus malus &c. Oculusπονηεός non tantùm invidiam notat, sed etiam sordes & avaritiam. *(Conf. Prov. 23. 6,Tob. 4, 7. & 17.Eccles. 14, 10.)* Siracid. 31, 13.Malum est oculus malus i. e. restrictus & sordidus. Contrà Sirac. 35, 7.Oculo bono honora Dominum i. e. largiter & benignè, Prov. 22, 9.bonus oculus i. e. liberalis & benignus. Theophyl. interpretatur de homine invido. Sic Graeci βασχαίνειν dicunt τό θθονείν seu invidere, quia videantur homines invidi εοοίς θάεσιχαίνειν oculis nocere & occidere. Casaubonus. *(S. Hieronymus: Quid quaeris ampliùs, & non tam ipse plus accipere, quàm alium nihil accipere desideras. Quasi alterius consortio minuatur praemii meritum? Hautquaquam igitur aliis invideamus salutem, sed potiùs ob aliorum conversionem laetemur. Vid. Luc. 15, 10.Act. 11, 18.)*

## 20:16
(v. 16. So the last shall be first, etc. See Anal. on c. 19, 30. and also on c. 22, 14. Let there also be compared the Blessed D. Frantzius on the Interpretation of Holy Scripture, Oracle 36. The Blessed D. Hunnius in this place thinks that by this epiphonema it is mystically indicated that the Gentiles, signified by those who were called into the vineyard at the eleventh hour, precede the Jews in the kingdom of GOD, so that those who were last and clearly cut off and alienated from the life of GOD, now in the kingdom of Christ become the first of all. Conversely, those who were first, on account of the confidence of performed labor and work, i.e., on account of the opinion of holiness and their own righteousness, become the last. There can also be compared with the last, the same Blessed D. Hunnius advising, those who performed a late, yet serious repentance, as the thief on the cross, Luc. 23. Whence also one must not easily despair of anyone's salvation. This saying of the Savior can be illustrated and explained by other examples. For thus in the following chapter v. 31 He says that publicans and harlots shall precede the Pharisees and priests into the kingdom of GOD. Thus the sinful woman was preferred to the Pharisee Luc. 7, 44. The adulteress to her accusers, Ioh. 8, 7. etc.)

(For many are called, but few are chosen. Rightly do the Orthodox infer from this that not all who are called, or who live in the external assembly of the Church, are inwardly regenerated, renewed, gifted with true faith, and grafted into Christ by the Holy Spirit. To which also pertain the parables below in c. 22. and 25, 1. above in c. 3, 12. c. 13, 24. 37. 38. 47. 49.) John 10, 1. and the sayings John 8, 39.Acts 20, 30.Rom. 2, 28. 29.ch. 9, 6.8.1 Cor. 11, 19.1 Tim. 3, 15. to which see the Analecta. Notably Gregory the Great, hom. 1 on the Gospel: Now the net of faith contains good and bad together as if mixed fish: but the shore indicates what the net of the Church draws. Fulgentius on faith to Peter, ch. 43: Hold most firmly and doubt in no way that the threshing floor of GOD is the Catholic Church, and within it until the end of the age the chaff is contained mixed with the wheat, that is, the bad are mixed with the good by the communion of the Sacraments. But if many are called, who nevertheless are not chosen, how does the Apostle write Rom. 8, 30., whom he predestined, these he also called? Answer: The Savior speaks of the calling considered in itself, but Paul, insofar as the chosen obey the calling through persevering faith. See Lord Dr. Weller, Comm. on the Ep. to the Rom. p. 34, 505, and 511. Nor is it to be thought that, because not all who are called embrace the grace of GOD, it is not itself saving. Nay rather, it is rightly called saving for all, since in itself it has shone savingly for all,Tit. 2, 11. and God seriously wills that all should obey the calling, do penance, and be saved, although as regards the saving fruit it becomes particular by the own fault of the unbelieving men. In the same sense must be taken his assertion 1 Cor. 1, 26. that not many are called. But it is asked here further, whether the word many in this place is to be taken for all, as it is also sometimes taken elsewhere in Holy Scripture, as is evident from the collation of Deut. 12, 2. with John 5, 28., likewise Rom. 5, 19. with v. 12. Answer: One must distinguish between the calling viewed in itself, and insofar as it is done in a solemn manner. Then between the intention of calling, and the act. In the former way the calling is universal, not in the latter, since the solemn calling is often hindered by the malice of most men. So that the serious intention of GOD, desiring to call all, is present: yet that it is not brought into act, that is, that all men are not actually called, happens by their own fault, while they despise the means of salvation , preferring earthly things to heavenly. Thus in this place we are taught that the first were indeed seriously called, yet on account of trust in their own merits, impious murmuring against the householder, and envy toward their fellow workers, they become the last, that is, they fall from salvation. Then it must be known that from a denied calling done solemnly, it should not be gathered either that those who were not so called were not called at all; much less is the intention of GOD to be denied on that account, or the benevolent will of internally calling and saving all. Against John Calvin, Instit. Theol. b. 3, ch. 24, John Georg Gross, Theatri Bibl. p. 1011. Concerning the solemn calling the sayings are to be understood Deut. 29, 29.Ps. 103, 7.Ps. 147, 20.Es 52, 15.Act. 14. 16.Rom. 1, 5.c. 9, 25.Eph. 2, 12. 13 That God indeed wishes all men to be saved, and therefore if any are not called and saved, they fall from that benefit by their own fault, is evident from Ps. 81, 12.Prov. 1, 24 25. 26.Es. 65, 2. 3.12.Amos 8, 11. 12.Matth. 22, 3.c. 23, 37.Luc 7, 30.Act. 13, 461. Petr 1, 2.6.8. Conf. B. D. Fewrbornium Fascic. 3 Dissert. Theolog. Disp. 1. B. D. Meisnerum Ανθςωπ. sacrae Disp. 13. q. 2. & 3. B Par. Disp. Isagog. de praedestinatione c. 6 § 10 11. B. D. Sigwartum in Admonitione Christ. ad Irenicum Paraei p. 463. seqq.)*

*( Few are chosen. The cause of this fewness is not an absolute decree of GOD, by which He himself, without intuition of foreseen unbelief, rejected the greatest part of men (for the contrary is evident both from the context of this and the parallel passage c. 22, 14, and from very many other oracles of Holy Scripture, as Ezech. 18. 33c. 33. 11.Ioh 3, 16,1. Tim. 2, 4) but the own fault of men, who reject the offered means of salvation. See Prov. 1, 24.Hos. 13, 9.Matth. 33, 37. which contempt of the means divinely ordained for salvation God as a just judge deservedly punishes. Nor was election made from a certain absolute σεσοχία, but χαεοά πςόγνωσιν of persevering faith. Those therefore whom God foresaw would finally believe, these He chose; just as on the contrary those whom He foresaw would not finally believe, them He reprobated, nor did He choose them to eternal life. Furthermore, if few are chosen, it will be false what Sam. Huberus once taught, that election is universal. He indeed distinguishes between εχλελεγμσανομς & εχλεχτούς, establishing that all men are chosen participially i.e. that all have been chosen to eternal life; although not all are chosen nominally i.e. that they obey the divine election. But Holy Scripture calls only those who obey the divine calling & persevere in true faith until the end of life, chosen by God to eternal life. Distinguish therefore between election, and love; between election in a broader sense and χαεοαχςηςιχός accepted (in the way some Theologians have employed it, namely for love.) and between election strictly so called, which is only of the truly faithful. Compare Iac. 2, 2. and add B. D. Calixtus Concord. Evang. p. 280. B. D. Hutterus Expl. F. C. p. 1116. following. item LL. Mai p 805. Finally it is to be noted, that the few are called elect, that this is to be accepted comparatively. See Anal. to c. 7, 14. and add Augustine book on correction and grace c. 10. item against Cresconius the Donatist l. 4. c. 53. B. D. Lobech. in Synopsis of the doctrine concerning the eternal predestination of GOD §. 155. following.)

Latin:

*(v. 16. Sic novissimi erunt primi &c. Vid. Anal. ad c. 19, 30. nec non ad c. 22, 14. Conferatur etiam B. D. Frantzius de Interpret. Sc. S. Oraculo 36. B. D. Hunnius in h. l. putat, epiphonemate hoc mysticè indicari, gentiles, significati per eos, qui undecimâ horâ in vineam vocati, praevenire in regno DEI Iudaeos, ita ut qui ultimi erant planeque abscissi & abalienatià vitâ DEI, nunc in Christi regno fiant omnium primi. Vicissim qui primi fuerant, ob fiduciam praestiti laboris & operis h. e. propter opinionem sanctitatis & propriae iustitiae, fiant ultimi. Possunt quoque cum ultimis, eod. B. D. Hunnio monente, conferri, qui seram quidem, at seriam egerunt poenitentiam, ceu latro in cruce, Luc. 23. Unde etiam haut facilè de cuiusquam salute desperandam. Potest hoc Salvatoris effatum aliis illustrari & explicari exemplis. Sic enim c. seq. v. 31. dicit, quòd publicani & meretrices praecessuri sint Pharisaeos ac sacerdotes in regnum DEI. Ita peccatrix foemina praelata Pharisaeo Luc. 7, 44. Adultera accusatoribus, Ioh. 8, 7. &c.)*

*( Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci verò electi. Rectè hinc inferunt Orthodoxi, non omnes vocatos sive qui in externo Ecclesiae coetu vivunt, interiùs per Sp. Sanctum regenerari, renovari, verâ fide donari ac Christo inseri. Quo faciunt etiam parabolae infrà c. 22. & 25, 1. suprà c. 3, 12. c. 13, 24. 37. 38. 47. 49. Ioh. 10, 1. ac dicta Ioh 8, 39.Act. 20 30Rom. 2, 28. 29c. 9, 6.81. Cor. 11, 19.1. Tim. 3, 15. ad quae vid Analecta. Notanter Gregorius M. hom. 1. in Evang. Nunc bonos & malos communiter quasi permixtos pisces fidei sagena continet: sed littus indicat, Ecclesiae sagena quid trahat Fulgentius de fide ad Petrum cap. 43. Firmissimè tene & nullatenus dubites, aream DEI esse Catholicam Ecclesiam, & intra eam usq ad finem secult frumento mixtas paleas contineri, h. e. bonis malos Sacramentorum communione misceri. Sed si multi vocati, qui tamen non sunt electi quomodo Apostolus Rom. 8, 30. scribit, quos praedestinavit, hos & vocavit? Resp. Loquitur Salvator de vocatione in se consideratâ, sed Paulus, quatenus electi per fidem perseverantem vocationi obtemperant. Vid. Dn. D. Wellerum Comm. in Ep. ad Rom. p. 34. 505. ac 511. Nec existimandum est, quòd propterea, quia non omnes vocati gratiam DEI amplectuntur, ipsa non sit salutaris. Imò potiùs salutaris omnibus rectè dicitur, cùm in se omnibus salutariter illuxerit,Tit. 2, 11. ac Deus seriò velit, ut omnes vocationi obtemperent, poenitentiam agant ac salventur, licet quoad salutarem fructum propriâ hominum incredulorum culpâ fiat particularis. Eodem sensu accipiendum eiusdem assertum 1. Cor. 1, 26. quòd non multi sint vocati. Quaeritur verò hîc porrò, an vox multorum h l accipienda sit pro omnibus, quomodo & alibi quandoque in Sc S. accipitur, ceu patet ex collatione Deut. 12. 2. cum Ioh. 5 28. it. Rom. 5, 19. cum v. 12. Resp. distinguendum inter vocationem in se spectatam, & quatenus solenni modo facta. Deinde inter vocandi intentionem, & actum. Priori modo vocatio universalis est, non posteriori, cùm plurimorum hominum malitiâ saepè impediatur solennis vocatio. ut ita seria DEI intentio, omnes vocare cupientis, adfit: quò minùs tamen in actum deducatur h e. omnes homines actu vocentur, propriâ eorum culpâ fiat, dum media salutis cōt-mnunt, terrena coelestibus praeferentes. Sich l. docemur, quòd primi seriò quidem vocati fuerint, attamē propter fidu-iam in propria merita, murmur impium adversùs patremfamiliâs, ac invidiam erga proximos cooperarios, fiant novissimi h. e. salute excidant. Deinde sciendum, quòd à negatâ vocatione solenniter factâ, non debeat colligi, vel quòd illi, qui ita non fuerunt vocati, planè non vocati fuerint; multò minùs propterea neganda DEI intentio est, sive benevola, omnes internè vocandi & salvandi, voluntas. Contra Ioh. Calvinum Instit. Theol. l. 3. c. 24 Ioh Georg Grossium, Theatri Bibl. p. 1011. De solenni vocatione intellig-nda dicta Deut. 29, 29.Ps. 103, 7.Ps. 147, 20.Es 52, 15.Act. 14. 16.Rom. 1, 5.c. 9, 25.Eph. 2, 12. 13 Quòd verò Deus omnes homines salvos velit, adeoque si qui non vocantur ac salvantur, propriâ suâ culpâ beneficio illo excidant, patet ex Ps. 81, 12.Prov. 1, 24 25. 26.Es. 65, 2. 3.12.Amos 8, 11. 12.Matth. 22, 3.c. 23, 37.Luc 7, 30.Act. 13, 461. Petr 1, 2.6.8. Conf. B. D. Fewrbornium Fascic. 3 Dissert. Theolog. Disp. 1. B. D. Meisnerum Ανθςωπ. sacrae Disp. 13. q. 2. & 3. B Par. Disp. Isagog. de praedestinatione c. 6 § 10 11. B. D. Sigwartum in Admonitione Christ. ad Irenicum Paraei p. 463. seqq.)*

*( Pauci electi. Paucitatis huius causa non est absolutum DEI decretum, quo ipse absque praevisae incredulitatis intuitu maximam hominum partem reiecerit (aliud enim patet tum ex contextu huius ac paralleli loci c. 22, 14. tum ex aliis plurimis Sc. S. oraculis, uti Ezech. 18. 33c. 33. 11.Ioh 3, 16,1. Tim. 2, 4) sed propria hominum, oblata salutis media reiicientium culpa. Vid. Prov. 1, 24.Hos. 13, 9.Matth. 33, 37. quem mediorum ad salutem divinitus ordinatorum contemtum Deus ut iustus iudex meritò punit. Neque electio facta ex absoluta quadam σεσοχία, sed χαεοά πςόγνωσιν fidei perseverantis. Quos igitur Deus praevidit, finaliter credituros esse, hos elegit. sicuti è contrà quos praevidit non credituros esse finaliter, eos reprobavit, nec ad vitam aeternam elegit. Porrò si pauci sunt electi, falsum erit quod Sam. Huberus quondam docuit, electionem esse universalem. Distingvit quidem ipse inter εχλελεγμσανομς & εχλεχτούς, statuens quòd omnes homines sint electi participialiter h. e. quòd omnes electi fuerint ad vitam aeternam; licet non omnes sint electi nominaliser h. e. electioni divinae obsequantur. Sed Sc S non nisi eos, qui vocationi divinae obsequuntur & in verâ fide us que ad finem vitae perseverant, à Deo ad vitam aeternam electos dicit. Dist. igitur inter electionem, & dilectionem; inter electionem in latiori significatione & χαεοαχςηςιχός acceptam (quomodo nonnulli Theologi adhibuerunt, nempe pro dilectione.) & inter electionemstrictè sic dictam, quae non nisi verè fideliū est. Conf. Iac. 2, 2. ac adde B. D. Calixtum Concord. Evang. p. 280. B. D. Hutterum Expl. F. C. p. 1116. seqq. it. LL. Mai p 805. Denique notandum, quòd pausi dicuntur electi, id comparativè esse accipiendum. Vid. Anal. ad c. 7, 14. ac adde Augustinum lib. de corr. & grat. c. 10. it. contra Crescon. Donatistam l. 4. c. 53. B. D. Lobech. in Synopsi doctr. de aet. DEI praedest. §. 155. seqq.)*

## 20:17
v. 17. He took the twelve disciples aside.Christ announces the mystery of His death to the Apostles in private, because a more precious treasure is always enclosed in better vessels.Chrysostom, however, assigns another reason in Homily 66.Privately, he writes, he speaks to them necessarily: for these things were not to be brought forth, from which no utility would follow. For if the disciples were troubled upon hearing them, what would the multitude not have done? Others add that He predicted His future passion to the Apostles in private for this reason, lest by predicting it to the Jews He might seem to have irritated their minds.But He also predicted the same to the multitude John 2:19. ch.7:33, Luke 11:29. but not so openly. But why did He predict it to this one [the multitude] as well? Namely, so that, remembering it afterwards, they might believe that He underwent the passion willingly, not ignorantly, nor compelled, as the same Chrysostom has it in the loc. cit.But why Christ predicted His passion to the disciples so often, the Blessed Doctor D.Glassius in his *Disputationes Elenchticae* on *Dominica Quinquagesima*, p. 460, enumerates the causes of that matter:1.That there might be a showing of the mystery lying hidden in His passion.2.A demonstration of His spontaneous offering.3.The removal of scandal.4.An abduction from worldly thoughts.5.The consolation of the Apostles.6. The commendation of His passion.)* *(

Latin:

*(v. 17. Adsumsit duodecim discipulos secretò. Secretò Apostolis mortis suae mysterium Christus annunciat, quia semper pretiosior the saurus in melioribus vasis includitur. Aliam tamen rationem adsignat Chrysostomus hom. 66. Privatim, scribit, eos necessariò alloquitur: non enim haec efferenda erant, ex quibus nihil utilitatis sequeretur. Nam si discipuli audientes turbabantur, quid non fecisset multitudo? Addunt alii, proptereà secretò Apostolis futuram passionem praedixisse, ne Iudaeis praedicendo irritâsse eorum animos videatur. Sed & multitudini idem praedicebat Ioh. 2, 19. c. 7, 33, Luc. 11, 29. verùm non ita apertè. Cur verò & huic praedixit? nempe ut posteà recordantes crederent, illum volentem, non ignorantem, nec coactum passionem subiisse, ut habet idem Chrysostomus l. c. Cur verò Christus tam saepè passionem suam discipulis praedixerit, illius rei B. D. D. Glassius in Disp. Elencht. super Dom. Quinq. p. 460 has enumerat causas. 1 ut sit mysterii in passione suâ latentis ostensio. 2. Spontaneae suae oblationis demonstratio. 3. Scandali amotio. 4. à mundanis cogitationibus abductio. 5. Apostolorum consolatio. 6. Passionis suae commendatio.)*

## 20:18
(v. 18. The Son of man shall be delivered etc. Here that which is proper to the human nature is predicated of the concrete of the human nature in Christ. But lest anyone should think, as if Christ were our Mediator only according to the human nature, elsewhere the same is predicated also of the concrete of the divine nature. See Acts 2, 36.Acts 20, 28.1 Cor. 2, 8. That the Son of God Himself truly suffered, the Blessed D. Glassius proves at length in a certain Disputation held under the presidency of the Blessed Pareus, which see in Explic. Elen. Evang. Domin. p. 478. seqq.

*( Τοίς ἀρχιερεῦσι χαί γραμματείς He names these alone, not as if they alone constituted the Sanhedrin, but because these others ought to have shone forth in piety and skill, just as they also desired to appear as such.)*

Latin:

*(v. 18. Filius hominis tradetur &c. Hîc proprium humanae naturae praedicatur de concreto hum. nat. in Christo. Ne verò quis existimet, quasi Christus secundùm humanam tantùm naturam noster Mediator sit, alibi idem praedicatur etiam de concreto divinae naturae. Vide Actor. 2, 36.c. 20, 28.1. Cor. 2, 8. Quòd verò ipse Filius DEI passus fuerit, prolixè probat B. D. Glass. in Disp. quadam sub B. Par. praesidio habitâ, quam vide in Explic. Elen ht. Evang. Domin. p. 478. seqq.

*( Τοίς ἀρχιερεῦσι χαί γραμματείς Hos solos nominat, non qs. illi soli Synedrium constituerint, sed quia hi aliipietare & peritiâ praelucere debebant, prout etiam tales videri cupiebant.)*

## 20:19
v. 19. They shall deliver him to the Gentiles to scourge him &c. The scourging indeed came from the outside, yet nonetheless all the evils are rightly and deservedly imputed to the Jews, because by their own wickedness they provided the occasion for these evils, as H. Grotius rightly advises in this place. Let us learn from this that Christ suffered willingly. For knowing his future passion, he nonetheless ascended to Jerusalem. Compare also Ps 40. John 10, 8. c. 18, 4. We recognize also from this that he is the true promised Messiah, as one of whom it was predicted that he would suffer and die. See Ps. 22. Is. 53, Dan. 9. Luke 24. Let us not be ashamed of this passion of Christ, since all our wisdom and salvation consists in it. Compare 1. Cor. 1, 18. 24. c. 2, 2. Let us also follow Christ suffering, Matt. 10, 38. and dying, that we may rise again with him, 1. Cor. 15. )* *(

To scourge &c. These are the three principal parts of Christ’s passion. For he was mocked most ignominiously, scourged most atrociously, and crucified most bitterly. Piously, Blessed Bernard, sermon on the fourfold debt: You owe your whole life to Christ Jesus, for he himself laid down his life for yours and sustained bitter torments, lest you should sustain eternal ones. The same, treatise on loving GOD: If I owe my whole self for having been made, what shall I now add for having been remade, and remade in this manner? For he was not as easily remade as he was made: for he who made himself by merely speaking, in remaking [man] certainly both said many things and performed wonders, and endured hard things, and not only hard things, but also indignities. But if we could now obtain salvation by our own works, which the Papists claim, Christ would have endured such hard and unworthy things in vain. Compare more things pertaining to this in the Analysis to Mark 10, 33. following.)* *(

Latin:

*(v. 19. Tradent eum gentibus ad flagellandum &c. Flagellatio extrinsecùs quidem advenit, nihilo tamen minùs rectè & meritò Iudaeis omnia mala imputantur, quia suo scelere occasionem malis praebuerunt, ut rectè monet H. Grotius in h. l. Discamus hinc, Christum sponte passum esse. Sciens enim futuram suam passionem, nihilo tamen minùs Hierosolymas adscendit. Conf. etiam Ps 40.Ioh. 10, 8.c. 18, 4. Agnoscimus etiā hinc, ipsum effe verum promissum Messiam, ut de quo praedictum, quòd passurus & moriturus sit. Vid. Ps. 22.Es. 53,Dan. 9.Luc. 24. Huius Christi passionis minimè nos pudeat, cùm in ea omnis sapientia ac salus nostra consistat. Conf. 1. Cor. 1, 18.24.c. 2, 2. Sequamur etiam Christum patientem, Matth. 10, 38. ac morientem, ut cum eo resurgamus, 1. Cor. 15.)*

*( Adflagellandum &c Tres hae praecipuae passionis Christi partes sunt. Illusus enim fuit ignominiosissimè, flagellatus atrocissimè, crucifixus amarissimè. Piè B. Bernhardus serm. de quadrupl. debito: Christo Iesu debes omnem vitam tuam, quis ipse vitam suam posuit pro tua & cruciatus amaros sustinuit, ne tu perpetuos sustineret. Idem tr. de diligendo DEO: si totum me debeo pro me facto, quid addam iam pro me refecto, & refecto hoc modo? nec enim tam facilè refectus, quàm factus: nam qui se mel & tantùm dicendo fecit, in reficiendo profectò & dixit multa & gessit mira, & pertulit dura, nec dura tantùm, sed & indigna. Quod si iam propriis nostris operibus possemus salutem consequi, quod Pontificii volunt, Christus frustrà tam dura & indigna sustinuisset. Conf. plura huc facientia in Anal. ad Marc. 10, 33. seqq.)*

## 20:20
*(v. 20. Something. See a similar manner of requesting in Bathsheba 1 Kings 2, 20. But just as she received a refusal from Solomon, when she requested ineptly and imprudently, so also here the mother of the sons of Zebedee from the heavenly Solomon.)*

Latin:

*(v. 20. Aliquid. Vide similem petendi modum Bethsabe 1. Reg. 2, 20. Sed ceu illa repulsam à Salomone tulit, cùm ineptè & imprudenter peteret, ita & hîc mater filiorum Zebedaei à coelesti Salomone.)*

## 20:21
(v. 21. What do you want? Saint Jerome well says in his Commentary on this passage: That the Lord asks, does not come from ignorance, but it is said from the person of him who was to be scourged and crucified, just as also in the case of the woman with the issue of blood: Who touched me? And concerning Lazarus: Where have you laid him? In the O. Testament: Adam, where are you?)

(She says to him, namely the mother of the sons of Zebedee, as is clear from the context. But Mark ch. 10, 35 reports that the sons themselves made the request. Response: Chrysostom, homily 66 on Matthew, teaches that they first requested it themselves, and afterwards employed their mother, so that they might render the intercession more evident, and as it were put the Master to shame, so that he would not refuse, since she was the own sister of Joseph, the foster-father of Christ, as the blessed Doctor Hunnius notes on this passage. This opinion pleases the blessed Doctor Walther in H. B. p. 781.)

(Say that these may sit, etc. She ought to have framed her prayers more modestly, namely, if you will, etc. Matth. 8, 2. Compare 2. Sam. 15, 25. below ch. 26, 39. But it is asked, whence did the mother of the sons of Zebedee conceive the opinion of a kingdom, when Christ had just been speaking of his passion and death? He himself had spoken of the torments and ignominy of the one suffering, she demands the glory of the one triumphing. Response: The Lord had added that he would rise again on the third day. She thought, therefore, that he would reign immediately after the resurrection, and that he would fulfill in his first coming what he promises in his second. Thus Saint Jerome determines in this passage, whom Erasmus of Rotterdam follows. It is probable that she herself dreamed of an earthly kingdom. Which opinion had occupied the minds of many at that time. And thus the blessed Doctor Hunnius judges in this passage, who also conveniently warns that parents ought to be solely concerned that their children be brought up in the instruction and correction of the Lord, Eph. 6, 4. and to commit the rest to GOD, for whom it is easy to raise them up, just as Joseph from prison, David from the flock, Daniel from captivity, Elisha from the oxen, etc. And if they should bear a similar lot, such as God has assigned to the sons of Zebedee, they should likewise bear it patiently.)

(είς σεξιόν. To sit at the right hand of the King, denotes to obtain the chief place with the King. See) 1. Reg. 2, 19. it. Sueton, in Nerone.)*

*( You do not know. It is not understood as mere ignorance at least, but joined with the vain desire of worldly glory. Conf, Marc. 9, 6.Luc. 23, 24. We are taught here that not all prayers are heard by God. See the note to Matth. 7, 7. Indeed, for a prayer that ought to be heard, there is required not only a turning away from sins, Es. 1.Ioh. 9, 31. and due intention, 1. Sam. 16, 7.Iacob. 5. 16. but also prudence and discretion, so that we do not ask for just anything without discrimination. In which matter the mother of the sons of Zebedee erred above all. But it is asked why He addresses the disciples, when the mother is read to have asked? Resp. Jerome in h. l. The mother asks, and the Lord speaks: understanding that her prayers descend from the will of the sons. Nay, the disciples themselves, James and John, the sons of Zebedee, had asked for this; according to Mark c. 10, 35. The sons of Zebedee therefore seem to have first sent their mother to ask for great things, as Jerome says, and afterwards to have added their own prayers as well. But it seems that those two Apostles were incited to that ambitious πρωτκοχαθεσείας petition both because they were related to Christ, and because they had seen themselves sometimes preferred by Christ to the other Apostles, for instance in His transfiguration c. 17, 1. and in the raising of the daughter of Jairus, Luc. 8, 51. We learn from this, however, how gross was the ignorance with which the disciples of Christ still labored, and at the same time their ambition. We are warned, however, by the response of our Savior to flee ambition: likewise that in the kingdom of Christ relationships and such external things are of no value &c.)*

Latin:

*(v. 21. Quid vis. Benè S. Hieronymus Comm. in h. l. Quod interrogat Dominus, non venit de ignorantiâ, sed ex eius persona dicitur, qui flagellandus & crucifigendus erat, quomodo & in haemorrhousa: Quis me tetigit? & de Lazaro: Ubi posuistis eum? In V. quoTestamento: Adam ubi es?)*

*( Ait illi, nempe mater filiorum Zebedaei, ceu ex contextu patet. At Marcus c. 10, 35. ipsos filios petiisse tradit. Resp. Chrysostomus hom. 66. in Matth. docet, quòd priùs ipsi petierint, postea matrem adhibuerint, ut intercessionem redderent evidentiorem, & quasi in pudorem darent Magistrum, ne abnueret, cùm ipsa fuerit soror germana Iosephi curatitii Christi patris, notante B. D. Hunnio in h. l. Arridet haec sententia B. D. Walthero in H. B. p. 781.)*

*( Dic ut sedeant hi &c. Debuisset modestiùs preces informare, nempe, si vis &c. Matth. 8, 2. Conf. 2. Sam. 15, 25. infrà c. 26, 39. Quaeritur autem, unde opinionem regni conceperit mater filiorum Zebedaei, cùm Christus de passione sua ac morre iam iam esset loquutus? Ipse locutus erat de tormentis & ignominiâ patientis, illa postulat gloriam triumphantis. Resp. Adiecerat Dominus, se tertio die resurrecturum. Putavit igitur, ipsum post resurrectionem illicò regnaturum, & hoc, quod in secundo adventu promittit, in primo esse completurum. Ita statuit S. Hieronymus in h. l. quem sequitur Erasmus Roterodam us. Probabile est, quòd ipsa terrenum regnum somniaverit. Quae opinio multorum tum animos occupaverat. Atque ita censet B. D. Hunnius in h. l. qui etiam commodè monet, quòd Parentes unicè solliciti esse debeant, quò liberi eorum educentur in eruditione & correptione Domini, Eph. 6, 4. reliqua DEO committere, cui facile sit, eosdem evehere, ceu Iosephum è carcere, Davidem à grege, Danielem ex captivitate, Elisaeum à bobus &c. Quòd si similem sortem, qualem filiis Zebedaei adsignarit illis Deus, pariter ferant patienter.)*

*( είς σεξιόν. Dextrae Regis adsidere, notat principem apud Regem obtinere locum. Vid. 1. Reg. 2, 19. it. Sueton, in Nerone.)*

*( Nescitis. Non intelligitur simplex saltem ignorantia, fed cum vana glorio-ae mundanae concupiscentiâ coniuncta. Conf, Marc. 9, 6.Luc. 23, 24. Docemur hîc, non omnes preces à Deo exaudiri, Vid. not. ad Matth. 7, 7. Requiritur nempe ad precationem, quae exaudiri debet, non solùm à peccatis declinatio, Es. 1.Ioh. 9, 31. ac debita intentio, 1. Sam. 16, 7.Iacob. 5. 16. verùm etiam prudentia ac discretio, ne quidvis sine discrimine petamus. Quâ in re cumprimis mater filiorum Zebedaei erravit. Sed quaeritur cur discipulos alloquatur, cùm mater petiisse legatur? Resp. Hieronymus in h. l. Mater postulat, & Dominus loquitur: intelligens, preces eius eoc filiorum descendere voluntate. Imò ipsi quoque discipuli, Iacobus & Iohannes, filii Zebedaei hoc petierant; teste Marco c. 10, 35. Videntur igitur filii Zebedaei primùm matrem immifisse ad grandia postulanda, ut loquitur Hieronymus, postea suas quoque adiecisse preces. Excitâsse verò ad ambitiosam istam πρωτκοχαθεσείας petitionem duos illos Aposto los videtur tum quòd Christum cognatione attingerent, tum quòd ipsi se coeter is Apostolis vidissent aliquando à Christo antepositos, puta in eius transfiguratione c. 17, 1. & in filiae Iairi suscitatione, Lnc. 8, 51. Discimus verò hinc, quàm crass â discipuli Christi laborarint adhuc ignorantiâ, simul etiam ambitione. Admonemur autem Salvatoris nostri responso fugere ambitionem: item quòd in regno Christi nil valeant cognationes & huiusmodi externa &c.)*

## 20:22
v. 22. Can you drink the cup &c. By a double metaphor He designates calamities, 1. by a bitter potion, 2. by the immersion of Baptism. Piscator absurdly posits that the latter metaphor is derived from a shameful drenching, such as it is, he says, when someone is drenched with filth. *(Nay, rather the metaphor is drawn from a multitude, just as elsewhere also calamities are denoted by the phrase of many waters and deep ones, Ps. -, 17. Ps 32, 6 &c. -ti long ago noted B. D. Glass. Rhet. S. p 434. add Grotius to Matth. 7, 27. Which opinion seems to be preferred to the opinion of Cameron, who writes that it usually happens, that when we exaggerate things that are hard and troublesome, we signify them, as it were, εἰρωνικῶς by the words of those things which are sweet and pleasant in life, as by the word bath a more grievous hardship.)* Cup is most commonly used for cross in the Scriptures. See Es. 5.Ier. 25.Matth. 26. *(B. D. Glassius presents more examples in Rhet. S. p. 399. Add Ludab Alcas. in cap. 16. Apoc. v. 19. Hieron. Lauretus of Ervar in Sylva allegor. tit. Cup p. 202. B. D. Tarnov. Comment. in Obad. to v. 16. St. Jerome brings forward the passage Matth. 26, 39. then also Ps. 116, 13. But why the cross is called a cup, and indeed of the Lord, M. Binchius shows at length in Mellif. part. 5. p. 392. and 393. It is called so, however, primarily 1 by reason of pleasantness. For it is not some great vessel, but a measured cup. See Wis. 11, 22. Ier. 30, 11.Act. 3, 16.1. Cor. 10, 23. 2. by reason of dignity, since it is given by GOD. 1. Sam. 2, 6.Ps. 68.Thren. 3, 37. seqq. consecrated by Christ, Matth. 26, 37 offered with a certain hope of exchange, Ps. 116, 6. Conf. Exod. 15, 25. 3. by reason of charity, because it is from a dear hand, Prov. 3. 12.2. Tim. 5, 12.1. Petr. 4, 17.Ebr. 12, 5. 4 by reason of necessity and 5. by reason of cheerfulness.Act. 5, 41.Rom. 5, 3. Death, however, is called baptism, because Christ was as it were totally immersed or submerged in it. It can also be said with Chrysostom, Theophylact, and others, that the death of Christ is called baptism, because He washes us through it, as happens in Baptism.)*

To drink. To drink are said those who are punished and chastised. Obadiah 1, v. 16. As you have drunk upon my holy mountain. Compare Jer. 49, 12. Ezek. 23, 32. A metaphor taken from the custom of banquets. *(To this also Sirach seems to look back, ch. 32, 1. 2. add. Mr. Dilherr. vol. 1. Dispp. A-ad p. 4-3.)* In which, how much each person and in what manner they ought to drink temperately, συμποσίαρΧος, used to prescribe, who was also called the arbiter and Master of the banquet, because he used to bring the laws of drinking. But this was troublesome to those drinking in many ways. From the measure, if it were greater than they could conveniently bear. From the drink itself, if it were either thinner or stronger, or more bitter or more sour. *(Christ indeed employs the word to drink concerning his own passion, because reproaches were for drink, torments for a beverage, when with the highest desire he himself suffered for us. To this pertains that Ps. 11- -7 he shall drink of the brook. For the Psalmist seems to have considered Christ as a traveler laboring from heat , who when he falls into a brook, cannot restrain himself from thirst, but that he drinks most greedily. Thus Christ, burning with the love of our salvation, desired with desire to drink of the brook of passion.)*

*( We can. Let human confidence and vain presumption be noted here. It must be known, however, that perseverance is a gift of GOD, Phil. 1, 6.c 2, 13.2. Thess. 3, 3.1. Petr. 1, 5.)*

Latin:

v. 22. Potestis bibere poculum &c. Duplici metaphorâ calamitates designat, 1. amarâ potione, 2. immersione Baptisini. Piscatorabsurde statuit, metaphoram posteriorem deductam esse à contumeliosâ perfusione, qualis est, inquit cùm quis perfunditur lotio. *(Imò potiùs metaphora ducta est à multitudine, utialiàs quoque phrasi aquarum multarum & profundarum calamitates denotantur, Ps. -, 17. Ps 32, 6 &c. -ti pridem notavit B. D. Glass. Rhet. S. p 434. adde Grotium ad Matth. 7, 27. Quae sententia praeferenda vid-tur opinioni Cameronis, qui usu fere venire, scribit, ut quae sunt dura & molesta, ea dum exaggeramus, significemus, velutεἰρωνικῶςearum rerum vocabulis, quae in vita suavia sunt, & iucunda, ut lavacri voce aerumnam graviorem.)* Calicem pro cruce poni in Scripturis usitatissimum. Vid. Es. 5.Ier. 25.Matth. 26. *(Plura exempla sistit B. D. Glassius Rhet. S. p. 399. Add Ludab Alcas. in cap. 16. Apoc. v. 19. Hieron. Lauretus ervariensis in Sylvâ allegor. tit. Calix p. 202. B. D. Tarnov. Comment. in Obad. ad v. 16. S. Hieronymus adducit locum Matth. 26, 39. tum quoque Ps. 116, 13. Cur verò crux calix vocetur, & quidem Domini, prolixè ostendit M. Binchius in Mellif. part. 5. p. 392. & 393. Dicitur autem ita potissimùm 1 ratione iucunditatis. Neque enim magnum aliquod vas est, sed calix demensus. Vid. Sap. 11, 22. Ier. 30, 11.Act. 3, 16.1. Cor. 10, 23. 2. ratione dignitatis, quippe à DEO datus. 1. Sam. 2, 6.Ps. 68.Thren. 3, 37. seqq. à Christo consecratus, Matth. 26, 37 certâ permutationis spe oblatus, Ps. 116, 6. Conf. Exod. 15, 25. 3. ratione caritatis, quia à cara manu, Prov. 3. 12.2. Tim. 5, 12.1. Petr. 4, 17.Ebr. 12, 5. 4 ratione necessitatis ac 5. ratione hilaritatis.Act. 5, 41.Rom. 5, 3. Mors verò baptismus dicitur, quia Christus fuit in illā quasi totus immersus vel submersus. Potest quoq; cum Chrysost. Theoph. & aliis dici, Christi mortē baptismum vocari, quia nos per illam abluit, uti fit in Baptismo.)*

Bibere. Bibere dicuntur, qui puniuntur & castigantur. Abdiae 1. v. 16. Sicut bibistis in monte sancto meo. Confer Ier. 49, 12.Ezech. 23, 32. Metaphora sumta à conviviorum consuetudi. ne. *(Ad hanc etiam respicere Siracides videtur c. 32, 1. 2. add. Dn. Dilherr. t. 1. Dispp. A-ad p. 4-3.)* In quibus quantum quisque & quo modo temperatum bibere debeat, praescribebat συμποσίαρΧος, qui arbiteretiam & Magister convivii dictus fuit, quòd bibendi leges f-rebat. Hoc verò bibenti bus multis modis molestum erat. A mensura, si maior, quàm ferre commodè possent. A potu ipso, si vel tenuior vel fortior, vel amarior vel acerbior esset. *(Adhibet verò Christus verbum bibendi de suâ passion-, quia opprobria pro -ibo, tormenta pro potu fuerunt, cùm s-mmo d-siderio ipse pro nobis suerit passus. Huc fa it ill-d Ps. 11- -7 bibet de torrente. Etenim videtur Psaltes Christum quasi-ator-m aestu laborantem considerasse, qui cùm in torrentem incidit, non potest prae siti sibi temperare, quin avidissimè bibat. Sic Christus amore nostrae salutis exaestuans desiderando desiderabat de torrente passionis bibere.)*

*( Possumus. Notetur hîc confidentia humana ac vana praesumtio. Sciendum verò, quòd perseverantia sit donum DEI, Phil. 1, 6.c 2, 13.2. Thess. 3, 3.1. Petr. 1, 5.)*

## 20:23
v. 23. You shall drink my cup. James was killed by the sword by Herod, Act. 12, 2. John was driven into exile under Domitian. Euseb. b. 3. Hist. Eccles. c. 16. Chrysost. hom. 65. in Matth. Because of me and the grace of my preaching you shall die, you shall be participants of my passion. *(But John died a natural death. Some say, therefore, that, as Tertull. testifies in de praescr. haeret., John was indeed cast into boiling oil at Rome, but was saved by divine aid, and that therefore the will for martyrdom was not lacking, but the martyrdom for the will. Conf. more in Anal. on Ioh. 21, 22. What of the fact that he (John) himself felt the most grievous torments, when he saw the life of his life, i.e., J. C. the Savior, being roasted on the cross on Mount Calvary for three hours as if by a slow fire? The Savior speaks, however, in general about calamities to be endured for the sake of the truth. Conf. Rom. 8, 17.2. Cor. 1, 7. Thus John was beaten with scourges, Act. 5, 40. and endured many calamities in exile, Apoc. 1, 9. (so thinks B. D. Tarnov. in Ioh. p. 16.)* He did not predict exactly the same, yet in a certain way a similar passion ἐν μεταφορῇ, much less did he ascribe the same ἐνέρλειαν to both because, as Aug. says in book 1 of Qq. Ev. c. 26., he was about to suffer not by the necessity of a debt because of his own sin, but by charity to pay for our sins. *(Furthermore, the Savior calls the cup his own, so that he may warn us that that cup is not to be feared because of its bitterness, which he himself had brought to his own most beautiful lips, full of graces: and thus had rendered it most sweet and most to be sought after. Conf. Cant. 5, 13.Ps. 45, 3.)*

But to sit at my right hand &c. is not mine to give. Christ adjusts his answer to their petition. They were fostering dreams about an earthly kingdom, therefore Christ answers that he does not give such a primacy in a worldly kingdom; elsewhere Ioh. 10, 28. he says that he gives eternal life to his sheep.Apoc. 3. 21.

If anyone shall have conquered, I will give him to sit with me in my throne. *(Conf. c. 2, 10. item Luc. 22, 29.)* Others explain this in this way. It is not mine to give, i.e., it is not of my office and duty. But Christ attributes this to the Father, because as the Father is the principle of the Deity, so also of the actions, whence August. repeats everywhere, The Son acts through himself, but not from himself. *(B. D. Glassius also leans almost to the same in Exegesi Ev. in Festo Apostoli Iacobi.)* Tossanus explains it thus: To confer singular glory and honor in heaven, viz. out of human grace because of the intercession of parents, is not mine, i.e., I did not come into the world as a judge, about to distribute crowns of glory, but as a Mediator about to merit that glory for believers. Some* (such as Ambrosius, Remigius, and Beda.)* deceived by the Latin Interpreter read, to give to you. *(But it must be known that the to you is not a genuine part of the text, whence also no Oriental Interpreters recognize it in this place)* Others after Augustinus de Trinit. b. 1. c. 12. wish that Christ spoke about himself according to the form of a servant, whether his humanity is signified in such a way, as pleases some; or his status, as long as he was in this life: because he had not come then to distribute the seats of the kingdom, as Boyardus noted on Wednesday after the Sunday Reminiscere. *(This opinion pleases B. D. Walther in H. B. p. 787, where he deduces the same more prolixly. H. Grotius also seems to aim at the same, annotating in this place that Christ does not deny that he will distribute the offices of his kingdom, since what Paul 1. Cor. 12, 28. attributes to GOD the Father, he also Eph. 4, 8. and 11. attributes to Christ as well: But that he refers at least the glory of the whole dispensation to the Father.)* Others prefer, it is not mine, except to whom it has been prepared by the Father, namely because the will and power of the Father and the Son is the same. *(However, even among the ancients Ambrosius b. 8. de Fide c. 3, who himself however in b. 5. de Fid. c. 2. seems to think a little differently,) Epiphanius haeres. 69. Cyrillus b. 10. Thesauri c. 5. Augustinus in Ps. 126. Isidorus b. 1. ep. 137. think that Christ is speaking about eternal life, which δίκαιος μισθαπωδότης he does not give simply to those asking: but to those who have undergone labors: --κ ἔςιγδ δικαίου κριτοῦ τοὺς ἱὸρῶτας παριδεῖν, καὶ ῥαθύμοις παραοχεῖν, writes Isidorus in the cited book. And thus, namely concerning eternal election, B. D. Calixtus also explains it in Cone. Ev. p. 283. then also B. D. Glassius in Exeg. Ev. Festo*

Of the Apostle James, item Gr. S p. 667. noting that Christ wished to recall his disciples with these words from foolish opinions about an earthly kingdom, and therefore to say: if you wish to be participants of heavenly glory, be also truly believing and humble, having cast aside the foolish imagination about a certain worldly kingdom, and every desire for being carnally eminent, lest you demand rewards before labors. Looking back to which also St. Jerome thus explains in this place: The kingdom of heaven is not of the one giving, but of the one receiving. More correctly, however, by sitting at the right and left hand are understood πρωτοκλισίαι καὶι πρωτοκαθεδρίαι in a worldly kingdom, which those disciples had sought, but He Himself denies that He was sent into the world to distribute them. Conf. B. D. Hunnius in h. l. B. Par. L. on GOD the Father and His eternal Son § 60. item on eternal life § 39. Dn. D. Mueller Judaism p. 974. By no means, therefore, does Christ deny in general or absolutely, as if He Himself could not confer political dignities and establish kingdoms: for this is a work ad extra, and therefore, just as it belongs to the remaining persons of the H. Trinity, it belongs to Him as the eternal Son of GOD. Conf. Matth. 11, 27.Luc. 22, 29.Ioh. 5, 19. c. 10, 30. c. 16, 15. but He at least denies that it belongs to Him by reason of the Mediatorial office, or that He was sent by the Father into this world for this purpose. Much less is it to be inferred from this, as if Christ absolutely and simply disapproves of political government, which is sufficiently established elsewhere in the H. S. both by words, --m promises, and approved examples. See Prov. 8, 15Dan. 2, 20.Eccles. 10, 4.14. Wisdom 6, 3. Ioh. 19, 11. c. 10, 35. Rom. 13. 1. seqq. &c. Just as, however, from the fact that those who are not called by God to it are kept away from the administration of the Ecclesiastical office, it is not permitted to infer that the Ecclesiastical Ministry is simply disapproved of: so neither from the fact that Christ keeps away from the desire for Political government those who are not called by God to it, but to another, namely an Ecclesiastical office, is it permitted to infer that political government displeases GOD. Conf. B. Par. L. on Political Magistrate § 67.)

*( They were indignant. Corn. à Lapide on this place Not so much because of the vice of the ambition of John, since all were laboring under the same disease of ambition (let Bellarmine, Becanus, and other fellow-members of the Society of Cornelius hear this, who are entirely occupied with removing ambition from Peter. Let them hear:

nay, the Roman Pontiff, who, led by the highest ambition, desires to be called universal or Oecumenical Bishop, indeed to be superior to the Emperor himself) than that through it they feared being postponed to them. Furthermore, how great vices ambition and envy are, the same Cornelius shows from Gregory, Moral. book 5, last chapter, and Basil the Great, homily on envy. Let there also be added B. Par., Aphor. Theol. Pract., title Envy. But especially relevant here are the divine dissuasions, which the same man arranged in order in the School of Piety.

Latin:

v. 23. Calicem meum bibetis. Iacobus ab Herode gladio fuit occisus, Act. 12, 2. Iohannes sub Domitiano in exilium pulsus. Euseb. l. 3. Hist. Eccles. c. 16. Chrysost. hom. 65. in Matth. Propter me & praedicationis meaegratiam moriemini, meaepassionis participes eritis. *(At Iohannes morte naturali obiit. Dicunt igitur nonnulli, quòd, teste Tertull. de praescr. haeret. Iohannes quidem Romae in fervens oleum fuerit iniectus, sed divinâ ope servatus, quòdq; adeo non voluntas martyrio defuerit, sed voluntati martyrium. Conf. plura in Anal. ad Ioh. 21, 22. Quid quòd ipse (Iohannes) gravissimos senserit cruciatus, quando vidit vitam vitae suae h. e. I. C. Salvatorem in monte Calvariae per trihorium lento quasi igne assari in cruce. Loquitur verò Salvator in genere de calamitatibus propter veritatem sustinendis. Conf. Rom. 8, 17.2. Cor. 1, 7. Ita Iohannes fuit flagris caesus, Act. 5, 40. & in exilio multas calamitates sustinuit, Apoc. 1, 9. (ita sentit B. D. Tarnov. in Ioh. p. 16.)* Non planè eandem, tamen similem quodammodo passionem ἐν μεταφορῇ praedixit, multò minùs eandem utrique ἐνέρλειαν adscripsit quia, ut Aug. inquit lib. 1. Qq. Ev. c. 26., erat ille non necessitate debiti propter peccatum suum, sed ad solvenda peccata nostra caritate passurus. *(Coeterùm Salvator calicem, suum vocat, ut admoneat nos, non esse propter amaritudinem formidandum illum calicem, quem ipse labris suis pulcerrimis plenisque gratiarum admovisset: adeoq; suavissimum & maximè expetendum reddidisset. Conf. Cant. 5, 13.Ps. 45, 3.)*

Sedere autem ad dextram meam &c. non est meum dare. Christus responsum suum attemperat ad illorum petitionem. Fovebant illisomnia de regno terreno, Christus igitur respondet, talem quēdam primatum in regno mundano se non dare, aliàs Ioh. 10, 28. dicit, se vitam aeternam ovibus suis dare.Apoc. 3. 21.

Si quis vicerit, dabo ei sedere mecum in thronomeo. *(Conf. c. 2, 10. item Luc. 22, 29.)* Alii h. m. explicant. Non est meum dare i. e. non est mei muneris atque officii. Patri autem Christus hoc tribuit, quia Pater ut est principium Deitatis, ita & actionum, unde August. passim repetit, Filius agit per se, sed non à se *(Eodem ferè inclinat etiam B. D. Glassius in Exegesi Ev. in Festo Apostoli Iacobi.)* Tossanus ita explicat: Singularem in coelogloriam & honorem conferre, exgratiâ sc. humanâ propter intercessionem parentum, non est meum, i. e. non veni in mundum tanquam iudex, coronas gloriae distributurus, sed ut Mediator credentibus eam gloriam promeriturus. Quidam* (uti Ambrosius Remigius & Beda.)* delusi ab Interprete Latino legerunt, dare vobis. *(At sciendum, quod Tò vobis non sit genuina textûs pars, unde etiam nullus Interpp. Orientalium illud h. l. agnoscit)* Alii post Augustinum de Trinit. l. 1. c. 12. de se Christum loquutum esse volunt secundùm formam servi, sive ita eius humanitas significetur, ut nonnullis placet; sive status eius, quamdiu fuit in hâc vitâ: quia non venisset ad distribuendas tunc sedes regni, ut Boyardus notavit Fer. 4. post Dom. Reminiscere. *(Placet haec sententia B. D. Walthero in H. B. p. 787. ubi prolixiùs eandem deducit. Eodem etiam collimare videtur H. Grotius, annota-h. l. Christum non negare, se distributurum munia regni sui, cùm quod Paulus 1. Cor. 12, 28. DEO Patri tribuit, idem Eph. 4, 8. & 11. Christo quoque tribuat: Sed referre saltem gloriam totius dispensationis ad Patrem.)* Alii malunt, non est meum, nisi cui praeparatum est à Patre, nimirum quia eadem sit & voluntas & potentia Patris ac Filii. *(Ut ut verò etiam ex veteribus Ambrosius l. 8. de Fide c. 3.) qui ipse tamen l. 5. de Fid. c. 2. paullò aliter sentire videtur,) Epiphanius haeres. 69. Cyrillus l. 10. Thesauri c. 5. Augustinus in Ps. 126. Isidorus l. 1. ep. 137. Christum de vitâ aeternâ loqui existiment, quam δίκαιος μισθαπωδότης non dat simpliciter postulantibus: verùm iis, qui labores subierunt: --κ ἔςιγδ δικαίου κριτοῦ τοὺς ἱὸρῶτας παριδεῖν, καὶ ῥαθύμοις παραοχεῖν, scribit Isidorus l. c. Atq; ita, nempe de aeternâ electione exponit quoque B. D. Calixtus in Cone. Ev. p. 283. tum quoq; B. D. Glassius in Exeg. Ev. Festo

Apostoli Iacobi, item Gr. S p. 667. annotans, revocare his verbis Christum voluisse discipulos suos à stultis opinionibus de regno terreno, adeoq; dicere: si coelestis gloriae vultis esse participes, sitis etiam verè credētes & humiles, abiectâ stultâ de regno quodam mundano imaginatione, omnique carnaliter eminendi studio, ne postuletis praemia ante labores. Quo etiam S Hieronymus respiciens ita h l. exponit: Regnum coelorum non est dantis, sed accipientis. rectiùs tamen per Tò sedere ad dextram & sinistram intelliguntur πρωτοκλισίαι καὶι πρωτοκαθεδρίαι in regno mundano, quas discipuli illi petierant, sed ipse ad eas distribuendas in mundum se missum esse negat. Conf. B. D. Hunnium in h. l. B. Par. L. de DEO Patre & aet. eius Filio § 60. it. de vita aet. §. 39. Dn. D. Muellerum Iudaismi p. 974. Minimè proinde in genere sive absolutè Christus negat, quasi ipse non possit dignitates Politicas conferre ac regna stabilire: est enim hoc opus ad extra, adeoq; aeque ac reliquis SS. Trinit personis, ipsi ut aeterno DEI Filio hoc competit. Conf. Matth. 11, 27.Luc. 22, 29.Ioh. 5, 19. c. 10, 30. c. 16, 15. sed saltem id sibi competere negat ratione officii Mediatorii, seu quòd hoc fine non missus sit à Patre in hunc mundum. Multò minùs etiam hinc inferendum, quasi Christus absolutè & simpliciter improbet regimen Politicum, alibi satis tum dictis, --m promissis, tum exemplis probatis in Sc. S. stabilitum. Vid. Prov. 8, 15Dan. 2, 20.Eccles. 10, 4.14. Sapient. 6, 3. Ioh. 19, 11. c. 10, 35. Rom. 13. 1. seqq. &c. Quemadmodum verò exinde, quòd ab Ecclesiastici muner is administratione arcentur, qui ad illud non sunt à Deo vocati, non licet inferre, quòd Ministerium Ecclesiasticum simpliciter improbetur: ita nec ex eo, quòd Christus à regiminis Politici desiderio arcet, qui à Deo non ad illud, sed ad aliud, puta Ecclesiasticum, officium sunt vocati, inferre licet, quòd regimen Politicum DEO displiceat. Conf. B. Par. L. de Magistr. Polit. §. 67.)*

*( Indignati sunt. Corn. à Lapide adh h. l. Non tam vitio ambitioni Iohannis, cùm eodem omnes ambitionis morbo laborarem (audiant hoc Bellarminus, Becan. & alii Cornelii Socienni, qui toti in eo sunt, ut à Petro ambitionem removeant. Audia:

imò Pontifex Romanus, qui summâ ambitione ductus Episcopus universalis seu Oecumenicus audire gestit, quin ipsô Caesare esse superior) quàm quòd per eam metuerent eis postponi. Porrò quanta vitia ambitio & invidia sint, idem Cornelius ex Gregorio l. 5. Moral. c. ult. & Basilio M. homil. de invidiâ ostendit. Addatur quoque B. Par. Aphor. Theol. Pract. tit. In-idia. Cumprimis verò huc spectant dehortationes divinae, quas idem in ordinem digessit in Scholâ Pietatis.)*

## 20:25
(v. 25. Οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν etc. H. Grotius confirms this very thing with political examples in this place, who can be consulted.)

Latin:

*(v. 25. Οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν &c. Exemplis Politicis hoc ipsum confirmat H. Grotius h. l. qui potest consuli.)*

## 20:26
(v. 26. It shall not be so among you. This command ought to be referred among those things which were given to the Apostles, both as they were Apostles and as they sustained the person of the Ministers of the Church, but not indeed of all the faithful. For Christ distinguishes ecclesiastical ministry from political rule; teaching that the former, not the latter, was committed to the Apostles and their successors. Whence Hosius the Bishop (as is in the epistle of Athanasius to those living the solitary life), speaking to the Emperor, excellently says: TO YOU, he says, God has committed the empire, but to us those things which are of the Church, Christ has committed. Others add (so among others Bellarmine and Erasmus determine) that τὸ κατακυριεύειν and κατεξουσιάζειν does not signify simply to have power, but to abuse power tyrannically against subjects. Just as Theophylact also explains, namely ἐξουσιαςικῶς καὶτυρανι ικῶς προσφέρεσθαι. But since the Papists try to break the force of the argument from this, which our people seek against the political lordship of bishops from this place, it is well to be noted that Luke in the parallel place, chapter 22, 25, calls that which Matthew here calls κατακυριεύειν and χατεξουσιάζειν, simply κυριεύειν and ἐξουσιάζειν. Just as Mark also has ἄρχει. Thus Gen. 1, 28. God commands man κατακυριεύειν τῆς γῆς, yet Adam was not constituted a Tyrant, but Lord of the earth. What, that Christ says κατακυριεύοντας them to be called εὐεργέτας. But those who exercise tyrannical rule do not deserve to be so called. But especially it is to be observed that Christ opposes his words to the earthly desires of the Apostles. Now indeed the Apostles were by no means affecting tyrannical lordship, but at least political dominion. So that it is manifest that the Papists seek a hiding place here in vain in the compound words. Nor does it help them also the word ἔθνη. For this is general, denoting not only those who are Gentiles in religion, but peoples and nations in general. See Matth. 24, 7.Luc. 7, 5.c. 23, 2.Ioh. 11, 48.Actor. 2, 5. Compare more things pertaining to this in B. Par L. de Minist. Eccles. §. 295. Dn. D. Danhaur. in Id. Boni Interpr. p. 285. following, to which add Marcus Antonius de Dominis l. 1. de Rep. Eccles. c. 11. Nor yet by this prohibition of Christ is all power taken away from the Ecclesiastical Ministry, since the sayings Matth. 18, 17.Ioh. 20, 23. 2. Cor. -0, 8. c. 13, 10. 1. Tim. 5, 17. sufficiently prove it, but at least ἀυτοκπατοπικὴ & πολιτική. How certain leaders of the Church, especially in the greatest cities, even then in the time of Origen, arrogated and exercised this very thing for themselves, H. Grotius shows in this place. For long since Satan has acted so that he might afflict the Church of Christ with that shameful lust for dominating, avarice, lasciviousness, and pride of the Bishops. Especially, however, the Roman Bishop or Pope arrogated such a primacy to himself, which he also finally attained through the cooperation of Satan. So that we may see in him the Apostolic prediction fulfilled 2. Thess. 2, 4. We learn indeed from this place that the affectation of such a primacy is most alien to the institution of our Lord. Certainly if Christ had wished that Peter among the other Apostles, and his successors among the successors of the Apostles, should have dominion, He would have determined the present dispute far otherwise, and would have bestowed such a primacy upon Peter and his successors. But someone may object that Christ granted the power of the keys to the Apostles, Matth. 16, 19. and indeed the tradition of the keys denotes power. I respond by conceding that the tradition of the keys denotes the collation of power, but not of just any power. But what kind of power was granted to the Apostles and their successors through the tradition of the keys can be learned best of all from the present passage, namely such as is distinct from that power which is granted to Kings and Political Magistrates by GOD, namely Ecclesiastical. Compare the note to Matth. c. 16.)*

*( Whoever wishes to become great &c. The observance of order among the Ministers of the Church is not prohibited, see Eph. 4, 11.1. Thess. 5, 12.1. Tim. 5, 17. but the affectation of Dominion. Whence also some note that Christ did not prohibit being greater, but wishing to become great i.e. in an illegitimate way, to affect primacy out of pride and arrogance. Nor indeed is it sufficient to simulate humility at least in words (that which the Roman Pontiff does, striving to deceive God and men , whom nevertheless, as Corn. à Lapide notes in this place, the Roman Pontiff prefers that title: Servant of servants from this sanction of Christ) but Christ requires this above all, that we learn from Him true humility, which consists not in bare words, but in deeds, Matth. 11, 29. In this, whether the Roman Pontiff is the vicar of Christ, and whether he is not rather openly contrary to Him, he will easily judge who has considered the more than royal pomp and most proud edicts of the Roman Prelate. Therefore, the grave invective of Chrysostom, which Corn. à Lapide himself cites in this place from Chrysostom hom. 40 on 1 Cor., excellently fits the Roman Pontiff.)*

Latin:

*(v. 26. Non erit ita inter vos. Referri mandatum hoc inter ea debet, quae Apostolis data sunt, tum quat. erant Apostoli, tum quat. Ministrorum. Ecclesiae, non verò omnium fidelium personam sustinebant. Distingvit enim Christus ministerium Ecclesiasticum à regimine Politico; illud, non hoc Apostolis eorumque successoribus commissum esse docens. Unde Hosius Episcopus (ceu est in epist. Athanasii ad solitariam vitam agentes) Imperatori verba faciens egregiè: TIBI, ait, Deus imperium, nobis autem ea, quae sunt Ecclesiae, Christus commisit. Addunt alii (ita inter alios statuunt Bellarminus, Erasmus,) quòd τὸ κατακυριεύειν & κατεξουσιάζειν on significet simpliciter habere potestatem, sed potestate tyrannicè adversùs subditos abuti. Quemadmodum etiam Theophylactus exponit, nempe ἐξουσιαςικῶς καὶτυρανι ικῶς προσφέρεσθαι. Verùm cùm -ontificii infringere hinc conentur vim argumenti, quod nostrates contra Politicum Episcoporum dominatum ex h. l. petunt, probè notandum est, quòd Lucas in loco parall. cap. 22. 25. id quod Matthaeus hîc vocat κατακυριεύειν & χατεξουσιάζειν, simpliciter appellet κυριεύειν & ἐξουσιάζειν. Sicuti & Marcus habet ἄρχει. Sic Gen. 1, 28. iubet Deus hominem κατακυριεύειν τῆς γῆς, nec tamen Adamus Tyrannus, sed terrae Dominus constitutus fuit, Quid quòd Christus κατακυριεύοντας illos dicit vo-ari εὐεργέτας. Ast qui tyrannicum exercent imperium, haut ita vocari merentur. Cumprimis autem observandum quòd Christus verba sua opponat Apostolorum terrenis cupiditatibus. Iam verò Apostoli minimè tyrannicum affectabant Dominatum, sed saltem Politicum dominium. Ut ita manifestum sit, quòd Pontificii frustra in verbis compositis latibulum hîc quaerant. Nec iuvat quoque eosdem vocabulum ἔθνη. Est enim hoc generale, notans non solùm, qui religione sunt gentiles, sed in genere populos ac gentes. Vid. Matth. 24, 7.Luc. 7, 5.c. 23, 2.Ioh. 11, 48.Actor. 2, 5. Confer plura huc facientia apud B. Par L. de Minist. Eccles. §. 295. Dn. D. Danhaur. in Id. Boni Interpr. p. 285. seqq. quibus adde Marcum Anton. de Dominis l. 1. de Rep. Eccles. c. 11. Neque tamen per hoc Christi interdictum omnis Ministerio Ecclesiastico ademta potestas est, quippe quam satis probant dicta Matth. 18, 17.Ioh. 20, 23. 2. Cor. -0, 8. c. 13, 10. 1. Tim. 5, 17. sed saltem ἀυτοκπατοπικὴ & πολιτική. Quam ipsam quomodo Ecclesiae praesules quidam, cumprimis in maximis civitatibus, iam tum Origenis tempore, sibi arrogarint atque exercuerint, ostendit H. Grotius in h. l. Iampridem enim Satanas hoc egit, ut Christi Ecclesiam turpi illâ Episcoporum dominandi libidine, avaritiâ, lasciviâ ac superbiâ affligeret. Praecipuè tamen talem primatum arrogavit sibi Episcopus seu Papa Romanus, quem etiam per cooperationem Satanae tandē consequutus est. Ut ita impletam in eo videamus praedictionem Apostolicam 2. Thess. 2, 4. Discimus verò ex h. l., istiusmodi primatus affectationem esse à Domini nostri instituto alienissimam. Certè fi Christûs voluisset, ut Petrus inter coeteros Apostolos, illius que successores inter Apostolorum successores Dominatum haberent, longè aliter praesentem disceptationem determinasset, ac Petro eius que successoribus talem primatum tribuisset. Sed opponat aliquis, quòd Christus clavium potestatem Apostolis concesserit, Matth. 16, 19. iam verò clavium traditio noret potestatem. Resp. concedendo, clavium traditionem notare potestatis collationem, sed non cuius libet. Qualis antem potestatis Apostolis horumq; successoribus per clavium traditionem concessa sit, omnium optimè è praesenti loco disci potest, talis nempe, quae distincta est ab eâ potestate, quae Regigibus ac Magistratibus Politicis concessa à DEO est, videlicet Ecelesiastica. Conf. not. ad Matth. c. 16.)*

*( Qui voluerit magnus fieri &c. Non prohibetur ordinis inter Ministros Ecclesiae observatio, vid. Eph. 4, 11.1. Thess. 5, 12.1. Tim. 5, 17. sed Dominii affectatio. Unde etiam nonnulli notant, quòd Christus non prohibuerit, maiorem esse, sed magnum fieri velle h. e. illegitimo modo, ex superbia ac fastu affectare primatum. Nec veròsufficit, verbis saltem humilitatem simulare (id quod Pontifex facit Romanus, Deo hominibusque illudere satagen-, quem tamen ex hâc Christi sanctione titulum istum: Servi servorum praeferre, Corn. à Lapide h. l. annotat.) sed hoc cumprimis Christus requirit, ut veram humilitatem, quae non in nudis verbis, sed in factis consistit, ab ipso discamus, Matth. 11, 29.
