## 21:28
v. 128 Approaching the former. The emphasis is in this, that the parent himself approaches the son, and asks him to go into the vineyard. Irenaeus lib 4 c. 70. pag. 301. pursues the explanation of this parable at length.

Latin:

v. 128 Accedens ad priorem. Emphasis in eo est, quòd parens ipse accedit filium, & rogat eum, ut in vineam abeat. Explicationem huius parabolae prolixè persequitur Irenaeus lib 4 c. 70. pag. 301.

## 21:29
*(v. 29. Μεταμεληθεὶς. Bellarm. l. 1. de poenit. c. 7. column. 1185. B. rightly limits his proposition with the word fo-when he writes there that the word μεβαμελειας hardly ever occurs in Holy Scripture when it is a matter of the conversion of a sinful man.)*

Latin:

*(v. 29. Μεταμεληθεὶς. Rectè limitat Bellarm. l. 1. de poenit. c. 7. column. 1185. B. propositionem suam dictione fo-quando ibi scribit, vocem μεβαμελειαςnunquam ferè in Sc. S. currere, cùm de conversione hominis peccatoris agitur.)*

## 21:30
v. 30. Εγω, sc. απέρχομαι I am going immediately.

Latin:

v. 30. Εγω, sc. απέρχομαι mox abeo.

## 21:31
v. 31. Which of the two did what the father wanted. Hieronymus h. l. Furthermore, what is said, who of the two did the will of the father and they say, the last, it must be known that in true copies the last is not held, but the first, so that by their own judgment they may be condemned If however If we wish to read the latest, the interpretation is manifest, so that we may say that the Jews indeed understand the truth, but they prevaricate, and do not wish to say what they feel, just as they did not wish to say that they knew the Baptism of John was from heaven.

*( Publicans and harlots. Conf. Cameron in Myrothec. Ev. p. 85.)*

Προαγούσιν ημας εις την βασιλειαν i. e. they will enter the kingdom of heaven, because they did penance, but you will be excluded on account of impenitence. Luther: M-gen wohl ehe ins Himmelreich kommen/denn ihr. By the example of their conversion they go before you, and thus they arrive into the kingdom of heaven, which you Pharisees ought to have imitated. *(And that this is the genuine sense, writes Grotius, appears from that which follows, ύμειςιςοντες &c.)* They are called publicans and harlots by reason of the term from which, because having laid aside a sinful life they are converted. *(Conf. similar expressions Matth. 10, 3.c. 11, 5.c 26, 6.Rom. 4, 5.Iac. 2, 25.Apoc. 2, 19. add. B. D. Glass. Gr. S. p. 8. 9. But penitent harlots and publicans are said to precede the Pharisees, not as if these also, persevering in their malice, were to enter the kingdom of heaven after them: but the comparative locution here is to be explained by a negative, as is evident from Matth. 5, 20. conf. similar examples Ps. 118, 8.Luc. 8, 14. and add B. D. Glassius Gramm. Sacr. p 483. & 484. But clearly from these words of Christ we learn against the Novatians, that a place for penance is given. Conf. Ezech. 18, 21.c. 33, 11Matth, 3, 7.c. 9, 14.1. Tim. 1, 15. 16. To this also pertain the examples Gen. 3.Exod. 32, 2.2. Reg. 11,2. Par. 33.Matth. 9, 26.Luc. 7, 9.22. 23.Ioh. 8. 1. 1. Tim. 1. Let fallen sinners therefore raise themselves up, and rejoice, because Christ is to cast out no one who comes to him, Ioh 6, 37.)*

Latin:

v. 31. Uter è duobus fecit, quod voluit pater. Hieronymus h. l. Porrò, quod dicitur, quis ex duobus fecit voluntatem patr& illi dicunt, novissimus, sciendum est, in veris exemplaribus non haberi novissimū, sed primum, ut proprio iudicio cōdemnentu Si autem novissimum voluerimus legere, manifesta est interpretatio, ut dicamus, intelligere quidem veritatem Iudaeos, sed tergiversari, & nolle dicere, quod sentiunt, sicut & Baptismum Iohannis scientes esse de coelo, dicere noluerunt.

*( Publicani & meretrices. Conf. Cameronem in Myrothec. Ev. p. 85.)*

Προαγούσιν ημας εις την βασιλειαν i. e. ipsi ingredientur regnum coelorum, quia egerunt poenitentiam, vos autem excludemini propter impoenitentiam. Lutherus: M-gen wohl ehe ins Himmelreich kommen/denn ihr. Exemplo suae conversionis praeeunt vobis, & ita perveniunt in regnum coelorum, quod vos Pharisaei debebatis imitari. *(Atque hunc genuinum esse sensum, scribit Grotius, apparere ex eo, qùod sequitur, ύμειςιςοντες &c.)* Dicuntur publicani & meretrices ratione termini â quo, quia depositâ vitâ peccatrice convertuntur. *(Conf. similes locutiones Matth. 10, 3.c. 11, 5.c 26, 6.Rom. 4, 5.Iac. 2, 25.Apoc. 2, 19. add. B. D. Glass. Gr. S. p. 8. 9. Dicuntur verò meretrices & publicani poenitentes praecedere Pharisaeos, non quasi & hi in suâ malitiâ perseverantes post illos ingressuri sint regnum coelorum: sed exponenda hîc locutio comparativa per negativam, ceu patet ex Matth. 5, 20. conf. similia exempla Ps. 118, 8.Luc. 8, 14. ac adde B. D. Glassium Gramm. Sacr. p 483. & 484. Clarè verò ex his Christi verbis discimus contra Novatianos, dari poenitentiae locum. Conf. Ezech. 18, 21.c. 33, 11Matth, 3, 7.c. 9, 14.1. Tim. 1, 15. 16. Huc faciunt quoque exempla Gen. 3.Exod. 32, 2.2. Reg. 11,2. Par. 33.Matth. 9, 26.Luc. 7, 9.22. 23.Ioh. 8. 1. 1. Tim. 1. Erigant igitur se lapsi peccatores, ac gaudeant, quòd Christus neminem, qui ad ipsum venit, for as eiecturus sit, Ioh 6, 37.)*

## 21:32
v. 32. John came to you in the way of justice i. e. he was leading a just and of a harder life. Tossanus. Luther: Iohannes lehret euch ben rechten Beg. *(For he was preaching penance, and likewise was showing the way of true justice, to be sought in Christ through faith.)*

*( ού -πιςοτσατε αύτω. You did not obey his precepts.)*

Latin:

v. 32. Venit ad vos Iohannes in viâ iustitiae i. e. agebat iustam & durioris insti-nti vitam. Tossanus. Lutherus: Iohannes lehret euch ben rechten Beg. *(Praedicabat enim poenitentiam, pariterque viam iustitiae vera, in Christo per fidem quaerendae, ostendebat.)*

*( ού -πιςοτσατε αύτω. Non obtemperastis praeceptis eius.)*

## 21:33
*(v. 33. Another parable. See the exposition of this parable in Athanas. t. 2. tr. de dictis & interpret. parab. Evang. p. 324. q. 13. it. in Analect. ad Luke 20, 9. et seqq.)*

*( He planted a vineyard. See Anal. on c. 20, 2. and add. Psal. 79, 9.)*

ᾠκοδόμησε πύργο. He surrounded it with a wall, he fortified the place, since a tower is the strongest part of the walls. By the tower is denoted the protection of the vineyard, because, namely, watchmen are established in it, by whom they may be forewarned concerning harmful things. The vineyard is the people of Israel; the hedge is the law; the winepress is the ministry of doctrine; the tower is the kingdom and the temple. *(Conf. Zech. 2, 5.Matt. 16, 18.)*

And went abroad. God is said to have gone abroad, according to the opinion of the wicked servants.

Latin:

*(v. 33. Aliam parabolam. Vid. huius parabolae expositionem apud Athanas. t. 2. tr. de dictis & interpret. parab. Evang. p. 324. q. 13. it. in Analect. ad Luc. 20, 9. seqq.)*

*( Plantavit vineam. Vid. Anal. ad c. 20, 2. ac add. Psal. 79, 9.)*

ᾠκοδόμησε πύργο. Murum circumdedit, locum munivit, cùm turris sit fortissima pars moenium. Per turrim denotatur vineae custodia, quòd sc. vigiles in eâ constituti, à quibus de noxiis rebus praemoneantur. Vinea populus Israel; septum lex; torcular ministerium doctrinae; turris, regnum & templum. *(Conf. Zac. 2, 5.Matth. 16, 18.)*

Ac peregrè profectus. Dicitur Deus peregrè profectus, iuxta opinionem malorum servorum.

## 21:34
*(v. 34. That they might receive the fruits. Conf. Matt. 3, 8.10.John 15, 2. et seqq.)*

Latin:

*(v. 34. Ut acciperent fructus. Conf. Matth. 3, 8.10.Ioh. 15, 2. seqq.)*

## 21:35
*(v. 35. ἔδειραν &c. Conf. 2 Kings 21, 10.16.2 Chron. 36, 16.Neh. 9, 26.Jer. 44, 4. 5. 6. below c. 23, 34.37.Acts 7, 51.Heb. 11, 37. We learn from this what the lot of the servants of GOD is. Which, however, they ought to bear patiently, rejoicing that their reward is to be great in heaven, Matt. 5, 10. et seqq. 2 Tim. 2, 11.chap. 4, 5. et seqq.)*

Latin:

*(v. 35. ἔδειραν &c. Conf. 2. Reg. 21, 10.16.2. Par. 36, 16.Nehem. 9, 26.Ierem. 44, 4. 5. 6. infrà c. 23, 34.37.Act. 7, 51.Ebr. 11, 37. Discimus hinc, quae sit sors servorum DEI. Quam tamen patienter ferre debent, gaudentes, quòd merces ipsorum magna futura sit in coelis, Matth. 5, 10. seqq. 2. Timoth. 2, 11.cap. 4, 5. seqq.)*

## 21:37
*(v. 37. He sent his son to them. At length from this Isidore of Pelusium, lib. 4, ep. 166, against the Arians proves that Christ is the only-begotten son of GOD, not just some holy man, as those had been whom the Jews killed in the O.T. And he gathers this, among other things, from the fact that by killing many prophets they never suffered anything of the kind as they sustained by killing Christ, since when this deed was done, it brought upon the Jews punishments devoid of all pardon.)*

*( They will reverence my son. Luke chap. 20, 13, notably adds ισως. For the heavenly Father does not indicate by these words what the husbandmen were going to do, but what by right and merit was expected from them. That also is to be noted here, that τό perhaps in Luke c. 20, 13, does not at all undermine the certain foreknowledge of GOD, as Theophylact noted long ago, who notably writes on the said place, He said, 'Perhaps,' not as one ignorant of the future, that they were going to treat him worse than the prophets: but he says that which ought to have happened: for they ought to have reverenced him. But they were so far from reverencing him that they even killed him, which is to their greater accusation: because after God affirmed that this was good, that perhaps there be reverence for the son, they brought a clearly contrary judgment. This property, however, is often found in the Scriptures, as when it is said, if perhaps they may hear. (See Jer. 26, 3.c. 36, 37.Ezek. 12, 3.) For he did not say it there as one ignorant of the future, but so that some might not say that the foreknowledge of God is a necessary cause of disobedience, for that reason he uses such a figure of speech. Jerome has almost similar things, whose words B. D. Glassius cites in Gramm. Sacr. page 494, where he also rightly warns that the particle of doubting is sometimes rather of one hoping well, nay, and of one wishing and seriously desiring, as in this place, than of one doubting.)*

Latin:

*(v. 37. Misit ad eos filium. Prolixè hinc Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 4. ep. 166. contra Arianos probat, Christum esse unigenitum DEI filium, non sanctum modô aliquem virum, ceu illi fuerant, quos Iudaei in V. Test. interfecerunt. Idque inter alia colligit inde, quòd multos Prophetas interficiēdo nil eiusmodi unquam perpessi fuerint, quale sustinuerunt Christum interficientes, quippe cùm factum hoc omnis veniae expertes poenas Iudaeis pepererit.)*

*( Verebuntur filium meum. Lucas cap. 20, 13. notanter addit ισως. Neque enim indicat his verbis Pater coelestis, quid facturi essent coloni, sed quid iure ac meritò ab iis expectaretur. Illud quoque hîc notandum, quòd τόfortasse apud Lucam c. 20, 13. hautquaquam labefactet certam DEI praescientiam, ceu pridem notavit Theophylactus, qui notanter ad d. l. Fortè, dixit, scribit, non ut ignorans futurum, quòd peius eum affecturi essent, quàm Prophetas: sed illud dicit, quod fieri debebat: de bebant enim revereri illum. At illi usadeò non sunt reveriti, ut etiam occiderint, quod in maiorem corum accusationem est: quia postquam affirmavit Deus, bonum hoc esse, reverentiam fortè haberi filio, illi planè contrariam tulerunt sententiam. Haec autem proprietas saepè in Scripturis invenitur, ut quum dicitur, si fortè audiant. (Vid. Ierem. 26, 3.c. 36, 37.Ezech. 12, 3.) Neenim illic ignorans futurum ita dixit, sed ne quidam praescientiam Dei necessariam inobedientiae causam esse dicant, idcircò eiusmodi verborum figurâ utitur. Similia ferè habet Hieronymus, cuius verba adducit B D. Glassius Gramm. Sacr pag. 494. ubi etiam probè monet, quòd particula dubitantis aliquando potiùs benè sper antis, imò & optantis ac seriò cupientis sit, ut h. l., quàm dubitantis.)*

## 21:39
(v. 39. They cast him out of the vineyard. Christ suffered and was crucified outside the city, Heb. 13, 12.)

Latin:

*(v. 39. Eiecerunt ex vinea. Christus extra urbem passus & crucifixus est, Ebr. 13, 12.)*

## 21:41
(v. 41. He will miserably destroy them. But in Luke 20, 16. and Mark ch. 12, 9. the Pharisees seem to disapprove of this sentence. Response: Both happened. For first they themselves passed the sentence, as our Evangelist reports: afterwards, noticing where the parable tends, and that it was spoken about them, they denied that they would kill the Messiah, and thus deserve that punishment. Christ therefore, while they were silent, brings forth the sentence passed by them, but suppressed, and clearly says that they are those wicked husbandmen. Similar examples are found in 2 Sam. 12, 5. ff. 1 Kings 20, 39. ff. And in this way, which has now been stated, the blessed D. Walth. reconciles the Evangelists here in H. B. p. 787. Similarly also Hugo Grotius on this passage and others commonly. Also Lud. Capellus in Spicil. page 29, who nevertheless thinks that the Pharisees at least conceived in their mind, with their conscience dictating to them that it was just that the husbandmen should be miserably punished, and when they were about to speak it, they repressed themselves and held their tongue Daniel Heinsius strives to bring another remedy: he imagines, namely, that those words of v. 41. λέγούσιν αὐτῷ. were inserted by another, and that for the reason that verse follows 42. λέγει. άνεοίς ό Ιησούς. For which, however, there is no need, then verse 42 has been transposed & 43. of which here those should have-

been proposed. The same conjecture, even before Heinsius, Ludov. Capellus proposed for consideration to learned men in Spicileg. l. c. But Response 1. If it is permitted to rely on conjectures, it will go badly with the authentic text. It must be known v. 2. that all Greek Codices, those most ancient and most approved, which both the Parisians and the Londoners diligently collated, constantly acknowledge those words of v. 41. 3. Similarly the Oriental Interpreters, the Syrian, Arab, Ethiopian, Persian. 4. that the transposition of verses is unusual in sacred writings. Furthermore, the Jesuit Cornelius à Lapide comments well on this passage: Morally learn here, that just as a vineyard produces good grapes, even if its cultivators are wicked: So the Church and its faithful produce good works of virtues, even if its Pastors and Doctors are sometimes wicked, as the Scribes were. He illustrates the same with the example of Zeuxis, who was painting a boy with a basket of grapes so beautifully that the birds were deceived by the grapes, yet they did not fear the boy. This is to be observed against the common opinion of the Papists, that the efficacy and integrity of the Sacraments depend on the intention of the minister. Against which error the blessed Par. disputes in Confess. Cathol. art. XI. c. 1.)

Latin:

*(v. 41. Malè perdet eos. Ast Lucae 20, 16. ac Marc. c. 12, 9. videntur hanc sententiam improbare Pharisaei. Resp. Utrumque factum. Primùm enim ipsi tulerunt sententiam, uti noster refert Evangelista: postmodum animadvertentes, quò parabolat tendat, & quòd de ipsis dicta sit, negarunt, se Messiam occisuros, adeoque istam poenam promerituros. Christus igitur, tacentibus illis, sententiam ab ipsis latam, sed suppressam, profert ac clarè dicit, quòd ipsi sint mali illi agricolae. Similia ferè exempla reperiuntur 2. Sam. 12, 5. seqq. 1. Reg. 20, 39. seqq. Atque isto, quo iam dictum modo Evangelistas hîc conciliat B. D. Walth. in H. B. p. 787. Similiter quoque Hugo Grotius in h. l. ac alii communiter. it. Lud. Capellus in spicil. pag. 29. qui tamen existimat, Pharisaeos saltem animo concepisse, conscientiâ eorum illis id dictanre, iustum esse, ut malè mulctarentur agricolae, cumq iamiam id elocuturi essent, repressisse se ac ling tam continuisse Daniel Heinsius aliam afferre fatagit medelā: fingit nempe, verba illa v. 41. λέγούσιν αὐτῷ.inserta esse ab alio, idq ideò, quia sequitur vers. 42. λέγει. άνεοίς ό Ιησούς.Quibus tamen non opus sit, tùm transpositus sit vers. 42. & 43. quorum hic illi debueri-

esse propositus. Eandem coniecturam iam ante Heinsium virdoctis considerandam proposuit Ludov. Capellus in spicileg. l. c. Verùm Resp. 1. Si coniecturis inniti licet, malè agetur cum textu authentico. Sciendum v. 2. quòd omnes Codd. Graeci, antiquissimi illi ac probatissimi, quos tùm Parisienses, tùm Londinenses diligenter contulerunt, constanter illa verba v. 41. agnoscant. 3. Similiter Interpp. Orientales, Syrus, Arabs, Aethiops, Persa. 4. quòd insolens in sacris sit versuum transpositio. Porrò benè ad h. l. commentatur Ie suita Cornelius à Lapide: Moraliter disce hîc, quòd sicut vinea producit bonas uvas, etsi mali sint eius coloni: Ita Ecclesia eiusque fideles producant bona virtutum opera, etiamsi subinde mali sint eius Pastores & Doctores, uti erant Scribae. Illustrat idem hoc exemplo Zeuxis, qui puerum pingebat cum canistro uvarum adeò bellè, ut aves fallerent uvae, neq; tamen eaedem metuerent puerum. Observandum hoc contra communem Pontificiorum sententiam, quòd Sacramentorum efficacia & integritas dependeat ab intentione ministri. Quem contra errorem disputat B. Par. Confess. Cathol. art. XI. c. 1.)*

## 21:42
v. 42. Λίθν. The accusative is placed absolutely, as Act. 10, 36,38. i.e., as far as the stone is concerned. Authors of the Latin language also speak in this way. The eunuch whom you gave to me, what disturbances he has caused! For the LXX Interpreters, that form of speaking is most customary. See Numer. 32, 4.Ios. 1, 3.2. Reg. 1, 4. Furthermore, the Cabbalists explain -- stone by -- father and -- son, because the Jews rejected both the Father and the Son by their own unbelief. *(Otherwise, by stone in this place is understood Christ, compare Ps. 118, 22.Esa. 28, 16.Act. 4, 11.Eph. 2, 20.1. Petr. 2, 7. &c.)* --

Builders i.e., the wise -- builders, who are occupied with the building of the world for their whole lifetime, i.e., with the law. *(The Senators of the Great Sanhedrin are understood. Compare Act. 4, 11. In the N. T., the ministers of the Church are called by the same kind of speaking σανεργοι όν τε οίχοσομε τού θεού, 1. Cor. 3, 9. Compare Eph. 4, 11, 12.)*

έγμενννεθη είς χεθαλεν has been established as the head. Head of the corner is named the chief cornerstone, which contains and embraces two walls, and fortifies the house against the impacts of passing carriages. Irenaeus book 4, chapter 42, page 276. Christ is the chief cornerstone sustaining all things and gathering into one faith of Abraham those who are fit from both Testaments for the building of GOD. *(Conf. Act. 4, 11,Rom. 9, 33.1. Cor. 3, 11.Es. 28, 16.Eph. 2, 14.20.1. Petr. 2, 6. seqq. Isidore of Pelusium lib. 1. ep. 497, St. Augustine, Basil, Euthymius, Cassiodorus, and among the more recent, B. D. Hunnius explain it in almost the same way. This can also be accommodated to the fact that in no other name is there salvation, except in this one. See Act. 4, 12.c. 15, 11.Rom. 3, 24. seqq.)*

ωτιά Κνείου έγειαοεο αὐτῇ, i.e. γονια this cornerstone was established by the Lord. *(Theophylact explains it thus. Others think the feminine was placed by Hebrew phrase for τούβο. Thus Ps. 27.One thing I have asked of the Lord. Casaubon approves the latter in his notes, because it is read word for word thus in David, as also Marc. 12, 11. *(Moreover, the divine ordination of the passion of Christ is signified here, to an end salutary for the whole human race. For while those inept builders, the Pharisees and Priests, cast this precious stone onto Mount Calvary and held it in contempt, divine wisdom so directed that worst deed of the Jews beyond all their intention, that the foundation of all our salvation was thus cast. Conf. Act. 2, 23. 24.)*

Latin:

v. 42. Λίθν. Accusativus absolutè ponitur, ut Act. 10, 36,38. q. d. quod ad lapidem attinet. Latinae linguae autores etiam sic loquuntur. Eunuchum quem de disti mihi, quas turbas dedit! LXX. Interpp. usitatissima est illa loquendi forma. Vid. Numer. 32, 4.Ios. 1, 3.2. Reg. 1, 4. Porrò -- lapis per -- Cabbalistae exponunt --pater & --filius, quòd Iudaei tam Patrem, quàm filium suà incredulitate reiecerint. *(Aliàs per lapidem h. l. intelligitur Christus, conf. Ps. 118, 22.Esa. 28, 16.Act. 4, 11.Eph. 2, 20.1. Petr. 2, 7. &c.)*

Aedificantes i. e. sapientes --aedificatores, qui occupati sunt circa aedificium mundi toto vitae tempore i. e. circa legem. *(Intelliguntur Senatores Synedrii Magni. Conf. Act. 4, 11. In N. T. ministri Ecclesiae eod. dicendi genere vocantur σανεργοι όν τε οίχοσομε τού θεού,1. Cor. 3, 9. Conf. Eph. 4, 11, 12.)*

έγμενννεθη είς χεθαλεν constitutus est pro capite. Caput anguli nominatur lapis angularis princeps, qui duos parietes continet atque complectitur, domumque munit contra impulsus praetereuntium curruum. Irenaeus l. 4. c. 42. p. 276. Christus lapis summus angularis omnia sustinens & in unam fidem Abrahae colligens eos, qui ex utroq Testamento apti sunt in aedificationē DEI. *(Conf. Act. 4, 11,Rom. 9, 33.1. Cor. 3, 11.Es. 28, 16.Eph. 2, 14.20.1. Petr. 2, 6. seqq. Eodem ferè modo explicant quoque Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 1. ep. 497. S. Augustinus, Basilius, Euthymius, Cassiodorus, è recentioribus B. D. Hunnius. Potest etiam hoc eò accommodari, quòd in nullo alio nomine sit salus, praeterquam in hoc uno. Vid. Act. 4, 12.c. 15, 11.Rom. 3, 24. seqq.)*

ωτιά Κνείου έγειαοεο αὐτῇ, sc. γονια lapis angularis iste à Domino constitutus est. *(Ita exponit Theophylactus. Alii putant,, foemininum positum phrasi Ebraicâ pro τούβο. Sic Ps. 27.Unam petii à Domino. Posterius probat Casaubonus in notis, quia in Davide ad verbum sic legitur, ut & Marc. 12, 11. *(Significatur autem hîc divina ordinatio passionis Christi, ad finem toti generi humano salutarem. Dum enim inepti illi aedificatores, Pharisaei & Sacerdotes, lapidem hunc pretiosum in montem Calvariae proiecerunt ac contemtim habuerunt, divivina sapien tia pessimum illud Iudaeorum factum praeter omnē illorum intentionem ita dixerit, ut iactum ita fuerit fundamentum omnis nostrae salutis. Conf. Act. 2, 23. 24.)*

## 21:43
*(v. 43. The kingdom of GOD shall be taken away from you &c. Conf. c. 8, 12.c. 22. 8, 9.Luc. 14, 21.Act. 13, 46, 47.Rom. 9, 10 11.2. Thess. 2, 3,10. seqq. And from this it is understood, both that the promises by which the stability of the Church is promised for eternity are to be understood of the universal Church, such as the promise Esa. 59, 21. and that God with the word is not tied to a certain place or people. But that the salutary knowledge of GOD and divine things has been taken away from the Jews, and ignorance and fables have succeeded in its place, the Talmud, to which they are entirely devoted today, speaks sufficiently.)*

*( Its fruits. See Luc. 3, 8.Rom. 6, 22.Gal. 5, 2.Ephes 5, 9)*

Latin:

*(v. 43. Auferetur à vobis regnum DEI &c. Conf. c. 8, 12.c. 22. 8, 9.Luc. 14, 21.Act. 13, 46, 47.Rom. 9, 10 11.2. Thess. 2, 3,10. seqq. Atque hinc intelligitur, tum quòd promissiones, quibus Ecclesiae stabilitas in aeternum promittitur, intelligendae sint de Ecclesia universali, ceu promissio Esa. 59, 21. tum quòd Deus cum verbo non sit ad certum locum vel populum alligatus. Quòd verò à Iudaeis salutifera DEI rerumque divinarum cognitio ablata sit, in illiusque locum ignorantia ac fabulae successerint, satis loquitur Talmud, cui toti hodie dediti sunt.)*

*( Fructus suos. Vid. Luc. 3, 8.Rom. 6, 22.Gal. 5, 2.Ephes 5, 9)*

## 21:44
v. 44. λιχμεσμεν will crush. This word properly signifies to separate by winnowing the chaff from the grain, scattered into small pieces.

It will scatter so that it flies apart into the smallest parts. Whoever opposes himself to Christ will feel destruction. Against whom Christ exerts His divine power, he is crushed. *(For in the Holy Scripture, perfect slaughter is accustomed to be signified by the breaking of earthen vessels. See Is. 30, 14.Jer. 19, 11. St. Jerome in this place: It is one thing to offend Christ through evil works, another to deny him. He who is a sinner, and yet believes in him, indeed falls upon the stone, and is broken, but is not entirely crushed: for he is reserved through repentance for salvation. But he upon whom that stone shall have fallen, that is, he upon whom the stone itself shall have rushed, and who shall have utterly denied Christ: it shall so crush him, that not even a shard shall remain, in which a little water may be drawn. Hugo Grotius thinks the -al sense of this saying to be this. He who shall strike against him (Christ) while he was acting on earth, shall feel his own weakness to his own detriment. But he who shall persist in opposing him, after he shall have already been raised into the heavenly palace, shall perish as thoroughly as a shard, upon which a huge rock is rolled down from a high place. It seems, however, to Grotius that there is a reference to the passage Dan. 2, 44. That indeed happened to the Jews by the destruction of Titus, and will happen much more on the day of the final judgment. It is well to be noted, however, that Christ becomes a stone of stumbling by accident, when by himself he is made nothing but a stone of eternal salvation. See Is. 28, 16. Let us therefore strive, that we may not strike against this stone but rather that as living stones we may be built up upon him. Compare above c. 11, 6. 1 Pet. 2, 4. following.)*

I. The just rejection of the Jews for their contempt of the Gospel and the calling of the Gentiles, proposed in the Parable of the Wedding, v. 1-14. II. The captious interrogation of the Pharisees concerning the tribute to be paid to Caesar, and Christ's solid response, v. 15-22. Just as also the refutation of the Sadducees, who were raising the question concerning the resurrection of the dead, v. 23-32. III. The question of the lawyer concerning the greatest commandment, and his instruction, v. 35-40. IV. The confusion of the Pharisees through the question concerning the Messiah, v. 41 to the end.

Latin:

v. 44. λιχμεσμενcomminuet. Significat verbum hoc propriè ventilādo paleas de frumento minutim dispersas separare.

Dissipabit ut in minutissimas partes dissiliat. Qui Christo se opponit, exitium sentiet. Contra quem Christus divinam suam virtutem exerit, comminuitur. *(Solet enim in Sc. S. per contritionem vasorum testaceorum perfecta internecio figni ficari. Vid. Es. 30, 14.Ier. 19, 11. S. Hieron. in h. l. Aliud est offendere Christum per mala opera, aliud negare. Qui peccator est, & tamen in illum credit, cadit quidem super lapidem, & confringitur, sed non omninò conteritur: reservatur enim per poenitentiam ad salutem. Super quem verò ille ceciderit h. e. cui lapis ipse irruerit, & qui Christum penitus negaverit: sic conteret eum, ut nec testa quidem remaneat, in quâ hauriatur aquae pusillum. Hugo Grotius -alem dicti huius sensum esse putat. Qui in ipsum (Christum) in terris agētem impinget, fentiet imbecillitatem suam damno suo. At qui perstiterit in eo oppugnando, postquam iamtum erit evectus in coelestem regiam, tam funditus peribit, quàm testa, in quam saxum ingens -x sublimi loco devolvitur. Videtur autem Grotio respici ad locum Dan. 2, 44. Id verò contigisse Iudaeis excidio Titi, multòque magis eventurum in extremiudicii die. Probè autem notandum, quòd Christus per accidens fiat petra scandali, cùm per se non nisi aeternae salutis petra fit. Vid. Es. 28, 16. Demus igitur operam, ne in hunc lapidem impingamussed potius ut tanquam lapides vivi illi superaedi ficemur. Conf. suprà c. 11, 6. 1. Petr, 2, 4. seqq.)*

Iusta Iudaeorum ob Evangelii contemtum reiectio ac gentium vocatio, proposita in Parab. de Nuptiis, v. 1 14. 11. Captiosa Pharisaeorum de censu Caesari persolvendo interrogatio, -c solida Christi responsio, v. 15. 22. sicuti & Sadducaeorum, de refurrectione mortuorum quaestionem moventium, refutatio, v. 23. 32. III. Legisperiti de maximo praecepto quaestio, eiusdemque informatio, v. 35. 40. IV. Pharisaeorum per quaestionem de Messiâ confusio, v. 41. ad fin.)*

## 22:1
v. 1. άποχειθεις is used in the Hebrew phrase for that which is, he began to speak.

*( όν παραβολαῖς i. e. parabolically. For only one parable is proposed here: yet it could have happened that more were proposed by Christ at that time, which, however, were not all noted down by the Evangelists. Furthermore, concerning the correct exposition of the parables proposed in the Gospel, the rules handed down everywhere by authors can be compared, concerning which see in the Analysis above at c. 13, 3. Add also B. D. Bald. in Idea Dispos. Bibl. p. 201. seqq.)*

Latin:

v. 1. άποχειθεις phrasi Ebraeâ ponitur pro eo, quod est, sormonem exorsus est.

*( όν παραβολαῖς i. e. parabolicè. Una enim tantùm proponitur hîc parabola: potuit tamen fieri, ut plures tum fuerint à Christo propositae, quae tamen non omnes ab Evangelistis annotatae. Coeterùm de Parabolarum in Evang. propositarum dextrâ expositione conferri possunt regulae, passim ab autoribus traditae, de quibus in Anal. suprà ad c. 13, 3. Add. quoque B. D. Bald. in Idea Dispos. Bibl. p. 201. seqq.)*

## 22:2
v. 2. The kingdom is made like unto &c. See the exposition of this parable in Irenaeus lib. 4. c. 70. p. 303. *(Item in Gregory the Great, homily 38. on the Gospel.)* The Bridegroom is most noble by origin, most beautiful in appearance, most eminent in power, most splendid in virtues. The bride is most despised by birth, most wretched in countenance, most weak in strength, most covered in vices. By the wedding Tossanus understands the spiritual union of Christ with the Church. *(But B. Par. L. de Eccl. §. 18. warns that rather, with B. D. Chemnitius, one should understand in this parable the personal wedding, between the Son of God and the assumed human nature (concerning which Cantic. 2, 11.) than the spiritual one between Christ and the Church, (concerning which 2. Cor. 11, 2.Eph. 5, 32.Apoc. 21, 2.9.) since the wedding feast is later distinguished from those, through which are properly understood the benefits which God distributes in the Church, and which Christ merited for the faithful by those personal nuptials. Conf.)* Isa. 25, 6.Rev. 19, 7,9.

CHAP. XXII. SUMMARY. I.

Latin:

v. 2. Simile factum est regnum &c. Expositionemhuius parabolae vide apud Irenaeum lib. 4. c. 70. p. 303. *(Item apud Gregorium M. homil. 38. in Evangel.)* Sponsus est origine nobilissimus, specie formosissimus, potentiâ eminentissimus, virtutibus splendidissimus. Sponsa ortu despectissima, vultu deterrimâ, viribus infirmissima, viti is opertissima. Per nuptias Tossanus intelligit spiritualem Christi cum Ecclesia unionem. *(Verùm B. Par. L. de Eccl. §. 18. monet, potiùs cum B. D. Chemnitio in hâc parabolâ intelligendas esse nuptias personales, inter Filium Dei & adsumtam humanam naturam (de quibus Cantic. 2, 11.) quàm spirituales inter Christum & Ecclesiam, (de quibus 2. Cor. 11, 2.Eph. 5, 32.Apoc. 21, 2.9.) cùm ab illis postea distingvatur convivium nuptiale, per quod propriè intelliguntur beneficia, quae Deus in Ecclesia distribuit, quaeque Christus personalibus illis nuptiis fidelibus promeruit. Conf. Esai. 25, 6.Apoc. 19, 7,9.

CAP. XXII. SUMMA. I.

## 22:3
v. 3. And sent forth servants &c. By the former servants are understood the Prophets, by the latter the Apostles. *(Especially also John the Baptist, above c. 3, 2. below c. 21, 32.)*

Καλέσαι τούς χεχλημένους to call those that were bidden. i. e. those who, before the preparation of the nuptial banquet, had been invited to it. For it is customary for guests to be invited some days before the wedding. Augustine in Psalm. 58. It is the part of servants to invite, of the Lord to separate. *(It is to be noted here, that this calling on the part of GOD is 1. Catholic, Matt. 28, 19.Mark 16, 15.Col. 1, 6.Ezek. 18, 23.1. Tim. 2, 4.2. Peter 3, 9. 2. serious, Ezek. 33, 11. above c. 21, 41.Luke 19, 41. 3. merely gratuitous, Eph. 2, 11.c. 5, 8.2. Tim. 1, 9. Compare at greater length B. D. Hunnius in this place, B. P. L. on the Church §. 41. seqq.)*

*( They would not come. Whom nevertheless God the King seriously desired to come, as is evident from His anger and punishment v. 7. The calling was therefore on the part of God sufficiently eff-ective, but hindered by the proper fault of men, namely by the contempt of the calling. Compare Matt. 23, 37.Luke 7, 30.John 3, 18. & 36.Acts 7, 51.c. 13, 46.2. Thess. 8.2. Thess. 2, 10. & 12. Although indeed men can resist the divine calling and hinder it, they cannot however convert themselves to God by their own powers or salutarily. Nor would they ever come, unless God were to prevent all by His gratuitous calling. Compare Rom. 9, 16.John 15, 5.Phil. 2, 13.1. Cor. 2, 14.2. Cor. 3, 5. It is well to be noted, however, that the external use of the means of faith is still placed in the will of man. God has indeed promised that through external obedience He wills to work internal obedience of faith, Rom. 10, 7. Let us therefore use the means divinely ordained for salvation, and let us not resist the operation of the Holy Spirit.)*

Latin:

v. 3. Et emisit servos &c. Per priores servos intelliguntur Prophetae, per posteriores Apostoli. *(Cumprimis etiam Ioh. Baptista, suprà c. 3, 2. infrà c. 21, 32.)*

Καλέσαι τούς χεχλημένουςut invitatos vocarent. i. e. eos, qui ante apparatū cōvivii nuptialis ad illud invitati fuerant. Solent enim aliquot diobus ante nuptias convivae invitari. Augustinus in Psalm. 58.Servorum est invitare, Domini separare. *(Notandum hîc, quod vocatio haec ex parte DEI sit 1. Catholica,Matth. 28, 19.Marc. 16, 15.Col. 1, 6.Ezech. 18, 23.1. Tim. 2, 4.2. Petri 3, 9. 2. seria,Ezech. 33, 11. suprà c. 21, 41.Luc. 19, 41. 3. merè gratuita,Eph. 2, 11.c. 5, 8.2. Tim. 1, 9. Conf. pluribus B D. Hunnium in h. l. B. P. L. de Eccles. §. 41. seqq.)*

*( Nolebant venire. Quos tamen Deus Rex seriò cupiebat venire, ceu patet ex eius irâ & poenâ v. 7. Fuit igitur vocatio ex parte Dei satis eff-ax, sed impedita propriâ hominum culpâ, vocationis nempe contemtu. Conf. Matth. 23, 37.Luc. 7, 30.Ioh. 3, 18. & 36.Actor. 7, 51.c. 13, 46.2. Thess. 8.2. Thess. 2, 10. & 12. Licet verò homines divinae vocationi possint repugnare eamque impedire, non tamen ad Deum ex propriis viribus sive salutariter sese convertere possunt. Nec unquam etiam venirent, nisi Deus gratuitâ suâ vocatione omnes praeveniret. Conf. Rom. 9, 16.Ioh. 15, 5.Philipp. 2, 13.1. Cor. 2, 14.2. Cor. 3, 5. Probè tamen notandum, quòd externa mediorum fidei usurpatio sit adhuc in hominis arbitrio posita. Promisit verò Deus, quòd per externam obedientiam operari velit internam fidei obedientiam, Rom. 10, 7. Utamur igitur mediis divinitus ad salutem ordinatis, nec Spiritus Sancti operationi resistamus.)*

## 22:4
v. 4. My dinner I have prepared. Chrysost. homil. 41. Oper Imperf. I have adorned the tables of the Scriptures.

*( Fatlings &c. The abundance and greatness of the benefits offered in the Gospel are signified. Chrysostom by fatlings understands the Prophets, by oxen the Priests, because as oxen are the leaders of the flock, so they are the princes of the people. Jerome takes oxen for the martyrs, as those who were sacrificed like victims, but fatlings for spiritual men, who are as it were fattened by the heavenly bread. But it must be known, that the abundance of divine grace is thus described parabolically. Compare Isa. 25, 6.c. 30, 22.c. 35, 60. 61. 62.John 6, 51.

Latin:

v. 4. Prandium meum paravi. Chrysost. homil. 41. Oper Imperf. Scripturarum mensas ornavi.

*( Altilia &c. Significantur beneficiorum in Ev. oblatorum ubertas & magnitudo. Chrysostomus per altilia intel igit Prophetas, per tauros Sacerdotes, quòd ceu tauri gregis duces, ita illi sint principes populi. Hieronymus tauros de martyribus accipit, ut qui tanquam hostiae immolati, altilia verò de hominibus spiritualibus, qui pane coelesti quasi saginati. Sed sciendum, quòd parabolicè ita describatur gratiae divinae copia. Conf. Es. 25, 6.c. 30, 22.c. 35, 60. 61. 62.Ioh. 6, 51.)*

## 22:5
v. 5. Another into his farm &c. Chrysost. hom. 41. Oper. Imperf. These are not sins in themselves, but by preferring them to God, you make them to be sins. Glossa Ordin. h l. To go into the farm is to apply oneself immoderately to earthly labor : but to trade is to gape after earthly gains. (But it must be thought about again and again, how preposterous and foolish, nay, most shameful it is, to choose earthly fields after having put heavenly feasts behind, that is, to prefer the husks of swine to the delights of kings.)

Latin:

v. 5. Alius in villam &c. Chrysost. hom. 41. Oper. Imperf. Haec per se peccata non sunt, sed tu praeferendo ea Deo, facis esse peccata. Glossa Ordin. h l. In villam ire est terreno labori immoderatè in-umbere: negotiari verò est terrenis lucris inhiare. *(Cogitandum verò etiam atque etiam est, quàm praeposterum sit ac stultum, imò turpissimum, coelestibus epulis posthabitis terrenos eligere agros h. e. regum deliciis porcorum praeferre siliquas.)*

(v. 6. The rest took his servants &c. Compare the Analysis to the preceding Chapter, v. 35. The modern Romanists are similar to the Jews, which the pyres of the Spanish inquisition and the streams of the Parisian slaughter, and many other specimens of the horrendous persecution of confessors, speak of sufficiently. Compare Apocal. 17, 6.)

Latin:

*(v. 6. Reliquitenuerunt servos &c. Conf. Anal. ad Cap. praeced. v. 35. Iudaeis similes sunt hodierni Romanenses, id quod inquisitionis Hispanicae rogi ac Parisiensis lanienae rivuli, multaque alia horrendae persecutionis confessorum specimina satis loquuntur. Conf. Apocal, 17, 6.)*

## 22:7
(v. 7. The king having sent his armies destroyed the murderers. The Anabaptists ineptly gather from this, that if God himself, who is understood here by the King, destroyed the murderers, it follows that the right of the sword and the power of waging war does not belong to the Magistrate. Resp. 1. Subordinated things are not opposed. 2. A parable is proposed here. Now, parabolic Theology is not argumentative. 3. It is a matter of the contempt of the word and the calling to the heavenly wedding, which we readily grant is not to be vindicated by capital punishment. But it is not to be inferred from thence that other crimes, for which such a penalty is established in Holy Scripture, are not worthy of capital punishment, and that such transgressors ought not to be punished by the Magistrate. 4. There are indeed some Interpreters, whom Hugo Grotius also follows, who understand by armies the Angels, who are so called 1 Kings 22, 19. 2 Chron. 18, 18. Luke 2, 13., and by whose ministry God governs kingdoms: and therefore through them sends wars, famine, and pestilence, all of which thundered as if in one assault upon the city of Jerusalem . Most interpreters, however, such as Theophylact, B. D. Hunnius, Dn. D. Friedlieb in h. l., B. D. Bald. in idea Dispos. Bibl. p. 204, B. D. Frantzius in de Interpr. Sc. S. p. 590, maintain that this prediction was fulfilled in the Jews by the Roman army, as being the by which God punished both the contempt of the truth and other most grave crimes of the Jews. So far, therefore, is it from being the case that just wars are disapproved here, that they are rather established.)

Latin:

*(v. 7. Rex missis excr-itibus suis perdidit homicidas. Ineptè hinc colligunt Anabaptistae, quòd si Deus ipse, qui per Regem hîc intelligitur, perdidit homicidas, sequitur quòd Magistratui non competat ius gladii ac belli gerenai potestas. Resp. 1. subordinata non sunt opposita. 2. Proponitur hîc parabola. Iam verò Theologia parabolica non est argumentativa. 3. Agitur de contemtu verbi & vocationis ad nuptias coelestes, quem supplicio capitali non esse vindicandum, ultrò largimur. Inde verò non inferendum, quòd nec alia scelera, quibus in Sc. S. talis constituta poena est, capitali supplicio digna sint, quòdq; tali transgressores à Magistratu affici nō debeant. 4. Sunt quidem nonnulli Interpretes, quos Hugo etiam Grotius sequitur, qui per ex-rcitus intelligunt Angelos, qui 1. Reg. 22, 19. 2. Paral. 18, 18. Luc. 2, 13. ita dicuntur, quorumque ministerio Deus regna gubernet: ac proinde per eos immittat bella, famem & pestilentiam, quae omnia uno quasi impetu in Hierosolymorum urbem detonuerintplerique tamen interpretes, uci Theophylactus, B. D. Hunnius, Dn. D. Friedlieb in h. l. B D. Bald. in ideâ Dispos. Bibl. p. 204. B. D. Frantzius in de Interpr. Sc. S. p. 590. statuunt, quòd praedictio haec impleta in Iudaeis per exercitum Romanum fuerit, utpote per quem Deus tum veri contemtum, tum alia gravissima Iudaeorum scelera punivit. Tantum igitur abest, ut iusta bella hîc improbentur, ut potiùs stabiliantur.)*

## 22:8
