## 23:2
v. 2. In the Chair of Moses. that is, destined for the reading of the Mosaic and Prophetic books. (For Moses here signifies the books of the O. T. in general. Nor were the Scribes and Pharisees successors in the Mediatorial office of Moses, but in the doctrine, which they ought to have delivered according to the mind of Moses and the books of the O. Test., as Camero rightly notes in Myroth p. 104. Thus also the Fathers explain it. Jerome on this passage: By the Chair he shows the doctrine of the Law. Theophylactus similarly: The Lord says, he writes, concerning those who sit in the Chair of Moses, i. e. those who teach the things which are contained in the law. Conf. Nehem. 8, 4.9.Act. 15. 21 Thus also Hilary: He commands, he says, to obey all the mandates of the law. Indeed, similar opinions of the Pontificians themselves will be brought forward a little later. But Cornelius à Lapide errs when by the Chair in this passage he understands absolutely the authority of teaching and commanding. And furthermore he infers, that when the Roman Pontiff sits in the Chair of Peter, he himself, although as a private man he may err, yet when he defines something concerning faith from the Chair, i. e. from Pontifical authority, he cannot err, on account of the assistance of the Holy Spirit. But the contrary is rather evident from this assertion and warning of Christ, so far is it from being the case that that erroneous opinion of the Pontificians concerning the infallibility of the Pope can be confirmed from it. For just as the Pharisees and Scribes, even though according to the testimony of our Savior they sat in the Chair of Moses, and thus taught with the same authority as Moses, were nevertheless by no means immune from the danger of error on that account, nay, they cherished most grave errors, which the Savior also taxes here and there. see, above c. 5 & 15. also. also. Mark 7. so, granted that the Roman Pontiff sits in the Chair of Peter, he is nevertheless no more to be considered immune from the danger of erring than they were. And how, I ask, could the Roman Pontiff, even if he were to sit in the Chair of Peter at Rome in the highest degree, not be able to slip? Truly, if the protoplasts, created in the image of GOD, could slip in the garden of Paradise, the Angels in the dwelling of heaven, Judas, Thomas, nay Peter himself in the choir of the Apostles, why not also the Roman Pontiff in the feigned throne of Peter? And this all the more, because he exalts himself against God and his inept dogmas against the revealed word of GOD, (to which whoever adds anything, is cursed, Apoc. 22, 18. if even an Angel from heaven were to be, Gal. 1, 8.) he not only adds, but even equates, nay prefers, as from the feigned cults of the saints, impious dispensations, etc., has been shown elsewhere. Confer Gregory the Great, book 6, epistle 5. But that must be well noted, that sometimes the Chairs of the more sincere Doctors of the Church are occupied by false teachers or impious successors. Thus, Uriah the idolater succeeded Aaron, as did Annas and Caiaphas, who condemned Christ. It will not, therefore, be absurd to establish that the Chair of the Apostle Peter, a faithful disciple of Christ, is occupied by the Roman Antichrist. To which pertains primarily the prophecy of the Apostle Act. 20, 29. and also that, as already three hundred years ago a not ignoble Scholastic, William Ockham of the Order of Minors, in the work of ninety days, ch. 124, handed down to memory from ancient chronicles, that there were about twenty-seven so-called Roman Bishops, after the Church was endowed with temporal riches, who were involved in the greatest, public, and notorious crimes, after they were assumed to the papacy, or in the very assumption to the papacy, namely the crime of heresy, idolatry, intrusion, patronage of heretical depravity, blasphemy, fornication, and many other enormous crimes. And lest anyone reject the authority of Ockham as a witness of shaky faith, for which however no reason appears, we shall add the testimony of Cardinal Baronius, complaining at A. 897, Annal. n. 4, that around the year of Christ 897, monstrous men, most base in life, most lost in morals, and everywhere most foul, were intruded into the Chair of Peter. But it pleases to hear the Cardinal himself at A. 900, n. 1. How many, he exclaims, monsters, horrible to behold, were intruded into the seat, which is to be revered by Angels! How many evils have arisen from them, completed

NOTES TO CHAPTER XXIII OF MATTHEW. SUMMARY AND DISPOSITION.

Tragedies! By which it then happened that it itself, without spot and without wrinkle, was sprinkled with filth, infected with stenches, defiled, and by these blackened with perpetual infamy! Let the Jesuit Erbermann now go, and settle with these most trustworthy witnesses before he maliciously accuses the Jena scholars in his Expostulation, as they call it, before our August Emperor and the Most Eminent Estates of the Holy Roman Empire, that while they write what is the case, they stubbornly oppose the desired Concord with atrocious crimes. Certainly, whoever has read these things in the aforementioned authors will confess not a foul accusation, but the very truth, when in the Glosses to the Arbor. haeret. its author (who however was not B. Pareus, as the Jesuit indeed strives to persuade the world) wrote: Just as Simon Magus was a lustful man, and permitted all kinds of impurities and wickedness: so is the greater part of the Roman Pontiffs. Erbermann adds: And by what witness is such a foul accusation supported? By Gerhard alone. έφα! How false this exclamation of the Jesuit is, even the few things at least which were just now adduced from Ockham and Baronius sufficiently prove. Not to mention the huge phalanx of very many witnesses who lived in the midst of the Papacy and held splendid offices, which B. Pareus produces into the battle line in Confess. Cath. book 2, Special. art. 3, ch. 4. But it is not the place here to dwell on these. It suffices for us that very many Roman Pontiffs occupied the Papal seat by evil and magical arts, which B. Pareus at the said place, p. 623 seqq., has proven at length. So that therefore the Papists, about to demonstrate the infallibility of the Pope, appeal in vain to that local succession in the Chair of Peter: The Papists ought to have distinguished between personal succession or local, and doctrinal succession. In the Canon Law, which the Papists are accustomed to value highly, this sentence is ascribed to Jerome: They are not the sons of the saints who hold the places of the saints: but those who exercise their works: C Non est facile, dist. 40. &c. Mu-ti dist. ead. from Chrysostom this twin one is adduced: The Chair does not make the Priest: but the Priest the Chair, nor does the place sanctify the man, but the man the place. Excellent also is that of Gregory of Nazianzus, Orat. 31, in praise of Athanasius, f. 526. He who professes the same doctrine of faith is also a participant of the same throne.

He who embraces the contrary faith must also be considered an adversary on the throne. And this indeed has the name, but that one truly has the thing itself and the truth of succession. We have also cited elsewhere that statement of Ambrose, On Repentance, book 1, chapter 6: They do not have the inheritance of Peter (the throne) who do not have the faith of Peter. Marcus Antonius de Dominis, Archbishop of Spalato, in On the Ecclesiastical Republic, book 1, chapter 12, page 150, observes from the present passage against the affected primacy of the Pope in controversies of faith, that Christ testifies that not the priests and high priests, who were not of the Levitical order, sat upon the Chair of Moses, in which the doctrine of faith was to be explained, but the Scribes and Pharisees. But such as today among the Papists are the religious and the Theologians, as Cornelius Jansenius, Bishop of Ghent, wishes in the Harmony of the Gospels, chapter 84. If, therefore, some infallible authority in controversies of faith were to reside among the Papists on account of the Chair of Peter, then that should be sought not in the Roman Pontiff, but in the religious and the Theologians, inasmuch as they, according to Jansenius, are that which the Pharisees were among the Jews. But just as the Pharisees by no means had supreme or authentic authority, whom nevertheless the Savior himself says sat in the Chair of Moses: so neither do the Papist Doctors, nor the Roman Pontiffs have any infallibility, even if it were most strongly proven that they sit in the Chair of Peter. Most vain, therefore, is the boasting of the Papists that the Roman Pontiff sits upon the chair of Peter, and is therefore infallible when pronouncing from the Chair. Indeed, the successors of the Apostles can also rightly be said to have sat upon their chairs in the same way that the successors of Peter sat upon his, nor were they for that reason immune from the danger of erring. Nor can any reason be given why the Chair of Peter alone should have that privilege, since the rest of the Apostles of Christ were equally infallible as Peter in delivering to us the dogmas of the Christian faith. But if the Papists think that this absolute authority and infallibility of the Roman Pontiff can be proven from this passage, they must also concede that the Scribes and Pharisees, because they sat upon the Chair of Moses, had such supreme authority and infallibility, and not only all taken together, but each one separately, since the Roman Pontiff is not the whole College.

but equally as the remaining ministers, a singular person. Indeed, an account will also have to be rendered, why infallibility from this place pertains more to the Roman Pontiff than to the other ministers of the Church, since, given that he sits in the Chair of Peter, the others sit upon the chair of the Apostles. Since therefore, as Augustine rightly notes in tract 46 on John, against the letters of Petilian book 2, chapter 6, and book 4 of On Christian Doctrine, chapter 27, Chrysostom in homily 10 on 1 Thessalonians, Isidore of Pelusium in book 4, epistle 18, this saying of Christ can be applied to the individual Pastors of the Church, inasmuch as by that very thing the Savior shows how much the hearers ought to obey them: it will have to be said that that authentic authority, if any can be proved from the present saying, must also be attributed to all and singular, or it must be confessed that it does not pertain to the Roman Pontiff either, or certainly it can by no means be proved from the present saying. Although, however, the ministers of the Church sitting in the chair of the Apostles are by no means endowed with infallible authority, nor are they even to be heard unless they propose the doctrine of Moses, that is, the truth divinely revealed and handed down to us in the Holy Scriptures: nevertheless, the ordination which such Ministers of the Church perform in the name of the whole Church is to be judged valid and firm. For just as, in the time of Christ, the ordination of those who were ordained and consecrated to the ecclesiastical ministry by Priests stained with the blemish of various errors and corruptions was held to be valid, and was not disapproved by Christ and the Apostles, but rather approved, as is evident from the present saying: so also the ordination of our own Doctors of the Church, who before the time of the reformation were ordained by Bishops of the Papistic Church, could be legitimate and was so as well, notwithstanding that those Bishops were participants in the gravest errors and corruptions in heavenly doctrine. And hence those frivolous objections of the Papists, and especially of the Jesuits, vanish into smoke, when they oppose this dilemma to us as if it were the club of Hercules. Luther was ordained either by a false or by a true Bishop. If by a true one, why did he depart from him? If by a false one, the ordination will not be legitimate, and therefore null, for who would entrust a sheep to a wolf? But one must distinguish between the ecclesiastical ministry itself, which was instituted by God, and the stain adhering to the person.

Although, therefore, that Bishop by whom Luther was ordained, just like the remaining orthodox ministers who said farewell to the Papacy, had embraced a doctrine teeming with many Papal errors, yet by this nothing was lost to the ministry itself. So that Luther could rightly and effectively be ordained by a false Bishop, that is to say, one so called because of corrupt doctrine. But it is to be observed above all that the calling belongs to the whole Church, as to that to which Christ entrusted the keys of binding and loosing. Truly, a certain recent apostate is wonderfully inept Casparus Schele, who professes himself a Candidate of Law and a Practitioner of Namslau, while in his Declaration of Apostasy, which he entitles The exchange of darkness with light, p. 25, proceeds thus from this point, that if for the reason that the Church is the bride of Christ, to whom the right of the keys belongs, the right of calling ministers of the Church pertains to the whole Church, which is what the Lutherans maintain, it follows from that, that all laymen and even women and infants still wailing in their cradles have the power of ordaining Ministers of the Church. But was, he continues, Paul ordained in this way? Was Titus, Timothy, Stephen? But the Apostate errs and is deceived, seeing grimly: for one must accurately distinguish 1 between the calling of Ministers, and the ordination of the same. For the Church uses the power of the keys in such a way that the whole Church by no means performs the ordination, but commits that very thing to the Ecclesiastical Ministry. 2. between the power of calling and the execution of this power. The power remains with the whole Church, but the execution of that power is done through certain persons, who represent the place of the rest of the Church. Which he could have easily learned from the Blessed Parent, whom the vain man despises with a haughty brow, had he not been blinded by the love of the world and loved darkness more than light. Let at least the Locus on the Eccl. Min. §. 87. and 157. be unrolled, and it will easily appear how inept that new disputer is. Compare also the most accurate Treatise of Mr. Dr. Haberkorn on the truth and efficacy of the Eccl. Min. which is among the Lutherans.

Sentence. Those who taught in the Synagogues did not sit, but stood, Luke 4, 16. Acts 13, 16. therefore by τό to sit in the Chair, is understood the office of teaching, which the Scribes and Pharisees performed because of the negligence of the Priests and Levites, to whom it had been committed. Compare Tossanus on this passage. *(Hugo Grotius reconciles the cited passages with the present one by warning that if to any to the common people the power of speaking was granted, and they were accustomed to speak forth standing, so that they might be more rightly heard by the whole assembly: But the Archisynagogues and others performing the public office of Teacher, interpreted the law no less than the Bishops of the Christians sitting in the Chair. He adds: They read the very words of the law standing, however, then they spoke the rest sitting. And he wishes for this to look especially to Nehem. 8, 5.Luc. 4, 17.)* Galatinus lib. 4 de Arcan. Cath. Verit. c. 5. And the Jewish kingdom and its judicial power failed while Herod was reigning, because he also took away the Sanhedrin. Therefore when Christ was speaking about these judges, who in that time were accustomed to be chosen from the Scribes and Pharisees, upon the Chair, he says, of Moses they sat, ηάθησαν in Aorist. 1. they do not sit, to demonstrate that their power had then ceased. *(The opinion of those is also not inconvenient, who teach that τό they sit here denotes the same thing as they are accustomed to sit. Which mode of speaking they confirm from our Evangelist c. 3, 17. also from Luc. 1, 47. Thus explains Dn. D. Wellerus Comm. in epist. ad Rom. p. 496.)*

Scribes and Pharisees. Ludov. Vives ad l. 18. de C. D. cap. 39. Scribes were those who taught only the letter of the sacred books, and did not depart from it even by a hair's breadth: but those who professed something more, were named Pharisees from Phrases, which is division, as if dividing and separating themselves as better from the many, and both, as much the Scribes as the Pharisees, sat in the Chair of Moses, explaining the law to the people. *(About the Pharisees it has also been treated above at c. 3, 7. Add. Camero t. 3. Praelect. p. 1. seqq. up to page 44. B. D. Chemn. H. E. p. 100. 162. 200. 265. but incidentally Ludov. Vives ad l. 18. Aug. de C. D. c. 39 B. Par Harm Evang. p. 3. 229. 480. 566. 515. others here and there. about the Scribes c. preceding v. 15. Add. Camero l. c. p. 45. & 11.)*

Latin:

v. 2. In Cathedra Mosis. h. e. destinata lectioni Mosaicorum & Propheticorum librorum. *(Moses enim hîc V. T. libros in genere significat. Nec Scribae & Pharisaei in officio Mediatorio Mosis erant successores, sed in doctrinâ, quam iuxta Mosis mentem ac libros V. Test. tradere debebant, ut rectè notat Camero in Myroth p. 104. Sic quoque Patres exponunt. Hieronymus in h. l. Per Cathedram doctrinam Legis ostendit. Theophylactus similiter: Dominudicit, scribit, de hi-, qui in Cathedrâ Mosis sedent, i. e. his, qui ea, quae in lege habentur, docent. Conf. Nehem. 8, 4.9.Act. 15. 21 Sic quoq Hi arius: Iubet, inquit, legis mandatis omnibus obedire. Quin ipsorum Pontificiorum similes sententiae adducentur paullò post. Errat verò Cornelius à Lapide, quando per Cathedram h. l. absolutè intelligit autoritatem docendi ac iubendi. Atque porrò infert, quòd cùm Pontifex Romanus sede at in Cathedrâ Petri, ipse, licet ut privatus homo errare possit, tamen cùm ex Cathedrâ i. e. ex autoritate Pontificiâ aliquid de fide definit, errare nequeat, ob adsistentiam Sp-ritûs San-ti. Verùm contrarium potiùs ex hoc Christi adserto ac monito patet tantum abest, ut erronea illa Pontificiorum de Papae infallibilitate sententia confirmari inde possit. Etenim quemadmodum Pharisaei & Scribae, etsi iuxta Salvatoris nostri testimonium in Cathedra Mosis sedebant, adeoque eâdem autoritate, quâ Moses, docebant, hautquaquam tamen propterea immunes ab erroris periculo erant, imò gravissimos sovebant errores, quos Salvator quoq; passim taxat. vid, suprà c. 5 & 15. it. it. Marc, 7. ita, posito, quòd Pontifex Romanus in Cathedra Petri sedeat, haut magis tamen ipse, quàm illi, ab errandi periculo censendus immunis est. Et quî quaeso Pontifex Romanus, si vel maximè Romae in Cathedrâ Petri sederet, labi non posset? Sanè si protoplasti, ad im-ginem DEI creati, labi potuerunt in Paradisi horto, Angeli icoeli domicilio, Iudas, Thomas, imò Petrus ipse in Apostolorum choro, quidni & Pontifex Romanus in ficto Petri throno? Atque hoc eò magis, quia contra Deum sese effert ac inepta sua placita verbo DEI revelato, (cui qui aliquid addit, maledictus est, Apoc. 22, 18. si vel Angelus etiam de coelo fuerit, Gal. 1, 8.) non solùm addit, verùm etlam exaequat, imò praefert, ceu ex-fictis sanctorum cultibus, impiis dispensationibus &c. alibi ostensum. Confer Gregor. Magnum lib. 6. epist. 5. Illud verô probè notandum est, quòd aliquando sincerorū Ecclesiae Doctorum Cathedrae à falsis Dd. sive successoribus impiis occupentur. Sic Aaroni successere Urias idololatra, Hannas item & Caiphas, qui Christum condemnarunt. Haut igitur absurdum erit, statuere, quòd fide lis quoque Christi discipuli, Apostoli Petri Cathedra ab Anti Christo Romano occupetur. Quò cumprimis facit vaticinium Apostoli Act. 20, 29. tum quoque quòd, ceu iamtum trecentis abhinc annis Scholasticus non ignobilis, Guilielmus Oceam Ord. Minorum, in opere nonaginta dierum c. 124. ex chronicis vetustis memoriae prodidit, circaviginti septem vocatos Episcopos Romanos, postquam Ecclesia extitit temporalibus divitiis dotata, fuisse, qui sceleribus maximis, publicis & notoriis, post quam fuerunt ad papatum adsumti, vel in ipsa adsumtione ad papatum irretiti, scilicet crimine haeresis, idololatriae, intrusionis fautoriae, pravitatis haereticae, blasphemiae, fornicationis & aliis multis enormibus criminibus involuti fuerunt. Ac ne quis autoritatem Occami, tanquam sublestae fidei testis cuius tamen nulla apparet ratio, reiiciat, adiiciemus testimonium Card. Baronii, conquerentis ad A. 897. Annal. n. 4. quòd circa annum Christi 897. in Cathedram Petri intrusi fuerint homines monstrosi, vita turpissimi, moribus perditissimi & usquequaq foedissimi. Sed placet ipsum Cardinalem audire ad A. 900. n 1. Quot, excclamat, in sedem, Angelis reverendam, visu horrenda intrusa sunt monstra! Quot ex eis oborta sunt mala, consummatae

NOTAE AD CAP. XXIII. MATTHAEI. SUMMA AC DISPOSITIO.

Tragaediae! Quibus tunc ipsam sine macula & sine ruga contigit aspergi sordibus, putoribus infici, inquinarispurc-tus, exhisq perpetua infamiâ denigrari! Eat nunc Iesuita Erbermannus, & cum his fide dignissimis testibus transigat priùs, quàm Ienenses coram Augustissimo nostro Imper. ac Eminentissimis S. R. Imp. Statibus malitiosè in suâ Expostulatione, quam ita vocant, accuset, quòd dum scribunt, quod res est, atrocibus criminibus desideratae Concordiae praefractè obsistant Certè qui ista apud praédictos autores legerit, non spurcam criminationem, sed ipsissimam veritatem fatebitur, quando in Glossis ad Arbor. haeret. illius autor, (qui tamen non fuit B. Parens, uti quidem Iesuita orbi persuadere satagit) scripsit: Sicut Simon Magus fuit luxuriosus homo, permisitq omnis generis impuritates & nequitias: it a maior pars Romanorum Pontificum. Subiicit Erbermannus: Et quo teste fulcitur tam spurca criminatio? Gerhardi unius solius.έφα! Quàm falsa sit haec Iesuitae exclamatio, vel pauca saltem, quae modò ex Occamo & Baronio adducta fuere, satis evincunt. Ut iam non memorem ingentem testium plurimorum, qui in medio Papatu vixerunt & splendidis functi officiis sunt, phalangem, quam in aciem producit B. Parens Confess. Cath. lib. 2. Special. art. 3. c. 4. Sed non est huius loci, hisce immorari. Sufficit nobis, quòd plurimi Pontifices Romani malis ac magicis artibus sedem Papalem occuparint, id quod prolixè B. Par. d. l. p. 623. seqq. evicit. Ut proinde frustrà Pontificii, Papae infallibilitatem demonstraturi, ad localem illam successionem in Cathedrâ Petri provocent: Distingvere debebant Pontificii inter successionem personalem vel localem, & inter successionem doctrinalem. In Iure Canonico, quod magni aestimare Pontificii solent, Hieronymo adscribitur haec sententia: Non sanctorum filii sunt, qui loca tenent sanctorum: sed qui exercent opera eorum: C Non est facile, dist. 40. &c. Mu-ti dist. ead. ex Chrysostomo adducitur gemella haec: Non Cathedra facit Sacerdotem: sed Sacerdos Cathedram, nec locus sanctificat hom-nem, sed homo locum. Egregium quoque est illud Gregorii Nazianzeni Orat. 31. in laudem Athanasii f. 526. Qui eandem fidei doctrinam profitetur, eiusdem quoq throni particeps est.

Qui autem contrariam fidem amplectitur, adversarius quoque in throno censeri debet. Atq haec quidem nomen, illa verò rem ipsam, & veritatem habet successionis. Adduximus quoque alibi illud Ambrosii de poenit. l. 1. c. 6. Non habent. Petri haereditatem (thronum) qui Petri fidem non habent. Marcus Antonius de Dominis, Archi Episc. Spalat. in de Republ. Eccles. lib. 1. c. 12. p. 150. è praesenti loco illud observat contra affectatum Pontificis in controversiis fidei, primatum, quòd Christus testetur, super Cathedra Mosis, in qua doctrina fidei erat explicanda, sedisse non. Sacerdotes & summos Pontifices, sed Scribas & Pharisaeos, qui ex ordine Levitico non erant. Sed tal-s, quales hodie apud Pontificios religiosi & Theologi ut vult Corn. Ian-enius Episcopus Gandavensis in Concord. Ev. c 84 Quod si igitur resideret aliqua, ob Petri Cathedram, apud Pontificios infallibilis in fidei controversiis autoritas, tunc quaerenda illa non apud Pontificem Romanum esset, sed apud religiosos & Theologos, quippe qui iuxta Iansenium illud sunt, quod apud Iudaeos fuerunt Pharisaei. At quemadmodum Pharisaei haudquaquam summam seu authenticam habuerunt authoritatem, quos tamen ipse Salvator in Cathedra Mosis sedisse dicit: ita nec Dd. Pontificii, nec P-. RR. infallibilitatem aliquam habent, si vel maximè fuerit evictum, quòd in Cathedra Petri sedeant. Vanissima igitur est gloriatio Pontificiorum, quòd P. R. super cathedrâ Petri sedeat, adeoque infallibilis sit, de Cathedrâ pronuncians. Sanè & Apostolorum successores eodem, quo Petri successores super Cathedra eorum sedisse, dici iure possunt, neq; tamen propterea ab errandi periculo immunes fuerunt. Nec ulla potest ratio dari, cur solius Petri Cathedra istud privilegium habeat, cùm aequè reliqui Christi Apostoli ac Petrus in tradendis nobis fidei Christianae dogmatibus infallibiles fuerint. Si verò ex hoc loco absolutam istam autoritatem P. R atque infallibilitatem evinci posse censent Pontificii, concedere quoque eos oportet, Scribas & Pharisaeos eò, quòd super Mosis Cathedram sederant, habuisse talem summam autoritatem & infallibilitatem, nec solùm omnes coniunctim sumtos, sed singulos seorsim, cùm Pontifex Romanus non sit totum Collegium,

sed aeque ac reliqui ministri, persona singularis. Imò reddenda quoque erit ratio, quare Pontifici Romano magis competat ex h. l. infallibilitas, quàm coeteris Ecclesiae ministris, cùm posito, quòd ille sedeat in Cathedra Petri, reliqui super cathedra Apostolorum sedeant. Cùm igitur, prout rectè notant Augustinus tr. 46. in Iohannem, contra litteras Petit. lib. 2. c. 6. ac l. 4. de D. C. c. 27. Chrysostomus homil. 10. in 1. Thess. Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 4. epist. 18. dictum hoc Christi ad singulos applicari Ecclesiae Pastores possit, quippe cùm eo ipso ostendat Salvator, quat. illis obedire auditores debeant: dicendum erit, quòd authentica illa autoritas, si quae è praesenti dicto probari potest, omnibus & singulis tribui quoque debeat, vel fatendum, quòd nec Pontifici Romano illa competat, certè è praesenti dicto probari minimè possit. Quamvis autem ministri Ecclesiae in Cathedra Apostolorum sedentes hautquaquam infallibili praediti autoritate sint, quin nec audiendi, nisi Mosis doctrinam h. e. veritatem divinitus revelatam & in Sc. S. nobis traditam proponant: nihilo tamen minùs ordinatio, quam tales Ministri Ecclesiae totius Ecclesiae nomine peragunt, rata censenda est ac firma. Quemadmodum enim, tempore Christi ordinatio eorum qui à Sacerdotibus, variorum errorū ac corruptelarum labe maculatis, ad ministerium Ecclesiasticum ordinabantur ac consecrabantur, rata fuit habita, nec à Christo & Apostolis improbata, sed potiùs approbata, ceu è praesenti dicto patet: ita quoque nostratium Ecclesiae Doctorum, qui ante tempus reformationis à Papisticae Ecclesiae Episcopis ordinati fuerunt, ordinatio legitima esse pot-it ac fuit quoque, non obstante, quòd Episcopi illi gravissimorum errorum ac corruptelarum in doctrinâ coelesti fuerint affines. Atq; hinc in fumum abeunc frivolae illae Pontificiorum, ac Iesuitarum cumprimis obiectiones, quando tanquam Herculis clavam dilemma hoc nobis opponunt. Aut à falso, aut à vero Episcopo ordinatus fuit Lutherus. Si à vero, cur ab illo discessit? Si à falso, non erit ordinatio legitima, adeoq nulla, quis enim lupo ovem committat. At distinguendum est inter ministerium Ecclesiasticum ipsum, quod à Deo institutum, & inter labem personae adhaerentem.

Licet igitur Episcopus ille, à quo ordinatus fuit Lutherus, sicuti & reliqui ministri orthodoxi, qui Papatui vale dixerunt, amplexus fuerit doctrinam, multis erroribus Papalibus scatentem, per hoc tamen ministerio ipsi nihil decessit. Ut ita rectè & efficaciter Lutherus à falso, puta à corrupta doctrinâ ita dicto, Episcopo ordinari potuerit. Cumprimis verò observandum, quòd vocatio toti competat Ecclesiae, ut cui Christus commisit claves ligandi ac solvendi. Mirè verò ineptit recens quidam Apostata Casparus Schele, qui Iuris se Candidatum profitetur ac Practicum Namslaviensem, dum in Apostasiae suae Declaratione, quam Tenebrarum cum luce permutationem inscribit, p. 25 ita porrò hinc infert, quòd si propterea, quia Ecclesia Christi sponsa, cui ius clavium competit, ius vocandi ministros Ecclesiae ad totam Ecclesiam spectat, id quod Lutherani statuunt, sequatur inde, omnes laicos adeoq etiam mulieres ac in cunis adhuc vagientes infantulos potestatem habere ordinandi Ecclesiae Ministros. Num verò, pergit, ordinatus ita fuit Paulus? Num Titus, Timotheus, Stephanus? Verùm fallit ac fallitur torvè videns Apostata: etenim accuratè distinguendum 1 inter Ministrorum vocationem, & eorundem ordinationem. Ita enim Ecclesia potestate illclavium utitur, ut minimè ordinationem peragat tota Ecclesia, sed illam ipsam Ministerio Ecclesiastico committat. 2. inter vocandi potestatem & potestatis huius executionem. Potestas manet penes totam Ecclesiam, sed executio illius potestatis fit per certas quasdam personas, quae Ecclesiae reliquae locum repraesentant. Quod facilè à B. Parente, quem vanus homo alto supercilio contemnit, discere potuisset, nisi amore mundi excoecatus tenebras magis dilexisset, quàmlucem. Evolvatur saltem Locus de Min. Eccl. §. 87. ac 157. & facilè apparebit, quàm ineptus sit novuille disputator. Conf. quoq; accuratissimus Tract. Dn. D. Haberkorn-i de Minist. Eccl. quod inter Lutheranos est, veritat. & efficacia.)*

Seaent. Qui in Synagogis docebant, non sedebant, sed stabant, Luc. 4, 16.Actor. 13, 16. ergo per τόsedere in Cathedra, intelligitur munus docendi, quo fungebantur Scribae & Pharisaei propter negligentiam Sacerdotum & Levitarum, quibus id erat commissum. Conf. Tossanus in h. l. *(Hugo Grotius allegata loca conciliat cum praesenti monendo, quòd si quibus è plebe potestas loquendi facta, illi stantes proloqui soliti fuerint, ut rectiùs ab omni coetu audirentur: At Archisynagogos & alios publico Magistri munere fungentes, non minùs quàm Episcopos Christianorum in Cathedrâ sedentes legem fuisse interpretatos. Addit: Stantes tamen legebant ipsa legis verba, deinde caetera sedentes loquebantur. Atque huc cumprimis spectare vult Nehem. 8, 5.Luc. 4, 17.)* Galatinus lib. 4 de Arcan. Cath. Verit. c. 5. Et regnum Iudaicum & iudiciaria eius potestas Herode regnante defecit, quia & Synedrion sustulit. Ideò cùm Christus de his iudicibus loqueretur, qui ea tempestate de Scribis & Pharisaeis eligi solebant, super Cathedrâ, inquit, Mosis sederunt,ηάθησαν in Aorist. 1. non sedent, ut demonstraret, quòd eorumtunc cessaverat potestas. *(Non incommoda quoque eorum sententia est, qui τόsedent idem hîc notare docent, quod sedere solent. Quem loquendi modum confirmant ex Evangelista nostro c. 3, 17. it. ex Luc. 1, 47. Ita exponit Dn. D. Wellerus Comm. in epist. ad Rom. p. 496.)*

Scribae & Pharisaei. Ludov. Vives ad l. 18. de C. D. cap. 39. Scribae erant, qui sacrorum librorum litteram tantùm docebant, nec ab eârecedebant vel culmen latum: qui verò magis quiddam profitebantur, Pharisaei nominati sunt à Phrases, quod est divisio, quasi se velut meliores à multis dividentes, separantesq, & utriq tàm Scribae, quàm Pharisaei in Cathedra Mosis sedebant, populo legem enarrantes. *(De Pharisaeis actum quoque suprà ad c. 3, 7. Add. ex professo de illis disserentes Camero t. 3. Praelect. p. 1. seqq. usque ad pag. 44. B. D. Chemn. H. E. p. 100. 162. 200. 265. obiter verò Ludov. Vives ad l. 18. Aug. de C. D. c. 39 B. Par Harm Evang. p. 3. 229. 480. 566. 515. alii passim. de Scribis c. praeced. v. 15. Add. Camero l. c. p. 45. & 11.)*

## 23:3
*(v. 3. All things, whatsoever they shall say to you, do. We learn from this, that because of the evil life of teachers we ought not to flee the Church itself: but rather to be certain, that even through the ministry or office of the unworthy God is effective. Concerning which matter our people treat at length against the Papists in art. on the Ecclesiastical Ministry, to which can be added here Cu-r. Rittershusius Ctus lib. 6 Lect Sacr. c. 13. p. 463. It is well to be noted, however, that the words of our Savior are to be understood reduplicatively namely insofar as the Scribes sit and Pharisees upon the Chair of Moses, i. e. insofar as they say and teach those things which agree with the doctrine of Moses. It is evident, because Christ above c. 16, 11. warns to beware of the leaven i. e. of the false doctrine, see v. 12. of the Pharisees. Conf. v. 16. seqq. also below c. 26, 65. c. 15, 14. also c. 28, 20. Rom. 16, 16.Gal. 1, 8.1. Tim. 6, 3. 4. Whence it is not the case that the Papists should so much rattle on about the seat of Peter. See the Jesuit Maldonatus and Corn. à Lapide in this place, who himself however, as if forgetting himself, τό all things limits, adding, namely not contrary to Moses and the law. Just as therefore the Scribes and Pharisees, although they sat upon the Chair of Moses, i. e. had received after Moses the authority of teaching and commanding which Moses had had among the Jews, could nevertheless err and teach things contrary to Moses, (as likewise Cornelius in this place shows, and well warns, that Maldonatus also τό restricts all things to only those which are commanded by Moses in the law,) and so they were not to be heard in all things: but their doctrine could and ought to be examined according to the doctrine of Moses, handed down in Holy Scripture and comprised therein: so also, although the Roman Pontiff may very much teach the place where Peter taught, he is by no means immune from the danger of error, and therefore, when he brings forth dogmas contrary to the doctrine of Peter, left to us in Holy Scripture, which he does here and there, he is not to be heard: nor will Pontifical authority make him any more immune from the danger of error than the authority received after Moses made the Scribes and Pharisees immune from errors. So far, therefore, is this place from patronizing the infallibility of the Roman Pontiff, that it rather vehemently opposes it. Whence it is evident how unjust the clients of the Roman Curia are toward us, when they do not want us to judge concerning Pontifical doctrine from the word of GOD handed down to us in Holy Scripture, whether, namely, the former is conformable to the latter, or otherwise: but that as an infallible truth the dictates of the Roman Pontiff R. should be accepted, for the reason that the Roman Pontiff sits (or rather, that we may speak more correctly, boasts that he sits,) in the Chair of Peter. Gravely Ioh. Wesselus of Groningen, Preacher of Worms, called the light of the world on account of his distinguished erudition, (he lived around A. C. 1460.) in the book whose title is, Farrago: It is necessary to observe the precepts of Prelates as long as they, sitting in the Chair of Moses, teach according to Moses, and if they decree anything against or outside of this, we are not bound, for we are servants of GOD, not of the Pope. In the same way Didacus Stella the Lusitanian, from

from the Order of Friars Minor, Bishop on chapter 12 of Luke: They sit upon the Chair of Moses, that is, in so far as they teach what Moses taught in the Chair, they are to be heard; otherwise, beware. Nor did the ancients explain it otherwise. Isidorus Pelusiota, book 4, ep. 18: Christ commanded that the life of the Masters should not be heeded, if at any time it provided any handle for reproach to those looking upon it: nor those things which are designed privately by them, if they do not agree with the heavenly oracles: but only the doctrine which is handed down in the Churches. For which reason he also made mention of the Chair of Moses the legislator: for then they do not speak their own dogmas, but those of the Scriptures. Augustinus, tr. 46 in Ioh.: By sitting upon the chair of Moses, they teach the law of GOD, therefore through them God teaches: but if they wish to teach their own things, do not hear, do not do. To this also pertain those things which Gabriel Biel, a Scholastic not ignoble, has in book 4, sentent. dist. 1, q. 4, art. 3: It is not permitted to spurn the counsel of a Prelate, which is true, unless he has spoken against the divine law. Because by commanding thus, he does not sit upon the Chair of Moses: for these things do not proceed from the Chair, that is, the doctrine of Moses, but from the chair of pestilence. But especially to this pertains that which our Savior himself Matth. 23, 8. says: Do not be called Rabbi: for one is the Master, namely Christ himself, hear him, Matth. 17, 5. Ioh. 10, 27. Cf. Matth. 28, 20. Rom. 16, 16. Gal. 1, 8. Eph. 2, 10. 1. Tim. 6, 3. The B. Parens brings forward the sayings of the Fathers confirming this same opinion in the Place on the Church § 119. Let the same be compared in the Confess. Cath. book 1, Gener. p. 330, seqq., also D. Rivetus, Isagog. ad Sc. S. c. 21, § 16, seqq. Furthermore, from the fact that Christ teaches that the Pharisees sitting in the Chair of Moses, in so far as they sit in the chair of Moses, that is, bring forth doctrine consistent with that of Moses and administer the Sacraments according to the prescription of Moses, are to be heard, notwithstanding that they are otherwise akin to many most grave errors, the Orthodox rightly conclude that the efficacy of the Sacraments and of the preached word does not depend upon the life of the Minister, that is, that through his impurity or unworthiness nothing is lost to the integrity of the Sacraments. Wherefore also the Baptism of heretics, provided they retain the substantials of Baptism, is to be judged valid and ought not to be repeated. See B. D. Roenig, Cas. Cons. p. 250, B. Par. L. de Bapt. § 27. Nor do the Pontificians dissent. See Becanus, l. V. Manual. Controv. c. 8. But someone might ask, if the life of the Minister does not change the force of the Sacrament and thus nothing is lost to the efficacy of the Sacraments because they are administered by a Minister whether wicked or heterodox, why did Luther and our ancestors make a secession from the Pontifical Church, and not use the Ministry of the Pontifical Churches? B. D. Mylius answers this doubt in A. C. part. 1, p. 144: that this was done because the Papists no longer sat in the Chair of Moses and the Apostles, but having destroyed these, they erected their own. The same must be established much more regarding the rite of ordination conferred by heretics. Concerning which matter one must consult Augustinus, book 2, cont. Epist. Parmen. c. 13, not far from the beginning. Gregorius M., l. 2, ep. 32, to Ioh. Bishop of Ravenna; the response of Gregory is related in the Canon law as C. sicut semel dist. 68, add. c. Quod quidam 1. q. 1, also C. Si qui, C. Ostenditur, C. rebaptizare. And hence it is clear that the Jesuit Reihing in fundam. 3, relig. Cathol. p. 59, ineptly rises up against Luther thus: Who, he exclaims, Luther, inaugurated you into the Priesthood? Who imparted to you the power of offering and remitting sins? A Catholic Bishop? True, or false? A Pastor, or a wolf? If a Pastor, by departing from him you have become a wolf. If a wolf, who would recognize you as a Pastor made by a wolf? &c. The same could certainly be objected to all those ordained by heretics, whom nevertheless the Pontifical laws affirm to be truly ordained, as was just shown. Next, one must accurately distinguish office from person. That that Bishop ordained Luther, pertained to the office; that he was immersed in Papal errors, was personal. Now, however, from the vice of the person, nothing is lost to the integrity of the Sacraments, let alone of the ordination, provided the substantials are observed. And it is well to note that that Pontifical Bishop, by whom Luther was ordained, did not in his own name, but in the name and authority of the Church (which it has been shown elsewhere was preserved even in the midst of the Papacy), bind Luther by the rite of ordination to teach the word of GOD. Concerning which matter it was also treated a little earlier. Furthermore, from the fact that God was efficacious through the corrupt ministry of the Pharisees, in so far as they sat in the Chair of Moses, that is, proposed the doctrine of Moses and administered the Sacraments of Circumcision, and yet the Jewish Church was not therefore a true Church at that time, it is clear that neither is the Papistical Church a true and pure Church, although through the Jesuits in India

indeed the gentiles are converted, namely, they propose heavenly doctrine to them and administer the Sacrament of Baptism, although it is not always done so purely. See B. Par. L. de Eccles. §. 188. Dun. Theol. Saxon. in Fundam. Pupillae Defens p. 42. Lud. de Dieu Praefat. and notes to the Hist. Christi & Petri written in Persian by Xavier.)*

( κα-ά -ά έςγα &c. i. e. do not do such works as they themselves do. Obj. This passage is against the Papists, who from Matth. 16, 27. and 1. Petr. 1, 17., where God is said to be about to render to each one κα-ά -ά έςγα, κα-ά τῶν πςάξιν άυτου., attempt to construct the merits of works. The vanity of whom Gregory the Great, Bishop of Rome, long ago refuted when in Ps. 7. of the penitential psalms, vol. 2, page 997, F, he writes thus: But if that happiness of the saints is mercy, and is not acquired by merits, where will that be which is written: ( Prov. 24.) And you will render to each one according to his works? If it is rendered according to works, how will it be considered mercy? But it is one thing to render according to works, another to render on account of the works themselves. For in that it is said according to works, the very quality of the works is understood, so that for whom good works have appeared, his also is the glorious retribution. For to that blessed life, in which one lives with God and from God, no labor can be equaled, no works compared, especially since the Apostle says: ( Rom. 8.) The sufferings are not worthy &c. Compare also Apoc 22, 12.)

( Do not do. It is the duty of a faithful Doctor to warn the simple against the frauds and errors of the heterodox. Compare above c. 7, 15. also Actor. 20, 29.1. Thess. 5, 21.2. Tim. 4, 3. 4.1. Ioh. 2, 19.c. 4, 1.)

v. 3. They say, and do not do. Anton. lib. 2. Meliss. c. 4. p. 85. from Chrysostom: ούέν διδασκάλου Ψυχςότεπο -ν λόγοις Φιλοσοφούντοσ μόνον: τούγ ού διδασκάλου, άλλ ωοκείτου. Nothing is colder than a Doctor philosophizing only in words. For this is not the work of a Doctor, but of an actor. (Compare many things on this matter in the Apostle Rom. 2, 19. and following, also in Isidore of Pelusium lib. 1. ep. 79. and 391. lib. 2. ep. 90. lib. 3. ep. 158. 120. 189. Conrad Rittershus. lib. 6. Sacr. Lect. c. 13. B. Par. Aphor. Pract. tit. Ministers of the Church.)

Latin:

*(v. 3. Omnia, quaecunq dixerint vobis, facite. Discimus hinc, quòd ob malam doctorum vitam Ecclesiam ipsam fugere non debeamus: quin potiùs certi esse, quòd etiam per indignorū ministerium seu officiū Deus effic-x sit. Quâ de re prolixè agūt nostrates contra Pontificios in art. dMinist. Ecclesiastico, quibus addi hîc potest Cu-r. Rittershusius Ctus lib. 6 Lect Sacr. c. 13. p. 463. Probè verò notandum, quòd prae-entia Sasvatoris nostri verba reduplicativè intelligenda sint -empe quatenus sedent Scribae ac Pharisaei super Cathedra Mosis, h. e. quatenus ea dicunt ac docent, quae cum doctrinà Mosis consentiunt. Patet, quia Christus suprà c. 16, 11. à fermento i. e. à falsâ doctrinâ, vid. v. 12. Pharisaeorum cavere monet. Conf. v. 16. seqq. it. infrà c. 26, 65. c. 15, 14. it. c. 28, 20. Rom. 16, 16.Gal. 1, 8.1. Tim. 6, 3. 4. Unde non est, quòd tantopere Pontificii sedem crepent Petri. Vid. Iesuitae Maldonatus ac Corn. à Lapide in h. l. qui ipse tamen sui quasi oblitus τόomnia limitat, addens, scilicet Mosi & legi non contraria. Quemadmodum igitur Scribae ac Pharisaei, quamvis super Cathedra Mosis sederent, h. e. autoritatem docendi ac iubendi, quam apud Iudaeos Moses habuerat, post Mosen accepissent, errare tamen ac Mosi contraria docere poterant, (ceu itidem Cornelius h. l. ostendit, ac benè monet, quòd Maldonatus quoque τόomnia ad sola illa, quae à Mose in lege sunt praecepta, restringat,) adeoque nec in omnibus audiendi erant: sed doctrina eorum iuxta Mosis doctrinam, in Scriptura S. traditam eâque comprehensam, examinari poterat ac debebat: sic quoque, licet vel maximè P. R. ibidem do-eat loci, ubi Petrus docuit, ab erroris tamen periculo hautquaquam immunis est, ac proinde, quando Petri doctrinae, in Sc. S. nobis relictae, contraria profert dogmata, id quod passim facit, audiendus non est: neque etiam magis eum ab erroris periculo immunem praestabit Pontificia autoritas, quàm ab erroribus Scribas ac Pharisaeos immunes praestitit autoritas post Mosen accepta. Tantum igitur abest, ut locus hic P. R. infallibilitati patrocinetur, ut potiùs vehementer illi adversetur. Unde patet, quàm iniqui in nos sint Curiae Romanae clientes, quando nolunt, ut de doctrinâ Pontificiâ ex verbo DEI in Sc. S. nobis traditâ iudicemus, num videl. huic illa conformis sit, an secus: sed ut tanquam infallibilis veritas dictatus P. P. R. R. acceptētur, eò quòd Pontifex Romanus sedeat (vel potiùs, ut rectiùs dicamus, sedere se glorietur,) in Cathedrâ Petri. Graviter Ioh. Wesselus Groningensis, Concionator Wormatiensis, propter insignem eruditionem lux mundi dictus, (vixit circa A. C. 1460.) in libro, cui titulus, Farrago: Oportet Praelatorum praecepta tamdiu observare, quamdiu sedentes in Cathedra Mosis secundùm Mosen docent, & si quid contra vel extra statuunt, non ligamur, DEI enim servi sumus, non Papae. Eodem modo Didacus Stella Lusitanus, ex

ex Ord. Min. Episcopus in c. 12. Lucae: Sedent super Cathedrae Mosis h. e. quat enus docent, quae Moses in Cathedra docuit, audiendi sunt, alioqui cavete. Nec aliter veteres exposuerunt. Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 4. ep. 18. Christus praecepit, ut neq vita attenderetur Magistrorum, si quando reprehensionis aliquam intuentibus ansam praeberet: neq ea, quae privatim ab ipsis designantur, si non consentiant cum coelestibus oraculis: sed sola doctrina, quae in Ecclesiis traditur. Quâ de causa etiam Cathedrae Mosis legislatoris fecit mentionem: tunc enim non sua dogmata, sed Scripturarum loquuntur. Augustinus tr. 46. in Ioh. Sedendo super cathedram Mosis, legem DEI docent, ergo per illos Deus docet: sua verò illisi velini docere, nolite audire, no-ite facere. Huc spectant quoque, quae habet Gabriel Biel, Scholasticus non ignobilis in l. 4. sentent. dist. 1. q. 4. art. 3. Non licet spernere consilium Praelati, quod verum est, nisi contra legem divinam dixerit. Quia sic praecipiendo, non sedet supra Cathedram Mosis: non enim haec procedunt de Cathedra i. e. doctrinâ Mosis, sed de cathedrâ pestilentiae. Cumprimis verò huc spectat, quòd ipse Salvator noster Matth. 23, 8. dicit: Nolite vocari Rabbi: unus enim est Magister, videl. ipse Christus, hunc audite,Matth. 17, 5.Ioh. 10, 27. Conf. Matth. 28, 20.Rom. 16, 16.Gal. 1, 8.Eph. 2, 10.1. Tim. 6, 3. Dicta Patrum, eandem sententiam hanc confirmantia, adducit B. Parens Loco de Eccl. § 119. Conferatur idem Confess. Cath. lib. 1. Gener. p. 330. seqq. it. D. Rivetus Isagog. ad Sc. S. c. 21. §. 16. seqq. Exinde porrò, quòd Christus docet, Pharisaeos in Cathedrâ Mosis sedentes, quat. nempe in cathedra Mosis sedent h. e. doctrinam Mosaicae consentaneam proferunt & Sacramenta iuxta Mosis praescriptū administrant, audiendos esse, non obstante, quòd aliàs multorum gravis simorum errorum sint affines, rectè colligunt Orthodoxi, efficaciam Sacramentorum & verbi praedicati non dependere à vita Ministri, h. e. per huius impuritatem vel indignitatem nil decedere integritati Sacramentorū. Quapropter etiam Bapt-smus haereticorum, modò substātialia Baptismi retineant, ratus censendus afirmus, nec repeti debet. Vid. B. D. Roenig Cas. Cons. p. 250. B. Par. L. de Bapt. §. 27. Nec dissentiunt Pontificii. Videatur Becanus l. V. Manual. Controv. c. 8. Sed quaerat aliquis, si vim Sacramenti non mutat vita Ministri, adeoq Sacramentorum efficaciae nihil per hoc decedit, quòd à Ministro sive improbo seu heterodoxo administrantur, cur Lutheruac maiores nostri secessionem à Pontificiâ Ecclesia fecerunt, nec Ministerio Pontificiorum Eccl. Dd. usi fuerunt? Respondet ad hoc dubium B. D. Mylius in A. C. part. 1. p. 144. id propterea esse factum, quia Papistae non ampliùs sederunt in Cathedrâ Mosis, & Apostolorum, sed his destructis suas erexerunt. Idem multò magis statuendum est de ritu ordinationis, ab haereticis collatae. Quâ de re evolvendi Augustinus lib. 2. cont. Epist. Parmen. c. 13. non longè à principio. Gregorius M. l. 2. ep. 32. ad Ioh. Episcopum Ravennatensem, Gregorii responsum relatum in ius Canonicum est C. sicut semel dist. 68. add. c. Quod quidam 1. q. 1. it. C. Si qui C. Ostenditur. C. rebaptizare. Atque hinc patet, quòd ineptè Iesuita Reihing in fundam. 3. relig. Cathol. p. 59. ita contra Lutherum insurgat: Quis te, exclamat, Luthere, Sacerdotio inauguravit? Quis tibi offerendi, & peccata remittendi potestatem impertivit? Catholicus Episcopus? Verus, an falsus? Pastor, an lupus? Si Pastor, ab illo discedens lupus factus es. Si lupus, quis te à lupo factum Pastorem agnoscat? &c. Idem certè hoc omnibus ab haereticis ordinatis obiici posset, quos tamen iura Pontificia verè ordinatos esse affirmant, ut modò ostensum. Deinde accuratè distinguendum officium à persona. Quod Episcopus ille Lutherum ordinavit, ad officium pertinuit; quòd Papalibus erroribus fuit immersus, personale fuit. Iam verò ex vitio personae Sacramentorum, nedum ordinationis, integritati nihil decedit, modò substantialia observentur. Ac probê notandum, quòd Episcopus ille Pontificius, à quo Luth. fuit ordinatus, non suo, sed Ecclesiae (quam in medio quoque Papatu conservatam fuisse, alibi ostensum) nomine & autoritate ordinationis ritu ad docendum verbum DEI, Lutherum adstrinxerit. Quâ dere paullò antè quoque actum fuit. Ex eo porrò, quòd Deus per corruptum Pharisae orum ministerium fuit efficax, quat. nempe sedebant in Cathedrâ Mosis, h. e. Mosis doctrinam proponebant & Sacr. Circumcisionis administrabant, nec tamen Iudaica Ecclesia propterea vera Ecclesia tum fuit, patet, quòd nec Papistica Ecclesia vera ac pura Ecclesia sit, licet per Iesuitas in India

quidem gentiles convertantur, quat. nempe doctrinam coelestem illi proponunt & Sacramentum Baptismi administrant, licet non usque adeò purè id semper fiat. Vid. B. Par. L. de Eccles. §. 188. Dun. Theol. Saxon. in Fundam. Pupillae Defens p. 42. Lud. de Dieu Praefat. ac not. ad Hist. Christi & Petri Persicè à Xavierio conscriptam.)*

*( κα-ά -ά έςγα &c. i. e. nolite talia opera facere, qualia ipsi faciunt. Obf. hic locus contra Pontificios, qui ex Matth. 16, 27. ac. 1. Petr. 1, 17. ubi Deus dicitur reddirurus unicuique κα-ά -ά έςγα, κα-ά τῶν πςάξιν άυτου. adstruere conantur operum merita. Quorum vanitatem pridem redarguit Gregorius Magnus P. R. quando in Ps. 7. poenit. t. 2. pag. 997. F. ita: Quòd si, scribit, illa sanctorum felicitas misericordia est, & non meritis acquiritur, ubi erit, quod scriptum est: ( Prov. 24.) Et tu reddes unicuique secundùm opera sua? Si secundùm opera redditur, quo modo misericordia aestimabitur? Sed aliud est secundùm opera reddere, aliud propter ipsa opera reddere. In eo enim, quòd secundùm opera dicitur, ipsa operum qualitas intelligitur, ut cuius apparuerint bona opera, eius sit & retributio gloriosa. Illi namq beatae vitae, in quo cum D-o & de Deo vivitur, nullus potest equari labor, nulla opera comparari, praesertim cum Apostolus dicat: ( Rom. 8.) Non sunt condignae passiones &c. Conf. etiam Apoc 22, 12.)*

v. 3. Dicunt, & non faciunt. Anton. l. 2.
