Poterat quidem ille, scribit de Christo, & praesens ab istis non teneri, si nollet: non occidi, si nollet; quia poterat & non nasci, si nollet: sed quia in omnire, quam gessit, ut homo hominibus in se credituris praebebat exemplum: quia unu-quisq servus DEI non peccat, si secesserit in alium locum, videns furorem fortè persequentium se, aut quaerentium in malum animam suam, Videretur autem servus Dei peccare, si faceret, nisi in faciendo Dominus praecessisset; fecit hoc ille Magister bonus, ut doceret, non quod timeret. Conf. Idem ep. 180. ad Honorat. it.

Socrates lib. 3. H. E. c. 6. Nicephorus Callistus lib. 10. H. E. c. 16. & videsis Analecta suprà ad c. 10, 23. it. B. Par. Dispp. Elencht. super Evang. Domin. p. 1305.)*

## 24:17
(v. 17. He who is on the housetop. He refers to the roofs of the Jews, which were so constructed, namely flat, that one could walk upon them, as is evident from Deut. 22. 7. And from this, the passages of Joshua 2, 6. 2. Sam. 11, 2.2. Reg. 1, 2.Matth. 10, 27.Act. 10, 9 &c. can also be understood. Let S. Jerome t. 3. epistle to Sunia and Fretela be compared. also B. Par. Comm. on the said place of Deuteronomy.)

Let him not take his garments i. e. let him not return to Papal abominations for the sake of temporal goods. *(Isidore of Pelusium l. 1. ep. 210. explains it in this way. He who has put off the old man, and has sent a message to carnal things, let him wear the new. But the literal sense is, he who is on the housetop, let him not descend to take anything, not even a cloak, which travelers otherwise especially need: but let him flee suddenly, so that he may at least preserve his life. But since the devastation of Judea and the city of Jerusalem by the Romans was not so sudden, some think that there is a hyperbole here. In the same way they also take the following: and he who is in the field &c. Comp. Jerem. 46, 5.c 48, 6.Gen. 19, 17. We learn, however, from this admonition of Christ, that greater account must be held of life than of faculties or fortune, if a loss of one or the other must be made in public calamities. See Gen. 19, 16. 17.Jerem. 39, last.)

Latin:

*(v. 17. Qui in tecto est. Respicit ad tecta Iudaeorum, quae ita erant constructa, planè nempe, ut iis inambulari possit, ceu patet ex Deut. 22. 7. Atque hinc intelligi quoq; possunt loca Iosuae 2, 6. 2. Sam. 11, 2.2. Reg. 1, 2.Matth. 10, 27.Act. 10, 9 &c. Conferatur S. Hieronymus t. 3. epist. ad Suniam & Frotellam. it. B. Par. Comm. ad d. l. Deuteron.)*

Non tollat vestimenta i. e. non redeat ad abominationes Papales propter bona temporalia. *(Isid. Pelusiota l. 1. ep. 210. h. m. exponit. Qui veterem hominem exuit, rebusq carnalibus nuncium misit, novum gestet. Sensus verò litteralis est, qui in tecto est, non descendat, tollere aliquid, ac ne penulam quidē, quâ aliàs pere grinantes cumprimis opus habent: sed subitò fugiat, ut vitam saltem conservet. Cùm verò non adeò repentina fuerit Iudaeae & urbis Hierusalem per Romanos vastatio, censent nonnulli, esse hîc hyperbolen. Eodem etiam modo accipiunt sequentia: & qui in agro est &c. Conf. Ierem. 46, 5.c 48, 6.Gen. 19, 17. Discimus verò ex hac Christi admonitione, quòd potior habenda racio vitaesit, quàm facultatum sive fortunae, si alterutrius facienda inpublicis calamitatibus iactura est. Vid. Gen. 19, 16. 17.Ierem. 39, ult.)*

## 24:19
v. 19. But woe to those who are with child. Piscator explains it thus: The condition of those women is going to be miserable above others, so much so that they will exclaim woe, woe, which is an interjection of one grieving. *(Moreover, although it is not denied that pregnant women will cry woe, woe, because of those immense calamities, and thus this particle is of one grieving: it is to be noted, however, that here also it is of one predicting all the most sad things that are to come. As it is taken Numbers 21, 29. Isaiah 1, 4. Habakkuk 2, 6. nay even of one pitying: (since the bowels of God are as it were moved, when He is forced to do a strange work, i. e. to punish impenitent men, when it is His own work to show mercy) but by no means of one condemning marriage, as Jerome seems to have understood, when to the words: Woe to those who are with child, he notes:

Not here are harlots condemned, but those swelling with womb: the wailing of infants, the fruits and works of nuptials. But how can God be a hater of that, namely of honest marriage, of which He is the author and preserver? See Gen. 1, 28.Psalm 113. 9Ps. 127, 3.Ps. 128, 3.1. Tim. 2, 15. More rightly, therefore, the same man in this place warns that τό woe is said of pregnant women, because burdened with a load they will not be able to flee. But this is by accident. See 1. Cor. 7, 26. and comp. S. Augustine serm. 20. on the V. D. But someone may ask, what is the cause that Christ denounces woe to pregnant women, but not to the sick and the decrepit, for whom, however, it is equally difficult as for them to provide for themselves by flight? Resp. Most Interpreters think that this is done because among the Jews fertility was otherwise held as a part of happiness, and in moderate war it was customary for women in childbirth to be spared. Therefore, the magnitude of the calamity and vengeance is described by these words, since it is going to be so great that the Romans will not show mercy even to pregnant women and infants, which is otherwise accustomed to happen in the occupation of cities. Isidore of Pelusium explains these words mystically in book 1. ep. 211. Woe, he writes, to those who are with child and to those who give suck in those days, the Lord says to those souls, which still carry the divine love as a womb, and do not dare to use freedom of words and confidence, and to bring forth the confession of GOD, and a sharp contention and struggle for Him, and which possess a childish and imperfect mind and sentiment concerning divine patience, and do not propose to themselves the hope of rewards, but are broken by threats or insults, and despoiled of future things.)*

Latin:

v. 19. Vae autem parturientibus. Piscator sic exponit: Condicio illarum foeminarum prae aliis misera est futura adeò, ut exclamaturae sint vae, vae, quae est dolentis interiectio. *(Coetetùm licet non negetur, quòd praegnantes ob ingentes illas calamitates clamaturae sint vae, vae, adeoque particula haec dolentis sit: notandum tamen, quòd etiam h. l. sit praedicentis tristissima quaeque futura. Ceu accipitur Numer. 21, 29. Esaiae 1, 4. Habacuc. 2, 6. quin etiam commiserantis: (cùm Deo viscera quasi commoveantur, quando alienum facere opus, h. e. homines impoenitentes punire cogitur, cùm proprium eius opus sit misereri) nequaquam verò coniugium damnantis, ceu Hieron. intellexisse videtur, quando ad verba: Vae praegnantibus, adnotat:

Non hîc scorta damnantur, sed utero tumentes: infantum vagitus, fructus atq opera nuptiarum. Ast quî Deus illius, nempe coniugii honesti, esse potest osor, cuius est autor ac conservator? Vid. Gen. 1, 28.Psalm 113. 9Ps. 127, 3.Ps. 128, 3.1. Tim. 2, 15. Rectiùs proinde idem in h. l. propterea τό vae de praegnantibus dici monet, quia sarcinâ gravatae fugere non poterunt. Hoc verò per accidens est. Vid. 1. Cor. 7, 26. ac conf. S. August. serm. 20. de V. D. Sed quaerat aliquis, quae causa sit, quòd Christus praegnantibus vae denunciet, non verò aegrotis ac decrepitis, quibus tamen aequè difficile ac illis, fugâ sibi consulere? Resp. Plerique Interpretes censent, id ideò fieri, cùm apud Iudaeos aliàs fuerit foecunditas in parte felicitatis habita, & in moderato aliàs bello puerperis parci conseveverit. Describitur proinde his verbis calamitatis & vindictae magnitudo, quippe quae tanta futura sit, ut ne quidem praegnantibus & infantibus, quod aliàs in urbium occupationibus fieri solet, Romani misericordiam sint exhibituri. Isidorus Pelusiota verba haec mysticè exponit lib. 1. ep. 211. Vae, scribit, praegnantibus & lactantibus in illis diebus, ait Dominus ad eas animas, quae divinum amorem velut uteradhuc gerunt, nec verborum libertate ac fiduciâ uti, DEiq confessionem, acremq pro eo contentionem ac dimicationem parere audent, quaeq puerilem & imperfectam de divinâ patientiâ mentem ac sententiam obtinent, nec praemiorum spem sibi proponunt, verùm minis aut insultibus fracta sunt, ac futuris rebus spoliatae.)*

## 24:20
(v. 20. Pray that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day. Our Savior speaks, as Chrysostom warns, whom Theophylactus and Euthymius followed, and of the more recent ones Ludov. Cappellus in Spic. p. 35. κατ ένδοξον: for the Jews thought, by an old superstition, see Ioseph. l. 13. A. I. and to this they also drew Exod. 16, 29. that it is not lawful to complete a just journey on the Sabbath, even if necessity were to press most strongly: but to proceed at least as far as is required for a walk. Although indeed they sometimes departed from that custom, vi-. 1. Macc. 2, 41. Compare also Capp l. c. p. 22. yet the Jews of following times by no means thought that one should remit from that old rigor, as is evident from -- (Cappellus cites the passage l. c. p. 35.). Christ indicates that it is to be wished, that the necessity of flight may not fall on the Sabbath, since indeed one must flee far beyond two thousand cubits, as much as was otherwise permitted for a journey on the Sabbath. The Savior indeed addresses Christians, converted from the Jews. Who although they were free from that forensic law, Christ nevertheless foresaw that they would still observe that law according to the old institution. Since Moses ought to have been buried with honor.)

Latin:

*(v. 20. Neq Sabbatho. Loquitur Salvator noster, monente Chrysostomo, quem sequuti Theophylactus & Euthymius, & ex recentioribus Ludov. Cappellus in Spic. p. 35. κατ ένδοξον: putabant enim Iudaei, veteri superstitione, vid. Ioseph. l. 13. A. I. eoque etiam trahebant Exod. 16, 29. non licere, iustū iter Sabbato conficere, si vel maximè necessitas urgeret: sed eo usque saltem progredi, quousque ad deambulationem requiritur. Licèt verò ali quando ab istâ consvetudine recesserint, vi-. 1. Macc. 2, 41. Conf. etiam Capp l. c. p. 22. hautquaquam tamen sequentium temporum Iudaei à veteri illo rigore remittendum duxerunt, ceu ex -- (locum adducit Cappellus l. c. p. 35.) constat. Indicat Christus, optandum esse, ne in Sabbatum incidat fugae necessitas, quippe cùm longè ultra bis mille cubitos, quantum aliàs iter Sabbato concessum, fugiendum sit. Alloquitur quidem Salvator Christianos, conversos è Iudaeis. Qui etsi liberi à lege istâ forensi, praescivit tamen Christus, ipsos adhuc legem eam ex veteri instituto observaturos. Quandoquidem Moses cum honore sepeliri debuerit.)*

## 24:21
v. 21. Such as has not been from the beginning &c. Josephus in the preface to the Jewish War: τό γούν πείντων άα αίωνος άτυχήματα προς -α Ιουδαίων ήττάσθαι μοι δοκεί κα-ά σύγυρισιν. All calamities from the beginning of the world do not seem able to be compared with those evils which rushed upon the Jews with great force. *(See also Isidore of Pelusium, book 4, ep. 74, 75. The Savior speaks of afflictions to be inflicted by men. Otherwise, it can hardly be denied that the punishment of the flood was greater. As the blessed D. Hunnius well advises in this place. Nor does He speak properly of the times which will precede the last day. As the Papist Doctors themselves well note: Stapleton, Promt. Cathol. Sunday 24 after Pentecost; Bessaeus in Script. praedic. on the same Sunday; Hoffmeister, Sunday 26 after Trinity; the Jesuit Tirinus in this place; and especially Corn. Jansenius, Bishop of Ghent, c. 122 of the Concordance. Whence there is no reason why Bellarmine, book 3 de P. R. c. 7, should urge from this that the Antichrist has not yet come, since calamities of that kind have not yet pressed upon the world.)*

ούδ ού μή γ-ύητομ. Nor ever shall be. A triple negation, which denies most strongly. He speaks, however, specifically of the Jewish people. But the affliction of those times will be miserable: 1. in its nature; 2. in its seduction, which is exaggerated 1. by the usurpation of a false name. They will call themselves Christs and Prophets. 2. by the confirmation of miracles. 3. from the multitude of the seduced. *(Compare Josephus, book 6, c. 11; book 7, c. 17. Although the Jews had suffered many disasters before also, namely in the Assyrian, Babylonian, and Syrian captivities, this one inflicted by Titus was the most grievous of all, as it brought the final destruction and desolation, which will last until the end of the world, according to the prediction of Daniel c. 9, v. last. The flood certainly also extended most widely, and was a heavy punishment:

but because that was sent immediately by GOD, without a hostile hand: therefore this is considered a more grievous punishment)*

Latin:

v. 21. Qualis non fuit à principio &c. Iosephus in praefat. Belli Iudaici: τό γούν πείντων άα αίωνος άτυχήματα προς -α Ιουδαίων ήττάσθαι μοι δοκεί κα-ά σύγυρισιν.Omnes calamitates ab initio mundi non videntur posse conferri cum iis malis, quae in Iudaeos magno impetu irruerunt. *(Videatur quoque Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 4. ep. 74. 75. Loquitur Salvator de afflictionibus per homines inferendis. Coeteroquin negari vix potest, quin poena diluvii fuerit maior. Uti benè monet B. D. Hunnius in h. l. Nec loquitur etiam propriè de temporibus, quae diem extremum praecedent. Ceu probè notant ipsi Dd. Pontificii Stapletonus Promt. Cathol. Dom. 24. post Pentec. Bessaeus in Ceript. praedic. eâdem: Dom. Hoffmeist. Dom. 26. post Trinit. Iesuita Tirinus in h. l. ac cumprimis Corn. Iansenius, Episcopus Gandav, c. 122. Concord. Unde non est, quòd Bellarminus l. 3. de P. R. c 7. urgeat hinc, Anti Christum nondum venisse, cùm istiusmodi calamitates nondum orbem presserint.)*

ούδ ού μή γ-ύητομ.Nec unquam fiet. Triplex negatio, quae fortissimè negat. Loquitur autem in specie de populo Iudaico. Misera verò erit 1. illorum temporum afflictio. 2. seductio, quae exaggeratur 1. à falsi nominis usurpatione. Vocabunt se Christos & Prophetas. 2. à miraculorum confirmatione. 3. ex seductorum multitudine. *(Conf. Ioseph. l. 6. c. 11. l. 7. c. 17. Licèt verò antè quoque, nempe in captivitate Assyriacâ, Babylonicâ, Syriacâ multas perpessi Iudaei clades fuerint, haec tamen à Tito illata omnium fuit gravissima, ut quae extremum attulit excidium, ac desolationem, quae ad finem usque mundi durabit, iuxta praedictionem Danielis c. 9. v. ult. Diluvium sanè latissimè quoque sese extendit, ac gravis fuit poena:

sed quia immediatè à DEO immissum illud fuit, citra hostilem manum: inde gravior haec censetur poenâ)*

## 24:22
*(v. 22. Unless those days had been shortened. Understand this by the eternal decree of GOD: for the discourse is concerning a matter still future. The sense is, unless God had decreed to shorten the time of that affliction, that is, to accelerate the occupation of the city. See a little later. Barth. Meyerus in de LXX. Heldom. p. 48. explains this prophecy concerning the final judgment.)* No flesh would be saved. i. e. no Jew would be preserved among the living: for thus σωζ σθαι, is used Mark 5, 23. Tossanus: unless the days of the siege were shortened, no Jew would be preserved among the living, because all would have perished by famine, but after the storming of the city some were preserved among the living. *(Concerning the phraseology see B. D. Glass. Gr. Sacr. p. 479. Hugo Grotius thinks that by these words reference is made to the robberies of the sicarii and Zealots, by which Galilee and Judea were being devastated, since they were so great that, unless the siege of the city had been accelerated, and unless God had brought it about that the Romans should emerge as victors of the city and occupy it sooner than could otherwise have happened by the powers of nature, without doubt as many as were in Judea would have fallen either by robbery or by mutual slaughters.)*

*( But for the elect's sake. Understand Christians, who would have been slaughtered like cattle by the sicarii, zealots, and tyrants, as being alien to the counsels of war. Thus Grotius in this place, who also shows that Christians are everywhere so called. B. D. Hunnius, however, understands it of the Jews, as those whom the Lord knew would be converted to the faith in the progress of the following centuries. It is evident, however, from this, that God takes care of His faithful ones: indeed in such a way that for the sake of the pious He sometimes suspends public calamities, sometimes finishes them sooner, or if He sends them at all, He nevertheless wondrously protects the pious. Conf. Gen. 6, 17.c. 7. 1. seqq. c. 18, 26. seq. c. 19, 21. 22,Ps. 27, 5.Ps. 31, 21.Ps. 91, 4.7.10.

Latin:

*(v. 22. Nisi decurtati fuissent dies illi. Intellige aeterno DEI decreto: sermo enim est de re adhuc futurâ. Sensus est, nisi Deus decrevisset, affliction is illius tempus abbreviare, h. e. accelerare occupationem urbis. Vid. paullò pòst. Barth. Meyerus in de LXX. Heldom. p. 48. exponit vatic. hoc de extremo iudicio.)* Non servaretur ulla caro. i. e. non conservaretur in vivis ullus Iudaeus: ita enim usurpatur σωζ σθαι,Marc 5, 23. Tossanus: nisi dies obsidionis decurtarentur, non servaretur in vivis Iudaeus, quia omnes fame periissent, sed post urbis expugnationem quidam in vivis servati. *(Do phraseologia vid. B. D. Glass. Gr. Sacr. p. 479. Hugo Grotius ad latrocinia sicariorum ac Zelotarum, quibus Galilaea ac Iudaea vastabatur, verbis his respici existimat, quippe quae tanta, ut nisi accelerata fuisset urbis obsidio, ac nisi Deus effecisset, ut Romani citiùs urbis evaderent victores, eamq; occuparent, quàm aliàs naturae viribus fieri posset, haut dubiè quotquot erant in Iudaeâ, aut latrocinio aut mutuis coedibus concidissent.)*

*( Sed propter electos. Christianos puta, qui sparti per Iudaeam & Galilaeam pecudū ritu caesi fuissent à sicariis, zelotis & tyrannis, utpote à belli consiliis alieni. Ita Grotius h. l. qui etiam ostendit, Christianos passim ita vocari. B. D. Hunnius verò de Iudaeis accipit ut quos Dominus noverit, sequentium seculorū progressu ad fidem conversum iri. Patet autem hinc, Deum fidelium suorum curam gerere: ita quidem, ut propter pios publicas calamitates aliquando suspendat, aliquando citiùs finiat, vel si omninò eas immittit, mirificè tamen pios protegat Conf. Gen. 6, 17.c. 7. 1. seqq. c. 18, 26. seq. c. 19, 21. 22,Ps. 27, 5.Ps. 31, 21.Ps. 91, 4.7.10.

## 24:23
*(v. 23. Lo, here is Christ &c. Conf. Luke 17, 21. The Savior now begins to treat of the signs of the final day, as indeed Interpreters commonly establish, and indeed among the ancients Chrysostom, Hilary, Jerome, Theophylact, Euthymius. Among the more recent, B. D. Hunnius in this place, among the Papists Sebastianus Barradius l. 9. Comm. in H. E. c. 9. Maldonatus in this place. (However, Abulensis, Salmeron, and some others disagree, having followed Origen) so that therefore τό you does not denote here the Apostles, but those believers whose age was to fall into those dangerous times. But someone might ask, why the Savior so suddenly changes the subject, and immediately subjects these things, which were to precede the last day, to the signs which were to precede the devastation of the city of Jerusalem? Resp. It was done not only because the disciples of Christ persuaded themselves, albeit falsely, that the end and limit of the city and of the world would be the same. Primarily, however, the Savior does this because that time which intervenes between the destroyed Jerusalem and the end of the world is considered in Holy Scripture as one age, one era, and the last time. See 1 Cor. 10:11Jas. 5:81 Pet. 4:71 John 2:18. Furthermore, Christ's prophecy is to be opposed to the superstitious pilgrimages to places, which the Papists call of the saints. For it must be known that Christ with his benefits is by no means tied to a certain place. See John 4:23. It is for the deceived to say, here is Christ, there is, etc. As regards places Exod. 20:24ch. 23:17 and similar. A distinction must be made between the times of the Old and New Testaments. But Henricus Lanceloz Mechlinensis ineptly opposes this prophecy of Christ to us in Anatomia Christiani deformati, p. 465. Just as, he exclaims, the proper mark of all heretics is the particularity of opinions and conventicles, for that is why they segregate themselves, that is why the Donatists boasted that the Church remained in Africa alone , that is why in the last times Pseudo-Christs and Pseudo-prophets rising will say, Matt. 24:23 Lo here is Christ, lo there; just as the Lutherans cry: Lo here, that is, in Wittenberg and in some other provinces of Germany, etc., is the true faith, knowledge, worship, Church, Sacraments, etc. of GOD, so the unique mark and credible testimony of the true, and therefore Roman, Catholic Church is the universality of place and doctrine, through which it extends itself to all places of the whole world, to all nations and kinds of men whatsoever, restricted by no certain corners, to all times, at least successively. Felicianus Capito opposes the same passage to us in Expos. Cathol. p. 615, writing against the truth about us, whom he brands as heretics, that we lack the word of GOD and the holy scripture, that we do not duly administer the Sacraments instituted by Christ, and lastly that we do not retain the succession of the elders and priests. All of which are manifestly false. But regarding the discourse of Lanzel. 1. That particularity or paucity is the mark of heretics is false: for it is evident that the number of believers is often greatly restricted, just as John the Baptist complains about the times in which Christ taught on earth John 3:32, saying of Christ: no one receives his testimony, i.e., few receive it. For although many flocked to Jesus: yet these, compared to the others remaining at home and neglecting the preaching of Christ, were few, and among these few some believed in Christ, others did not believe, such as the Scribes, Pharisees, and their followers. As the Jesuit Corn. à Lapide explains, and conformably to him also other Jesuits, such as Toletus, Maldonatus, Emanuel à Saa. But if few received Christ's testimony, i.e., believed in him, it follows that the number of true believers was then small, and therefore the multitude of believers is by no means a mark of the true Church, and the paucity of the false. 2. This also is false, that the Lutheran religion is circumscribed by the narrow boundaries of Germany, let alone of Wittenberg alone: Cardinal Bellarmine testifies to the contrary in the preface to book 1 of the Controversies, and likewise in the Oration prefixed to vol. 4 of his Works. 3. It must be accurately noted that although the religion which we profess received its name from B. Luther, that strong opponent of the Roman Anti-Christ, it is by no means new or first invented or devised by Luther: but is that very one which was handed down by Christ and the Apostles, and left to us in the monuments of the Sacred Scriptures. This is what a comparison of the articles of faith, which we embrace, with Holy Scripture most clearly teaches. Whence also our Church is truly Catholic, because it embraces the Catholic or Apostolic doctrine. See B. Par. Dispp. Elencht. super Ev. Dom. p. 1317. 4. How false is the rash assertion of Lanceloz, and his boasting that the doctrine of the Roman Church, as it is handed down by the Papists today, extends itself to all nations and all times whatsoever, was shown long ago by Philippus Marnixius in his discourse on the falsely called Catholic and Evangelical, part 3, ch. 11. See more things pertaining to this.

In B. Par. Confess. Cathol. book 2, special article 5, chapter 4, page 1165 and following. Some Calvinists are also accustomed to this, see Bucanus in Instit. Loc. 27, p. 276, Tossanus in the marginal notes of the Bibles. Luc. 17, 21. Zwileg. l. t. 2. Instit. p. 287. & others oppose this saying to our orthodox doctrine concerning the real and substantial presence of the body and blood of Christ in the Holy Eucharist, indeed in every kind of presence of Christ-man. But we respond 1. if the collection were legitimate, it would follow that Christ does not dwell in the hearts of the faithful, indeed that He is not even present on earth according to His divine nature, since it is said absolutely that one must not believe those who say: Behold here is Christ &c. It must be known therefore 2 that Christ here predicts that before the devastation of Jerusalem many False Prophets and False Christs would arise, who would claim for themselves the honor of the Messiah, would gather a numerous people to themselves, and would promise them external liberation from the oppression of the Romans. Christ seriously exhorts them not to have faith in those. That this is the genuine sense of the words of Christ, and that it is gathered from the circumstances, the blessed Par. rightly advises in L. de S. Coenâ §. 110. For the Savior is not speaking about the Eucharist, but about False Prophets, and He wishes that we expect no other Redeemer besides Himself. Now, however, in the Holy Eucharist no other Redeemer is proposed, but that same One who, born in time as a man from the Virgin Mary, is said to exhibit His body and blood in the Holy Eucharist by the power of His promise. Furthermore, the Savior speaks literally about the times of the devastation of Jerusalem, but accommodatively about the times that will immediately precede the consummation of the world. That He is present to us in the Holy Eucharist, and truly and substantially distributes His body and blood to those present who communicate, has always been handed down and believed in the Church. If anyone wishes to accommodate this to the last times, he will be able to understand it concerning the Papal Doctors, who bind Christ with His benefits to desert places: especially, however, do Monks and Nuns do this, who persuade themselves that the grace of Christ is to be sought in the desert, or in monasteries and especially in the inner chambers of these, and to they strive to apply their works to others.

See the blessed D. Hunnius on this passage p. 531. & 532. The blessed D. Heerbrand on this passage. The blessed Par. Dispp. Elencht. in Evang. Dom. p. 1313. Calvin himself in Harm. Evang. p. 363. compares it with the present passage. Luc. 17, 23. and similarly he explains concerning the Pseudo-Christs, who gathered whatever forces they could into the receptacles of the desert, or into caves or into other recesses, so that they might shake off the yoke of the Roman Empire by force and armed hand. And he adds: the sense therefore is, whoever collects his own forces into a hidden place, so that he may recover the liberty of the nation with arms, to sell himself falsely for Christ.

* (Do not believe, Similar admonitions and predictions concerning Pseudo-Prophets are spoken of also elsewhere, see above c. 7, 15. Actor. 20, 28.2. Cor. 11, 2.Gal. 3, 1. But why ought we not to have faith in those saying: Behold here, behold there is Christ, when nevertheless Christ is to return visibly at some time? Resp. Christ is indeed to return visibly, Act. 1, 11. but because his coming is to be unexpected, v. 27, and thus one can by no means pre-indicate or certainly point out to another the day of Christ's coming, from that it is manifest that they are frauds, if anyone should wish to point out Christ here in some visible form.) *

Latin:

*(v. 23. Ecce hîc est Christus &c. Conf. Luc. 17, 21. Incipit iam Salvator agere de signis extremi diei, uti quidem communiter Interpretes statuunt, & quidem è veteribus Chrysostomus, Hilarius, Hieronymus, Theophylactus, Euthymius. Erecen-ioribus, B. D. Hunnius in h. l. è Pontificiis Sebastianus Barradius l. 9. Comm. in H. E. c. 9. Maldonatus in h. l. (Dissentiunt tamen Abulensis, Salmeron aliique nonnulli, Originem sequuti) ut proinde τόvobis non notet hîc Apostolos, sed eos fideles, quorum aetas in periculosa illa tempora ut incideret, futurum erat. Quaerat verò aliquis, cur Salvator tam subitò mutet sententiam, atq haec, quae diem extremum praecessura sunt, immediatè subiiciat signis, quae vastationem urbis Ierusalem praecedere debebant? Resp. Factum non so-ùm proptereà, quia discipuli Christi eundem & urbis & orbis finem ac terminum fore, licet falsò, sibi persvadebant. Cumprimis tamen ideò hoc facit Salvator, quia tempus illud, quod inter eversam Hierosolymam ac mundi finem intercedit, unum quasi seculum, una aetas ac novissimum tempus in Sc. S. censetur. Vid. 1. Cor. 10, 11.Iacob. 5, 8.1. Petri 4, 7.1 Ioh. 2, 18. Coeterùm opponendum Christi vaticinium superstitiosis peregrinationibus ad loca, quae Pontificii vocant, sanctorum. Sciendum enim, quòd -hristus cum beneficiis suis minimè ad certum locum sit alligatus. Vid. Ioh. 4, 23. Deceptorum est, dicere, hîc est Christus, illic est &c. Quod attinet loca Exod 20, 24.c. 23, 17. & similia. Distingvendum inter Veteris, ac Novi Testamenti tempora. Ineptè verò nobis vaticinium hoc Christi opponit Henricus Lanceloz Mechlinensis in Anatomia Christiani deformati, p. 465. Quemadmodum, exclamat, haereticorum omnium propria tessera est opinionum & conventiculorum particularitas, ideò enim segregant semetipsos, ideò Donatistae in sola remansisse Africâ Ecclesiam ia-tit abant, ideò novissimis temporibus Pseudo Christi & Pseudo prophetae surgentes dicent,Matth. 24, 23. Ecce hîc est Christus, ecce illic; sicut Lutherani clamant: Ecce hîc, id est, Wittenbergae atq in aliis aliquot Germaniae provinciis &c. est vera DEI fides, cognitio, cultus, Ecclesia, Sacramenta &c. ita Ecclesiae Catholicae verae, adeoq Romanae unica nota & Testimonium credibile nimis, est universalitas loci atque doctrinae, per quam ad omnia totius mundi loca, omnes omninò nationes & hominum genera, nullis certis angulis adstricta, ad omnia tempora, successivè saltem, se extendat Eundem nobis locum opponit Felicianus Capito in Expos. Cathol. p. 615. invitâ veritate de nobis, quos haereticos indigitat, scribens, quòd careamas verbo DEI sanctâq scripturâ, quòd Sacramenta à Christo instituta non debitè administremus, ac ultimò maiorum & Sacerdotum successionem non retineamus. Quae omnia manifestè falsa sunt. Ad Lanzel. verò discursum resp. 1. particularitatem seu paucitatem esse tesseram haereticorum, falsum est: constat namque, quòd credentium numerus saepè valdè coarctetur, quemadmodum Iohannes Baptista de temporibus, quibus Christus in terris docuit, conqueritur Ioh. 3, 32. dicens de Christo: testimonium eius nemo accipit, q. d. pauci accipiunt. Etenim licet multi confluerent ad Iesum: tamen hi prae coeteris domi manentibus & Christi praedicationem negligentibus, erant pauci, atq inter hos paucos alii in Christum credebant, alii non credebant, ut Scribae, Pharisaei & eorum adseclae. Uti exponit Iesuita Corn. à Lapide, eidemque conformiter etiam alii Iesuitae, uti Toletus, Maldonatus, Emanuel à Saa. Si verò pauci Christi testimonium acceperunt h. e. in ipsum crediderunt, sequitur, quòd verè credentium exiguus tùm fuerit numerus, adeoque verae Ecclesiae nota minimè sit credentium multitudo, ac falsae paucitas. 2. falsum & hoc est, quòd Lutherana religio angustis Germaniae nedum solius Wittebergae cancellis circumscripta: contrarium testatur Cardinalis Bellarminus in praefat. l. 1. Controv. itemque in Orat. t. 4. Oper. prae fixâ. 3. accuratè notandum, quòd licèt religio, quam nos profitemur, à B. Luthero, forti isto Anti Christi Romani opppugnatore, nomen acceperit, minimè tamen nova sit vel à Luthero primùm inventa vel excogitata: sed ipsa illa, quae à Christo & Apostolis tradita est, inque Sacrarum monumentis litterarum nobis relicta. Id quod collatio articulorum fidei, quos amplectimur, cum Sc. S. clarissimè docet. Unde etiam nostra Ecclesia verè Catholica est, quia amplectitur doctrinam Catholicam seu Apostolicam. Vid. B. Par. Dispp. Elencht. super Ev. Dom. p. 1317. 4. quàm falsum sit temerarium Lancelozi adsertum, ac gloriatio, quòd Romanae Ecclesiae doctrina, quatenus à Papistis hodie traditur, ad omnes omninò nationes atque omnia tempora sese extendat, pridem ostendit Philippus Marnixius in discursu falsò dictae Catholicae & Evang. part. 3. c. 11. Vid. plura huc facientia

apud B. Par. Confess. Cathol. l. 2. spec. art. 5. c. 4. pag. 1165. seqq. Solent quoque Calviniani nonnulli, vid. Bucanus in Instit. Loc. 27. p. 276. Tossanus in not. margin. Bibliorum Luc. 17, 21. Zwileg. l. t. 2. Instit. p. 287. & alii dictum hoc opponere orthodoxae nostrae doctrinae de reali ac substantiali corporis ac sangvinis Christi in S. Eucharistiâ praesentiâ, imò in genere omni praesentiae Christi-hominis. Verùm resp. 1. si collectio esset legitima, sequeretur, Christum nec in cordibus fidelium habitare, imò nec secundùm divinam naturam in terris esse praesentem, cùm absolutè dicatur, non esse credendum illis, qui dicunt: Ecce hîc est Christus &c. Sciendum igitur 2 quòd Christus hîc praedicat, ante Hierosolymitanam devastationem multos surrecturos Pseudo Prophetas & Pseudo Christos, qui honorem Messiae sibi sint vendicaturi, numerosum populum sibi aggregaturi & externam à Romanorum oppressione liberationem eidem promissuri. Illis ne fidem habeant, seriò Christus hîc hortatur. Quem genuinum verborum Christi sensum esse, eundemque ex circumstantiis colligi, rectè monet B. Par. L. de S. Coenâ §. 110. Etenim Salvator non de Eucharistia loquitur, sed de Pseudo Prophetis, vultque, ut nullum alium, praeteripsum, expectemus Redemtorem. Iam verò in S. Eucharistiâ nō alius proponitur Redemtor, sed idem ille, qui in tempore natus homo ex Maria Virgine est, suum corpus & sanguinem in S. Eucharistiâ vi suae promissionis exhibere dicitur. Praetereà loquitur Salvator litteraliter de Temporibus devastationem Hierosolymorum, accommodativè verò de temporibus, mundi consummationem proximè praecessuris. Quòd verò in S. Eucharistia praesens nobis ipse sit, suumq; corpus & sanguinem verè ac substantialiter praesentia communicantibus distribuat, semper in Ecclesia traditum ac creditum fuit. Si quis ad tempora novissima hoc velit accommodare, poterit intelligere ea de Doctoribus Pontificiis, qui Christum cum suis beneficiis alligant ad deserta loca: cumprimis verò id faciunt Monachi & Moniales, qui Christi gratiam in deserto, seu in coenobiis & horum quidem penetralibus cumprimis quaerendam esse sibi persvadent, ad eo-ue opera sua aliis applicare satagunt.

Vid. B. D. Hunnius in h. l. p. 531. & 532. B. D. Heerbrandus in h. l. B. Par. Dispp. Elencht. in Evang. Dom. p. 1313. Calvinus ipse in Harm. Evang. p. 363. confert cum praesenti Loco Luc. 17, 23. ac similiter de Pseudo Christis, qui quascunpoterant copias in receptacula deserti, vel in speluncas vel in alios recessus contraxerunt, ut iugum Romani Imperii vi & manu armat â à se excuterent, exponit. Ac addit: sensus ergò est, quicunopes suas in locum abditum colligit, ut gentis libertatem armis recuperet, se pro Christo mendaciter venditare.) *

* (Nolite credere, Similes admonitiones ac praedictiones de Pseudo Prophetis loguntur quoque alibi, vid. suprà c. 7, 15. Actor. 20, 28.2. Cor. 11, 2.Gal. 3, 1. Sed cur non debemus fidem habere dicentibus: Ecce hîc, ecce illic est Christus, cùm tamen Christus visibiliter aliquando rediturus sit? Resp. Christus quidem visibiliter rediturus est, Act. 1, 11. ast quia adventus eius futurus inopinatus, v. 27. adeoque alter alteri minimè praemonstrare sive certò indicare adventûs Christi diem potest, inde manifestum est, fraudes esse, si quis praemonstrare Christum in visibili aliquâ specie hîc voluerit.) *

## 24:24
v. 24. For there shall arise Pseudo-Christs. Concerning these, let there be consulted by all means Christianus Gerson in the Talmud of the Jews c. 9, Weidnerus in the preface of his book, Frantzius Disp. on Sacrifices XI. §. 4. * (Compare also Analect. to v. 5, likewise H. Grot. to this place.) * Augustinus in Expos. Ps. 147. Pseudo-Christs and Pseudo-Prophets shall arise, and shall say: Behold here, behold there: for they shall not say concerning the head himself: Behold here, behold there: for it is known that Christ is in the heavens, but concerning the Church, where Christ is, who says: Behold I am with you, even to the consummation of the age. Furthermore, Hieronymus in his Commentary on this place warns that this prediction is to be understood concerning the times of the Anti-Christ, and it is also evident from similar sayings, such as Luc. 18, 7.2. Thess. 2. 34.1. Tim 4, 1. 2. 3.2. Tim. 4, 3. 4.2. Pet. 2, 1.Apoc. 12, 6.c. 13, 8.16.c. 17, 2.c. 18. 3. By no means, therefore, is it to be thought that the public ministry of the visible Church in the N. T. will be perpetually uncorrupted and pure. Contrary to the boastings of the Papists. Compare B. Par. Book on the Church §. 112. It is to be observed well, however, that in the Greek text here there is ἐγερθήσονται they shall be raised up, so that it may be hinted that the Pseudo-Prophets are not called by GOD, but are raised up by Satan. And this is the property of Pseudo-Prophets, to come without a divine calling, Ier. 23, 21. concerning which matter B. Par. treats at length in the Place on the Ministry of the Church §. 55. seqq.) *

* (They shall give many signs and wonders. Compare parallel passages Exod. 7, 22.c. 8, 7.Deut. 13, 1. 2.2. Tim. 3, 8. above c. 7, 22.Luc. 11. 19.2. Thess. 2. 3.Apoc. 13, 13. Since, therefore, false prophets and heretics also perform miracles, which, however, are not truly and strictly called miracles, but at least wonders, see B. Par. L. de Eccl. §. 271.) it is manifest that miracles are not a proper, genuine, and infallible mark of the Church. As was also shown long ago at length by B. D. Meisner against Leonh. Lessius p. 20. 54. 205. and elsewhere. B. P. L. de Eccl. §. 273. Confess. Cathol. l. 2. spec. part. 1. Dispp. Elencht. p. 1317. and others. But why God permitted those who sold themselves as Christs to produce such signs, H. Grotius explains in this place, which can be consulted. We have a clear example of such false prophets among the Papists, for whom nothing is as customary as to boast of miracles. Compare more things pertaining to this in Analect. ad Marc. 13, 22.) *

* (To seduce, if it were possible, even the elect. That by the elect in this place are understood those elected to glory is the almost common opinion of interpreters. Although they may be thought to be understood specifically as Christians who could and ought to have fled from Jerusalem: likewise those who, during the siege already then occurring, were struck by such a disaster and converted to Christ: nevertheless, our people rightly infer from this in general that the elect cannot perish finally. This is what the Savior also teaches elsewhere, see Ioh. 10, 28. and likewise the Apostle Rom. 11, 7. St. Augustine excellently agrees in book 13 de Trin. c. 16. None of the predestined will perish with the Devil, none will be under the power of the devil unto death. Thus also elsewhere, for instance tr. 45 in Ioh. If he is predestined, he has erred for a time, he will not perish for eternity. The same author has twin statements in his book de fide ad Petrum. But it is by no means to be thought as if Christ means this as though the elect could not fall from some absolute εὐδοκίᾳ or decree of GOD, or that they could not absolutely become reprobate, in whatever manner they might conduct themselves, but this is said to be impossible because God from eternity foreknew that they would not maliciously, like the rest, persevere in their sins, but would return to Christ by true faith and would finally persevere in the same. Now the knowledge of God is infallible. If, therefore, God had known that those very persons would finally persevere in their sins, or that, having fallen, they would not return again to Christ through true repentance, then He would not have chosen them. Although, however, the elect cannot finally to fall from the grace of GOD, they can nevertheless through mortal sins that is, against knowledge and conscience, more grave crimes having been committed, fall from that divine grace totally. As is evident from c. 26, 31. 34. Gal. 2, 14. Against the Calvinists. Against whom the blessed Doctors dispute at length: Sigwart in Admin. Christianâ de Irenico Paraei p. 483. Mentzer in his declaration to the Response of Ioh. Appel. c. 10. c. B. D. Meisner Anthropol. S. Disp. 19. B. Durfeld in his treatise on the Perseverance of the Saints, B. D. Tarnov in the inaugural Disputation held under the presidency of D. Affelmann, likewise in another, which the President himself held in the year 1620, Giesens. t. 2. dispp. p. 126. following. Marp. Dispp. t. 1. page 154. The same blessed Theologians of Marburg in Deduct. Fundam. p. 269. following. B. Par. Dispp. Isagog. L. de Elect. c. 1. §. 14. c. 8. §. 9. 10. c. 9. §. 3. 4. following, likewise Dispp. Elencht. super Ev. Domin. p. 1320. 1321. Compare more in the Analects to Mark 13, 22. Furthermore, just as it is rightly gathered from this place against the Calvinists, that the elect cannot become reprobate, that is, finally fall from the grace of GOD and perish: so the Papists attempt less rightly to elicit from this that the Church (by which they understand only the Papal or Roman, or rather, as the final analysis teaches, the Roman Pontiff) cannot err. But it must be noted 1. that one man, such as the Roman Pontiff is, cannot be called the Church. 2. if they should even at most understand by the Church the whole assembly, that then a distinction must be made 1. between the Catholic Church, concerning which it is granted, and a particular one, such as the Roman also is, concerning which it is denied. 2. between fundamental errors and less fundamental ones. 3. between τὸ erring for a time, and finally, 4. between the external splendor of the Church, such as the Papists defend, (of which, however, no promise exists in Holy Scripture, but rather the contrary. See. Apoc. 14, 17. 18.) & between her internal beauty, Psalm. 45. and her perpetual duration: Therefore, Christ at least indicates by these present words that it is impossible for the true Church to perish entirely, without there being found from time to time some holy remnants, some elect and faithful ones, who are immune from all errors, or certainly from such errors as overturn the foundation, although they may be entangled in lighter errors, or finally, who in the final examination of temptation perform penance for their errors, and with the stubble of erroneous opinions burning away, they themselves are saved upon the rock of salvation, Christ, for all eternity, as the blessed D. Hunnius sets forth our opinion in this place; confer also the blessed Par. L. on the Church §. 104.) *

Latin:

v. 24. Surgent enim Pseudo Christi. De his videatur omninò Christianus Gerson in Talmud Iudaeorum c. 9. Weidnerus in praefat. sui libri, Frantzius Disp. de Sacrific. XI. §. 4. * (Conf. etiam Analect. ad v. 5. it. H. Grot. ad h. l.) * Augustinus in Expos. Ps. 147.Exurgent Pseudo Christi & Pseudo Prophetae, & dicent: Ecce hîc, ecce illic: non enim de ipso capite dicent: Ecce hîc, ecce illic: notum enim est, quòd Christus in coelis est, sed de E-clesia, ubi Christus est, qui ait: Ecce ego vobiscum sum, usad consummationem seculi. Coeterùm praedictionem hanc de temporibus AntiChristi accipiendam esse, monet Hieronymus Comm. h. l. & patet quoque ex similibus dictis, uti Luc. 18, 7.2. Thess. 2. 34.1. Tim 4, 1. 2. 3.2. Tim. 4, 3. 4.2. Pet. 2, 1.Apoc. 12, 6.c. 13, 8.16.c. 17, 2.c. 18. 3. Hautquaquam igitur existimandum est, publicum visibilis Ecclesiae ministerium in N. T. perpetuò in corruptum purumq; futurum. Contra Pontificiorum gloriationes. Conf. B. Par. L. de Eccles. §. 112. Observandum autem probè est, quòd in Graeco textu hîc sit ἐγερθήσονταιsuscitabuntur, ut innuatur, Pseudo Prophetas non vocari à DEO, sed à Satana suscitari. Atque hoc est proprium Pseudo Prophetarum, absque divinâ vocatione venire, Ier. 23, 21. quá de re prolixè agit B. Par. Loco de Minist. Eccles. §. 55. seqq.) *

* (Dabunt signa & prodigia multa. Conf. loca parallela Exod. 7, 22.c. 8, 7.Deut. 13, 1. 2.2. Tim. 3, 8. suprà c. 7, 22.Luc. 11. 19.2. Thess. 2. 3.Apoc. 13, 13. Quia igitur Pseudoprophetae & Haereticifaciunt quoque miracula, quae tamen verè & strictè sic dicta miracula non sunt, sed mira saltem, vid. B. Par. L. de Eccl. §. 271.) manifestum est, quòd miracula non sint propria, genuina & infallibilis Ecclesiae nota. Ceu pridem etiam ostensum prolixè à B. D. Meisnero contra Leonh. Lessium p. 20. 54. 205. alibi. B. P. L. de Eccl. §. 273. Confess. Cathol. l. 2. spec. part. 1. Dispp. Elencht. p. 1317. aliis. Cur verò Deus permiserit, ut illi, qui se Christos venditabant, talia signa ederent, exponit H. Grotius in h. l. qui potest evolvi. Luculentum verò huiusmodi Pseudoprophetarum exemplum in Pontificiis habemus, ut quibus nil ae què solenne est, quàm miracula iactitare. Conf. plura huc facientia in Analect. ad Marc. 13, 22.) *

* (Ut seducerentur, si fieri posset electi. Per electos h. l. intelligi electos ad gloriam, communis ferè Interpretum sententia est. Licet verò in specie intelligi censeant Christianos, qui è Ierusalem fugere poterant ac debebant: item qui durante iam tum obsidione, tantâ quippe clade perculsi à ad Christum conversi fuerunt: rectè tamen nostrates hinc in genere inferunt, quòd electi non possint finaliter perire. Id quod etiam alibi Salvator docet, vid. Ioh. 10, 28. itemque Apostolus Rom. 11, 7. Adstipulatur egregiè S. Augustinus lib. 13. de Trin. c. 16. Praedestinatorum nemo cum Diabolo peribit, nemo usad mortem sub diaboli potestate erit. Sic & alibi, puta tr. 45. in Ioh. Si praedestinatus est ad tempus erravit, in aeternum non peribit. Gemella habet idem lib. de fide ad Petrum. Hautquaquam verò existimandum, ac si Christus hoc velit, quasi electi non possint cadere ex absolutâ quâdam DEI εὐδοκίᾳ vel decreto, aut quòd absolutè non potuerint fieri reprobi, quocunque tandem sese gererent modo, sed dicitur hoc impossibile, quia Deus ab aeterno praescivit, illos non malitiosè, ceu reliqui, in peccatis suis perseveraturos esse, sed verâ fide ad Christum redituros inque eâdem finaliter perseveraturos. Iam scientia Dei infallibilis est. Si igitur Deus scivisset, illos ipsos finaliter in peccatis suis perseveraturos, vel lapsos iterum per veram poenitentiam non redituros ad Christum esse, tunc eos non elegisset. Licèt verò electi non possint finaliter excidere gratiâ DEI, possunt tamen per peccata mortalia h-e. contra scientiam ac conscientiam graviora admissa scelera gratiâ illâ divinâ excidere totaliter. Ceu patet ex c. 26, 31. 34. Gal. 2, 14. Contra Calvinianos. Quos contra prolixè disputant Bb. Dd. Sigwartus in Admin. Christianâ de Irenico Paraei p. 483. Mentzerus declar. ad Responsum Ioh. Appelii. c. 10. c. B. D. Meisner Anthropol. S. Disp. 19. B. Durfeldius in pec. tr. de Persev. Sanctorum, B. D. Tarnov. in Disp. inaug. sub D. Affelmanni praesid. habitâ, it. in aliâ, quam ipse Praeses An. 1620. habuit, Giesens. t. 2. dispp. p. 126. seqq. Marp. Dispp. t. 1. pag. 154. Idem Dnn. Theologi Marpurg. in Deduct. Fundam. p. 269. seqq. B. Par. Dispp. Isagog. L. de Elect. c. 1. §. 14. c. 8. §. 9. 10. c. 9. §. 3. 4. seqq it. Dispp. Elencht. super Ev. Domin. p. 1320. 1321. Conf. plura in Analectis ad Marc. 13, 22. Coeterùm sicut rectè ex h. l. colligitur contra Calvinianos, quòd electi non possint fieri reprobi h. e. finaliter excidere gratiâ DEI ac perire: ita minùs rectè elicere hinc Pontificii conantur, quòd Ecclesia (per quam Pontificiam solùm sive Romanam, vel potiùs, ceu ultima analysis docet, Pontificem intelligunt Romanum) non possit errare. Verùm notandum 1. quòd unus homo, qualis Pontifex Romanus est, non possit vocari Ecclesia. 2. si vel maximè per Ecclesiam intelligant coetum totum, quòd tunc distingvendum sit 1. inter Ecclesiam Catholicam, de quâ conceditur, & inter particularem, qualis etiam Romana est, de quâ negatur. 2. inter errores fundamentales & minùs fundamentales. 3. inter τὸerrare ad tempus, & finaliter, 4. inter externum Ecclesiae splendorem, qualem Ponficii defendunt, (cuius tamen nullum in Sc. S. extat promissum, sed potiùs contrarium. Vid. Apoc. 14, 17. 18.) & inter internum eius decorem,Psalm. 45. ac perpetuam eius durationem: Hoc igitur saltem Christus praesentibus verbis indicat, quòd impossibile sit, ut Ecclesia vera penitùs intercidat, quin subinde reperiantur reliquiae aliquae sanctae, aliqui electi & fideles, qui à cunctis erroribus immunes, aut certè à talibus erroribus, qui fundamentum evertunt, licèt levioribus erroribus implicentur, aut denique, qui in novissimo tentationis examine errorum suorum poenitentiam agunt, & deflagrantibus opinionum erronearum stipulis, ipsi super rupe salutis Christo in omnem aeternitatem salvantur, uti sententiam nostram proponit B. D. Hunnius in h. l. confer. quoque B. Par. L. de Eccles. §. 104.) *

## 24:25
* (v. 25. Behold I have told you beforehand. Beautifully the Author of the Imperfect Work in this place: Therefore he says this, so that he may take away the excuse of ignorance from men, and so that the preceding warning may make the following punishment just. For it is mercy to forestall danger with commands. For he does not wish anyone to perish, who shows to all the coming of destruction Conf Rom. 2, 4.) *

Latin:

* (v. 25. Ecce praedixi vobis. Pulcrè Auctor Op. Imperf. in h. l. Propterea hoc dicit, ut excusationem ignorantiae tollat ab hominibus, & ut praecedens contestatio iustam faciat sequentem poenam. Misericordia enim est, mandatis praevenire periculum. Non enim vult quemquam perire, qui omnibus monstrat perditionis adventum Conf Rom. 2, 4.) *

## 24:26
v. 26. Behold he is in the desert. He seems to refer to the Gerasene, the son of Gioras, of whom Josephus treats in *Bellum Iudaicum*, book 5, ch. 7. For impostors were accustomed to lead miserable men into the desert, so that they might gather forces more safely there.) * * (

* (Behold in the inner chambers, namely, of the temple. For it seems to have been fulfilled in Eleazar and John, the leaders of the Zealots, who occupied the inner approach of the temple. See Josephus book 6, Jewish War, ch. 1 & 4; add the same book 7, ch. 11. Or it can be taken concerning secret conventicles in general, which deceivers were seeking, not yet being equipped with sufficient strength. The blessed D. Glassius, Philology of Scripture, p. 96, judges that the plural number is placed here for the singular, namely for some one of the inner chambers. Furthermore, Thomas Stapleton seizes the opportunity from this to proclaim our Church as heretical, in that it does not enjoy external splendor, which, as is known, the Papists falsely establish as a mark of the true Church. But one must accurately distinguish between the external and internal splendor of the Church. Concerning the latter, which consists in the sincerity of Apostolic doctrine, we deny that our Church lacks it. We add, however, that that interior beauty of the Church Ps. 45, 14. let it be known to GOD alone. vit. 1. Sam. 16. 7.1. Reg. 8, 39.c. 19, 14. & 18.Ier. 5, 3.c, 17, 10.Ioh 10, 14.2. Tim 2, 19.Apoc. 2, 19. Compare more things making for this in B Par. Disp. p. Elencht. p. 1319. Confess. -athol. lib. 2. spec. part. 1. LL. Theolog. de Eccl. § 172. But as it concerns the present information of Christ, it is so far from favoring the Papists, that it rather beautifully convicts their institutions of error. See the notes above at v. 23.) *

* (Do not believe. Compare Deut. 13, 1. 2. 3. for there will be spirits of error, and they will teach doctrines of demons, 1. Tim. 4. 1. Compare 2. Petr. 2, 1. following Coloss. 2, 13.)

Latin:

* (v. 26. Ecce in deserto est. Videtur respicere ad Gerasenum, Giorae filium, quô de Iosephus agit lib. 5. B. I. c. 7. Solebant nempe imposteres miseros homines in desertum abducere, ut eò tutiùs vires sumerent.) *

* (Ecce in penetralibus, sc. templi. Videtur enim impletum in Eleazaro & Iohanne, Zelotarum ducibus, qui interiorem templi aditum insederunt. Vid. Iosephus l. 6. B. I. c. 1. & 4. add. idem l. 7. c. 11. vel potest accipi de clanculariis conventibus in genere, quos quaerebant seductores, nondum sufficientibus instructi viribus. B. D. Glassius Gr. S. p. 96. pluralem numerum pro sing. hîc poni censet, nempe pro aliquo penetraliū Coeterùm Thomas Stapletonus occasionem arripit hinc. Ecclesiam nostram ut haereticam proclamandi, eò quòd non gaudeat splendore externô, quem, ut notum est, Pontificii Ecclesiae verae notam falsò constituunt. Verùm accuratè distinguendum est inter splendorem Ecclesiae externum, & internum. De hoc, qui in doctrinae Apostolicae sinceritate consistit, negamus, quòd nostra Ecclesia illô careat. Addimus tamen, quòd interior illa Ecclesiae pulchritudo Ps. 45, 14. soli DEO cognita sit. vit. 1. Sam. 16. 7.1. Reg. 8, 39.c. 19, 14. & 18.Ier. 5, 3.c, 17, 10.Ioh 10, 14.2. Tim 2, 19.Apoc. 2, 19. Conf. plura huc facientia apud B Par. Disp. p. Elencht. p. 1319. Confess. -athol. lib. 2. spec. part. 1. LL. Theolog. de Eccl. § 172. Quod verò praesentem Christi informationem concernit, tantum abest, ut Pontificiis patrocinetur, ut potiùs pulcrè illorum instituta erroris convincat. Vid. notata suprà ad v. 23.) *

* (Nolite credere. Conf. Deut. 13, 1. 2. 3. erunt enim spiritus erroris, docebuntque doctrinas daemoniorum, 1. Tim. 4. 1. Conf. 2. Petr. 2, 1. seqq. Coloss. 2, 13.) *

## 24:27
v 27. As the lightning &c. Just as lightning is not tied to any certain place, so neither is the Church: but wherever the word and Sacraments will be in true use, in whatever place of the world, whether in the East or in the West, there will Christians be gathered. Tossanus understands it of the last coming of Christ to judgment, so that the sense is: that coming will be public and sudden, so that it is not necessary to seek him here or there, as if he had indeed come, but secretly and hiddenly, 2. Petr. 3, 10. * (Corn. à Lapide likewise understands it of the coming of Christ to judgment, which he writes will be like lightning, because it will be 1. sudden. 2. unexpected. 3. manifest to all. 4. glorious. 5. effective. 6. not on earth, but in the air. In the same way, that is, concerning the last coming of Christ, Chrysostom also understood it from the Fathers. As also the author of the Opus Imperfectum. Who also, (which is to be observed against the Calvinists, Sadeel, de veritate humanae nat. in Christo. p. 7. & 488. Sohnium t. 2. p. 545. Wendelinum Syst. Mai. p. 602. & 1247., establishing that the coming of Christ to judgment is opposed to his real and substantial presence according to human nature) notably adds: Christ, since he is everywhere, does not come from place to place: but he who was hidden everywhere will be shown everywhere. He distinguishes, indeed, between the visible and invisible, or local and illocal, presence of Christ the man. Which distinction our people also rightly urge against the Calvinists. Of the former it is treated in Matth. 18. & 28., of the latter in Act. 1, 11.1. Thess. 1, 10. &c. See Bb. Dd. Hutterus LL. Theol. Mai.

p. 185. Lobechius in A. C. p. 450. following. Mentzerus against Crocium p. 210. B. Par. L. de Extr. Iud. §. 34. also Dispp. Elencht. p. 1343. Furthermore, B. Par. L. de Extr. Iudic. §. 89. joins both expositions mentioned above, where he also observes that the restoration of heavenly doctrine is promised in these words, to be accomplished by the preaching of the word with incredible speed before the end of the world. The same is also established by B. D. Hunnius in this place. Cornelius Iansenius Comm in Conc. Ev. p. 844. brings forward Origen, Jerome, and Augustine for this opinion. He could also have added Hilary in Ps. 134. Meanwhile, it seems most likely that Christ is speaking here primarily of his coming to the final judgment, which can most conveniently be compared to lightning. Secondarily, however, of the restoration of heavenly doctrine, once the darkness of the Anti-Christian abominations has been dispelled.

Latin:

v 27. Sicut fulgur &c. Quemadmodum fulgur non alligatur certo alicui loco, sic nec Ecclesia: sed ubicunq; erit verbum & Sacramenta in vero usu, quocunque orbis terrarum loco, sive in Oriente, sive in Occidente, ibi congregabuntur Christiani. Tossanus accipit de ultimo Christi ad iudicium adventu, ut sit sensus: adventus ille erit publicus & repentinus, ut non sit necesse, eum hîc vel illic quaerere, quasi venerit quidem, sed clam & occultè, 2. Petr. 3, 10. * (Corn. à Lapide itidem de adventu Christi ad iudicium accipit, quem fulguris instar futurum scribit, quia futurus. subitus. 2. inexpectus. 3. omnibus manifestus. 4. gloriosus 5. efficax. 6. non in terrâ, sed in aêre. Eodem modo, puta de adventu Christi ultimo, è Patribus intellexit quoque Chrysostomus. Quemadmodum etiam autor Operis Imperfecti. Qui etiam, (quod contra Calvinianos, Sadeelm, de veritate humanae nat. in Christo. p. 7. & 488. Sohnium t. 2. p. 545. Wendelinum Syst. Mai. p. 602. & 1247. observandum, statuentes, quòd adventus Christi adiudicium oppositus, sit reali eius ac substantiali secundùm humanam naturam praesentiae) notanter addit: Christus cùm sit ubique, non venit â loco ad locum: sed ubique ostendetur, qui erat celatus ubique. Distingvit nempe inter praesentiam Christi hominis visibilem & invisiblem, seu localem & illocalem. Quam distinctionem rectè quoque nostrates contra Calvinianos urgent. De hâc agitur Matth. 18. & 28. de illa Act. 1, 11.1. Thess. 1, 10. &c. Vid. Bb. Dd. Hutterus LL. Theol. Mai.

p. 185. Lobechius in A. C. p. 450. seqq. Mentzerus contra Crociump. 210. B. Par. L. de Extr. Iud. §. 34. it. Dispp. Elencht. p. 1343. Coeterùm utramque expositionem suprà memoratam, coniungit B. Par. L. de Extr. Iudic. §. 89. ubi etiam observat, promitti his verbis instaurationem doctrinae coelestis, incredibili celeritate ante mundi finem praedicatione verbi perficiendam. Idem etiam statuit B. D. Hunnius in h. l. Cornelius Iansenius Comm in Conc. Ev. p. 844. pro sententiâ hâc adducit Origenem, Hieronymum, Augustinum. Addere quoque potuisset Hilarium in Ps. 134. Interea maximè verisimile videtur, Christum primariò loqui hîc de adventu suo ad extremum iudicium, qui commodissimè cum fulgure conferri potest. Secundariò verò de doctrinae coelestis restauratione, discussis Anti Christianarum abominationum tenebris.)*

## 24:28
v. 28. Wheresoever the body shall be, there will the eagles be gathered together. (The sense is as if incomplete: for it must be repeated from the preceding or understood: so also believers seek only Christ. Especially when he shall have come to judgment, they will be gathered to him alone, nay, they will be caught up to meet him, 1 Thess. 4, 17. Grotius opposes this opinion, 1. because many things intervene before one comes to the description of the judgment. 2. because the venerable body of Christ, after it has been sent into the fullest possession of divine life, cannot be called πτῶμα, and he wonders how it could have entered the minds of the ancients to call it so. But I answer to 1. by denying it, since the context teaches otherwise. See v. 36. 2. by observing that it is one thing for the Body of Christ to be called πτῶμα or a corpse; but another thing for Christ in some third respect to be compared to a corpse. Thus his coming is compared to a thief coming in the night, below v. 43. Hilary thinks that a regard is had as it were to the very place where Christ suffered, because he is also to celebrate the final judgment in the same place, namely in the valley of Jehoshaphat. His words in can. 25. p. 319. are these: He called the saints eagles because of the flight of the spiritual body: whose (the Angels gathering them) assembly he shows will be in the place of the passion. And worthily (the Basil. edit. of the year 1570 has unworthily here erroneously) will he be awaited there at the coming of brightness: where he wrought for us the glory of eternity by the passion of bodily humility of the struggle. But what is to be thought of this opinion has been noted elsewhere) * It is a proverbial expression, taken from Job 39. v. 33. There is a certain kind of eagle, which is called ὑπακτον i.e. sub-eagle or sub-vulture, which is most greedy for prey, and is intensely delighted by corpses, when the remaining kinds of eagles abstain from them. But the properties of the sub-eagle or vulture are 1. the height of their nests. See Aristot. l. 6. Hist. Anim. c. 5. 2. the sharpness of sight, Job 28, 7. 3. the sagacity of smelling. Plin. l. 10. c. 6. 4. greed for prey. Believers like eagles 1. place all their trust in Christ, as the rock of salvation, and store their nests in heaven. 2. direct their internal sharpness of eyes, mind, and all thoughts uniquely to this goal. 3. from the scent or smell of the Gospel and the preceding signs, they presage the return of Christ to judgment. 4. they await the same most greedily. Pliny l. 10. c. 4. Eagles do not establish a certain place where they wish to be gathered, but where the corpse is, there they are gathered. Thus the pious will be gathered to Christ, who was made for our sake a corpse-like worm. A type of this is in the corpse of the lion, from which Samson ate honey etc. Christ calls himself a corpse 1. because he was so despised, that they hid their faces before him. 2. because access to him is open to anyone. Let us be eagles 1. by flying. 2. by looking at the Sun. 3. by cherishing our young. 4. by panting for prey. Thus it will happen to us that we are safe from adversities, just as the eagle is not touched by thunder or lightning. Conf. also Theodor. Orat. 5. de Provid. Hieron. in c. 40. Es. Scultetum in Annot. c. 67. That similitude is otherwise explained in two ways, first, that Christ is designated by the corpse, but the pious by the eagle. Christ compares himself to a corpse 1. by reason of his emptying, 2. in respect of his passion. The pious are compared to eagles 1. on account of the clarity of their sight. 2. on account of their greed for food. 3. on account of their lightness. They fly on high, * (See Phil. 3. 20. Es. 40, last. It can also be added 4. on account of their dignity. The eagle is the king of animals, thus the saints are kings of heaven. Thus Origen and the author of the Oper. Imperf. 5. on account of the newness of life. Conf. Ps. 103, 5. Ambrose in Luke c. 17, last Body (thus he reads here with the Vulgate, although in the Greek text there is not σῶμα, but πτῶμα, is also the Church, in which through the grace of Baptism

we are renewed in spirit, and are restored to rejuvenated ages. 6 on account of longevity. Whence it is easily evident that by eagles in this place are not understood all men, which Beza, Tostatus, Maldonatus, and Barradius maintain after Theophylact: from whom Corn. Iansenius, Franciscus Lucas Brugensis, and indeed the associates of the Jesuits Maldonatus and Barradius themselves, Iacobus Tirinus, Corn. à Lapide, and other Jesuits rightly dissent. Nor does Tirinus inconveniently allege for this matter the passage 1. Thess. 4. 16.) * Secondly: that Christ may be compared to an eagle, and the pious to a corpse. Christ is an eagle, 1. by reason of His Royal nature. 2. by reason of His fatherly care. The pious are compared to a corpse 1. by reason of their spiritual condition outside of Christ. 2. by reason of natural death. * (Compare also concerning this place Isid. Pelus. lib. 1. ep. 282. Furthermore, whether the body of Christ, having died on the cross and resting in the sepulcher, can be called a corpse, there are diverse opinions of authors, concerning which in the Analysis to Act. 2, 27. But it does not follow, Christ can in a certain way be compared with a corpse. Therefore corpse it can be called. See B. D. Gesnerus, disputation for the Book of Concord, ch. 3. §. 42. The Theologians of Marburg in the Fundamental Deduction, p. 165. following. B. Par. Catholic Confession, book 2. special part 1. appendix art 2. p. 514. That indeed it is not at all ineptly that Christ is compared with a corpse, as Weigelius in part 2 of his Postil, p. 358, persuaded himself, and on that account attacks us, B. Par. shows at length in Academic Disputations, part 1. p. 915. Salmeron takes τὸ πτῶμα for the prey of an animal or for the body of a bird, hare, or other animal, since the eagle is so noble that it does not feed on a corpse, unless it has captured and killed it alive itself. Corn. à Lapide nevertheless warns in this place that Aristotle mentions eagles which follow corpses.) *

Latin:

v. 28. Ubi fuerit corpus, illic congregabuntur aquilae. *(Sensus est imperfectus quasi: repetendum enim ex praecedentibus vel subintelligendum: ita & credentes Christum solùm quaerunt. maximè cùm venerit ad iudicium, ad ipsum solum congregabuntur, imò obviam ei rapientur, 1. Thess. 4, 17. Sententiae huic opponit Grotius, 1. quòd multa intercedant, ante quam ad iudicii descriptionem veniatur. 2. quòd venerandum Christi corpus, postquam missum est in plenissimam vitae divinae possessionem, πτῶμα vocari nequeat, seque mirari, quomodo veteribus ut ita vocarent, in mentem venire potuerit. Verùm resp. ad 1. negando, cùm aliud contextus doceat. Vid. v. 36. 2. observando, quòd aliud sit, Corpus Christi vocari πτῶμα seu cadaver; aliud verò, Christum in aliquo tertio conferri cum cadavere. Ita confertur eius adventus cum fure veniente in nocte, infrà v. 43. Hilarius existimat, quasi hoc ipso ad locum, ubi Christus passus est, respectus habeatur, quòd in eodem quoque iudicium extremum sit celebraturus, nempe in valle Iosaphat. Verba eius can. 25. p. 319. haec sunt: Sanctos de volatu spiritualis corporis, aquilas nuncupavit: quorum (congregantibus Angelis) conventum futurum in loco passionis ostendit. Et dignè (Basil. edit. A. 1570. vitiosè hîc habet indignè) illic claritatis advēto expectabitur: ubi nobis gloriam aeternitatis passione corporeae humilitatis militatis operatus est. Sed quid de hâc sententiâ habendum fit, alibi monitum) * Proverbialis locutio est, sumta ex Iob. 39. v. 33. Est genus quoddam aquilarum, quod vocatur ὑπακτον q. d. subaquilam vel subvulturem, quod praedae avidissimum, & cadaveribus impensè delectatur, cùm reliqua aquilarum genera illis abstineant. Sunt verò subaquilae vel vulturis proprietates 1. nidorum celsitudo. Vid. Aristot. l. 6. Hist. Anim. c. 5. 2. acumen visûs, Iobi 28, 7. 3. sagacitas odorandi. Plin. l. 10. c. 6. 4. aviditas praedae. Credentes instar aquilarum 1. fiduciam omnem in Christum, tanquam petram salutis collocant, & suos nidos in coelo reponunt. 2. ad hunc scopum internam oculorum aciem, mentem & cogitationes omnes unicè dirigunt. 3. ex nidore vel o-factu Evangelii signisque antecedentibus reditum Christi ad iudicium praesagiunt. 4. eundem cupidissimè expectant. Plinius l. 10. c. 4. Aquilae certum locum non constituunt, ubi congregari velint, sed ubi cadaver est, ibi congregantur. Sic pii congregabuntur ad Christum, qui factus est propter nos vermis cadaverosus. Typus eius in cadavere leonis, ex quo Simson mel comedit &c. Christus se vocat cadaver 1. quia fuit tàm contemtus, ut faciem absconderent coram ipso. 2. quia cuivis ad ipsum patet aditus. Nos simus aquilae 1 volando. 2. Solem intuendo. 3. pullous sovendo. 4. praedae inhiando. Ita continget nobis, ut simus tuti ab adversis, sicut aquila non tangitur à tonitru vel fulmine. Conf. etiam Theodor. Orat. 5. de Provid. Hieron. in c. 40. Es. Scultetum in Annot. c. 67. Dupliciter aliàs illa similitudo exponitur, primò, ut Christus per cadaver, pii verò per aquilam designentur. Christus comparat se cadaveri 1 ratione exinanitionis, 2. respectu passionis. Pii conferuntur aquilis 1. propter visûs claritatem. 2. propter escae aviditatem. 3. propter levitatem, Volant in sublime, * (Vid. Phil. 3. 20.Es. 40, ult. Potest etiam addi 4. propter dignitatem. Aquila est rex animalium, sic sancti reges coeli. Ita Origenes & autor Oper. Imperf. 5. propter vitae novitatem. Conf. Ps. 103, 5. Ambrosius in Lucae c. 17, ult Corpus (ita legit h. l. cum Vulgato, cùm tamen in Graeco textu non sit σῶμα, sed πτῶμα,est etiam Ecclesia, in quâper Baptismi gratiam

renovamur spiritu, & occiduâ senectutis in redivivas reparantur aetates. 6 propter longaevitatem. Unde facilè patet, quòd per aquilas h. l. non intelligantur omnes homines, quod post Theophylactum volunt Beza, Tostatus, Maldonatus, Barradius: à quibus rectè diffentiunt Corn. Iansenius, Franciscus Lucas Brugensis, quin ipsorum Iesuitarum Maldonati ac Barradii socienni, Iacobus Tirinus, Corn. à Lapide, aliique Iesuitae. Nec incomodè in hanc rem Tirinus allegat locum 1. Thess. 4. 16.) * Secundò: ut Christus aquilae, pii cadaveri comparentur. Christus est aquila, 1. ratione Regiae naturae. 2. ratione paternae curae. Pii cadaveri conferuntur 1 ratione conditionis spiritualis extra Christum. 2. ratione mortis naturalis. * (Conf. etiam de h. l. Isid. Pelus. lib. 1. ep. 282. Coeterùm, an Christi in cruce defuncti, inque sepulcro quiescentis corpus cadaver dici possit, diversae sunt autorum sententiae, de quibus in Anal. ad Act. 2, 27. Non verò sequitur, Christus certô modô conferri potest cum cadavere. E. cadaver dici potest. Vid. B. D. Gesnerus disput. pro Lib. Concord. c. 3. §. 42. Dnn. Theologi Marpp. in Fundam. Deduct. p. 165. seqq. B. Par Confess. Cath. lib. 2. spec. part. 1. append. art 2. p. 514. Qùd verò minimè ineptè Christus cum cadavere comparetur, ceu Weigelius part. 2. Postill. p. 358. sibi persuasit, eoque nomine nos exagitat, prolixè ostendit B. Par. Dispp. Acad. part. 1. p. 915. Salmeron τὸ πτῶμα accipit pro praeda animalis seu pro corpore avis, leporis aut alterius animalis, cùm aquila adeò generosa sit, ut non vescatur cadavere, nisi quod ipsa vivum ceperit & necarit. Monet tamen Corn. à Lapide in h. l. Aristotelem meminisse aquilarum, quae cadavera sectentur.) *

## 24:29
v. 29. εὐθὲως. So that no notable slaughter of the Jews intervenes. * (There is therefore a tribulation, which will precede the final day, closest to the slaughter of the Jews, if not in time, yet in parity and atrocity. Whence also the Prophets, describing the destruction of Babylon, of Tyre, etc., soon pass over to its antitype, for instance the destruction of the world. See Es. 13. 19.Ierem 15, 9.Amos 8, 9.Ioël 2, 10. That indeed in these words and the subsequent ones, just as also in the parallel passages Marc. 13, 24. 25.Luc. 21, 25, 26. the Savior treats of the proper and proximate signs of the final judgment, and those distinct from the common ones which have been recounted thus far, B. P. L. proves at greater length in de Extr. Iud. §. 93. who himself also in the same place §. 94. following, discourses at length concerning these signs, and how variously they are expounded. Corn. à Lapide also accepts those things which now follow concerning the signs of the final judgment, having followed Jerome, Theophylact, and Euthymius, and refutes the Socinian Ludovicus ab Alcasar, who in Comm. ad Apocal. 6, 12. judges that all these things pertain to the Jerusalem destruction. Nor does the particle stand in the way εὐθέως, since one day with God is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day, 2. Petr. 3, 8. 9.1 Ioh. 2, 181. Cor. 10, 11 etc. See B. D. Glassius Gram. Sacr. p. 444. B. D. Calixtus book on the Supreme Judgment p. 4. 5. B. D. Mylius in A. C. part. 1. p. 231. 6. thinks that these signs will either immediately precede the consummation of the age, or rather are to be joined with the same.

The sun shall be darkened etc. The sun and moon will lose their light because of the splendor and glory in which Christ will come to judgment, because a greater light obscures a lesser one. Es. 13, 10c. 24. 23.Ezech. 32, 7. Joel 3. 15. (Beautifully the Author of the Opus Imperfectum hom. 49. on Matthew When the master of the house is dying, his whole house is troubled, the whole family laments, and with their tunics torn, they cover themselves in black garments: so with the human race established near its end, the whole world is saddened, all the ministries of heaven mourn, and having laid aside their brightness, they are clothed in mournful darkness. The same adds that creatures will do this, either grieving on account of the unworthy persecution of the saints, or indignant over the worst works of the impious, or demonstrating the final wrath of GOD in them. Compare B. Par. L. on the Final Judgment §. 96. 98. But some take that darkening of the sun properly, and indeed concerning one or more eclipses that are entirely prodigious and preternatural. But it is asked, how can the darkening of the sun and moon be a sign of the final day, since eclipses are natural. Answer: Just as the rainbow could be ordained by God after the flood to be a sign of divine grace, although it existed even before the flood, so also eclipses, especially if they are accumulated, can be a sign of the final day, although otherwise they are natural. B. D. Hunnius inclines toward this in this place, who nevertheless adds that it is possible that the sun and moon might also be obscured by some supernatural reason, so that they shine with a much weaker light, and from this it is easy to conclude that the end of the world is at the doors. B. D. Quistorpius thinks the same in this place. Some, like Hilary, Jerome, Chrysostom, Theophylact, explain, Mystically and allegorically, concerning the light of doctrine in the Church obscured by corruptions. For since Christ is the Sun of righteousness, of joy, and of life, from whom the Church, which is the Moon, receives all splendor and light: therefore, the light of heavenly Doctrine being obscured by the darkness of human traditions, it is necessary that spiritual darkness should follow in the Church. See B. Par. in the same place.) *

The stars shall fall from heaven. i.e., they shall yield to Christ, and shall be moved from their place. * (according to Chrysostom, homily to the Neophytes, vol. 5. Others, however, such as Jerome and Bede, whom the Scholastics follow, as well as Corn. à Lapide in this place, explain it by being so obscured that they seem to men to have fallen from heaven, since Scripture often speaks of things, not as they are in themselves, but as they appear to men. Those who follow allegories take it with the author of the Imperfect Work metaphorically concerning the apostasy of the great Doctors of the Church. To this point are the sayings Ps. 14. 12.Apoc. 8, 10,12.c. 12, 4.Dan. 8, 10. Augustine, book 20 of the City of God, chapter 24, takes it concerning exhalations ignited in the air, and falling after the conflagration. Others explain it from Joel 3, 15 in this manner: they shall fall not by reason of substance, but of light, because they shall withdraw their light, so that they may seem as if they had fallen from heaven and were no longer in it. Thus the blessed D. Hunnius takes it, namely concerning the inclined power of the stars and their imminent light. Finally, others take this figuratively and comparatively in this sense: There shall be such a shaking of the whole heavenly machine that the stars themselves shall be thought to fall from heaven. B. Par. in his book on the Final Judgment, § 99, reviews these opinions in order and concludes that the event and the day of the Lord will explain those things best of all. The blessed D. Calixtus, in his book on the Supreme Judgment, p. 7, takes all these things at least concerning huge calamities, since for those who are overwhelmed by these, the heaven is said to press down with its own mass, the earth to tremble, light to turn into darkness, and the bright day into black. And that the state of a mind, established in the greatest fear and sorrow, is accustomed to be described in this way. He compares to this matter the passages Amos 8, 9. Ioel. 2, 30.Es. 13, 10.c. 34, 5.Ezech. 32, 7.) *

The powers of the heavens i.e., the firmament of the starry heaven and the Angels themselves shall be moved. Thus Tossanus, or also Army, because δυνὰμεις also signifies army, just as the LXX rendered Lord Sabaoth as κύριος δυνάμεων. See Theodoret in Epit. Divin. Dogm., Drusius, book 10, Observ. ch. 14. Some (such as Augustine, Jerome, Gregory) understand it of the Angels, who are called צבאת השמים by the Hebrews. Some explain this phrase as powers of the heavens, that is, the heavens however robust they may be, by a Hebrew hypallage. The powers of the heavens, that is, the heavens of powers, that is, prevailing in powers or most firm. (Conformable to this opinion is the view of those who accept these things concerning the waning of the heavenly powers. Likewise those who explain it concerning some remarkable change in the ethereal and aerial heaven and its wonderful appearance, so that unusual chasms, comets, whirlwinds, hailstorms, new stars, etc., are denoted, which interpretation B. Pareus prefers to the others in L de Extr. Iudic. §. 100. Cornelius à Lapide in this place thinks that by the powers of the heavens are most plainly meant the poles and hinges, as if to say: All the heavens at the end of the world will be shaken and torn away from their poles and hinges, so that they may seem to fall downward. And he thinks that Christ is alluding to Iob. 26, 11. and Isaiah 34, 4. Hugo Grotius thinks that by the name οὐρανοῦ the Christian Church is indicated, so that in this way a great change of things in the Church is indicated. But there is no need for us to depart from the letter without urgent necessity.)

Latin:

v. 29. εὐθὲως. Ita ut nulla interveniat insignis clades Iudaeorum. * (Est proinde tribulatio, quae diem praecedet extremum, cladi Iudaeorum proxima, si non tempore, tamen paritate & atrocitate. Unde etiam Prophetae, excidiū Babylonis, Tyri &c. describentes, mox transeunt ad eius antitypum puta excidium orbis. Vid. Es. 13. 19.Ierem 15, 9.Amos 8, 9.Ioël 2, 10. Quòd verò in his verbis ac subsequentibus, quemadmodum etiam in locis parallelis Marc. 13, 24. 25.Luc. 21, 25, 26. Salvator agat de propriis ac proximis iudicii extremi signis, iisque à communibus, quae hactenus recensita, distinctis, prolixiùs probat. B. P. L. de Extr. Iud. §. 93. qui ipse etiam l. c. §. 94. seqq. multis de signis istis, & quàm variè exponantur, disserit. De extremi iudicii signis ea, quae iam sequuntur, accipit quoque Corn. à Lapide, Hieronymum, Theophylactum & Euthymium sequutus, refellitq; sociennum Ludovicum ab Alcasar, qui in Comm. ad Apocal. 6, 12. omnia haec ad Hierosolymitanum excidium pertinere censet. Nec obstat particula εὐθέως, cùm unus dies apud Deum sit sicut mille anni, & mille anni sicut unus dies, 2. Petr. 3, 8. 9.1 Ioh. 2, 181. Cor. 10, 11 &c. Vid. B. D. Glassius Gram. Sacr. p. 444. B. D. Calixtus lib. de Supremo Iudic. p. 4. 5. Existimat B. D. Mylius in A. C. part. 1. p. 231. 6. signa haec consummationem seculi vel proximè praecessura esse, vel potiùs cum eâdem coniungenda. *

Sol obscur abitur &c. Sol & Luna amittent lumen suum ob splendorem & gloriam, in quâ Christus ad iudicium veniet, quia maius lumen obscurat minus. Es. 13, 10c. 24. 23.Ezech. 32, 7. Ioelis. 3. 15. * (Pulcrè Autor Operis Imperf. hom. 49. in Matth. Patrefamiliàs moriente tota eius domus turbatur, omnis familia plangit & conscissis tunicis suis, nigris se cooperiunt vestimentis: sic humano genere circa exitum constituto totus constristatur mundus, universa coeli ministeria lugent, & candore deposito luctuosis tenebris vestiuntur. Addit idem, facturas id creaturas, aut propter indignam persecutionem sanctorum dolentes, aut super impiorum pessima opera indignantes, aut novissimam in eis DEI iracundiam demonstrantes. Conf. B. Par. L. de Extr. Iudic. §. 96. 98. Istam verò Solis obscurationem quidam propriè accipiunt, & quidem de eclipsi unâ vel pluribus prorsus prodigiosis & praeternaturalibus. Sed quaeritur, quomodo Solis & Lunae obscuratio possit esse signum extremi diei, cùm eclipses sint naturales. Resp.
