## 24:50
v. 50. διχοτομήσει, he will cut him in two, he will tear him into two parts.

That punishment is still used among the Barbarians. Justin reports that Isaiah was cut asunder by the Jews with a saw. An example of this punishment is proposed 1. Sam. 15, 33. Therefore the most grievous punishment is understood, which awaits such servants. Casaubon in his notes: It moved me at one time, both the passage of Homer, ὀδυω. σ ἵνα λαὶ σε διαμελεισὶ τάμησι, and the authority of Tertullian and others, to think that these things were to be understood concerning the most grievous punishment used by the ancients: now I think it is a pure and unmixed Hebraism, because of those things which follow, to which they are similar Ioh. 13, 8.Apoc. 21, 8. Some therefore translate he will separate, i.e., he will repudiate them from his kingdom and the fellowship of the elect, Deut. 29, 21. which interpretation the following words certainly favor. Piscator embraces the same interpretation: for he explains it in this manner, he will distribute the servants, namely into those whom he will retain with himself and affect with rewards, and those whom he will separate from them and punish: and then he will separate him from the others: it follows: and will assign his portion among the hypocrites. *(The same opinion also pleases Mr. D. Friedlieb. Lud. de Dieu prefers the meaning of cutting asunder, and thinks that it is indicated that such an unfaithful servant will not be a participant in the future victim of Christ, but must be held himself like a piacular victim, namely to be handed over to the hands of the infernal torturer, by whom he is to be treated no differently than victims τῶν δ-χ-τομούντων subjected to knives. Furthermore, although the Syrian and the Arab also favor this opinion, because it is nevertheless unusual in Holy Scripture to compare the punishment of the impious with slaughtered victims, the opinion of those who take it in the meaning of separating, namely from the fellowship of the pious, seems simpler. And the Persian also seems to have looked to this, who says thus: he will separate him from himself. So also Jerome: He will divide, not that he cuts him asunder with a sword, but that he separates him from the fellowship of the Saints. Compare the following chapter 25, v. 33. It also seems to make for this, that just as ὀρσθοτομεῖν notes to treat rightly, κα-οτ-μειν to devise new things. See Füller, book 3, Miscell. Sacr. c. 16, so διχοτομεῖν you may not inconveniently translate to reject. And thus also Mr. D. Danhauverus explains in Idea Bon. Interpret. p. 20. The Ethiopian follows the Arab, except that he prefixes of his own: i.e., and he will judge, or he will condemn him and will allot his portion. For that which is in the Greek διχοτομήσει, he has -m indeed has not only the meaning of cutting asunder, but also of cutting off, separating. Especially Ps. 89, 23. seems to make for this, where the Ethiopian says thus: and I will cut down from his face his enemies. In Hebrew it is: and I will crush. The Arab: I will cut off.) *

* (With hypocrites. Compare Iob. 20, 29.c. 8, 13.6.Es. 33, 14.) *

This Chapter comprises I. the warning against security under the parable both of the ten virgins, v. 1-13, and of the faithful and wicked servant, v. 14-30, a grave admonition of the Savior. II. The description of the final judgment, v. 31 to the end. Indeed, in the delineation of that judgment there is proposed 1. the majesty of Christ the Judge, v. 31. 2. The solemnity of the judgment, v. 32, where it is taught how 1. Christ is about to prepare all things for judgment, v. 32, 33. 2. To promulgate the judicial sentence, v. 34, 35. 3. To execute the passed sentence omnipotently, v. 46.

Latin:

v. 50. διχοτομήσει,secabat medium, in duas partes discindet.

Supplicium illud apud Barbaros etiamnum usitatum. Iustinus refert, Esaiam à Iudaeis serrâ dissectum esse. Supplicii huius exemplum proponitur 1. Sam. 15, 33. Intelligitur ergò gravissimum supplicium, quod tales servos manet. Casaubon. in notis: Movit me aliquando, tum Homerilocus, ὀδυω. σ ἵνα λαὶ σε διαμελεισὶ τάμησι, tum Tertulliani & aliorum autoritas, ut putarem de gravissimo veteribus usitato supplicio haec esse accipienda: nunc puto, purum putum esse Ebraismum, ob ea, quae sequuntur, quibus sunt similia Ioh. 13, 8.Apoc. 21, 8. Nonnulli igitur vertunt separabit i. e. à suo regno & consortio electorum eos repudiabit, Deut. 29, 21. cui interpretationi favent utique sequentia. Piscator eandem interpretationem amplectitur: exponit enim h. m. distribuet servos, in eos scil. quos secum retinebit & praemiis afficiet, & eos, quos ab istos separabit ac puniet: ac deinde illum à coeteris separabit: sequiturn.: & partem ei adsignabit inter hypocritas *(Eadem sententia arridet quoque Dn. D. Friedlieb. Lud. de Dieu dissecandi significationem praefert, existimatque id indicari, quôd talis infidus servus non sit particeps futurus victimae Christi, sed ipsemet instar piacularis victimae habendus sit, tradendus nempe tortoris in fernalis manibus, à quo non aliter tractandus, quàm victimae, τῶν δ-χ-τομούντων cultris subiectae. Coeterùm licet Syrus quoque & Arabs sententiae huic faveant, quia tamen in Sc. S. insolens est, poenam impiorum cum victimis caesis conferre, simplicior videtur illorum sententia, qui in separandi, à consortio nempe piorum, significatione accipiunt. Et respexisse huc quoque Persa videtur, qui ita: eum à se separabit. Sic quoque Hieron. Dividet, non quòd gladio eum dissecet, sed quod à Sanctorum consorsio eum separet. Conf. cap. seq. 25. v. 33. Facere quoque huc videtur, quod sicut ὀρσθοτομεῖν notat rectè tractare,κα-οτ-μεινres novas moliri. Vid. Füller. l. 3. Miscell. Sacr. c. 16. ita διχοτομεῖν non incommo dè vertas re-icere. Atq; ita etiam exponit Dn. D. Danhauverus Ideâ Bon. Interpret. p. 20. Aethiops Arabem sequitur, nisi quôd de suo praemittat: i. e. & iudicabit s. condemnabit eum & tribuet portioaem suam. Pro eò ver. quod in Graeco est διχοτομήσει, habet -m verò non solùm dissecandi, sed etiam abscindendi, separandi significationem habet. Cumprimis huc facere videtur Ps. 89, 23. ubi ita Aethiops: & concidam à facie ipsius inimicos eius. in Ebr. est: & contundam. Arabs: praes indam.) *

* (Cum hypocritis. Conf. Iob. 20, 29.c. 8, 13.6.Es. 33, 14.) *

Complectitur hoc Caput I. de securitate vitandâ sub parabolâ tum decem virginum, v. 1. 13. tum servi fidelis & nequam, v. 74. 30. gravem Salvatoris admonitionem. II. Extremi iudicii descriptionem, v. 31. ad finem. Proponitur vero in iudicii illius delineatione 1. Christi Iudicis maiestas v. 31. 2. Iudicii solennitas v. 32. ubi docetur, quomodo 1. Christus omnia ad iudicium sit praeparaturus, v. 32. 33. 2. sententiam iudiciariam, promulgaturus v. 34. 35. 3. latam sententiam omnipotenter executurus, v. 46.) *

## 25:1
v. 1. The kingdom of heaven is like unto ten virgins. A similar parable exists in David Chytraeus Jos. 65. 13. Rabbi Johanan son of Zakkai says, it is like a king who ordered his servants to be ready, nor did he define for them a certain time. Those among them who were wise adorned themselves and sat at the door of the palace, and said: is anything lacking for the Lord King? The foolish who were among them went away and did their work, and said: is there any supper without labor? Suddenly the King required his servants. They entered adorned, and these were soiled. The king rejoiced having met the wise, and was angry with the foolish. He said to them: those shall sit and eat, but these indeed shall stand and see. Macarius hom. 4 adapts the present parable to the saying of Paul Rom. 8. If any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his. For he interprets the lamp as the heart, and the oil as the Holy Spirit: Hilary gathers from this parable that good works cannot be applied to others. Isidore of Pelusium also treats of the same parable in book I, ep. 286.

(Ten. Ten is the number of a multitude, See Gen. 31, 7. Levit. 26, 26. Numer. 14, 22. therefore this certain number is placed here for an uncertain one.)

(Virgins. Chrysostom, Theophylact, Euthymius, Augustine, and Gregory understand by Virgins only those who are virgins in body. But rightly Cornelius à Lapide, having followed Dionysius the Carthusian, Jansenius, and his associates, Thomas Stapleton in his Antidotes, Salmeron vol. 7, tr. 58, Sebastian Barradius, Emanuel Sa, and others, warns in this place that this is more restricted than the scope Of Christ, who through virgins may understand all the faithful. There are, therefore, those who think that the same virgins are denoted here, of whom Psalm 45:15 and 2 Cor. 11:2 treat.) *

CHAPTER XXV. SUMMARY AND DISPOSITION.

* (And of the bride. The Greek codices do not recognize this word, just as neither do the Greek interpreters Chrysostom, Theophylact, Euthymius, nor indeed the Arab, nor the Ethiopian. Yet not only the Vulgate has it, but also the Persian, and what you might wonder at, the most ancient Syriac interpreter. Origen, Hilary, and Augustine in epistle 120 recognize the same. Therefore, Don Laur. Ramirez, in Pentecont. C. 14. p. 138, and Hugo Grotius in this place defend this reading. But how it does not stand in the way of this reading, that mention was just made of virgins, through whom the faithful are understood; but these do not meet the Church, but Christ, the same Grotius strives to show, who can be consulted.)

* (They went out. See concerning this custom Alexander ab Alexandro, book 2, Genialium dierum, chapter 5, and Tiraquellus upon him.) *

* Five, however, were wise, five foolish. Since exactly as many wise virgins are commemorated here, who entered with the bridegroom to the heavenly nuptials, and thus became partakers of eternal beatitude, as there are foolish ones named, whom we read were excluded from the nuptials: someone might suspect that only as many of those who were actually called by the voice of the Gospel, and once even embraced the means of salvation, will be blessed, as there are of the same who are to be damned. Cardinal Cajetan seems to think so, when on this passage he writes, Of the Christians themselves, who appear good, and have some care for salvation, half are lost. But just as it is manifest that a definite or certain number is placed here for an indefinite one (according to the received mode of speaking in sacred matters, concerning which the blessed D. Glassius treats at length in Rhet. S. p. 450.), so it is hardly the case that it can be clearly proven from this passage that exactly as many of the called, and those who had some care for salvation, or lived under the state of the Gospel, will be damned as will be blessed. Otherwise, if the question is asked absolutely and in general concerning men, whether the number of the damned will be greater than that of the blessed, there will surely hardly be anyone who will not embrace the affirmative opinion, especially if, besides that saying of the Savior, many are called etc., he has pondered with himself that hardly a fourth or fifth part of the globe is inhabited by Christians, which thing Edward Brerewood the Englishman strove to show most recently, with an accurate examination instituted to this end, in Scrut. Relig. p. 58. seqq. But if the question were instituted concerning those, Regarding those to whom the means of salvation are actually present, indeed who have even once been reborn, at least in infancy through that saving sacrament of regeneration, I mean Baptism, I add, who have received the preached word with joy, we see that authors then go into diverse opinions. For the Calvinists, indeed, as those who deny that any are truly reborn except the elect, this question will be idle and superfluous, and they will immediately affirm that all whoever have once been reborn will be saved, and that not one of them will perish, since according to them, the little spark of true faith once conceived can never be extinguished either totally or finally. But since we have been taught otherwise by our Savior, (See Matt. 13, 20. 21.Mark 4, 16.Luke 8. 13.Ch. 11, 24. seqq. John 15, 2. add. 1. Tim. 4, 1.1. Cor. 9, 27.I. Tim. I, 5.19.Heb. 6, 4. 5.Ch. 10, 26. 27.) we think that a question can entirely be instituted concerning the reborn as well. And so it is a manifest calumny of Alfonso Mendoza, prefect of the Scotist Chair in the Academy of Salamanca, when in Controvers. Theolog. q. 1. p. 84. he attributes to us that we maintain that all the faithful are predestined to glory. This, I say, is false. Nor does it follow, as Mendoza indeed concludes, Lutherans say that faith alone suffices for salvation, Therefore according to their opinion all the faithful are saved. For it must be known that we distinguish between true, persevering, and living faith, and between false and hypocritical faith: for there are many who feign faith, and concerning such faithful we by no means assert that they are saved by faith alone. Then it must be noted that although every persevering faith is true faith, yet not every true faith is also persevering, as has been shown elsewhere. See Analect. ad C. 13. Matth. v. 20. it. ad C. 8. Luc. v. 13. so that consequently the alleged question can be ventilated among our own people as well. As far therefore as these and the Papists are concerned, it is to be noted that they maintain the negative opinion regarding the question, whether of those called more are to be damned than saved, Sylvester in Rosâ aurâ tr. 2. super Evangel. Domin. Septuag., Franciscus à Christo in l. 1. sentent. dist. 40. & 41. q. un. concl. 3. Franciscus de Cathagena discurs. de Praedest., Suarez lib. 6. de Praedest. C. 3. n. 6. and hence he calls the above-mentioned opinion of Card. Caietan very rigorous. Indeed, even Damascenus in a certain sermon on the deceased descends into that opinion, that almost all the faithful are saved. Against the affirmative opinion, that is, that of those who live under the state of the Gospel, hear the word, and use the sacraments, more are to be damned, are embraced not only by the Jesuits among the Papists, Carolus Regius in Orat. Christ. lib. 9. c. 15. Ad. Tannerus Theol. Schol. t. 1. Disp. 3. de Provid. & Praed. q. VI. dub. 2. p. 984. (who for this opinion urges the words of the Savior: Enter through the narrow gate etc. it. Many are called, but few are chosen etc. which are understood most of all concerning the faithful, as the gloss and expositors commonly understand them,) but also by the Doctors of the primitive Church. Gregory the Great, homil. 19. super Evang. expressly writes: Many come to faith, but few are led to the heavenly kingdom. To the same is also referred Augustine lib. 3. Contra Cresconium Gram. C. 66. it. p. 48. ad Vincentium. But the words of Chrysostom are especially tremendous, thus addressing the people of Antioch hom. 40. How many, he exclaims, do you think there are in this city of ours who are saved? It is hateful what I am about to say, yet I will say it. There cannot be found among so many thousands a hundred who are saved, and indeed I even doubt about these. From the Lutherans also B. Simon Pauli in Disp. Ev. Sexag. it. B. D. Smuck. in Expl. dicti Matth. 25. 46. §. 123. B. D. Cramerus, B. D. Hunnius and some others, whose opinion B. D. Maior senior also embraced, collect from Matth. 13, 19. seqq., that among the hearers of the sincere and uncorrupted doctrine, only the fourth part of men is saved. This same thing, namely that among the very hearers of the divine word the smallest part is to be introduced to the heavenly nuptials (not indeed from some absolute decree of reprobation, but because of the own fault of men) is also accustomed to be proved from 1. Cor. 9, 24. But although it is perhaps not improbable that the greater part of those who have been actually called to the nuptials and live under the state of the Evangelical law will be excluded from the nuptials of eternal happiness by their own fault, I would by no means wish to approve that harsh opinion of Chrysostom with Tanner, who adds to it: that I wish it could not be truly said of individual Christian cities: nor do I think, while saving the authority of those great men who feel this way, that it can be firmly concluded from the parable of our Savior Matth. 13, 19. seqq., that only the fourth part precisely of men hearing the word of GOD is saved. (since in it [the focus is] not so much on the number, as on the manner

Christ may be seen to have regard, namely, that there are four kinds of men in the Church, to whom the word of GOD is preached. Thus in the parable Matth. 22, 11. One at least is read of among the guests of the wedding feast, destitute of a wedding garment, and yet there is no doubt that very many live in the Church, lacking a wedding garment. I think that that of the same Jesuit Tanner is much less to be tolerated, when, intending to prove the paucity of the elect, he writes that it is evident from the distribution of all men into their classes: and he adds: of which the first and by far the greatest is and always has been that of the Gentiles, who do not worship the true God; the second that of the Mohammedans and Jews; the third that of the heretics; the fourth that of the Christians, of whom the three former are reprobate in their entirety and in their whole kind; the fourth is reprobate for the greater part. These things, I say, cannot be tolerated. For although it may be easily conceded that the classes of the Gentiles, and of the Jews rejecting Christ, and of the Mohammedans, insolently denying the deity of Christ, are reprobate in their whole kind (although concerning infants, even born in the very Gentilism, Turkism, and Judaism, some still doubt, being unwilling to exclude them, having died in infancy, absolutely from the fellowship of salvation, since although they are not regenerated through the ordinary medium, GOD nevertheless, such is His immense mercy, can hear the prayers of the Church, praying in the Litany that GOD may be willing to have mercy on all, namely, those who do not maliciously reject and contemn the means of salvation, which falls only upon adults or those who have the perfect use of reason, and can extraordinarily endow them with faith, and consequently save them. On which opinion the blessed D. Meisner discourses in Sacred Anthropology, Disp. 7, q. 2), nevertheless this must by no means be conceded concerning those whom the Papists ascribe to the number of heretics. Of which kind, according to their opinion, are all who refuse to submit themselves to the tyranny of the Roman Pontiff. We think far more mildly of entire Churches, even if the ecclesiastical ministry be imbued with heretical opinions, as among the Papists and Calvinists, and we are so far from wishing to condemn them that we rather judge that one must accurately distinguish between those seducing, and those seduced. Compare the Preface to the F. C. and the blessed D. Hunnius, Book on the Church, p. 80, following. Therefore, the modesty of Vasquez, a fellow-member of Tanner, pleases us more, who all these things, whether, namely, of those called, living in the external assembly of the Church, the greater part is predestined or elected to eternal life, or indeed reprobate) He judges that it ought to be left to the judgment of God: as also that question, whether the number of predestined men is greater than that of the Angels, or not? or especially for the reason that controversies of this kind do not pertain much to the edification of the faithful. Nor, however, do we oppose this, but we consider it entirely to be in the interest of the hearers that the ministers of the Church, among men who are secure and, alas, too prodigal of their own eternal salvation, should diligently inculcate that the way is narrow which leads to eternal life, and that we ought to work out our salvation with trembling and fear, Phil. 2, 12.

* (Foolish. Because, therefore, the foolish virgins are also called to the heavenly nuptials, it follows that the Church, considered by reason of external calling and conversation, does not consist of the saints alone. Just as this same thing can also be gathered from other similitudes in Holy Scripture, as proposed above in c. 13, 12. 24. & 47. item C. 22. 10. 2. Tim. 2, 20.. This is what is to be noted against the Audaeans, Donatists, and Anabaptists, concerning whom the Blessed Par. treats in his book on the Church §. 49. Nor, however, is it to be conceded that even manifestly wicked men and secretly unfaithful men are members of the Catholic Church, provided they submit themselves to the rule of the Roman Pope, as the Blessed D. Hülsemann rightly noted this error of the Papists, and especially of Bellarmine in book 3 of Eccl. c. 9. & 10., in his Manual of the Augsburg Confession, p. 224. But the Jesuit Erbermannus undoubtedly embraces that very error as well, when in his Expostulation he especially urges and desires that there may be one faith of all (that is, one profession of faith, since secretly unfaithful men are likewise, as was just said, members of the Catholic Church according to the opinion of the Papists) and one Shepherd, (namely, the Roman Pontiff). But one must accurately distinguish between being in the Catholic Church, and being a member, a true and living one, of the Catholic Church. We willingly grant that unfaithful hypocrites are in the Church, but that they belong to the Church itself, as living members of the body of Christ, is denied, even if they should submit themselves to the Roman Pontiff to the greatest degree, or even adore him. But as for these foolish virgins, of whom it is treated here, the Blessed D. Hülsemann rightly warns in the place cited that it is sufficiently clear from the context, see v. 3 & 4, that by them are not understood those sinning stubbornly or manifestly wicked men: But those sinning out of ignorance and infirmity, since they had a zeal for piety, but not according to knowledge. Which Costerus in his Enchirid.

Controv. p. 106. & 172. attempts to prove from this passage, have been shaken in the Analecta to C. 22, 11. item to C. 13, 37. Furthermore, Corn. à Lapide notes in this passage, through Virgins are understood as any believers, by prudent ones those who have faith with works of mercy, charity, etc., but by foolish ones those who have only faith without good works. But if he himself understands by faith a naked and empty profession of faith, or a hypocritical faith, he does not have us as opponents. But if by faith understood he means saving faith or the fiducial apprehension of the merit of Christ, of which we speak when we teach that a man is justified by faith alone, we deny that such faith is given without charity. For although faith alone justifies, it is nevertheless never alone, that is, it is destitute of good works, as was shown elsewhere.) *

Prudent. The discourse is concerning Christian prudence, which is acquired from the constant meditation of the divine word. See Ps. 1, 1. Psal. 111, 10. ) *

Latin:

v. 1. Simile est regnum coelorum decem virginibus. Similis parabola extat in Davide Chamio Ios. 65. 13. Ait R. Iohannan filius Zachaei, simile est regi, qui iussit servos suos esse paratos, nec definivit illis certum tempus. Qui inter eos sapientes erant, adornarunt seipsos & sederūt ad ostium regiae, dixeruntq;: quicquāne Domini Regis deest? Fatui qui inter eos, abierunt, & fecerunt opus, dixeruntque: ullane coena est absque labore? Subito requisivit Rex servos suos. illi ingressi sunt ornati, & hi sordidati. Gavisus est rex obviam factus sapientibus, & succensuit fatuis. Dixit eis: illi sedebunt & comedent, hi verò stabunt & videbunt. Macarius hom. 4. accommodat praesentem parabolam ad dictum Pauli Rom. 8.Si quis Spiritum Christi non habet, non est eius. Interpretatur enim lampadem de corde, & oleum de Sp. Sancto: Hilarius ex hâc parabola colligit, bona opera non posse aliis applicari. De eadem parabola agit quoque Isidorus Pelusiota lib. I. ep. 286.

* (Decem. Denarius est numerus multitudinis, Vid. Gen. 31, 7.Levit. 26, 26.Numer. 14, 22. ponitur igitur hic numerus certus pro incerto.) *

* (Virginibus. Chrysostomus, Theophylactus, Euthymius, Augustinus & Gregorius per Virgines accipiunt solùm illas, quae corpore virgines sunt. Sed rectè Cornelius à Lapide, Dionysium Cathusianum, Iansenium, ac sociennos suos, Thomam Stapletonum in Antidotis, Salmeronem t. 7. tr. 58. Sebast. Barradium, Eman. Sa, aliosque sequutus, in h. l. monet, arctius hoc esse scopo Christi, qui per virgines intelligat omnes fideles. Sunt igitur, qui easdem hîc virgines denotari putant, de quibus Psalm. 45, 15. ac 2. Cor. II, 2. agitur.) *

CAPUT XXV. SUMMA AC DISPOSITIO.

* (Et sponsae. non agnoscunt hanc vocem Codd. Graeci, quemadmodum nec Graeci Interpp. Chrysostomus, Theophylactus, Euthymius, imò nec Arabs, nec Aethiops. Habet tamen illā non Vulgatus modò, sed & Persa, ac quod mireris, antiquissimus Interpres Syrus. Agnoscunt eandem Origenis, Hilarius & Augustinus epist. 120. Defendunt igitur lectionem hanc Don Laur. Ramirez, in Pentecont. C. 14. p. 138. & Hugo Grotius h. l. Quomodo verò non obstet huic lectioni, quòd modò virginum facta mētio fuerit, per quas intelliguntur fideles; hi autē nō Ecclesiae, sed Christo occurrunt, idem Grotius ostendere satagit, qui potest evolvi.)

* (Exierunt. Vid. hâc de consvetudine Alexander ab Alexandro l. 2. Genial. c. 5. & in eum Tiraquellus.) *

* (Quinque autem erant prudentes, quinque fatuae. Cùm tot praecisè hîc cōmemorentur prudentes virgines, quae cum sponso introiverunt ad nuptias coelestes, adeoque aeternae beatitudinis factae compotes, quot fatuae nominantur, quas à nuptiis exclusas legimus: posset aliquis suspicari, quòd tot solùm ex illis, qui actu per vocem Evangelii vocati sunt, ac semel etiam salutis media amplexi fuerunt, beati sint futuri, quot ex iisdem damnandi. Ita sentire videtur Cardinalis Caietanus, quando ad h. l. Ex ipsismet, scribit, Christianis, qui apparent boni, & habent aliquam curam salutis, medietas perditur. Verùm sicuti manifestum est, numerum definitum sive certum poni hîc pro indefinito (iuxta receptum in sacris loquendi modum, quo de prolixè agit B. D. Glassius Rhet. S. p. 450.) ita vix est, ut liquidò probari ex h. l. possit, tot praecisè ex vocatis, quique aliquam salutis curam habuerunt, vel sub statu Evangelii vixerunt, fore damnatos, quot beati futuri. Aliàs si de hominibus absolutè & in genere quaeratur, an maior futurus sit numerus damnatorum, quàm beatorum, vix sanè erit, qui non affirmativam amplexurus sit sententiam, cumprimis si praeter illud Salvatoris, multi vocati &c. secum perpenderit, quòd vix quarta aut quinta pars orbis terrarum à Christianis inhabitetur, id quod novissimè, accurato isthâc fini instituto examine, ostendere sategit Edoardus Brerowodus Anglus in Scrut. Relig. p. 58. seqq. Si verò de illis quaestio fuerit instituta, quibus salutis media actu praesto sunt, imò qui semel quoque fuerunt renati, minimum in infantiâ per salutare illud regenerationis sacramentum, Baptismum dico, addo, qui verbum praedicatum cum gaudio receperunt, tunc in diversas sententias autores ire videmus. Calvinianis quidem, ut qui negant, ullos nisi electos verè regenerari, otiosa & supervacanea erit haec quaestio, statimque affirmabunt, omnes quicunque semel regeniti fuerunt, salvos fore, nec ullum ex iis periturum, quippe cùm iuxta eos, fidei verae igniculus semel conceptus, nunquam vel totaliter vel finaliter extingvi possit. Ast cùm aliter à Salvatore nostro simus edocti, (Vid. Matth. 13, 20. 21.Marc. 4, 16.Luc. 8. 13.C. 11, 24. seqq. Ioh. 15, 2. add. 1. Tim. 4, 1.1. Cor. 9, 27.I. Tim. I, 5.19.Ebr. 6, 4. 5.C. 10, 26. 27.) existimamus, omninò de renatis quoque institui quaestionem posse. Adeoq; manifesta Alphonsi Mendozae, in Acad. Salmantic. Scoti Cathedrae praefecti calumnia est, quādo Controvers. Theolog. q. 1. p. 84. nobis tribuit, quod statuamus, omnes fideles esse ad gloriam praedestinatos. Falsum inquam hoc est. nec sequitur etiam, uti quidem Mendoza colligit, Lutherani solam fidem ad salutem sufficere dicunt, Ergò ex eorum sententia omnes fideles salvantur. Sciendum enim, quòd distinguamus inter fidem veram, perseverantem, ac vivam, & inter fidem falsam ac hypocriticā: multi enim sunt, qui simulant fidē, & de huiusmodi fidelibus minimè adserimus, quòd solùm fide salventur. Deinde notandum, quòd licet omnis perseverans fides, vera fides sit, non tamen omnis vera fides sit etiam perseverans, ceu alibi ostensum. Vid. Analect. ad C. 13. Matth. v. 20. it. ad C. 8. Luc. v. 13. ut proinde inter nostrates quoque allegata quaestio ventilari possit. Quantum igitur ad hos ac Pontificios, notandum est, quòd negativam sententiam circa quaestionem, an ex vocatis plures damnandi, quàm salvandi, tueantur Sylvester in Rosâ aurâ tr. 2. super Evangel. Domin. Septuag., Franciscus à Christo in l. 1. sentent. dist. 40. & 41. q. un. concl. 3. Franciscus de Cathagena discurs. de Praedest., Suarez lib. 6. de Praedest. C. 3. n. 6. atq; hinc supra memoratā Card. Caietani sententiam valdè rigorosam appellat. Imò & Damascenus in serm. quodam de defunctis, in eam descendit opinionem, omnes ferè fideles salvari. Contrà affirmativam sententiam, hoc est, quòd ex iis, qui sub statu Evangelii vivunt, verbum audiunt & sacramentis utuntur, plures damnādi, amplectuntur non solùm ex Pōtisciis Iesuitae Carolus Regius in Orat. Christ. lib. 9. c. 15. Ad. Tannerus Theol. Schol. t. 1. Disp. 3. de Provid. & Praed. q. VI. dub. 2. p. 984. (qui pro hâc sententiâ urget verba Salvatoris: Intrate per angustam portam &c. it. Multi vocati, pauci verò electi &c. quae maximè de fidelibus intelligantur, ut etiam intelligant glossa, & expositores cōmuniter.) verùm etiā primitivae Ecclesiae Doctores. Gregorius M. homil. 19. super Evang. disertè scribit: Ad fidem multi veniunt, sed ad coeleste regnum pauci perducuntur. Eodem refertur quoque Augustinus lib. 3. Contra Cresconium Gram. C. 66. it. p. 48. ad Vincentium. Tremenda verò cumprimis verba Chrysostomi sunt, ita populum Antiochenum alloquentis hom. 40. Quot, exclamat, putatis esse in hàc civitate nostrâ, qui salvi fiant? Infestum est, quod dicturus sum, dicam tamen. Non possunt inveniri in tot millibus centum, qui salventur, quin & de his dubito. Ex Lutheranis etiam B. Simon Pauli in Disp. Ev. Sexag. it. B. D. Smuck. in Expl. dicti Matth. 25. 46. §. 123. B. D. Cramerus, B. D. Hunnius aliique nonnulli, quorū sententiam amplectebatur etiam B. D. Maior senior, ex Matth. 13, 19. seqq. colligunt, quòd inter auditores verbi synceri & incorruptae doctrinae, quarta demum pars hominum salvetur. Idem hoc, quòd nempe inter ipsos quoque verbi divini auditores minima pars ad nuptias coelestes introducenda sit (non quidem ex absoluto quodam reprobationis decreto, sed ob propriam hominū culpam) probari etiā solet ex 1. Cor. 9, 24. Verùm licet fortè non improbabile sit, maiorem partem ex illis, qui actu ad nuptias vocati sunt & sub Evangelicae legis statu vivunt, culpâ suâ nuptiis aeternae felicitatis exclusum iri, hautquaquam tamen approbare duram illam Chrysostomi sententiam cum Tannero velim, subiiciente illi: quod utinam non de singulis Christianorum civitatibus verè dici possit: nec existimo etiam, salvâ magnorum illorum virorum, qui ita sentiunt, autoritate, firmiter ex parabola nostri Salvatoris Matth. 13, 19. seqq. concludi posse, quòd quarta solùm praecisè pars hominum, verbum DEI audientium, salvetur. (cùm in illa non tam ad numerum, quam ad modum

respicere Christus videatur, videl. quòd quatuor hominum genera in Ecclesia sint, quibus verbum DEI praedicatur. Sic in parabola Matth. 22, 11.unus saltem legitur inter hospites convivii nuptialis, veste nuptiali destitutus, & tamen nullum dubium est, quin plurimi in Ecclesia vivant, veste nuptiali carentes.) multò minùs tolerandum puto illud eiusdem Iesuitae Tanneri, quando paucitatem electorum probaturus, patere eam, scribit, ex distributione omniū hominū in suas classes: & addit: quarū prima & longè maxima est & semper fuit gentilium, qui Deum verum non colunt; secunda Mahummetanorum & Iudaeorum; tertia haereticorum; quarta Christianorum, è quibus tres priores universum ac to to genere; quarta maiori ex parte reproba est. Haec, inquam, tolerari non possunt. Licèt enim facilè concedatur, quòd gentilium, it. Iudaeorum Christum reiicientium, ac Mohammedanorum, Christi deitatem protervè negantiū, classes toto genere reprobae sint. (quamvis de infantibus, etiam in ipso gentilismo, Turcismo ac Iudaismo natis nonnulli adhuc ambigant, nolentes eosdem in infantiâ defunctos, absolutè à salutis consortio excludere, cùm licet per ordinarium medium non regenerentur, DEUS tamen, quae immensa eius misericordia est, preces Ecclesiae, in Litania orantis, ut DEUS omnium velit misereri, puta, qui non malitiosè salutis media reiiciunt ac contemnunt, id quod in solos adultos sive qui perfectum rationis usum habent, cadit, possit exaudire atque extraordinariè fide eos donare, & per consequens salvare. quâ de sententia disserit B. D. Meisnerus Anthrop. sacrae Disp. 7. q. 2.) minimè tamen hoc concedi debet de illis, quos Pontificii haereticorum adscribunt numero. cuiusmodi ex illorum opinione sunt omnes, qui Pontificis Romani tyrannidi submittere se recusant. Longè mitiùs de integris Ecclesiis, si vel maximè ministerium Ecclesiasticum haereticis opinionibus imbutum sit, ceu apud Pontificios & Calvinianos, sentimus, tantum que abest, ut eas damnare velimus, ut potiùs accuratè distingvendum censeamus inter seducentes, & seductos. Conf. Praefat. in F. C. it. B. D. Hunnium L. de Eccl. p. 80. seqq. Magis proinde arridet nobis Vasquezii, Tanneri socienni, modestia, qui haec omnia, num videl. è vocatis, in externo Ecclesiae coetu viventibus, maior pars praedestinata sive electa ad vitam aeternam sit, an verò reprobata) DEI iudicio relinquenda censet: sicut & illud, utrum sit maior numerus hominum praedestinatorum, quàm Angelorum, annon? vel eo praesertim, quòd huiusmodi controversiae non multum ad aedificationem fidelium pertineant. Neq; tamen repugnamus, sed omninò è re auditorum esse ducimus, ut ministri Ecclesiae apud homines securos ac salutis suae aeternae nimis, proh dolor! prodigos, diligenter inculcent, quòd arcta via sit, quae ad vitam aeternam ducit, quòdque cum tremore & timore salutem nostram operari debeamus, Phil. 2, 12.) *

* (Fatuae. Quia igitur fatuae quoque virgines ad nuptias coelestes vocantur, sequitur, quòd Ecclesia, ratione externae vocationis & conversationis considerata, non solis constet sanctis. quemadmodum idem hoc ex aliis quoque colligi similitudinibus potest, in Sc. Sacra, uti suprà c. 13, 12. 24. & 47. it. C. 22. 10. 2. Tim. 2, 20. propositis. id quod notandum contra Audaeanos, Donatistas, Anabaptistas. de quibus agit B. Par. L. de Eccl. §. 49. Neque tamen concedendum, quòd etiam manifestè scelerati & occultè infideles sint membra Ecclesiae Catholicae, modò Papae Romani regimini sese subiiciant, ceu hunc Pontificiorum, ac cumprimis Bellarmin. lib. 3. de Eccl. c. 9. & 10. errorem meritò notavit B. D. Hülsem. Man. Aug. Confess. p. 224. Illum ipsum verò errorem haut dubiè amplectitur quoque Iesuita Erbermannus, quando in Expostulatione cumprimis urget atq; optat, ut omnium sit una fides (id est, una fidei professio, quippe cùm occultè infideles itidem, ceu modò dictum, ex Pontificiorum sententia Catholicae Ecclesiae membra sint.) & unus Pastor, (Pontifex sc. Romanus.) Ast accuratè distinguendum inter esse in Ecclessia Catholicâ, & esse membrum, verum & vivū, Ecclesiae Catholicae. Ultrò largimur, infideles hypocritas esse in Ecclesiâ, sed quòd ad ipsam Ecclesiam, tanquam viva corporis Christi membra, pertineant, negatur, ut ut vel maximè Pontifici sese subiiciant Romano, quin eundem quoque adorent. Quod autem fatuas has virgines, de quibus hîc agitur, spectat, benè monet B. D. Hülsemannus l. c. quòd satis è contextu, Vid. v. 3. & 4. pateat, per illas non intelligi praefractè peccantes sive manifestè sceleratos: Sed ex ignorantiâ & infirmitate peccantes, cùm habuerint studium pietatis, sed non secundùm scientiam. Quae Costerus in Enchirid.

Controv. p. 106. & 172. ex h. l. evincere conatur, excussa sunt in Analect. ad C. 22, 11. item ad C. 13, 37. Coeterùm Corn. à Lapide in h. l. notat, per virgines intelligi quoslibet fideles, per prudentes illos, qui habeant fidem cum operibus misericordiae, charitatis &c. per fatuas autem quae solam habeant fidem sine bonis operibus. Quod si ipse per fidem intelligit nudam ac vacuam fidei professionem, sive hypocriticam fidem, nos non habet repugnantes. at si per fidem intellectam vult fidem salvificam sive fiducialem meriti Christi apprehensionem, de qua nos loquimur, quando fide solâ hominem iustificari docemus, negamus quòd talis fides detur sine charitate. licet enim sola fides iustificet, nunquam tamen est sola, hoc est, bonis operibus destituitur, ut alibi ostensum fuit.) *

* (Prudentes. Sermo est de prudentiâ Christiana, quae ex iugi verbi divini meditatione acquiritur. Vid. Ps. 1, 1.Psal. 111, 10.) *

## 25:3
v. 3. By lamps are understood hearts, by oil the gifts of the Holy Spirit, especially faith. * (Conf. Heb. 1, 9.1 John 2, 20.27. According to Blessed Luther in the margin note, lamps without oil are good works without faith, which perish. Which exposition does not oppose Chrysostom, who in homily 78 on Matthew, and likewise in sermon 4 on the Epistle to the Ephesians, understands oil as alms. For this is to be accepted not exclusively, but inclusively, since alms are the fruits of true faith. The opinion of those who understand by lamps the human heart, and by oil Christ with his most holy merit, comes to the same thing, as it is that which flows like most precious balsam from the head of the heavenly Aaron, Psalm 133, 3. Faith attracts this spiritual oil, which can be compared to a wick, see Is. 42, 3. But after faith has attracted that oil, it spreads from itself the rays of good works, Matt. 5, 16.) *

Latin:

v. 3. Per lampades intelliguntur corda, per oleum Spiritûs Sancti dona, cumprimis fides. * (Conf. Ebr. 1, 9.1. Ioh. 2, 20.27. Iuxta B. Lutherum in not. margin. lampades sine oleo sunt bona opera sine fide, quae pereunt. Quae expositio non adversatur Chrysostomo, qui hom. 78. in Matth. item serm. 4. in Epist. ad Ephes. per oleum intelligit Eleemosynas. Etenim non exclusivè, sed inclusivè hoc accipiendum est, cùm eleemosynae sint fructus verae fidei. Eodem recidit sententia eorum, qui per lampades intelligunt cor humanum, per oleum Christum cum sanctissimo eius merito, ut pote quod instar balsami pretiosissimi de capite coelestis Aaronis defluit, Psalm. 133, 3. Hoc spirituale oleum attrahit fides, quae cum ellychnio conferri potest, vid. Es. 42, 3. Postquam autem oleum illud fides attraxit, spargit de se radios bonorum operum, Matth. 5, 16.) *

v. 4. in their vessels. Cf. 2. Cor. 4, 7. ) *

## 25:5
v. 5. ἐνύσταξαν, they were inclined to sleep. νυςάζειν made from the word νευςάζειν to doze, to be inclined to sleep. * (Isidore of Pelusium, book 1, ep. 87. If you desire your praises to be proclaimed as if by the voice of a herald, keep your lamps unextinguished: and do not commit that any sleep of pleasure should weigh you down, which keeps the sluggish and somnolent outside the doors of the bridal chamber. It is evident, therefore, from the present parable Our human infirmity. For even the pious, as long as they dwell in this world, and carry around this flesh, as it were infected with the poison of sins, are subject to various weaknesses. Cf. Rom. 13, 11. 1. Cor. 13, 9. Iac. 3, 2. Faith often wavers, often the pious also begin to be oppressed by the sleep of sins and security, but this must be guarded against, that we do not fall asleep completely in sins, but that we wake up again through true repentance, when GOD causes it to be proclaimed to us through His ministers: awake, you who sleep etc. Eph. 5, 14. GOD must be asked daily that He may rouse us from the sleep of sins, and succor our infirmity. 2. Divine kindness. For although even the wise virgins begin to slumber at times, GOD nevertheless does not wish to extinguish the smoking flax, Es. 42, 3. nor to enter into judgment with us, Psal. 143, 2. provided there is present a pious desire to obey GOD, provided there is a contrite heart, Es. 51, 19. 3. The necessity of spiritual vigilance. For the Lord will come, as a thief in the night 1. Thess. 5, 2. and at an hour which we do not know, Luc. 12, 4. below v. 13.) *

Latin:

v. 5. ἐνύσταξαν, proclives erant ad somnum. νυςάζειν factum ex verbo νευςάζεινdormitare, ad somnum proclivem esse. * (Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 1. ep. 87. Si laudes vestras tanquam praeconis voce praedicari cupitis, inextinctas vestras lampades conservate: neque committite, ut vos ullus voluptatis somnus deprimat, qui socordes atque somnolentas extra thalami fores retinet, Elucet igitur è praesenti parabola l. humana nostra infirmitas. etenim & pii, quantisper in hoc hoc mundo versantur, & carnem hanc, peccatorum veneno quasi infectā circumferunt, variis imbecillitatibus sunt subiecti. Conf. Rom. 13, 11.1. Cor. 13, 9.Iac. 3, 2. Fides saepè vacillat, saepè peccatorū ac securitatis somno pii quoq; premi incipiunt, id verò cavendū, ne planè in peccatis obdormiscamus, sed per veram poenitentiam iterum evigilemus, quando DEUS per ministros suos acclamari nobis curat: evigila qui dormis &c. Eph. 5, 14. rogandus DEUS quotidie est, ut à peccatorum nos somno exci. tet, ac infirmitati nostrae succurrat. 2. Divina benignitas. Licet enim prudentes quoque virgines dormitare aliquando incipiant, DEUS tamen lignum fumigans non vult extingvere, Es. 42, 3. nec intrare nobiscum in iudicium, Psal. 143, 2. modò adsit pium desiderium DEO obediendi, adsit cor contritū, Es. 51, 19. 3. Spiritualis vigilantiae nocessitas. etenim Dominus veniet, sicuti fur in nocte 1. Thess. 5, 2. ac horâ quâ nescimus, Luc. 12, 4. infrà v. 13.) *

## 25:6
v. 6. Μέσηςδὲνυκτὸς. Christ is said to be about to come ἐν μεσονύκτῳ, 1. when he is not expected, When one least expects it. 2. when it will be deep night in the world, that is, when all things will be full of ἀταξίᾶ, errors, calamities. * (Chrysostom, Jerome and Euthymius take it literally or word for word, and from this they gather, that Christ will come to judgment at midnight: but although Jerome adds also, that this is an Apostolic tradition, nevertheless Cornelius à Lapide rightly judges on this passage, that this matter is uncertain, and thus that nothing else is indicated here, than that Christ will come to judgment unexpectedly, when men are not thinking of it. It can also be said, that Christ may have looked to the custom of the ancients, by which the bride was not led home except at night, as some gather from Sextus Pompeius and Valerius Maximus book 1, R. M. C. 5. See the Academic Disputation of Mr. D. Sagittarius on the Rite of Marriage which is inserted in Vol. 1 of the Academic Disputations of Mr. Dilherr p. 802. following, and add Don Laur. Ramirez in Pente. cont. chapter 14.) *

A cry was made. That cry will be the sound of the trumpet, through which the living and the dead will be called to appear before the judgment of Christ, 1. Thess. 4, 16. * (Thus explain from the ancients St. Jerome, likewise Origen, Chrysostom, others. Of the more recent ones, besides the commentators on this passage, also Ioh. de Pineda Comment. on chapter 14 of Job, v. 15. no. 1.) *

* (The Bridegroom comes. Christ is compared with the Bridegroom 1. by reason of betrothal,Hos. 2, 19.Ezech. 16, 8. 2. by reason of love,Eph. 5, 25. 3. by reason of the most precious pledge, which is the Holy Spirit, of the gift,Es. 59, 21.Rom. 14, 17. 1. Ioh. 3, 20. 4. by reason of adornment. He adorns us with His righteousness as with a garment, Esa. 61, 10. 5. by reason of exhilaration. See Esa. 62, 5. 6. by reason of defense. 7. by reason of leading home. here v. 10. & Apoc. 19, 7. It is therefore our duty to love this most beautiful, most noble, most powerful, most faithful Bridegroom in return, to proclaim His immense benefits shown to us, to devote ourselves to holiness, to keep the faith, to await His coming with vigilance, prayers, etc., and thus worthily to prepare ourselves daily to receive this Bridegroom properly.) *

Latin:

v. 6. Μέσηςδὲνυκτὸς. Christus dicitur venturus ἐν μεσονύκτῳ, 1. quando non expectatur, Wenn man sichs am wenigsten wird versehen. 2. quando in mundo erit alta nox, id est, quando omnia erunt plena ἀταξίᾶ, erroribus, calamitatibus. * (Chrysostomus, Hieronymus & Euthymius literaliter sive de verbo ad verbum accipiunt, at que hinc colligunt, Christum mediâ nocte ad iudicium venturum: verùm licet Hieronymus addat etiam, esse hanc traditionem Apostolicam, rectè tamen Cornelius à Lapide super h. l, iudicat, esse rem hanc incertam, adeoque nihil hîc indicari aliud, quàm inexpectatè, hominibus non cogitantibus, Christum ad iudicium venturum. Potest etiam dici, quòd Christus respexerit ad consuetudinem veterum, quâ non nisi noctu domum fuisse sponsam deductam, nonnulli ex Sexto Pompeio & Valerio Maximo l. 1. R. M. C. 5. colligunt. Vide Dn. D. Sagittarii Disput. Acad. de Ritu Nupt. quae inserta Tom. 1. Dispp. Acad. Dn. Dilherri p. 802. seqq. ac adde Don Laur. Ramirez in Pente. cont. cap. 14.) *

Clamor factus est. Clamor ille erit sonus tubae, per quam vivi & mortui vocabuntur ad comparendum coram Christi iudicio, 1. Thess. 4, 16. * (Ita explicant ex veteribus S. Hieronymus, item Origenes, Chrysostomus, alii. ex recentioribus praeter commentatores in h. l. etiam Ioh. de Pineda Comment. in c. 14. Iobi, v. 15. num. 1.) *

* (Sponsus venit. Christus confertur cum Sponso 1. ratione desponsationis,Hos. 2, 19.Ezech. 16, 8. 2. ratione dilectionis,Eph. 5, 25. 3. ratione pretiosissimae arrhae, quae Sp. Sanctus, donationis,Es. 59, 21.Rom. 14, 17. 1. Ioh. 3, 20. 4. ratione exornationis. ornat nos iustitiâ suâ tanquam veste, Esa. 61, 10. 5. ratione exhilarationis. Vid. Esa. 62, 5. 6. ratione defensionis. 7. ratione domiductionis. hîc v. 10. & Apoc. 19, 7. Nostri igitur officii est, Sponsum hunc pulcerrimum, nobilissimum, potentissimum, fidelissimum unicè redamare, ingentia eius nobis exhibita beneficia depraedicare, sanctitati, operam dare, fidem servare, vigilantiâ, precibus &c. adventum eius expectare, sic-ue dignè nos ad Sponsum hunc ritè excipiendum cottidie praeparare.) *

## 25:7
v. 7. They trimmed the lamps, that is, they prepared, they furnished, they poured on oil. * (Compare entirely Isidorus Pelus. lib. 3. p. 408. where among other things he says excellently: You, render the light of knowledge more splendid continually, irrigating it through the probity of life and virtue. And await the Bridegroom, who will indeed enter with those who are virgins in souls (& bodies): but concerning those who have brought insult upon the dignity of virginity and priesthood through their own shameful acts, He will exact punishment.) *

Latin:

v. 7. Ornaverunt lampades, id est, appararunt, instruxerunt, oleum affuderunt. * (Conf. omninò Isidorus Pelus. lib. 3. p. 408. ubi inter alia egregiè: Tu scientiae lumen splendidius subinde redde, per vitae probitatem ac virtutem ipsum irrigans. Atque Sponsum expecta, ingressurum quidem cum iis, qui animis (& corporibus) virgines sunt: de iis autem, qui virginit atis & sacerdotii dignitate per flagitia sua contumeliam intulerunt, supplicium sumturum.) *

## 25:8
* (v. 8. αἱ λαμπάδες ἡμῷν σβέννυνται. Compare Exod. 27. v. 20.1. Thess. 5, 19.) *

Latin:

* (v. 8. αἱ λαμπάδες ἡμῷν σβέννυνται. Confer. Exod. 27. v. 20.1. Thess. 5, 19.) *

## 25:9
v. 9. Lest perhaps it be not enough. etc. Ellipsis of a negative sentence μηδαμῷν, & of a verb βλεπτέον. * (Compare Mr. Glass. Gramm. Sacr. p. 706.) * Everyone shall live by his own faith. Habac. 2. * (But if works of supererogation are given, which the Papists boast of so greatly, the wise virgins must truly have been too unmerciful, because they did not apply them to the others in need, namely by denying oil to them. It is also evident from this, that prayers for the dead are futile, since everyone must live by his own faith, nor can one help another, just as the wise virgins could not help the foolish here. The Jesuit Maldonatus excepts that, at least it is signified here, that on the last day everyone is to be judged from his own works, not from those of another. But just as on the last day, which Cornelius à Lapide rightly warns, so also after the particular judgment of each one, which happens immediately after death, No time for working, nor help or assistance, or the prayer of the saints can benefit anyone. Since, according to St. Augustine, ep. 80, in whatever state his last day finds each man, in that state the last day of the world will overtake him. For such as each one dies on that day , such will he be judged on that day. Since this is so, D. Paludanus, Professor of Louvain, in Vindic. p. 238, makes a different exception, namely that the answer of the virgins pertains properly to this, that it may be understood that the works of others cannot avail anyone, without his own, so that he may be received to the heavenly nuptials. He continues: but to make satisfaction for the penalty of another, who is already in grace, is not the same as giving oil, by which charity is designated; therefore, similar to those prudent virgins was Paul, who nevertheless said that he communicated his sufferings to the Church, Col. 1. I fill up etc. which passage Augustine explains thus in Psal. 61. Christ suffers in his members, that is, in us ourselves, for this common republic, as it were. For each one of us has set forth according to our measure what we owe. From which words, Paludanus adds, it is clear that these sufferings of the members of the Church have the power of satisfying and paying off for the debt of sin for the common utility of Christians. If, therefore, the satisfactions of Christ and the Saints, which were not necessary for them to expiate penalty, remain for the Church as a certain treasure stored up in divine acceptance, it is entirely consistent with Scripture and reason that the power of dispensing that treasure, that is, of accommodating the value of those satisfactions for a just cause to those who are in need, should rest with the prelates of the Church. Gregorius de Valentia also uses the same exception. But it must be noted 1. that Paludanus and his accomplices presuppose that the foolish virgins were not in grace. But this hypothesis is false, for it is explicitly mentioned that the foolish virgins also went to meet the bridegroom at first. Now, indeed, no one can go to meet Christ unless the Father has drawn him. It is certain, therefore, that the foolish virgins were no less in grace at first than the prudent ones, or had the first grace from GOD, and indeed the second as well. This is proven by that fact alone, that they had their lamps lit at first, because they say v. 8, our lamps are going out. Therefore, they were lit at first, and they had oil from the beginning (by which the Jesuits Salmero, Maldonatus, others, Good works they understand.) but not sufficient ones. If, therefore, the works of supererogation of others could be communicated to others, it would certainly have been most equitable that those wise virgins should have helped the others from the abundance of their works, and supplied the lack of oil among the others. Since they did not do this, it follows that satisfactions or Good works cannot be communicated to others. Or it must be said that those wise virgins were too unmerciful. We also showed above in the analects to v. 1, that quite a few Jesuits willingly grant that by these ten virgins are to be understood all the faithful. Now, to be a believer, and yet to lack Divine grace, cannot subsist together. 2. As concerns the passage Coloss. 1, 24., it was treated at length in the Analects to that [passage], where it was shown from the Papists themselves that Papistic satisfactions are ineptly proven from it. 3. The saying of Augustine does not hinder us in the least: for it does not have even a word about satisfactions or sufferings for others, but rather teaches the contrary, writing explicitly that EACH ONE, not one for another, should set forth according to his measure what he owes. And even if Augustine had added in the highest degree that one should set forth for another, yet merit could not immediately be inferred from this. Certainly, it is so far from the case that Augustine in this place asserts the merits of others, that he rather destroys them. For he says that each one should set forth what he owes. If each one sets forth only that which he owes, how can he set it forth for others? Conf. Luke 17. 10. 4. The reason for the satisfaction and merit of Christ is different: for we ourselves know that Christ is the propitiation not only for our sins, but for the sins of the whole world. Shamefully, therefore, the satisfaction and merit of Christ is confused with those fictitious merits of the saints. To these, indeed, as much as the Papists arrogate and attribute, so much do they derogate from and take away from the most sufficient merit and satisfaction of Christ. We could here agitate or at least point out that cloak with which Paludanus tries to cover Papistic frauds, when he says that the Church dispenses the treasury of satisfactions for a just cause. He should have said that this is done when the desire to increase the papal treasury, or rather to enrich nephews and nieces, vexes the Pope. We do not wish to repeat those things by which our people otherwise bravely impugn the Papistic works of supererogation. See B. Par. Confess. Cathol. lib. 2. Spec. part. 3. art. 16. C. 5. p. 73.) *

* (The structure or imposture of that mass sacrifice is also destroyed by the present parable, by which it is feigned that a priest, through his own consumption and sacrifice, can merit the grace of GOD and the remission of sins for others, and those both living and dead. See B. D. Mylius on the Aug. Confess. part. page 89. Certainly the wise virgins here confess that if they wish to bestow of their oil upon the foolish virgins, it will be lacking to both.) *

Buy for yourselves. We ought to buy the grace of GOD and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, but without price, Isaiah 55, 1. Apoc. 3, 18. that is, we ought to apply the greatest diligence, through the mediation of the word, prayer, etc., so that we may obtain them: this, however, must be done in this life. * (It must therefore be known that those words buy etc. are not of those admonishing, as if there were still time for buying, but of those reproaching. For after the door has once been closed, the time for buying will no longer remain. St. Augustine observed this long ago, whence he writes: they are not to be thought to have given counsel, but to have mentioned their crime obliquely.) *

Latin:

v. 9. Ne fortè non sufficiat. &c. Ellipsis sententiae negativae μηδαμῷν, & verbi βλεπτέον. * (Conf. Dn. Glass. Gramm. Sacr. p. 706.) * Quilibet suà fide vivet. Habac. 2. * (Quod si dantur opera supererogationis, quae tantopere Pontificii iactitant, nimis profectò immisericordes oportet virgines prudentes fuisse, quòd non applicarint ea coeteris egentibus, oleum nempe illis denegando. Patet quoq; hinc, quòd frustraneae sint orationes pro defunctis, cùm unusquisque suà fide vivere debeat, nec alter alterum iuvare possit, quemadmodum prudentes virgines fatuis hîc non potuerunt succurrere. Excipit Iesuita Maldonatus, id, saltem hîc significari, quòd in die extremo unusquisque ex propriis operibus, non ex alienis sit iudicandus. Verùm sicuti in extemo die, quod rectè Cornelius monet à Lapide, ita quoque post particulare cuiusque iudicium, quod statim post mortem fit, nullum tempus operandi, nec auxilium aut subventio, vel oratio sanctorum prodesse alicui potest. Cùm, iuxta S. Augustinum ep. 80. in quo quemque invenerit suus novissimus dies, in hoc eum comprehendet mundi novissimus dies. quoniam qualis in die isto quismoritur, talis in illo iudicabitur. Quod cùm ita sit, aliter excipit D. Paludanus, Prof. Lovaniensis in Vindic. p. 238. nimirum responsum virginum eo propriè pertinere, ut intelligatur, non posse alicui valere opera aliena, sine suis propriis, ut recipiatur ad coelestes nuptias. pergit: satisfacere autem pro poena alterius, qui iam est in gratiâ, non est idem, quod daere oleum, per quod charitas designatur; prudentium itaque illarum virginum similis fuit Paulus, qui tamen dixit, suas passiones se Ecclesiae communicare,Col. 1.Adimpleo &c. quem locum sic explicat Augustinus inPsal. 61. Patitur Christus in membris suis, id est, nobis ipsis, ad communem hanc quasi rempublicam. nam quisque pro modulo nostro exposuimus, quod debemus. Ex quibus verbis, subdit Paludanus, clarum est, passiones has membrorum Ecclesiae, habere vim satisfaciendi & exsolvendi pro debito peccati in communem Christianorum utilitatem. Si igitur satisfactiones Christi & SS. quae ipsis ad poenam expiandam necessariae non fuerunt, manent Ecclesiae, tanquam thesaurus quidam repositus in acceptatione divina, Scripturae & rationi omninò consentaneum est, ut penes Ecclesiae praesules sit potestas, illum thesaurum dispensandi, hoc est, accommodandi valorem earum satisfactionum, ex iusta causâ iis, qui indigent. Eâdem exceptione Gregorius quoque utitur de Valentia. Verùm no. tandum 1. quod Paludanus & complices praesupponant, fatuas virgines non fuisse in gratiâ. At hypothesis haec falsa est, disertè enim memoratur, quòd primùm & fatuae virgines occurrerint sponso. iam verò nemo potest ad Christum obviam ire, nisi Pater eum traxerit. certum igitur est, quòd non minùs fatuae, quàm prudentes virgines in gratiâ primùm fuerint, sive primam gratiam à DEO habuerint, imò & secundam. Id quod vel illud solùm probat, quòd habuerint primùm lampades accensas, quia dicunt v. 8. lampades nostrae extingvuntur. E. primùm fuerunt illae accensae, & habuerunt ab initio oleum (per quod Iesuitae Salmero, Maldonatus, alii, bona opera intelligunt.) sed non sufficientia. Si igitur aliena opera supererogationis possent aliis communicari, aequissimum sanè fuisset, ut prudentes illae virgines de abundantiâ suorum operum coeteris succurrissent, ac olei apud coeteras defectū supplevissent. Quod cùm non fecerint, sequitur, quòd satisfactiones sive Bona opera aliis non possint communicari. Aut dicendum, quòd virgines illae prudentes nimis fuerint immisericordes. Ostendimus quoque suprà in analectis ad v. 1., plusculos Iesuitas ultrò largiri, per decem has virgines intelligendos esse omnes fideles. Iam fidelem esse, & tamen gratiâ Divinâ carere, simul subsistere nequeunt. 2. quod concernit locum Coloss. 1, 24. de eo prolixè actum fuit in Anal. ad illum, ubi ex ipsis quoque Pontificiis ostensum, quòd ineptè satisfactiones Papisticae inde probentur. 3. Augustini dictum minimè nobis obest: neque enim vel verbulum habet de satisfactionibus vel passionibus pro aliis, sed contrariū potiùs docet, disertè scribens, quòd QUISQUE, non alius pro alio, pro modulo suo exponat, quod debet. Et si vel maximè addidisset Augustinus, quòd alius pro alio exponat, nō statim tamen hinc inferri meritum posset. Certè tantum abest, ut Augustinus h. l. merita aliena adstruat, ut potiùs destruat. dicit enim quòd quisque exponat, quod debet. Si quisque illud solum exponit, quod debet, quomodo pro aliis exponat? Conf. Luc. 17. 10. 4. Alia ratio satisfactionis ac meriti Christi est: scimus enim & ipsi, quòd Christius sit propitiatio non solùm pro nostris, sed pro totius mundi peccatis. Turpiter igitur Christi satisfactio & meritū confunditur cum fictis illis sactorum meritis. His sanè quantum Papistae arrogant ac tribuunt, tantum sufficientissimo Christi merito & satisfactioni derogant ac adimunt. Possemus hîc exagitare vel saltem indicare palliolum illud, quo fraudes Papisticas tegere Paludanus conatur, quando dicit, quòd Ecclesia iustâ ex causa satisfactionum thesaurum dispenset. Dicere debuisset, quòd hoc fiat, quando Pontificem libido vexat, fiscum augendi papalem, vel potiùs nepotes neptesque ditandi. Nolumus repetere ea, quibus aliàs nostrates supererogationis Papisticae opera fortiter impugnant. Vid. B. Par. Confess. Cathol. lib. 2. Spec. part. 3. art. 16. C. 5. p. 73.) *

* (Destruitur quoque per praesentem parabolam ficti illius missatici sacrificii structura vel impostura, quâ fingitur, sacerdotem per suam sumtionem & sacrificium aliis, iisque tum vivis, tum mortuis, posse DEI gratiam & remissionem peccatorum promereri. Vid. B. D. Mylius in Aug. Confess. part. pag. 89. Certè prudentes virgines hîc fatentur, quòd si de suo oleo largiri fatuis virginibus velint, utrisque defuturum.) *

Emite vobis. Emere debemus DEI gratiam & Sp. Sancti dona, sed sine pretio, Esaiae 55, 1. Apoc. 3, 18. id est, summam adhibere debemus diligentiam, verbi mediatione, oratione &c., ut ea consequamur: id verò in vitâ debet fieri. * (Sciendum igitur, quòd verba illa? emite &c. non sint admonentium, quasi adhuc tempus sit emendi, sed exprobrantium. Postquam enim ianua semel fuerit clausa, non ampliùs emendi tempus supererit. Pridem hoc observavit S. Augustinus, unde: non sunt, scribit, put andae dedisse consilium, sed crimen earum ex obliquo commemorasse.) *

## 25:10
* (v. 10. And the door was shut. Conf. concerning the rite of the ancients, to which respect seems to be had here, Ramirez in Pentecont. p. 141. Furthermore, Cor. à Lapide correctly comments on this place: This is an enthymeme, signifying that in this life there is time for acting well and repenting; but this is closed at death, and will be closed on the day of judgment. If, however, the door for acting well and repenting is closed after death, the door for showing mercy will also be closed, and thus there will be no use for indulgences. They are therefore figments, and nets for collecting money, when the Papists promise relief to souls burning in Purgatory through I know not what indulgences. See B. D. Meisnerus in the second Opusculum, opposed to Papistic Indulgences p. 1072. seqq. B. Parens L. on Death §. 186. the gate will be closed through which the damned might be able to exit; the gate will be closed through which either consolation or even the slightest hope of liberation might be able to enter. Whence it is also manifest that infernal punishments are to last eternally, contrary to what some of the ancients think, and indeed what the Photinians seem to maintain even today. See Dn. D. Calovius, Profligation of Socinianism p. 1120. B. Par. L. on Hell §. 58. seqq. it. Dispp. Acad. p. 1203. We must therefore well and always consider that after death the door of grace, the door of mercy, the door of indulgence etc. will be closed, and hence in time, while our heavenly Bridegroom still knocks at the door of our heart, Apoc. 3, 20. we ought to open it. Suppose through true faith, serious repentance, of good works. tireless zeal and diligence. Lest at some time the gate of heaven be closed to us by the irrevocable sentence of the just judge. See below v. 41. 46.) *

Latin:

* (v. 10. Et clausa est ianua. Conf. de ritu veterum, ad quem respectus hîc haberi videtur, Ramirez in Pentecont. p. 141. Coeterùm rectè ad h. l. Cor. à Lapide commentatur: Enthymema hoc est, significans, in hâc vitâ benè agendi ac poenitendi esse tempus; hoc verò claudi in morte, & clausum fore in die iudicii. Si vero clausa post mortem ianua benè operandi ac poenitendi, clausa quoque erit ianua miserendi, adeoque nullus erit usus indulgentiarum. Figmenta igitur sunt, ac pecuniae colligendae retia quando Pontificii animabus in Purgatorio aestuantibus levamen per nescio quas indulgentias pollicentur. Vid. B. D. Meisnerus in Opusc. secundo, Indulg. Papisticis opposito p. 1072. seqq. B. Parens L. de Morte §. 186. clausula erit porta, per quam damnati possint exire; clausa erit porta, per quam aut consolatio aut minima etiam liberationis spes possit introire. Unde manifestum quoque est, quòd poenae infernales aeternùm sint duraturae. contrà ac quidam veterum existimant, quin adhuc hodie Photiniani statuere videntur. Vid. Dn. D. Calovius Socinismi Profligat. p. 1120. B. Par. L. de Inferno §. 58. seqq. it. Dispp. Acad. p. 1203. Probè igitur semperque considerare debemus, quòd post mortem clausa sit futura ianua gratiae, ianua misericordiae, ianua indulgentiae &c. atque hinc in tempore, dum adhuc coelestis noster Sponsus cordis nostri ianuam pulsat, Apoc. 3, 20. aperire illam debemus. puta per fidem veram, poenitentiam seriam, bonorum operum. indefessum studium ac diligentiam. ne aliquando coeli ianua nobis occludatur per irrevocabilem iusti iudicis sententiam. Vid. infrà v. 41. 46.) *
