## 25:13
v. 13. γρηγορεῖται οὖν. The epiphonema and scope of the parable. One must watch because it is not known at what hour the Bridegroom is to come.

* ( ἐν ᾗ ὁ ὑιὸς ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται. The Vulgate omitted these words, just as they were also missing in three Greek manuscripts which Beza consulted. Whence neither the Arab, nor the Ethiopian, nor the Persian has them, and what you might wonder at, neither the Syrian, the most ancient interpreter of all. They are read, however, in most very ancient Greek codices. The context and the integrity of the sense also seem to require the same, as Mr. D. Calovius rightly judges in Crit. Sacr. p. 496. and p. 576.) *

Latin:

v. 13. γρηγορεῖται οὖν. Epiphonema ac scopus parabolae. Vigilandum quia nescitur, quâ horâ venturus sit Sponsus.

* ( ἐν ᾗ ὁ ὑιὸς ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται. Vulgatus haec verba omisit, quemadmodum etiam in tribus MSS. Codd. Graecis, quos Beza consuluit, fuerunt desiderata. Unde nec Arabs, nec Aethiops, nec Persa habēt, & quod mireris, nec Syrus, antiquissimus omninò interpres. Leguntur tamen in plerisque Codd. Graecis vetussimis. requirere quoque eadem contextus videtur ac sensûs integritas, uti rectè iudicat Dn. D. Calovius Crit. Sacr. p. 496. & p. 576.) *

## 25:14
* (v. 14. A man traveling abroad. Origen once gathered from this that Christ as man is not always present to us: but he changed his opinion again, as the Blessed D. Chemnitius shows in his book on the two natures in Christ. C. 30. p. 192.) *

He delivered to them his goods. By goods are understood the gifts of the Holy Spirit. Ministers of the Church can gain much through their diligence in the works of their vocation. * (Nor does it hinder, however, that here in general are understood 1. gifts of grace, both administering and sanctifying. 2. gifts of nature. 3. gifts of fortune. For GOD distributes all these unequally, so that each may use them for the glory of the divine name and the utility of his neighbor. Compare 1. Cor. 12, 7.Gal. 6, 10.1. Petr. 4, 10.) *

Furthermore, the apodosis of the similitude is missing here: so will the Son of man do.

Latin:

* (v. 14. Homo peregrè proficiscens. Collegit hinc aliquando Origenes, Christum hominem non esse nobis semper praesentem: sed mutavit iterum sententiam, ceu ostendit B. D. Chemnitius lib. de duabus naturis in Christo. C. 30. p. 192.) *

Tradidit illis bona sua. Per bona intelliguntur Spiritus Sancti dona. Ministri Ecclesiae per suam in operibus vocationis diligentiam multum possunt lucrari. * (Neque tamen impedit, quò minùs hîc in genere intelligantur 1. dona gratiae, tum administrantia, tum sanctificantia. 2. dona naturae. 3. dona fortunae. Omnia enim haec DEUS inaequaliter distribuit, ut quisque iis utatur ad divini nominis gloriam & proximi utilitatem. Conf. 1. Cor. 12, 7.Gal. 6, 10.1. Petr. 4, 10.) *

Coeterùm deest hîc apodosis similitudinis: ita aget Filius hominis.

## 25:15
* (v. 15. To each according to his own ability. Some Papists try to prove from this that God in election to glory looked to foreseen merits. But it must be known 1. that according to the Jesuit Maldonatus in this place, these words: to each etc. were not added to signify something in the parable, but to complete the narration from the custom of men, or, as Corn. à Lapide speaks, for the elegance of the parable. 2. if they even signified something in the parable, it is by no means to be inferred from this immediately that GOD looked to that ability as a merit of glory: but rather, as the Jesuit Tirinus rightly warns, it is indicated by the adduced words that God is lacking to no one in necessary things, but gives other subsidies to Kings than to rustics, others to Bishops than to sailors. Therefore, by that ability are denoted not the merits of men, but the gracious gifts of GOD. For that very ability of rightly administering the entrusted talents is equally from GOD as the author of nature, as are the talents themselves. 3. by talents entrusted to the servants are understood either gifts of grace or first grace, just as Cornelius Jansenius, Bishop of Ghent, wishes in his Concordance. It is certain, however, against the Pelagians, that this is not given according to natural powers and merits, indeed that there is no disposition in nature toward grace, as Corn. à Lapide rightly writes; or gifts of glory are understood. Although Thomas teaches in 1. p. q. 62. art. 6. that GOD distributed these according to the gifts of nature, he is nevertheless deserted by Cornelius, who writes expressly, that GOD often does the contrary. And he concludes finally: Therefore from this saying of Christ it does not follow that gifts of GOD are conferred on individuals according to the gift of their own merit, which Calvin falsely attributes to Catholics here: for it is one thing to be by nature capable of the gifts of GOD, another to merit the gift of GOD. Nor should that be omitted, that GOD also gave a talent to the evil servant according to his own ability. Now if eternal life were understood by the talents, it would follow that eternal life also falls to evil or unfaithful servants. It is added that only after the servants rendered an account of the entrusted talents did the reward come to them, namely to those who had administered them legitimately. Now, however, beyond or after eternal life there is no further reward destined for the faithful. How finally Hincmar, Archbishop of Reims, from the fact that GOD committed his business to his servants and to each according to his own ability, rightly gathers that each Bishop administers his own Church from divine ability and power handed down to him by GOD, and that all Bishops are also with the Roman [Bishop] servants of Christ and fellow servants among themselves, and therefore that supreme primacy, which he arrogates to himself, by no means belongs to the Pontifical Kingdom, teaches Marcus Anton. de Dominis, Archbishop of Spalato, L. 4. de Republ. Eccl. p. 663.

Latin:

* (v. 15. Unicuique secundùm propriam virtutem. Conantur hinc Pontificii nonnulli evincere, quòd Deus in electione ad gloriam respexerit merita praevisa. Ast sciendum 1. quòd iuxta Maldonatum Iesuitam in h. l. verba haec: unicuique &c. non addita sint ad aliquid in parabola significandum, sed ad explendam narrationem ex consvetudine hominum, sive, ut loquitur Corn. à Lapide, ad elegantiam parabolae. 2. si vel maximè aliquid in parabola significant, minimè tamen hinc statim inferendum, quòd tanquam meritum gloriae virtutem illam respexerit DEUS: quin potiùs, uti rectè monet Iesuita Tirinus, hoc adductis verbis indicatur, quòd Deus nemini desit in necessariis, sed alia det subsidia Regibus, quàm rusticis, alia Episcopis, quàm nautis. Denotantur igitur per istam virtutem non hominum merita, sed gratiosa DEI dona. etenim ea ipsa virtus rectè administrandi talenta concredita, aeque à DEO autore quippe naturae, ac ipsa talenta. 3. intelliguntur per talenta servis concredita, vel dona gratiae sive gratia prima, quemadmodum Cornelius vult Iansenius Episcopus Gandav. in Concord. Hanc verò certum est contra Pelagianos, non dari secundùm naturales vires & merita, imò nullam esse in natura dispositionem ad gratiam, ut rectè scribit Corn. à Lapide; vel intelliguntur dona gloriae. Licet vero haec iuxta dona naturae DEUM distribuisse Thomas 1. p. q. 62. art. 6. doceat, deseritur tamen à Cornelio, disertè scribente, saepè DEUM facere contrarium. & concludit tandem: Ergò ex hoc Christi dicto non sequitur, singulis conferri DEI dona secundùm meriti sui donum, quod Calvinus Catholicis hîc per calumniam affingit: aliud enim est naturā capacem esse donorum DEI, aliud mereri donum DEI. Nec illud omittendum, quòd etiam ma-o servo dederit DEUS talentum secundùm propriam virtutem. Iam si per talenta intelligeretur vita aeterna, sequeretur, etiam malis servis sive infidelibus obtingere vitam aeternam. Accedit, quòd demum post, quàm de talentis concreditis rationem reddiderunt servi, praemiū illis obtigerit, nempe qui legitimè administraverant. Iam verò ultra sive post vitam aeternam nullū ampliùs destinatū fide libus praemium est. Quomodo denique Hinc marus, Renensis Archi-Episcopus exinde, quòd DEUS commiserit servis suis negotia sua & unicuique secundùm propriam virtutem, optimè colligat, unumquemque Episcopum suam Ecclesiam administrare ex virtute divina & potestate ei à DEO tradita, omnes que Episcopos etiam cum Rom-no esse servos Christi & inter se conservos, adeominimè Pontifici Regno primatus ille supremus, quem sibi arrogat, competat, docet Marcus Anton. de Dominis, Archi-Episcopus Spal. L. 4. de Republ. Eccl. p. 663.

## 25:16
* (v. 16. He has traded. See 1 Cor. 3, 8.1 Cor. 9, 16.1 Cor. 15, 10.2 Cor. 6, 11.2 Tim. 1, 6. This spiritual trading requires, as regards a faithful Doctor of the Church, 1. an accurate reading of Holy Scripture and pious meditation, concerning which scrutiny see John 5, 39. 2. sincere and pure preaching of the divine word, and legitimate administration of the sacraments. For since the ministers of the Church are stewards of GOD, 1 Cor. 4, 1.Tit. 1, 7.1 Pet. 4, 10. and the Word and sacraments are goods of the Church, it is fitting from this that they rightly dispense and distribute these goods. 3. Diligent labor, so that more may continually be brought to Christ and be snatched from the snares of the devil. Rightly also do our people gather from this place that a reborn man ought not to be idle in Christianity, but through new powers gifted by the Holy Spirit to cooperate in his salvation. To stand in the way of the Lord is to go backward.) *

Latin:

* (v. 16. Negotiatus est. Vid. 1. Cor. 3, 8.C. 9, 16.C. 15, 10.2. Cor. 6, 11.2. Tim. 1, 6. Negotiatio haec spiritualis requirit, quantum ad fidelem Ecclesiae Doctorē 1. accuratā Sc. Sacrae lectionem ac piam meditationem, de quo serutinio vid. Ioh. 5, 39. 2. sinceram ac puram verbi divini praedicationem, ac legitimam sacramentorum administrationem. Cùm enim ministri Ecclesiae sint DEI oeconomi, 1. Cor. 4, 1.Tit. 1, 7.1. Petr. 4, 10. Verbum verò & sacramenta sint bona Ecclesiae, inde convenit, ut bona haec rectè dispensent ac distribuant. 3. Sedulam, quò plures subinde Christo adducantur, & è diaboli laqueis eripiantur, allaborationem. Rectè quoque ex h. l. colligunt nostrates, quòd homo renatus non debeat esse in Christianismo otiosus, sed per novas à Sp. Sancto donatus vires salutem cooperari. In viâ Domini stare, est retrocedere.) *

## 25:18
v. 18. He dug in the earth. Compare Eccles. 20:31. The proverb of the Arabs, which is read in Erpenius in the *Arabic Adages* page 20, makes for this: The worst of men is the learned man who does not profit by his learning. For not only he who abuses the gifts granted to him by God—whether of mind or body, whether of nature, grace, or fortune—out of malice, but also he who does not use them out of sloth, buries his talent, and will therefore be gravely punished by GOD at some time.) * * (

Latin:

* (v. 18. Fodit in terram. Conf. Eccles. 20, 31. Huc facit Arabum proverbium, quod apud Erpenium in Adagiis Arabicis pag. 20. legitur: Pessimus hominum est eruditus, qui non prodest eruditione sua. Neque enim is solùm, qui donis tum animi tum corporis; tum naturae, tum gratiae, tum fortunae divinitus sibi concessis ex malitia abutitur, verùm etiam qui ex ignaviâ non utitur, defodit talentum, ac propterea graviter aliquando à DEO punietur.) *

## 25:21
v. 21. Over a few things. See 2 Cor. 4:17. ) * * (

I will set you over many things. Although it is not denied that he who rightly uses the gifts given by God for the honor of GOD and the benefit of his neighbor brings it about that he is set over many things, and thus is rendered more capable of spiritual gifts even in this age, yet the scope of Christ—as the consideration of the preceding and following verses 19, 20, 23 clearly seems to intimate—is that here Christ primarily and especially treats of the retribution to be expected only on the last day. Whence also the degrees of glory in eternal life are rightly proven from this place. Yet it is not to be inferred from this that there is merit in good works. Because the industry of the faithful servant is brought forward here not as merit, but as a testimony of a true and living faith, according to which he is judged. Nor is that placement over many things a debt-owed reward, but a gratuitous remuneration, as is evident from comparing Luke 17:10. 1091

Whence also Bellarmine himself, book 5 of Justification, chapter 19, section. ItemLuke 19. adapts this passage to prove that GOD rewards His good things beyond what is deserved. But if this is so, certainly good works will not be meritorious of eternal life. Especially also against the same Bellarmine, book 5 of Justification, chapter 5, it is to be noted that neither in the Greek text, which alone is authentic in the New Testament, nor in the most ancient Syriac version is the causal particle because read here, just as Franciscus Lucas Brugensis also noted on this passage. Another Franciscus, namely Costerus, indeed objects in Enchiridion of Controversies, p. 284, to Luke 17, 10. that Christ is speaking at least of those works to which man is obligated by the law and commandments of GOD. And he adds: For he who does only these things, and attempts nothing further, there is no reason why he should greatly boast of his excellent duties toward God, etc. It is truly a wonder how it happened that, when Bellarmine and Becanus gathered from everywhere various evasions by which they attempted to ward off this weapon against the merits of good works, they nevertheless did not think of this one. For the glory of this newly invented hiding place ought to have been left to Costerus alone. But it is a vain evasion of the Jesuit. For since the law of GOD is the perfect norm of good works, as has been proven elsewhere, see Analecta above to chapter 15, 9, Col. 2, 20., it is manifest that if a man can boast in any good works, he can do so especially in those to which he is obligated by the law or divine commandments. But by no means in those which GOD turns away from, of which kind is all that worship of GOD which is not commanded by GOD. Next, this also is to be noted, that if a man could boast in any good work, he could do so especially in that which Christ will commemorate in the final judgment. But Christ is read to be about to commemorate only those things which are prescribed in the law and divine commandments, and to which men are bound by the law of GOD. Therefore, if in any, in these a man could boast. Certainly, if there were given certain good works beyond those to which a man is obligated by divine law, in the merit of which a man could rightly boast, without ambiguity Christ would have commemorated them on the final day. But since mention is made only of those to which we are obligated by divine law in the process of the final judgment, described below, as is evident from verses 35 and 36, it is plain that a man can by no means boast in the merits of such works to which he is not obligated by divine law. As to that, however, which the Papists (see Becanus, book 1 of the Manual of Controversies,

chapter 18, question 2, section 9) are accustomed to commonly object, the passage Luke 17, 10. by no means overturns the merits of good works, since when that same servant, who out of humility ought to call himself useless, Luke 17. is here called by Christ a good and faithful, and therefore a useful servant. To this, I say, the answer is easy, if at least it is observed that in this place the servant, who had rightly used the talents entrusted to him, is by no means called good and faithful because he had merited many talents. That is certainly not at all the case: but he is called faithful at least for this reason, because he had declared his faith by fidelity and diligence. And so there is a great difference between a faithful servant, who declares his faith by diligence, and a useful servant, that is, as the Papists understand it, one who can merit eternal life by his own works. Compare Rom. 6, 23. The Jesuit Alphonsus Salmeron goes even further, and maintains that it is hinted here, and tacitly promised, that the Saints will be set in charge by GOD in heaven over certain places, in which they labored in life, so that they may work more good there. e.g., that they may heal diseases, etc. But it must be noted 1. that Corn. à Lapide himself in this place admits that it is a parable, taken from a king who is accustomed to reward his servants, and therefore it is signified by catachresis that the saints, who have strenuously used the grace given to them by God, will be partakers of glory, joy, etc. 2. Christ speaks of rewards, to be conferred only then, when He Himself shall have returned to institute the final judgment. For thus the other Cornelius, namely Jansenius, in his Commentary on the Harmony of the Gospels, ch. 87, p. 640, writes explicitly: The Lord signifies parabolically that those who, having been set over this Christian family with faith, have performed their duty in the best way, will be set by Him, when He returns for judgment, over all good things: which will happen when He makes them partakers of His heavenly goods. 3. Gregory the Great himself, P. R. homily 17 on the Gospel, teaches that this will happen only at the final judgment, whose words Corn. à Lapide cites at length in this place. More on this matter was brought forward above in the Analysis on ch. 24, 47.) *

* (Enter into the joy of the Lord. For an ineffable joy will arise in the hearts of the blessed from the beatific vision of GOD, as is evident from Ps. 16, 11. Psalm. 68, 4. Psalm. 84, 3. Isa. 25, 8. ch. 35, 10. ch. 61, 3. 7. ch. 65, 14. 18. 19. ch. 66, 14. John 61, 22. 2 Cor. 1, 7. 2 Tim. 2, 12. 1 Pet. 1, 8. ch. 4, 13. 1 John 1, 4. Jude v. 24. Apoc. 19, 7. Compare regarding this joy of the blessed several very beautiful sentiments of the Fathers in B. Par. Book on eternal life §. 66.

And this joy will be 1. Eternal both by reason of continuation, for no sadness will interrupt it, and by reason of duration. 2. since. rum. 3. ineffable and highest. Conf. 1. Petr. 1, 4. The blessed will rejoice above themselves in the beatific vision of GOD, within themselves concerning their own glorification, around themselves concerning the association and conversation of the Angels, below themselves concerning the evasion of hell. There are those who think that by the word Χαρᾶς an allusion is made to the upper room or chamber, which the Lord called or designated by this name, or inscribed Χαρὰν, just as Mr. Dilherr makes mention of this opinion in Dispp. Acad. t. 1. p. 710. B. Par. Harm. Evang. p. 864.

Latin:

* (v. 21. Super pauca. Vid. 2. Cor. 4, 17.) *

* (Super multa de constituam. Ut ut non negetur, quòd is, qui donis divinitus ad DEI honorem ac proximi commodum rectè utitur, efficiat, ut super multa constituatur, adeoque donorum spiritualium, etiam in hoc seculo, magis capax reddatur, scopus tamen Christi, quemadmodum & antecedentium ac consequentium v. 19. 20. 23. consideratio clarè innuere videntur, quòd hîc Christus primariò ac potissimùm agat de retributione, in die novissimo demum expectandâ. Unde etiam rectè ex h. l. gradûs gloriae in vitâ aeternâ probantur. Neque tamen hinc inferendum Bonorum operum meritum est. quia fidelis servi industria adducitur hîc non ut meritum, sed ut fidei verae ac vivae testimonium, iuxta quod iudicatur. nec collocatio illa super plura est merces debita, sed remuneratio gratuita, ceu patet ex collat. Luc. 17, 10.

Unde etiam Bell. ipse lib. 5. Iustif. c. 19. §. ItemLuc. 19. locum hunc eò accommodat, ut probet, quòd DEUS bona sua ultra condignum remuneretur. Quod si hoc, certè B. O. non erunt vitae aeternae meritoria. Cumprimis etiam contra eundem Bell. l. 5. de Iustif. C. 5. notandum, quòd nec in textu Graeco, qui solus authenticus in N. T. est, nec in antiquissima versione Syriaca particula causalis quia hîc legatur, prout Franciscus quoque Lucas Brugensis in h. l. annotavit. Excipit quidem alter Franciscus, puta Costerus in Enchir. Controv. p. 284. ad Luc. 17, 10. quòd Christus de his saltem operibus loquatur, ad quae homo lege & mandatis DEI obligetur. & addit: Qui enim haec sola agit, & nihil molitur ampliùs, non est quòd magnopere glorietur de praeclaris suis erga Deum officiis &c. Mirum sanè est, quî factum, quòd cùm Bellarminus ac Becanus undique varia effugia, quibus telum hoc contra B. O. merita praecavere tentarunt, conquisiverint, de hoc tamen non cogitarint. debuit nempe gloria novi huius latibuli inventi soli Costero relinqui. sed vanum effugium Iesuitae est. Etenim cùm lex DEI perfecta bonorum opera norma sit, ceu alibi. vid. Analect. suprà ad c. 15. 9. Col. 2, 20. probatum, manifestum est, quòd si in ullis bonis operibus homo gloriari potest, id in iis cumprimis possit, ad quae in lege sive mandatis divinis obligatur. minimè vero in iis, quae DEUS aversatur, cuiusmodi est omnis ille cultus DEI, qui à DEO non est mandatus. Deinceps & hoc notandum, quòd si homo in ullo bono opere posset gloriari, hoc ipsum in eo cumprimis possit, quod Christus in extremo iudicio commemorabit. At Christus non nisi illa legitur commemoraturus, quae in lege ac mandatis divinis praecepta sunt, & ad quae homines lege DEI alligantur. E. si in ullis, in his homo gloriari posset. Sanè si darentur quaedam bona opera praeter illa, ad quae homo lege divinâ obligatur, in quorum merito homo iure gloriari posset, procul ambiguo Christus in die extremo ea esset commemoratus. cùm verò illorum saltem, ad quae lege divinâ obligamur, in processu iudicii extremi, infrà descripto, fiat mentio, ceu patet ex v. 35. & 36., palam est, quòd minimè homo in talium operum meritis, ad quae lege divina non obligatur, gloriari possit. Ad illud vero, quod Pontificii (vid. Becanus lib. 1. Manualis Controv.

cap. 18. q. 2. §. 9.) communiter excipere solent, locum Luc. 17, 10. minimè Bonorum operum merita evertere, quippe cùm idem ille servus, qui ex humilitate sese inutilem vocare debeat,Luc. 17.hîc â Christo bonus & fidelis, adeoque utilis servus dicatur. ad hoc, inquam, facilis est responsio, si saltem observetur, quòd h. l. servus, qui concreditis talentis rectè usus fuerat, hautquaquam propterea bonus & fidelis dicatur, quòd meritus fuisset plurima talenta. id sanè minimè: sed ideo saltem dicitur fidelis, quia fidem suam declaraverat fidelitate & diligentiâ. adeoque multum interest inter servum fidelem, qui fidem suam diligentiâ declarat, & inter servum utilem, hoc est, uti Pontificii intelligunt, qui propriis suis operibus mereri possit vitam aeternam. conf. Rom. 6, 23. Iesuita Alphonsus Salmeron longiùs adhuc progreditur, statuitque, innui hîc, ac tacitè promitti, quòd Sancti certis locis, quibus in vit â laborarunt, in coelo à DEO praeficiantur, ut ibi plus boni operentur. v. g. ut morbis medeantur &c. Verùm notandum 1. quòd Corn. à Lapide ipse in h. l. fateatur, esse parabolam, sumtam à rege, qui servos suos soleat munerari, adeoque per catachresin significari, sanctos, qui strenuè usi sunt gratiâ à Deo sibi datâ, fore consortes gloriae, gaudii &c. 2. loquitur Christus de praemiis, tum demum conferendis, cùm ipse ad iudicium extremum instituendum redierit. Sic enim alter Cornelius, nempe Iansenius, in Comment. ad Concord. Evang. c. 87. p. 640. disertè scribit: Parabolicè signifieat Dominus, eos qui hâc praefecti familiae Christianae fide, optimâ munus suum obierunt, ab ipso, cùm ad iudicium redierit, praeficiendos omnibus bonis: quod fiet, cùm coelestium suorum bonorum eos participes faciet. 3. Ipse quoque Gregorius Magnus, P. R. homil. 17. in Evang. Dom. demum in extremo iudicio id futurum docet, cuius verba satis prolixa adducit Corn. à Lapide in h. l. Plura in rem hanc allata suprà in Anal. ad c. 24, 47.) *

## 25:23
v. 23. Well done, good and faithful servant. Bernard, sermon 13 on the Song of Songs: You are a truly faithful servant if, concerning the great glory of your Lord, even if it does not originate from you, yet passing through you, it happens that nothing sticks to your hands. (But one asks here, why were he who had doubled five talents by gaining, and he who had doubled two, affected by the same reward? Isidore of Pelusium, book 4, epistle 106, answers that this was done because he made a difference between them not by the sloth of the one and the industry of the other, but by the diverse quantity of the deposit.)

Latin:

v. 23. Euge serve bone & fidelis. Bernhardus serm. 13. in Cantic. Fidelis revera famulus es, si de multâ gloriâ Domini tui, etsi non exeunte ex te, tamen transeunte per te, nihil manibus tuis adhaerere contingat. * (Q. vero hîc, cur qui talenta quinque lucrando duplicarat, & qui duo, eodem fuerint affecti praemio? Respondet Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 4. ep. 106. id propterea factum esse, quia differentiam inter illos fecerit non huius socordia, illius vero industria, sed depositi quantitas diversa.) *

## 25:24
* (v. 24. Reaping where you have not sown. Conf. John 4, 38.) *

Latin:

* (v. 24. Metens, ubi non seminasti. Conf. Iohan. 4, 38.) *

## 25:25
* (v. 25. I have hidden the talent Conf. 1 Cor. 9:16. It is to be observed that the burying of the talent is attributed here to him who had received only one talent, not as if others, who have received more talents from GOD, do not sometimes do the same: but that we may learn and gather from this that if he was so sharply rebuked and so severely punished who did not rightly use the single talent entrusted to him, it is necessary that those who abuse, or do not use in the way that is fitting, the more numerous and greater gifts and goods granted to them by GOD, must expect the most grave punishments of all. Nor yet is it to be immediately inferred from this with the Anabaptists that he who thinks himself instructed to teach the word of GOD, and thus judges that he has received a talent from GOD, ought to arrogate to himself an ecclesiastical office without a prior calling, lest, forsooth, he bury the entrusted talent. Nay, rather, since in the Church all things ought to be done in order and decently, 1 Cor. 14:40, and elsewhere GOD gravely rebukes those who run uncalled, see Jer. 23:21 ch. 27:14, add John 10:8 Rom. 10:15, therefore he who feels himself instructed with sufficient gifts for teaching should pray to GOD, who thrusts out laborers into His vineyard, that He may deign to send him through an ordinary calling. Indeed, it is neither indecorous nor inconvenient that such a one should offer his service to the Church for an ecclesiastical function, and thus await an honest calling. For this is to be guarded against most greatly, that one should not intrude himself by evil arts, nor, being legitimately called, withdraw himself from labors without sufficient causes. See B. Par. L. on the Ministry of the Church § 116. Some observe from this place that the Lord entrusted talents only to those who were called, so that they might trade with them.) *

Latin:

* (v. 25. Abscondi talentum Conf. 1. Cor. 9, 16. Observandum, defossionem talenti tribui hîc illi, qui unum tantùm talentum acceperat, non ideo, quasi non & alii, qui plura à Deo acceperunt talenta, idem quandoque faciant: sed ut inde discamus, ac colligamus, quòd si is tam acriter fuit reprehensus ac tam graviter punitus, qui unico saltem talento sibi concredito non rectè usus fuit, gravissimas omninò poenas expectare necessum habeant, qui pluribus & maioribus à DEO ipsis concessis donis ac bonis abutuntur, vel non eo, ceu decet modo utuntur. Neque tamen statim hinc inferendum cum Anabaptistis est, quòd ille, qui do-ad docendum verbum DEI se instructū putat, adeoque talentum à DEO se accepisse censet, absq; praeviâ vocatione munus sibi arrogare Ecclesiasticum debeat, ne videl. concreditū talentum defodiat. Imò potiùs cùm in Ecclesiâ omnia fieri ordine debeant & decenter, 1. Cor. 14, 40. alibique DEUS graviter reprehendat, qui non-vocati currunt, vid. Ier. 23, 21.c. 27, 14. add. Ioh. 10. v. 8.Rom. 10, 15. proinde qui donis ad docendum sufficientibus instructum se sentit, oret DEUM, qui operarios extrudit in vineam suam, ut per vocationem ordinariam ipsum mittere dignetur. quin nec indecorum vel inconveniens est, ut talis operam suam Ecclesiae ad Ecclesiasticam functionem offerat, atque sic honestam vocationem expectat. id enim cavendum maximopere est, ne malis quis se artibus intrudat, nec legitimè vocatus laboribus absque sufficientibus causis sese subtrahat. Vid. B. Par. L. de Min. Eccl. §. 116. Observant ex h. l. nonnulli, quòd Dominus non nisi vocatis talenta, ut iis negotientur, commiserit.) *

## 25:26
* (v. 26. You knew that I reap &c. The Lord speaks κατ᾽ ἔνδοξον or from the hypothesis of the servant, which although it may be false, nevertheless from it it is rightly concluded against the wicked servant, that he ought to have lent out the talent entrusted to him.) *

Latin:

* (v. 26. Sciebas, quòd meto &c. Loquitur Dominus κατ᾽ ἔνδοξον sive ex hypothesi servi, quae licet falsa sit, tamen ex eâ rectè contra servum nequam concluditur, quòd debuerit elocare talentum concreditum.) *

## 25:27
v. 27. You ought to have committed the money to the bankers. Salvianus quite aptly explains such bankers as these as referring to beggars. His statement will be adduced below at v. 40.) * * (

With interest. Petrus de Well, in his treatise on usury, chapter 4, strives to prove from this that usury is lawful. But if he himself understands compensatory interest, we easily admit it, since the principle of equity, under which a creditor demands a moderate gain from the principal entrusted to a debtor—from which the debtor perceives a great profit—is founded in the common reason of commutative justice. See B. D. Hüsem. Brev. Extens. p. 168. But if that same person, or others perhaps, attempts to cloak by this means immoderate or biting usury, as they call it, which is also prohibited by Imperial laws, they by no means deserve our approval. Nor does the present passage favor them even in the slightest. For the Savior speaks of gain in spiritual matters, which He commends and proposes for us to imitate. See Prov. 19, 17. and add B. P. L. de Magistr. Polit. §. 248.) * * (

* For to everyone who has, it will be given. that is, he who rightly uses the gifts divinely entrusted. Conf. 1. Cor. 15. v. 10. Theologians gather from this, that to that Minister of the Church, who rightly uses the gifts divinely entrusted, a more sublime task can be committed, and that he ought not to reject it, but can with a safe conscience accept it when offered. see B. D. Waltherus Miscell. Theol. p. 10. seqq. and Conf. entirely B. D. König Cas. Catechet. p. 718. seqq. But lest anyone should think as if by this present pronouncement of the Savior: To him who has, it shall be given, let the Oracle Num. 11, 25. be set against it, as it is read in the Vulgate version: The Lord spoke to him (Moses) taking from the spirit that was in Moses, and giving to the seventy men. Therefore it is to be noted that in the original text of the said passage there is the word אצל, which properly signifies to reserve, and it is indicated by that word that GOD wished to lift up Moses, who was complaining about the burdens of the administration, by making him certain that although He had instructed Moses with very many gifts of the Holy Spirit, namely of prophesying and of happily ruling the Jewish people, He nevertheless reserved many things for Himself, with which He also wishes to adorn others, and thus those LXX men, who might relieve him in that most difficult function.) *

* (But he who does not have, etc. that is, he who conducts himself as if he had received nothing from GOD, who neglects the opportunity of progressing in the knowledge of GOD. Thus indeed GOD is accustomed to punish the contempt of His gifts, namely by taking away what was entrusted. See the note to Luke 8, 18. Acts 13, 46. and compare B. Pareus, Book on Election and Reprobation, §. 139. also Academic Homilies, part 1, p. 501.) *

Latin:

* (v. 27. Oportuit te committere pecuniam numulariis. Salvianus huiusmodi numularios haut inconcinnè de mendicis exponit. dictum eius adducetur infrà ad v. 40.) *

* (Cum usurâ. Petrus de Well tr. de usuris cap. 4. probare hinc satagit, usuras esse licitas. Quod si ipse usuras compensatorias intelligit, facilè admittimus, cùm ratio aequitatis, sub quâ creditor de sorte debitori concreditâ, unde debitor magnum sentit lucrum, locrum postulat moderatum, in ratione communi iustitiae commutativae fundetur. Vid. B. D. Hüsem. Brev. Extens. p. 168. Si vero vel idem ille, vel alii fortè, immoderatas sive mordentes, ceu loquuntur, usuras, quae & legibus Imperatoriis prohibitae sunt, palliare hinc conatur, minimè calculum nostrum merentur. Nec locus etiam praesens vel tantillum eis favet. loquitur enim Salvator de lucro in rebus spiritualibus, quod cōmendat, nobisque imitandum proponit. Vid. Prov. 19, 17. ac add. B. P. L. de Magistr. Polit. §. 248.) *

* (Omni enim habenti dabitur. hoc est, qui donis divinitus concreditus rectè utitur. Conf. 1. Cor. 15. v. 10. Colligunt hinc Theologi, quòd illi Ecclesiae Ministro, qui donis divinitus concreditis rectè utitur, sublimior committi sparta possit, quòdq; respuere eam non debeat, sed salvâ conscientiâ acceptare oblatam possit. vid. B. D. Waltherus Miscell. Theol. p. 10. seqq. ac Conf. omninò B. D. König Cas. Catechet. p. 718. seqq. Ne vero quis existimet quasi praesenti Salvatoris pronunciato: habenti dabitur, adversetur Oraculum Numer. 11, 25. uti in Vulg. vers. legitur: Locutus est (Dominus) ad eum (Mosen) auferens de spiritu, qui erat in Mose, & dans septuaginta viris. proinde notandum, quod d. l. in textu originali sit verbum אצל, quod propriè reservare significat, indicaturq; illo, quòd DEUS Mosen conquerentem de administrationis molestiis erigere voluerit, certum eum reddendo, quòd licet plurimis Sp. Sancti donis, vaticinandi nempe ac populum Iudaicum feliciter regendi, Mosen instruxisset, nihilo tamen minùs multa sibi reservarit, quibus & alios, adeoque & LXX. illos viros, exornare velit, qui ipsum in functione illâ difficillimâ sublevent.) *

* (Qui verò non habet &c. hoc est, qui ita se gerit, ac si nihil à DEO accepisset, qui negligit occasionem proficiōdi in agnitione DEI. Ita verò DEUS donorum suorum contemtum punire solet, tollendo nempe concredita. Vid. not. ad Luc. 8, 18.Act. 13, 46. ac Conf. B. Par. L. de Elect. & Reprob. §. 139. item Homil. Acad. part. 1. p. 501.) *

## 25:30
v. 30. Unprofitable servant, etc. Augustine in Psalm 38. The servant is punished not as a destroyer for wasting, but as a sluggard for not dispensing. What ought they to expect, who have consumed with luxury, if they are condemned who have saved with sloth? Chrysost. λόγῳς περὶ ἱερως. It did not profit that slothful servant that he did not diminish the talent, but this destroyed him, that he did not return it increased by some addition. * (Ambrose gravely: Let the goats placed on the left terrify you, not because they stole, but because they did not feed. In this judgment not only positive acts will be argued, but also negative ones. Compare Annotations to Matt. 3, 10. To this also pertain the sayings below, verse 42. Luke 12, 47. c. 13, v. 7. John 15, 2. James 4, 17. 1 John 3, 17.) *

* (Into outer darkness. This is a description of the punishment of the damned. See above c. 8, 12. c. 22, 13. Jude v. 13. But what is denoted by this darkness, B. Pareus explains more lengthily in his Commentary on the Later Epistles of Peter, p. 313 and p. 296. Compare also the notes to the passages of Matthew just alleged. Moreover, beside the point, the Jesuit Gaspar Sanctius, Commentary on the Acts of the Apostles, c. 12, p. 243, doubts whether the exposition of his Socinian John Maldonatus, by which he maintains that outer darkness is called the place outside the nuptial delights, or banquets, because they were held at night with many lamps, and those who were thrust out from the banquets spent the night outside the house, and in darkness; since therefore in Holy Scripture the kingdom of heaven is proposed everywhere under the likeness of a banquet, he further thinks that, because of the said custom, those who are thrust out from the kingdom of heaven are said to be cast into outer darkness, has a place here or can square with outer darkness. But that, writes Sanctius, is said to have been done at night, nor is the name of a banquet heard. But there was not sufficient cause why Gaspar Sanctius should here desert the master of the house: for although mention of a banquet was not made then, when the Lord distributed the talents, nor was there need for it to be made then, since the distribution of talents happens in this, not in the other life: it suffices, however, that there is no obscure mention of a banquet when, about to reward the faithfulness of the diligent servant, He said to that servant: enter into the joy of the Lord. where by the word joy it is not absurdly maintained that respect is had entirely to that banquet most full of spiritual joy, from that therefore, since that wicked and unfaithful servant was exterminated, with respect had entirely to that banquet, and thus to that custom of the ancients, he can be said to have been sent into outer darkness. It indeed seems to stand in the way of this opinion that concerning that darkness, into which that wicked servant is here said to be cast, it is commemorated that in it there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, which is the customary description of infernal punishments, (by which very thing also some Interpreters are moved, denying that in the former words respect is had to a banquet, but that by the word joy the blessedness of eternal life is absolutely described?) but if for that reason it must be denied that in the phrase into outer darkness in this passage respect is had to the ancient custom, it follows that neither in the other passage, namely Matthew chapter 8, verse 12, is respect had to it. But concerning the passage just cited, Matt. 8, 12. Sanctius concedes that that exposition is not inept for it. Either therefore it must be said that the mentioned exposition does not fit that passage either, since it is likewise asserted there that in that darkness there is weeping and gnashing of teeth; or it must be conceded that it also fits the present passage. Although therefore we easily grant that weeping and gnashing of teeth is a description of infernal punishments, and thus also the joy of the Lord is of the blessedness of eternal life

describe blessedness: we think, however, that it is not ineptly said that nevertheless by that expression, by which the faithful servant is commanded to enter into the joy of the Lord; but the unfaithful and negligent one is said to be cast out into the outer darkness, where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, regard is had to that custom of the ancients feasting. We add, however, that just as any King, if he had prepared a sumptuous banquet for his courtiers, and they indeed not only despised this, but furthermore blasphemed and persecuted the King besides, certainly he would not only remove them from the table, and cast them out of the dining room, but also, having thrown them into a prison not ordinary, but most squalid, deep, and dark, for the joy prepared and the gladness offered, he would consign them to perpetual sorrow and horror, i.e., to weeping and gnashing of teeth, (as the Blessed D. Chemnitius grants this to us from his own Harm. Evang. chap. 50, p. 535), the same thing can be said of the heavenly King. Namely, that he not only casts the contemners of offered grace and the squanderers of entrusted goods out of the heavenly dining room, but also consigns them to the prison of eternal damnation, so that in this way regard is had at the same time to the removal from the table and the rejection into prison by that mode of speaking.) *

Weeping. is so called on account of the fire, which is not extinguished, but the gnashing of teeth on account of the worm, which does not die. Clearly, weeping arises from pain, the gnashing of teeth from fury. For the immensity of the torments will extort the weeping, and the very vehemence of the withering envy and the obstinate malignity will extort the gnashing of teeth.

Latin:

v. 30. Inutilem servum &c. Augustinus in Psalm. 38. Punitur servus non eversor ad perdendum, sed piger ad erogandum. Quid expectare debent, qui cum luxuriâ consumserunt, si damnantur, qui cum pigritiâ servarunt? Chrysost. λόγῳς περὶ ἱερως. Non profuit servo illi ignavo, quòd non imminuit talentum, sed hoc eum perdidit, quòd non reddidit accessione aliquâ auctum. * (Ambrosius graviter: Terreant te haedi ad sinistram constituti, non quia rapuerunt, sed quia non paverunt. Arguentur in iudicio hoc non actus solùm positivi, sed & negativi. Conf. Annot. ad Matth. 3, 10. Huc faciunt quoque dicta, infrà vers. 42. Luc. 12, 47.c. 13. v. 7.Ioh. 15, 2.Iacob. 4, 17.1. Ioh. 3, 17.) *

* (In tenebras exteriores. Est haec descriptio poenae damnatorum. Vid. suprâ c. 8, 12. c. 22, 13. Iudae v. 13. Quid verò per has tenebras denotetur, prolixiùs exponit B. Parens Comm. in Post. Epist. Petri p. 313. ac p. 296. Conf. etiam notata ad loca Matthaei modò allegata. Coeterùm praeter rem Iesuita Gaspar Sanctius Comment. in Act. Apost. c. 12. p. 243. dubitat, num socinni sui Iohannis Maldonati expositio, quâ statuit, tenebras exteriores vocari locum extra nuptiales delicias, aut convivia, quia noctu cum multis lucernis peragebantur, qui extrudebantur è conviviis, pernoctabant foris extra domum, & in tenebris; cùm igitur in Sc. S. passim regnum coelorum sub similitudine convivii proponatur, porrò existimat, quòd ob dictam consuetudinem, qui é regno coelorum extruduntur, in tenebras exteriores eiici dicantur, locum hîc habeat vel quadrare possit in tenebras exteriores. Sed ea, scribit Sanctius, nenoctu facta esse dicuntur, neque convivii nomen auditū est. Verùm non satis causae fuit, cur virum domûs hîc desereret Gasparus Sanctius: etenim licet tum non facta fuerit convivii mentio, cùm Dominus talenta distribuit, neque etiam ut fieret tum, opus erat, quippe cùm talentorum distributio fiat in hoc, non in altero seculo: sufficit tamen, quòd haut obscura convivii mentio fiat, quando fidelitatem servi diligentis remuneraturus, dixit ad servum illum: intra in gaudium Domini. ubi voce gaudii ad convivium illud spiritualis gaudii plenissimum, omninò respectum haberi haut absurdè statuitur, ex eo igitur cùm servus ille nequam & infidelis fuerit exterminatus, omninò respectu ad convivium illud, adeoque ad consvetudinem illam veterum habito, in tenebras exteriores missus dici ille potest. Videtur quidem sententiae huic obstare, quòd de tenebris illis, in quas nequam servus ille eiectus hîc dicitur, commemoratur, quòd in illis sit fletus & stridor dentium. quae usitata poenarū infernalium descriptio est, (quo ipso etiam Interpretes nonnulli moti, negant, prioribus verbis ad conviviū respectū haberi, sed absolutè voce gaudii aeternae vitae beatitudinem describi?) verùm si propterea negandū, quòd phrasi in tenebras exteriores h. l. respectus habeatur ad veterem consvetudinem, sequitur quòd nec in altero loco, Matthaei puta Octavo versu 12. ad illam respectus habeatur. At de laudato modò loco, Matth. 8, 12. Sanctius concedit, quòd expositio ista ad illum non sit inepta. Aut igitur dicendum erit, quòd nec illi loco memorata expositio conveniat, quippe cùm itidem ibi adseratur, quòd in tenebris istis sit ploratus ac stridor dentium; aut concedendum, quòd etiam praesenti loco conveniat. Licet igitur facilè largiamur, quòd ploratus ac stridor dentium sit descriptio poenarum infernalium, adeoque & gaudium Domini aeternae vitae

beatitudinem describat: existimamus tamen, non ineptè dici, quòd nihilominus loquutione illa, qua servus fidelis intrare in gaudium Domini iubetur; infidelis verò & negligens in tenebras exteriores, ubi fletus & stridor dentium, extrudi dicitur, respectus habeatur ad morem illum convivantium veterum. addimus tamen, quòd sicuti Rex aliquis, si aulicis suis instruxisset sumtuosum convivium, ipsi verò hoc non tantùm contemnerent, sed insuper Regem praeterea blasphemarent & persequerentur, certè non tantùm removeret illos à mensa, & foras extra coenaculum eiiceret, sed & proiectos in carcerem non vulgarem, sed maximè squalidum, profundum & tenebrosum pro instructo gaudio & oblatâ laetitiâ, perpetuo maerori & horrori h. e. fletui & stridori dentium eos manciparet, (ut de suo hoc nobis largiatur B. D. Chemnitius Harm. Evang. cap. 50. p. 535.) idem hoc de coelesti Regi dici queat. quòd nempe gratiàe oblatae contemtores ac bonorum concreditorum dilapidatores non solùm extra coeleste coenaculum reiiciat, verùm etiam carceri aeternae damnationis mancipet, ut ita simul ad remotionem â mensâ ac reiectionem in carcerem isto loquendi modo respectus habeatur.) *

Fletus. dicitur ita ob ignem, qui non extingvitur, stridor verò dentium ob vermem, qui non moritur. Planè fletus ex dolore, stridor dentium ex furore. Fletum nempe tormentorum immanitas, stridorem dentium vehementia ipsa tabescentis invidiae & obstinata malignitas extorquebit.

## 25:31
v. 31. Son of man. Augustine, sermon 64 on the words of the Lord Col. 245. The Son of man will be the judge here; he will judge here in that form which was judged; he will sit as judge who stood under the judge; he will condemn the true guilty ones who was condemned as a false guilty one. * (Conf. the same, book 1 on the Trinity, ch. 13 & 16; also in John, tr. 21, 22; on the City of God, book 20, ch. 30; vol. 2, ep. 85 & 112; vol. 9, tr. on John 76.; on the Creed to the Catechumens, book 2, ch. 8; book 3, ch. 7. Cyril, book 2 on John, ch. 140. and 144. The sayings John 5, 22. 27. Acts 10, 42. ch. 17, 31. Rom. 14, 9. also contribute to this. Maximus of Turin, homily on the Exposition of the Creed: It is necessary that he who created should examine the race of men, and he who redeemed should judge; and it is just that the almighty Lord should discern his mortals, whom he formed by the power of divinity and saved by the piety of the Father, by the examination of a judge. Conf. more in the Annotations on John 5, 27. In his first advent he comes in with humility,Phil. 2. he will come here in majesty; there about to suffer, here about to judge. But the things said in the present place Matth. 16, 27.Marc. 8, 38. where he says that he will come in the glory of the Father, do not stand in the way. For this glory belongs to Christ as true GOD, or according to the divine nature, because he is of the same essence in number with GOD the Father, essentially; as the Son of man or according to the human nature personally, or through and because of the personal union. And thus he rightly calls that glory his own. Whence also the true Deity of Christ is firmly proved from this against the Photinians.) *

* (In his glory. Conf. Psalm. 97, 35.Malach. 4, 1. above chapter 19, 28. c. 24, 30. & the things noted there. Since this glory belongs to Christ also as man, namely personally, and he himself as man is also about to administer the final judgment, because he is expressly called here as Judge the Son of man, conf. Ioh. 5, 27.Act. 17, 31. it is manifest that the truly divine glory and majesty has been truly communicated to the human nature of Christ. Against the Calvinists. See more things making for this in B. D. Menzerus against Steinius p. 110. B. D. Lobechius in A. p. 446. B. Par. Dispp. C. Elencht. on the Sunday Gospels p. 1344.) *

* (And all the holy Angels with him. Conf. Dan. 7, 9.Zach. 14, 5. above c. 24, 31 1. Cor. 15, 52.1. Thess. 4, 16.2. Petr. 3. 1. Jude v. 15. The Angels will indeed be present 1. for ornament, Conf. Apoc. 12, 15.c. 19, 6. 2. for ministry, see above chapter 13, 39. 49. c. 24, 24, 31. 3. for testimony.) *

* ( ἐπὶ σθρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ. Conf. Luc. 22, 29.Eph. 1, 21.Ebr. 1, 3.C. 8, 1. For the same thing is indicated here by the throne of majesty of the divine, which is indicated elsewhere by the right hand of God. See Annotations on c. 26, 64. and Conf. B. Par. Dispp. Elencht. on the Sunday Gospels p. 1330. It is well to be noted here that since Christ is said to be about to place the elect on his throne, Apoc. 3, 21. a distinction must be made between the throne of God, on which only Christ is placed, and the throne of Christ, on which the elect will be placed. By the former is understood the immense power and majesty of GOD; by the latter, however, eternal blessedness, Iohan. 14. verse 2. That is the eternal and uncreated throne, but these are the thrones of the saints prepared, below v. 34. Whence it is not the case that the Calvinists, from the fact that the saints are said to be about to be placed on the throne of Christ, may conclude that it cannot be proved by us from the session of Christ at the right hand of GOD that infinite majesty has been communicated by Christ to the man. But the Marburg Theologians deal with this controversy at greater length in Fundam. Deduct. against Cassell. p. 176. B. Par. not. in Apoc. c. 3, 21. Here this only is still to be warned, that Cornelius à Lapide errs, when he writes here, that Christ's power of judging was merited by his humble obedience even unto death, according to Philipp. 2, 8. 9. For it must be known 1. that the whole Holy Scripture teaches that Christ merited whatever he merited in his office, not for himself, but for us. See Es. 45, 24. Ioh. 17, 19. 1. Tim. 1, 15. 1. Cor. 1, 10. etc. that therefore 2. the particles διὰ καὶ διὸ do not denote Phil. 2. a meritorious cause, but at least a consequence, as Ebr. 1, 9. and this even some Papists grant, led by B. Par. Confess. Cathol. 1. 2. Spec. part. 1. art. 2. c. 4. §. 3.)

Latin:

v. 31. Filius hominis. Augustinus serm. 64. de verbis Domini Col. 245.Iudex hîc erit Filius hominis, formâ illâ hîc iudicabit, quae iudicata est, sedebit iudex, qui stetit sub iudice, damnabit veros reos, qui damnatus est falsus reus. * (Conf. idem lib. 1. de Trinit. c. 13. & 16. item in Ioh. tr. 21. 22. de C. D. I. 20. c. 30. t. 2. ep. 85. & 112. t. 9. tr. in Ioh. 76. in Symb. ad Catech. l. 2. c. 8. l. 3. c. 7. Cyrillus I. 2. in Ioh. c. 140. ac 144. Huc faciunt etiam dicta Ioh. 5, 22.27.Actor. 10, 42.c. 17, 31.Rom. 14, 9. Maximus Taurinensis homil. in Expos. symb. Necesse est, ut hominum genus ille discutiat, qui creavit, & ipse iudicet, qui redemit. iustumque est, ut omnipotens Dominus mortales suos, quos divinitatis virtute formavit, Patris pietate salvavit, iudicis examinatione discernat. Conf. plura in Annot. ad Ioh. 5, 27. In primo adventu venit in humilitate,Phil. 2. hîc veniet in maiestate; illic passurus, hîc iudicaturus. Non obstant verò praesenti loco dicta Matth. 16, 27.Marc. 8, 38. ubi dicit, se venturum in gloria Patris. Competit enim haec gloria Christo ut vero DEO, sive secundùm divinam naturam, quia est eiusdem numero essentiae cū DEO Patre, essentialiter; ut Filio hominis sive secundùm humanam naturam personaliter, sive per ac propter unionem personalem. adeoque rectè gloriam illam suam vocat. Unde etiam firmiter hinc vera Christi Deitas contra Photinianos probatur.) *

* (In gloriâ suâ. Conf. Psalm. 97, 35.Malach. 4, 1. suprà cap. 19, 28. c. 24, 30. & ibi notata. Cùm gloria haec Christo etiam ut homini competat, nempe personaliter, ipse quoque ut homo iudicium extremum sit administraturus, quia expressè hîc dicitur Iudex Filius hominis, conf. Ioh. 5, 27.Act. 17, 31. manifestum est, quòd gloria ac maiestas verè divina humanae Christi naturae revera sit communicata. Contra Calvinianos. Vid. plura huc facientia apud B. D. Menzerum contra Steinium p. 110. B. D. Lobechium in A. p. 446. B. Par. Dispp. C. Elencht. super Evang. Domin. p. 1344.) *

* (Et omnes sancti Angeli cum eo. Conf. Dan. 7, 9.Zach. 14, 5. suprà c. 24, 31 1. Cor. 15, 52.1. Thess. 4, 16.2. Petr. 3. 1. Iudae v. 15. Aderunt vero Angeli 1. ob ornamentum, Conf. Apoc. 12, 15.c. 19, 6. 2. ob ministerium, vid. suprà cap. 13, 39. 49. c. 24, 24, 31. 3. ob testimonium.) *

* ( ἐπὶ σθρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ. Conf. Luc. 22, 29.Eph. 1, 21.Ebr. 1, 3.C. 8, 1. Idem namque per thronum maiestatis divinae hîc indicatur, quod alibi per dextram Dei. Vid. Annot. ad c. 26, 64. ac Conf. B. Par. Dispp. Elencht. super Evang. Dom. p. 1330. Probè hîc notandū, quòd cùm Christus dicatur collocaturus electos in throno suo, Apoc. 3, 21. distingvendum sit inter thronum Dei, in quem solus Christus eollocatus, & thronum Christi, in quem electi collocabuntur. Per illum intelligitur immensa DEI potestas ac maiestas; per hunc verò aeterna beatitudo, Iohan. 14. vers. 2. Il. le est thronus aeternus & increatus, hi verò sanctorum throni sunt parati, infrà v. 34. Unde non est, quòd Calviniani exinde, quòd fancti dicuntur collocandi in throno Christi, colligant, non posse à nobis ex sessione Christi ad dextram DEI probari, communica ā Christo homini esse maiestatem infinitam. Sed hâc de cōtroversia pluribus agunt Dnn. Theologi Marpurg. in Fundam. Deduct. contra Cassell. p. 176. B. Par. not. in Apoc. c. 3, 21. Hîc illud solùm adhuc monendum, errare Cornelium à Lapide, quando hîc scribit, Christum potestatem iudicandi meritum esse suâ humili obedientiâ usque ad mortem, iuxtaPhilipp. 2, 8. 9. Etenim sciendum 1. quòd tota Scriptura S. doceat, Christum non sibi, sed nobis promeruisse, quie quid in officio suo promeruit. Vide Es. 45, 24.Ioh. 17, 19.1. Tim. 1, 15.1. Cor. 1, 10. &c. quòd proinde 2. particulae διὰ καὶ διὸ non notent Phil. 2. causam meritoriam, sed saltem consequentiam, ut Ebr. 1, 9. id que ipsi Pontificii nonnulli largiuntur, adducti à B. Par. Confess. Cathol. 1. 2. Spec. part. 1. art. 2. c. 4. §. 3.) *

## 25:32
v. 32. And all nations shall be gathered before him. There will be a universal council of the whole world. The impious will be separated from the pious by ἀφρρισμὸν and a certain excommunication. (Conf. Act. 10, 42. c. 17, 31. 2. Thess. 2, 1.)

(All nations, Conf. Ioh. 5, 28. Act. 24, 15. also of every age. The administration of the final judgment will consist in five acts, as it were: 1. in the gathering of all peoples. 2. in the separation of those gathered. 3. in the placement of those separated. 4. in the addressing of those placed and the promulgation of the decretory sentence. 5. in the execution of the promulgated sentence. But that all nations are mentioned here as to be set before the tribunal of Christ is to be opposed to the error of Durandus, who in 2. Disp. 33. q. 3. denies that little children will appear on the day of judgment. which the Jesuit Corn. à Lapide himself also refutes in this place, who nevertheless errs in this, while he asserts that little children will rise again in stature and manly age. and he thinks that this is evident from Eph. 4, 13. But the Apostle speaks in the said place not of the perfection of quantity or of age and stature, but of quality. that is, of the acknowledgment and knowledge of divine mysteries, which will be consummated in the future life, as will be proved in its own place. Nor can we approve the opinion of the same Jesuit, establishing that infants not baptized or dead in original sin will receive a middle sentence between the elect and the reprobate. For of this middle sentence Holy Scripture knows nothing, so much so, that not even in this place, where nevertheless the judicial sentence of Christ is most diligently noted, or γρυ or μυ may exist concerning this. Furthermore, as regards infants born in the Christian Church, far be it that we should deprive them of eternal beatitude: nay, we are rather certainly persuaded that they, on account of the prayers of the Church and the faith of their parents, are endowed and eternally saved. But concerning those who are born outside the Church, we judge it safer to ἐπέχειν, than to determine anything certain. See also the notes below on v. 34. But if the impious are to be presented to Christ the judge, they will certainly be resurrected on the last day, according to Act. 24, 15.Dan. 12, 2. which some Jews stubbornly deny. Compare R. David Kimchi on Psal. 1. 5. and 82. Certainly, that R. Saadia Gaon on Dan. 12, 2., R. Aben-Ezra, Rashi, and Kimchi on Isaiah 26, 14, and likewise Moses Gerundensis, Ezra, and Kimchi on Psal. 1. and Es. 38, 18. restrict the resurrection to the pious alone is testified by D. Ioan. Hornbeck, book 8, for the Convincing of the Jews, ch. 4. Among the more recent, R. Menasse ben Israel is occupied with that opinion, which he says is that of all the ancients, that not all men will rise again, but many, among whom there will be men of every and any condition, pious, impious, and intermediate, as can be seen from his book 2 on the Resurrection, ch. 8. But those Photinians approach very closely to this error of the Jews, that only the pious will live eternally, but the impious not at all, if they do not entirely cherish the same. Their opinion is presented for inspection by Dn. D. Calov, Socin. Proflig. p. 1114. seqq. B. Par. Dispp. Acad. p. 623. item L. d. Resurr. §. 101.

* (And he will separate them from one another as a shepherd &c. Compare Ioh. 10, 11.Ebr. 13, 20. But at Ioh. 10, 16. it is said there will be one fold. Response: one must distinguish between the militant and triumphant Church; also between the Church, insofar as it was to be gathered from the elect of the Jews and Gentiles, Ioh. 10, 16. and insofar as it is to be at some time entirely freed from hypocrites, who by reason of external society are mixed with the pious in this world. Moreover, Christ will carry out this separation through the Angels. See above ch. 13, 49. And the same was prefigured in the O. T., Deut. 27. and indicated in the N. T. by parables, Matth. 3, 10.c. 13, 24.47. Because, therefore, this separation is to be instituted only on the last day, it is clear that the golden age of the Chiliasts is expected in vain.) *

Latin:

v. 32. Et congregabuntur ante eum omnes gentes. Erit universale totius orbis Concilium. impii per ἀφρρισμὸν & ex communicationem quandam à piis separabuntur. * (Conf. Act. 10, 42.c. 17, 31.2. Thess. 2, 1.) *

* (Omnes gentes, Conf. Ioh. 5 28.Act. 24, 15. omnis quoque aetatis. Consistet autem extremi iudicii administratio in quinque quasi actibus 1. in omnium populorum congregatione. 2. in congregatorum separatione. 3. in separatorum collocatione. 4. in collocatorum alloquutione & decretoriae sententiae promulgatione. 5. in promulgatae sententiae executione. Quòd verò omnes gentes hîc commemorantur sistendae coram Christi tribunali, opponendum errori Durandi, qui in 2. Disp. 33. q. 3. negat, parvulos comparituros in die iudicii. quam ipse etiam refellit Iesuita Corn. à Lapide h. l. qui tamen in eo errat, dum adserit, parvulos in statura & aetate virili resurrecturos. idque constare putat ex Eph. 4, 13. Verùm loquitur Apostolus d. l. non de perfectione quantitatis sive aetatis ac staturae, sed qualitatis. hoc est, agnitionis & cognitionis divinorū mysteriorum, quae in futura vitâ consummabitur, uti suo loco probabitur. Nec approbare possumus eiusdem Iesuitae sententiam, statuentis, infantes non baptizatos sive in peccato origninali mortuos mediam inter electos & reprobos accepturos sententiam. Etenim de hac media sententiâ Script. S. nil scit, adeò quidem, ut nec h. l. ubi tamen ex professo iudiciaria Christi sententia quādiligētissimè annotata est, vel γρυ vel μυ de ea extet. Praeterea quod parvulos in Christianâ Ecclesiâ natos attinet, absit, ut beatitudine privemus aeternâ: quin certò potiùs persvasi sumus, eosdem ob preces Ecclesiae & parentum fide donari, aeternùque salvari. De iis vero qui extra Ecclesiam nati sunt, tutius censemus ἐπέχειν, quàm certi quid determinare. Vid. etiam notata infrà ad v. 34. Si verò impii Christo iudici sistendi, utique in extremo die resuscitabuntur & ipsi, iuxta Act. 24, 15.Dan. 12, 2. quod Iudaei quidam protervè negant. Conf. R. David Kimchi in Psal. 1. 5. & 82. Certè ad solos pios resurrectionem restringere R. Saadian à Gaon in Dan. 12, 2. R. Aben-Ezram, Raschi & Kimchi in Iesa. 26, 14. Mosen item Gerundensem, Esram, Kimchi in Psal. 1. & Es. 38, 18. testatur D. Ioan. Hornbeck lib. 8. pro Convinc. Iudaeis c. 4. E recentioribus R. Menasse ben Israel in eâ versatur opinione, quam omnium antiquorum esse dicit, non omnes homines resurrecturos esse, sed multos, inter quos sint futuri omnis & cuiusvis conditionis homines, pii, impii & intermedii, ceu videre est ex eiusd. l. 2. de Resurr. C. 8. Isti verò Iudaeorum errori, quòd soli, pii aeternum sint victuri, impii vero minimè, proximè accedunt, si non penitus eundem fovent Photiniani. quorum sententiam conspiciendam sistunt Dn. D. Calov. Socin. Proflig. p. 1114. seqq. B. Par. Dispp. Acad. p. 623. item L. d. Resurr. §. 101.

* (Et separabit eos ab invicem sicut pastor &c. Conf. Ioh. 10, 11.Ebr. 13, 20. At Ioh. 10, 16.Unum dicitur fore ovile. Resp. distingvendum inter Ecclesiam militantem & triumphantem; item inter Ecclesiam, quat. ex electis Iudaeorum ac gentilium congreganda erat, Ioh. 10, 16. ac quatenus ab hypocritis, qui ratione externae societatis in hoc mundo piis mixti, aliquando penitus liberanda. Coeterùm peraget Christus separationem hanc per Angelos. vid. suprà c. 13, 49. fuitque eadem in V. T. praefigurata, Deut. 27. in N. a. T. parabolis indicata, Matth. 3, 10.c. 13, 24.47. Quia igitur separatio haec in die demum extremo instituenda, patet, quòd frustrà aureum expectetur Chiliastarum seculum.) *

## 25:33
v. 33. And he will set the sheep &c. See Isid. Pelusiota book 1, ep. 288. Compare Ezech. 34, 17.) *

* At the right hand. Bellarmine, in book 3 of On the Incarnation, chapter 15, section secondly I say, strives to prove from the fact that the sheep, by whom the elect are understood (called so 1. on account of innocence of lifePs. 26, 6.Ps. 73, 13. 2. on account of patience,Is. 53, 7.Luke 21, 19.Heb. 10, 32. 3. on account of cleanness,Psalm 51. verse 4.12. 4. on account of abundance of the cross,Psalm 44, 22.Rom. 8, 36. 5. on account of obedience,John 10. verses 27. 28. or so 1. because of simplicity, 2. because of humility, verse 37. following 3. because of usefulness, and B. O. fruitfulness, v. 35. 36. 40. 4. because of charity,John 10, 28. item here v. 34. Compare more on this matter in B. D. Glass. Exeg. Evang. Dom. in Festo Epiph. p. 964. item in Exeg. Ep. Dom. 26. post Trin. p. 1221 B. P. Harm. Evang. c. 165. p. 889. item Homil. Acad. part. 2. p. 952. But the damned are called goats on account of wildness, rapacity, filthiness, lechery or impudence.) are said to be placed at the right hand of Christ, that when Christ is said to be exalted to the right hand of the Father, it is not indicated that according to his human nature he was made a participant of divine glory and majesty, but at least blessedness. I respond 1. by conceding that heavenly blessedness is insinuated by that phrase. Compare Psalm 16, 11. (to which points the fact that ἐυλογίαι of the law pronounced were with face turned toward Mount Gerizim, which is situated to the south, which the Hebrews call ימיז the right, just as they call the north שמאל the left, and ἀραὶ toward Mount Ebal, situated to the left. See Deut 11, 29. Add that the right denotes virtues, the left vices. See Eccles. 10, 2. Jonah c. 4, 11.) 2. by distinguishing, first between the right hand of GOD the Father, and the right hand of Christ, just as it is customary to distinguish between the throne of the Father, and the throne of Christ, concerning which distinction some things were noted above against 31. item in Anal. to c. 19, 28 secondly between sitting at the right hand of GOD, and being placed at the right hand of Christ. The former denotes communication of divine majesty, the latter does not. 3. by warning that the right hand of Christ in this place has an opposite left hand, but that a left hand is opposed to the right hand of GOD, to which Christ as man was exalted, is nowhere mentioned in Holy Scripture. 4. by observing that it is one thing to make to sit together in the heavenly places in Christ, Eph. 2, 6. and another to sit at the right hand of GOD, ibid. chapter 1, 20. Whence 5. Bellarmine himself in the said place, section Thirdly I say, confesses that it is more probable that by the right hand of GOD, to which Christ sits, should be understood divine glory, power and majesty, so that the sense of that article is: Christ sits at the right hand of the Father, here: Christ reigns with equal power and honor, judges and governs all things with the Father himself. And he confesses that almost all the Fathers, Athanasius, Basil, Cyril, etc., interpret it in this way. Whence also the same man finally grants that divine majesty is indicated as communicated to the human nature of Christ through that exaltation to the right hand of GOD, but not in itself, but in the suppositum. But what should be thought of this evasion has been shown elsewhere. Furthermore, as far as the present passage is concerned, the Savior seems to John Drusius to look to the custom formerly received in the judgments of the Jews, as in those, according to the same author in book 1 of Praeterit. p. 52, there were two scribes, of whom one stood at the right, the other at the left; one wrote the words that acquitted, the other those that condemned the accused.) *

Latin:

v. 33. Et statuet oves &c. Vid. Isid. Pelusiota lib. 1. ep. 288. Conf. Ezech. 34, 17.) *

* (à Dextris. Ex eo, quòd oves, per quas electi intelliguntur, (appellati ita 1. propter vitae innocentiamPs. 26, 6.Psal. 73, 13. 2. propter patientiam,Es. 53, 7.Luc. 21, 19.Ebr. 10, 32. 3. propter munditiam,Psalm. 51. vers. 4.12. 4. propter crucis abundantiam,Psalm. 44, 22.Rom. 8, 36. 5. propter obedientiam,Iohan. 10. vers. 27. 28. vel ita 1. ob simplicitatem, 2, ob humilitatem, vers. 37. seqq. 3. ob utilitatem, & B. O. foecunditatem, v. 35. 36. 40. 4. ob charitatem,Ioh. 10, 28. item h. l. v. 34. Conf. plura in hanc rem apud B. D. Glass. Exeg. Evang. Dom. in Festo Epiph. p. 964. item in Exeg. Ep. Dom. 26. post Trin. p. 1221 B. P. Harm. Evang. c. 165. p. 889. it. Homil. Acad. part. 2. p. 952. Damnati verò haedi dicuntur ob feritatem, rapacitatem, foeditatem, salacitatem sive procacitatem.) dicuntur statui â dextris Christi, evincere satagit Bellarm. lib. 3. de Incarn. C. 15. § secundò dico, quando Christus dicitur exaltatus ad dextram Patris, tunc non indicari, quòd secundùm humanam naturam divinae gloriae ac maiestatis fuerit particeps factus, sed saltem beatitudo. Resp. 1. concedendo, per phrasin illam insinuari beatitudinem coelestem. Conf. Psalm. 16, 11. (quo spectat, quòd ἐυλογίαι legis pronunciatae fuerint obverso vultu ad montem Garizin, qui situs ad meridiem, quem Ebraei ימיזdextram vocant, ceu septentrionem שמאלsinistram,ἀραὶ verò ad montem Hebal, ad sinistram situm. Vid Deut 11, 29. Adde, quòd dextra virtutes, sinistra vitia notet. Vid. Eccles. 10, 2. Ionae c. 4, 11.) 2. distingvendo, primum inter dextram DEI Patris, & dextram Christi, quemadmodum dist. solet inter thronum Patris, & thronum Christi, de quâ dist. suprà quaedam monita adv. 31. item in Anal. ad c. 19, 28 secundò inter sedere ad dextram DEI, & statui à dextris Christi. illud notat communicationem divinae maiestatis, hoc non. 3. monendo, quòd dextra Christi h. l. habeat oppositam sinistram, sed quae dextrae DEI, ad quam Christus homo exaltatus fuit, opponatur sinistra, nullibi in Script. S. memoratur. 4. obs. quòd aliud sit facere consedere, in coelestibus in Christo, Eph. 2, 6. aliud ad dextram DEI consedere ibid. cap. 1, 20. Unde 5. Bellarminus ipse d. l. §. Tertio dico, faretur, probabilius esse, per dextram DEI, ad quam Christus sedet, intelligi debere gloriam, potentiam & maiestatem divinam, ita ut sensus sit illius articuli: Christus sedet â dextris Patris, hic: Christus pari potentiâ & honore regnat, iudicat & gubernat omnia cum ipso Patre. atque ita exponere fatetur, omnes ferè Patres, Athanasium, Basilium, Cyrillum &c. Unde etiam idem tandem largitur, quòd divina maiestas per illam exaltationem ad dextram DEI humanae Christi naturae communicata indicetur, sed non in se, verum in supposito. Ast quid de hoc effugio habendum sit, alibi ostensum est. Coeterùm quod praesentem concernit locum, videtur Iohanni Drusio Salvator respicere ad morem in iudiciis Iudaeorum olim receptum, utpote in quibus, referente eodem l. 1. Praeterit. p. 52. duo fuere scribae, quorum unus stetit ad dextram, alter ad sinistram; unus scribebat verba, quae absolvebant, alter quae damnabant reos.) *

## 25:34
* (v. 34. Then the King shall say, etc. Q. here 1. Whether the promulgation of the sentence is to be heard by all with an external voice; or whether it will indeed take place only interiorly in the conscience of each? Remigius, Thomas Aquinas, in the supplement, q. 88, art. 2, and Jansenius in his Commentary on the Harmony of the Gospels affirm the latter. But Alfonsus Tostatus, q. 333, on chapter 25 of Matthew, Richard in 4 sent., dist. 47, art. 1, q. 2, and Soto on the same dist., q. 2, art. 4, assert the former more correctly, to whom Leonh. Coquaeus also subscribes in his Commentary on book 20 of Augustine, De C. D., ch. 5. B. Parens also, in his Book on the Final Judgment, ch. § 69, proves with several reasons that it is more likely that, even if not everything is to be carried out in the same words that are held in the judicial process in this place, some words will nevertheless be uttered by the judge, to be heard externally by all, by which he may call the just to rewards and adjudge the unjust to hell. And most Catholics today add their vote to this opinion. Francis Lucas, Corn. à Lapide, and others think so on this place, as does Leonh. Lessius, book 13, De perfect. div., ch. 22, n. 142. Q. 2. Why is the sentence for the just pronounced in the first place? Resp. because the Judge here is more inclined to reward than to punish. For when GOD punishes, he then performs, as it were, a strange work, since he is goodness itself.) *

Come, you blessed, viz., in that blessed seed, which is Christ. And not blessing themselves and trusting in their own works. * (The voice of the Judge will be as pleasant to the pious; so horrendous to the impious and damned. Pleasant to the pious 1. because of the friendly address: Come. Conf. Gen. 24, 31.27,26.c. 45, 18. 19. above v. 23. 2. because of the honorific appellation. blessed,Gen. 12, 3.c. 22. v. 18.Eph. 1, 4. of my Father.

See. John 14, 21.23.ch. 16, 23.27.ch. 20, 21. 3. on account of the assignment of this most precious inheritance: κληρονομήσατε possess the kingdom. as sons, adopted through faith, John 1, 12.Rom. 8, 17. heirs of the promised goods, of a kingdom not falling or earthly, but eternal, 1. Pet. 1, 4,Tit. 3, 7.Heb. 9, 15. 4. on account of the splendid commemoration of whatever good works there are: v. 35. 36. for I was hungry &c. 5. on account of the sweetest response to the exception of the elect, v. 40. Amen, I say to you &c. To the reprobate, on the contrary, the voice of Christ the judge will be horrendous 1. on account of the austere address: v. 41. depart from me, from the author of life, into death, because you have turned away from me; from the fountain of all consolation, drink from the sulfurous lake of despair; depart from me, the Sun of joy, to the horrible darkness of eternal sadness. 2. on account of the infamous denomination. cursed. not cursed by the Father, because my Father willed you to be saved no less than the elect, 1. Tim. 2, 4.2. Pet. 3, 9. &c. but because you yourselves, willingly and out of most stubborn resistance, have rendered yourselves execrable and cursed. nor cursed by the Son, who died for the reprobate also, whose most precious blood poured out for you you have held as profane, Heb. 10, 29. 3. on account of the irrevocable condemnation to eternal punishments, to eternal fire. 4. on account of the formidable association of devils, which is prepared &c. 5. on account of the just reproach of lack of mercy. for I was hungry &c.) *

* (Come. you who have come to me laboring,Matt. 11, 27. add. Is. 55, 1.John 6, 35.Rev. 22, 16. come now triumphing. from the kingdom of grace to the kingdom of glory. from the school of the cross, to the kingdom of light. The elect will come, so that they may appear in judgment, render an account, hear the sentence of absolution, receive rewards, Rom. 14, 11. 12. they will not come, however, so that they may be confounded or condemned. Therefore, one must accurately distinguish here between the judgment of discretion, of approval, and of condemnation. The former is treated in John 3, 18.ch. 5, 24.29. the latter in the present place, likewise 1. Cor. 4, 4. the former Rom. 14, 10. it. above v. 32. Compare many things making for this in B. P. L. on the Extreme Judgment §. 6. Add Thomas Gataker in Cinno p. 52.) *

Blessed of the Father. that is, who are blessed by the heavenly Father with every spiritual blessing in the heavens, as the Apostle explains Eph. 1, 3.6. * (add. Gal. 3, 8. 9. which passage Corn. à Lapide himself compares, & adds, by the merit of my blood (N. B. not indeed of your works) merit. Come, you blessed, whom my Father chose before the world, justified and sanctified in the world, now he will glorify after the world. See August. in Soliloq. But lest the Jesuit just now brought forward might seem to have discarded every merit of good works, he excepts at this place that glory is given to the saints by Christ, as an inheritance as to sons; and at the same time as a reward, as to the deserving and worthy, since GOD does not give the kingdom to sons, whether they be worthy of it, or whether they be unworthy. I answer by conceding that GOD gives the kingdom of heaven to the worthy, but it must be known that not our merits, which are like a menstruous cloth, Isa. 64, 6. but the merit of Christ alone, apprehended by true faith, renders us worthy. Conf. Eph. 1, 6. Christ will indeed give the heavenly kingdom to the worthy and to those working well, but not on account of their own works.)*

Κληρονομήσατε. enter into the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom, but do not receive the merit of your works. *(you are sons of GOD, Ioh. 1, 12. therefore also receive the inheritance, conf. Gal. 3, 26 1. Petr. 1, 4. for if sons, then also heirs, Rom. 8, 17. Compare the blessed Pareus discussing at length in his Commentary on the said Petrine passage concerning this most august, most ample, most durable, and most constant heavenly inheritance, etc. Since therefore an inheritance is kept for us in the heavens, let us forget those things which are behind in these lands, Philipp. 3, 14. Add. Analecta to Coloss. 3, 1. 2. Finally, since an inheritance is obtained only by sons, and we obtain ὑιοσθεσίαν only through faith in Christ, Ioh. 1, 12. it is evident that Thammerus, Latomus, Andradius, Isengrinius, Cinglius, etc., err vehemently in promising this inheritance or eternal life to Gentiles without the knowledge of Christ. Concerning which error, see the blessed D. Schmuckius in his Explanation of the passage Matth. 25, 46., the blessed D. Mentzerus in his Exegesis of the A. C., and the blessed Pareus in his Academic Disputations passim.)*

Prepared for you before the foundation of the world. not acquired by your merits. *(Vain therefore are the glorifications of the Papists concerning their own merits, which even Corn. à Lapide here elevates beyond merit, writing that the saints have merited eternal glory decreed by Christ in judgment by their own works. item, that the elect are chosen and adjudged to heaven by Christ on account of good works, and thus B. O. they merit heaven. To which error we oppose the notable passage of the Apostle Eph. 1, 3. and following, add Rom. 6, 23.c. 11, 5. 6. Compare the consensus of the Adversaries themselves in B. Par. Confess. Cathol. b. 2. Spec. part. 3. art. 22. c. 2. th. 2. It is to be noted here further 1. that although the possession of the heavenly kingdom does not immediately upon death fully accrue to those who have died blessedly in Christ, either as regards both parts, namely body and soul: for they are indeed made partakers of eternal happiness as regards the soul as soon as they die in Christ, so that the body is reunited to the soul only on the last day, and thus together with the soul enjoys eternal blessedness, yet it is by no means permitted to infer from this that the heavenly kingdom is not fully prepared for the elect from the foundation of the world, as Guil. Perkinsius in Catech. p. 363. and 364. maintains. For just as election to eternal life is one, full, and perfect, so also the preparation of the kingdom is one and perfect. 2. that it is proved by the orthodox against the Calvinists from the phrase that the kingdom, eternal life, heaven, are here and elsewhere, see Isaiah c. 64, 8. 1. Cor. 2, 9. said to be prepared for the pious, but not created, that the heaven of the blessed is not some created place, but objectively GOD himself; formally heavenly joy; subjectively however what it is, or what concerns its quality and location ποῦ, they warn that this is not revealed to us in Holy Scripture, and therefore it is better to be solicitous in this life about its possession than about an accurate definition, since Scripture is silent. Wendelinus replies in Exerc. 22. § 6. by denying 1. the consequence, since both fire and other works of creation are not expressly said to be created in Holy Scripture. But I respond by denying that any substantial works of GOD are not said to be created. 2. that this phrase, the heaven of the blessed is created, is unknown to Holy Scripture, since he himself by heaven Gen. 1, 1. understands the Empyrean heaven. But it is not sufficient that Wendelinus understands the Empyrean heaven by the name of heaven Gen. 1, 1., having indeed followed in this matter the opinion of the Scholastics and of some Jesuits. But how slippery that exposition is, B. Par. showed long ago in L. de Vit. aet. §. 170. where, especially against the claim that the heaven of the blessed is a place immediately above the firmament, he urges 1. the denial of knowledge, Es. 64, 4.1. Cor. 2, 9. 2. the moderation of the Apostle, 2. Cor. 12, 3. 4. 3. the assertion of the Savior, Matth. 18, 10. 4. the opposition of hell. 5. the conflagration of visible things 2. Petr. 3, 7.10.12. 6. the consequence of many absurdities. 7. the confession of the adversaries themselves, such as Biel and Thomas Aquinas, (to whom can also be added the Jesuit Pererius Comm. in Gen. c. 1, 1. §. 51. where he also alleges St. Jerome and Basil for his opinion). The same author destroys the remaining foundations of Wendelinus in the same book and chapter §. 171. so that there is no need to dwell on discussing them at greater length. Meanwhile, we readily grant that ποῦ that place of the blessed can be called a place, in the broader acceptance of the word, just as B. D. Rungius also writes in c. 5. Gen. p. 276: by the heaven to which Enoch and other patriarchs are said to have been translated after death, is denoted not the Empyrean heaven, which the Sophists place above the starry heaven, or firmament, but a certain place, destined for the blessedness and glory of the pious, where God will reveal himself to the blessed in ineffable light and glory. Where that place is, however, Scripture has nowhere left expressed, but has relegated that to the heavenly school. Compare altogether more on the Empyrean heaven of the Scholastics in B. D. Martini in Art. A. C. first part, second section, Dispp. 4. §. 20. and following.)*

Latin:

* (v. 34. Tunc dicet Rex &c. Q. hîc 1. An sententiae promulgatio voce externâ ab omnibus audienda sit; an verò interius duntaxat in cuiusconscientiâ sit futura? Posterius affirmat Remigius, Thomas de Aquino, in supplem. 9. 88. art. 2. Iansenius in Comm. ad Conc. Evang. Sed rectiùs adserunt prius Alfonsus Tostatus q. 333. in cap. 25.
