Matth Richardus in 4. sent. dist. 47. art. 1. q. 2. Sotus ead. dist. q. 2. art. 4. quibus etiā subscribit Leonh. Coquaeus Comment. in l. 20. Aug. de C. D. c. 5. B. quoque Parens L. de Extr. Iud. c. § 69. aliquot rationibus probat, verisimilius esse, si vel maximè non sint omnia iisdem verbis, quae in processu iudiciali h. l. habentur, peragenda, quaedam tamen à iudice prolatum iri verba, exteriùs ab omnibus audienda, quibus iustos ad praemia vocet, & iniustos inferno adiudicet. Et huic sententiae calculum suum adiiciunt plerique hodie Pontificii. Ita sentiunt Franc. Lucas, Corn. à Lapide, aliique in h. l. item Leonh. Lessius l. 13. de perfect. div. c. 22. n. 142. Q. 2. Cur primo loco proferatur sententia pro iustis? Resp. quia Iudex hic pronior ad remunerandum, quàm ad puniniendum. quando enim DEUS punit, tunc alienum quasi agit opus, cùm sit ipsa bonitas.) *

Venite benedicti, sc. in benedicto illo semine, quod est Christus. non autem seipsos benedicentes & confidentes in operibus suis. * (Erit vox Iudicis uti piis iucunda; ita impiis ac damnatis horrenda. Iucunda piis 1. ob amicam compellationem: Venite. Conf. Gen. 24, 31.27,26.c. 45, 18. 19. suprà v. 23. 2. ob honorificam appellationem. benedicti,Gen. 12, 3.c. 22. v. 18.Eph. 1, 4.Patris mei.

Vid. Ioh. 14, 21.23.cap. 16, 23.27.c. 20, 21. 3. ob pretiosissimae hae. reditatis adsignationem: κληρονομήσατεpossidete regnum. tanquam filii, per fidem adoptati, Ioh. 1, 12.Rom. 8, 17. haeredes promissorum bonorum, regni non caduci sive terreni, sed aeterni, 1. Petr. 1, 4,Tit. 3, 7.Ebr. 9, 15. 4. ob splendidam qualium qualium bonorum operum commemorationem: v. 35. 36. esurivi enim &c. 5. ob svavissimam ad exceptionem electorum, responsionem, v. 40. Amen, dico vobis &c. Reprobis contrà horrenda erit vox Christi iudicis 1. ob austeram compellationem: v. 41. discedite à me, ab autore vitae, in mortem, quia me aversati estis; à fonte omnis consolationis, bibite de stagno sulphureo desperationis; discedite â me Sole laetitiae, ad horribiles tenebras aeternae tristitiae. 2. ob infamem denominationem. maledicti. non maledicti Patris, quia Pater meus non vos minùs quàm electos voluit salvos, 1. Tim. 2, 4.2. Petr. 3, 9. &c. sed qui vos ipsos sponte & ex pertinacissima repugnantiâ reddidistis execrandos & maledictos. nec maledicti Filii, qui pro reprobis quoque mortuus, cuius pretiosissimum sangvinem pro vobis effusum prophanum habuistis, Ebr. 10, 29. 3. ob irrevocabilem ad aeterna supplicia condemnationem, ad ignem aeternum. 4. ob formidabilem diabolorum adsociationem, qui paratus est &c. 5. obiustam immisericordiae exprobrationem. esurivi enim &c.) *

* (Venite. qui venistis ad me laborantes,Matth. 11, 27. add. Es. 55, 1.Ioh. 6, 35.Apoc. 22, 16. venite iam triumphantes. ex regno gratiae ad regnum gloriae. ex schola crueis, ad regnum lucis. Venient electi, ut in iudicio compareant, rationem reddant, sententiam absolutoriam audiant, praemia recipiant, Rom. 14, 11. 12. non venient autem, ut confundantur vel damnentur. Accuratè proinde distingvendum hîc est, inter iudicium discretionis, approbationis, ac condemnationis. De hoc agitur Ioh. 3, 18.c. 5, 24.29. de isto in praesenti loco, item 1. Cor. 4, 4. de illo Rom. 14, 10. it. suprà v. 32. Conf. multa huc facientia apud B. P. L. de Extremo Iudic. §. 6. Adde Thom. Gatakerum in Cinno p. 52.) *

Benedicti Patris. hoc est, qui à Patre coelesti omni benedictione spirituasi in coelis sunt benedicti, ut exponit Apostolus Eph. 1, 3.6. * (add. Gal. 3, 8. 9. quem locum ipse Corn. à Lapide confert, & addit, per sanguinis mei (N. B. non verò operum vestrorum) meritum. Venite benedicti, quos elegit Pater meus ante mundum, iustificavit & sanctificavit in mundo, iam nunc glorificabit post mundum. Vid. August. in Soliloq. Ne verò omne bonorum meritum deservisse Iesuita modò adductus videatur, excipit ad h. l. quòd gloriae detur sanctis à Christo, quasi haereditas tanquam filiis; & simul quasi merces, tanquam meritis & dignis cùm DEUS non det regnum filiis, sive digni eo sint, sive indigni sint. Resp. concedendo, quòd DEUS regnum coelorum det dignis, at sciendum, quòd non nostra merita, quae sunt instar panni menstruati, 64, 6. sed Christi solius meritum, verâ vide apprehensum, nos dignos reddat. Conf. Eph. 1, 6. Dabit utique Christus coeleste regnum dignis ac benè operantibus, sed non propter opera eorum propria.)*

Κληρονομήσατε. haereditatem regni coelestis adite, non autem operum vestrorum meritum accipite. *(estis filii DEI, Ioh. 1, 12. ideò etiam haereditatem accipite, conf. Gal. 3, 261. Petr. 1, 4. si enim filii, utique etiam haeredes, Rom. 8, 17. Confer de haere ditate hâc coelesti augustissima, amplissimâ, durabilissimâ, constantissima &c. prolixè disserentē B. Par. Com. ad dict. locum Petrinū. Cùm proinde in coelis haereditas nobis servetur, obliviscamur eorum, quae retro sunt in his terris, Philipp. 3, 14. Add. Analecta ad Coloss. 3, 1. 2. Denique cùm haereditas non nisi filiis obtingat, ὑιοσθεσίαν verò tantùm per fidem in Christum obtineamus, Ioh. 1, 12. patet, quòd vehementer errent Thammerus, Latomus, An dradius, Isengrinius, Cinglius &c. gentilibus sine Christi cognitione haereditatem hanc sive vitam aeternam promittentibus. De quo errore videantur B. D. Schmuckius in Expl. dict. Matth. 25, 46. B. D. Mentzerus in Exegesi A. C. B. Par. in Dispp. Academ. passim.)*

Paratum est vobis ante constitutionem mundi. non vestris meritis acquisitum. *(Vanae igitur sunt Pontificiorum glorificationes de propriis meritis, quae etiam Corn. à Lapide praeter meritum hîc evehit, scribens, quòd sancti aeternam gloriam à Christo in iudicio decretam suis operibus meruerint. item, quòd electi propter bona opera à Christo eligantur & adiudicentur coelo, adeoque B. O. mereantur coelum. Cui errori opponimus insignem locum Apostoli Eph. 1, 3. seqq. add. Rom. 6, 23.c. 11, 5. 6. Conf. ipsorum Adversariorum consensum apud B. Par. Confess. Cathol. l. 2. Spec. part. 3. art. 22. c. 2. th. 2. Notandum hîc ulterius 1. quòd licet regni coelestis possessio beatè in Christo defunctis non statim â morte plenariè sive quoad utramque partem, corpus puta & animam, obtingat: ita enim illi statim ac in Christo moriuntur quoad animā aeternae felicitatis redduntur participes, ut corpus in extremo demum die animae reduniatur, atque sic unà cum anima beatitudine fruatur aeternâ, minimè tamen hinc inferre liceat, quòd nec regnum coeleste plenariè praeparatum sit electis à mundi origine, ceu Guil. Perkinsius in Catech. p. 363. ac 364. statuit. Etenim quemadmodum electio ad vitam aeternam non nisi una, plena & perfecta est, ita quoque praeparatio regni non nisi una & perfecta est. 2 quòd ab orthodoxis ex phrasi, quòd regnum, vita aeterna, coelum, hîc & alibi, vid. Esaiae c. 64, 8. 1. Cor, 2, 9. piis dicuntur praeparata, non verò creata, contra Calvinianos probetur, quòd coelum beatorum non sit creatus aliquis locus, sed obiectivè ipse DEUS; formaliter laetitia coelestis; subiectivè autem quid sit, sive quod ποῦ illius qualitatem ac situm concernit, monent, id in Script. S. nobis non esse revelatum, adeoque satius esse, de eius possessione, quàm accuratâ definitione, tacente quippe Scripturâ, in hâc vitâ esse solicitum. Regerit Wendelinus Exerc. 22. § 6. negando 1. consequentiam, siquidem & ignis & alia creationis opera in Script. S. expressè non dicantur creata. At respond. negando, quòd ulla opera DEI substantialia non dicantur creata. 2. quod phrasis haec, coelum beatorum est creatum, Sc. Sacrae incognita sit, cùm ipse per coelumGen. 1, 1.intelligat coelum Empyreum. At non sufficit, quòd Wendelinus nomine coeliGen. 1, 1. empyraeum coelum intelligat, sequutus quidem hâc in re opinionē Scholasticorū ac nonnullorum Iesuitarum. Sed quàm lubrica ea sit expositio, pridem ostendit B. Par. L. de Vit. aet. §. 170. ubi cumprimis contra illam, quòd coelum beatorum sit locus proximè supra firmamentum, urget 1. cognitionis denegationem,Es. 64, 4.1. Cor. 2, 9. 2. Apostoli moderationem, 2. Cor. 12, 3. 4. 3. Salvatoris adsertionem, Matth. 18, 10. 4. inferni oppositionem. 5. visibilium conflagrationem 2. Petr. 3, 7.10.12. 6. multorum absurdorum consecutionem. 7. ipsorum quoque adversariorum, puta Bielis ac Thomae de Aquino, (quibus addi quoque potest Iesuita Pererius Comm. in Gen. c. 1, 1. §. 51. ubi etiam pro sua sententia allegat S. Hieronymum ac Basilium) confessionem. Reliqua Wendelini fundamenta destruit idem l. c. §. 171. ut adeò non opus sit, prolixiùs illis discutiendis inhaerere. Interea facilè largimur, quòd ποῦ illud beatorum locus, in latiori vocis acceptione, vocari possit, quemadmodum etiam B. D. Rungius in c. 5. Gen. p. 276. scribit: per coelum ad quod Henoch & alii patriarchae post mortem translati dicuntur, denotatur non coelum empyreum, quod supra stellatum coelum, seu firmamentum collocant Sophistae, sed locus certus, beatitudini & gloriae piorum destinatus, ubi Deus ineffabili luce & gloriâ se beatis patefaciet. Ubi autem locus ille sit, nus quam Scriptura expressum reliquit, sed id ad coelestem scholam reiecit. Conf. omninò pluribus de coelo Scholasticorum Empyreo B. D. Martini in Art. A. C. primi part. poster. Dispp. 4. §. 20. seqq.)*

## 25:35
v. 35. For I was hungry &c. The Rabbis say: The attributes of GOD are, to clothe the naked, to visit the sick, to console the mourning, to bury the dead. Whence he is said to walk after Him, who does such things. See the book Musar f. 120. pag. 1. Furthermore, it is by no means taught in this place that good works are meritorious of eternal life, but that Christ is about to judge according to works, and to render good to those who have done good, because works are testimonies of true faith in Christ, and they please GOD on account of Christ: whence also GOD rewards them out of grace. (But why in the description of the judicial process only works of mercy, and indeed corporal ones, are enumerated, with the remaining fruits and effects of faith being passed over, the cause of that matter is not (as indeed St. Augustine thought in book 21 of The City of God, ch. 27) that the remaining sins could be expiated by them: But, that just as in the preceding parts under the parable of the entrusted talents He had admonished the Apostles and their successors in the office of teaching, and others established in the eminence of a duty, of their duty, so here He might teach all Christians in general, that an account must also be demanded of them at some time. That we should be martyrs, is for few; that we should be Doctors and pillars of the Church, is likewise for few. But to offer a draught of cold water to a neighbor who is thirsty, no one cannot do. And that this is the genuine scope of the present place, the blessed Pareus shows at length in his book On the Last Judgment §. 56. Therefore the Papists err, establishing, That Christ therefore makes mention of good works in the words of the judicial process, so that He might teach that eternal life is to be rendered to the elect as a debt for the merits of their works. See Bellarmine, book 5 on Justification, chapters 3 & 7. Ribera on the Temple, book 1, chapter 21, p. 67. Barradius, Francis Lucas, Jansenius on this passage. Costerus in Enchiridion of Controversies, p. 276. Hagerus in the Collection of the Augsburg Confession & the Council of Trent, p. 88, and others. Much more so those who establish, as Vasquez and Pighius are recorded to teach, that the kingdom of heaven was prepared for the blessed from the foundation of the world, because they were going to live piously in this age. But, to be silent for now on the fact that Christ does not here explain the cause why the kingdom was prepared for the elect, but at least indicates the signs from which the faith of those who ought now to enter the kingdom of GOD might be known, we oppose to this error of the Papists 1. the analogy of faith. For Holy Scripture nowhere teaches that on account of works Christ is going to give us eternal life, but it testifies at least to this, that He is going to judge according to works or according to the testimonies of works. See the Analysis on chapter 16, verse 27. For the judgment will be visible and audible. Therefore, good works, as testimonies of faith, which otherwise is not immediately evident but is known from its fruits, will be brought forward. It remains, therefore, that the sentence to be passed fundamentally respects faith and unbelief, and sign-wise respects external recognition according to works. Blessed D. Hutterus in his Explanation of the Formula of Concord, p. 366, not undeservedly commends a rule most firmly grounded in the sacred letters, and most useful for correctly understanding very many sayings of Holy Scripture, namely, that in Holy Scripture beatitude, salvation, perfect righteousness, and life are frequently ascribed to the effects of faith, that is, to good works: which, however, ought properly and uniquely to be ascribed to the efficient cause. The cause of this matter, as he also warns, is 1. because Scripture wishes judgment to be made from the effects, as from witnesses, concerning the cause, that is, faith. 2. because GOD compensates good works not only in this life with various benefits, but will also adorn them in the future with greater degrees of glory. But both not out of debt or merit, whether of congruity or condignity: but solely freely on account of the promise made, not to our good works, which by their nature are due, imperfect, and polluted, but to faith. And from the rule just brought forward, the arguments of the Papists can be solved, which from the sayings, Ps. 1, 1.Ps. 15, 1. following Ps. 41, 2.Is. 1, 16. 17. 18.Ezek. 18, 9.17. 18. & 19. Joel c. 2, 32. Jonah 3, 10. above c. 5, 9. 12. c. 10, Luke 7, 47.c. 11, 41.John 5, 29.c. 13, 17.c. 14, 21.Rom. 2, 6. 7. & 8.1 Cor. 3, 8. etc. are accustomed to form the merits of the B. O. Compare also on this matter P. D. Hafenrefferus LL. Theol. p. 685. 825. there can also be added Anal. to c. 16, 27. We oppose the error of the Papists. 2. the definitive sentence of Christ. He calls the elect blessed of His Father, namely, in Him apprehended by true faith, Gal. 3, 9. 10.14.Eph. 1, 3. but not those blessing themselves in the merits of their own works. He says furthermore κληρονομήσατε receive the inheritance, as sons indeed, John 1, 12.Gal. 3, 26. Now truly a servile wage differs from a filial inheritance. Compare Rom. 8, 17.Gal. 3, 18.1 Pet. 1, 4. etc. Theophylact notes in this place: He calls the Saints blessed, as having been received by the Father. He makes them heirs, however, of the kingdom. Showing that GOD makes them partakers of His kingdom, as His sons. For He did not say, receive, but possess the kingdom as an inheritance, as a paternal substance. Similarly, Fulgentius l. 1. de Praedest. ad Monimum: But even this very work is of grace. For from grace is given not only to the justified a good life, but also to the glorified eternal life. 3. the contrary assertion of the Apostle, Rom. 6, 23. For if eternal life is τοῦ σθεοῦ χάρισμα a free gift of GOD, it will not be a merit of our works. Compare also Rom. 3, 28.c. 11, 6.Gal. 2, 16.Eph. 2, 8. 9.Phil. 3, 9.Tit. 3, 5.2 Tim. 2, 28. Chrysostom hom. 80, after he had recounted that the damned are justly punished on account of omitted works of mercy, concludes: For these reasons, therefore, both they are not unjustly punished, and those (standing at the right) even if they had done a thousand such things, are nevertheless crowned through grace. For that kindness is entirely of grace, that for the smallest and most vile things the heavenly kingdom and so great an honor should be bestowed. 4. the gratuitous election. For: In what way or for what cause or merit GOD from eternity chose or decreed to save some men, in the same way or for the same cause and merit He justifies and saves the same in time. But GOD chose men from eternity on account of the merit of Christ apprehended by persevering faith, not on account of their foreseen works. Therefore, He also justifies and saves the same in time not on account of their own works, but solely on account of the merit of Christ, apprehended by constant faith. The immutability of the divine will proves the consequence of the major proposition, Num. 23, 19.Mal. 3, 6. The Papists themselves concede the minor, and certainly they wish to appear as if they do not want to deny it in the least, as is especially to be seen from Ioh. Malderus, Bishop of Antwerp, Consider. Decretorum Synodi Dordrechp. 9. seqq. Bell. l. 1. de Gr. & Lib. Art. c. 10. It must be known, therefore, that the particle γὰρ is not in this place causal, but ratiocinative: for works are adduced by Christ not as ποιητικὰ, or as efficient causes meritorious of the kingdom of heaven, but as σημαντικὰ, or as testimonies and fruits of true faith, lying hidden within in the heart. For love, from which these works arise, is an inseparable companion of faith, Gal. 5, 6. Whence, although we do not require works of mercy from those to be saved as a merit of eternal life, for this glory is owed to the satisfaction of Christ alone, we do nevertheless require them as a testimony and fruit of true faith. Compare more in B. D. Hulsem. in A. C. p. 205. B. Par. L. de extr. Iud. §. 57. item Dispp. Elencht. p. 1348. That indeed the particles כי, γὰρ, ὅτι &c. because, for, and similar ones are not always causal in Holy Scripture, the Jesuit Maldonatus readily grants, in c. 8. v. 29. Iohannis p. 721, writing: This little word because and for does not sometimes signify a cause, there are innumerable examples even in the Psalms alone. Places among others are in our Evangelist c. 6, 14. c. 7, 8. c. 16, 2. 3. Lucae 7, 471. Cor. 10, 5.1. Thess. 2, 17. 18.1. Tim. 13, 1.Ioh. 3, 14. Michael also Gislerus, a Roman cleric, in Expos. cap. 3. Cant. Cantiv. 11. p. 472, warns of a phrase frequently observed in sacred writings, by which the particle because is used for another particle, such as therefore, and does not signify a cause so much as an effect. The same is admitted by the Jesuits, Alfonsus Salmeron--. 1. p. 327, and also Com. in Ep. ad Eph. c. 1. Dispp. 3. Likewise Iacobus Tirinus, tr. de Idiot. Ling. Ebr. & Graecae, Commentariis in V. ac N. T. praemisso, num. 12. p. 86. Thus also Gregorius Magnus lib. 6. epist. 22. Toletus ad Luc. 7, 42. Salmeron t. 1. p. 327, accept the particle because Luc. 7, 47., namely, that the cause is gathered from the effect, to wit, the remission of sins from love. A similar example is had 1. Cor. 10, 5. add. Rom. 3, 23. That indeed also in this place the particle γδ is so accepted, that is, it does not denote a cause of the thing, but of the consequence (for the cause of eternal life is not expressed here, but the quality of those who are to be called to the kingdom of heaven,) is clear from the reasons brought forward before. Compare more things making for this in B. Par. Confess. Cathol. t. 4. p. 877. seqq. Nor is there finally any reason that someone should say: How the particle γὰρ is accepted in v. 42, in the same way it is accepted here. But in v. 42 it is accepted causally, therefore it ought to be accepted in this way here too. For the consequence is denied, since the reason for good works is one thing, and evil works is another. For these are perfectly evil, but those are not perfectly good. See Es. 64, 6. Iacobi 2, 10.) *

Latin:

v. 35. Esurivi enim &c. Rabbini dicunt: Proprietates DEI sunt, vestire nudos, visitare aegrotos, solari lugentes, sepelire mortuos. Unde ambulare post eum dicitur, qui talia facit. Vid. lib. Musar f. 120. pag. 1. Coeterùm nequaquam h. l. docetur, bona opera esse vitae aeternae meritoria, sed quòd Christus iudicaturus sit secundùm opera, & iis, qui bona egerunt, bonum retributurus, quia opera sunt verae in Christum fidei testimonia, placent DEO propter Christum: unde etiam ex gratiâ DEUS ea remuneratur. *(Cur verò in descriptione iudicialis processûs duntaxat opera misericordiae, & quidem corporalis, enumerentur, praetermissis reliquis fidei fructibus, & effectis, illius rei causa non est (ut quidem S. Augustinus l. 21 de C. D. c. 27. existimavit) quòd peccata reliqua illis potuerint expiari: Verùm, ut sicuti in praecedentibus sub parabolâ concreditorum talentorum Apostolos horumque in docendi officio successores, & alios in muneris eminentiâ constitutos sui admonuerat officii, ita hîc Christianos in universum omnes doceret, ab ipsis quoque exigendam esse aliquando rationem. Ut simus martyres, paucorum est; ut simus Doctores & columnae Ecclesiae, itidem paucorum est, At haustum frigidae aquae proximo sitienti praebere, nemo non potest. Atq; hunc esse genuinum praesentis loci scopum, prolixè ostendit B. Par. L. de Extremo Iudicio §. 56. Errant proinde Pontificii, statuentes, quòd Christus propterea bonorū operū in verbis processus iudicialis faciat mētionē, ut doceret, electis propter operū merita tanquā debit ā mercedē reddendā esse vitam aeternā. Vid. Bell. lib. 5. de Iustif. c. 3. & 7. Ribra de Templo l. 1. c. 21. p. 67. Barradius, Franc. Lucas, Iansenius in h. l. Costerus in Enchir. Controv. p. 276. Hagerus in Coll. A. C. & Concilii Trident. p. 88. alii. multò adhuc magis, qui statuunt, ceu Vasquez & Pighius ita docere commemorantur, propterea beatis paratum esse regnum coelorum â mundi constitutione, quia piè victuri erant in hoc seculo. Verùm, at iam nunc taceamus, quòd Christus hîc nō exponat causam, quare electis paratum sit regnū, sed indicet saltem signa, è quibus cognita fuerit fides eorum, qui ingredi regnum DEI iam debeant. opponimus errori huic Pontificiorum 1. fidei analogiam. Etenim Scriptura Sacra nullibi docet, quòd propter opem Christus daturus nobis sit vitam aeternam. sed hoc saltem testatur, quòd secundùm opera vel secundùm operum testimonia sit iudicaturus. Vid. Anal. ad c. 16. v. 27. Erit enim iudicium visibile & audibile. Bona proinde opera ut testimonia fidei, quae alias non immediatè patet, sed ex fructibus suis cognoscitur, adducentur. Manet igitur, quòd sententia ferenda fundamentaliter fidem & incredulitatem, signotenus externam cognitionem secundùm opera respiciat. B. D. Hutterus in Explan. F. C. p. 366. non immeritò commendat regulam in sacris litteris fundatissimam, & ad plurima Sc. S. dicta rectè intelligenda utilissimam, quòd nempè in Sc. S. frequenter effectibus fidei, hoc est, bonis operibus, adscribatur beatitudo, salus, perfecta iustitia, vita: quae tamen propriè & unicè causae efficienti adscribi debeant. Causa vero huius rei, eodem monente, est 1. quia ex effectibus, tanquam testibus, de causa, hoc est fide, Scriptura fieri iudicium vult. 2. quia DEUS bona opera non in hâc modò vitâ variis beneficiis compensat, sed etiam in futura maioribus gloriae gradibus exornabit. Sed utrumque non ex debito sive merito, vel congrui vel condigni: Verùm duntaxat gratis propter promissionem factam, non bonis nostris operibus, quae naturâ suâ sunt debita, imperfecta, polluta, sed fidei. Atque ex allatâ modò regula solvi possunt argumenta Pontificiorum, quae ex dictis, Psal. 1, 1.Ps. 15, 1. seqq. Psal. 41, 2.Es. 1, 16. 17. 18.Ezech. 18, 9.17. 18. & 19. Ioelis c. 2, 32. Ionae 3, 10. suprà c. 5, 9. 12. c. 10, Lucae 7, 47.c. 11, 41.Ioh. 5, 29.c. 13, 17.c. 14, 21.Rom. 2, 6. 7. & 8.1. Cor. 3, 8. &c. pro B. O. meritis formare solent. Conf. etiam in hanc rem P. D. Hafenrefferus LL. Theol. p. 685. 825. addi quoque possunt Anal. ad c. 16, 27. Opponimus Pontificiorum errori. 2. sententiam Christi definitivam. vocat electos benedictos Patris sui, videl. in ipso verâ fide apprehenso, Gal. 3, 9. 10.14.Eph. 1, 3. non autem benedicentes se in operum suorum meritis. dicit praeterea κληρονομήσατεhaereditatē accipite, ut filii nempe, Ioh. 1, 12.Gal. 3, 26. Iam vero merces servilis differt ab haereditate filiali. Conf. Rom. 8, 17.Gal. 3, 18.1. Petr. 1, 4. &c. Notanter Theophylactus in h. l. Sanctos vocat benedictos, ut à Patre susceptos. Haeredes autem ipsos facit regni. Ostendens, quòd DEUS eos participes faciat regni sui, ut filios suos. Non enim dixit, accipite, sed possidete regnum in haereditatem, ut paternam substantiam. Similiter. Fulgentius l. 1. de Praedest. ad Monimum: Sed & hoc ipsum opus est gratiae. Ex gratiâ enim datur non solùm iustificatis vita bona, sed etiam glorificatis vita aeterna. 3. adsertionem Apostoli contrariam,Rom. 6, 23. Etenim si vita aeterna est τοῦ σθεοῦ χάρισμαdonum DEI gratuitum, non erit operum nostrorum meritum. Conf. etiam. Rom. 3, 28.c. 11, 6.Gal. 2, 16.Eph. 2, 8. 9.Philipp. 3, 9.Tit. 3, 5.2. Tim. 2, 28. Chrysostomus hom. 80. postquam recensuisset, quòd damnati ob intermissa misericordiae opera iure puniātur, concludit: His igitur rationibus & isti non iniuriâ puniuntur, & illi (à dextris stantes) etiamsi mille talia fecerint, per gratiam tamen coronantur. Gratiae namque omninò illa benignitas est, ut pro rebus minimis & vilissimis coeleste regnum & tantus honor tribuatur. 4. electionem gratuitam. Etenim: Quomodo sive propter quam causam aut meritum DEUS aliquos homines ab aeterno elegit sivesalvare decrevit, eodem modo sive propter eandem causam meritumque eosdem in tempore iustificat & salvat. Atqui propter, meritum Christi fide perseverante apprehensum DEUS homines ab aeterno elegit, non propter praevisa eorum opera. E. eosdem etiam non propter opera eorum propria, sed unicè propter meritum Christi, fide constanti apprehensum, eosdem in tempore iustificat & salvat. Consequentiam maioris propositionis probat voluntatis divinae immutabilitas, Num. 23, 19.Mal. 3, 6. Minorem Pontificii ipsimet concedunt, certè minimè negare velle, videri cupiunt, ceu cumprimis videre est ex Ioh. Malderi Episcopi Antverpiensis Consider. Decretorum Synodi Dordrechp. 9. seqq. Bell. l. 1. de Gr. & Lib. Art. c. 10. Sciendum proinde, quòd particula γὰρ non sit h. l. causalis, sed ratiocinativa: adducuntur enim à Christo opera non ut ποιητικὰ, sive ut causae efficientes meritoriae regni coelestis, sed ut σημαντικὰ, sive ut testimonia ac fructus verae fidei, interiùs in corde latentis. Dilectio enim, unde haec opera oriuntur, individua fidei comes est, Gal. 5, 6. Unde licet non requiramus opera misericordiae à salvandis, ut vitae aeternae meritum, haec enim gloria solius Christi satisfactioni debetur, requirimus tamen illa, ut verae fidei testimonium ac fructum. Confer plura apud B. D. Hulsem. in A. C. p. 205. B. Par. L. de extr. Iud. §. 57. item Dispp. Elencht. p. 1348. Quôd verò particulae כי,γὰρ, ὅτι &c. quia, enim, similesq; non semper in Script. S. sint causales, ultrò largitur Iesuita Maldonatus, in c. 8. v. 29. Iohannis p. 721. scribens: Haec vocula quia & quoniam non causam aliquando significare, innumer a vel in solis Psalmis exempla sunt. Loca inter alia sunt apud nostrum Evangelistam c. 6, 14. c. 7, 8. c. 16, 2. 3. Lucae 7, 471. Cor. 10, 5.1. Thess. 2, 17. 18.1. Tim. 13, 1.Ioh. 3, 14. Michael quoque Gislerus Clericus Romanus in Expos. cap. 3. Cant. Cantiv. 11. p. 472. frequenter in sacris observatam monet phrasin, quâ particula quia usurpetur pro alia particula, uti ideò, & nō tam causam significet, quàm effectum. Idem fatentur Iesuitae, Alfonsus Salmeron--. 1. p. 327. nec non Com. in Ep. ad Eph. c. 1. Dispp. 3. Iacobus item Tirinus tr. de Idiot. Ling. Ebr. & Graecae, Commentariis in V. ac N. T. praemisso, num. 12. p. 86. Sic Gregorius quoque Magnus lib. 6. epist. 22. Toletus ad Luc. 7, 42. Salmeron t. 1. p. 327. particulam quiaLuc. 7, 47. accipiunt, videl. quat. ex effectu colligitur causa, scil. ex dilectione remissio peccatorum. Simile exemplum habetur 1. Cor. 10, 5. add. Rom. 3, 23. Quòd verò etiam h. l. particula γδ ita accipiatur, hoc est, non denotet causam rei, sed consequentiae (neque enim causa vitae aeternae hîc exprimitur, sed qualitas eorum, qui ad regnum coeleste vocandi sunt,) patet ex antè allatis rationibus. Conf. plura huc facientia apud B. Par. Confess. Cathol. t. 4. p. 877. seqq. Nec est tandem, quòd aliquis dicat: quomodo particulaγὰρaccipitur v. 42. eodem modo & hîc accipitur. Atque v. 42. accipitur causaliter, E. & hîc accipi ita debet. Etenim negatur consequentia, cùm alia sit ratio bonorum operum, alia malorum. haec enim sunt perfectè mala, sed illa non perfectè bona. Vid. Es. 64, 6. Iacobi 2, 10.) *

## 25:36
* (v. 36. I was naked &c. Conf. Esai. 58, 7.Ezech. 18, 7.16.Tob. 1, 20.c. 4, 17. How much both the Jews and the Turks perform alms, and how much they bestow upon them, B. Hackspanius shows at length in his tract on the utility of Rabbinical reading, with the book Nizachon subjoined, p. 438.) *

* I was sick &c. Conf. Sirac. 7, 39.) *

* I was in prison. How greatly the men of the Mohammedan sect commend the liberation of captives is evident from their own Bibles, the Alcoran at their fingertips, from which Hackspan brings forward some things on this matter in the place cited, p. 439.) *

Latin:

* (v. 36. Nudus eram &c. Conf. Esai. 58, 7.Ezech. 18, 7.16.Tob. 1, 20.c. 4, 17. Quanti etiam tum Iudaei, tum Turcae eleemosynas faciant, quantumque illis tribuant, prolixè ostendit B. Hackspanius tract. de util. Lect. Rab. subiuncto lib. Nizachon p. 438.) *

* (Aegrotavi &c. Conf. Sirac. 7, 39.) *

* (In carcere eram. Quantopere Mohammaedanae sectae homines captivorum liberationem commendent, patet ex eorundem Bibliis, Alcoranum in digito, è quo nonnulla in hanc rem adfert Hackspan. l. c. p. 439.) *

## 25:37
* (v. 37. When did we see you hungry &c. And yet the pious know that those things which they have performed for the ministers of Christ or for those believing in Christ, those needy and afflicted ones, Christ wishes to accept as if they had been performed for himself. see above c. 10, 40. following c. 18, 5. Mark 9, 37.41. Resp. The pious do not deny their good works, but humbly and deservedly acknowledge their imperfection, knowing well indeed that the greatest part of those things which they have done is the least of those things which they ought to have performed, Luke 17, 10. Conf. Ps. 65, 4. item Psalm 130, 3.Ps. 143, 2.Job 9, 2.Rom. 7, 16. That which is well to be noted against the Papist Justiciaries. It is indicated, however, at least by those words or by this discourse, that the pious will admire the goodness of Christ. For it is not to be thought that on the last day a lengthy conversation is to be instituted.) *

Latin:

* (v. 37. Quando te vidimus esurientem &c. Atqui sciunt pii, quòd ea, quae Christi ministris sive credentibus in Christum, egenis illis afflictisque praestiterunt, Christus ita acceptare velit, ac si ipsi illi praestita fuissent. vid. suprà c. 10, 40. seqq. c. 18, 5. Marc. 9, 37.41. Resp. Non negant pii sua opera bona, sed eorum imperfectionem humiliter meritòq; agnoscunt, probè quippe scientes, quod maxima pars eorum, quae fecerunt, minima sit eorum, quae praestare debuerunt, Luc. 17, 10. Conf. Ps. 65, 4. item Psalm. 130, 3.Psal. 143, 2.Iobi 9, 2.Rom. 7, 16. Id quod probè notandum contra Iustitiarios Pontificios. Indicatur autem saltem illis verbis sive hoc discursu, pios admiraturos esse Christi bonitatem. Noque enim existimandum est, in die extremo prolixum instituendum esse colloquium.) *

## 25:40
v. 40. One of these my brethren &c. Chrysostom in this place exclaims: O the goodness of Christ! As long as He was in this world, in a contemptible body, because of the visible likeness He could easily call us His brethren: But now, when He is established in such great glory and majesty, He still deigns to honor us with the title of brethren, for whom it would suffice for praise, if He even called us good servants. * (Also relevant to this is that statement of Cyprian in his treatise on Almsgiving: What greater thing could Christ declare to us? How could He more provoke the work of our justice and mercy, than by saying that whatever is provided to the needy and the poor is provided to Himself? So that he who is not moved by the regard of a brother in the Church, and he who does not think of his fellow-servant in labor and poverty, may think of the Lord Himself, established in that very person whom he despises. And to this also refers Salvian in book 3 against Avarice, p. 90, edition of Rittershus, when he calls the poor and needy Christ's money-changers, because money committed and entrusted to such, or dispensed to them, is increased, and with interest, he says, is without doubt rendered by GOD, whatever is distributed to the needy. Compare more things relevant to this in Salvian, in the said place. On the same matter Chrysologus writes in sermon 40: He will see an evil day, who enters the day of judgment without the advocacy of poverty. He who lends to the poor has made the Judge Himself his debtor. The foundation of that sentiment, however, is that Christ is the spiritual head of His Church, and the pious are the members. See Eph. 1, 22. 23.c. 4, 15. 16.c. 5, 23.30. or also that Christ is the bridegroom, and the Church or the pious are the bride. It can also be considered that Christ names the pious in this way having regard to His incarnation Heb. 2, 10. and our spiritual regeneration and adoption. John 1, 12. and then also because of His singular love, compare below c. 28, 19. John 20, 17.) *

To the least. so called 1. because of their zeal for humility. 2. because of their contempt in the world. Let Origen be compared.) *

Latin:

v. 40. Uni de his fratribus meis &c. Chrysostomus h. l. exclamat: ô bonitas Christi! quamdiu erat in hoc mundo, in corpore contemtibili, propter similitudinem visibilem nos appellare fratres suos facilè potuit: Nunc autem quando in tantâ gloriâ & maiestate, constitutus adhuc dignatur nos titulo fratrum, quibus ad laudem, sufficeret, si vel bonos servos vocaret. * (Spectat quoque huc illud Cypriani tr. de Eleemosynâ: Quid potuit nobis maius Christus edicere? quomodo potuit magis iustitiae ac misericordiae nostrae operam provocare, quàm quòd praestari id dixit sibi, quicquid egenti praestatur & pauperi? ut qui respectu fratris in Ecclesiâ non movetur, & qui non cogitat in labore & egestate conservum, vel Dominum, cogitet, in illo ipso quem despicit, constitutum. Atque huc respicit etiam Salvianus l. 3. contra Avaritiam p. 90. edit. Rittershus. quando pauperes & egenos Christi numularios vocat, quia pecunia talibus commissa ac concredita sive illis dispensata, augetur, & cum usuris, ait, absque dubio à DEO redditur, quicquid egentibus erogatur. Conf. plura huc facientia apud Salvianum, d. l. In eandem rem Chrysologus serm. 40. Videbit, scribit, diem, malum, qui diem iudicii sine advocatione paupertatis intrarit. Qui foenerat pauperi, ipsum sibi iudicem praestitit debitorem. Fundamentum autem sententiae illius est, quòd Christus Ecclesiae suae spirituale caput, pii membra. vid. Eph. 1, 22. 23.c. 4, 15. 16.c. 5, 23.30. vel etiam quòd Christus sponsus, Ecclesia sive pii sponsa. Potest quoque cogitari, quòd Christus pios ita nominet respectum habens ad suam incarnationem Ebr. 2, 10. ac spiritualem nostram regenerationem & adoptionem. Ioh. 1, 12. tum etiam ob singularem dilectionem, conf. infrà c. 28, 19. Ioh. 20, 17.) *

* (Minimis. dicti ita 1. ob humilitatis studium. 2. ob eorundem in mundo contemtum. Conferatur Origenes.) *

## 25:41
v. 41. Then also to those who are on the left. To this point refer those things which Drusius reports from Moses of Coucy in the great book of precepts 186. col. 2., cited above at v. 33. near the end. * (

* (Cursed. He does not say as he had said before blessed of the Father, so also here he says, cursed of the Father. For indeed GOD is the author and administrator of blessing, but each one has become the author of his own curse, who performs things worthy of a curse. As Origen well advises in this place. To whom, Chrysostom conforms: The Lord will say to the impious: Go you cursed, not indeed from the Father: for he himself did not, but their own works cursed them. If therefore GOD is not the cause of the curse of the impious, much less will he be the cause of the unbelief or of the sins, on account of

which the impious will be condemned. It will also be false, that he reprobated the greatest part of men out of a certain absolute hatred.) *

Into eternal fire. It is manifest that hell-fire is called eternal, not from the time before, but from the time after. Augustine refutes Origen, who taught the liberation of devils and the impious from hell, from this passage, because in one and the same sentence, both punishment and life are called eternal. Therefore, either both will endure with an end, or both will be perpetual without an end. * (Compare more things pertaining to this in the *Analecta* on Mark 9:43, 44.) * * Q. 1. How can hell-fire be said to be prepared for the devils, when a corporeal fire cannot act upon them, as they are spirits? Resp. There are those who posit that hell-fire is incorporeal, invisible, and devoid of all matter.

* (Of the devils Q. 1. how can the infernal fire be said to be prepared for the devils, when, as they are spirits, corporeal fire cannot act upon them? Resp. There are those who posit that that infernal fire is incorporeal, invisible, and devoid of all matter. 2. Others, although they do not deny that that fire will be corporeal, nevertheless hesitate to affirm this for certain, since in Holy Scripture this has not been clearly revealed. Augustine is of this opinion in book 20 of The City of God, chapter 16. 3. It seems that a distinction must be made between infernal fire, considered by reason of itself, and by reason of the principal agent, of which it is an instrument. Therefore, even if that fire were in the highest degree corporeal, and thus by reason of itself would not be apt to act upon the devils, as they are spirits; yet, insofar as it is an instrument of divine justice, it can certainly act even upon spirits, since any instrument, besides the power inherent in itself, also obtains another certain power from the principal agent. Thus, not only our own people posit this, but also the Papists. See Tanner, Scholastic Theology, vol. 1, Disputation 5, question 6, Dubitation 6, number 16. Hence 4. just as the souls of the wicked, although they are immaterial, will by no means be immune from infernal torments, but with the body afflicted they themselves also will be tormented: so by divine power it can happen, and indeed it does happen, that separated souls also, even before they are reunited with their bodies, and thus also the devils, may feel infernal torments, as the Blessed Pareus shows at greater length in his Isagogic Collections, Book on Evil Angels, chapter 3, § 9; likewise in his Theological Commonplaces, Book on Hell, § 98. Q. 2. Does not the eternity of infernal punishments conflict with the mercy of GOD, likewise with the divine promise, that GOD does not wish to be angry forever, Jer. 3:12 Conf. Ps. 77:8, 9, 10 Resp. I distinguish 1. between the objects of divine mercy, which are not the damned, or men persevering in their final unbelief to the end of life: but in the other life the blessed, and in this life repenting sinners. 2. between The time of this and of the future age is that of grace and mercy, this is of the just vengeance of GOD. To which pertain the sayings Is. 49, 8.Matt. 25, 10.2 Cor. 6, 2.Heb. 3, 13. Q. 5. Whether only adult unbelievers, that is, those who have died in impenitence, or indeed also infants who have died without having received Baptism, are to be subjected to infernal punishments? Resp. Bellarmine, book 6 on the loss of grace and the state of sin, ch. 5, §. Therefore, and other Papists commonly imagine, that unbaptized infants are indeed going to a place, around which is eternal fire, but not into the eternal fire itself. But before all things a distinction seems necessary, between infants born in the Church and offered to Christ through the prayers of the Church and of pious parents, and between infants born in heathendom. Concerning the former, the constant opinion of the Orthodox is (See Blessed Pareus, Disp. 4 on the Fundamentals of Consolation, §. 49 ff. L. on Baptism, §. 237 ff. L. on Circumcision, §. 15, on the sacraments in general §. 53. Mr. Dilherrus in a special dissertation on the blessedness of unbaptized infants. Blessed D. Schilterus in Chapters of pure and uncorrupted doctrine, etc., p. 485, who also bring forward the sayings of Augustine and Bernard, and even of the Scholastics, in support of this opinion.) that if they are deprived of the Sacrament of Baptism by some inevitable necessity, GOD, moved by the prayers of the Church and of pious parents, extraordinarily kindles faith in them, and thus renders them participants in eternal blessedness, no less than the baptized. Concerning which matter we have at some time treated in a special dissertation, and it will be treated at greater length in the Analecta on John 3, 5. and thus an extraordinary place or some dwelling is not to be imagined for them. But as far as it concerns the infants of the Gentiles, and those who have died in the maternal womb or in early infancy, there theologians go off into different parties, some πὸ ὲπέχειν think it safest here, since the Apostle himself, having been caught up to the third heaven, did not wish to determine anything certain about those who are outside (the Church), 1 Cor. 5, 12. which most take to refer to infants. For as regards adults in heathendom, who maliciously persevere in their unbelief, the Apostle would certainly not have hesitated to pass judgment on them according to the sentence of the Savior Mark 16, 16.. See Blessed D. Hulsemann, Brev. Extens. p. 239. Blessed Pareus, Academic Disputations p. 181. Which modesty of our theologians is to be well noted

is against the accusations of the Calvinists, as if by our doctrine concerning the necessity of Baptism the mercy of GOD were weakened. The Calvinists do this rather, who with entirely praetorian authority adjudge to the children of the gentiles, dying without Baptism in infant age, infernal fire. Just as Nicolaus Vedelius, Professor of Theology at Deventer, defends this opinion at greater length against the Arminians in the Preface to part 4 of the Arcana Arminianismi, Consid. p. 18. 19. Others extend the condemnatory sentence of Christ, in the cited manner, to them as well, for the reason that it is general, and excludes from salvation all who do not believe, and thus also condemns or adjudges to eternal damnation, and does not acknowledge a third state or place between the blessed and the damned, who feel infernal torments. They urge, therefore, that one or the other must be asserted, namely that they either believe or do not believe. If the former, they are to be saved; if the latter, they are to be damned. But damnation consists not only in the penalty of loss, but also in the penalty of sense. Finally, others, although they by no means deny original sin in infants, nor go so far as to deny that they are guilty of eternal damnation on that account, think nevertheless that, since the Church prays in the Litany that GOD may be willing to have mercy on all, who do not maliciously resist the means of salvation, and indeed such a thing cannot be affirmed concerning the children of the gentiles who died in infancy, it is not entirely improbable that GOD, regarding the infants of the gentiles also who died in early infancy, hears the prayers of the Church, has mercy on them, extraordinarily kindles faith in them, and thus saves them, as being believers. Concerning which matter we have adduced the opinion of the blessed D. Meisner elsewhere. It suffices for us that the limbo of children is a figment of the Papists and a shred of the other errors of the Papacy. Nor does the example of infants departing without Baptism compel us to admit such a limbo. Bellarmine indeed urges against the present passage, where mention is made only of hell and eternal life, that here is proposed at least the form of those to be judged who are in the Church; but since unbaptized infants, or those departing without baptism, do not belong to this, whence it was not necessary that mention of the place into which such are to be sent should be made in this place. But that the present form of judgment pertains only to those who are in the Church, the Cardinal attempts to prove both from Augustine against the Donatists after the conference, chapter 4, and other places, and That the good and the evil are compared to sheep and goats, who are numbered in the same flock of the same shepherd. But it is certain that such a flock is the Church, since infidels are compared to wolves, dogs, etc. he adds, that there was no need to describe in the Gospel the form by which infidels are to be judged, since it was enough to say in general, he who does not believe shall be condemned. But the Savior directly contradicts the Cardinal, who says in v. 32, all nations are to be gathered before Christ the Judge. That by those all nations all men whatsoever ought to be understood here, Chrysostom clearly teaches, who explains it by πᾶσαν τῶν ἀνσθρώπων φύσιν, that is, the universal nature of man. So also the Glossa interlinearis, and in complete agreement with it the Jesuit Emanuel Sa, all nations, that is, of every time, of every condition, of every sex, of every age. Augustine, however, in sermon 14 on the words of the Apostle, asserts in clear words that even infants are then to be judged: no, he says, middle place is left where you can place infants. What of the fact that the Jesuit Maldonatus writes in explicit words, that he answers with certainty and without any hesitation, that unbaptized infants will be on the left, just as on the right other infants, who are to be saved not on account of B. O. but on account of the grace of the Baptism received. As far as the opinion of Augustine is concerned, to which Bellarmine appeals, it must be known that he himself does not speak exclusively, but inclusively. It is truly strange that the Cardinal restricts goats only to the faithful or those who live in the Church, when Christ does not speak of a congregation which is made in this world or for the kingdom of grace, but which will be at the final judgment, from which congregation certainly no man will be excluded. That Gentiles or infidels are compared rather with dogs and wolves, than with goats, is frivolous. For they, just as much as sinners hiding in the bosom of the Church, can be compared with goats, just as heretics are accustomed to be compared with dogs and wolves by the Papists. And if specifically infidels can be compared with wolves, it follows that either all infidels, insofar as they are such, are to be killed, or the collection of the Jesuits, Coster in Enchir. C. 2. Ribaden. l. 1. de Prim. c. 26. p. 172. is frivolous, nay even that of Bell. himself de Laic. c. 21. from which, because heretics in Holy Scripture are compared with wolves, they collect, that they as such are to be visited with capital punishment. I pass over now the remaining things which Bellarmine brings forward quite ineptly, especially

while he presupposes, as if At least those who have faith are to be reproved by Christ in judgment, because they did not show the works of faith. item, not to be reproved because they did not have the right or true faith, but because they did not show the works of faith. As if indeed he had true faith who, without serious repentance, acted wickedly, since good works are the fruits of faith. Thus the hypothesis is also false, that infants born in the bosom of the Church, yet without baptism, of which they are deprived for some inevitable cause, departing from here, do not belong to the Church, since GOD has expressly promised that He wishes to be GOD to us and to our seed. But about this matter more prolixly elsewhere.) *

He who is prepared for the Devil &c. Irenaeus lib. 3. c. 35. p. 223. Saying to those on the left: Depart &c. he signifies that the eternal fire is not prepared primarily for man, but for him who seduced and caused man to offend. For him, I say, who is the prince of apostasy, the prince of withdrawal, and for those angels who became apostates with him. Which indeed those also will justly receive who similarly like them persevere in the works of malice without repentance and without return.

Latin:

v. 41. Tunc & eis, qui â sinistris. Huc spectant, quae Drusius ex Mose de Kotsi in libro magno praeceptorum 186. col. 2. refert, adducta supra ad v. 33. circa finem.

* (Maledicti. non sicut antè dixerat benedicti Patris, ita & hîc dicit, maledicti Patris. etenim benedictionis autor & administrator DEUS est, maledictionis autem sibi unusquisque autor extitit, qui maledictione digna operatur. Uti benè Origenes in h. l. monet. Cui, conformiter Chrysostomus: Impiis dicet Dominus: Ite maledicti, non quidem â Patre: non enim ipse, sed opera eis propria maledixerunt. Si igitur DEUS non est causa maledictionis impiorum, multò minùs incredulitatis seu peccatorum, propter

quae impii damnabuntur, causa erit. falsum quoque erit & hoc, quòd ex absoluto quodam odio maximam hominum partem reprobarit.) *

In ignem aeternum. Manifestum est, ignem infernalem vocari aeternum, non â parte ante, sed â parte post. Origenem, diabolorum & impiorum ex inferno liberationem docentem, Augustinus ex h. l. refellit, quia in unâ eademque sententia, & poena & vita dicitur aeterna. aut ergo utrumque cum fine duraturum, aut utrumque sine fine perpetuum futurum. * (Conf. plura huc facientia in Analect. ad Marc. 9, 43. 44.) *

* (Diabulis Q. 1. quomodo ignis infernalis paratus possit dici diabolis, cùm in ipsos, utpote spiritus, ignis corporalis non possit agere? Resp. Sunt, qui ignem illum infernalem incorporeum, invisibilem, omnisque materiae expertem statuunt. 2. alii licet non negent, ignem illum corporeum fore, haerent tamen id certò affirmare, siquidē in Scriptura S. hoc non clarè revelatum sit. In hac sententia est Augustinus l. 20. de C. D. c. 16. 3. Videtur distinguendum inter ignem infernalem, consideratum ratione sui, ac ratione principalis agentis, cuius est instrumentum. Quod si igitur vel maximè ignis ille corporeus esset, adeoque ratione sui non aptus esset agere in diabolos, utpote spiritus. quatenus tamen est instrumentum divinae iustitiae, utique etiam in spiritus agere potest, cùm quodvis instrumentum praeter vim sibi insitam, aliam quandam etiam sortiatur ab agente principali. ita non solùm nostrates statuunt, sed etiam Pontificii. vid. Tannerus Theolog. Scholast. t. 1. Disp. 5. q. 6. Dub. 6. n. 16. Proinde 4. quemadmodum impiorum animae licet sint immateriales, hautquaquam tn. â cruciatibus infernalibus immunes futurae erunt, sed corpore afflicto ipsi quoque cruciabuntur: ita per divinam potentiam fieri potest, fit imò, ut animae quoque separatae sive priusquam corporibus suis reduniantur, & sic quoque diaboli cruciatus infernales sentiant, ceu pluribus ostendit B. Par. Coll. Isag. L. de Angelis malis c. 3. § 9. it. LL. Theol. L. de Infern. §. 98. Q. 2. Annon aeternitas suppliciorum infernalium pugnet cum misericordia DEI, item cum promissione divina, quòd DEUS non velit in aeternum irasci,Ierem. 3, 12.Conf.Ps. 77, 8. 9. 10. Resp. disting. 1. inter misericordiae divinae obiecta, quae non sunt damnati sive homines in finali suâ incredulitate ad finem vitae perseverantes: sed in alterâ vita beati, in hâc verò peccatores resipiscentes. 2. inter tempus huius & futuri seculi illud est gratiae & misericordiae, hoc iustae DEI vindictae. quò faciunt dicta Es. 49, 8.Matth. 25, 10.2. Corinth. 6, 2.Ebr. 3, 13. Q. 5. Num solùm adulti increduli, h. e. qui in impoenitentia demortui sunt, an verò etiam infantes absque suscepto Baptismo defuncti suppliciis infernalibus, subiiciendi? Resp. Bell. l. 6. de amiss. grat. & statu pecc. c. 5. §. Itaque, aliique Pontificii communiter fingunt, quòd infantes non baptizati ituri quidem sint in locum, circa quem est ignis aeternus, non verò in ipsum ignem aeternum. Verùm ante omnia dist. videtur, inter infantes in Ecclesia natos ac per preces Ecclesiae & piorum parentum Christo oblatos, & inter infantes in gentilismo natos. De illis constans est Orthodoxorum sententia (Vid. B. Par. Disp. 4. de Fundam. Consol. §. 49. seqq. L. de Bapt. §. 237. seqq. L. de Circumcis. §. 15. de sacram. in genere §. 53. Dn. Dilherrus in pecul. dissert. de beat. Infant. non baptiz. B. D. Schilterus in Capp. purae & incorr. doctrinae &c. p. 485. qui etiam in hanc sententiam adducunt dicta Augustini & Bernhardi, quin & Scholasticorum.) quòd si ex inevitabili quadam necessitate Sacramento Baptismi priventur, DEUS precibus Ecclesiae ac piorum parentum, motus extraordinariè in illis fidem accendat, adeoque aeternae beatitudinis, non minùs ac baptizatos participes eos reddat. quâ de re in peculiari dissertatione aliquādo egim-, ac pluribus etiam agetur in Analect. ad Ioh. 3, 5. adeoque non fingendus extraordinarius pro illis locus vel habitatio quaedā est. Quod verò gentilium infantes, eosque in utero materno vel in primâ infantia defunctos concernit, ibi in diversas Theologi abeunt partes, nonnulli πὸ ὲπέχειν tutissimum hîc putant, cùm ipse Apostolus ad tertiū eosq;coelū evectus noluerit certi quid determinare de iis, qui extra (Ecclesiam) sunt, 1. Cor. 5, 12. id quod de infantibus plerique accipiunt. quod enim adultos in gentilismo attinet, qui malitiosè in suâ incredulitate perseverant, de illis utique nō dubitasset Apostolus ex sententiâ Salvatoris Marc. 16, 16. iudicium ferre. vid. B. D. Hulsem. Brev. Extens. p. 239. B. Par. Dispp. Acad. p. 181. Quae nostratiū Theologorum modestia probè notanda

est contra Calvinianorum accusationes, quasi per doctrinam nostram de Baptismi necessitate DEI misericordia labefactetur. Calviniani potiùs hoc faciunt, qui praetoriâ omninò autoritate gentilium liberis, absque Bapt. in infantili aetate decedentibus ignem adiudicant infernalem. quemadmodum sententiam hanc prolixiùs contra Arminianos defendit Nicolaus Vedelius, Theol. Profess. Davent. in Praefat. ad part. 4. Arcan. Arminianismi, Consid. p. 18. 19. Alii ad ilios quoque extendunt damnatoriam Christi sententiam, modo allegato, eò quòd illa generalis sit, & â salute excludat, omnes qui non credunt, adeoque etiam damnet seu aeternae damnationi adiudicet, tertium verò sive statum seu locum inter beatos, & damnatos, qui cruciatus sentiunt infernales, non agnoscat. Urgent igitur, quòd alterutrum adserendum, nempe quod vel credant, vel non credant. Si illud, erunt salvandi; sin minus, damnandi. Consistit vero damnatio non solùm in poena damni, sed etiam in poenâ sensùs. Alii denique licet minimè peccatum originis in infantibus negent, nec inficias eant, reos propterea illos esse aeternae damnationis, existimant tn., quòd, cùm Ecclesia in Litania oret, ut DEUS omnium velit misereri, qui np. non malitiosè salutis mediis repugnant, & verò de gentilium liberis in infantiâ defunctis tale quid affirmari nequeat non prorsus improbabile sit, DEUM quoad gentilium quoq; infantulos, in primâ infantiâ defunctos, Ecclesiae preces exaudire, illorum misereri, fidem in illis extraordinariè accendere, adeoq; eosdem, utpote credentes, salvare. quâ de re B. D. Meisneri sententiam alibi adduximus. Nobis sufficit, limbum puerorum esse figmentum Pontificiorum ac laciniam coeterorum Papatùs errorum. nec exemplum infantium absq; Bapt. discedentium nos, ut talem limbum admittamus, cogere. Urget quidem contra praesentem locum, ubi tantùm inferni & vitae aeternae fit mentio, Bellarminus, quòd hî proponatur saltem forma iudicandorum, qui sunt in Ecclesia; ad hanc verò cùm infantes non baptizati, sive absque baptismo discedentes, non pertineant, unde nec loci, in quem tales mittendi sint, h. l. mentio ut fieret, necesse fuerit. Quòd verò praesens iudicii forma ad eos tantùm pertineat, qui in Ecclesia sunt, probare conatur Cardinalis tum ex Augustino contra Donat. post collat. cap. 4. aliisq; locis, tum quòd boni & mali comparentur ovibus & haedis, qui in eodem grege eiusdem pastoris numerantur. talem verò gregem constat esse Ecclesiam, cùm infideles conferantur lupis, canibus, &c. addit, non opus fuisse, in Evangelio describere formam, quâ iudicandi infideles, cùm satis fuerit dicere in genere, qui non crediderit, condemnabitur. Verùm directè Cardinali contradicit Salvator, qui dicit v. 32. omnes gentes congregandas ante Christum Iudicem. quòd verò per illas omnes gentes omnes omninò homines intelligi hîc debeant, clarè docet Chrysostomus, qui exponit per πᾶσαν τῶν ἀνσθρώπων φύσιν, id est, universam hominum naturam. Sic quoque Glossa interlinearis, eique prorsus consentaneè Iesuita Emanuel Sa, omnes gentes, id est, omnis temporis, omnis conditionis, omnis sexûs, omnis aetatis. Augustinus verò serm. 14. de verbis Apost. perspicuis verbis etiam infantes tum iudicandos asserit: nullus, inquit, relictus est medius locus, ubi ponere queas infantes. Quid quòd Iesuita Maldonatus exsertis verbis scribat, se certum & minimè haesitantem respondere, infantes non-baptizatos ad sinistram futuros, sicut ad dextram alios infantes, qui non propter B. O. sed propter suscepti Baptismi gratiam salvandi sunt. Quod Augustini sententiam concernit, ad quam Bellarminus provocat, sciendum est, quòd ipse non loquatur exclusivè, sed inclusivè. Mirum verò est, quòd Cardinalis haedos tantùm ad fideles sive eos, qui in Ecclesia vivunt, restringat, cùm Christus non loquatur de congregatione, quae in hoc mundo sive ad regnum gratiae facta, sed quae in extremo demum iudicio futura, à quâ sanè congregatione nemo hominum erit exclusus. Quòd gentiles sive infideles potiùs cum canibus cōparentur ac lupis, quàm cum haedis, frivolum est. Etenim & illi aequè ac peccatores in Ecclesiae gremio latentes, cum haedis comparari possunt, quemadmodū haeretici cum canibus & lupis conferri à Pontificiis solent. Et si specialiter infideles, cum lupis conferri possunt, sequitur, quòd aut omnes infideles, quatenus tales interficiendi sint, aut frivola sit collectio Iesuitarum, Costeri in Enchir. C. 2. Ribaden. l. 1. de Prim. c. 26. p. 172. quin ipsius Bell. de Laic. c. 21. quâ exinde, quòd haeretici in Sc. S. cum lupis conferuntur, colligunt, eos ut tales capitali supplicio esse afficiendos. Mitto iam reliqua, quae Bellarminus satis ineptè adducit, cumprimis

dum praesupponit, quasi saltem ii, qui fidem habent, à Christo in iudicio redarguendi sint, eò, quòd fidei opera non ostenderint. item, non reprehendendos, quòd rectam sive veram fidem non habuerint, sed quòd fidei opera non ostenderint. Quasi verò ille veram fidem habuerit, qui absque seriâ poenitentia malè operatus fuit, cum B. O. sint fructus fidei. Sic falsa est quoque hypothesis, quòd infantes in Ecclesiae gremio nati, absque baptismo tamen, quo ex inevitabili quadam causa privantur, hinc discedentes, ad Ecclesiam non spectent, cùm disertè DEUS promiserit, quòd velit esse DEUS noster ac seminis nostri. Sed hac de re alibi prolixiùs.) *

Qui paratus est Diabolo &c. Irenaeus lib. 3. c. 35. p. 223. Dicens ad sinistros: Abite &c. significat, quoniam non homini principaliter praeparatus est aeternus ignis, sed ei, qui seduxit & offendere fecit hominem. ei, inquam, qui princeps apostasiae est, principi abscessionis, & his Angelis, qui apostatae facti sunt cum eo. quem quidem iustè percipient etiam hi, qui similiter ut illi sine poenitentia & sine regressu in malitiae perseverant operibus.

## 25:42
* (v. 42. For I was hungry &c. Conf. Isaiah 58, 7. Ezech. 18. v. 7. Gravely Salvianus of Marseille lib. 4. against Avarice p. 153. after he had alleged the present saying, he adds: Where then are those who say that the Lord J. C. does not need the service of our gifts? Why does He commemorate that He Himself likewise hungers and thirsts and is cold? Let any of these answer, if He does not need, who testifies that He thirsts? I add something more, that Christ not only needs along with the others, but needs much more than the others. For in the whole number of the poor, the poverty of all is not one &c. Christ alone is the only one who begs in the universality of all the poor. (let the excellent opinion of Chrysost. also be seen in Rittershus. Comm. ad Salv. p. 535.) Conf. very many things there pertaining to this. This also pertains to that of Basil Conc. 4. on Almsgiving That bread which you keep with you belongs to the hungry; the silver which you have buried in the ground belongs to the needy. Therefore you afflict as many with injury as you do not help with your goods, while it is permitted. item of Ambrose serm. 81. It is no less a crime to take away from one who has, than when you can and abound, to deny those who are in need. Conf. similar things in Hieron. p. 110. which is to Hedibia, Augustine in Psalm. 147. item serm. 38 on the saints, and also lib. on faith to Peter c. 45. Chrysostom to the people of Antioch. Bernard ep. 42. Gregory the Great Pastor. care part. 3.

admonit. 21. whose words were in part adduced by B. P. Dispp. Elencht. on the Lord's Gospels p. 1339. Although indeed it is gathered from this place that unmercifulness, and thus sins, are the cause of damnation, it does not follow, however, that evil works are the adequate and proper cause of damnation. But rather that final unbelief alone is the adequate cause of damnation, the Orthodox rightly assert against the Papists and Calvinists, and that according to John 3, 18.36.Mark 16, 16. See B. P. Dispp. Isagog. Book on Predestination Ch. 6. §. 2. 3. Dispp. Elencht. on the Lord's Gospels p. 1342.) *

* (And you did not give to me. Chrysostom homily 80 on Matthew expresses this so pathetically: If I had been an enemy, would not those passions, namely, starvation, cold, chains, nakedness, sickness, have sufficed to bend and mitigate even the unmerciful? For these things can move even enemies. You, however, did not bestow these things upon a friend, I say a friend and Lord and benefactor. But we are broken seeing a dog usually starving, and we are sometimes moved by the starvation of wild beasts: you, however, are not moved when the Lord is starving, etc. It is indeed well to be noted that while Christ says that He was hungry in the needy and poor, He speaks not at all of superstitious poor, of which kind are the Capuchin Monks, nor of malicious ones, laboring under the disease of sloth; for nothing is to be given to these, lest they be confirmed in superstition and laziness. See Gen. 3, 19.1 Thess. 4, 11.2 Thess. 3, 7. 8. Sirach 12, 4. 5. 6. 7. ch. 7, 16. but Christ speaks of calamitous and sickly poor, to whom one must promptly succor. 1. because of GOD'S command. 2. because of spiritual kinship. 3. because the administration of temporal things is entrusted to us. 4. because of the most generous reward, here and above ch. 10, 42. Compare B. D. Chemnitius Harm Ev. p. 811, 1278. 1306. also part 2. LL. Theol. p. 149. following. Compare Ritterh. Lect. Sacr. p. 164. 166. B. Par. Dispp. Elencht. p. 1351. also Book on Political Magistrates § 228. and also Commentary on Deut. Ch. 15, 4.11. But concerning the restraining of able-bodied beggars, let Johannes Boterus be consulted, on the Politics of Illustrious Men book 4. chapter 5. Mr. Ahasv. Fritschius special treatise on able-bodied beggars. It must also be well considered, lest alms be distributed with a blind hand to the unworthy no less than to the worthy, as B. D. Bald. well warns in Comm. on Ep. Paul. p. 1355. 1356.) *

* (I was sick etc. compare Sirach 7, 39.) *

Cur & esurire se pariter & sitire & algere commemorat. ## 25:46
* (v. 46. And these shall go (the damned) into everlasting punishment. In Greek it is ἀπελεύσονται they shall be driven away. for it will not be permitted then to reply anything further, or to appeal to the Apostolic See. Furthermore, the blessed Par. LL. Theol. discourses at length concerning the eternity and atrocity of infernal punishments in §. 35. et seqq. item Dispp. Elencht. on the Dominical Gospels p. 1341. To this pertain especially the sayings of Isaiah 66. 24. Jer. 7. & 19.Hos. 13.Dan. 12.Sir. 18, 8.Apoc. 9. v. 6.c. 21, 1. but concerning the joy and incredible happiness of eternal life, the same B. P. L. treats in de vita aeterna §. 55. et seqq. Dispp. Elencht. page 1342. it. B. D. Schilterus in Capp. purae & incorr. doctrinae Christ. p. 1002. et seqq. B. D. Smuckius in Explic. dicti Matth. 25, 46. But especially the beatific vision of GOD commends the sweetness of eternal life: for from this vision results the love of the beloved, the praise of the praised, the eternal enjoyment of the praised. Elegantly also Bonaventura in diaet. c. 15. The saints shall rejoice because of the pleasantness of the place, which they shall possess; because of the pleasant society, in which they shall reign; because of the world, which they have despised; because of hell, which they have escaped.) *

From the fact, however, that mention is made of at least two receptacles, our people conclude that there is no Purgatory. Becanus objects in lib. 1. Manualis. c. 8. n. 61. by conceding, that after the day of the final judgment there will be only those two places; but now, just as also in the O. T. there are more. Resp. Holy Scripture also in this life shows no other than two ordinary receptacles of separated souls, as is evident from John 3, 16.36.cap. 5, 24.Luke 3, 36. For the time being, therefore, our opinion stands, that just as after this life there are given no other than two receptacles, namely eternal life and hell, so neither are more given now, until the Papists have proven more in the present age by clear sayings of Holy Scripture. But there are also many other arguments by which Purgatory is destroyed, which it is not the place here to recount. See B. D. Meisner in the two opuse. against Papist Indulgences, B. D. Gerlach. t. 2. Dispp. Disp. 28. B. D. Mentzer. in Anti. Pist. Disp. 12. B. Par. Confess. Cathol. l. 2. Spec. part. B. art. 9. Dispp. Elenchr. p. 1353. Dispp. Acad. p. 439. B. D. Chemnit. Exam. Concilii Trid. part. 3. p. 138. et seqq. The present statement of the Savior also strongly destroys the Photinian error concerning the annihilation of the devils and the damned, about which a little before at verse 41. For how, I ask, can those who have been reduced to nothing be said to endure eternal punishments? And no less is their error refuted by the present oracle, who have dreamed that the punishments of the damned will at some time have an end. For in no other sense are the punishments of the impious said to be eternal than the joys of the blessed. And this is said to be eternal in such a way, because it will never have an end. Therefore, the torments of the damned and the devils are said to be eternal in that sense. Notably Gregory the Great l. 4. dialog. c. 44. It is certain and doubtlessly true, that just as there is no end to the joy of the good, so there will be no end to the torment of the wicked. Nor does it conflict with the equity of divine justice that, on account of their temporal crimes, demons and damned men are punished with eternal torments. For since, according to the philosophers also (see Aristotle, book 5 of the Ethics), punishment is inflicted according to the dignity of him against whom the sin is committed. And indeed, demons and the impious have sinned against GOD the Best and Greatest, that is, against an infinite good; deservedly, therefore, they are compelled to sustain an infinite punishment. In the same way, the passion and death of Christ, although accomplished in a certain space of time, was of infinite value λύτρον, and thus a satisfaction for our sins, for which, however, we had deserved eternal death, on account of the dignity of the person suffering and dying. See B. P. L. de Iustif. §. 50. B. D. Grawer. Polem. Sacr. p. 678. Others add (see Gregory, in the place cited) that the damned have sinned infinitely, as much as is in them, since they always desire to live in sin, and also that they do not perform penance infinitely, dying as they do in their sins. St. Augustine, 12 de C. D. c. 11, urges that even human laws punish some with death for a great crime, which, although it may have been committed in a very brief space of time, the guilty party who is therefore afflicted with the punishment of death is nonetheless removed forever from the society of the living. Compare more on this matter in B. Par. L. de Inferno §. 60. item. Dispp. Elencht. super Evang. Domin. p. 1354.) *

Ex eo verò, quòd duorum saltem mentio fit receptaculorum, colligunt nostrates, non dari Purgatorium. Excipit Becanus lib. 1. Manualis. c. 8. n. 61. concedendo, post diem extremi iudicii duo tantùm fore ista loca; nunc verò, sicut etiam in V. T. plura esse. Resp. Script. S. etiam in hac vita non nisi duo ostendit receptacula animarum saparatarum ordinaria, ceu patet ex Ioh. 3, 16.36.cap. 5, 24.Luc. 3, 36. Tantisper igitur stat nostra sententia, quòd sicuti post hanc vitam non nisi duo dantur receptacula, vita nempe aeterna, & infernus, ita nec nunc plura dentur, dum Pontificii plura in praesenti seculo claris Scripturae Sacrae dictis probarint. Suppetunt vero & alia plurima argumenta, quibus Purgatorium. destruitur. quae non est huius loci recensere. Vide B. D. Meisnerum in duobus opuse. Indulgentiis Papist. oppos. B. D. Gerlach. t. 2. Dispp. Disp. 28. B. D. Mentzer. in Anti. Pist. Disp. 12. B. Par. Confess. Cathol. l. 2. Spec. part. B. art. 9. Dispp. Elenchr. p. 1353. Dispp. Acad. p. 439. B. D. Chemnit. Exam. Concilii Trid. part. 3. p. 138. seqq. Fortiter etiam praesens Salvatoris effatum destruit Photinianorum errorē de annihilatione diabolorum & damnatorum, de quo paullò ante ad vers. 41. Quî enim, quaeso, illi, qui in nihilū redacti sunt, supplicia aeterna perferre dici possunt? Nec minus refellitur praesenti oraculo eorum error, qui supplicia damnatorum finem aliquando habitura esse somniarunt. neque enim alio sensu impiorum supplicia aeterna dicuntur, quàm gaudia beatorum. Atque hoc ita aeternum dicitur, quia nunquam finem habiturum. E. & cruciatus damnatorum ac diabolorū eo sensu aeterni dicuntur. Notanter Gregorius M. l. 4. dialog. c. 44. Constat & incunctanter verum est, quia sicuti finis non est gaudio bonorum, ita finis non erit tormento malorum. Nec pugnat cum iustitiae divinae aequitate, ut propter temporalia sua scelera Daemones & homines damnati aeternis suppliciis puniantur. Etenim cùm secundùm Philosophos quoque (videatur Aristoteles lib. 5. Ethicorum) poena infligatur secundùm dignitatem eius, in quem peccatur. Et vero daemones atque impii in DEUM Opt. Max. hoc est in infinitum bonum peccarint, meritò quoque infinitam poenam sustinere coguntur. Ad eundem modum Christi passio ac mors licet certo temporis spatio peracta, fuit infiniti pretii λύτρον, adeoque satisfactio pro nostris peccatis, quibus tamen aeternam mortem eramus promeriti, propter personae nempe patientis ac morientis dignitatem. Vid. B. P. L. de Iustif. §. 50. B. D. Grawer. Polem. Sacr. p. 678. Addunt alii, (vid. Gregorium). M loco cit.) quòd damnati in infinitum peccarint, quantum nempe in se est, cum semper in peccato vivere cupiant, item quòd in infinitum non agant poenitentiam, morientes nempe in peccatis. S. August. 12. de. C. D. c. 11. urget, quòd etiam humanae leges morte aliquos mulctent pro grandi crimine, quod licet perbevi spatio commissum sit, reus tamen qui propterea mortis supplicio afficitur, in sempiternum aufertur de societate viventium. Conf. plura in hanc rem apud B. Par. L. de Inferno §. 60. item. Dispp. Elencht. super Evang. Domin. p. 1354.) *
