## 26:2
v. 2. That after b-d-ium the Passover will take place. Clement of Alexandria determines this to be the first Passover after the Baptism of Christ. Epiphanius in heresy 51 wishes it to be the third. But the Harmony of the Evangelists teaches it to be the fourth. The first is described Ioh. 2. in which Christ instituted the first reformation of the temple. The second is had Luc. 6. where the disciples going through the ripe crops pluck the ears of grain, and rub them with their hands. For that it was then the Passover is evident from this: 1. because the crops were ripe around the Passover, since on the second day of the Passover the Priests used to lift them up before the Lord. 2. because Luke calls it the Sabbath δευτρόπρωτον. for that cannot be anything other than the last of the Sabbaths of the unleavened bread: for that is the first day of the second week, just as Epiphanius also explains that word in the said place & since the Jews had no other feast around the time of the ripe crops, in which they continued several Sabbaths except the Passover, it is manifest that this History happened in the second feast of the Passover. The third Passover is that of which we read Ioh. 6. that the Lord satisfied five thousand with five loaves. For there it is added: now the Passover was a feast of the Jews. And this opinion concerning the four Passovers is confirmed by the analogy of the 70 weeks of Daniel. For Dan. 9. To the abrogation of the Levitical sacrifices, half of a week, that is, three and a half years, are attributed; but Christ, from the beginning of his ministry until his death, did nothing else than lead men from typical and Mosaic ceremonies to the victim of the New Testament, which he himself was about to offer to the eternal Father in his most sacred body. Gesnerus. Moreover, Josephus, book 3, chapter 10, says, that the feast of unleavened bread is celebrated for seven days, but in book 2, chapter 5, he says, that there are eight days of unleavened bread. Indeed, the evening of the feast day is sometimes attributed in Scripture civilly to the preceding day, and sometimes legally to the following feast day * (see Ribera, book 5, on the Temple, chapter 3, page 314, and following; but Gerardus Ioh. Vossius discourses at length on the number of years of Christ's ministry. Also Mr. Elias Taddelius in a special treatise on this matter.) *

CHAPTER XXVI. SUMMARY. I.

The Son of man shall be betrayed, on the very day of the Passover, as the true and only lamb of God, of which the Paschal lamb of the Old Testament was a type. * (In the Greek text it is the present tense, used for the future. But Christ speaks indefinitely or impersonally, nor does he express by whom he is to be betrayed. By which very thing, according to Origen, tract 35 on Matthew, he wished to signify that he was to be betrayed by various persons and in various ways. And indeed it cannot be denied that Christ was betrayed by various people and for various reasons. For the heavenly Father delivered his Son into death out of the highest mercy toward the human race to be redeemed, Rom. 5, 32. Christ delivered himself into death both out of holy obedience toward the Father, and out of the vehemence of love toward the human race, Gal. 2, 20. Eph. 5, 2. The Devil delivered him, when he put it into the heart of Judas that he should betray him, Ioh. 13, 2. out of envy. Judas out of avarice, Matth. 10, 4. c. 20, 18. c. 26, 15. 24. The chief priests, priests, and scribes out of wrath and envy, Matth. 20, 19. c. 27, 2. 18. Marc. 15, 1. Ioh. 18, 35. c. 19, 11. etc. Conf. Mr. D. Weller, Commentary on the Epistle to the Romans, page 514. Mr. D. Walter, H. B. page 1057. This betrayal done by Judas, the chief priests, priests, etc., is accustomed to be called active; just as that betrayal of Christ, that is, that he sustained himself to be betrayed into death by Judas and the priests, is passive. See B. P. H. Ev. chapter 172, page 1137. Conf. Hieron. in Epistle to Gal. c. 2, 20.

Meanwhile, Christ in this place speaks especially of the betrayal by which he himself was delivered by the priests and elders to Pontius Pilate, and by him to the soldiers so that he might be crucified. See B. P. Harm. Ev. chapter 166, page 942. Although indeed The handing over of Christ is attributed to the Father, and to Judas, and to the High Priests in Holy Scripture, yet this handing over is by no means to be considered in the same way. Since God handed over His Son without sin, mercifully, and judicially; but Satan and his instruments sinfully and wickedly, regarding which matter the blessed D. Fewerb. brings forward excellent passages from Augustine vol. 8 on Ps. 93 p. 433, act. 9 in the epistle 1 John c. 8 tr. 7 p. 57, Synt. 2 Dissert. Theol. p. 149, 150. Conf. B. D. Bald. on the Epistle to the Ephesians c. 5 part 1, 9, 1.) *

Latin:

v. 2. Quòd post b-d-ium Pascha fiet. Clemens Alexandrimus statuit. hoc esse primum Pascha post Christi Baptismum. Epiphanius haeresi 51. vult, esse tertium. Sed Harmonia Evangelistarum docet, esse quartum. Primum describitur Ioh. 2. in quo Christus primam templi reformationem instituit. Alterum habetur Luc. 6. ubi discipuli euntes per maturas segetes aristas vellunt, manibusque confricant. fuisse enim tunc Pascha, patet ex eo 1. quia fruges circa Pascha erant maturae, quandoquidem altero die Paschatis coram Domino levabant Sacerdotes. 2. quia Lucas vocat Sabbathumδευτρόπρωτον. id enim non potest esse aliud, quàm ultimum in Sabbatis azymorum: is enim secundae septimanae primus dies, est, sicut etiam vocem illam exponit Epiphanius d. l. & cùm Iudaei nullum aliud festum circa tempus maturarum frugum habuerint, in quo aliquot Sabbata continuaverint praeter Pascha, manifestum est, hanc Historiam in altero festo Paschatis evenisse. Tertium Pascha est illud, de quo legimus Ioh. 6. quòd Dominus quinque panibus quinque millia saturaverit. Ibi enim additur: erat autem Pascha festum Iudaeorum. Et hanc de quatuor Paschatis sententiam confirmat analogia 70. hebdomadum Danielis. Nam Dan. 9. abrogationi Leviticorum sacrificiorum dimidium hebdomadis i. e. anni sesquiquatuor tribuuntur, Christus autem ab exordio sui muneris usque ad mortem nihil aliud fecti, quàm quòd à typicis & Mosaicis ceremoniis ad victimam N. T. quam ipse in sacratissimo suo corpore aeterno Patri oblaturus erat, homines deduxit. Gesnerus. Coeterùm Iosephus l. 3. c. 10. dicit, festum azymorum per septem dies celebrari, lib. 2. verò c. 5. dicit, octo esse azymorum dies. Nimirum vespera diei festi modò attribuitur in Scriptura civiliter antecedenti, modo legaliter subsequenti diei festo * (vid. Ribera lib. S. de Templ. c. 3. p. 314. seqq. de numero verò annorum Ministerii Christi prolixè disserit Gerardus Ioh. Vossius. item Dn. Elias Taddelius in pecul. tract. de hac materiâ.) *

CAPUT XXVI. SUMMA. I.

Filius hominis tradetur, ipso se. Paschatis die, tanquam verus & unicus agnus DEI, cuius typus fuit agnus Paschalis V. T. * (In textu Graeco est praesens, positum pro futuro. Loquitur verò Christus indefinitè sive impersonaliter, nec exprimit, à quo fit tradendus. quo ipso, iuxta Origenem tr. 35. in Matth. significare voluit, quòd à variis personis & modis sit tradendus. Et sanè negari nequit, à variis idque varias ob causas Christum fuisse traditum. Etenim Pater c--lestis tradidit Filium suum in mortem ex summâ erga genus redimendum humanum misericordiâ, Rom. 5, 32. Christus tradidit se in mortem tùm ex sanctâ erga Patrem obedientiâ, tum ex amoris erga genus hum. vehementia,Gal. 2, 20.Eph. 5, 2. Diabolus tradidit, dum in cor Iudae immifit, ut traderet eum, Ioh. 13, 2.ex invidia. Iudas ex avaritiâ,Matth. 10, 4.c. 20, 18.c. 26, 15.24. Pontifices, Sacer dotes & Scribae ex iracundia & invidia, Matth. 20, 19.c. 27, 2.18.Marc. 15, 1.Ioh. 18, 35.c. 19, 11. &c. Conf. Dn. D. Weller. Comm. in Ep. ad Rom. p. 514. B. D. Walter. H. B. p. 1057. Haec à Iudâ, Pontificibus, Sacerd. &c. facta traditio dici solet activa; ceu illa Christi traditio, h. e. quat. se à Iuda & Sacerd. in mortem tradi sustinuit, passiva. vid. B. P. H. Ev. c. 172. p. 1137. Conf. Hieron. in Epist. ad Gal. c. 2, 20.

Interea Christus h. l. loquitur praecipuè de traditione, quâ ipse Sacerdotibus & Senioribus traditus fuit Pontio Pilato, & ab hoc militibus ut crucifi geretur. Vid. B. P. Harm. Ev. c. 166. p. 942. Licet vero traditio Christi & Patri, & Iudae, & Pontificibus in Sc. S. tribuatur, minimè tn. eodem traditio haec eodem consideranda modo est. cùm Deus Filium suum tradiderit impeccabiliter, misericorditer & iudicialiter; Satanas vero & organa eius peccabiliter & sceleriter, quam in rem egregia loca ex Augustino t. 8. super Ps. 93. p. 433. act. 9. in ep. 1. Ioh. c. 8. tr. 7. p, 57. adducit B. D. Fewerb. Synt. 2. Dissert. Theol. p. 149. 150. Conf. B. D. Bald. in Ep. ad Ephes. c. 5. part. 1. 9. 1.) *

## 26:3
v. 3. τότε συνήχθησαν at that very time, when Jesus had indicated to the disciples the day of His passion, namely two days before the Passover. Mark 14, 1.

Regarding this congregation, it was predicted by David Ps. 2, 2. and Ps. 41, 8. ) * * ( ὁι ἀρχιερεἶς |

* ( ὁι ἀρχιερεἶς etc. is understood as the Great Sanhedrin, about which it has been treated elsewhere. It is also gathered from this, that the visible and particular Church, such as the Roman one also is, can err. Although Nicodemus and Joseph did not consent to the counsel of the others, yet they remained hidden, nor perhaps dared they contradict the others: indeed, even if they had contradicted them most strongly, they would have been oppressed by the rest, who were powerful in multitude and authority. The same happens in the Councils which the Roman Pontiff convenes with his followers. Vainly, therefore, do Papists boast of the authority and infallibility of such Councils.) *

Occident. [The killing/betrayal] what one does through another, he is considered to have done himself. see above ch. 21, 38. Acts 3, 15. ) * * (

Latin:

v. 3. τότε συνήχθησαν eo ipso tempore, quo Iesus discipulis indicaverat diem suae passionis, biduo scil. ante Pascha. Marc. 14, 1.

* (De congregatione hac praedictum à Davide Ps. 2, 2. ac Ps. 41, 8.) *

* ( ὁι ἀρχιερεἶς &c. intelligitur Synedrium Magnum, de quo alibi actum. Colligitur quoque hinc, quòd Ecclesia visibilis & particularis, qualis etiam Romana est, possit errare. Licet verò Nicodemus & Iosephus non consenserint in consilium coeterorum, tamen ipsi latuerunt, nec fortè ausi fuerunt coeteris contradicere: quin si vel maximè contradixissent, à reliquis tamen, multitudine atque autoritate pollentibus fuissent oppressi. Idem in Conciliis quae Pontifex Romanus cum suis adseclis convocat, accidit. Vanè igitur talium Conciliorum autoritatem atq; infallibilitatem Papicolae iactitant.) *

* (Occident. quod quis per alium facit, ipse fecisse existimatur. vid. suprà c. 21, 38. Act. 3, 15.) *

## 26:5
* (v. 5. But they said, not in the feast, lest a tumult might arise. Beautifully no less than truly St. Jerome: they are not studying devotion, but crime. Otherwise, it was a custom received among the Jews that evildoers should be subjected to punishment near the time of the three solemn feasts, so that more people might be instructed by their punishments, as Paul Fagius notes on Deut. 17, 12. 13. Although the Great Sanhedrin did not want to subject Christ to punishment as the feast was approaching, for fear of the people adhering to Christ, GOD nevertheless directed this whole business in such a way that Christ, as the lamb who takes away the sins of the world, was sacrificed as the Passover was drawing near, both so that the type might be fulfilled, and also so that the most innocent passion and death of Christ, and likewise His most glorious resurrection, might become known to more people.) *

Latin:

* (v. 5. Dicebant autem, non in festo, ne fortetumultus fiat. Pulcrè nôn minùs quàm verè S. Hieronymus: non student devotioni, sed facinori. Aliàs more receptum apud Iudaeos fuit, ut in propinquo trium solennium festorum malefici supplicio afficerentur, quò plures nempe eorum poenis erudirentur, ceu notat Paulus Fagius ad Deut. 17, 12. 13. Licet vero Synedrium Magnum festo appropinquante Christum supplicio afficere nollet, metu populi Christo adhaerentis DEUS tamen ita totum hoc negotium direxit, ut Christus tanquam agnus, qui tollit peccata mundi, Paschato instante immolaretur, tum quò typus impleretur, tum etiam, quò Christi passio ac mors innocentissima itemq; resurrectio gloriosissima pluribus innote scerent.) *

## 26:6
v. 6. In the house of Simon the leper. Simon is called leper, even after the leprosy was healed, for that surname remained with him according to the rule of Jerome in this place: Sometimes in Scripture, the former name remains even when the condition is changed. * (Which rule is established by examples by B. D. Glassius in Gr. S. p. 8. 9. 10. Some are also accustomed to refer here Matth. 1, 6. τῆς τοῦ οὐρίου. ) * Chrysostom: The former name remained, so that the power of the healer might appear. Nicephorus book 1. Hist. c. 27. Simon the leper of Bethany received him into his hospitality, whom the apocryphal books openly hand down to have been the father of Lazarus.

* (But that it cannot be understood of a leprosy still present, is clear, because lepers were forbidden from the company of men, see Num. 5, 2. Moreover, the present history happened as it were six days before the feast of the Passover Ioh. 12, 1. where it is also mentioned that Lazarus was present.) *

Latin:

v. 6. In domo Simonis leprosi. Simon dicitur leprosus, etiam post sanatam lepram, cognomen enim illud ei remansit iuxta regulam Hieronymi in h. l. Aliquando in Script. mutatâ repristinum nomen manet. * (Quae regula stabilitur exemplis à B. D. Glassio in Gr. S. p. 8. 9. 10. Referri etiam huc à nonnullis solet Matth. 1, 6.τῆς τοῦ οὐρίου.) * Chrysostomus: Permansit pristinum nomen, ut virtus curantis appareat. Nicephorus l. 1. Hist. c. 27. Simon leprosus Bethaniae eum hospitio excepit, quem apocryphi libri patrem Lazari fuisse apertè tradunt.

* (Quòd verò non accipi possit de praesenti adhuc Ieprâ, patet, quia interdictum Ieprosis hominum commercio, vid. Num. 5, 2. Contigit autem Historia praesens ipsis quasi sex diebus ante Paschatos festum Ioh. 12, 1. ubi etiam memoratur, quòd Lazarus adfuerit.) *

## 26:7
v. 7. προῆλσθεν. Those who establish that this history is the same --my, which John describes c. 12, 1. which had happened on the sixth day before the Passover, translate this verb in the form of the pluperfect, he had come to him. * (Nor does it stand in the way that it is read in John: they made him a supper, and Martha was serving. for this is not to be understood as if Martha and Mary had prepared the banquet in their own house, as indeed Chrysostom and Euthymius wish: but in general, namely that the citizens of Bethany, friends of Christ, among whom the chief was Simon the leper, had received Christ with a banquet, and that Martha had served at this supper, whether because village--, or also because she was a relative and intimate to Simon: Thus expound Com. à Lapide, and several others.) *

* (A woman who is believed to have been the sister of Lazarus, Ioh. 11, 2.c. 12, 3. And so also H. Grotius establishes, who proves at length that this history is clearly the same as that which Ioh. c. 12. relates. But as for the history Luc. 7, 38. That one is different from her whom Matthew here & Iohannes c. 11. & 12. report, as the Lord Dr. Muller shows in many places in his Iudaismi p. 1367. The Biblical Glosses of the Ernestis also accept it as being about Mary, the sister of Lazarus.) * ἀλάβοαςρον or ἀλάβοαςρον * (a kind which Callimachus extolled in his hymn to Pallas. item in Latin Cic. lib. 2. Acad.) * a kind of ointment vessel, with a pointed length, ending in a fuller sphere, or of a turbinate shape without handles. It is called either παρὸ τὸ οὗ λάβεσθαι ἀδύνατον, because it is impossible to grasp on account of its smoothness, or διὰ τὸ μὴ λαβὰς ἔχειν, because it does not have handles. In both etymologies there is a pleonasm of the letter ς. Pliny l. 36. c. 8. They hollow out alabaster for ointment vessels, since it is said to preserve them incorrupt in the best way.

* (Let Grotius, the Lord Dr. Friedlieb, and others be seen here in this place, item the Lord Dilherrus Dispp. Acad. t. 1. p. 402. where many things pertaining to the present history are unearthed from antiquity.) *

* (Of ointment: From Ioh. 12, 3. it is gathered that it was of Spikenard, concerning the excellence of which see Pliny l. 13. C. 1. & 2. lib. 12. c. 17. Dioscorides l. 1. c. 6. The Blessed Dr. Quistorp presents many things on this matter at Marc, 14, 3) *

* (Upon the head. The same is also testified by Marcus c. 14, 3. but Iohannes c. 11, 2. and c. 12, 3. reveals that she anointed his feet. The position of one is not the exclusion or denial of the other. It is credible, however, that Mary first anointed the feet of Christ, afterwards broke the vessel, and poured all the ointment upon his head, with a huge affection of piety and veneration, see August. l. 2. de Consens. Evang. c. 79. It was however a custom among the Jews as the Psalmist also alludes to it Ps. 23, 5. item Ps. 141, 5. conf. also Cant. 1, 13. Sap. 2, 7. Ruth. 3, 3. Iudith. 10, 3. nor only among these, but among the Romans also, see Horat. lib. 2. Od. 7. item l. 3. Od. 29. item Pliny in the places cited a little before. Furthermore, just as Jacob Gen. 28, 18. poured oil upon the stone on which he had rested peacefully, so this woman poured ointment upon the rock of salvation, Christ, in whom she rested firmly.) *

Latin:

v. 7. προῆλσθεν. Qui statuunt, hanc historiam esse eandem --meâ, quam describit Iohannes c. 12, 1. quae sexto die ante Pascha contigerat, hoc verbum vertunt in plusquam perfecti formâ, venerat adeum. * (Nec obstat, quòd apud Iohannem legitur: fecerunt ei coenam, & Martha ministrabat. neque enim hoc ita intelligendum, quasi Martha ac Maria convivi-in in domo sua instruxerint, uti quidem Chrysostomus & Euthymius volunt: sed in genere, mempe quòd cives Bethaniae Christi amici, quos inter praecipuus erat Simon Ieprosus convivio Christum exceperint, quòd que Martha in coenâ hac ministraverit, sive quia vici--, sive etiam quia cognata ac familiaris erat Simoni: Ita exponunt Com. à Lapide, & alii nonnulli.) *

* (Mulier quae fuisse creditur Lazari soror, Ioh. 11, 2.c. 12, 3. Atque ita etiam statuit H. Grotius, qui planè eandem historiam hanc esse cum ea, quam Ioh. c. 12. refert, prolixè probat. Quod verò attinet historiam Luc. 7, 38. illa diversa est ab ea, quam Matthaeus hic & Iohannes c. 11. & 12. referunt, ceu multis ostendit Dn. D. Mullerus Iudaismi p. 1367. De Maria Lazari sorore accipiunt quoque Glossae Bibl. Er nestinorum.) * ἀλάβοαςρον vel ἀλάβοαςρον * (quo genere Callimachus in hymno in Pallada extulit. it. Latinè Cic. lib. 2. Acad.) * genus vasis unguentarii, longitudine fastigiata, in pleniorem orbem desinens, vel forma turbinata sine ansulis. Dicitur vel παρὸ τὸ οὗ λάβεσθαι ἀδύνατον, quod prehendere propter levorem est impossibile, vel διὰ τὸ μὴ λαβὰς ἔχειν, quod ansas non habeat. in utraque etymologia est pleonasmus litterae ς. Plinius l. 36. c. 8. Alabastriten cavant ad vasa unguentaria, quoniam optimè servare incorrupta dicitur.

* (Videantur hîc Grotius, Dn. D. Friedlieb, alii in h. l. item Dn. Dilherrus Dispp. Acad. t. 1. p. 402. ubi plurima ad praesentem historiam spectantia ex antiquitate eruuntur.) *

* (Unguenti: Ex Ioh. 12, 3. colligitur, fuisse ex Nardo, de cuius praestantia vid. Plinius l. 13. C. 1. & 2. lib. 12. c. 17. Dioscorides l. 1. c. 6. Multa in rem hanc exhibet B. D. Quistorp. ad Marc, 14, 3) *

* (Super caput. Idem testatur quoque Marcus c. 14, 3. sed Iohannes c. 11, 2. ac. c. 12, 3. prodit, quòd pedes unxerit. Unius positio, non est alterius exclusio s. negatio. Credibile autem est, Ma-iam priùs unxisse Christi pedes, postmodum vas f--gisse, omneque unguentum super caput eius effudisse, ingenti pietatis ac venerationis affectu, vid. August. l. 2. de Consens. Evang. c. 79. Fuit -autem hoc apud Iudaeos moris ceu eò alludit quoque Psaltes Ps. 23, 5. it. Ps. 141, 5. conf. etiam Cant. 1, 13. Sap. 2, 7. Ruth. 3, 3.Iudith. 10, 3. nec apud hos solùm, sed apud Romanos quoque, vid. Horat. lib. 2. Od. 7. it. l. 3. Od. 29. it. Plinius locis paulò antè citatis. Coeterùm sicuti Iacob Gen. 28, 18. lapidem, super quo placidè quieverat, oleo perfudit, ita mulier haec petram salutis Christum, in quo firmâ receubuit, unguento perfudit.) *

## 26:8
v. 8. But the disciples seeing. The plural number is placed for the singular: for this is commemorated particularly concerning Judas Ioh. 12, 4. It could, however, have happened that the rest followed his example. * (seduced, to wit, by Judas, hypocritically pretending that it could have been sold for much and spent on the poor. And thus Corn. Iansenius, Calvin, and others determine. August. mentions both expositions in book 2 de consensu Evang. c. 79. But that John made mention of Judas alone, it can be believed to have happened from this, that Judas was a thief, and seduced the others under the appearance of pity for the poor. The Jesuit Maldonatus considers this interpretation harder, and fromIohann. c. 12, 4.thinks it is manifest, that only Judas murmured. The same is determined by the ancients Jerome, Augustine, Chrysostom, Euthymius, Theophylact, Bede. Of the more recent ones, Thomas Gataker in Cinno s. Advers. Sacr. p. 341. But that that syllepsis, by which something is said of one as if of many, is not unusual in Holy Scripture, could perhaps be proven from our Gospel c. 4, 3. coll with Luc. 4, 3.c. 14, 15. coll with Ioh. 6, 8. item exc. 27, 44. coll. with Luc. 23, 39. thus also from Ioh. 6, 45.Act. 13, 40. similarly from the O. T. from Iud. 12, 7.c. 7, 10.2. Chron. 24, 25. coll. with v. 20. 21. item from 2. Chron. 28, 3. coll. with 2. Reg. 28, 3. It could also have happened that, just as Peter by his example moved the remaining disciples to trust too much in themselves, inf-à v. 37. so also Judas here had the remaining Apostles as supporters, although with a different intention.) *

* ( εἰς τι to what end. Hebraism ל מה. see Gen. 25. 22. & 32.Es. 1, 11.) *

To be sold for much.Ioh. 12, 5. it is said for three hundred denarii. Matthaeus Hostus in book 2 of ancient coinage c. 7 reduces the sum of three hundred denarii to thirty-seven and a half imperial thalers, namely with each denarius valued at an eighth part of a thaler. *(Isidorus Pelusiota book 2 p. 88 calls the ointment πολύτιμον μύρον. where he also explains at length the question, how Christ, when he otherwise commends alms, thus rebukes the disciples, who were urging the same.) *

Latin:

v. 8. Videntes autem discipuli. Numerus pluralis ponitur pro singulari: de Iuda enim hoc peculiariter commemoratur Ioh. 12, 4. fieri tamen potuit, ut reliqui eius exemplum sequerentur. * (seducti scil. à Iuda, hypocriticè praetexente, quòd multò venundari & in pauperes impendi potuisset. Atq; ita statuunt Corn. Iansenius, Calvinus, alii. Utriusq; expositionis meminit August. l. 2. de consensu Evang. c. 79. Quod verò Iohannes solius Iudae mentionem fecit, inde factum credi potest, quod Iudas fur fuerit, coeterosque seduxerit specie miserationis pauperum. Iesuita Maldonatus interpretationem hanc duriorem censet, & exIohann. c. 12, 4.manifestum esse putat, solùm Iudam murmur asse. Idem è veteribus statuunt Hieronymus, Augustinus, Chrysostomus, Euthymius, Theophylactus, Beda. è recentioribus Thomas Gataker in Cinno s. Advers. Sacr. p. 341. Quòd verò syllepsis illa, quâ de uno aliquid tanquam de multis dicitur, non insolens in Sc. S. sit. probari fortè posset ex nostro Evangelio. c. 4, 3. coll cum Luc. 4, 3.c. 14, 15. coll cum Ioh. 6, 8. it. exc. 27, 44. coll. cum Luc. 23, 39. sic quoq; ex Ioh. 6, 45.Act. 13, 40. similiter ex V. T. ex Iud. 12, 7.c. 7, 10.2. Chron. 24, 25. coll. cum. v. 20. 21. it. ex 2. Chron. 28, 3. coll. cum 2. Reg. 28, 3. Fieri quoque potuit, ut sicuti Petrus exemplo suo reliquos discipulos permovit, ut nimium sibi confiderent, inf-à v. 37. ita & Iudas hîc reliquos Apostolos habuerit adstipulators, quanquam animo diverso.) *

* ( εἰς τιad quid. Ebraismus ל מה. vid. Gen. 25. 22. & 32.Es. 1, 11.) *

Venundari multò.Ioh. 12, 5. dicitur trecentis denariis. Matthaeus Hostus lib. 2. rei nummariae veteris c. 7. summam trecentorum denariorum redigit ad thaleros imperiales triginta septem & dimidium, singulis sc. denariis aestimatis octava thaleri parte. *(Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 2. p. 88. unguentum vocat πολύτιμον μύρον. ubi etiam prolixè explicat quaestionem, quomodo Christus cùm aliàs eleemosynas commendet, sic discipulos, easdem urgentes, reprehendat.) *

## 26:9
v. 9. To be given to the poor. Add Deut. 15. but in the same place vers. 11.

it is read: There shall be no poor among you. Resp. it is understood: if you observe my law. see Gerund. on the said passage. (Others respond that this is of one commanding, that of one predicting. Looking to which, Tertullian, book 4 against Marcion, writes: But let there not be a needy person among you, i.e., take care of your own accord that there may not be, by which he the more prejudices the giving to the one asking even in the following: if there shall be a needy person etc.)

Latin:

v. 9. Dari pauperibus. Add. Deut. 15. at ibidem vers. 11.

legitur: Non erit pauper in te. Resp. subintell. si legem meam observaveris. vid. Gerund. ad d. l. * (Alii re spondent hoc esse praecipientis, illud praedicentis. Quò respiciens Tertullianus lib. 4 ad v. Marc. scribit: Sed non sit indigens in te i. e. cura ultrò ne sit, quo magis petenti praeiudicat dandum etiam in sequentibus: si fuerit indigens &c.) *

## 26:10
(v. 10. She has done a good work. Isidore of Pelusium, book 2, p. 88, Behold the wisdom (of CHRIST) more excellent than every faculty of speech. For he did not say: A good work has been done, but she has done. For he does not weigh the deed itself privately, but together with the person of the Woman. and a little later: Just as if he had been asked before the ointment was poured out, he would undoubtedly have ordered it to be sold and given to the poor: so after it had been poured out, to extinguish the woman's faith through rebuke was absurd.)

Latin:

* (v. 10. Opus bonum fecit. Isid. Pelusiota lib. 2. p. 88 Vide sapientiam (CHRISTI) omni orationis facultate praestantiorem. Non enim dixit: Bonum Opus factum est, sed fecit. Neque enim ipsum facinus privatum expendit, verùm unà cum Mulieris persona. & paulò post: Quemadmodum si ante effusum unguentum interrogatus fuisset, haut dubiè illud vendi & pauperibus dari iussisset: sic posteaquàm effusum fuerat, mulierus fidem per obiurgationem extinguere abiurdum erat.) *

## 26:11
(v. 11. For you have the poor always. Since Christ says elsewhere (above c. 25, 40): Inasmuch as you have done it to one of these my least brethren, you have done it to me: it seems at any rate that it would have been better if that ointment had been sold and given to the poor? Resp. to this objection Isidore of Pelusium, book 2, ep. 88, who can be consulted.)

But me you do not have always, namely, visibly and in the manner of the poor, so that you may be able to show me a benefit, as is sufficiently clear from the context. Conf. Mark 14, 7. above C. 18. 20. below C. 28, 10. Eph. 1, 22. Jerome on this passage: Another question arises, why the Lord after the resurrection said, Behold I am with you all days, and here says, me you will not have always. It seems to me that in these places he speaks of bodily presence, that he will by no means be with them after the resurrection, as he is now in every association and liberality. Augustine, tr. 50 on John: You will not have me always. Why? Because he lived according to the presence of the body for forty days with his disciples and while they were leading him by seeing, not by following, he ascended into heaven, and is not here. For there he sat at the right hand of the Father, and here he is, for he did not depart by the presence of his majesty. According to the presence of Majesty we always have Christ, according to the presence of the flesh it was rightly said to the disciples: But me you will not have always. For the Church had him according to the presence of the flesh for a few days, now it holds him by faith, it does not see him with the eyes. Indeed, Calvin himself acknowledges in his Commentary that CHRIST is speaking here of carnal presence, writing thus: That he denies he will always be with the disciples ought to be referred to the kind of presence to which carnal worship and sumptuous honor are appropriate. For as to the fact that he is present with us by the grace of his Spirit, that he dwells in us, that he even feeds us with his flesh and blood, this has nothing to do with bodily worship. But that from a denied presence, considered in a certain way, it is not permitted to argue to the denying of presence absolutely, is manifest. GOD is said to depart from the impious, namely by his gracious presence, who nevertheless is always present to them and remains by the presence of his power. Conf. John 2, 9. and add the singular dissertation of the Blessed D. Fewerb. Theological Disputations on the Universal presence of God and Θεανσθρώπου J. C., printed at Marburg 1625, likewise the Blessed Par. Exeg. L. on the Nature of GOD §. 187. 188. LL. Theol. L. on the Nature of GOD §. 118 In this place it must at least still be warned that even some Papists themselves acknowledge that the Savior in sayings of this kind, and especially in the present one, speaks at least of visible presence and in mortal body, capable of bodily service, such as that anointing was. Thus explains not only Johannes Ferus, Ecclesiastes of Mainz, Comm. on John 12, 8. But also the Jesuits Barradius and Conzen, the latter on this passage, the former in vol. 3, Conc. Evang. l. 7. c. 3. p. 419. Similarly also the Cardinal and likewise Jesuit Franciscus Toletus, Comm. on John, p. 986. whose words the Blessed Par. brings forward in Confess. Cathol. book 2, art. 2, c. 1, p. 393. There can also be added to them Ioh. Paludanus, Th. D. and Professor of Louvain, in Vind. Theolog., where he explains this passage in the very same way, and besides for this explanation alleges St. Augustine, tr. 95 on John, writing thus: What is, I go to the Father, and you will not see me? except in the way I am, when I am with you: for then he was still mortal, in the likeness of the flesh of sin: who could hunger and thirst. This Christ therefore, that is, such a Christ, when he had passed from this world to the Father, they were no longer to see. all of which are to be well noted against the common doctrine of the Jesuits today, by which not only from the opinion of their predecessors, the Scholastics, as it pertains to the doctrine of omnipresence

they depart from Christ-the-man, but also most sharply against us, because we defend the omnipresence of Christ-the-man, having followed, to wit, S. Matth. 18. & 28, they are attacked, as can be seen especially from the Ubiquitarian War of Forerus; to which malicious writing, however, the blessed D. Keslerus has abundantly satisfied. Nor does the Jesuit Erbermannus set forth anything except cabbage twice cooked in the vindications, as he calls them, of Bellarmine, vol. 1, p. 179, et seqq., as I showed in public lectures. Nor, finally, does Augustine contradict our doctrine in the passage alleged by Wendelinus, Exerc. 105, §. 52, in which, however, W. seeks the chief defense of the desired cause, but in vain, since Augustine speaks there of the visible presence of the body of Christ, and also of Christ the man considered in the state of humiliation, but not as he was exalted to the right hand of the Father. For as far as concerns illocal and majestic presence, Augustine expressly teaches in the passage alleged a little earlier that according to that we always have him. Compare entirely B. Schroterus, Sceptro Regali Christi, p. 637, et seqq.

Latin:

* (v. 11. Nam semper pauperes habetis. Cùm Christus alibi (suprà c. 25, 40.) dicat: Quatenus fecistis ani de his fratribus meis minimis, mihi fecistis: videtur utiq;, satius fuisse, si unguentum illud fuisset venditum ac datum pauperibus? Resp. ad hanc obiectionem Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 2. ep. 88. qui potest consuli.) *

* (Me autem non semper habetis, scil. visibiliter ac more pauperum, ut possitis mihi beneficium exhibere, ceu satis ex contextu patet. Conf. Marc. 14, 7. suprà C. 18. 20. infrà C. 28, 10. Eph. 1, 22. Hieronymus in h. l. Alia oboritur quaestio, quare Dominus post resurrectionem dixerit, Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus, & hic dicat, me non semper habebitis. Mihi videtur in his locis dicere de praesentia corporali, quòd nequaquam cum illis futurus sit post resurrectionem, quomodo nunc in omni convictu & liberalitate. August. tr. 50. in Ioh. Non semper me habebitis. Quare? quia conversatus est secundùm corporis praesentiam quadraginta diebus cum discipulis suis & eis deducentibus videndo, non sequendo ascendit in coelum, & non est hic. ibi enim sedit ad dextram Patris, & hic est non enim recessit praesentia maiestatis. Secundùm praesentiam Maiestatis semper habemus Christum, secundùm praesentiam carnis rectè dictum est discipulis: Me autem non semper habebitis. Habuit enim illum Ecclesia secundùm praesentiam carnis paucis diebus, modò fide tenet, oculis non videt. Quin ipse Calvinus de carnali praesentiâ CHRISTUM hîc loqui in Comm. agnoscit, ita scribens: Quod se negat cum discipulis semper fore, ad genus praesentiae referri debet, cui carnalis cultus & sumtuosus honor conveniat. Nam quod Spiritûs sui gratià nobis adest, quod habitat in nobis, quòd nos etiam carne suâ & sanguine pascit, nihil hoc ad corporeos cultus. Quod verò à negatâ praesentiâ, certo modo consideratâ, non liceat argumentari ad negandam absolutè praesentiam, manifestum est. DEUS dicitur recedere ab impiis, praesentiâ sc. gratiosâ, qui tamen semper illis praesens est ac manet praesentiâ potentiae. Conf. Ioh. 2, 9. ac add. singularem dissert. B. D. Fewerb. Disputationes Theologicasde Dei & Θεανσθρώπου I. C. Universali praesentiâ, Marpurgi 1625. excusas, item. B. Par. Exeg. L. de Nat. DFI. §. 187. 188. LL. Theol. L. de Nat DEI §. 118Hoc loco illud saltem adhuc monendum, quòd ipsi etiam Pontificii quidam agnoscant, Salvatorem in huiuscemodi dictis, & cumprimis in praesenti, loqui saltem de praesentiâ visibili & in corpore mortali, obsequiicorporalis, qualis erat uctio illa, capaci. Ita exponit non solùm Iohannes Ferus Ecclesiastes Moguntinus Comm. ad Iohann. 12, 8. Verùm etiam Iesuitae Barradius ac Conzen, hic in h. l. ille t. 3. Conc. Evang. l. 7. c. 3. p. 419. Similiter etiam prorsus Cardinalis idemque Iesuita Franciscus Toletus Comm. in Ioh. p. 986. quorum verba adducit B. Par. Confess. Cathol. lib. 2. art. 2. c. 1. p. 393. Addi quoque illis potest Ioh. Paludanus Th. D. & Prof. Lovaniensis in Vind. Theolog. ubi eodem prorsus modo h. l. explicat, & praetereà pro explicatione hac allegat S. Augustinum, tr. 95. in Ioh. ita scribentem: Quid est, ad Patrem vado, & non videbitis me? nisi quomodo sum, cùm vobiscum sum: tunc enim adhuc mortalis erat, in similitùdine carnis peccati: qui esurire poterat & sitire. hunc ergò Christum, quod est talem Christum, cùm transiisset de hoc mundo ad Patrem, non erant iam visuri. quae omnia probè notanda contra communem Iesuitarum hodiè doctrinam, qua non modò ab Antecessorum suorum, Scholasticorum, sententiâ, quod attinet doctrinam de omnipraesentia

Christi-hominis discedunt, sed & acerrimè in nos, quòd omnipraesentiam Christi-hominis defendamus, secuti scil. S. Matth. 18. & 28, invehuntur, ceu cumprimis è Bello Ubiquetistico Foreri videre est; cui tamen malitioso scripto abundè satisfecit B. D. Keslerus. Nec quicquam etiam nisi erambem bis coctam apponit Iesuita Erbermannus in vindiciis, quas ita vocat, Bellarmini, t. 1. p. 179. seqq. ceu in Lect. publicis ostendi. Nec adversatur denique doctrinae nostrae Augustinus loco à Wendelino Exerc. 105. §. 52. allegato, in quo tamen praecipuum optatae causae praesidium, sed frustrà, W. quaerit, cùm Augustinus ibi loquatur c'praesentia corporis Christi visibili, item de Christo homine in statu exinanitionis considerato, non verò quatenus ad dextram Patris fuit exaltatus. Quod enim praesentiam illocalem & maiestaticam concernit, expressè loco paulò antè allegato Augustinus docet, quòd secundùm illam semper illum habeamus. Conf. omninò B. Schroterus Sceptro Regali Christi p. 637. seqq.) *

## 26:12
v. 12. Pouring this ointment, etc. By the deed of the woman, Christ reminds the guests of his impending death and burial, the life-giving odor of which would be for all sinners fleeing to him.

ἐνταφιάζειν is distinct from σθάπτειν:, for it signifies to prepare for burial, by anointing the body with aromatics and wrapping it in linens. The Latins call it to perform funeral rites, to prepare for burial. (Concerning the custom of embalming and anointing the bodies of the deceased, see Gen. 50, 2.26,2. Par. 16, 14.C. 21. 16.Ioh. 19, 40. and the commentaries on these passages; also Pliny, book 11, N. H. C. 27, book 12, C. 18. But especially let the work of Mr. D. Quensted on the burial of the Jews and Christians be unrolled. Kirchmannus on funerals, Roman. l. 1.c. 7. p. 54, et seqq. Mr. Dilherrus in the passage cited a little earlier. Also, she anointed him while alive as if he were already about to be buried: for she could not anoint him dead, since Joseph of Arimathea anticipated her in that; nor afterwards, since Christ himself by his resurrection anticipated that duty. The sense, however, is: No one perhaps would disapprove of expenses made on a dead body. Now, however, since that pious woman cannot anoint me dead , she holds me already as dead, as one who is about to die immediately, and therefore she is deservedly excused, and even praised, since to anoint the dead is considered a praiseworthy act. Although this woman may have understood as little as possible that Christ was already near to death (from which, however, the contrary seems to be able to be gathered from Luke 24, 7.) It is not said inconveniently, however, that she wished to prepare Christ for burial as one already about to die, since in Holy Scripture someone is also said to do that for this or that end, which nevertheless is not intended by him, provided that it follows the act. See 1 Kings 17, 18.Proverbs 8, 36.ch. 17, 19.) *

Latin:

v. 12. Mittens hoc unguentum &c. Christus facto mulieris admonet convivas vicinae suae mortis ac sepulturae, cuius odor vivificus esset omnibus peccatoribus ad ipsum fugientibus.

ἐνταφιάζειν distinctum est à σθάπτειν: significat enim ad sepulturam praeparare, ungendo corpus aromatibus & involvendo linteis. Latini vocant funerare, pollincire. * (De more condiendi & ungendi defunctorum corpora vid. Gen. 50, 2.26,2. Par. 16, 14.C. 21. 16.Ioh. 19, 40. & Comment. in dd. ll. it. Plin. lib. 11. N. H. C. 27. lib. 12 C. 18. Cumprimis verò etiam evolvatur Dn. D. Quensted. de Sepult. Iudaeorum. Christian. &c. Kirchmannus de suner. Roman. l. 1.c. 7. p. 54. seqq. Dn. Dilherrus loco paulò antè cit. Item unxit vivum quasi iamiam sepeliendum: neque enim mortuum ungere potuit, cùm ipsam Iosephus ab Arimathia praevenerit; nec posteà, cùm Christus ipse resurrectione suâ officium illud praevenerit. Sensus verò est. Sumtus in corpus mortuum factos nemo fortè improbaret. Iam verò cùm mortuum me ungere pia illa mulier haut possit, habet me iam pro mortuo, quippe iam iam moriturum, adeoq; meritò exeusatur, quin & laudatur, cùm mortuos ungere in laude positum sit. Licet verò mulier haec quàm maximè non intellexerit, Christum morti esse iam proximum (cuius tamen contrarium colligi posse videtur ex Luc. 24, 7.) non inconvenienter tamen dicitur, quòd Christum uti iam iam moriturum pollincire voluerit, cùm in Sc. S. quis illud quoque ad hunc vel illum finem facere dicatur, quod tamen ab ipso non intenditur, modò actum sequatur. Vid. 1. Reg. 17, 18.Proverb. 8, 36.c. 17, 19.) *

## 26:13
* (v. 13. This Gospel. i.e. those things which I did and suffered in the flesh.) *

This also shall be told. For this anointing was by far most pleasing to Christ, not because the whole vessel was broken by Mary, but because it was done by her with a contrite and fervent spirit; not on account of the expense, but because of the faith which she offered together with the ointment: for this was to Christ like a most fragrant perfume.) * * (

Latin:

* (v. 13. Hoc Evangelium. h. e. ea, quae in carne feci & passus sum.) *

* (Hoc quoque narrabitur. Fuit enim unctio haec Christo longè gratissima, non quòd totum vas à Mariâ fuerit fractum, sed quia animo contrito ac fervente id fuit ab ipsâ factum; non propter impensas, sed ob fidem, quam unà cum unguento obtulit: haec enim Christo fragrantissimi instar odoramenti fuit.) *
