Ludov. de Dieu in this place. Moreover, you may see a fuller exposition of this and the preceding verse in the Blessed Par. part 1. Homil. Acad. p. 758. seqq.) *

* (You have forsaken me. This forsaking is an infernal punishment. For it is a taste not of the love and favor, but of the wrath of GOD, which Christ felt in our place, Es. 53.Gal 3, 13. Also the hiding from the face of GOD, 2. Thess. 1, 9. But it is asked, how could Christ complain that he was forsaken by the Father, when nevertheless the divine τοῶ λόγου nature was never separated from the assumed flesh? Resp. Irenaeus and Damascenus warn that ὁλόγος rested while Christ was suffering. Yet in such a way that it nevertheless sustained the human nature, lest it succumb under so great a burden, and indeed even added weight to the passions and death of Christ, so that they might be a price of infinite value for the sins of the whole world. But indeed ὁλόγος rested in such a way that the assumed human nature did not feel divine joy, but rather bodily and spiritual torments, to be sustained in our place. see August. in Ps 21. Euthymius and the Glossa Ordin. in this place. conf. B. D. Chemn. L. de diebus nat. in Christo p. 16. Nor yet does it follow: Christ sustained infernal pains, therefore he despaired. For 1. he retained filial confidence. 2. he was devoid of sin. Now indeed despair is a most grave sin. 3. he could not have redeemed us if he had despaired. But that the Devils and damned men despair on account of infernal torments, this happens from the fact that all hope of liberation is taken away from them. conf. Ioh. 3. 39. It is added that even the pious in this life sometimes feel infernal pains, see Pf. 18, 6. Ps. 86, 13.1. Sam. 2, 6. whom, however, no one would easily say despair. That cry of Christ on the cross was therefore not of one despairing, but of one struggling with despair, and overcoming it, and expiating the punishment of those who despair.

Whence it is clear that the Papists ineptly conclude from the fact that we maintain that Christ felt infernal pains, as if we maintain that Christ despaired. That indeed we expressly deny. see B. Par. Dispp. Acad. p. 57. & 1512. Confess. Cathol. l. 2. Spec. part. 1. art. 2. c. 2. §. 1. L. de Iustif. §. 54. Harm. Ev. c. 202. p. 2015. Those same people also strive to smear the same error upon the Calvinists. See Malderus in Antisynod. p. 89. Felic. Capito Expl. Cathol. p. 645. Corn. à Lapide in this place. But Calvin denies this in express words in Harm. p. 427. & 428. so that they attribute this error to him even against the truth. Conf. also Crocius both in Anti Becano, and in Vindiciis pro Anti Becano p. 66. & 67. tom. 1. Moreover, Christ's pains are not to be so extenuated with the Papists, as if the soul of Christ remained in its higher part ἀπασθεὶς free from the sense of divine wrath, and from the burden of sins which had to be carried, entirely immune from infernal pains and the taste of the second death. For the Blessed Father Confessor Catholic taught the contrary of this at length in the cited place. Much less do the Jews and Photinians rightly infer from that desertion that Christ was not true God, since men complain that they are deserted by GOD. For it must be known that although Christ was in the form of GOD, Phil. 2, 6. God blessed forever, Rom. 9, 5. true GOD, 1. John 5, 20. the great God, Tit. 2, 15. nevertheless, so that he might sustain the punishments which we had deserved and thus complete the work of redemption, he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men etc. Phil. 2, 7. Distinguish therefore between the divine and human nature of Christ, and the latter indeed considered in the state of exaltation and humiliation. It is concerning this, and the same considered in the state of humiliation, not concerning the former, that we are dealing in this place. item Ps. 8, 6. and Ps. 22, 1. Let more be seen on this matter in Mr. Dr. Muller in Judaism p. 976. item Mr. Dr. Calovius in the Examination of the book of Crellius §. 271. The same distinction is also to be observed against the reasoning of the Photinians, when, from the fact that it is recorded that Christ cried out, prayed, and sought help from the heavenly Father, they likewise attack his true divinity, which objection Dr. Calovius examines at greater length in the cited place §. 206. Furthermore, learned men gather from these words uttered by Christ on the cross which idiom the Savior used, namely Syriac, (not indeed Maronite or Antiochene, in which the Syriac Paraphrase of the N. T. exists, but Jerusalem). See Barthol. Mayerus Sacred Philology part 2, page 78 ff. Schickardus in Bechin. Happer p. 21. others.

Latin:

* (v. 45. Asexta autem &c. Quaeritur, quomodo Matthaeus (cum quo etiam consentiunt Marc. c. 15, 33. & Lucas c. 23, 44.) dicat, tenobras factas esse ab horâ sextâ, Christo nempe in cruce pendente, conciliandus fit cum Iohanne, c. 19, 14. scribente, fuisse horam quasi fextam, cum Pilatus Iudaeis dixit: Ecce Rex vester? ac constat etiā ex Marco c. 15, 25. quòd Christus fuerit crucifixus horâ tertiâ: quomodo igitur demum horâ sextâ à Pilato, pro tribunali sedente potuit condemnari, si iamtū horâ tertiâ fuit crucifixus? Resp. dist. inter horas simplices, quarum Iudaei duode cim numerabant, initio numerandi facto ab ortu Solis, & inter horas composit as, quarum quaelibet tres simplices complectebatur, & appellationem sortiebantur ab initio cuiusque. Non de illis, sed de his Evang. hîc loquuntur. Iohannes igitur hoc vult, quòd Pilatns Christum condemnarit circiter horam sextam, minimè eâ praeterlapsa, sed cùm incepisset tertia, cuius finis incidebat in sextam. Reliqui Evangelistae itidem non ita accipiendi sunt, quasi praecisè tertii quadrantis initio Christus fuerit crucifixus: sufficit, quòd intra illum diei quadrantem hoc fuerit factum, qui ab horâ tertiâ initium sumebat, ac sextâ finiebatur. Ut ita omninò iudiciaria sententia crucifixionem praecesserit, facta quippe secundi quadrantes initio, crucifixio verò circa eius dem quadrantis finem. Conf. plura huc facientia apud B. D. Walth. in H. B. p. 39. 40. 823. B. Par. H. E. c. 195. p. 1928. B. D. Thum. de Festis p. 3. 4. Add. Ramirez in Pentecont. c. 38. nec non Anal. ad Marc. 15, 25] *

* [ Tenebrae super universam terram. Patet hinc, quôd Eclipsis haec fuerit miraculo sa ac praeter naturalis, tū quia fuit universalis, tum etiam, quia obtigit in plenilunio. (Iam verò in plenilunio non potest aliàs fieri eclipsis, quia tunc luna à sole longissimè distat, adeoque interponi Solem inter & nostrum adspectum non potest) etenim 14. dies mensis primi, quo pascha celebrabatur apud Iudaeos, incidit in plenilunium. Vid. August. t. 5. l. 3. C. D. c. 15. Chrysost. hom. 89. in Matth. Euthym. & Theoph. in h. l. Athanas. de Pass. & cruce Domini. Dionysius Areopagita ep. 7. ad Polycarpum contra Apollophanem refert, se Heliopoli in Aegypto vidisse eam Solis defectionem, simul cum ipso Apollophane. quod etiam repetit ep. 10 ad eundem Apollophanem. Quamvis de antiquitate, & num genuina Dionysii scripta sint, quae nomen eius prae se ferunt, nonnulli ambigant. Quâ de re prolixè agit B. Par. in Patrol. p. 18. seqq. adde B. D. Calixt. Conc. Ev. p. 401. Robert. Cocum Censur. Script. p. 48. seqq. Memorat etiam Tertullianus in Apolog. c. 21. notatam fuisse illam Eclipsin Romae & in commenmentaria publica relatam. Ex Graecis Historicis Phlegon l. 13. Olymp. eiusdem Eclipsis meminit, teste Origene tr. 35. in Matth. & Euseb. in Chronico sub Tiberio. Lactantius l. 4. Instit. c. 19. refert, eclipsin hanc à Sibillis fuisse praedictam. Existimant quidem Dionysius ac Thomas de Aquino, contigisse eclipsin hanc ex interpositione Lunae inter Solem & terram, nec tamen sine miraculo, eo quòd Luna, cùm paullò antè in proprio fuerit situ, maximè distans à Sole subitò retroacta fuerit, Solique obiecta. Alii putant, quòd orta fuerit ex interpositione densarum nubium inter Solem & terram. Alii denique ita factum fuisse tradunt, quod Deus suspenderit concursum suum, ita ut non potuerit Sol emittere radios, ad eum modum, ceu ignis Babylonius non potuit urere, Deo concursum suum retrahente. In hâc sententia est Leonh. Coquaeus Com. ad d. l. August faventque etiam huic sententiae ea, quae olim memoravit Oros. l. 1. c. 4. Cyprianus sermone de Bono patientiae ita de hae eclipsi iudicat, quòd Sol, ne Iudaeorum facinus adspicere cogatur, & radios & oculos suos subtraxerit. Similia habent Chrysost. in Catenâ ex serm. de Pass Domini. Conf. plurima huc facientia apud Grotium in Matth. p. 491. ubi etiam evincere satagit, similes, si non pares, irae divinae adversus graviora scelera significationes aliis quoque temporibus extitisse. Q. verò, an per universam terram intelligatur solùm terra Iudaeae, an verò totus terrarum orbis? Posterius sentiunt Interpretes ferè plerique omnes. Loquentes scil. de superiori hemisphaerio. Quod enim inferius concernit hemisphaerium, ibi aliàs dies tum non erat, nec esse poterat, uti benè notat Grotius, qui multa etiam in rem hanc adducit. Prius tamen voluit Origenes, quem sequitur Iesuita Maldonatus, qui eclipsin hanc ad solam Iudaeam arctat, quem propterea refutat proprius sociennus Cornelius â Lapide in h. l. Idem etiam statuit Calvinus in Harm. p. 427. urgetque 1. quòd si tale quid contigisset, haut debuerit â tam multis, qui illorum temporum historiam accuratè tradiderunt, omitti. 2. quòd si toti mundo communis fuisset defectio, potuerit videri naturalis, è contra verò magis notabile fuisse prodigium, tenebris obrui Iudaeam, sole alibi fulgente. Cumprimis verò sententiam priorem avidè amplexus est Isaacus Peyrerius System. Theolog. lib. IV. Cap. 3. p. 199. Ast cùm errorem dictus autor suum de Prae Adamitis, in cuius gratiam hypothesin eam arripuit, eiurarit ipse, ac praepterea â multis doctissimis Viris refutatus fit, nolumus hâc actum agere. Nec rationes etiam Calvini tanti momenti sunt, ut aliquem â recepta sententiâ dimovere debeant, cumprimis, quia prorsus insolens est in Sc. S., phrasi omnis terrae solam Iudaeam indicare.) *

* (Eli, Eli. Conciliationem Evangelistarum Matthaei, qui habet -λὶ, & Marci, apud quem est ἐλωὶ, instituit B. D. Walth. Miscell. Theol. p. 370. qui potest evolvi. add. Ludov. de Dieu in h. l. Coeterum uberiorem huius & praecedentis versiculi expositionem videsis apud B. Par. part. 1. Homil. Acad. p. 758. seqq.) *

* (Dereliquisti. Derelictio haec est poena infernalis. Etenim est gustus non amoris ac favoris, sed furoris DEI, quem Christus nostri loco sensit, Es. 53.Gal 3, 13. Item absconsio â facie DEI, 2. Thess. 1, 9. Sed quaeritur, quomodo Christus cōqueri potuerit, se â Patre derelictum, cùm tamen divinaτοῶ λόγουnatura nunquam ab assumtâ carne fuerit separata? Resp. Monent Irenaeus ac Damascenus quòd ὁλόγος Christo patiente quieverit. Ita tamen, ut nihilominus humanam naturam sustentarit, ne sub tanto onere succumberet, imò & pondus addiderit passionibus ac morti Christi, quò essent infiniti valoris pretium pro totius mundi peccatis. Ita verò ὁλόγος tum quievit, ut humana natura adsumta non sentiret laetitiam divinam, sed potiùs corporales & spirituales cruciatus, nostri loco sustinendos. vid. August. in Ps 21. Euthymium ac Glossam Ordin. in h. l. conf. B. D. Chemn. L. de diebus nat. in Christo p. 16. Neq; tamen sequitur. Christus sustinuit dolores infernales, E. desperavit. Etenim 1. retinuit fiduciam filialem. 2. fuit expers peccati. Iam vero desperatio est peccatum gravissimum. 3. non potuisset nos redimere, si desperasset. Quòd vero Diaboli ac homines damnati ob infernales cruciatus desperant, hoc inde fit, quia omnis illis spes liberationis ademta est. conf. Ioh. 3. 39. Accedit, quòd etiam pii in hac vita quandoq; dolores infernales sentiant, vid. Pf. 18, 6. Ps. 86, 13.1. Sam. 2, 6. quos tamen desperare, nemo facilè dixerit. Fuit igitur clamor ille Christi in cruce non desperantis, sed cum desperatione Inctantis, eamq; superantis, & poenam desperatorum expiantis.

Unde patet, quod ineptè Pontificii ex eo, quòd statuimus, Christum sensisse dolores infernales, colligant, ac si statuamus, Christum desperasse. Id verò disertè negamus. vid B. Par. Dispp. Acad. p. 57. & 1512. Confess. Cathol. l. 2. Spec. part. 1. art. 2. c. 2. §. 1. L. de Iustif. §. 54. Harm. Ev. c. 202. p. 2015. Calvinianis quoq; eundē affricare errorē iidem illi satagunt. Vid. Malderus in Antisynod. p. 89. Felic. Capito Expl. Cathol. p. 645. Corn. à Lapide in h. l. Sed expressis id verbis negat Calvinus in Harm. p. 427. & 428. ut adeò invitâ veritate errorem hunc illi tribuāt. Conf. etiam Crocius tum in Anti Becano, tum in Vindiciis pro Anti Becano p. 66. & 67. tom. 1. Coeterùm nec ita extenuandī cum Pontificiis Christi dolores sunt, quasi anima Christi in parte sui superiore manserit ἀπασθεὶς à sensu irae divinae, & à peccatorum, quae portanda erant, onere libera, à doloribus infernalibus ac gustu mortis secundae prorsus immunis. Huius enim contrarium prolixè docuit B. P. Confess. Cathol. l. c. Multò minùs existâ desertione rectè inferunt Iudaei ac Photiniani, quòd Christus non fuerit verus Deus, cùm homines se à DEO deseri conquerantur. Sciendum enim, quòd licet Christus in formâ DEI fuerit,Phil. 2, 6.Deus benedictus in secula,Rom. 9, 5. DEUS verus, 1. Ioh. 5, 20.Deus magnus,Tit. 2, 15. nihilo tamen minùs, quò poenas, quas nos eramus promeriti, sustinere adéoque opus redemtionis perficere posset, seipsum exinaniverit, formâ servi adsumtâ, in similitudine hominum constitutus &c. Phil. 2, 7. Disting. igitur in divinam, ac humanam Christi naturā, & hanc quidē in statu exaltationis, & exinanitionis consideratā. De hac, eademq; in statu exinanitionis consideratâ, non de illa agitur h. l. it. Ps. 8, 6. ac Ps. 22. 1. Videantur plura in hanc rem apud Dn. D. Mullerum in Iudaismo p. 976. it. Dn. D. Caloviū in Exam. lib. Crellii §. 271. Eadem quoq; distinctio observanda contra ratiocinium Photinianorum, qn. ex eo, quòd Christus clamasses. orasse, & auxiliū petiisse à Patre coelesti, comemoratur, itidem veram eius divinitatem impugnant, quam obiectionem prolixiùs examinat D. Calovius l. c. §. 206. Coeterùm quo idiomate usus fuerit Salvator, nempe Syriaco, (non quidem Maronitico aut Antiocheno, quo Paraphrasis N. T. Syriaca extat, sed Hierosolymitano) ex verbis his à Christo in cruce prolatis, viri docti colligunt. Vid. Barthol. Mayerus Philol. S. part. 2. pag. 78. seqq. Schickardus in Bechin. Happer p. 21. alii) *

## 27:47
* (v. 47. But some, etc., were saying: This man is calling for Elias. Just as it is customary for the Papists to scrape together even obvious sayings of Holy Scripture to cloak their errors, so Salmeron also provides an excellent example of this matter when, in order to establish what they call the religious invocation of saints, Disp. 7 on 1 Tim. 2, he gathers from this place that it was customary at that time for afflicted men to take refuge with the Saints, and that the Jews said this, who knew this from the law, and understood that he had asked for help from Elias. A blind man follows a blind man, a Jesuit follows a Jesuit, Adam Contzen, likewise writing on this place, q. 1 on the present verse: We learn from this that the Jews were of that opinion, and that the soldiers learned from the Jews that those who have died in the Lord are sometimes called upon for the help of others. But 1. how could the Jews have known from the law that Christ was asking for help from Elias, when in the whole law not even γρυ exists concerning imploring or obtaining help either from Elias or from any other deceased saint? Whence even the Papists themselves grant that in the Old Testament there was no custom of approaching saintly intercessors. Which Salmeron does not deny in the place cited, p. 473. 2. The Jesuit Contzen notes, the soldiers said v. 49. Let us see whether Elias comes, not because the profane men thought that Elias was now present and would deliver him, (thus Menochius and Em. Saa seem to think) but out of a certain curiosity, etc., namely, just as the latter mocked Christ, so the former likewise, through a diabolical sarcasm, twisted the well-understood words of Christ into a foreign sense, and strove to deform Christ with this insult, as if, being placed in his agony, he had cast aside all trust in God and turned himself to the saints. So that they considered the invocation of saints to be a reproach rather than a praise, as the Blessed Pareus well advises, L. de Morte §. 471. Grotius thinks that those standing by were not Roman soldiers, as those to whom nothing was known about Elias, nor Palestinian Jews, but Hellenists, who, since they did not understand the Hebrew words, thought that he was calling upon the name of Elias, which was known to them, etc. But it is sufficiently manifest from the context that they transferred the words of Christ to Elias through sarcasm. And this is also granted by the Papist Laur. Ramirez the Spaniard in Pentecont. p. 268. Cornelius à Lapide notes on this place that St. Jerome and others judge that those who uttered these words were Roman soldiers: Since therefore they did not know the Hebrew language, they heard, they heard Christ crying out, Eli, Eli, and thought that Elias was being called and invoked by Christ: he adds: For they had heard from the Jews that Elias was to return at the coming of the Messiah. Therefore, the Roman soldiers did not think that Elias was being called because they had learned from the Jews that the dead are sometimes called to the aid of others, which Conzen thinks: but according to Cornelius, because in particular they had heard about Elias, that he himself would return at the coming of the Messiah. But what is this for the invocation of saints? For the opinion of the Jews concerning the return of Elias was erroneous, namely, they were accepting the words of Malachi concerning Elias the Tishbite, when the Prophet is speaking about John the Baptist, who in the spirit of Elias was to go before Christ, by no means about to provide aid to Christ.) *

Latin:

* (v. 47. Quidam autem &c. dicebant: Eliam vocat iste. Quemadmodum Pontificiis solenne ast, obvia quoque Sc. S. dicta ad palliandos suos errores corradere: ita egregium quoque huius rei exemplum praebet Salmeron, quando ut religiosam quam vocant, sanctorum invocationem stabiliat, Disp. 7. in Tim. 2. ex h. l. colligit, fuisse tum temporis consuetum afflictis hominibus, ad Sanctos confugere, ac Iudaeos hoc dixisse, quiid ex lege noverant, & intellexerunt, postulasse auxilium ab Helia. Sequitur coecum coecus, Iesuitam Iesuita Adamus Couzen, itidem in h. l. q. 1. ad praes. vers. scribens: Discimus hinc, Iudaeos in ea fuisse sententiâ, & milites à Iudaeis didicisse, defunctos in Domino in auxilium aliorum interdum vocari. At 1. quomodo Iudaei ex lege nosse potuerunt, Christum ab Eliâ auxilium postulare, cùm in totâ lege ne γρυ quidem extet de auxilio, vel ab Elia vel ab alio sancto defuncto implorando aut impetrando. Unde etiam ipsi Pontificii largiuntur, in V. Test. non fuisse morem adeundi sanctos intercessores. Quod nec Salmero diffitetur l. c. p. 473. 2. notat Iesuita Conzen, milites dixisse v. 49. Sine videamus, an veniat Elias, non quòd homines profani putarent, iam adfore Eliam, & liberaturum, (ita Menochius & Em. Saa sentire videntur.) sed curiositate quadam &c. nempe quemadmodum hi posteriores Christo illudebant, ita priores pariter per diabolicum sarcasmum verba Christi probè intellecta in peregrinum sensum detorquebant, ac convitio hoc Christum deformare satagebant, quasi in agone constitutus abiectc omni in Deum fiducia ad sanctos se converteret. Ut ita sanctorum invocationem vituperio potiùs, quàm laudi duxerint, ceu bene monet B. Par. L. de Morte §. 471. Existimat Grotius, adstantes eos non fuisse Romanos milites, ut quibus de Elia nihil cognitum, neIudaeos Palaestinos, sed Hellinistas, quae cùm Ebraea verba non intelligerent, Eliae nomen sibi notum adire se existimarint &c. Verùm è contextu satis manifestum, quòd per sarcasmum verba Christi ad Eliam transtulerint. Idque è Pontificiis quoque largitur Laur Ramirez Hispanus in Pentecont. p. 268. c. Corn. à Lapide in h. l. annotat, S. Hieronymum & alios censere, qui haec verba protulere, fuisse milites Romanos: hos ergo cùm Ebraeam linguam non callerent, audirent, audirentChristum clamantem, Eli, Eli, putasse, Eliam vocari & invocarià Christo: addit: Eliam enim rediturum in adventu Messiae, à Iudaeis inaudierant. Non igitur propterea Romani milites Eliam vocari putant, quòd à Iudaeis didicerant, defunctos in auxilium aliorum interdum vocari, quod Conzen censet: sed iuxta Corneliū, quia in specie de Eliâ audierant, ipsum in adventu Messiae rediturum. Ast quid hoc pro sanctorum invocatione? etenim erronea fuit Iudaeorum de Eliae reditu opinio, accipientium nempe verba Malachiae de Elia Tesbite, cùm Propheta loquatur de Iohanne Baptista, qui in spiritu Eliae praecessurus Christum erat, minimè Christo patenti auxilium praestiturus) *

## 27:48
* (v. 48. Πλήξας τε ὂξους. Hugo Grotius notes, that one of those who were standing by gave Christ to drink, not to hasten death, but against a fainting of the soul, as if sustaining his life in the hope of aid coming from heaven. But it is less credible that those mockers thought that aid would come to Christ from heaven.) *

* ( Καλάμω. By κάλαμον the same person in this place understands what is said by John ὕ-ωπον, namely a rod of hyssop, H. Grotius shows at length in this place. Salmasius and Ludov. de Dieu at Ioh 19. p. 493 think that it can be understood as fragrant reed, which Exod. 30, 23. קנת בשם the LXX κάλαμος πὐώδης call; they judge that such a thing was brought to him, so that Christ, whom the vehemence of pain had almost rendered lifeless, might be refreshed. Furthermore, it is not the place here to discuss this matter at greater length. Compare Heinsius in Aristarch. B. Par. in Harm. Passionis, Salmasius and Lud. de Dieu in the cited places.) *

* (He gave, that he might drink. See Isidore of Pelusium lib. 1. ep. 249. But Ioh. 19, 29. it is commemorated as having been done by many. Resp. Many are said to have done it, because one of the others did it with the consent and applause of the rest.) *

Latin:

* (v. 48. Πλήξας τε ὂξους. Notat Hugo Grotius, illorum quendam, qui adstabant, Christo ut biberet dedisse, non accelerandae morti, sed adversùs animi deliquium, quasi in spem adventantis coelitùs auxilii vitam ei sustentantem. Ast minùs credibile est, quòd illusores illi existimarint, coelitùs auxilium Christo adventurum.) *

* ( Καλάμω. Per κάλαμον Idem h. l. intelligi, quod à Iohanne ὕ-ωπον dicitur, nempe bacillum ex hyssopo, prolixè ostendit H. Grotius in h. l. Salmasius ac Ludov. de Dieu ad Ioh 19. p. 493. de calamo odorato, qui Exod. 30, 23.קנת בשם LXX. κάλαμος πὐώδης dicitur, accipi posse existimant; talem verò adsibitum fuisse censent, ut Christus, quem doloris vehementia propè exanimasset, reficeretur. Coeterùm non est huius loci, prolixiùs hâc de re disserere. Conf. Heinsius in Aristarch. B. Par. in Harm. Passionis, Salmasius ac Lud. de Dieull. cc.) *

* (Dabat, ut biberet. Vide Isid. Pelusiotam lib. 1. ep. 249. At Ioh. 19, 29. à pluribus hoc factum commemoratur. Resp. Plures dicuntur fecisse, quia unus reliquorum fecit consensu & applausu.) *

## 27:49
* (v. 49. The others were saying. But Marcus c. 15, 35. reports that it was done by one . Resp. One began to mock in this way, the others continued.) *

* (Crying with a loud voice. Q. what did Christ cry out? Ans. Most interpreters (See B. Par. Harm Ev. p. 2026. H. Grotius on this passage, others,) judge that this cry was τετέλεςαι, in John, ch. 19, 30. & πάπρ, εἰς χεῖρὰς σουπαραθήσομαι τὸ πνεῦμα μου, Luke 23, 46. And that the Centurion accepted this very thing as a miracle, because Christ expired immediately, and thus the thing itself showed that his soul was truly received by GOD. But the Savior cried out, both to declare that he was dying not out of necessity, but out of free will, John 10. and to show that he was God, whence Mark adds that the Centurion, seeing this, said: Truly this was the son of GOD. and finally, to manifest his vehement love for GOD, as well as his obedience, and desire for our salvation. Conf. Heb. 5, 7. Whence it is also easily evident how that of Isaiah ch. 53, 7 he did not open his mouth &c. can be reconciled with this cry (which interpreters also judge to have been predicted Ps. 69, 4.). He was silent, namely, when he was falsely accused and condemned though innocent, out of supreme patience; but he cried out and prayed, with firm confidence in God, to whom he was commending his spirit. Damascenus lib. 3. de O. F. C. 24. establishes that Christ was by no means abandoned by his deity, but putting on our person he cried out in this way. Furthermore, this is not to be drawn to the conclusion as if Christ did not truly feel infernal pains: the contrary has been proven elsewhere. The Evangelist John ch. 19, 30. commemorates that with his head bowed Christ sent forth his spirit, concerning which matter St. Athanasius q. 6. to Antiochus says thus: With head bowed, because death fearing Christ, did not dare to approach him: but Christ with head bowed called it &c. He bowed his head, because the burden of our sins was pressing upon him; he bowed it, as if to bid farewell to the world, and to call the faithful to himself, so that he might kiss them. Conf. August. de Virgin.) *

Latin:

* (v. 49. Coeteri dicebant. At Marcus c. 15, 35. ab uno id factum refert. Resp. Unus ita subsannare coepit, coeteri continuarunt.) *

* (Clamans voce magnâ. Q. quid Christus clamarit? Resp. Plerique interpp. (Vid. B. Par. Harm Ev. p. 2026. H. Grotius in h. l. alii,) exstimant, quòd clamor hic fuerit τετέλεςαι, apud Iohannem, c. 19, 30. & πάπρ, εἰς χεῖρὰς σουπαραθήσομαι τὸ πνεῦμα μου,Luc. 23, 46. Hoc ipsum autem pro miraculo accepisse Centurionem, quia statim Christus exspirarit, adeoque res ipsa ostenderit, verè animam eius à DEO fuisse susceptam. Clamavit verò Salvator, tum ut declararet, se non ex necessitate, sed ex libera voluntate mori, Ioh. 10. tum ut se Deum esse, ostenderet, unde Marcus adiicit, quòd Centurio hoc videns, dixerit: Verè fililus DEI erat iste. tum denique, ut vehementem suum in DEUM amorem, item obedientiam, ac salutis nostrae desiderium manifestaret. Conf. Ebr. 5, 7. Unde facilè quoque patet, quomodo conciliari cum clamore hoc (quem etiam praedictum Interpp. censent Psal. 69, 4.) possit illud Esaiae c. 53, 7. non aperuitos suum &c. Tacuit nempe, cùm falsò accusaretur ac innocens demnaretur, ex summâ patientiâ; clamavit autem & oravit, firmâ in Deum, cui spiritum suum commendabat, fiduciâ. Damascenus lib. 3. de O. F. C. 24. statuit, quòd Christus minimè relictus fuerit à suâ deitate, sed nostram induens personam ita clamarit. Coeterùm hoc non eò trahendum, quasi Christus non senserit revera dolores infernales: contrariumn. alibi evictum. Evangelista Iohannes cap. 19, 30. comemorat, quòd inclinato capite Christus spiritum suum emiserit, quâ de re ita S. Athanasius q. 6. ad Antiochum: Inclinato capite, quia mors Christum metuens, ad ipsum non audebat accedere: Christus autem inclinato capite eam vocavit &c. Inclinabat caput, quia peccatorum nostrorum onus eum premebat; inclinabat, ut mundo quasi valediceret, fideles verò ad se, quò eos oscularetur, vocaret. Conf. August. de Virgin.) *

## 27:50
* (v. 50. He sent forth his spirit i. e. his soul. compare John 10, 18. Because therefore the soul was released from the body through death, thence it is rightly said that Christ was truly dead, since death consists in the release of the soul from the body. Nevertheless body and soul remained τῳ λόρῳ inseparably joined. Distinguish, therefore, between natural union, and personal. The former was dissolved by death, but the latter not at all: but as it is most tight, so it was never dissolved, nor will it ever be dissolved. See Damasc. b. 3. on the O. F. ch. 27. Bonavent in 1. Sent. dist. 21. q. 1. & 2. But it is asked here 1. how Christ could be said to be dead, while the personal union of the divine and human nature remained, since the vivifying power of GOD is greater s. τοῦ λόγου, than that of the soul? Resp. Thomas p. 3. q. 50. art. 2. to 3. that the soul has the power of vivifying formally; but the divinity effectively, nor can it be the form of the body, and thus it is not necessary that, while the union of the divinity to the flesh remains, the flesh be alive, because God does not act out of necessity, but out of will. Q. 2. Whether Christ remained true man during the three days of death? Resp. there are diverse opinions on this matter, even of our own Theologians, while some affirm, others deny. See B. D. Balth. Meisnerus in Qq. vexatis q. 2. B. D. Grawerus part. 1. Praelect. in A. C. p. 449. 450. B. Par. Harm. Evang. ch. 202. p. 2031. 2032. Dn. D. Iohan. Meisnerus in pecul. Disput. on this question.) *

Latin:

* (v. 50. Emisit spiritum i. e. animam. confer. Ioh. 10, 18. Quia proinde anima per mortem â corpore soluta fuit, inde rectè dicitur, quòd Christus reverà fuerit mortuus, cùm mors consistat in solutione animae à corpore. Manserunt tamen corpus & anima τῳ λόρῳ inseparabiliter coniuncta. Disting. proinde inter unionem naturalem, & personalem. Illa per mortem fuit soluta, haec autem minimè: sed uti arctissima est, ita nunquam fuit soluta, nec unquam etiam solvetur. vid. Damasc. l. 3. de O. F. c. 27. Bonavent in 1. Sent. dist. 21. q. 1. & 2. Sed quaeritur hîc 1. quomodo Christus potuerit dici mortuus, manente unione personali divinae ac humanae naturae, cùm maior sit virtus vivificativa DEI s.τοῦ λόγου,quàm animae? Resp. Thomas p. 3. q. 50. art. 2. ad 3. quòd anima habeat vim vivificandi formaliter; divinitas verò effectivè, nec possit esse corporis forma, adeoque non necesse sit, ut manente unione divinitatis ad carnem, caro sit viva, quia Deus non ex necessitate agat, sed ex voluntate. Q. 2. An Christus in triduo mortis permanserit verus homo? Resp. diversae hâc de re funt sententiae, etiam nostratium Theologorum, dum alii affirmant, alii negant. Vid. B. D. Balth. Meisnerus in Qq. vexatis q. 2. B. D. Grawerus part. 1. Praelect. in A. C. p. 449. 450. B. Par. Harm. Evang. c. 202. p. 2031. 2032. Dn. D. Iohan. Meisnerus in pecul. Disput. de hâc quaestione.) *

## 27:51
* (v. 51. The veil of the temple was torn. For Christ, after he entered the holy of holies through his own blood, and found eternal redemption, Ebr. 9, 12. abrogated the Levitical worship, and removed the veil, so that a free approach to the throne of GOD, to the mercy seat, might be open to us. See Daniel. 9, 27.Ebr. 9, 8.c. 10, 10.Ephes. 2, 14. Add Isid. Pelusiotam b. 1. ep. 252. It can also be thought that just as the Jews were accustomed to tear their garments upon hearing blasphemy: so also the Temple, having seen the, as it were, horrendous crime of the Jews and heard their blasphemies, tore its veil as if it were a garment. But it is asked here, 1. When did these miracles happen? Resp. the common opinion is that they happened after the death of Christ. The Evangelist Luke indeed places it before the death of Christ: but this seems to have been done by him because he wished to join the miracles, according to August. b. 3. on the Consensus of the Evangelists ch. 19. Q. 2. Whether it is about the exterior veil i.e. that which was spread before the Priestly temple, or rather about the interior i.e. that which was spread before the adytum or holy of holies, here is the discourse? Resp. that this, not that, is understood in this place, the veil, teach B. Par. in H. E. Dn. D. Friedl. H. Grotius in this place, and they think that this is established especially from the fact that the exterior veil is called in H. S. κάλυμμα, but the interior either nakedly καταπέτασμα as in this place, or with the epithet δεύτερον καττέτασμα, as Ebr. 9, 3. Q. 3. What was the proper significance of this tearing? Resp. Although various things were signified by that tearing, and indeed 1. The entry of Christ the high Priest into the holy of holies, Ebr. 9, 12. coll. with Lev. 16, 12. 2. The fulfillment of those things which were prefigured by that furniture contained in the holy of holies. conf. Eph. 5, 2.Ebr. 5, 7.16.Ioh. 6, 33. 3. The violent laceration of Christ's body, by which as a veil the divinity του λόρου was personally covered in the assumed humanity, Ebr. 10, 19. conf. Ioh. 2, 19. 4. The uncovering of the figures of the O. T., by which Christ with his benefits was as it were wrapped, brought about by Christ's passion and death. 5. The abolition of Jewish ceremonies, Dan. 9, 27.Ebr. 9, 10.Col. 2, 16. 17. 6. The removal of the distinction between Jews and gentiles, Gal. 3, 28.Eph. 2, 14. 7. The detestation of the unspeakable crime of the Jews, committed in the accusation and condemnation of the innocent Christ. As B. Par. shows at greater length H. E. p. 2038 2039. However, the most important cause of this tearing seems to Grotius in this place, which he himself also deduces at length, and B. Par. also brings up in the said place, the opening of the approach to heavenly things acquired through the death of Christ. To which point Rom. 3, 25.1. Cor. 13, 12.Ebr. 9, 8.) *

* (And the earth was moved. Isidore of Pelusium, book 2, epistle 132. The earth itself was moved and shaken, seeking a place to which it might flee, so that it might not behold that crime. Saint Augustine has similar things in sermon 120, on the Season. The earth was moved, as if desiring to leap upon those blasphemers, so that it might swallow them alive. compare Joel 3, 16. Therefore, the earthquake was made 1. for the designation of its Lord, Ps. 24, 1. 2. for the signification of divine wrath, Ps. 18, 8. Amos 8, 8. 3. For the testimony of the majesty and innocence of Christ, compare B. Par. Harm. Pass. ch. 203. Binchium in Mellif. Book 3, p. 375. it can also be added. 4. that this was done for a mystical signification, namely, that the world is to be moved, and that a new state of it was to come forth from the death of Christ, Is. 65. 17. Blessed Par. also shows in the same place that by this earthquake not only the mountain of Golgotha, and the whole city, but also the neighboring regions were horribly shaken.) *

Latin:

* (v. 51. Velum templi scissum est. Christus enim, postquam per proprium sanguinem ingressus sanctum sanctorum est, aeternamq; redemtionem invenit, Ebr. 9, 12. abrogavit cultum Leviticum, sustulitq; velum, ut ad thronum DEI, ad propitiatorium liber nobis pateat aditus. Vid. Daniel. 9, 27.Ebr. 9, 8.c. 10, 10.Ephes. 2, 14. Adde Isid. Pelusiotam l. 1. ep. 252. Potest etiam cogitari, quòd sicuti Iudaei auditâ blasphemiâ vestes suas disrumpere solebant: ita & Templum, viso quasi horrendo Iudaeorum scelere atque auditis eorundem blasphemiis velum suum tanquam vestem disruperit. Quaeritur autem hîc, 1. Quando miracula haec contigerint? Resp. communis sententia est, contigisse post Christi mortem. Evangelista quidem Lucas ponit ante mortem Christi: sed propterea hoc ab eo factum videtur, quia voluit miracula coniungere, iuxta August. l. 3. de Consensu Evangel. c. 19. Q. 2. Num de exteriori velo h. e. quod templo Sacerdotali oppansum, an vero de interiori h. e. quod adyto s. sancto sanctorum oppansum erat, hîc sermo sit? Resp. hoc, non illud intelligi h. l. velum docent. B. Par. in H. E. Dn. D. Friedl. H. Grotius h. l. idque potissimum inde constare putant, quòd exterius velum dicatur in Sc. S. κάλυμμα, interius verò vel nudè καταπέτασμα ut h. l. vel cum epitheto δεύτερον καττέτασμα, ceu Ebr. 9, 3. Q. 3. Quaenam propria scissurae huius fuerit signifieatio? Resp. Licet varia scissione illa fuerint significata, & quidem 1. Christi summi Sacerdotis in sanctum sanctorum introitio, Ebr. 9, 12. coll. cum Lev. 16, 12. 2. Eorum, quae suppellectili illa in sancto sanctorum contentâ, praefigurata fuerunt, impletio. conf. Eph. 5, 2.Ebr. 5, 7.16.Ioh. 6, 33. 3. violenta Christi corporis, quo quasi velo divinitas του λόρου personaliter in adsumta humanitate fuit tecta, Ebr. 10, 19. laceratio. conf. Ioh. 2, 19. 4. figurarum V. T. quibus Christus cum suis beneficiis quasi involutus fuit, Christi passione ac morte facta retectio. 5. Iudaicarum ceremoniarum abolitio, Dan. 9, 27.Ebr. 9, 10.Col. 2, 16. 17. 6. Discriminis inter Iudaeos & gentes sublatio, Gal. 3, 28.Eph. 2, 14. 7. Sceleris Iudaeorum nefandi, in Christi innocentis accusatione ac condemnatione commissi, detestatio. Uti pluribus ostendit B. Par. H. E. p. 2038 2039. Potissima tamen scissionis huius causa Grotio in h. l. videtur, quam ipse etiam prolixè deducit, ac B. quoq; Par. d. l. adducit, aditûs ad coelestia per Christi mortem acquisita apertio. Quo spectant Rom. 3, 25.1. Cor. 13, 12.Ebr. 9, 8.) *

* (Et terra mota est. Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 2. ep. 132. Terra ipsa movebatur & concutiebatur, locum quo fugeret, quaerens, ut ne scelus illud perspiceret. Similia habet S. Augustinus serm. 120. de Tempore. Commota fuit terrae, quasi insilire cupiens istis blasphemis, ut vivos eos absorberet. conf. Io-el. 3, 16. Factus igitur terrae motus est 1. ad Domini sui designationem, Ps. 24, 1. 2. ad irae divinae significationem, Ps. 18, 8. Amos. 8, 8. 3. Ad maiestatis & innocentiae Christi testificationem, conf. B. Par. Harm. Pass. c. 203. Binchium in Mellif. L. 3. p. 375. potest quoque addi. 4. quòd hoc factum fuerit ob mysticum significationem, videl. quòd orbis terrarum sit commovendus, quòdque novus eius status ex Christi morte sit proventurus, Es. 65. 17. Ostendit etiam B. Par. l. c. isthoc terrae motu non montem solùm Golgotha, totamq urbem, sed & vicinas regiones horribiliter fuisse concussas.) *

## 27:52
* (v. 52. The rocks were rent. Namely, the stones spoke, Luke -9, 40. while men were silent, and the disciples were struck dumb with fear. It was also mystically signified that the stony hearts of the Gentiles were to be softened by the blood of Christ for the receiving of the faith. O truly hard, nay, harder than stones, are the breasts of the Jews! The rocks are rent, but their hearts are hardened: their immovable hardness remains, while the world is shattered, exclaims St. Ambrose in his book on Luke. Otherwise, it is established that the breaking of rocks has the signification of divine wrath. See 1 Kings 19, 11. Nahum 1, 6. Compare also Ps. 114, 7. 8.) *

Latin:

* (v. 52. Petrae scissae sunt. Lapides nempe loquuti sunt, Luc. -9, 40. silentibus hominibus, & prae metu obmutescentibus discipulis. Significatum quoque mysticè fuit, emollienda Christi sauguine esse saxea gentilium corda ad suscipiendam fidem. O dura verò, imò saxis duriora pectora Iudaeorum! finduntur petrae, sed horum corda durantur: horum immobilis duritia manet, orbe concasso, exclamat S. Ambrosius lib. in Lucam. Aliàs constat, quòd petrarum ruptura habeat significationem irae divivae. Vid. 1. Reg. 19, 11.Nahum. 1, 6. Conf. etiam Ps. 114, 7. 8.) *

## 27:53
* (v. 3. The monuments were opened. Concerning the sepulchers of the ancients and the great expenses made upon them, let Ioh. de Pineda, Comment. on c. 3 of Job v. 14. n. 4, Dn. D. Quensted, Dissert. on Burial, Kirchmannus on the rite of funerals, and others be consulted. In this place we note at least the allegory which Jerome uses in his letter to Hedibia, q. 8. Monuments, he writes, of which it is written; You are sepulchers whitened on the outside, etc. are therefore opened, that they might go out from them, who were previously dead in infidelity, and might live with Christ rising and coming to life. Compare Isidore of Pelusium, b. 1, ep. 253. At the very moment of Christ's death, the monuments were indeed opened, so that it might appear more clearly that he through death might destroy him who had the empire of death, Heb. 2, 14. Nevertheless, those buried in them were only raised and went out after Christ's resurrection, as will be taught shortly in v. 53.) *

And many bodies etc. Whether those who rose with Christ died again, Viegas discusses widely on both sides in Apocalypse, p. 28. * (Augustine seems to embrace the affirmative opinion in ep. 99 to Evodius. Theophylact in this place, Thomas Aquinas in part 1, q. 33, art. 2, Franc. Lucas and Barradius in this place, and Dominicus à Soto in dist. 43, q. 2, art. 1, in 4 of the Sentences, establish the same. The negative opinion pleases St. Jerome, Anselm, and Bede in this place, Clement of Alexandria in book 6 of the Stromata, Eusebius in book 4 of the Evangelical Demonstration, c. 12, Epiphanius in heresy 75, and Ambrose in the Psalm, which B. Par. also proves at length in the Evangelical Harmony, c. 203, p. 2042; Corn. à Lapide follows the same in Acts of the Apostles, p. 87. D.) *

* (v. 53. After his resurrection, viz. of Christ. And thus, namely αὐτοῶν in the singular, the most approved Greek Codices read, which the Syrian and the Persian also follow: the Arab, however, seems to have read ἀμτ-, for thus he translates: And they went out of their monuments& after their resurrection they entered &c. The Ethiopian otherwise still, having it thus: And they went out of their sepulchers, & entered into the holy city,after they had been raised. But the reading by αὐτοῶ is genuine, and it is therefore certain that the bodies of the Saints did not rise at the time of the passion of Christ (as indeed the Jesuit Becanus writes in lib. 1. Manual. Controvers. cap. 8. n. 62.), but that this resurrection of the Saints happened only after the resurrection of Christ. And Cornelius à Lapide rightly observed this and proves it from v. 53. and Coloss. 1, 18. add. 1. Cor. 15, 20.Apoc. 1, 5. add. Alphons. Mendoza Controv. Theol. pag. 426. Nor is there any reason for anyone to say that even before then, both in the O. T. by the Prophets, and in the N. T. by Christ, some had been raised, so that thus nothing prevents these also from having been raised before Christ. For those who were raised in the O. Testament by the Prophets, and in the N. Testament by Christ, died again, which is the common opinion. See besides our own, H. Grotius in h. l. but these rose to immortal life: whence it is fitting that Christ should precede them. Although it may also be said that he himself is called the firstfruits of them that sleep, not so much in respect of time, as of virtue, inasmuch as not only did he himself rise by his own virtue: but also our resurrection is the fruit and effect of the death and resurrection of Christ. See B. Par. Harm. Ev. p. 2041. Compare the treatise ascribed to Justin Martyr under the title Q-. & Respp. ad Orthodoxos Q. 80. Whence also Dan. Heinsius determines, that these saints, as soon as the monuments were opened, were also raised, and went out of them, although they entered into the holy city only after the resurrection of Christ. Dn. D. Friedlieb seems to agree with this opinion p. 217. Let Simon Episcopius also be compared lib. 3. Instit. Theol. s. 4. c. 17. But Becanus asks, where were the souls of these, before they were recalled to life? Not, he continues, in the place of damnation, because there is no redemption there. Nor in the place of beatitude, dinis, because otherwise it would not have been a benefit but a punishment, if they had had to return from heavenly beatitude to this mortal life. He concludes: It remains therefore that they were in another place, which was distinguished from both, namely in Purgatory. Resp. By conceding that they were in the place of beatitude, (See B. D. Fewrb. Fasc. 5. Diss. Theol. Di p. 7. §. 40. B. D. Meisn. Ἀσθρωπ. sacrae Decad. 1. Disp. 2. q. 2. §. 22. seqq. B. Par. L. de Morte §. 86.) although their souls were indeed recalled then, so that they might be joined to their bodies, and in them might likewise enjoy eternal beatitude as Christ ascended, yet it by no means follows from this that that resuscitation or translation of those blessed souls from the place of beatitude was a punishment, since they did not return to this mortal life, i.e., so that they were forced to live a mortal life again, but rather to an immortal one, or so that they might fully enjoy their bodies and soon eternal joys. See B. Par. Hom. Acad part. 2. p. 104. Although there may perhaps be some among the ancients who think that they were raised to a mortal life, i.e., that after their appearance they returned to the places from which they came out, in which opinion they are reported to be by Alph. Mendoza Controv. Theol. p. 425. Theophylactus & Euthymius in h. l. also Augustine ep. 99. and Thomas 3. p. q. 53. art. 3. ad. 2. yet more correctly Origen l. 2. in Epistolam ad Rom, Clement of Alexandria l. 6. Strom. Justin Martyr q. 65. Eusebius l. 4. Demonstr. Evangelic. Gregory of Nyssa l. de Cogn. DEI, Remigius in Matth. (whom the author of the Gloss follows in h. l. the same Thomas Aquinas in c. 27. Matt. & 4. S. d. 43. q. 1. art. 3. Carthus. ibid. q. 6. Cardinal Caietanus in h. l. Iansenius in Concord. c. 143. Corn. à Lap. in 1. Cor. 15. and the same in h. l. Franciscus Suarez t. 2. in 3. part. Thomae q. 53. art. 3.) determine that they were raised to an immortal life. And Anselm thinks this so manifest in h. l. that he does not hesitate to write, that by no reason should faith be given to the rashness of those who say that they (the raised) afterwards returned to ashes. But it is also worth the effort to note that among those who rose with Christ, and also ascended into Heaven, some are also counted by the Papists whose relics others trifle are still preserved here and there. Thus the Jesuit Pineda in c. 19, 25. of Job thinks that then likewise

to have risen again Daniel and his three companions, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, whose remains and bodies, however, are shown at Rome in the church of St. Adrian, other Jesuits testify, see Corn. à Lap. here and Lorinus on Acts c. 2, 29. Thus Franc. Lucas Brugensis, following Epiphanius in the Ancoratus, maintains that Zacharias, Simeon, John the Baptist seemed to have risen again then, and yet the head of the latter is shown at Rome and Amiens, a finger at Florence, and the ashes of the rest of the body at Genoa, as Corn. à Lapide testifies in this place, but about this matter elsewhere.) *

v. 53. They came into the holy city * (so also it is said Matt. 5.) * i. e. which once had been such. * (see Hugo Grotius in Quat. Ev. p. 408.) * Now, however, it was nothing less than holy. Jerome on c. 26 of Matthew: Sometimes in Scripture the former name remains even when the thing is changed. Luke 19, 46. It can, however, be said that it was still holy, 1. on account of the divine ordination, which the infidelity of men did not remove, Rom. 3, 3. 2. On account of the holy and ordinary office of teaching the word of GOD, Matt. 23, 2. 3. on account of the holy remnants of believers, Rom. 11, 1. & 2. * (For the Church is accustomed to be named from the nobler, i. e. better, not from the greater.) * Most especially, however, because the Holy of holies, as a great King, inhabited it, Matt. 5. 33. Sanctius in Es. p. 509: It was called holy on account of the holiness of the temple, and because it was a religious duty to perform many sacred rites, and those the principal ones, elsewhere than in this city. * (Those resurrected saints are said to have come into the holy city, because in former times the dead were buried outside the city, concerning which matter let Ioh. de Pineda Comm. in Job c. 3, 14. n. 4, Ramirez in Pentec. p. 158, and others be consulted. Cf. note above on v. 7.) *

* (They appeared to many, understand to believers, not to all the people, just as Christ also did, Acts 10, 41. If, however, those holy ones resurrected with Christ appeared not to any chance passersby by the constitution of a natural body, but at least to some by a special dispensation, it follows that not every body is visible, and thus it is not permitted to conclude that because the body of Christ is not visible in the Holy Eucharist, it is not present there either. Against the Calvinists: for it must be known that glorified bodies are πνευματικὰ on account of ποιότητας πνευματικας, 1 Cor. 15, 44. If, however, it is not a perpetual truth in other glorified bodies that they are always seen, how much less will that have a place in the glorified body of Christ, and the same assumed into the hypostasis of the Son of GOD, and raised to the right hand of GOD. Concerning which matter more things may be seen in B. D. Meisn. Consid. Theol. phot. p. 874. seqq., B. D. Hutt. LL. Mai. p. 703. 704., B. Par. L. de S. Coena §. 115., also L. de vitâ aet. §. 101., B. Schröderum in Sceptro Regali p. 639. seq. But the question concerning these resurrected saints, whether they ascended when Christ ascended, or whether they died again after the apparition? Some maintain the latter, and they attempt to prove it from Heb. 11, 13. & Rev. 6, 11. But B. D. Waltherus Miscell. Theol. p. 391, following Epiphanius against heresies, heresy 75, more correctly affirms the former; Ambrose in Ps. excellently confirms that opinion in the cited place. cf. notes on v. 52, on the words: many bodies. If, however, these resurrected ones ascended with Christ as He ascended, which many Papists, led by the cited place, admit themselves, it is clear that the Papists ineptly allege the example of these for the apparition of the dead. And Mendoza himself seems to acknowledge this in Controv. Theol. p. 427.) *

Latin:

* (v. 3. Monumenta aperta sunt. De sepulcris veterum magnisque impensis in illa factis consulatur Ioh. de Pineda Comment. in c. 3. Iobi v. 14. n. 4. Dn. D. Quensted Dissert. de Sepult. Kirchmannus de ritu funerum, alii. Hoc loco saltem notamus allegoriam, quâ utitur Hieron. ad Hedibiam q. 8. Monumenta, scribit, de quibus scriptum est; Vos estis sepulcra extrinsecus dealbata &c. ideò sunt aperta, ut egrederentur de iis, qui priùs in infidelitate mortui erant, & cum resurgente Christo atvivente viverent. Confer Isid. Pelusiotam l. 1. ep. 253. In ipso quidem mortis Christi articulo monumenta aperta sunt, quò clariùs nempe appareret, ipsum per mortem abolere eum, qui mortis habebat imperium,Ebr. 2, 14. Attamen sepulti in illis demum post Christi resurrectionem & suscitati fuerunt, & egressi sunt, ut mox v. 53. idocebitur.) *

Et multa corpora &c. An hi, qui cum Christo resurrexerunt, iterum fuerint mortui, latè in utramque partem disputat Viegas in Apocal. p. 28. * (Affirmativam sententiam amplecti videtur Augustinus ep. 99. ad Evodium. Idem statuunt Theophylactus in h. l. Thomas de Aquino parte 1. q. 33. art. 2. Franc. Lucas ac Barradius in h. l. Dominicus à Soto dist. 43. q. 2. art. 1. in 4. Sententiarum. Negativa arridet S. Hieronymo, Anselmo, Bedae h. l. Clementi Alexandrino lib. 6. Strom. Euseb. l. 4. Demonst. Evang. c. 12. Epiphanio haer. 75. Ambrosio in Psalm. quam etiam prolixè probat B. Par. Harm. Evang. c. 203. p. 2042. sequitur eandem Corn. à Lapide in Act. Apost. p. 87. D.) *

* (v. 53. Post resurrectionem eius, sc. Christi. Atque ita, nempe αὐτοῶν in singulari, legunt Codd. Graeci probatissimi, quos sequuntur etiam Syrus ac Persa: Arabs tamen ἀμτ- legisse videtur, ita enim vertit: Et exierunt è monumentis suis& post resurrectionem suam ingressi sunt &c. Aethiops adhuc aliter, ita habens: Et exierunt è sepulcris suis, & introierunt in civitatem sanctam,postquam suscitati fuissent. Verùm lectio per αὐτοῶ est genuina, certumque adeo est, quòd corpora Sanctorum non tempore passionis Christi surrexerint (uti quidem Iesuita Becanus lib. 1. Manual. Controvers. cap. 8. n. 62. scribit,) sed quòd haec resurrectio Sanctorum contigerit post Christi demum refurrectionem. Idque rectè observavit Cornelius à Lapide probatque ex v. 53. ac Coloss. 1, 18. add. 1. Cor. 15, 20.Apoc. 1, 5. add. Alphons. Mendoza Controv. Theol. pag. 426. Nec est, quòd aliquis dicat, etiam iam antè tum in V. T. à Prophetis, tum in N. T. à Christo quosdam fuisse resuscitatos, ut ita nihil obstet, quò minùs & hi ante Christum fuerint resuscitati. Etenim qui in V. Test. à Prophetis, & in N. Test. à Christo fuere resuscitati, iterum sunt mortui, quae communis sententia est. Vide praeter nostrates, H. Grotium in h. l. sed hi ad vitam immortalem resurrexerunt: unde conveniens est, ut Christus eos praecederet. Quamvis etiam dici possit, ipsum dici primitias dormientium, non tam respectu temporis, quàm virtutis, utpote cùm non solùm ipse propriâ virtute resurrexerit: verùm etiam resurrectio nostra sit fructûs & effectus mortis, & resurrectionis Christi. Vid. B. Par. Harm. Ev. p. 2041. Confer tractatū, Iustino Martyri adscriptum sub titulo Q-. & Respp. ad Orthodoxos Q. 80. Unde etiam Dan. Heinsius statuit, quòd sancti hi statim ac monumenta fuerunt operta, etiam resuscitati sint, ac prodierint ex illis, licet post Christi resurrectionem demum in urbem sanctam fuerint ingressi. Adstipulari sententiae huic videtur Dn. D. Friedlieb p. 217. Conferatur etiam Simon Episcopius lib. 3. Instit. Theol. s. 4. c. 17. Sed quaerit Becanus, ubi animae horum fuerint, antequam ad vitam revocarentur? Non, pergit, in loco damnationis, quia ibi nulla est redemtio. Nec in loco beatitudinis, dinis, quia alioqui non fuisset beneficiū sed poena, si ex colesti beatitudine debuissent redire ad hanc vitam mortalem. Concludit: Superest ergo, fuisse in alio loco, qui ab utroque distinguebatur, nempe in Purgatorio. Resp. Concedēdo, fuisse in loco be atitudinis, (Vid. B. D. Fewrb. Fasc. 5. Diss. Theol. Di p. 7. §. 40. B. D. Meisn. Ἀσθρωπ. sacrae Decad. 1. Disp. 2. q. 2. §. 22. seqq. B. Par. L. de Morte §. 86.) licet verò revocatae eorum animae tum fuerint, ut corporibus suis iungerentur, inq; ac eum illis Christo adscendente itidē aeternâ fruerentur beatitudine, minime tamen hinc sequitur, resuscitationem illam vel translationem animarum istarum beatarum è loco beatitudinis fuisse poenam, cùm non reversae fuerint in hanc vitam mortalem, h. e. ut iterum mortalem colere vitam cogerentur, sed potiùs ad immoratalem, sive ut plenèm suis corporibus mox aeternis fruerentur gaudiis. Vid. B. Par. Hom. Acad part. 2. p. 104. Licet verò sint fortè nōnulli inter veteres, qui existiment, resuscitatos fuisse illos ad vitam mortalem, h. e. quòd post apparitionem reversi fuerint ad loca, unde exierunt, quâ in sententia esse referuntur ab Alph. Mendoza Controv. Theol. p. 425. Theophylactus & Euthymius in h. l. it. Augustinus. ep. 99. ac Thomas 3. p. q. 53. art. 3. ad. 2. rectiùs tamē Origenes l. 2. in Epistolam ad Rom Clemens Alexan. drinus l. 6. Strom. Iustinus Martyr q. 65. Eusebius l. 4. Demonstr. Evangelic. Gregorius Nyssenus l. de Cogn. DEI, Remigivis in Matth. (quos sequuntur autor Glossae ad h. l. idem Thomas de Aquino in c. 27. Matt. & 4. S. d. 43. q. 1. art. 3. Carthus. ibid. q. 6. Cardinalis Caietanus in h. l. Iansenius in Concord. c. 143. Corn. à Lap. in 1. Cor. 15. idemque in h. l. Franciscus Suarez t. 2. in 3. part. Thomae q. 53. art. 3.) statuunt, fuisse eos ad vitammortalem resuscitatos. Et hoc adeò manifestum putat Anselmus in h. l. scribere non dubitet, nullâ ratione istorum temeritati fidem accommodandam esse, qui illos (resuscitatos) postea reversos in cinerem dicunt. Sed pretium quoque operae est notare, quòd inter eos, qui cum Christo resurrexerunt, atque etiam in Coelum adscenderunt, numerentur quoque à Pontificiis nonnullis illi, quorum reliquias adhuc hinc inde adservari, alii nugantur. Sic Iesuita Pineda in c. 19, 25. Iobi censet, tunc pariter

refurrrexisse Danielem ac tres eius socios, Ananiam, Azariam & Misaelem, quorum tamen reliquiae ac corpora ostendi Romae in templo S. Adriani, testantur alii Iesuitae, vit Corn. à Lap. hîc & Lorinus in Act. c. 2, 29. Sic Franc. Lucas Brugensis sequutus Epiphanium in Ancorato statuit, videri tunc refurrexisse Zach, Simeonem, Iob. Baptistam, & huius tamen caput Romae & Ambiani, digitus Florentiae, reliqui corporis cineres Genuae ostenduntur, teste Corn. à Lapide. h. l. sed de hâc re alibi.) *

v. 53. Venerunt in sanctam civitatem * (sic quoq; diciturMatth. 5.) * i. e. quae olim talis fuerat. * (vid. Hugonem Grotium in Quat. Ev. p. 408.) * Iam vero nihilminùs, quàm sancta erat. Hieronymus in c. 26. Matth. Aliquando in Scriptur â mutatâre pristinum nomen manet.Luc. 19, 46. Potest tamen dici, quòd adhuc sancta fuerit, 1. propter divinam ordinationem, quam hominum infidelitas non sustulit, Rom. 3, 3. 2. Propter sanctum & ordinarium docendi verbum DEI munus,Matth. 23, 2. 3.propter sanctas credentium reliquias,Rom. 11, 1. & 2. * (Ecclesia enim denominari solet â nobiliori s. meliori, non à maiori.) * Cum. primis verò quia Sanctus sanctorum, ceu magnus Rex eam inhabitabat, Matth. 5. 33. Sanctius in Es. p. 509. Vocata fuit sancta propter templi sanctitatem, & quia multa sacra eaque praecipua, alibi quàm in hac civitate obire, religio erat. * (Dicuntur sancti illi resuscitati venisse in sanctam civitatem, quia extra urbem mortui olim sepeliebantur, quâ de re consulantur Ioh. de Pineda Comm. in Iob. c. 3, 14. n. 4. Ramirez in Pentec. p. 158. alii. Conf. not. suprà ad v. 7.) *

* (Apparuerunt multis, intellige credentibus, non omni populo, quemadmodum & Christus, Act. 10, 41. Si verò non quibusvis obviis ex naturalis corporis constitutione, sed aliquibus saltem ex peculiari dispensatione sancti illi cum Christo resuscitati apparuerunt, sequitur, quòd non omne corpus sit visibile, adeoque non liceat colligere, quia corpus Christi in S. Eucharistia visibile non est, quòd nec ibi sit praesens. Contra Calvinianos Sciendum enim, quòd corpora glorificata sint πνευματικὰ propter ποιότητας πνευματικας, 1. Cor. 15, 44. Si verò in aliis glorificatis corporibus non est perpetuae veritatis, ut semper videantur, quantò minùs in glorificato corpore Christi, eodemq; in hypostasin Filii DEI adsumto, & ad dextram DEI evecto, id locum habebit. Quam in rem plura videantur apud B. D. Meisn. Consid. Theol. phot. p. 874. seqq. B. D. Hutt. LL. Mai. p. 703. 704. B. Par. L. de S. Coena §. 115. it. L. de vitâ aet. §. 101. B. Schröderum in Sceptro Regali p. 639. seq. Q. verò de his sanctis resuscitatis, num Christo adscendente adscenderint & ipsi, an verò post apparitionem iterum fuerint mortu? Posterius nonnulli statuunt, idque evincere conantur ex Ebr. 11, 13. & Apoc. 6, 11. Sed rectiùs affirmat prius. B. D. Waltherus Miscell. Theol. p. 391. sequutus Epiphan. contra heareses, haeresi, 75. Ambrosium in Ps. eamsententiam l. c. egregiè confirmat. conf. natata ad v. 52. ad verba: multa corpora, Si verò resuscitati hi cum Christo adscendente adscenderunt, id quod multi Pontificii d. l. adducti fatentur ipsi, patet, quòd ineptè horum exemplum pro apparitione mortuorum Papicolae allegent. Idque agnoscere ipse Mendoza videtur in Controv. Theol. p. 427.) *

## 27:54
* (v. 54. The centurion, however, etc. An example of a pious centurion, of which kind there is also mention above in c. 8, 8. 10. Acts 10, 1. 2.4.20. Regarding the custom, however, of those crucified being guarded by soldiers, let the commentators on Petronius be consulted.) *

* (Truly He was the Son of GOD. This centurion opposes his speech to the blasphemy of the Jews, that Christ was not the natural Son of GOD, and thus he remarkably declared his faith. Although indeed he had not yet known from the reading of Holy Scripture the mystery of the Trinity, and that Christ was the Son of GOD by eternal generation from God the Father, nothing, however, prevents it from being said that GOD miraculously and extraordinarily illuminated the intellect of this centurion, kindled faith in him, and converted him, an example of which we also have in the converted thief. He acknowledged, therefore, not only that Christ is just, not unjust, but also that He did not lie when He said that He was the own Son of GOD. see August. b. 3. on the Harmony of the Gospels. Jerome on this passage. By no means, therefore, did Hugo Grotius judge rightly concerning the faith of the centurion, who, having followed Beza, from then on, That the Centurion and the Roman soldiers were, he gathers, that they thought of Jesus in the same way as they thought of Hercules, Bacchus, Quirinus, etc. The contrary is evident from that which Luke ch. 23, 4. writes, that they glorified God, namely, the true God of Israel. But for this glorification it is required that the Son be honored, John 5, 23. not as Hercules or Quirinus, that is, as some Gentile god, but as the Son of the true God. But it is false that that knowledge of the sonship of Christ, that is, that He was begotten from eternity by GOD the Father, is not necessary for salvation, as Simon the Arminian Bishop argues, book 4, Instit. s. 2, c. 33. The contrary was solidly proven by Mr. Dr. Calovius in the Consideration of Arminianism, p. 114, seqq.) *

Latin:

* (v. 54. Centurio autem &c. Exemplum pii Centurionis, cuiusmodi etiam sit mentio suprà c. 8, 8. 10. Act. 10, 1. 2.4.20. De more autem crucifixos per milites custodiendi consulantur Commentatores ad Petronium.) *

* (Verè Filius DEI erat. Centurio hic opponit sermonem suum Iudaeorum blasphemiae, quòd Christus non esset naturalis Filius DEI, sieque egregiè fidem suam declaravit. Licet vero nondū ex S. S. lectione cognovisset mysterium Trinitatis, quòdq; Christus esset Filius DEI per aeternam generationem à Deo Patre, nihil tamen impedit, quò minus dicatur, DEUM miraculosè & extraordinariè Centurionis huius intellectum illuminasse, fidem in eo accendisse, eumq; convertisse, quale etiam exemplum in converso latrone habemus. Agnovit igitur non solùm, Christum est iustum, non-iniustum, verùm etiam, non mentitum esse ipsum, quando dixit, se esse Filium DEI proprium. vid. August. l. 3. de Cons. Evang. Hieronymus in h. l. Hautquaquam igitur dextrè de Centurionis fide iudicavit Hugo Grotius, qui Bezam sequutus exinde, quòd Centurio ac Milites Romani fuerunt, colligit, eos de Iesu ita existimasse, quomodo de Hercule, Baccho, Quirino existimabant. &c. Contrarium patet ex eo, quòd Lucas c. 23, 4. scribit. eos Deum glorificasse, verum sc. Israelis Deum. ad hanc vero glorificationem requiritur, ut Filius quohonoretur,Ioh. 5, 23. non ut Hercules vel Quirinus, h. e. ut Deus aliquis gentilis, sed ut veri Dei filius. Falsum autem est, quòd notitia illa filiationis Christi, quòd sc. ab aeterno sit genitus à DEO Patre, non sit ad salutem necessaria, ceu Simon Episcopus Arminianus disputat, l. 4. Instit. s. 2. c. 33, Contrarium solidè evicit Dn. D. Calovius in Arminianismi Consid. p. 114. seqq.) *

## 27:55
v. 55. There were women there, etc. Euthymius in this place. See the reversed order: the disciples had fled, but the female disciples remained standing by.) * * (

from afar. But John c. 19, 25. says that near the cross they stood. Resp. Near in this place denotes opposite or over against the cross, so that they stood neither entirely near to the soldiers, who were indeed the guards and would have prevented them, nor yet too far away, namely, so that they could conveniently see and hear Christ.) * * (

Ministering to him, that is, from their own resources, Luke 8, 3. ) * * (

Latin:

* (v. 55. Erant ibi mulieres &c. Euthymius in h. l. Vide conversum ordinem: discipuli fugerant, discipulae verò adsistentes permanebant.) *

* (à longè. At Ioh. c. 19, 25. dicit, quòd iuxta crucem steterint. Resp. Iuxta h. l. notat contrà vel ex adverso crucis, ita ut nec omninò propè à militibus quippe custodibus prohibitae, nec tamen etiam nimis remotè starent, videl, ut Christum commodè videre & audire potuerint.) *

* (Ministrantes ei, puta de suis facultatibus, Luc. 8, 3.) *

## 27:56
v. 56. Mary, of James, etc. See Cappell. in Spic. p. 39.) * * (

Latin:

* (v. 56. Maria, Iacobi &c. Vid. Cappell. in Spic. p. 39.) *

## 27:57
v. 57. And when evening had come, i.e., evening was beginning. Conf. Luke 24, 29. * (

* (A rich man from Arimathea. Not as if he lived in Arimathea, and therefore came from there, but because he was born there, but now was a Jerusalem Senator. But in the fact that Joseph is mentioned as rich, the prophecy of Isaiah 53, 9 was fulfilled, He gave his grave with the wicked, (because indeed in the vicinity the punishment was being taken from the wicked or criminals) & with the rich man, that is, at the rich man's in his deaths. that is, he was buried in the garden of the rich man Joseph. Thus the blessed Pareus explains this prophecy in Harm. Ev. cap. 205, p. 2070. B. Dr. Calixtus, Conc. Ev. 405. The question here, whether Joseph was an assessor of the Great Sanhedrin? Thus our own people, the blessed Pareus, determine in Harm. Ev. page 2060, and others, for that reason especially, because a little later it is mentioned concerning him that he did not consented by counsel and deed of his colleagues, conspiring in the death of Christ. But H. Grotius replies, that this argument is not sufficiently certain: since many also disapprove of many things, who do not have the right of suffrage: furthermore, there is no reason why those words should be taken precisely concerning that consultation of the last day, since before it had been deliberated several times concerning the matter of Jesus, and indeed as is credible, in a larger assembly, and into which besides the judges of the Sanhedrin also others, holding magistracy, had been called. But since the Holy Spirit seems here to look entirely to that last consultation of the Great Sanhedrin, nor is there any reason present which might persuade that this Joseph was not an assessor of the Great Sanhedrin, not undeservedly do we subscribe to the received opinion.) *

Ioseph. Note, just as the care of the newborn Christ was entrusted to Joseph, to whom indeed Mary was betrothed, so another Joseph claimed for himself the care of the dead and deceased Christ. The piety of the latter is praised, the chastity of the former. Just as the body of the deceased Jacob was honorably treated by his son Joseph, so here Christ’s [body] by Joseph, a disciple or spiritual son. He who wishes to receive Christ, let him be a Joseph, that is, pious and chaste. Let him likewise be rich in faith and good works.) * * (

Latin:

* (v. 57. Cùm autem vespera facta esset, i. e. inciperet vespera. Conf. Luc. 24, 29.

* (Homo dives ab Arimathia. Non quasi habitarit Arimathiae, adeoque inde venerit, sed quia inde fuit oriundus, iam nunc verò Senator Hierosolymitanus. In eo verò quòd Iosephus dives memoratur, impletum fuit vaticinium Esaiae 53, 9. De-t cum impiis sepulcrum eius, (quia nempe in vicinia supplicium sumebatut ab impiis seu sceleratis) & cum divite s. apud divitem in mortibus eius. h. e. in horto divitis Iosephi fuit sepultus. Ita exponunt hoc vaticinium B. Par. H. Ev. cap. 205. p. 2070. B. D. Calixtus Conc. Ev. 405. Q. hîc, num Iosephus hifuerit assessor Synedrii Magni? Ita statuunt è nostratibus B. Par. in Harm. Ev. pag. 2060. & alii. ob istam cumprimis rationem, quia paullò pòst de eo memoratur, quòd non consenserit consilio & facto Collegarum suorum, in Christi necem conspirantium. Ast regerit H. Grotius, argumentum hoc non satis esse certum: cùm multi multa etiam, qui ius suffragii non habent, improbent: praeterea non esse, quòd verba illa praecisè sumantur de illâ consultatione postremae diei, cùm antea quodeliberatum aliquoties de re Iesu fuerit, & quidem ut credibile, in conventu maiore, & in quem praeter Synedrii iudices etiam alii, magistratum gerentes vocati fuerint. Verùm cùm Sp Sanctus ad ultimam illam Synedrii M. consultationē omninò hîc respicere videatur, nec ulla adsit ratio, quae suadeat, quò minùs Iosephus hic Synedrii Magni Adsessor fuerit, non immeritò receptae sententiae subscribimus.) *

* (Ioseph. Nota, uti Christi nati cura commissa fuit Iosepho, cui quippe desponsata fuit Maria, ita Christi denati ac mortui curam alter sibi vendicavit Iosephus. Huius laudatur pietas, illius castitas. Ceu etiam Iacobi defuncti corpus â filio Iosepho fuit honorificè habitum, ita hîc Christi à Iosepho, discipulo s. filio spirituali. Qui Christum vult suscipere, Iosephus sit, h. e. pius & castus. Sit item dives in fide ac B. O.) *

## 27:58
v. 58. To be rendered i. e. to be given. Or because he had already been handed over to the soldiers to be crucified, it is said to be rendered: That the Roman magistrates were lenient in granting the bodies of those affected by capital punishment for burial, unless they had been condemned for treason or rebellion, is shown by Grotius, who may be consulted. Since, therefore, Pilate ordered the body of Christ to be rendered to Joseph, it seems it can be gathered from this that he himself by no means considered Christ to be such a one who had committed the crime of high treason.) * * (

Latin:

* (v. 58. Reddi i. e. dari. Vel quia iamtum traditum erat militibus ad crucifigendum, dicitur reddi: Faciles autem fuisse Romanos Magistratus in cōcedendis corporibus supplicio affectorū, nisi Maiestatis vel perduellionis essent damnati, ad sepulturam, ostendit Grotius, qui potest evolvi. Cùm igitur Pilatus Christi corpus Iosepho reddere iusserit, exinde colligi posse videtur, quòd ipse Christum minimè talem habuerit, qui crimen laesae Maiestatis commisisset) *

## 27:59
* (v. 59. He took the body of Christ, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth &c. By linen cloth is not understood here silk, (since not even the Princes of the Senate could be buried with silk) but a covering made of linen of no great price, H. Grotius warns in this place. Compare also what has been observed by B. Par. in Harm. Ev and others. He adds that although mention is made here of one linen cloth, it is certain, however, that there were several coverings with which the body was wrapped, and he gathers that from John 19, 40.c. 20, 6, 7. and even from John 11, 44. The burial of Christ was therefore glorious Is. 11, 10. although the impious have despised it. To which Isaiah Ch. 53. 9. refers, concerning which statement B. D. Glass. Gr. S. p. 3. B. D. Fewrb. Fasc. 2. diss. Theol. p. 4. 5. B. Par. Harm. Evang. c. 195. p. 1918 and c. 205. p. 2070. B. D. Quistorp. in the said place can be consulted. Furthermore, he wraps Jesus in a clean linen cloth, who has received Him with a pure mind, according to Jerome. Indeed, also with a pure body. For the linen cloth of the soul, writes Theophylact on ch. 15 of Mark, is the body as a garment. It is necessary, therefore, not only to receive the divine body of the Lord in a pure soul, but also in a pure body. Let us, therefore, also embrace Christ with the linen cloth of pure faith, let us season Him with myrrh, that is, with serious repentance, which is gently bitter and of a most sweet odor before the Lord, and also with aloes, that is, let us repress the rot of vices with the tolerance of calamities. Let us place the Savior in the monument of a heart that is entirely renewed, and hewn from the rock through the firmness of a good purpose: let us also roll the stone, lest the love of this world penetrate beyond the love of the Lord. Let B. D. Calixtus Concord. Ev. p. 405 be seen, add entirely B. P. H. E. p. 2064.) *

Latin:

* (v. 59. Accepit corpus Christi, involvitsindone mundâ &c. Per sindonem non intelligi hî sericum, (quippe cùm ne Principes quidem Senatûs cum serico sepeliri potuerint) sed operimentum ex lino pretii haut magni, monet H. Grotius in h. l. Conf. quoq; quae à B. Par. in Harm. Ev aliisq; observata. Addit ille licet unius sindonis fiat hîc mentio, certum tamen, plura fuisse operimenta, quibus corpus involutum fuerit, idq; colligit ex Ioh. 19, 40.c. 20, 6, 7. quin etiam ex Ioh. 11 44. Fuit ergo Christi sepultura gloriosa Es. 11, 10. quamvis impii eam spreverint. Quo respicit Esaias C. 53. 9. de quo dicto consuli possunt B. D. Glass. Gr. S. p. 3. B. D. Fewrb. Fasc. 2. diss. Theol. p. 4. 5. B. Par. Harm. Evang. c. 195. p. 1918 ac. c. 205. p. 2070. B. D. Quistorp. in d. l. Coeterùm ille in sindone mundâ involvit Iesum, qui purâ mente eum susceperit, iuxta Hieronymum. Quin & corpore puro. Nam sindon animae, scribit Theophylactus in c. 15. Marci, est corpus quasi vestis. Oportet igitur non solùm in anima pura suscipere divinum corpus Domini, sed & in corpore puro. Amplectamur igitur & nos Christum sindone mundae fidei, condiamus myrrhâ h. e. seriâ poenitentiâ, quae leniter amara, & suavissimi coram Domino est odoris, nec non aloë, h. e. tolerantiâ calamitatum putredinem vitiorum reprimamus. Reponamus Salvatorem in monumento cordis prorsùs innovati, & per firmitatem boni propositi è petra excisi: advolvamus etiam saxum, ne praeter amorem Domini penetret amor huius seculi. Videatur B. D. Calixtus Concord. Ev. p. 405. add. omninò B. P. H. E. p. 2064.) *

## 27:60
* (v. 60. in a new monument. August. Just as in the womb of the virgin Mary no one was conceived before Him, no one after Him: so in this new monument, no one was buried before Him, no one after Him. Theophylact in this place He hid in a new sepulcher (Joseph the body of Christ,) in which no one had ever been placed ( Luke 23, 53.) That which was done by divine dispensation, lest when the Lord had risen, someone could say that another who had been buried there before Him had died and risen. The honor of burial was deservedly shown to the most holy body of Christ, because it was the temple of the whole fullness of the Godhead, Col. 2, 9. Not undeservedly also are the bodies of deceased Christians honestly buried by us. D. Chrysostom brings forward some causes of this in Hom. 4. ep. to the Hebrews. Add Lactant. book 6. of divine Institutions c. 12. August. book 1. of the City of God cap. 13. compare also B. P. L. on Death §. 79. 80. How Herod was deterred, desiring to open the sepulcher of David, Josephus shows in book 16. A. I. c. 11. To this can be referred that the action of a violated sepulcher brings infamy and is deservedly punished. See Ulpian. l, 1. D. Concerning the Violation of a Sepulcher.

Marcell. l. 8. D. Of the Same. Paul l. 11. Of the Same. Compare Kirchm. on Roman Funerals book 3. c. 26) *

* (That he had departed. Christ wished to be buried in another's sepulcher. For he who did not have a house in life, neither has a sepulcher, but is laid down in another's, and since he is naked, he is clothed by Joseph.) *

* (Hewn from rock. Theophylact on chapter 15 of Mark allegorizes: Let us receive the body of Jesus through communion, and let us place it in a monument hewn from rock, that is, in a mindful soul, which may not forget God. But let that soul be hewn from the rock, that is, from Christ, who is the rock, in whom we shall be able to stand. *

* (At the door of the monument. See Analysis on chapter 28, 2.) *

Latin:

* (v. 60. in monumento novo. August. Sicut in Mariae virginis utero nemo ante illum, nemo post illum conceptus est: ita in hoc monumento novo, nemo ante illum, nemo post illum sepultus est. Theophylactus in h. l. In sepulcro novo recondidit (Iosephus corpus Christi,) in quo nullus unquam positus erat ( Luc. 23, 53.) Id quod divina dispensatione factum, ne quum resurrexisset Dominus, posset quis dicere, quòd alius ante eum sepultus illic, mortuus resurrexisset. Sepulturae honor meritò exhibitus fuit sanctissimo corpori Christi, quia fuit templum totius plenitudinis Deitatis, Col. 2, 9. Non immeritò quoque Christianorum defunctorum corpora à nobis honestè sepeliuntur. Cuius aliquot causas affert D. Chrysostomus Hom. 4. ep. ad Ebr. Add. Lactant. lib. 6. divini Instit. c. 12. August. l. 1. de C. D. cap. 13. conf. quoque B. P. L. de Morte §. 79. 80. Quomodo Herodes deterritus fufuerit, Davidis sepulcrum aperire cupiens, ostendit Iosephus l. 16. A. I. c. 11. Huc referri potest, quòd sepulcri violati actio infamet ac meritò puniatur. Vid. Ulphian. l, 1. D. De. Sepulcr.

Violar. Marcell. l. 8. D. Eod. Paulus l. 11. Eod. Conf. Kirchm. de Funer. Rom. lib. 3. c. 26) *

* (Quod exciderat. Alieno Christus sepulcro voluit sepeliri. Qui enim non habuit domum in vita, neque sepulcrum habet, sed in alieno deponitur, & cum sit nudus, à Iosepho vestitur.) *

* (Inpetra. Theoph. in c. 15. Marci alleg. Accipiamus corpus Iesu per communionem, & collocemus in monumento exciso ex petra h. e. in anima memori, quae Deum non obliviscatur. Sit autem anima illa ex petra excisa h. e. à Christo, qui est petra, in quâ consistere poterimus.) *

* (Ad ostium monumenti. Vid. Anal. ad c. 28, 2.) *

## 27:63
* v. 63. ὁπλἀνος. See John 7, 12.2. Cor. 6, 8.) *

* (He said while living: after three days I rise again. Q. Whence the Pharisees had this, when Christ had predicted this privately to the disciples, but never so clearly to the Pharisees or the people? Resp. Theophylact in this place: It can be said that they knew it from the figure of Jonah, especially when Christ said: As Jonah was three days in the belly of the whale, so also I shall be in the belly of the earth. Or from that which he said: destroy this temple: Which they did not understand at first, but thought that he meant it concerning the Jewish temple, and therefore they brought this testimony against him: but now when they have known that he had called his own body a sepulcher, they are afraid. *

* ( Μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας. Compare above 40. chapter 12. Mark 8, 31. See the notes above on chapter 12, 40. also on Mark 8, 31.) *

* (And the last error will be &c. A proverbial expression. See Luke 11, 26. above chapter 12, 45.2. Peter 2, 20.) *

Latin:

* v. 63. ὁπλἀνος. Vid. Ioh. 7, 12.2. Cor. 6, 8.) *

* (Dixit vivens: post tres dies resurgo. Q. Unde hoc habuerint Pharisaei, cùm Christus hoc privatim ad discipulos praedixerit, nunquam verò ita clarè Pharisaeis vel populo? Resp. Theophylactus in h. l. Dici potest, quòd à figura Ionae cognoverint, praesertim quum Christus dixerit: Sicut Ionas fuit tribus diebus in ventre ceti, ita & ego in ventre terrae. Vel ex illo, quod dixit, solvite templum hoc: Quod priūs non intellexerunt, sed putabant, quòd de templo Iudaico sentiret, & ideo testimonium hoc contra eum protulerunt: nunc autem ubi congnoverunt, quòd sepulcrum dixerat copus proprium, timent.) *

* ( Μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας. Conf. suprà 40. c. 12. Marc. 8, 31. Vid. notata suprà ad c. 12, 40. it. ad Marc. 8, 31.) *

* (Et erit novissimus error &c. Proverbialis locutio. Vid. Luc. 11, 26. suprà c. 12, 45.2. Petr. 2, 20.) *

## 27:66
* (v. 66. They secured the sepulcher with a sealed stone &c. Well Theophylact in this place: They indeed (the Pharisees) are goaded by their own malice, so that they go to the sepulcher and secure it. But by the dispensation of GOD this was done, so that the resurrection might be proven by hostile witnesses, while the sepulcher is secured and guarded. Namely so, that as Jerome speaks beautifully, the diligence of the enemies of Christ has profited our faith. For the more the sepulcher is reserved, the more the power of the resurrection is shown. Just as also from this, that when the pit, in which Daniel was enclosed, had been secured with seals, Daniel 6:17 God willed it to be established that he had been preserved by divine aid: so also it pleased divine wisdom that the sepulcher of Christ be fortified with a seal, so that in the same way, indeed, it might be manifest to all that the body of Christ had been guarded divinely in the sepulcher, and not taken from there by men. Furthermore, let us take care that we also faithfully guard Christ received in our heart, let us be vigilant, and let us not suffer the sleep of sins to creep in, lest anyone snatch Jesus from us. Let us seal our heart with an adamantine seal, as it were. Moreover, let us ask God that He may seal our hearts with His Holy Spirit, that most firm seal Eph. 1:13 c. 4:30. Finally, concerning the custom of the ancients of confirming pledges and other things for the sake of greater faith with a signet ring, see Ioh. Kirchm. in his single book on Rings, ch. 10; Conradus Rittershus. in book 7 of Sacred Readings, ch. 19, page 556, and others.

The present chapter comprises I. The apparition of the angel near the sepulcher of Christ, v. 1-8. II. The presentation of Christ himself, appearing to the women, v. 9-11. III.
