For it is established from this place 1. the true Deity of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. 2. the distinct personality of the same. The first member is evident from this, because in whose name we are baptized, he is true GOD. The reason is, because that phrase εἰς τὸ ὄνομα, comprises 1. divine institution: for to institute Sacraments is proper to GOD alone: because it is his to institute the means of grace, whose it is to give grace. 2. the invocation of GOD over the baptized. 3. the testification of the covenant of grace. 4. the obligation of the baptized, to invoke and worship him, in whose name he is baptized, just as B. Par. explains all these things at length in Exegt. L. de S S Trinit. §. 86. The ὁμοουσία or unity of these three persons pertains here, which the Doctors of the primitive Church prove from the singular number of the name ὄνομα, taken essentially here. Ambrose lib. 1. de Spiritu Sanct. c. 4. Who would dare to separate the unity of the name, when he sees the unity of the operation? But why do I establish unity with arguments, when there is an evident testimony of the divine voice, that there is one name of the F. S. & H. Spirit. For it is written: Go, baptize the nations in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the H. Spirit. In the name he said, not in names. Therefore not one name of the Father, another name of the Son, another name of the Holy Spirit, because one, not many names, because not two Gods, not three Gods. Theoph, Comm. in h. l. one name, one Deity. Jerome has similar things in h. l. As for what further concerns the equality of the divine majesty, common to all these three persons, the ancients proved the same likewise from this place, as can be seen from Isidore of Pelusium lib. 1. ep. 109. who says thus of the H. Spirit among other things: If he is a servant, let him not be numbered with the Lord. If he is created, let him not be joined with the creator. The second member, namely the distinct personality of these three, the Father, the Son, and the H. Spirit, is confirmed by 1. the denomination of the three distinct ones. concerning which matter Basil the Great ep. 64. The nature of the Father and of the Son and of the H. Spirit is indeed the same, and the divinity one, but the distinct names offer to us determined and absolute understandings. 2. the triple repetition of the article δεικτικοῦ and the addition to each name. 3. the repetition of the copulative conjunction καὶ made twice. 4. the collation of other Sc. S. Sayings, as those which teach that each person distributes peculiar benefits in and through Baptism. see concerning the Father Tit. 3, 5.1. Petr. 3, 21. concerning the Son Rom. 6, 4.Eph. 5, 26, 27.Gal. 3, 27. concerning the H. Spirit Ioh. 3, 5.Tit. 3, 5. Concerning the exceptions of the Photinians it is to be noted 1. that when 1. Cor. 10, 2. the Israelites are said to be baptized into Moses, the name Baptism is not taken for the Sacrament of initiation, divinely instituted for conferring the remission of sins and eternal salvation, which neither can, nor ought to be conferred in the name of any man, 1. Cor. 1, 13. but metaphorically and typically, for the leading through the Red Sea, which was a type of Baptism. nor are the Israelites said to be baptized into the name of Moses, but into Moses. 2. when certain ones are said to be baptized into John's baptism,Actor. 19, 3. that then nothing else is indicated, than that by the work and ministry of John baptism was conferred upon them. 3. that we are commanded to be baptized in the name of the Son and of the H. S. in the same way in which we are commanded to be baptized in the name of the Father, as is evident from the particle καὶ. But we are baptized in the name of the Father as true GOD, and as a distinct person. Therefore we are also baptized in the name of the Son and of the H. Spirit. that 4. when other things or persons are joined with GOD in divine works, then it clearly shines forth from the antecedents and consequents, that those created things or persons are not joined with GOD equally, but instrumentally. But in the form of baptism, the S. and H. S.

are joined equally with the Father. E. Gregory of Nyssa, Brother of Basil the Great, Oration on Holy Baptism, p. 259. Why do you cut and divide those three hypostases into diverse natures, and make three Gods unlike one another, when you receive one and the same grace from all? 5. Because this passage is a genuine part of Holy Scripture, since it is read not only in the most ancient Greek Codices, just as also among the Oriental Interpreters, the Syrian, the Arab, the Persian, and the Ethiopian, but is also cited by the Fathers. See Ignatius, Epistle to the Philadelphians; Tertullian, Against Praxeas, ch. 2, etc. Compare more on this matter in Blessed Par. Exeg. L. on the Mystery of the Most Holy Trinity, §. 89, following. Blessed D. Tarnov. Tractate on the Most Holy Trinity, p. 1004, following. Furthermore, Becanus, On the Judgment of Controversies, p. 81, §. 53, among other arguments by which he strives to destroy the perfection of Holy Scripture, urges this also, that it cannot be refuted from these words alone, if anyone should dare to deny that it is necessary to pronounce these words in Baptism: In the name of the F. S. and H. Spirit, but that it suffices if anyone while baptizing has the internal will and intention of baptizing in the name of the most holy Trinity, since those words: baptizing them etc. do not say that a vocal invocation of the Trinity must be employed. He adds, if the practice and tradition of the Church are rejected, there is no defense held against such an adversary. But Blessed D. Garthius has prolixly refuted the contrary against Becanus, adduced by Blessed Par. Tractate on Baptism, §. 88, newest edition, p. 262. But if the form of Baptism is handed down in these words, it is asked why the Apostles did not observe it, seeing that they baptized in the name of Jesus, as Luke testifies Acts 2, 38.c. 8, 16.c. 10, 48. Response. Luke is not speaking of the formal cause of Baptism, but of the efficient and final, and therefore his words are not to be taken dispensatively, but recitatively. Eulogius looks to this in sermon 2, in Photius, in the Library, ch. 190, and this pleases Blessed P. L. on Baptism, Blessed D. Walth. in H. B. p. 804. Compare also Blessed D. Bald. on the Epistle of Paul, p. 114, 115. Or it can be said that Luke used a compendious narration, saying that that which was performed by the Apostles in the name of the F. S. and H. S. was performed in the name of Christ, since when Christ is named, the whole Most Holy Trinity is indicated. Basil feels this way in On Holy Baptism, ch. 12, writing: ἡ τοῦ χριςοῦ προσηγορία τοῦ παντὸς ἐςι ὁμολογία. δηλοῦ γδ τόντε χρίσαντα θεὸν καὶ χρισθέντα ὑιὸν, καὶ τὸ χρίσμα τὸ πνεῦμα. So also Irenaeus, book 3, ch. 20. In the name of Christ, he writes, is understood he who anointed, and he himself who was anointed, and the anointing itself, in which he was anointed. Fulgentius, book on the Incarnation and grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, ch. 11, p. 727. Everyone who is washed in the sacrament of holy regeneration in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, is baptized in nothing other than in the death of Christ Rom. 6, 3. and in his name. Ambrose has similar things in book 1 on the Holy Spirit, ch. 3, and from him the Master of the Sentences, book 4, dist. 3, §. 2. Compare the Analysis on Act. 2, 38. Although it ought indeed to be a matter of religion for a Christian to use no other formula of Baptism than that which is held in the words of the Institution, namely: I baptize you in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, (whence it is also ascribed to the Eunomians as a peculiar heresy, because they rashly baptized not in the Most Holy Trinity, but in the death of Christ, as Socrates testifies, book 5, chapter 34), nevertheless our people warn (See Blessed D. Bald. Comm. on the ep. to ch. 6 Rom. p. 115; Blessed D. Hutterus, Loci Theologici Mai. p. 640; Blessed D. Konig, Cas. Catech. p. 212 seqq.; B. Par. L. on Baptism §. 93; Blessed D. Lobechius on the A. C. p. 233; Blessed D. Tarnovius, cited in the Theological Consultations of Dedek. Vol. 1, part 2, sect. 5, and others) that if certain Churches, for certain most grave reasons, were to use some other equivalent formula, that is, in the name of the Most Holy Trinity, or in the name of Christ, or in the death of Christ, or in the faith or Confession of God the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth, and of his only-begotten son our Lord Jesus Christ and of the Holy Spirit, since by this variation nothing is detracted from the substance of Baptism, therefore a baptism administered by this formula is not to be pronounced invalid. And hence they pronounce as erroneous the opinion of Bellarmine, book 1 on Baptism, ch. 3; Greg. de Valentia, Disputations 4 on Baptism in itself, q. 1, point 3; Thomas, q. 66, a. 5, ad 7; Altisiodorensis, Alensis, Bonaventura, Scotus, Richard, Paludanus, Marsilius, Gabriel, etc., in 4, dist. 3, q. 2, a. 2 & 3, 1, and others, who establish that Baptism is to be repeated, either absolutely or under condition, if it is given in the name of Christ, or of some other person of the Most Holy Trinity, without the expression of the others. Which opinion some Papists themselves, such as Cardinal Cajetan upon book 3 of Thomas, q. 66, art. 6, and Hugo, book 2 on the Sacraments, part 6, ch. 3, disapprove, having followed Ambrose, book 1 on the Holy Spirit, ch. 3, and Bede on ch. 10 of Acts. Tanner treats this controversy more prolixly in Scholastic Theology, vol. 4, Disp. 3, question 1, dub. 3, who himself also accedes to the common opinion of the Papists, and establishes that, that baptism must be repeated, if administered in the name of Christ or the Trinity; otherwise, if someone has baptized out of ignorance: I baptize you in the name of the Father etc. That also must be observed, that this precept concerning the preaching of the divine word and the administration of Baptism was given not only to the Apostles, but also to their successors in the Ecclesiastical Ministry, since Christ immediately adds: I will be with you even unto the consummation of the age. Which words certainly can by no means be applied to the Apostles alone, since they have long since been dead. Therefore, in the mentioned words of our Savior is contained a general precept, no less concerning the administering of the baptism of water than the preaching of the heavenly word until the end of the world. But the Photinians are foolish, see Socinus Disp. de Bapt. c. 2. p. 13. Volckelius de Verit. Relig. p. 414. 496. 665. asserting that that word baptizing, ought to be taken improperly, concerning the baptism namely of doctrine, and not indeed of water. And yet 1. the word βαπτίζειν nowhere in Holy Scripture denotes διδάσκειν, but commonly to wash, whether by immersion, or by sprinkling. 2. if it even denoted the same as to teach, nevertheless the proper and customary signification, by which it signifies the same as to submerge, to immerse or to sprinkle with water, to wash, ought to obtain for the time being, until the Photinians have proven that the proper and customary signification cannot have a place here. For the canon is known, to be observed especially in the interpretation of Holy Scripture, that we ought not to depart from the native and proper signification of words, unless necessity or some urgent reason requires it. Which here is none: nay rather 3. from the practice of the Apostles, which was entirely conformable to the command of the Master, it is sufficiently clear that the word βαπτίζειν ought to be taken here concerning the baptism of water. For it is certain that the Apostles not only preached the word, but also baptized with water as many as had given their name to Christ. See Act. 2, 41.c. 8, 38.c. 10, 47. 48. Nor do the passages Acts 18, 25.C. 19, 3. help the Photinians, since in those also the discourse is concerning the baptism of water. Finally, it is to be noted that in this latter member baptizing etc. the word all is to be repeated, so that the command of Christ is universal, comprehending infants also, as is clear both from the sentence of Christ John 3, 5. 6. coll. with Ps. 51.Eph. 2.

as also from the practice of the Apostles, Acts 16, 15.32. 33.c. 18, 8.1 Cor. 1, 16. Just as, therefore, if anyone were to deny that females ought to be baptized, this universal command of Christ would rightly be opposed to him, since indeed they also are included under the inclusion of all nations: so also from the same universal command it is rightly gathered that infants also (namely, those born in the Church, or whose parents have embraced the Christian faith, and likewise those who have lawfully come into our power, for the Sacraments are the proper goods of the Church) ought to be baptized. The Photinians and Anabaptists object, that τὸ teach precedes, and that therefore those at least are to be baptized who have first been taught concerning the articles of the Christian faith. I reply: 1. by conceding that those at least are to be baptized who can become disciples of Christ. Now, however, infants also born in the Church become disciples of Christ, since the kingdom of heaven belongs to them also, Matt. 18, 3.c. 19, 14. they are called by Christ, etc.; indeed, through the very administration of baptism, faith is kindled in them, see Tit. 3, 5. and thus they themselves become disciples of Christ. See B. D. Meisn. in Consid. Theol. Phot. p. 599. 2. by noting that Christ sent his Apostles not to infants, but to adults, and indeed to Gentiles, to whom nothing at all was known about Baptism; therefore, they had to be instructed first. Therefore, having instituted them in the Christian faith, he commanded Baptism to be conferred, yet not only on their persons, but also on their members, which are capable of sanctification; and such are infants. See Innocent III, C. Maiores de Bapt. & eius effect. Beautifully Augustine, ep. 89. to Hilar. We ought to speak so much the more for infants, the less they can speak for themselves. Distinguish, therefore, between a Church already planted, and one to be planted. V. B. Par. L. de Bapt. §. 185. B. D. Fewbr. Synt. 2. Dissert. Theol. p. 182. It is also to be noted that both from this place, and from Matt. 18 and 19. and from 1 Cor. 1. and Acts 16. certain Papists, see Capiro Explic. Cathol. p. 648. seqq., rightly prove infant baptism. Whence it is clear how ineptly those Papists act who, among other things, try to prove the imperfection of Holy Scripture from this also, that one must believe that the baptism of little ones is valid; but that this cannot be proved from the Scriptures alone. Thus Bell. l. 4. de V. d. C. 4. Tannerus in Coll. Ratisb. Gretserus in Defens., whom B.

Par. Conf. Cathol. l. 1. Gen. p. 59. seqq. Here it is at least to be noted that the Jesuit Petrus Cotonus in Instit. Cathol. p. 348. and 349., where he is very busy trying to prove the imperfection of H. S., omits infant baptism, and thus tacitly implies that it can be proved from H. S. But something must also be added concerning the end of Baptism. It is not only that it may be a mark of the profession of a people to be gathered from all nations, which is what the Photinians want; but also, and indeed primarily, that it may be a washing of regeneration and renewal, Ioh. 3, 5.Tit. 3, 5.

Latin:

* (v. 10. Docete &c. Quòd cùm non solùm praedicatione, sed & scriptione peragatur, neque enim praesentis solùm, sed & futuri temporis gentes docere Apostoli debuerunt, patet, quòd & scribendi mandatum illi ipsi acceperint. Id quod protervè inficias eunt Pontificii. Vid. Bellarminus lib. 4.

de V. D. c. 4. W. Lindanus lib. 1. Panopliae c. 23, Franc. Costerus in Enchir. Controv. pag. 43. quos contra prolixè disputant B. Par. Exeg. Loc. 1. §. 23. seqq. it. Confess. Cathol. l. 2. Spec. part. 1. art. 1. cap. 4. §. 2. Laur. Laelius de Verbo Dei, in praefat. Add. quoq; Rivetus in Isagog. ad Sac. S. c. 24. Notanter Augustinus lib. 1. de Consensu Evang. C. ult. Quicquid (Christus) de suis factis & dictis nos scire voluit, scribendum Apostolis tanquam suis manibus imperavit. Quae verba ipse Ederus, acerrimus aliàs errorum Papalium defensor, adducit lib. 3. Oecon. Bibl. pag. 326. Addatur quoque omninò Irenaeus lib. 3. contra Haeres. c. 1. Nicephorus lib. 2. c. 34. Huc facit quoque observatio autoris Manualis Curatorum, in quo docetur, quòd praedicatio alia fiat in scripto, ut Paulus ad Romanos, Corinthios &c. epistolas scripsit; alia in facto, ut omnis Christi actio nostra institutio; alia in verbo. Conf. quoque Gabr. Biel in Canon. Missae lect. 71.) *

* (Omnes gentes. Conf. Ps. 19, 5Marc. 16, 15.Luc. 24, 47.Actor. 17, 30.Rom. 10, 18.Col. 1, 6.28.2. Petr. 3, 9. Ambrosius lib. 2. de vocatione gentium C. 1. Numquid hâc praeceptione ( Matth. 28, 19.) ullarum nationum, ullorumve hominum facta disertio est? neminem merito excepit, neminem separavit genere, neminem conditione distinxit. Ad omnes prorsus homines missum est Evangelium crucis &c. Conferatur idem l. c. C. 2. 5. 6. sed dicat aliquis, 1. Si Evangelium ab Apostolis omnibus praedicari debuit gentibus, videri minùs rectè factum à Petro, quod ipse, conventione factâ, munus praedicandi gentibus Paulo reliquerit, ipse verò inter Iudaeos saltem praedicarit. Resp. distingvendo inter munus praedicandi ordinarium, & extraordinarium. Etsi Petrus ordinariè ac principaliter Iudaeis praedicarit, non tamen intermisit, gentibus quandoque praedicare, id quod factum etiam â Paulo, quantum ad Iudaeos. 2. Si Apostoli debuerunt praedicare omnibus gentibus, adeoque vocatio & gratia DEI universalis est, sequitur quod Evangelium etiam infantibus debuerit praedicari, imò & brutis, cùm Christus dicat: praedicate Evangelium omni creaturae. Hoc telo contra nostram sententiam arietat Ioh. Piscator Heborn. pag. 23. contra Hemming. Resp. Licet infantibus non potuerit praedicari Evangelii verbum audibile h. e. ita, ut per verbi auditum fuerint ad Christum conversi ac salutis aeternae facti compotes: praedicatum tamen illis fuit Evangelium per verbum visibile, hoc est, baptizati fuerunt in nomine P. F. & Sp. S. adeo-ue regeniti, Conf. Ioh. 3, 5.Tit. 3, 5. Quod instantiam de brutis attinet, risu potiùs ea & commiseratione digna est, quàm refutatione. Quis enim non videt, disertè Christū loqui, & Orthodoxos eius verba accipere, non nisi de creaturis rationalibus, h. e. quae beneficiorum, per Evangelilii praedicationem conferendorum capaces sunt, cuiusmodi soli homines, non bruta animalia. Neque verò sine causa Calviniani clarissimo huic oraculo tenebras offundere satagunt, quippe cùm egregiè hinc universalitas vocationis divinae, & quòd DEUS neminem ex absoluto quodam reprobationis decreto â salute excluserit, probetur. Excipiunt quidem contra praesentem locum variis modis. Verùm pridem abunde â nostratibus effugiis illis satisfactum est. vid. B. D. Menzerus in Dispp. contra Steinium ac Crocium, B. D. Meisnerus in Anthropol. B. D. Hutterus in L. L. Mai. B. Par. Coll. Isag. L. de Reprob. alii passim. Wendelini exceptiones variae Exerc. 71. §. 6. Exerc. 73. §. 2. seqq. Exerc. 117. §. 11. 12. quas iam nunc per temporis angustiam examinare non licet, ordine in Analectis ad Marc. 16, 15. discutientur) *

Antverpiensibus,) i. e. discipulum, quàm ordinis illius, inter ipsos quoque Pontificios passim malè audientis, nominare socium.) *

* (baptizate eos in nomine Patris, Filii & Spiritus Sancti. Basilius M. ep. 78. Baptizari nos oportet, sicut accepimus, credere autem, sicut baptizamur, glorificare autem, sicuti credimus, Patrem, Filium & Spiritum Sanctum. Principale hinc argumentum pro adstruendo S. S. Trinitatis mysterio depromitur. Etenim stabilitur ex h. l. 1. Patris, Filii ac Spiritus Sancti pera Deitas. 2. eorundem distincta personalitas. Primum membrum inde patet, quia in cuius nomine baptizamur, ille est verus DEUS. ratio est, quia phrasis illa εἰς τὸ ὄνομα, complectitur 1. divinam institutionem: Sacramenta namque instituere, est solius DEI proprium: quia eius est media gratiae instituere, cuius est gratiam dare. 2. DEI super baptizatum invocationem. 3. de foedere gratiae testificationem. 4. baptizati obligationem, ad eum, in cuius nomen baptizatur, invocandum & colendum, prout haec omnia prolixè exponit B. Par. Exegt. L. de S S Trinit. §. 86. Pertinet huc trium personarum istarum ὁμοουσία sive unitas, quam probant primitivae Ecclesiae Doctores ex sing. numero nominis ὄνομα, essentialiter hîc sumti. Ambrosius lib. 1. de Spiritu Sanct. c. 4. Quis unitatem separare audeat nominis, cùm operationis videat unitatem? sed quid ego unitatem argumentis adstruo, cùm divinae vocis evidens testimonium sit, unum nomen esse P. F. & Spir. Sanct. Scriptum est enim: Ite, baptizate gentes in nomine Patris, & Filii & Spir. Sancti. In nomine dixit, non in nominibus. Non ergo aliud nomen Patris, aliud nomen Flii, aliud nomen Spiritus Sancti, quia unus, non plura nomina, quia non duo Dii, non tres Dii. Theoph, Comm. in h. l. unum nomen, una Deitas. Similia habet Hironymus in h. l. Quod porrò maiestatis divinae, omnibus istis tribus personis communis, aequalitatem spectat, itidem ex h. l. eandem veteres probarunt, ceu ex Isidoro videre est Pelusiota lib. 1. ep. 109. qui ita de Spir. Sanct. inter alia: Si servus est, cum Domino minimè numeretur. Si creatus est, cum creatore minimè coniungatur. Alterum membrum, nempe trium istorum, Patris, Filii ac Spir. Sancti distinctam personalitatam, confirmant illam 1. trium distinctorum denominatio. quâ de re Basilius M. ep. 64. Patris & Filii & Spir. Sanctinaetura quidem eadem est, & divinitas una, nomina verò discreta determinatas nobis & absolutas intelligentias offerunt. 2. articuliδεικτικοῦtrina repetitio, & cuilibet nomini additio. 3. Coniunctionis copulativaeκαὶbis facta repetitio. 4. aliorum Sc. S. Dictorum collatio, utpote quae docent, quamlibet personam peculiaria beneficia in ac per Bapt. distribuere. vid. de Patre Tit. 3, 5.1. Petr. 3, 21. de Filio Rom. 6, 4.Eph. 5, 26, 27.Gal. 3, 27. de Spir. Sancto Ioh. 3, 5.Tit. 3, 5. Circa exceptiones Photinianorum notandum 1. quòd quando 1. Cor. 10, 2. Israelitae in Mosen baptizati dicuntur, nomen Baptismi non accipiatur pro Sacramento initiationis, ad conferendam peccarorum remissionem & aeternam salutem divinitus instituto, quod nec potest, nec debet ullius hominis nomine, conferri, 1. Cor. 1, 13. sed metaphoricè & typicè, pro deductione per mare rubrum, quae fuit Baptismi typus. nec dicuntur Israelitae. in nomen Mosis, sed in Mosen baptizati. 2. quando quidam in Iohannis baptisma dicuntur baptizati,Actor. 19, 3. quòd tunc nihil aliud indicetur, quàm quòd operâ ac ministerio Iohannis illis baptismus fuerit collatus. 3. quòd eo modo baptizari iubeamur in nomen Filii ac S. S. quo modo iubemur baptizari in nomen Patris, ceu patet ex partic. καὶ. Atqui in nomen Patris baptizamur ut veri DEI, & ut personae distinctae. E. etiam in nomen Flii ac Spir. Sanct. baptizamut. quòd 4. quando res vel personae aliae cum DEO in operibus divinis coniunguntur, tunc ex antecedentibus & consequentibus manifestè eluceat, illas res vel personas creatas non aequaliter, sed instrumentaliter cum DEO coniungi. At in formâ baptismi, F. ac Spir. Sanct.

aequaliter cum Patre coniunguntur. E. Gregorius Nyssenus Fr. Basilii M. Orat. de S. Bapt. p. 259. Cur trinas illas hypostaseis cōcidis atque dividis in diversas naturas, ac tres efficis Deos inter se dissimiles, quum unam & eandem ab omnibus gratiam accipiaas? 5. quòd locus hic genuina Sc. Sacrae pars sit, cùm non solùm in antiquissimis Codd. Graecis legatur, quemadmodum etiam apud Interpp. Orientales, Syrum, Arabem, Persam & Aethiopem, sed etiam â Patribus allegetur. vid. Ignatius ep. ad Philad. Tertul. adv. Praxeam c. 2. &c. Conf. plura in hanc rem apud B. Par. Exeg. L. de SS. Trin. Myst. §. 89. seqq. B. D. Tarnov. Tract. de S. S. Trinit. p. 1004. seqq. Porrò Becanus de iudic. Controv. p. 81. §. 53. inter alia argumenta, quibus Sc. S. perfectionem destruere satagit, hoc quoque urget, quòd ex solis bis verbis non possit confutari, si quis negare ausus fuerit, opus esse pronunciare in Baptismo haec verba: In nomine P. F. & Sp. Sancti, sed sufficere si quis inter baptizandum habeat internam voluntatem & intentionem baptizandi in nomine sanctissimae Trinitatis, siquidem verba illa: baptizantes eos &c. non dicant, vocalem Trinitatis invocationem adhibendam esse. addit, si praxis & traditio Ecclesiae respuantur, non haberi ullum praesidium contra talem adversarium. Verùm contrarium prolixè evicit B. D. Garthius contra Becanum, adductus à B. Par. Tract. de Bapt. §. 88. edit. noviss. p. 262. Ast si in his verbis forma Baptismi tradita est, quaeritur, cur Apostoli eam non observarint, baptizantes quippe in nomine Iesu, teste Lucâ Act. 2, 38.c. 8, 16.c. 10, 48. Resp. Loquitur Lucas non de causa Bapt. formaeli, sed efficiente ac finali, adeoque verba eius non dispensativè accipienda sunt, sed recitativè. Huc respicit Eulogius serm. 2. apud Phot. in Bibl. c. 190. placetque hoc B. P. L. de Bapt. B. D. Walth. in H. B. p. 804. Conf. quoque B. D. Bald. in Epist. Pauli p. 114. 115. Vel dici potest, quòd Lucas compendiosà narratione usus fuerit, illud, quod ab Apostolis in nomine P. F. & Sp. S. peractum est, in nomine Christi peractum dicens, quippe cùm Christo nominato, tota S. S. Trinitas indicetur. Ita sentit Basilius de S. Bapt. c. 12. scribens: ἡ τοῦ χριςοῦ προσηγορία τοῦ παντὸς ἐςι ὁμολογία. δηλοῦ γδ τόντε χρίσαντα θεὸν καὶ χρισθέντα ὑιὸν, καὶ τὸ χρίσμα τὸ πνεῦμα. Sic quoque que Irenaeus lib. 3. c. 20. In Christi, scribit, nomine subauditur qui unxit, & ipse qui unctus est, & ipsaunctio, in qua unctus est. Fulgentius l. de Incarn. & gratia D. N. I. C. c. 11. p. 727. Omnis qui in, nomine Patris & Filii & Sp. Sanct. sacramento sanctae regenerationis abluitur, non nisi in Christi morte ( Rom. 6, 3.) ac nomine baptizatur. Similia habet Ambros. l. 1. de S. S. C. 3. & ex eo Magister Sententiarum l. 4. dist. 3. §. 2. Conf. Anal. ad Act. 2, 38. Licet verò Christiano meritò religio esse debeat, aliâ Baptismi formulâ uti, quàm quae in verbis Institutionis habetur, nempe: baptizo te in nomine P. F. & Spiritus Sancti, (unde etiam Eunomianis ut peculiaris haeresis adscribitur, quòd temerariè non in SS. Trinitatem, sed in mortem Christi baptizarint, teste Socrate lib. 5. cap. 34.) monent tamen nostrates (Vid. B. D. Bald. Comm. in ep. ad c. 6. Rom. p. 115. B. D. Hutterus LL. Theol. Mai. p. 640. B. D. Konig Cas. Catech. p. 212. seqq. B. Par. L. de Bapt. §. 93. B. D. Lobechius in A. C. p. 233. B. D. Tarnovius, adductus in Cons. Theol. Dedek. Vol. 1. part. 2. sect. 5. alii.) quòd si Ecclesiae quaedam certis gravissimisq; de causis alia quadam formulâ uterentur aequipollente, hoc est, in nomine SS. Trinitatis, vel in nomine Christi, vel in mortem Christi, vel in fidē aut Confessionē Dei Patris omnipotētis, creatoris coeli & terrae, & unigeniti filii eius D. N. I. C. & Sp. S. quâ variatione cùm substantiae Baptismi nil derogetur, propterea baptismum istâ formulâ administratum non pronunciandum esse irritum. Atque hinc erroneam pronunciant sententiam Bellarmini l. 1. de Bapt. cap. 3. Greg. de Valentia Dispp. 4. de Bapt. secundum se q. 1. puncto 3. Thomae q. 66. a. 5. ad 7. Altisiodorensis, Alensis, Bonaventurae, Scoti, Richardi, Paludani, Marsilii, Gabrielis &c. in 4. dist. 3. q. 2. a. 2. & 3. 1. aliorumque, statuentium, Baptismum aut absolutè, aut sub conditione repetendum, si detur in nomine Christi, aut alterius cuiusdam personae SS. Trinitatis, sine expressione aliarum. Quā sententiam ipsi nonnulli Pontificii, ut Cardin. Caietanus super l. 3. Thomae q. 66. art. 6. Hugo l. 2. de Sacr. part. 6. c. 3. improbant, sequuti Ambrosium l. 1. de Sp. S. c. 3. Bedam in c. 10. Actor. Prolixius controversiam hanc pertractat Tannerus Theol. Schol. t. 4. Disp. 3. quaest. 1. dub. 3. qui ipse etiam communi Pontificiorum sententiae accedit, statuitque, iterandum esse baptismum, administratum in nomine Christi aut Trinitatis; secus, si quis ex ignorantia baptizarit: Ego baptizote in nomine Patria &c. Illud quoque observandum, quòd praeceptū hoc de verbi divini praedicatione & Baptismi administratione, non Apostolis solùm, sed eorum quoque in Ministerio Ecclesiastico successoribus datum sit, quippe cùm Christus immediatè subiungat: Ego ero vobiscum usque ad consummationem seculi. quae sanè verba minimè ad solos Apostolos possunt accommodari, cùm dudum illi fuerint defuncti. Continetur igitur in memoratis Salvatoris nostri verbis generale praeceptum, non minùs de Baptismo aquae administrando, quàm verbo coelesti praedicando usque ad mundi finem. Inepti verò, sunt Photiniani, vid. Socinus Disp. de Bapt. c. 2. p. 13. Volckelius de Verit. Relig. p. 414. 496. 665. statuentes, verbum illud baptizantes, impropriè accipi debere, de baptismo scil. doctrinae, non verò aquae. Atqui 1. verbum βαπτίζειν nullibi in Script. S. notat διδάσκειν, sed communiter abluere, sive per immersionem, sive per adspersionem. 2. si vel maximè idem notaret, ac docere, tantisper tamen propria & usitata significatio, quâ idem significat, quòd mergere, immergere vel aquâ adspergere, abluere, obtinere debet, dum evicerint Photiniani, propriam & usitatam significationem locum habere hîc non posse. notus enim est canon, in S. Sacrae interpretatione cumprimis observandus, quòd à nativâ & propria verborum significatione non debeamus recedere, nisi necessitas vel urgens quaedam ratio id requirat. quae hîc nulla: imò potiùs 3. ex Apostolorum praxi, quae mandato Magistri omninò conformis fuit, satis patet, quòd verbum βαπτίζειν de baptismo aquae accipi hîc debeat. Constat enim, quòd Apostoli non solùm verbum praedicarint, sed & aquâ baptizarint, quotquot Christo nomen dedissent. Vid. Act. 2, 41.c. 8, 38.c. 10, 47. 48. Nec iuvant Photinianos loca Actor. 18, 25.C. 19, 3. siquidem & in illis de Baptismo aquae sermo est. Denique notandum, quòd in posteriori hoc membro baptizantes &c. repetenda sit vox omnes. ut adeò mandatum Christi sit universale, infantes quoque comprehendens, ceu patet tum ex sententiâ Christi Ioh. 3, 5. 6. coll. cum Ps. 51.Eph. 2.

tum ex Apostolorum praxi, Actor. 16, 15.32. 33.c. 18, 8.1. Cor. 1, 16. Quemadmodum igitur si quis foemellas baptizandas esse negaret, rectè universale hoc Christi mandatum ei opponeretur, quippe cùm sub omnium gentium complexu illae quoque comprehendantur: ita quoq; ex eodem universali mandato rectè colligitur, infantes quoque, (puta in Ecclesia natos, sive quorum parentes Christlanam amplexi fidem sunt, item que qui in nostram potestatem legitimè pervenerunt, sunt enim Sacramenta Ecclesiae bona propria) baptizandos esse. Excipiunt Photin. & Anabaptistae, praecedereτὸ docete. adeoque illos saltem esse baptizandos, qui priùs fuerint edocti de fidei Christianae capitibus. Resp. 1. concedendo, illos salrem baptizandos esse, qui fieri Christi discupuli possunt. Iam verò infantes quoque in Ecclesia nati, fiunt Christi discipuli, quoniam ad eos quoque pertinet regnum coelorum, Matth. 18, 3.c. 19, 14. vocantur per Christum &c. imò per ipsius baptismi collationem fides in illis accenditur, vid. Tit. 3, 5. adeoque Christi discipuli ipsi fiunt. Vid. B. D. Meisn. in Consid. Theol. Phot. p. 599. 2. monēdo, quòd Christus Apostolos suos miserit nō ad infantes, sed ad adultos, & quidem gentiles, quibus nihil quicquā de Bapt. constabat, informandi igitur priùs illi erant. iis igitur in fide Christianâ institutis praecepit conferri Baptismum, nec tamen eorum tantùm personis, sed & membris, quae sanctificationis capacia sunt; huiusmodi verò sunt infantes. Vid. Innocentius 3. C. Maiores de Bapt & eius effect. Pulcrè August. ep. 89. ad Hilar. Tantò magis pro infantibus nos loqui debemus, quantò minùs pro se loqui possunt. dist. itaque inter Ecclesiam plantatum, & plant andam. V. B. Par. L. de Bapt. §. 185. B. D. Fewbr. Synt. 2. Dissert. Theol. p. 182. Illud quoque notandum, quòd tum ex h. l. tum ex Matth. 18 & 19. tum ex 1. Cor. 1. & Actor. 16. rectè Pontificii quidam, vid. Capiro Explic. Cathol. p. 648. seqq. Paedobaptismum probent. Unde patet, quàm ineptè agant Pontificii illi, qui inter alia ex eo quoque Scripturae S. imperfectionem probare conantur, quòd credere oporteat, Baptismum parvulorum esse ratum; id autem ex Scripturis solis probari nequeat. Ita Bell. l. 4. de V. d. C. 4. Tannerus in Coll. Ratisb. Gretserus in Defens. quos prolixè refellit B.

Par. Conf. Cathol. l. 1. Gen. p. 59. seqq. Hîc illud saltem notandum, quòd Iesuita Petrus Cotonus in Instit. Cathol. p. 348. & 349. ubi admodum occupatus est, ut Sc. S. imperfectionem probet, paedobaptismum omittat, adeoque tacitè innuat, è Sc. S. probari eum posse. Sed & de fine Baptismi aliquid adiiciendum est. Ille non solùm est, ut sit nota professionis populi ex omnibus gentibus congregandi, id quòd Photiniani volunt; verùm etiam, & quidem primarius, ut sit lavacrum regenerationis & renovationis, Ioh. 3, 5.Tit. 3, 5.) *

## 28:20
(v. 20. Teaching them to observe all things, whatsoever I have commanded you. Corn. à Lapide adds: namely all the precepts which I have commanded in the Gospel: for faith alone does not suffice for salvation, but the observation and assiduous operation of virtues is required. For not the hearers of the law are just before GOD, but the doers of the law shall be justified, Rom. 2.&3. Resp. What the sense of the Pauline saying is, will be taught in its own place. Here at least this must be observed 1. that we by no means posit that a dead faith, or one which is separated from good works, or rather a vain persuasion of faith, justifies: but we teach that true faith is never without good works. 2. nor do we deny that the observation of the commandments of Christ and the assiduous operation of virtues are required from the justified, but we defend this at least, that faith is that sole organ by which we apply the righteousness of Christ to ourselves. We exclude therefore G. W. not from the act of presence, but from the communication of efficiency. as has been shown elsewhere at greater length. See also B. Par. Confes. Cathol. l. 2. Spec. part. 3. art. 22. c. 3. Dn. D. Hülsem. Disp. de quaest. An G. W. sint necessaria ad salutem. 3. nor do we deny this, that around the times of the primitive Church those who received baptism from among the adults were ordered not only to give a profession of their faith in the SS. Trinity, as H. Grotius shows in this place from several things from the Constit. of Clement, Irenaeus, Tertullian, and others, but truly also to renounce the age, that is, to promise that they wish henceforth to lead their life according to the norm handed down by Christ. To which also the admonition of the Apostle is wont to be referred Rom. 12, 2. likewise the passage Art. 2, 41. When this had been done by them, with prayers offered to God, they were baptized, as H. Grotius deduces from antiquity in this place.)

Behold I am with you. Consult the parallel passages above c. 18, 20. Eph. 4. verse 10. Theophylact writes thus on this passage: He did not promise this to the Apostles alone, (namely that He would be with them,) but also to all His disciples without exception. For the Apostles were not going to live until the consummation of the age. (see above c. 13. verse 39. 49. chapter 24. verse 3.) And therefore He was promising the same thing both to us and to our successors. * (Theophylact indeed seems to have followed Chrysostom, who writes thus on this passage: He did not say that He would be present only with them, but also with all who were to believe after them. For neither were the Apostles going to live until the consummation of the age, but He speaks to the faithful as to one body. Augustine book 6 on Genesis literally chapter 8 said that Christ addressed us not yet born, even those to be born long after, and not only us, but also all those who are to be after us. Prosper book 2 on the calling of the nations chapter 2. Since you have entered as sheep into the midst of wolves, do not tremble at your own infirmity, O disciples! but trust in my power, who will not abandon you in all this work until the consummation of the age. But not to this end, that you may suffer nothing, but, which is much greater, I will provide that you are not overcome by any cruelty of the raging ones. Ezek. 48. verse 15. The name of the city from that day, The Lord is there. * (Beautifully Chrysostom in a homily before he went into exile: I do not trust in my own virtue, I have the scripture of my Lord, I hold His hand, that is a sufficiently safe security for me, that renders me secure and intrepid. Even if the world is shaken, I hold the security of my Lord. Do you wish that I recite it to you etc. Behold I am with you all the days of the age. Consult Isa. 45. verse 15. chapter 55, 21. chapter 59, 21. Jer. 1, 8. Zech. 2. verse 5. Exod. 20. verse 24. Levit. 26. verse 11. 12. Psalm 46. verse 5. 6. Psalm 48. verse 9. Psalm 89. verse 37. Daniel 2. verse 44. chapter 7. verse 14. Above chapter 18. verse 20. John 14. verse 18. Nor was this promise made only to the successors of the Apostles in the ministry of teaching, or to the ministers of the Church: but it concerns all the faithful entirely, as Jerome and Chrysostom rightly establish on this passage. Consult above chapter 18. verse 20. Elegantly Mr. Dr. John Olearius in the School of Patience page. 1084. Christ walking in the midst of the lampstands Apoc. 1. is present to the Church insofar as He has a head, eyes, voice, right hand, mouth, face, and feet, by which all things are subjected to Him, as it is written, Psalm 8. and whose footstool are the enemies, Psalm 110. Therefore He knows our distresses, which He sees, Apoc. 2. and is able μετριοπασθεῖν, Heb. 5. 2. to conquer death the last enemy, 1. Cor. 15. to crush Satan, Rom. 16. Because He is present with us, as King in the Kingdom, Father in the house etc. His delights are among men. Furthermore, our people rightly prove His omnipresence according to His human nature from this promise of Christ. See Blessed Dr. Mentzer against Crocius, Blessed Dr. Hutter, LL. Mai. page 186. and others. Beza objects on this passage: since the same Lord said a little before, you will not always have me, and soon ascended into heaven, it appears that the mode of presence and absence must be distinguished, so that He who is absent in body, is nevertheless most present by power, by which He truly communicates both Himself and all His things to us spiritually through faith. I reply 1. the genuine sense of the alleged saying of Christ was treated above chapter 26. verse 10. 2. Nor is His omnipresence to be denied from Christ's ascension, as has been noted elsewhere. 3. The modes of presence are indeed to be distinguished, but not as Beza wishes, but rather into visible, and invisible; local, and illocal. 4. Although therefore Christ is no longer present to us according to His human nature visibly and locally, He is nevertheless truly and substantially present with us invisibly, illocally and majestically. For He has sat down at the right hand of GOD, which is not a finite place in heaven, but the infinite and omnipresent majesty of GOD, of which Christ has been made a participant according to His human nature. And thus He is present not only as to operation or by virtual presence, which is also the opinion of the Jesuits, whence Corn. à Lap. on this passage: I am with you both as GOD, and as man, but by present aid, grace, strength, consolation etc. but substantially. Nor does Christ say: I work but I am with you etc. Thus Christ was present to Paul, 9. 22. and 26. Stephen. Acts 7. And for that reason He is called Emmanuel, Isa. 7. Consult also Apoc. 2. verse 1. John 14. verse 18. 33. Mr. Dr. Weller also rightly advises in his Commentary on the Ep. to the Rom. page 19 that all the preceding Δεικτικῶς designate the human nature, as that according to which Christ died, rose again, ascended into heaven, so that now the GOD-Man may send preachers, Eph. 4. verse 10. 11. Consult also Blessed Dr. Mylius

part. 1. Expl. A. C. page 77. b. B. D. Hutterus LL. Mai. page 192. Dnn. Theologi Sax. in Defens. Fundam. Pupillae c. 41. 85. B. D. Waltherus Miscell. Theol. Centur. page 360. B. Schrôterus in Sceptro Regali. B. D. Fewerb. Fascic. Dispp. on the omnipresence of Christ, as he is man, against Philippus Caesar, and others here and there. The things which Wendelinus Exerc. 67. 68. and 105. opposes to the orthodox opinion, can easily be dissolved, if at least the distinction is observed between local, and illocal; visible, and invisible presence; also between the human nature of Christ, considered from its own natural principles, and as it τοῦ λόγου ὑποςάσει subsists in itself, and is raised to the right hand of GOD. Those things which Cornelius à Lapide trifles about here concerning transubstantiation, by which Christ, through an admirable conversion of bread and wine into his body and blood, wishes to remain in the Church, are discussed elsewhere. See the Analecta above on Chapter 26, verse 26. Furthermore, there are those who think that the departure of Christ is insinuated by these words, as if he wished to say: I am indeed about to go into heaven, nor shall I be present with you in a visible manner: but I shall be present by divine efficacy. Certainly it is true that Christ promised his divine help and his gracious presence as σθεάνσθρωπος (to which point it belongs that to be with someone is said peculiarly of GOD, see Judg. 6, 12. 13.Jer. 1, 8.Acts 7, 9.) in these words to his disciples, and not to these alone, but also to their successors in the ministry, indeed to all the faithful.) *

* (Even to the consummation of the age. We have here an evident example of the rule that the particle ἕως so posits the antecedent that it nevertheless does not exclude the consequent. Concerning which matter it was treated at greater length in the Analecta on Matt. ch. 5, 26. To which things also brought forward in the said place can be added that of Nazianzen, Oration 2 on the Son: p. 579. τὸ ἕως οὐ πάντως ἀντιαιρεῖται τῷ μέλλοντι ἀλλὰ τὸ μέχρι μεν τόδε τίσθησι τὸ ὑπὲρ τοῦτο δὲ οὐκ ἀναίνεται. Especially also the passages Gen. 8, 7.Psalm 110, v. 1. seem to confirm this rule for the Blessed D. Hutter in LL. Mai. p. 74. Furthermore, the Papists, from the fact that Christ here promises to the Apostles and the remaining disciples, and thus to the visible Church, that he will be present to his Church, gather that the visible Church will endure perpetually. Bellarm. lib. 3 de Eccl. c. 13. I answer by distinguishing between the perpetual duration of the Church, and the external splendor of the visible Church. He proves that. The promise of Christ is not denied by us, but the question is concerning this, namely the external splendor of the Church, and it is denied by us. Conf. B. Par. L. de Eccl. §. 97. item Confess. Cathol. l. 2. Spec. part. 2. art. 5. c. 3. p. 1118. B. D. Mylium Expl. A. C. part. 1. p. 121. Nor does it follow, Christ said these words: Behold I am with you &c. to the visible Church, therefore a visible Church conspicuous to the whole world will always exist. For someone could similarly infer thus: Christ said these things visibly, therefore He will also be visibly present to the Church forever. Furthermore, Christ speaks here of the perpetual duration of the Church in general, but not of this or that Church in particular, and therefore not of the Roman one. For whatever promise was made here to Peter, the same was also made to the remaining Apostles. If therefore very many particular Churches planted by the Apostles have failed, conf. Apoc. 2, 5. why could the same not happen to the Roman one, since it has no special privilege anywhere in the Holy Scriptures. And experience itself also testifies that many Roman Pontiffs have apostatized from the faith and have become heretics. See B. P. Confess. Cathol. lib. 1. Gen. parte priore c. 2. B. D. Hutter. LL. Mai. p. 523. Camero in Myrothec. p. 121. maintains, there is no need for this promise to be understood concerning the successors of the Apostles, since it concerns the mission of the Apostles, which was not transmitted to any successors, as those whom the Apostles, insofar as they were Apostles, had none. Nor is there, he continues, any reason why anyone would want to say that this passage cannot be applied to the Apostles alone, because the Apostles did not live until the consummation of the age. For he answers, that Christ used this manner of speaking to indicate that He always wishes to be present with them, and it can be explained in such a way that the sense is, if it were possible that you should live until the end of the world, I would be present with you for the whole time, and so I will always be present with you. But there is no need at all to restrict this promise to the Apostles alone. For although the Apostles do not have successors insofar as they were Apostles, they did have them insofar as they were Teachers of the Church of Christ, and such are all faithful Ministers of the Church, to whom Christ wishes to be present. Indeed to the whole Church, which He also addresses in this place, as Beza himself admits here, and promises perpetual presence, as D. I. Crocius expressly writes in Anti-Becano. And this is the common opinion of the ancients, as we saw a little before. As regards the saying 1. Tim. 6, 14. which Camero compares with this place, where the Apostle declares to Timothy, that you keep these commandments until the glorious appearing of our Lord J. C. there likewise that precept regards not only Timothy, but all faithful Ministers of the Church, and ought to be kept by them until the coming of our Lord. And thus the contrary is rather proven from it. Nor does this place finally support Becanus, who desires to prove from this, that H. S. is obscure, in that it cannot be grasped by anyone, since those things which are said in H. S. to be given to Christ, are sometimes understood of Christ the head, sometimes of the body, sometimes of both, whether here the discourse is of the head. For while Christ here distinguishes himself clearly enough from his members or his mystical body, it is manifest that the mystical body cannot be understood here in the subject I. Finally, the Socinians err, urging that from this promise of Christ it can by no means be proven that the true Church will endure perpetually, until the end of the world, if indeed Christ wishes at least this, that he will be present with the faithful until the end of the world, if indeed such are always to be; but not promising that such are always to be. For it must be known, that Christ not only promises that he will always be present with the faithful, but also promises this, that there will always be some faithful, to whom he wishes graciously to be present. Conf. Matth. 16, 18.Eph. 6, 12. seqq. Add. Camero in Myroth p. 39. vers. 40. item in Praelect. But here we finish and THANKS BE TO GOD.

Latin:

* (v. 20. Docentes eos servare omnia, quaecunque mandavi vobis. addit Corn. à Lapide: puta omnia praecepta, quae in Evangelio mandavi: non enim sola fides sufficit ad salutem, sed requiritur observatio & adsidua virtutum operatio. Non enim auditores legis iusti sunt apud DEUM, sed factores legis iustificabuntur,Rom. 2.&3. Resp. Quis dicti Paulini sensus sit, suo docebitur loco. hîc illud saltem observandum 1. quòd minimè statuamus, fidem mortuam, vel quae à bonis operibus separata est, vel vanam potiùs fidei persvasionem iustificare: quin docemus, quòd vera fides nunquam sit sine bonis operibus. 2. nec negamus, mandatorum Christi observationem & adsiduam virtutum operationem requiri à iustificatis, sed hoc saltem defendimus, quòd fides sit unicum illud organon, quo Christi iustitiam nobis applicamus. Excludimus igitur B. O. non ab actu praesentiae, sed à communicatione efficientiae. uti pluribus alibi ostensum. Vid. etiam B. Par. Confes. Cathol. l. 2. Spec. part. 3. art. 22. c. 3. Dn. D. Hülsem. Disp. de quaest. An B. O. sint necessaria ad salutem. 3. nec hoc negamus, quòd circa primitivae Ecclesiae tempora illi, qui ex adultis baptismum suscipiebant, non solùm fidei suae in SS. Trinitatem edere professionem iussi fuerint, ceu plusculis ex Constit. Clementis, Irenaeo, Tertulliano, aliisque ostendit H. Grotius in h. l. verùm etiam seculo renunciare hoc est, promittere, quòd vitam ad normam à Christo traditam exigere deinceps velint. quo etiam referri solet monitum Apostoli Rom. 12, 2. item locus Art. 2, 41. Quod cùm factum ab illis esset, praemissis ad Deum precibus, baptizabantur, ceu multis ex antiquitate deducit H. Grotius ad h. l.) *

Ecce ego vobiscum sum. Confer loca parallela suprà c. 18, 20. Ephs. 4. vers. 10. Theophylactus ita in hunc locum scribit Non solis Apostolis hoc pollicitus est, (nempe se cum eis futurum,) sed & omnibus simpliciter suis discipulis. Nam Apostoli non erant victuri usque ad consummationem seculi. (vid. suprà c. 13. vers. 39. 49. cap. 24. vers. 3.) Et nobis igitur & successoribus nostris idipsum pollicebatur * (Sequutus vero videtur Theophylactus Chrysostomum, qui ita in hunc locū: Non cum illis tantùm se adfuturum esse dixit, sed & cum omnibus, qui post eos credituri essent. Neque enim Apostoli usque adconsummationem seculi victuri erant, sed tanquam uni corpori loquitur fidelibus. Augustinus lib. 6. de Genesi ad litt. cap. 8. Christum nos nondum natos, etiam longè pòst futuros, nec tantùm nos, sed etiam omnes eos, qui futuri sunt post nos, alloquutum dixit. Prosper lib. 2. de vocat. gentium cap. 2. Cùm sicut oves introieritis in medium luporum, nolite de vestr â infirmit ate trepidaze, ô discipuli! sed de meâ potestate confidite, qui vos usque ad consummationem seculi in omni hoc opere non derelinquam. sed non ad hoc, ut nihil patiamini, sed, quod multò maius est, praestiturus, ut nullâ saevientium crudelitate superemini.Ezech. 48. vers. 15.Nomen civitatis ex illa die, Dominus ibidem. * (Pulcrè Chrysostomus homil. antequam iret in exilium: Non ego propriae virtuti confido, habeo scripturam Domini mei, manum ipsius teneo, illa mihi cautio satis tuta est, illa me securum reddit & intrepidum. Etiomsi orbis terrarum commoveatur, ego cautionem Domini mei teneo. Vultis ut vobis recitam &c. Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus seculi. Conf. Esa. 45. vers. 15.cap. 55, 21.cap. 59, 21. Ierm. 1, 8. Zach. 2. vers. 5.Exod. 20. vers. 24.Levit. 26. vers. 11. 12.Psalm. 46. vers. 5. 6.Psalm. 48. vers. 9.Psalm. 89. vers. 37.Daniel. 2. vers. 44.cap. 7. vers. 14. Suprâ cap. 18. vers. 20.Ioh. 14. vers. 18. Neque solùm Apostolorum in docendi ministerio successoribus, sive ministris Ecclesiae facta haec promissio est: sed omnes omninò fideles concernit, uti rectè Hieron. ac Chrysostomus in hunc locum statuunt. Conf. suprà cap. 18. vers. 20. Eleganter Dn. D. Iohan. Olearius in Scholâ Patientiae pag. 1084. Christus in medio candelabrorum ambulansApoc. 1.Ecclesiae praesens est, quatenus caput, oculos, vocem, dextram, os, faciem habet, & pedes, quibus omnia subiecta l. d. &Psalm. 8.quorum scabellum sunt inimici Psam. 110. Ergo scit angustias nostras, quas videt,Apoc. 2.& potestμετριοπασθεῖν,Ebr. 5. 2.mortem ultimum hostem vincere,1. Cor. 15.Satanam conterere,Rom. 16.Quia adest nobis, ut Rex in Regno, Pater in domo &c. delitiae eius apud homines. Rectè porrò ex hac Christi promissione omnipraesentiam illius secundùm humanā naturā nostrates probant. Vid. B. D. Mentzerus contra Croc. B. D. Hutter. LL. Mai. pag. 186. alii Excipit Beza in h. l. cùm idem Dominus paulò ante dixerit, me verò non semper habebitis, & mox in coelū adscenderit, apparere, distinguendum esse praesentiae & absentiae modum, ut qui corpore est absens, virtute tamē sit praesentissimus, qua & seipsum & sua omnia nobis verè per fidem spiritualiter communicat. Resp. 1. de genuino allegati dicti Christi sensu suprà cap 26. vers. 10. actum. 2. Nec ex Christi adscensione omnipraesentia eius neganda, ut alibi monitum. 3. Distinguendi utique praesentiae modi sunt, sed non ut Beza vult, verùm in visibilem, & invisibilem; localem, & illocalem. 4. Licet proinde Christus non ampliùs praesens secundùm humanam suam naturam nobis sit visibiliter & localiter, verè tamen ac substantialiter nobis adest invisibiliter, illocaliter & maiestaticè. Consedit enim ad dextram DEI, quae non est finitus in coelo locus, sed infinita & omnipraesens DEI maiestas, cuius secundùm humanam naturam Christus factus est particeps. adeoque praesens est non solùm quoad operationē seu praesentiâ virtuali, quae etiam Iesuitarum sententia est, unde Corn. â Lap. h. l. vobiscum sum tum qua DEUS, tum qua homo, sed per praesentem opem, gratiam, robur, consolationem &c. sed substantiali. Neque dicit Christus: ego operor sed ego sum vobiscum &c. Ita Christus adfuit Paulo, 9. 22. & 26. Steph. Act. 7. Atq; eâ de causa vocatur Emanuel, Esa. 7. Conf. quoque Apoc. 2. vers. 1.Iohan. 14. vers. 18.33. Rectè etiam monet Dn D. Wellerus Comm. in Ep. ad Rom. pag 19. omnia antecedentia Δεικτικῶς humanam naturam designare, utpote secundùm quam Christus mortuus est, resurrexit, in coelum adscendit, ut nunc DEUS-Homo concionatores mittat, Ephes. 4. vers. 10. 11. Conf. etiam B. D. Mylius

part. 1. Expl. A. C. pag. 77. b. B. D. Hutterus LL. Mai. pag. 192. Dnn. Theologi Sax. in Defens. Fundam. Pupillae c. 41. 85. B. D. Waltherus Miscell. Theol. Centur. pag. 360. B. Schrôterus in Sceptro Regali. B. D. Fewerb. Fascic. Dispp. de omnipraesens. Christi, ut homo est, adversus Philippum Caesarem, aliosque passim. Quae Wendelinus Exerc. 67. 68. ac 105. Orthodoxae sententiae opponit, facilè possunt dissolvi, si observetur saltem distinctio inter praesentiam localem, & illocalem; visibilem, & invisibilem; it. inter humanam Christi naturam, consideratam ex principiis suis naturalibus, & quat. in ipsâ τοῦ λόγου ὑποςάσειsubsistit, & ad dextram DEI erecta. Quae Cornel. à Lapide de transsubstantiatione, quâ Christus per admirabilem conversionem panis & vini in corpus & saugvinem suum, velit in Ecclesia manere, hîc nugatur, alibi discutiuntur. Vid. Analect. suprà ad C. 26. vers. 26. Sunt porrò, qui putant, insinuari his verbis Christi abscensionem, quasi dicere voluerit ipse: Abiturus sum quidem in coelum, nec adero vobis adspectabili modo: sed adero divinâ efficaciâ. Sanè certum est, quòd Christus divinum auxilium suum ac gratiosam suam praesentiam ut σθεάνσθρωπος (quo spectat, quòd esse cum aliquo, peculiariter de DEO dicatur, vid. Iudic. 6, 12. 13.Ierem. 1, 8.Act. 7, 9.) promiserit his verbis discipulis suis, nec his tamen solùm, sed etiam eorum in ministerio successoribus, imò omnibus fidelibus.) *

* (Usque ad consummationem seculi. Evidens hîc habemus exemplum regulae, quòd particula ἕως ita ponat antecedens, ut tamen consequens non excludat. quâ de re prolixiùs actum in Anal. ad Matth. cap. 5, 26. Quibus etiam d. l. allatis addi potest illud Nazianzeni Orat. 2. de Filio: p. 579. τὸ ἕως οὐ πάντως ἀντιαιρεῖται τῷ μέλλοντι ἀλλὰ τὸ μέχρι μεν τόδε τίσθησι τὸ ὑπὲρ τοῦτο δὲ οὐκ ἀναίνεται. Cumprimis etiam regulam hanc confirmare B. D. Huttero in LL. Mai. p. 74. videntur loca Gen. 8. 7.Psalm. 110. v. 1. Goeterùm Pontificii ex eo, quòd Christus hîc Apostolis & reliquis discipulis, adeoque Ecclesiae visibili, promittit, se praestò futurum Ecclesiae suae, colligunt, Ecclesiam visibilem perpetuò duraturam. Bellarm. lib. 3. de Eccl. c. 13. Resp. dist. inter Ecclesiae perpetuam durationem, & visibilis Ecclesiae externum splendorem. Illam probat. Christi promissio, nec à nobis negatur, sed de hoc, nempe externo Ecclesiae splendore quaestio est, & à nobis negatur. Conf. B. Par. L. de Eccl. §. 97. item Confess. Cathol. l. 2. Spec. part. 2. art. 5. c. 3. p. 1118. B. D. Mylium Expl. A. C. part. 1. p. 121. Nec sequitur, Christus verba haec: Ecce ego vobiscum sum &c. ad Ecclesiam visibilem dixit, ergo visibilis totique mundo conspicua Ecclesia semper futura. Posset enim similiter quis ita colligere: Christus visibilis haec dixit, E. etiam visibiliter semper praesto Ecclesiae futurus erit. Praeterea loquitur hîc Christus de Ecclesiae in genere perpetua duratione, nō vero huius vel illius Ecclesiae in specie, adeoq; nec Romanae. Qualis enim promissio hîc Petro facta, eadem quoque facta Apostolis reliquis. Si igitur plurimae Ecclesiae partic. ab Apostolis plantatae defecerunt, conf. Apoc. 2, 5. quidni idem contingere Romanae potuit, cum nullibi in Sc. S. peculiare ea habeat privilegium. Et testatur quoque ipsa experientia, multos PP. RR. apostatasse à fide, factos que esse haereticos. Vid. B. P. Confess. Cathol. lib. 1. Gen. parte priore c. 2. B. D. Hutter. LL. Mai. p. 523. Camero in Myrothec. p. 121. statuit, nihil opus esse, ut promissio haec intelligatur de posteris Apostolorū, siquidē agatur de missione Apostolorū, quae non fuerit transmissa in ullos successores, ut quos Apostoli, quatenus Apostoli, nullos habuerunt. Nec esse, pergit, quòd aliquis velit dicere, solis Apostolis non posse hunc locum accommodari, quia Apostoli non vixerunt usque ad consummationem seculi. Respondet enim, Christum usum esse loquutione hac ad indicandum, quòd semper illis velit adesse. ac posse eam sic exponi, ut sensus sit, si fieri posset, ut viveretis usque ad sinem mundi, ego toto tempore vobis adessem, itaque semper adero vobis. Sed minimè opus est, ad solos Apostolos promissionem hanc adstringere. licet enim Apostoli non habeant successores, quat. fuerunt Apostoli, habuerunt tamen quatenus Ecclesiae Christi Doctores fuerunt, ac tales sunt omnes fideles Ecclesiae Ministri, quibus Christus adesse vult. Imò toti Ecclesiae, quam etiam h. l. alloquitur, ipso Beza hîc fatente, promittitque perpetuam praesentiam, uti expressè scribit D. I. Crocius in Anti-Becano. Estque haec communis veterum sententia, ut paullò ante vidimus. Quod attinet dictum 1. Tim. 6, 14. quod Camero cum h. l. confert, ubi Apostolus Timotheo denunciat, ut servet haec mandata usque ad illustrem adventum Domini nostri I. C. ibi pariter praeceptum illud non solùm Thimotheum, sed omnes fideles Ecclesiae Ministros respicit, & ab illis servari debet usque ad Domini nostri adventum. adeoque contrarium ex eo potiùs evincitur. Nec quicquam tandem locus hic Becano patrocinatur, probare hinc cupienti, quòd Sc. S. sit obscura, eò quòd non possit à quolibet deprehendi, cùm quae in Script. S. data Christo dicuntur, aliquando intelligantur de Christo capite, aliquando de corpore, aliquando de utroque, an hîc de capite sermo sit. Etenim dum Christus hîc satis elarè se distingvit à membris sive corpore suo mystico, manifestum est, quòd hîc non possit intelligi corpus mysticum in subiecto Ego. Denique errant Sociniani, urgentes, quòd ex promissione hâc Christi minimè probari possit, Ecclesiam veram perpetuò duraturam, usque ad mundi finem, siquidem Christus hoc saltem velit, se adfuturum fidelibus usque ad mundi finem, si nempe tales semper futuri; non verò promittere, quòd tales semper futuri sint. Etenim sciendum, quòd Christus non solùm promittat, se fidelibus semper adfuturum, sed etiam hoc promittat, quòd futuri semper aliqui fideles sint, quibus gratiosè velit adesse. Conf.
